docs.text: 40 1.4 Data Transfers between SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA and SAP EWM The master data in SAP EWM is classified into two primary categories. The first category is external data , which must be replicated from the SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA system into the SAP EWM environment. This external data includes information like material master, vendor master, customer master, plant, and other similar data . The replication of this data is a necessary step in order to ensure accurate and up-to-date data in the SAP EWM environment. The second category is internal data , which is created exclusively within the SAP EWM environment.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This type of data includes storage bin master data and packaging specification master data. These data elements are typically created when setting up the SAP EWM system and are maintained within the SAP EWM system. Note that the master data replication process from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to SAP EWM is a critical component of the overall system setup. This process ensures that the data in the SAP EWM system is consistent with the data in the SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA system. Additionally, the replication process also ensures that any changes made to the data in the ERP or in the SAP S/4HANA system are reflected in the SAP EWM system.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Let’s now consider the di ff erent data transfer processes, for SAP NetWeaver deployments, embedded EWM deployments, and decentralized EWM deployments: Data transfer for SAP NetWeaver deployment (SAP EWM 9.5 and below) As shown in Figure 1.9 to enable the deployment of SAP EWM 9.5 and lower through the SAP NetWeaver SAP Business Suite, the system utilizes the CIF technology to transfer master data between SAP ERP and SAP EWM. CIF is primarily utilized for exchanging data between SAP ERP and SAP Supply Chain Management (SAP SCM).

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, in the case of SAP EWM, only master data is transferred from SAP ERP to SAP EWM, and no communication occurs in the opposite direction via CIF. In contrast, transactional data , such as inbound and outbound delivery documents originating from SAP ERP, are integrated into SAP EWM through the queued remote functional call (qRFC) technology. However, note that the transmission of transaction data from SAP S/4HANA to embedded EWM still requires the use of qRFC technology. qRFC is a communication method used by SAP systems to transfer data between systems in a reliable and e ff icient manner.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA

Overall, integrating production with a WMS improves supply chain visibility and operational e ff iciency, resulting in increased customer satisfaction and profitability. By combining the production planning, materials management, and SAP EWM modules, e ff icient production management can be achieved. This is possible due to the modules providing end-to-end visibility and control over the entire production process.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The production planning module facilitates production planning and scheduling, while the SAP EWM module covers goods receipt and goods issue process. By integrating production processes with SAP EWM, the precision of inventory management has been enhanced, enabling improved tracking of raw materials, components, and finished goods . Furthermore, it facilitates real-time monitoring of production activities, leading to informed decision-making based on up-to- date data. Moreover, the integration of production processes with SAP EWM o ff ers enhanced inventory visibility by allowing the receipt of final products directly from production to warehouses.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It also enhances the operation of production supply areas by optimizing the staging of components and semi- finished materials. Finally, posting the goods consumption provides improved inventory and cost visibility. The process of integrating production processes with SAP EWM commenced in the early 2010s with the introduction of production integration functionality. This enabled real-time communication between SAP EWM and other SAP modules, including production planning and materials management. The result was a more cohesive and integrated approach to warehouse and production management. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 59 SAP EWM has undergone significant evolution over the years, continuously enhancing and adding new capabilities to better cater to the dynamic needs of businesses in warehouse and production management. Presently, SAP EWM is widely adopted across various industries, and its integration with production processes remains a vital aspect of the solution. The primary objective of integrating production and extended warehouse management, as shown in Figure 2.1, is to facilitate the timely and e ff icient staging of products , also known as production staging , from the warehouse to the assembly line.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This step also involves posting consumption for the production process, returning unused components, and receiving finished products into the warehouse. Modern automated warehouses employ a variety of technologies, including material flow systems , automated storage and retrieval systems , automated guided vehicles (AGVs) , and warehouse robotics solutions, to fulfill production integration requirements. By leveraging these technologies, businesses can optimize warehouse operations, lower costs, and enhance productivity, resulting in improved business outcomes.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The integration of SAP EWM with production processes is gaining popularity in several industries, including discrete manufacturing , process manufacturing , and repetitive manufacturing . This integration serves various business functions, such as transferring raw materials or semi-finished components from the warehouse to production lines and receiving finished or semi-finished materials from production or assembly lines to the warehouse. Figure 2.2 Delivery-Based Production Integration The benefits of integrating delivery-based production include the following: The warehouse operation team can perform multiple tasks within the SAP ERP system. The warehouse can transport materials from the warehouse to the production location in a shuttle scenario. Moreover, they have access to the shipping functionality within SAP ERP, which enables them to manage the shipment of goods. The team can also utilize the Kanban functionality within SAP ERP, which is a tool used in lean manufacturing to regulate production levels based on Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

Figure 2.3 One SAP EWM-Managed Storage Location Separate locations (two SAP EWM-managed storage locations in one warehouse) As shown in Figure 2.4, SAP EWM handles production inventory separately from other kinds of stock, allowing for clear tracking of stock down to the storage bin level in SAP EWM and at the storage location level in the SAP ERP system. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 66 Figure 2.6 Materials Management-Inventory Management Storage Location for Production 2.2.2 Staging for Manufacturing Orders In simpler terms, staging to production refers to the process of selecting the requested raw materials or components and delivering them to designated supply area to production, with the help of SAP EWM. The necessary materials for production assembly lines are stored in a warehouse, which is managed by a team responsible for making the required components and materials available for manufacturing orders.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This process involves transferring the materials and components from the warehouse to the production supply area and preparing the workstations and resources necessary for the production process. This transfer of materials from the warehouse to the production supply area is known as the staging process in SAP EWM. As shown in Figure 2.7, SAP EWM o ff ers various options for staging to production, which can be triggered by SAP EWM itself or a core system such as SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, or a production system such as SAP Manufacturing Execution or SAP Digital Manufacturing.

docs.text: 67 As shown in Figure 2.8, SAP provides the following staging options: Staging for production with deliveries Production supply with Kanban Production supply with just-in-time (JIT) Figure 2.8 Process Overview: Picking and Staging In the following sections, we’ll walk through the business process for staging production with deliveries and with one SAP EWM-managed storage location (AFS storage location). We’ll discuss the configuration and master data for this process and then walk you step-by-step through a process demo.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Business Process As shown in Figure 2.9, for this business process, you would follow these high- level steps: A manufacturing order for both pick parts and release parts is created in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. The manufacturing order is released, and staging for individual production orders (pick parts) is performed using Transaction CO02, while collective staging for multiple orders (release order parts) is carried out using Transaction MF60. The release of the manufacturing order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA triggers warehouse management material staging, which can be automated.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 68 The replenishment process starts in SAP EWM, and a production supply delivery (posting change delivery) is created in the background. The warehouse task is created based on the posting change delivery, which is confirmed in SAP EWM. The destination bin is determined from the production supply area. The confirmation of the warehouse task triggers a dummy transfer posting within the AFS storage location, using movement type 411. Figure 2.9 Staging for Production with Deliveries: AFS Storage Location Note The production staging, consumption and goods receipt process for delivery- based production integration is using one SAP EWM storage location for warehouse and production location and hence in the following section configuration and master data setting has been set accordingly.

docs.text: 95 2.3 Advanced Production Integration As shown in Figure 2.55, in an advanced production integration system, SAP EWM controls all essential steps including component supply, supply of semi- finished materials, and receipt of finished or semi-finished products. There is no need for a delivery document on the ERP side. Advanced production supply using PMRs has several features including: The introduction of the new PMR object, which o ff ers greater flexibility in the staging process within SAP EWM. A new option for SAP EWM staging has been added to the control cycle in addition to the existing pick parts and release order part options.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system supports single-order staging, cross-order staging, and manual staging. Status and quantity updates for manufacturing orders are supported. The system allows for user-driven staging via desktop transactions or in the background. Figure 2.55 Advanced Production Integration The advantages of using an advanced production integration system include the following: Once PMRs are created, your warehouse operations teams can work independently of SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. The system allows for the warehouse to stage the quantity of components into smaller quantities (pallet by pallet staging), which provides flexibility in Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 96 better utilizing space in the production supply area or when manufacturing orders run over longer periods. Users have more flexibility to post goods issues for a material than was planned in PMR. PMR-based production supply uses a lean system communication approach by sending just one goods movement message to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, rather than creating several delivery documents. Advanced production integration provides flexibility to receive packed HUs from production lines or conveyor systems using radio frequency (RF) devices.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system also o ff ers the option to return to the warehouse unused pallets that are no longer needed for production or any additional pallets sitting at a production supply area. SAP EWM is responsible for staging, adding more flexibility to augment production supply. In this section, we’ll walk through each part of advanced production integration, including staging, consumption, goods receipt, and clearing the production supply area bin for manufacturing orders as well as how to create part replenishments. 2.3.1 Staging for Manufacturing Orders In this section, we’ll delve into staging for manufacturing orders in advanced production integration processes, which involves the preparation and gathering of materials required for production.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This phase includes activities such as creating PMRs from the warehouse and transferring them to the production area. Staging ensures that all necessary components are available when needed, thus optimizing the production process and minimizing delays. Business Process Business warehouses utilize a staging process to supply materials, whether packed or unpacked, to production and then consume these materials during the production process. To ensure that materials are supplied as needed and to prevent delays, the staging process is planned systematically with the help of advanced production integration in SAP EWM.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 97 quantity or a significant amount of manufacturing time, production can occur either with the full requested quantity or with partial quantities, HU after HU. This approach also maximizes the utilization of space in the production supply area. As shown in Figure 2.56, with advanced production integration, the SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA system automatically creates a PMR in SAP EWM when a manufacturing order is released. This PMR triggers the warehouse management material staging process, which can be done manually or automatically.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 2.56 Material Staging for Production In SAP EWM, the Transaction /SCWM/STAGE (Schedule Staging for Production) can be used to create a staging warehouse task. This transaction can be executed manually or as a background job with input parameters such as warehouse, production staging area, and staging method. If a user needs to select a specific PMR and stage materials accordingly, the Web Dynpro user interface (UI) Transaction NWBC can be used to provide more flexibility and enable a user to view the stock overview in the production supply area.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In advanced production integration, SAP EWM provides several options for staging materials, including the following: Single-order staging In this staging approach, the system generates a warehouse task for each line item in a PMR to move the product to the production supply area, as shown in Figure 2.57. Each warehouse task is linked to a single PMR, and once confirmed, the task is associated with the specific PMR item. The material and batch consumption posting can be done for the same PMR. If a HU or material Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 98 is not required for production, the user can manually release the PMR item reference for stock. The single-order staging method enables the staging of products for a particular PMR or for a PMR with unique characteristics. For example, products can be staged from a specific batch for a particular PMR. Figure 2.57 Single-Order Staging Cross-order staging In this material staging method, the system accumulates material from multiple PMRs and generates a warehouse task to move the material together. The warehouse task created in this method is not linked to any specific PMR item.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: After the warehouse task is confirmed, it does not have any reference to a PMR item. Consumption posting for material and batch can be posted for the PMR that has an item for the material and batch. This method o ff ers flexibility since warehouse users can stage products for a single PMR or for several PMRs. To maintain a minimum quantity of the product on the production supply area, the bin assignment is used. If the sum of the quantity in the production supply area and open warehouse task quantity is less than the minimum quantity, the system generates a warehouse task to move the replenishment quantity to the production supply area.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The replenishment quantity is also maintained in the bin assignment. In addition to single-order staging and cross-order staging, you also have the option for part replenishment creation or to use no order staging at all, but these methods are not as widely used so they will not be covered in depth here. docs.text: 119 2.3.2 Consumption for Manufacturing Orders In this section, we’ll provide a detailed explanation of the consumption process in advanced production integration. In short, a manufacturing order process in SAP entails tracking and recording the utilization of materials and resources throughout the production of goods. Business Process After products, batches, or HUs have been used in a manufacturing process, an important step is recording their consumption in both the SAP EWM and SAP ERP systems. This consistency helps you maintain accurate inventory levels and enables better planning of raw materials and components.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP EWM provides an option for advanced production integration, which allows for consumption posting using RF or desktop transactions in SAP EWM. Consumption posting can be performed for the entire quantity of a product at once or for partial quantities at regular intervals, depending on the manufacturing process, as shown in Figure 2.90. You can also reverse consumption postings if needed. Over-quantity consumption refers to posting consumption for more of a product than was planned in the PMR, while partial consumption allows users to post consumption based on quantities that have already been used or on remaining quantities.

docs.text: 136 Note The clear production supply area process using advanced production integration is now complete. 2.3.5 Create Part Replenishment Process In this section, we’ll provide a detailed explanation of the create part replenishment process for advanced production integration. In short, create part replenishment process refers to the procedure of generating replenishment requests to ensure an adequate supply of parts is always available in the production supply area. Business Process In SAP EWM, Create Part Replenishment is a process that helps ensure that there are su ff icient inventory levels of parts available at production supply area to fulfill demand manufacturing order.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In a production BOM, some raw materials or components may not be included in the single-order staging or cross-order staging process but may still need to be staged under specific circumstances. This scenario can be achieved either by pallet-based staging, based on predefined packaging specifications, or by staging a predefined quantity using Transaction /SCWM/PSASTAGE. When a manufacturing order is released, a PMR is generated to request the creation of a part for replenishment. This step triggers the creation of a warehouse task to pick the part from a storage location that maintains inventory for the material and stage it to the production supply area.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Automation of the replenishment process is possible by setting parameters that determine when the inventory level falls below a certain quantity at the production supply area, prompting the system to initiate the replenishment process automatically. Overall, the create part replenishment process in SAP EWM helps ensure that inventory levels are optimized and that parts are available when needed for outbound processing or production processes. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 150 3 Quality Management Quality management is a pivotal component of SAP S/4HANA that enables businesses to implement and operate quality control processes with ease. It is crafted to prevent defects, foster continuous process improvement, and establish sustainable quality control programs. The aim of this chapter is to provide you with a comprehensive guide to various quality management processes and their seamless integration with SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM), especially with embedded Extended Warehouse Management in SAP S/4HANA (embedded EWM).

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP EWM has the ability to integrate with quality management in order to guarantee adherence to quality standards during the storage and handling of goods. Organizations can reap numerous benefits from quality management, including compliance with manufacturing quality regulations, reduced operating costs, and enhanced customer satisfaction. The integration between SAP EWM and quality management allows for quality inspections to be conducted at various stages of the warehouse process, such as during goods receipt , putaway , and outbound processes .

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The result of this integration is the assurance that quality standards are met prior to the dispatch of products to customers. SAP EWM can activate quality inspections and apprise quality management of the outcomes, thereby allowing quality management to create quality notifications or update inspection lots. The integration also facilitates the monitoring of quality-related data throughout the warehouse process, granting organizations visibility into quality-related key performance indicators (KPIs) and enabling data-driven decisions.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This chapter examines various aspects of quality management integration and di ff erent quality management business processes that can be integrated with SAP EWM. The introductory section provides a synopsis of quality management in SAP EWM, followed by an analysis of di ff erent quality management processes such as the inspection of material and batch during an inbound delivery in SAP. This process is further categorized into the inspection of material for externally procured and in-house inspection . Furthermore, this chapter delves into another quality management process, internal warehouse inspection, which is further divided into stock inspection and recurring inspection for batches.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 151 In essence, this chapter presents a comprehensive guide to the di ff erent quality management scenarios that can be implemented in SAP EWM. We’ll include the essential configuration steps, master data, and end-to-end process demonstrations for each scenario. By the end of this chapter, you will have a better understanding of how SAP EWM can be integrated with quality management, thereby enabling your company to streamline its quality management process. 3.1 Overview of Quality Management in SAP EWM In this section, we’ll present an overview of quality management in SAP EWM, including its architecture and deployment options.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll discuss the key terminology used with quality management, then dive into the strategy for maintaining inspection rules. SAP EWM employs a thorough quality management system that comprises diverse processes, procedures, and tools to guarantee the conformity of stored goods and materials with the appropriate quality standards and to ensure that warehouse operations meet the required standards. The main goal of quality management in SAP EWM is to ensure uniform product quality, minimize the risk of defects and errors, and enhance customer satisfaction.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The essential elements of quality management in SAP EWM encompass quality inspection, quality control, quality documentation, non- conformance management, and continuous improvement. SAP EWM’s quality management functionality guarantees products received and packaging meet your quality criteria. The Quality Inspection Engine is utilized to execute inspection processes in the warehouse. The Quality Inspection Engine can be employed to conduct quality inspections exclusively in SAP EWM or can be merged with the Quality Management (QM) component of SAP ERP if you have previously configured it.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For more intricate quality management procedures, the Quality Inspection Engine can be linked to an external quality management system , like QM in SAP ERP, that includes comprehensive analytical inspections and characteristics. Once an inspection document is initiated in SAP EWM, the Quality Inspection Engine prompts the creation of an inspection lot in the quality management function of the enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. The inspection procedure is then performed in the external system, which is the ERP quality management system.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Once the inspection process is completed, the ERP quality management transmits the usage decision back to the Quality Inspection Engine. This option is available for both SAP EWM connected to ERP or SAP S/4HANA systems, whether they are SAP S/4HANA or non-SAP S/4HANA (ERP). Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

In SAP EWM, quality management encompasses the utilization of several essential concepts to handle goods inspections and uphold quality. Let’s consider the following terms: Inspection object types An inspection object type refers to the software component, process, and object for which an inspection document can be created in the Quality Inspection Engine.

docs.text: Di ff erent types of inspection object types, including Preliminary Inspection of Inbound delivery (IOT1), Counting Inbound delivery (IOT2), Q-Inspection of Return delivery (IOT3), Q-Inspection Product/Batch Inbound delivery (IOT4), Q-Inspection of Product/ Batch Warehouse – Internal (IOT5), and Preliminary Inspection of Handling Unit (IOT6). docs.text: Inspection types Inspection types are used to define the controls associated with each inspection. The type of inspection determines how an inspection is carried out. In a decentralized system, the SAP EWM module in SAP S/4HANA is responsible for quality management using inspection rules. These rules are maintained as master data, and inspection documents are created in the SAP EWM system based on this data.

docs.text: 163 3.2 Inspection Product/Batch for Inbound Deliveries SAP EWM o ff ers various inspection processes for product/batch inbound delivery, such as the following: Inspection after goods receipt from external procurement (with inspection rule) In this process, individual products or batches are subject to inspection during the goods receipt process, controlled by inspection object type IOT4. Pre-sampling in production or inspection after goods receipt (SAP EWM 9.2 and higher) Pre-sampling is a process utilized for internally produced goods in SAP EWM.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Acceptance sampling (SAP EWM 9.2 and higher) Before posting a goods receipt for externally procured goods, a necessary step is to conduct a quality inspection. Acceptance sampling can be used to determine whether to allow or block a goods receipt and, if allowed, whether to impose restrictions until a usage decision is made. If a restricted goods receipt is allowed, the stock category for the goods receipt posting (e.g., blocked stock) can be defined through the configuration of the follow-up action. Additionally, acceptance sampling can be combined with inspection control after goods receipt.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, based on the acceptance sample result, a decision can be made to allow a restricted goods receipt into blocked stock, followed by a more detailed inspection after goods receipt. To combine acceptance sampling with inspection control after goods receipt, an inspection rule must be maintained for both acceptance sampling and inspections after goods receipt. We’ll discuss the first two options in more depth in the following sections. Because acceptance sampling is not commonly used, we won’t cover that topic further in this chapter.

Depending on the system configuration, the inspection document is generated either upon activation of the inbound delivery or when the inbound delivery status is set to In Yard .

In this section, we’ll walk through the business scenario, configuration, and master data setup needed for pre-sampling in production. We’ll then walk you step-by-step through a process demo.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Business Scenario Pre-sampling is a process utilized for internally produced goods. In SAP EWM, pre-sampling allows inspections to commence prior to the receipt of goods into the warehouse stock from production. This step permits the initiation of a result recording and usage decision at the earliest possible stage. The inspection document can be directly created by releasing the manufacturing order in SAP ERP. Moreover, you can complete a result recording and usage decision even before generating the inbound delivery in SAP EWM.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Alternatively, the inspection document can be created while activating the inbound delivery in SAP EWM, and the usage decision can be made before posting the goods receipt. Another choice is to generate the inspection document while activating the inbound delivery in SAP EWM and then making the usage decision before posting the goods receipt. The pre-sampling process after an inbound delivery is shown in Figure 3.46. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 192 3.3 Warehouse Stock Inspections Internal warehouse inspections involve the examination of inventory within a warehouse and is not directly tied to any inbound or outbound stock processes. The purpose of this inspection is to ensure that inventory levels are accurate, items are in good condition, and the warehouse is operating e ff iciently. This section will cover stock inspections with inspection rules as well as recurring inspections with inspection rules. Finally, we’ll look at customer return inspections using advanced returns. 3.3.1 Stock Inspections (With Inspection Rules) Stock inspection involves the examination of inventory either on a recurring basis (for batch-managed products) or on selected stock.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To create an internal inspection document for a warehouse, manual creation is required using either a radio frequency (RF) environment or through desktop transactions. In this section, we’ll walk through the business scenario, configuration, and master data setup needed for internal warehouse stock inspections. We’ll then walk through a process demo step-by-step. Business Scenario Internal warehouse inspection is the process of examining inventory within a warehouse to ensure that the items are in good condition, accurately tracked, and properly stored.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This inspection is not associated with any inbound or outbound processes related to stock. These inspections can be conducted on either selected stock or a recurring basis for batch-managed products. To create an internal warehouse inspection document, one must be manually created either an RF environment or desktop transactions. Conducting regular internal warehouse inspections is crucial for ensuring inventory accuracy and e ff icient warehouse operations. This task enables warehouse personnel to detect and address issues or discrepancies promptly, thus reducing inventory shrinkage, increasing productivity, and enhancing customer satisfaction. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

A recurring inspection is a type of warehouse-internal inspection that is not related to inbound or outbound processes, but rather to internal warehouse processes. Recurring inspections are essential for batch-managed products, but they can also be performed for any product that requires periodic inspection.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To carry out recurring inspections, inspection object type 5 (Q-Inspection Product/Batch Warehouse Internal) is used. In this section, we’ll walk through the business scenario, configuration, and master data setup needed for recurring internal stock inspections. Business Scenario As shown in Figure 3.72, the system can determine the date of next inspection for a batch-managed product via the Inspection Interval feature. To use this feature, you must first assign a class that includes the standard characteristic LOBM_QNDAT (next inspection date) to the batch. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 201 Figure 3.72 Recurring Inspection When a new batch is created, the system automatically assigns the next inspection date by following these conditions: If the manufacturing date is available for the batch, the system calculates the next inspection date by adding the inspection interval (which is maintained in the material/product master) to the manufacturing date. If the manufacturing date is NOT available for the batch, the system calculates the next inspection date by adding the inspection interval (which is maintained in the material/product master) to the batch creation date.

docs.text: 211 quality inspections, manually generating free-of-charge sales orders to send replacement material, and verifying the availability of that material via multiple transactions Additionally, creating credit memos for refunds and manually adjusting the price based on the quality inspection results were necessary. However, all of these manual tasks can be streamlined through advanced returns management, which is a powerful tool for all reverse logistics. Advanced returns management can capture almost all complex return processes with minimal e ff ort.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Business Scenario As shown in Figure 3.90, you can e ff ectively manage customer returns through the utilization of SAP ERP’s advanced returns management feature. This exceptional functionality seamlessly integrates with SAP EWM, so you can e ff iciently handle returned items at the granular level of storage bins. Figure 3.90 Customer Return Process in Advanced Returns Management This remarkable quality management component of SAP EWM means you can conduct meticulous inspections on returned items, thereby significantly enhancing the e ff iciency and transparency of the entire process.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To initiate the returns process, you can create either an advanced returns management returns order or a returns stock transport order. Consequently, you’re presented with two distinct options for conducting comprehensive quality inspections: Option 1: Performing the inspection prior to the goods being received in the SAP ERP system via advanced returns management Option 1 entails carrying out the inspection, making a decision, and performing subsequent logistical actions entirely within the SAP ERP system. If a follow-on document for a logistical action is generated in SAP ERP, the Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 212 external inspection ID is transmitted to SAP EWM alongside the delivery document. This crucial information is then stored with the corresponding stock item, facilitating the accurate determination of the stock item for the follow-on document, which is subsequently replicated from SAP ERP. Option 2: Performingthe inspection during the goods receipt process by leveraging the capabilities of SAP EWM or the Quality Inspection Engine With Option 2, the return items undergo a meticulous inspection within SAP EWM as soon as they arrive at the goods receipt area or designated work centers.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Simple logistical actions, such as putaway or scrapping, can be conveniently performed directly within SAP EWM. However, for more intricate follow-up actions, the responsibility can be seamlessly transferred to SAP ERP. The processing of follow-on documents created in SAP ERP is conclusively executed within SAP EWM, e ff ectively finalizing the comprehensive inspection process. Within this section, our primary focus will be on Option 2. This approach involves conducting the inspection during the goods receipt process by leveraging the robust capabilities of SAP EWM or the sophisticated functions of the Quality Inspection Engine.

docs.text: 228 4 Transportation Management SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) is an innovative software solution that empowers enterprises to strategically orchestrate the movement of goods and materials within their supply chains. This cutting- edge program a ff ords organizations invaluable real-time visibility into transportation operations, enabling them to adroitly optimize logistics processes, curtail costs, and bolster customer service. The program’s robust features facilitate the agile planning and booking of freight, the expeditious management of carriers, the seamless tracking and visibility of shipments, and intuitive analytics and reporting capabilities.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The objective of this chapter is to provide you with a complete guide to integrating SAP TM with SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM) through embedded Extended Warehouse Management in SAP S/4HANA (embedded EWM). To accomplish this goal, we’ll o ff er an exhaustive exposition of the business processes linked to each technique, followed by an elaborate examination of the configuration and master data prerequisites crucial to facilitate end- to-end testing of your business scenarios. Ultimately, we’ll provide step-by- step demonstrations of each process to further solidify your comprehension.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP EWM can be seamlessly integrated with SAP TM to optimize logistics operations and bolster supply chain visibility. This integration engenders a harmonized platform for end-to-end logistics management, thereby streamlining transportation planning and execution, while also facilitating e ff icient warehouse operations. By integrating SAP EWM with SAP TM, businesses can reap a multitude of advantages and benefits. These benefits include enhanced transportation planning and execution, real-time visibility into shipment and delivery status, improved inventory accuracy and control, and augmented productivity through automation and streamlined processes.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Additionally, the integration of SAP EWM and SAP TM culminates in a centralized data repository for logistics information, thereby enabling better decision- making and analysis. This chapter provides a thorough exploration of the most up-to-date business processes within SAP EWM and SAP TM. We cover advanced shipping and © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 229 receiving processes, as well as freight order integration between SAP EWM and SAP TM using Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) messaging. Additionally, this chapter examines various business scenarios, breaking them down into specific processes, required configurations, necessary master data, and end-to-end demonstrations for each. The introductory section provides an overview of transportation management systems and highlights how they can be advantageous for businesses in terms of facilitating growth.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We then focus on the diverse options available for shipping and receiving in both inbound and outbound processes. We delve into the option of integrating transportation management with extended warehouse management for inbound and outbound processes, triggered by LDAP messaging. Moreover, this chapter discusses SAP’s recently introduced advanced shipping and receiving functionality for inbound and outbound processes. The final section covers the integration of shipment and transportation planning processes in SAP ERP as well as in SAP EWM. 4.1 Overview of Transportation Management Systems A transportation management system is a software platform that the transportation industry employs to plan, execute, and optimize the movements of goods, including both inbound and outbound shipments.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A transportation management system ensures compliance with regulations and furnishes the necessary documentation. Managing transportation can be complex, expensive, and time consuming, and thus, a transportation management system is a crucial tool for streamlining supply chains. Transportation was once viewed as a distinct business process, but now it is integrated into overall supply chain and logistics management. A transportation management system frequently forms part of a larger supply chain management system.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To deal with the growing complexity and uncertainty of global logistics, businesses must improve logistics processes, enhance services, and increase visibility and control. A transportation management system provides a holistic perspective of daily transportation operations, encompassing trade compliance data, essential documentation, and the timely delivery of goods and freight. docs.text: 230 management system solutions streamline shipping processes, allowing an enterprise to oversee and enhance its transportation operations across various modes of transportation, such as land, air, and sea. Transportation management systems play a crucial role in modern supply chains, a ff ecting each stage of the process, from planning and procurement to logistics and lifecycle management. A strong transportation management system o ff ers comprehensive visibility, facilitating more e ff ective transportation planning and execution, leading to improved customer satisfaction and increased sales growth.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Given the continuously changing global trade environment, having a transportation management system that can assist businesses in successfully navigating complex trade policies and guaranteeing compliance with regulations is vital. Transportation management systems are primarily employed by businesses that require frequent shipping, moving, and receiving services, such as manufacturers, distributors, e-commerce companies, and retail businesses. Additionally, logistics service providers, including third-party logistics (3PL) and fourth-party logistics (4PL) firms, commonly use transportation management systems to provide logistics services to their clients.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The SAP TM application integrates fleet management and logistics management, streamlining the movement of goods across various modes of transportation. In this way, SAP TM enhances operational e ff iciency and reduces costs. This solution o ff ers a range of features, including transportation demand management, order consolidation, shipment monitoring and tracking, and transportation spend optimization. Additionally, it facilitates strategic freight procurement, capacity monitoring, freight order management, and transportation planning optimization.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Furthermore, SAP TM assists in the management of freight financials through freight settlement and provides analysis and reporting capabilities to make informed transportation decisions. Employing SAP TM, enterprises can implement a uniform transportation system that results in decreased transportation expenses and increased customer contentment. This software streamlines transportation planning, execution, and cost reconciliation, while also furnishing valuable data analytics to augment the overall transportation process.

docs.text: 231 Figure 4.1 SAP TM Deployment Options The following list describes these options in more detail: Internal system or embedded integration In this first scenario, referred to as internal system integration or embedded integration , SAP TM is directly integrated into the SAP S/4HANA system instance. In this approach, SAP TM can directly access logistics data within the SAP S/4HANA system, thus eliminating the need for data transfers between the systems. This approach eliminates the possibility of redundant data and reduces the e ff ort required for data transfer.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: External system or side-by-side integration In this second scenario, referred to as external system integration or side-by- side integration , SAP TM is implemented as a separate system . In this approach, master data and transactional data are transmitted from the SAP S/4HANA or SAP ERP system to SAP TM using various techniques for replicating master data. SAP TM, which is a component of SAP S/4HANA, can function as a standalone system in side-by-side scenarios in the following ways: SAP TM can be integrated with existing enterprise resource planning (ERP) instances that have not yet been converted to SAP S/4HANA, as part of the SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.text: 236 4.2 Shipping and Receiving in Inbound and Outbound Processes Shipping and receiving in inbound and outbound processes in SAP EWM are essential components of warehouse management systems. SAP EWM streamlines shipping and receiving processes, providing real-time visibility, e ff icient order processing, and enhanced inventory control. By automating and optimizing these processes, a business can improve in overall warehouse e ff iciency, can reduce errors, and can enhance customer satisfaction. SAP provides a range of business processes aimed at facilitating seamless integration between transportation management processes and warehouse management processes , with the ultimate goal of meeting customer requirements.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These processes are designed to ensure the smooth management of inbound and outbound shipments, as well as the e ff icient use of transportation units (TUs) and vehicles within a warehouse. The shipping and receiving aspects of EWM encompass the following key areas: Utilization of vehicles and TUs to manage goods transport to and from the warehouse Loading and unloading operations, including docking and undocking procedures at warehouse doors Yard management, which involves the organization and optimization of warehouse yard space Regarding inbound and outbound processes, shipping and receiving processes play a vital role in e ff iciently planning and executing warehouse activities.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: By leveraging these processes, your business can e ff ectively manage the flow of goods, handle incoming shipments, and ensure timely and accurate deliveries to customers or other destinations. The integration of shipping and receiving functionalities in both inbound and outbound operations enhances overall warehouse e ff iciency, inventory control, and customer satisfaction as well as enable the following capabilities: Integration of freight orders in SAP TM (processes based on freight order integration in SAP TM) © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 238 4.3 Freight Order Integration For inbound goods receipts as well as outbound goods issues, transportation planning is performed in SAP TM based on purchase orders, deliveries, sales orders, or customer return orders in SAP ERP. SAP TM sends planned freight order data directly to SAP EWM, which converts the information from the freight order into planned shipping and receiving activities in SAP EWM, namely, activities involving vehicles or TUs. You can perform all warehouse activities, such as loading or unloading, and perform goods receipts or goods issues for all deliveries. 4.3.1 Inbound Process In this section, we’ll go through the inbound goods receipt process using freight order integration in SAP TM.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll explore transportation planning based on purchase orders in the following sections. Business Process Figure 4.6 shows the step-by-step process for inbound goods receipt, which is performed in the following sequence: 1. Purchase orders are received by SAP TM from either SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, and their corresponding transportation requirements and freight units are generated. 2. Transportation planning is carried out based on transportation requirements, and freight orders are created in SAP TM. 3. If transportation planning is based on purchase orders, SAP TM generates deliveries in either SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. 4.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Inbound deliveries are then distributed by SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to SAP EWM, which automatically generates corresponding warehouse requests. 5. Freight order information is sent by SAP TM to SAP EWM, which automatically creates planned shipping and receiving activities for the assigned vehicle or TU. Inbound deliveries are also assigned to the created TU activities. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 239 6. The system automatically changes the status of the shipping and receiving activity from Planned to Active when a warehouse operator or checkpoint clerk executes the arrival at checkpoint action for the vehicle or TU. 7. An operator or goods receipt clerk then assigns a door to the vehicle or TU. If yard management is active, the vehicle or TU is moved from the yard to the assigned door; if not, the Arrival at Door action is executed for the vehicle or TU. 8. Warehouse activities, such as unloading goods, posting goods receipts, and putting away goods, are then carried out. 9.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If yard management is active, the vehicle or TU is moved from the door to the yard; if not, the Departure from Door action is executed for the vehicle or TU. 10. The operator executes the Departure from Checkpoint action for the vehicle or TUs, and SAP EWM automatically changes the status of the shipping and receiving activity from Active to Completed . This action triggers a notification to SAP TM about the executed shipping and receiving activities for the vehicle or TU, and the freight order is updated accordingly. 11.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The SAP TM freight order’s execution status is then set to Completed . 12. Freight settlement is carried out in SAP TM, and the freight settlement document serves as the basis for invoice verification and settlement in SAP ERP. docs.text: 252 Figure 4.30 Inbound Delivery Document Flow Status 4.3.2 Outbound Process Throughout this section, we’ll provide a comprehensive overview of the outbound goods issue process and the integration of freight orders in SAP TM. We’ll also delve into transportation planning based on sales orders in detail. Business Process As shown in Figure 4.31, the step-by-step process for outbound processes involves the following sequence: 1. A sales order is created in SAP SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. 2. SAP TM receives orders and deliveries from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA and utilizes the information to create transportation requirements and freight units. 3.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: After establishing the transportation requirements, SAP TM performs transportation planning and generates freight orders. 4. If the transportation planning is based on sales orders, SAP TM generates deliveries in the ERP system. These outbound deliveries are then forwarded to SAP EWM, which automatically generates the corresponding warehouse requests of the outbound delivery order type. 5. Based on the freight orders, SAP TM sends a loading appointment request message to SAP EWM, which creates a vehicle or TU along with planned shipping and receiving activities. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 253 6. The outbound delivery orders are assigned to TU activities. Warehouse activities, such as picking, packing, staging, and loading of goods, can be performed before the vehicle or TU arrives at the door. 7. When the vehicle or TU arrives, the Arrival at Checkpoint action is executed, and the system changes the status of the shipping and receiving activity from Planned to Active . A door is then assigned to the vehicle or TU, and if yard management is active, the vehicle or TU is moved from the yard to the assigned door. 8.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Once the warehouse activities are finished, the goods issue is posted, and transportation documents are printed. The delivery information is transferred to SAP ERP, where the deliveries are automatically updated with execution data. The information is also sent to SAP TM to update the consumed transportation requirements. 9. If yard management is active, the vehicle or TU is moved from the door to the yard, and if not, the Departure from Door action is executed. When the Departure from Checkpoint action is executed, SAP EWM automatically changes the status of the shipping and receiving activity from Active to Completed . 10.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A loading appointment notification message is then transmitted to SAP TM, where the freight orders are updated with execution data. The execution status of the SAP TM freight order is set to Completed , and freight settlement is conducted in SAP TM. The freight settlement document in SAP TM serves as the foundation for invoice verification and settlement in the ERP system. Figure 4.31 Freight Order Integration in SAP TM and SAP EWM: Outbound Process Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 263 4.4 Advanced Shipping and Receiving Advanced shipping and receiving empowers individuals to e ff iciently send, receive, and transport goods through a comprehensive and seamless procedure. It streamlines the process from the moment a truck arrives at the gate to the ultimate receipt of goods in the warehouse by enabling mixed and multi- warehouse scenarios to be managed within a single freight order. This system allows a truck that has registered its arrival at a checkpoint to perform loading and unloading operations at a single location or to distribute goods to multiple warehouses at the same site.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To create transportation requirements, both materials management and sales and distribution must be in place, and information exchange among various SAP S/4HANA application components, such as SAP TM, SAP EWM, stock room management, inventory management and physical inventory, and logistics execution is streamlined through the utilization of a unified data model. The application of the EDIFACT standard to electronic data interchange (EDI) messages and the provision of specialized applications further simplify the exchange of information.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Additionally, existing apps and RF transactions for shipping and receiving processes are expanded to facilitate communication, allowing users to track the status of products throughout the shipping and receiving processes and gain valuable insights. The advanced shipping and receiving process is based on the freight order and does not utilize either the TUs or vehicles in SAP EWM. 4.4.1 Inbound Process In this section, we’ll delve into to an inbound goods receipt process using advanced shipping and receiving in SAP TM and SAP EWM.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Business Process As shown in Figure 4.51, the inbound goods receipt process involves the following steps: 1. SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA generates a purchase order. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 264 2. The embedded SAP TM funtionality creates a freight unit according to the freight unit building rule. 3. The freight order is created in embedded SAP TM using the previously created freight unit. 4. The inbound delivery is generated in SAP S/4HANA as a result of the delivery suggestion from the freight order in embedded SAP TM. 5. Once the inbound delivery is dispatched from SAP S/4HANA, it is created in embedded SAP EWM. The advanced shipping and receiving capability’s new freight order application is used to mark this inbound delivery as Ready for Warehouse Processing , and the corresponding warehouse operations (such as goods receipt, putaway, etc.) are carried out within this embedded SAP EWM instance. 6.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 276 Business Process As shown in Figure 4.76, the outbound delivery process with advanced shipping notifications (ASNs) involves the following steps: 1. To initiate the outbound process in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, a sales document such as a sales order or scheduling agreement is generated. This triggers the creation of freight Units for order-based planning, which are then replicated to Transportation Management. 2. In SAP TM, freight orders are created for the freight units and outbound deliveries are generated. These outbound deliveries are replicated to SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA as well as to SAP EWM. 3.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The pick, pack, and stage processes for the outbound delivery order are executed in the embedded EWM system. 4. Once the freight order is marked as Ready for Transportation Execution and the outbound delivery orders are marked as Ready for Shipping , the loading process can be initiated in SAP EWM via the Load or Unload Freight Orders app or an RF device. 5. Using the Load or Unload Freight Orders app in SAP Fiori, door assignment, loading, loading completion, and goods movements can be posted on the outbound delivery order.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The goods movement can be posted either in SAP TM or SAP EWM. docs.text: 290 4.5 Shipment Integration To transport multiple outbound delivery documents using the same means of transportation, SAP ERP utilizes shipment documents as a foundation for planning the logistics. The system converts handling units (HUs) within SAP ERP shipments into vehicles, TUs, or both, and schedules shipping and receiving activities in SAP EWM. Following the completion of the warehouse operations, transport details are transmitted back to SAP ERP to facilitate freight cost settlement and invoicing. 4.5.1 Transportation Planning in an ERP System In this section, we’ll explore the outbound transportation planning process in your ERP system followed by the execution of warehouse activities in SAP EWM.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Business Process As shown in Figure 4.103, the outbound process involves the following steps: 1. In SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, an outbound delivery (with reference to a sales order) is created. SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA automatically distributes outbound deliveries to SAP EWM, where warehouse requests for outbound deliveries are generated. 2. To create a shipment with HUs and assign outbound deliveries, you can use SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. The shipment details are then sent to SAP EWM, where a vehicle or TU and a planned shipping and receiving activity are automatically created, and the outbound delivery order is assigned to the TU activity. 3.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Warehouse activities related to outbound delivery orders, such as picking, packing, staging, and loading the goods, are carried out in SAP EWM. 4. To activate the shipping and receiving activity from Planned to Active , you need to execute the Arrival at Checkpoint action for the vehicle or TU. Then, you can assign a door to the vehicle or TU. 5. If yard management is enabled, the vehicle or TU is moved from the yard to the assigned door. However, if yard management is not activated, the © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 291 Arrival at Door action for the vehicle or TU is executed. 6. When the goods issue posting takes place in SAP EWM, the transport details are transferred to SAP ERP, where a shipment is automatically updated with the execution data. 7. If yard management is enabled, the vehicle or TU is moved from the door to the yard. Conversely, if yard management is not activated, the Departure from Door action for the vehicle or TU is executed. Figure 4.103 Transportation Planning in an ERP System Configuration In this section, we’ll review the key customization steps required for the process.

docs.text: 319 5 Dock Appointment Scheduling Dock appointment scheduling is a proactive and anticipatory planning technique employed by companies to manage shipping docks, warehouses, and distribution centers. This method entails the allocation of designated time slots for the arrival and departure of trucks transporting inbound and outbound shipments. Moreover, the optimization of schedules for dock doors and yard operations is an integral aspect of dock scheduling. The objective of this chapter is to serve as a comprehensive manual on diverse dock management procedures and their seamless assimilation with SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM) through embedded Extended Warehouse Management in SAP S/4HANA (embedded EWM).

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll walk through the business processes for each technique, discuss the setup and primary data requirements needed to enable end-to-end testing of business scenarios, and provide a complete step-by-step process demonstration for each scenario. The integration of SAP with SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling presents a synergistic opportunity for warehouse and distribution centers to streamline and optimize their goods flow. The process entails configuring and linking the dock appointment scheduling system with SAP EWM’s inbound and outbound delivery procedures.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: At the outset, the SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling system meticulously schedules precise time slots for the arrival and departure of trucks that ferry inbound and outbound shipments. Subsequently, this scheduling information is conveyed to SAP EWM, which then triggers the generation of inbound or outbound deliveries based on the designated time slots. Following the creation of the inbound or outbound delivery in SAP EWM, the system automatically assigns a specific dock door for the truck to utilize, based on the schedule information retrieved from SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This approach ensures the accurate routing of trucks to designated dock doors, thereby optimizing the flow of goods. In sum, the integration of SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling with SAP EWM enables warehouse and distribution center operators Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 320 to enhance operations, diminish congestion and waiting periods, and heighten e ff iciency and throughput. This chapter scrutinizes the many facets of dock processes and the diverse business processes for dock appointment scheduling that can be integrated with SAP EWM. The preliminary section furnishes a comprehensive overview of dock appointment scheduling in SAP EWM, the manifold options available for the implementation of dock appointment management, and the divergent concepts employed in the dock appointment scheduling process.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Additionally, this chapter delves into various dock appointment planning options that encompass dock appointment planning in both the SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling and SAP EWM systems. Essentially, this chapter o ff ers a comprehensive manual on the various dock appointment scheduling scenarios that can be executed in SAP EWM. We cover the requisite configuration steps, master data, and end-to-end process demonstrations for each scenario, so your business can optimize its supply chain operations and augment productivity.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: By the end of this chapter, you’ll possess a deep comprehension of how SAP EWM can be integrated with SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling to empower your enterprise to streamline its dock appointment processes. 5.1 Overview of Dock Appointment Scheduling The process of dock scheduling is a valuable tool for businesses looking to optimize their use of resources and improve e ff iciency in their supply chain operations. By reducing wait times for truck drivers during the loading and unloading of goods, your business can minimize overcrowding and congestion, particularly on traditionally busy days like Mondays and Fridays.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A delay in the dock scheduling process can lead to increased detention charges and negatively impact the operational margins of a warehouse. On the other hand, an accurate dock scheduling system can revolutionize warehouse dock operations and drastically improve tra ff ic flow, leading to more e ff icient and cost-e ff ective supply chain management During loading and unloading operations at docks, delays can occur, which can put pressure on warehouse operators to work quickly to meet manufacturing or distribution schedules.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 321 By scheduling appointments in advance, warehouses can e ff ectively plan and manage their sta ff for receiving and shipping processes, as well as allocate their equipment resources e ff iciently. This feature helps minimize delays and idle time for trucks waiting to be loaded or unloaded. Providing carriers with a link to your warehouse’s dock appointment system can reduce the need for phone- based or email bookings, resulting in shorter wait times and faster responses for carriers. Dock appointment scheduling systems are often integrated into warehouse or transportation management software, o ff ering a range of helpful features.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These features may include online booking portals, automated appointment confirmations, and real-time visibility into dock availability and tra ff ic conditions. These capabilities allow for smoother, more streamlined operations, reducing wait times and improving overall e ff iciency in the supply chain. E ff icient planning of vehicle arrivals and departures for unloading and loading goods is crucial to ensure a well-organized running of the warehouse and to balance the workload throughout the working day. Scheduling dock appointments in advance can help prevent appointment blowouts during the week and reduce the tra ff ic on busy days at the warehouse.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The ultimate goal is to ensure the e ff icient use of warehouse doors, parking spaces, and yard checkpoints for loading and unloading trucks from various carriers while avoiding interruptions in warehouse operations. Allowing carriers to schedule their own appointments online helps them plan their routes e ff ectively and eliminates the need to arrive early to ensure they can pick up or deliver in a timely manner. The e ff icient scheduling of dock appointments can be instrumental in optimizing sta ff ing levels and averting scenarios of understa ff ing or oversta ff ing.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This optimization, in turn, can result in enhanced labor planning, a pivotal component of warehouse operations. A dock scheduling system serves as a valuable tool for capacity and resource planning, allowing for seamless communication between carriers and the system, while simultaneously providing real-time visibility to customers, warehouse personnel, suppliers, and carriers. By means of dock appointment scheduling, carriers and warehouse users can coordinate appointments for incoming vehicles or transportation units (TUs) during loading and unloading processes.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The scheduling process can be executed online, meaning vendors and carriers can book appointments and track progress in real-time using software. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 322 Additionally, dock appointment scheduling software can be seamlessly integrated with warehouse management systems (WMS) or transportation management systems. Streamlined dock appointment scheduling can result in optimized hours of service, enhanced warehouse e ff iciency, improved partner collaboration, and augmented inventory turns. A dock scheduling system may also include reporting functionalities, such as audits on delivered loads, which can facilitate the automatic recording and transmission of compliance information.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP provides a web browser-based application called SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling . This application enables e ff icient planning of vehicle arrivals in warehouses and allows carriers to enroll their TUs for the yard, book time slots for loading and unloading, and view the workload at each loading point for each day. SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling can be deployed as a standalone solution or integrated with a local SAP EWM system. To use SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling functionalities, SAP has provided the standard Transaction NWBC or several SAP Fiori applications, as shown in Figure 5.1.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Additionally, an SAP Fiori app called the Dock Appointment Scheduling for Carriers app is available in SAP S/4HANA to o ff er a user interface (UI) for carriers. When integrating SAP EWM and SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling, the scheduling appointment serves as the planning object for the transport. Planning is performed using time slots for loading points and defined capacities, with carriers collaborating via web access. In extended warehouse management (EWM), the TU is the processing object for the transport. docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 323 activities in SAP EWM. This integration facilitates the exchange of loading appointment status updates and related TU activity information between SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling and SAP EWM. Additionally, the shipping cockpit in SAP EWM can be used to track outbound loading appointments created in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling. Overall, the integration of SAP EWM and SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling provides several benefits for both inbound and outbound processes. The requirements for integrating SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling include the following: 1.
