docs.text: You have enabled the business function SCM_EWM_FND (EWM, Essential Foundation Functions). 2. You have configured the Basis customization setting for SAP EWM. 3. Within SAP EWM, you have established configurations for means of transport. Additionally, you have created a connection between packaging materials and TUs via the SAP Easy Access menu transaction. 4. Within SAP EWM, you have defined a number range for the TU. Note that the number range for TU numbers must not be the same as the number range for the loading appointment numbers. 5.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You have defined a number range for vehicles in SAP EWM, if applicable. 6. You have defined a number range for shipping and receiving activities in SAP EWM. 7. You have defined a number range for appointment numbers under the customization path in SAP EWM. Some crucial concepts utilized in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling include the following: Docking locations A docking location refers to a collection of loading points, such as a warehouse or distribution center, and represents the physical location of these loading points.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This element allows for the definition of attributes that are uniform across the entire location, such as an address. If you’re using SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling in conjunction with SAP EWM, a docking location represents an SAP EWM warehouse in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling. You can specify if the loading points are integrated with SAP EWM within the docking location. Imperative is that the integration Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 324 with SAP EWM be consistent for all the loading points in a docking location, as well as the docking location itself. Docking locations can be established by a user with role /SCWM/DAS_ADMINISTRATOR . Loading points Loading appointments for vehicles are organized based on loading points. A loading point represents a group of warehouse docks that share the same processing characteristics, such as loading or unloading. In practice, these “docks” could be fuel dispensers, loading docks, or any location where goods are received or dispatched from a warehouse.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can combine the loading points of a particular geographical location into a docking location. When using docking locations, a crucial requirement is that the integration with SAP EWM is consistent for all the loading points belonging to a docking location as well as for the docking location itself. However, if docking locations are not used, you can specify whether a loading point is integrated with SAP EWM for each loading point individually. Loading appointments are scheduled at the loading point level, which is a collection of warehouse docks with similar attributes.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Each loading point is allocated a defined time slot duration and a range of appointment numbers. Loading points can be established by a user with the role /SCWM/DAS_ADMINISTRATOR . Time slots To plan the times for loading appointments, time slots are used. The duration of each time slot is defined within the loading point and is fixed across all time slots. When creating loading points and assigning them to a docking location, the time slot duration can be specified in the docking location. The system will automatically use this duration for new loading points.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When modifying a time slot duration is necessary, such as when using a greater number of time slots with shorter durations to enhance planning, you can change this duration individually in each loading point. This modification has no impact on previously generated time slots and their loading appointments and only applies to new time slots generated for upcoming time frames. A user with the role /SCWM/DAS_ADMINISTRATOR can create time slots. Time slot management This function allows you to create time slots for a loading point and adjust its capacity.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 325 master data. Each time slot has a capacity, which indicates the maximum number of vehicles that can be loaded or unloaded simultaneously during that time slot. To create time slots, you would define the working time of the loading point by specifying the start date of the first time slot and specify the capacity for each time slot according to the circumstances at that time. In this way, you can adjust the capacity for each time slot by taking into account factors such as sta ff availability. If you’re using the graphical view, you can set the capacity for time slots for one day and then copy these values forward to the next day.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Once you’ve created the time slot capacity for the week, you can carry these values forward for the next several weeks. The system automatically sets the capacity to 0 for days when the loading point is not available, such as public holidays, based on the factory calendar assigned to the loading point. You can also change the capacity of time slots for a loading point or delete all future time slots for a loading appointment after a certain date. If you need to delete time slots in the future that already have loading appointments associated with them, you must cancel the loading appointments.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If you want to delete a loading point, you must delete all the time slots and appointments associated with it. Appointment management This function enables you to create and edit loading appointments for loading points. You can use loading appointments to plan vehicle arrivals at your warehouse and to balance the workload across the working day. You can assign more than one time slot to a loading appointment. In this way, you can plan flexibly for loading appointments that require di ff erent amounts of time for loading or unloading.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, in a loading point with a time slot duration of 15 minutes, you can create one loading appointment that lasts for 30 minutes, perhaps to unload a small delivery, and then create another loading appointment that lasts for 90 minutes, perhaps to unload a larger delivery with more handling units (HUs). Appointments of variable duration You can create loading appointments of di ff erent durations by assigning more than one time slot to a loading appointment. The shortest loading appointment possible is one time slot.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 326 consist of consecutive time slots. If you need to create a loading appointment that includes some time when no workers are available at the loading point, you must include this time in the duration of the appointment. Provisional appointments When working with docking locations, you can create loading appointments for a docking location without specifying a loading appointment, without specifying time slots, or both. These loading appointments have the status Provisional . Provisional appointments do not fill any capacity in a loading point, and you cannot process provisional appointments without further planning.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When you enter a loading point and time slots into a provisional appointment, the loading appointment status changes to Planned , and it fills capacity at the loading point. You can then proceed with the loading appointment. Managing loading appointments You can change loading appointments, when the expected vehicle has not yet arrived at its checkpoint, to di ff erent time slots in the loading point. However, appointment planners for carriers can change the time slots of their loading appointments only if the restricted planning period has not begun.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As long as both loading points are in the same docking location, you can change a loading appointment to a di ff erent loading point if the vehicle has not yet arrived at the warehouse. If you’re using docking locations, the new loading point must have the same docking location as the original loading point. You can cancel loading appointments if the vehicle has not yet arrived at the checkpoint. Indicating loading appointment direction You can specify whether a loading appointment is an inbound appointment or an outbound appointment, if required.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Creating loading appointments for time slots without free capacity You can create loading appointments for a time slot at your loading point even if there is no free capacity for the slot. However, appointment planners for carriers can create loading appointments for time slots with free capacity only. Indicating that a loading appointment has arrived at the dock If you’re using SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling without integration with SAP EWM, you can indicate that a vehicle has arrived at the dock without © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 327 first indicating that the vehicle has arrived at the checkpoint. You can also indicate that a vehicle has departed from the checkpoint without first indicating that the vehicle has departed from the dock. Changing the date and time after the action is performed SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling saves a record of the time when you update the status of each loading appointment. You can change the date and time related to actions for the loading appointment after the actions are performed. For example, if you set the status of a loading appointment to Departed from Checkpoint later than when the vehicle actually left, you can enter the actual time of departure in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can then store these actual times for later analysis. Appointments can be created by a user with the role DAS_EXT_CARR_PLANNER . docs.text: 329 5.2 Dock Appointment Planning This section delves into a few scenarios with dock appointment planning: one scenario where the TU is created without yard management (which we’ll focus on in Section 5.2.1) and another scenario using yard management, where the TU is created in SAP EWM first (which we’ll cover in Section 5.2.2). 5.2.1 Inbound Process in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling Let’s take a deeper look into the inbound goods receipt business process, specifically the scenario where a TU is created without yard management, based on dock appointment planning.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this business process, the dock appointment serves as a planning object and is first planned in the SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling module. The next step is the creation of a TU in SAP EWM. Business Process As shown in Figure 5.4, the business process for dock appointment planning without yard management involves the following steps: After receiving information about a delivery and its scheduled date, the carrier’s appointment planner logs on to SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling. Via the web-based application, this user creates an appointment for the delivery date.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The appointment planner enters the warehouse’s docking location and the purchase order as a reference document. The system automatically calculates the loading point, appointment duration, and the number of required time slots based on the purchase order data. The carrier then selects a suitable start time slot. At least 1 day prior to the delivery date, the warehouse clerk reviews the scheduled appointments for the next day. This user ensures that enough capacity at the loading point is available to accommodate the planned 1 2 3 Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 330 trucks for unloading. If necessary, the warehouse clerk reschedules the appointment or increases the available workforce in the warehouse. Upon the truck’s arrival, the driver provides the appointment number to the checkpoint clerk. The checkpoint clerk then searches for the appointment in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling using the appointment number and changes the status to Arrived at Checkpoint . Subsequently, the checkpoint clerk finds an available door in SAP EWM, creates a planned door activity, and guides the truck to the designated door.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The truck driver takes the delivery note to the goods receipt department, where a goods receipt o ff ice clerk locates the corresponding inbound delivery in SAP EWM. A warehouse worker confirms the truck’s arrival at the door and begins unloading the truck. A warehouse clerk cross-checks the goods with the delivery note and brings the revised delivery note to the goods receipt o ff ice. The goods receipt o ff ice clerk records the goods receipt, and the system automatically generates and prints warehouse orders for the inbound delivery.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These warehouse orders facilitate the movement of goods into the warehouse. Subsequently, the truck leaves the door, and a warehouse clerk updates the status to Departed from Door . Figure 5.4 Dock Appointment Planning Creates TU without Yard Management The truck proceeds to the checkpoint, and the checkpoint clerk searches for the appointment in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling using the 4 5 6 © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 331 appointment number and then updates the status to Departed from Checkpoint . The warehouse worker transfers the goods from the goods receipt area to their respective storage types within the warehouse. Towards the end of the week or the month, the warehouse clerk selects all the appointments from the previous week or month in the Analyze Appointments screen to analyze the waiting and processing times as well as the disparities between planned and actual times. The warehouse clerk determines the number of trucks that arrived on time and whether the processing time aligns with the planned times.

docs.text: Business Process As shown in Figure 5.27, the business process for inbound deliveries using SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling with yard management involves the following steps: 1. The process begins with the creation of an inbound delivery document (with reference to a purchase order) in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. The inbound delivery is replicated to SAP EWM. A warehouse operator generates a TU in SAP EWM and associates the inbound delivery with it. These elements form the planned appointment in SAP EWM as well in SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling.

The TU is unloaded and is directed to a checkpoint for release by a checkpoint clerk. 5.

docs.text: 361 6 Warehouse Automation Systems A warehouse automation system encompasses a meticulously coordinated amalgamation of components that, through synergy, optimize e ff iciency, precision, and productivity within the warehouse. Ranging from automated storage and retrieval systems and robotic picking systems to conveyors, sortation systems, warehouse management system (WMS) software, and automated guided vehicles (AGVs), these components spearhead progress in the industry, empowering businesses to meet the ever-mounting demands of the contemporary world.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This chapter delves into an array of warehouse automation components that can be seamlessly integrated with SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM). Moreover, we provide an extensive exploration of diverse automation system components, including material flow systems, warehouse robotics systems, automated storage and retrieval systems, and AGVs. The integration of SAP EWM with warehouse automation systems aims to create a seamless and tightly synchronized environment where manual and automated processes work in harmony.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This integration enables businesses to leverage the benefits of automation technology while maintaining control and visibility over warehouse operations through a unified system. The integration of SAP EWM enables seamless data exchange, e ff icient process coordination, optimized resource utilization, and enhanced traceability. By leveraging the power of automation alongside a robust WMS like SAP EWM, organizations can achieve greater operational excellence and stay competitive in the fast-paced world of modern warehousing.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This chapter commences by providing an overview of warehouse automation systems. We discuss detailed information about the di ff erent warehouse automation systems that are being utilized in state-of-the-art warehouses, as well as their integration with WMSs. Furthermore, we delve into the intricacies of the material flow system and its application in both inbound and outbound processes. This chapter covers essential aspects such as business processes, configuration requirements, and Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 362 master data and concludes with a practical demonstration of the material flow process. Moreover, this chapter explores ongoing warehouse robotics solutions and presents various deployment options for integrating these solutions into warehouse operations. Finally, the chapter delves into a few warehouse automation components, namely, automated storage and retrieval systems and AGVs. We’ll provide comprehensive information about these components, including their functionalities and benefits within a warehouse setting. 6.1 Overview of Warehouse Automation Systems In today’s fast-paced world of logistics, the demand for e ff icient and productive warehouse operations has never been greater.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Thankfully, the advent of warehouse automation systems has brought about a transformative change in the industry. By integrating cutting-edge technology and advanced robotics, these systems have streamlined processes, minimized errors, and significantly increased operational e ff iciency. A warehouse automation system involves the implementation of di ff erent software and technologies to automate and streamline the various processes associated with managing and operating a warehouse. These technologies can include AGV systems, material flow systems, WMSs, conveyor systems, robotics systems, and automated storage and retrieval systems.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Numerous businesses across various industries are using warehouse automation to optimize their supply chain management and improve overall productivity. The aim of warehouse automation is to enhance the e ff iciency, precision, and swiftness of warehouse tasks , while simultaneously minimizing costs and errors. By automating inventory management, order processing, and material handling activities, warehouse automation facilitates organizations to enhance their supply chain management and overall productivity. At the heart of a warehouse automation system are several key components working in harmony to optimize every aspect of the supply chain.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: First and foremost, automated storage and retrieval systems play a vital role. These systems utilize computer-controlled mechanisms to handle the storage and retrieval of goods, eliminating the need for manual intervention and maximizing space utilization. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 363 Next, robotic picking systems have emerged as game-changers. Equipped with sensors and advanced algorithms, these robots navigate through the warehouse, accurately identifying and picking items for order fulfillment. By eliminating human error and drastically reducing picking time, these systems have revolutionized the e-commerce sector. Conveyors and sortation systems are another integral part of warehouse automation. These systems transport goods seamlessly throughout the warehouse, ensuring timely and e ff icient movement from one area to another.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: They enable continuous flow and facilitate the sorting and routing of items based on predefined criteria, optimizing order processing. To manage and orchestrate these complex operations, WMSs provide the necessary intelligence. WMS software integrates with various components of the automation system, overseeing inventory control, order processing, and real- time tracking. This centralized control ensures smooth coordination and enhances visibility across the supply chain. Finally, to ensure a safe and secure working environment, AGVs have gained prominence.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These autonomous vehicles navigate through the warehouse, transporting goods, and even interacting with other automation components. With built-in safety measures and e ff icient route planning, AGVs contribute to reducing accidents and improving operational e ff iciency. Businesses can utilize various types of automation systems to streamline their warehouse operations, which include the following: Conveyor systems These automated systems transport goods from one location to another within a warehouse. Automated storage and retrieval systems These systems utilize computer-controlled cranes to retrieve and store products in high-density storage systems.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Robotics systems These systems employ robots for tasks like palletizing, depalletizing, and order picking. AGVs These unmanned vehicles transport products through the picking process, enhancing accuracy and speed. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

In general, these automation systems can improve e ff iciency, increase productivity, reduce errors, and lower labor costs for businesses. Starting with SAP EWM 5.1, an integration option for automated warehouses has been available. This integration allowed for the connection of programmable logic controllers (PLCs) to various systems such as conveyor belts, rack feeders, lifts, and more through SAP EWM.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: One key aspect of integrating SAP EWM with warehouse automation systems is the exchange of real-time data and information. Automated systems such as conveyor belts, sorters, robots, and automated storage and retrieval systems are equipped with sensors and other technologies that capture data on inventory movements, order statuses, and equipment performance. This data is seamlessly shared with SAP EWM, providing accurate and up-to-date information for decision-making and process optimization. By integrating with warehouse automation systems, SAP EWM can e ff ectively manage and orchestrate various automated processes.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, it can control and monitor the movement of AGVs within a warehouse, ensuring e ff icient material flow and picking processes. It can also coordinate with robotic © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 365 systems for tasks such as picking, packing, and palletizing, improving order fulfillment speed and accuracy. Furthermore, integration with warehouse automation systems allows SAP EWM to optimize resource utilization and warehouse layout. The system can analyze real-time data from automated equipment, such as storage capacity, equipment availability, and congestion points, to make intelligent decisions on task assignment, equipment allocation, and routing. This optimization minimizes unnecessary movements, reduces idle time, and maximizes the use of available resources, leading to improved throughput and operational e ff iciency.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Another significant benefit of integrating SAP EWM with warehouse automation systems is enhanced traceability and visibility. Automated systems generate a wealth of data regarding inventory movements, picking and packing processes, and quality control. By integrating this data with SAP EWM, businesses can have a comprehensive view of their warehouse operations in real-time. They can track the progress of orders, identify bottlenecks, and proactively address any issues that may arise. Furthermore, SAP EWM can be integrated with various other warehouse automation systems, including the following: Material flow systems SAP Warehouse Robotics for robotic integration Automated storage and retrieval systems AGVs Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 366 6.2 Material Flow Systems A material flow system, as shown in Figure 6.1, allows for the connection of an automatic warehouse to SAP EWM without requiring an additional warehouse control unit. The material flow system can be configured to divide warehouse tasks from a source location to a destination location into smaller subtasks. These subtasks are then transmitted step-by-step to a PLC, which is a real-time system responsible for controlling the physical transportation of handling units (HUs) and their components on the conveyor system.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 6.1 Overview of Material Flow Systems The communication between the material flow system and PLCs is facilitated through telegram communication . With this setup, the putaway and removal from storage of HUs can be accomplished without the need for additional software systems. Business warehouses can define the capacity limits for communication points , conveyor segments , or resources , and as a result, the SAP EWM system holds back tasks for the PLC as soon as these limits are being approached. A material flow system provides the following features: Identification of HUs is automatic through scanners in the automatic storage retrieval facility.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 367 Fully automatic putaway of HUs in the storage bin is possible using any number of interim steps. These interim steps are represented by communication points. Malfunctions reported by the controls are taken into account. Capacity limits for communication points, conveyor segments, and vehicles are taken into account. Task interleaving is used to reduce empty traveling paths for stacker cranes. Goods-to-person picking is available. Stock is available for deliveries during transportation within the system. Parallel, bidirectional communication channels ensure stable telegram communications between SAP EWM and PLCs.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the following sections, we’ll discuss both inbound and outbound processes of the material flow system. 6.2.1 Inbound Process In this section, we’ll explore inbound processes using the material flow system in detail. The inbound process flow with a material flow system involves the movement of materials into a warehouse. The material flow system is a module within the SAP EWM solution for managing and optimizing material flows within a warehouse. Business Process As shown in Figure 6.2, an inbound process flow with the material flow system involves the following steps: 1.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The inbound goods receipt process begins with creation of an inbound delivery with reference to a purchase order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. 2. As the truck physically arrives at the warehouse, the material is physically unloaded, and the warehouse operations team performs a goods receipt in the SAP EWM system. The goods receipt document records the actual receipt of the material in system and updates the inventory in SAP EWM as well as SAP ERP system. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 368 3. Posting a goods receipt in SAP EWM creates a warehouse task automatically, based on the postprocessing framework (PPF) configuration. The pallet HU is physically loaded at the scanner area, which is mapped to communication point. Pallet movement from the unloading area to the scanner area or communication point will vary depending on the business process. 4. Once the pallet HU is scanned for a weight and dimension check, communication between the PLC/conveyor system and SAP EWM start. The PLC communicates to SAP EWM about the current source location.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP EWM confirms the message is received and communicates back to the PLC regarding the next destination location. 5. The pallet HU is moved from one communication point to another with reference to the creation and communication of the warehouse task between PLC and SAP EWM. 6. With the help of a crane, the pallet HU is finally putaway in an aisle bin, and the warehouse putaway process is complete. Throughout the inbound process flow, a material flow system provides real-time visibility and control over material movements, ensuring e ff icient and accurate handling of incoming goods within a warehouse.

docs.text: 392 Note The inbound goods receipt process using SAP EWM, a material flow system, and SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA is now complete. 6.2.2 Outbound Process In this section, we’ll go through the outbound process using the material flow system in detail . Business Process The outbound process flow with a material flow system, shown in Figure 6.52, typically involves the movement of goods from the warehouse to a production area or a shipping area. The material flow system is a component of SAP EWM for managing and optimizing material flows within a warehouse.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: An outbound process flow with a material flow system generally involves the following steps: 1. The outbound goods issue process begins with the creation of an outbound delivery with reference to a sales order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. 2. This outbound delivery is automatically replicated to SAP EWM, and the SAP EWM system creates a wave with reference to the outbound delivery order. Upon release of the wave, the pick warehouse task is getting to move the material from the aisle bin to the outbound staging area. 3.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: With the SAP EWM-PLC interface, the SAP EWM system communicates to the crane PLC to pick the pallet HU from the source aisle bin and move to the next communication point. 4. The crane picks the pallet HU and physically moves to the next communication point and communicates back to SAP EWM about the HU move. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 393 Figure 6.52 Outbound Process with the Material Flow System 5. The SAP EWM system acknowledges the message and communicates the next destination location to the crane or conveyor PLC. 6. With the communication between SAP EWM and PLCs, and with reference to the creation and confirmation of warehouse tasks, the pallet HU finally moves to the outbound shipping area. 7. As the truck arrives, the loading of pallet the HU is performed, and the warehouse operation team performs the post goods issue for the outbound delivery order.

docs.text: 405 6.3 SAP Warehouse Robotics SAP Warehouse Robotics simplifies the integration of robots, making their use as easy as plug-and-play . Although a new class of human-safe, collaborative robots is available from hundreds of low-cost vendors, challenges still exist related to software stack and system integration . SAP Warehouse Robotics helps users of SAP EWM to swiftly integrate nearly any warehouse robot, requiring only hours or days instead of weeks or months. The solution can be easily scaled as needed and enables the operation of diverse fleets using the same software stack.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: By integrating the latest generation of collaborative robots with SAP EWM, warehouse automation becomes a ff ordable and e ff ortless. SAP Warehouse Robotics has made agile robotics more accessible by o ff ering the following features: Simple setup and scalability, with the ability to quickly add additional robots as needed to handle peak demand. Freedom from vendor lock-in, thanks to compatibility with a wide range of transportation robots commonly used in warehouses. This flexibility eliminates the need for expensive integration projects.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: E ff ortless management of diverse fleets, without the need for additional integration e ff orts. SAP Warehouse Robotics can be operated with out-of-the-box scenarios for SAP EWM. This resource provides simplified security and IT governance, lower costs, and easier entry into the world of warehouse robotics. Additionally, SAP Warehouse Robotics facilitates easy robot integration and allows for the addition of new ad-hoc robots. It also enables the management of heterogeneous fleets in one solution, where di ff erent robots can perform di ff erent tasks.

docs.text: SAP Warehouse Robotics allows warehouses to automate operations using robots. docs.text: 408 6.4 Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems An automated storage and retrieval system is a technology-driven solution designed to streamline inventory management in manufacturing warehouses and distribution centers. It integrates software technologies and hardware to automate the process of storing and retrieving goods from storage locations. Essentially, an automated storage and retrieval system can be thought of as a “mini-warehouse” within a larger warehouse, with bulk storage, small racks, and other storage areas arranged in a specific physical layout.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The automated storage and retrieval system serves several purposes, including receiving and storing inventory from external sources, holding in-process inventory for production lines, managing inventory levels, and facilitating the retrieval of pallets for order picking and customer delivery. Typically, automated storage and retrieval systems utilize various storage technologies such as pallet racks, shelving, vertical lift modules, and carousels. These storage units are controlled by computer software that manages inventory and directs the movement of goods throughout the facility.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The automated storage and retrieval process begins with the arrival of goods at the warehouse. The items are received and entered into the inventory management system, which determines the optimal storage location based on various factors such as size, weight, and demand. The automated storage and retrieval system then automatically retrieves the appropriate storage unit and transports it to a picking station where the items are removed and prepared for shipment. The advantages of an automated storage and retrieval system include increased e ff iciency, improved accuracy, and reduced labor costs.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It also helps to minimize the amount of space required for storage, enabling companies to optimize the use of floor space in the warehouse. We’ll discuss the two automated storage and retrieval system integration options in the following sections. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 409 6.4.1 Integration with a Material Flow System Automated storage and retrieval systems and material flow systems are two important systems used in the manufacturing and warehousing industry. The automated storage and retrieval system is used for automated storage and retrieval of goods, while the material flow system is used for managing the material flow in a warehouse. To interface between these two systems, the following technical details must be considered: Communication protocol The automated storage and retrieval system and the material flow system communicate through a standard communication protocol.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Commonly used protocols include OPC-UA (Open Platform Communications - Unified Architecture) and TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol). The protocol used for communication will depend on the specific requirements of the warehouse. Data exchange The automated storage and retrieval system and the material flow system exchange data in real time. The automated storage and retrieval system provides information on the locations and statuses of goods, while the material flow system provides information on the demand for goods and their destinations.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The exchange of data is done through the communication protocol, and the data is processed by the respective systems to update their own databases. Interface development The interface between the automated storage and retrieval system and the material flow system needs to be developed based on the specific requirements of the warehouse. The interface can be developed using middleware tools, such as production integration, or using custom-developed software. The interface should be designed to handle the exchange of data in real time and should be scalable to handle large volumes of data.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: An automated storage and retrieval system and a material flow system can be integrated with each other by developing an interface between them. This interface typically involves developing custom code or middleware to facilitate the exchange of data between the two systems. The interface may use APIs, web services, or other integration technologies to connect the two systems. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 410 System integration Once the interface is developed, the automated storage and retrieval system and the material flow system must be integrated. This step involves connecting the systems to the interface, configuring the communication protocol, and testing the interface to ensure that it is functioning correctly. Error handling The automated storage and retrieval system and the material flow system must be designed to handle errors that may occur during the data exchange. For example, if the automated storage and retrieval system fails to provide the location of a product, the material flow system should be able to handle this error and take appropriate action.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In summary, the interface between the automated storage and retrieval system and the material flow system involves the development of a communication protocol, data exchange, interface development, system integration, and error handling. These technical details should be carefully considered to ensure that the interface is functioning correctly and can handle the requirements of your warehouses. 6.4.2 Integration with Automated Guided Vehicles The integration of an automated storage and retrieval system with AGVs can greatly enhance the e ff iciency and productivity of a warehouse or distribution center.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA

AGVs are equipped with sensors for obstacle detection and can communicate with the central control system. Integration The integration between the automated storage and retrieval system and AGVs involves coordination between the two systems. The central control system of the automated storage and retrieval system communicates with the AGVs to instruct them on the locations of items to be retrieved or stored. Retrieval process When an order is received, the central control system identifies the location of the requested item within the automated storage and retrieval system.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It then sends instructions to the AGVs, specifying the location and item details. Once the item is retrieved, the automated storage and retrieval system communicates with the AGVs to inform them that the item is ready for transport.

System optimization The integration of automated storage and retrieval system with AGVs allows for real-time optimization of material flows within a facility. docs.text: 413 6.5 Automated Guided Vehicles AGVs are autonomous vehicles used to transport materials or products within manufacturing warehouses or distribution environments. They are equipped with sensors, navigation systems, and control systems so they can move around a facility without human intervention. AGVs can follow predefined paths or use real-time mapping and localization to navigate around obstacles and other vehicles. The journey of AGVs has been a long one, starting from simple trucks and culminating in modern laser-guided AGVs.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: An AGV is a mobile robot that follows predefined paths or series of paths, typically along the floor of a manufacturing or warehouse facility, to transport materials or goods. These vehicles are designed to operate autonomously and are guided by various technologies such as magnetic tape, lasers, or cameras. AGVs are used in various industries such as manufacturing, automotive, aerospace, pharmaceuticals, and logistics to move materials and products e ff iciently and safely. They can be programmed to move goods between di ff erent locations, such as between storage areas, assembly lines, or shipping docks, without requiring human intervention.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: AGVs come in di ff erent forms, including forklifts, pallet trucks, and carts, and can be powered by batteries, electric motors, or a combination of both. Some AGVs are equipped with sensors so they can detect obstacles in their paths and avoid collisions, making them safe to operate around humans and other machinery. AGVs come in many shapes and sizes, from small, simple machines to large, complex vehicles capable of carrying heavy loads. They can be designed to transport goods on flat surfaces, to move up and down ramps, or to enter and exit elevators.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: AGVs follow predefined paths and handle battery charging separately. On average, in most industries, AGVs require 12 minutes of high-speed charging per hour of usage. AGVs can adapt to options such as wireless charging, automatic battery swaps, or solar-powered batteries to quickly get back to business. AGVs use various forms of sensors and signals to guide them to their destination. These sensors can range from a computer vision system that builds a real-time Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 414 view of the plant, with obstacle detection and collision avoidance algorithms, to a wire or coded tape on the floor defining a more static route. While many types of AGVs and navigation methods exist on the market, they all use some form of sensor and signal system to tell the AGV where it is located in the space, where it needs to go, and how to get there. Overall, AGVs are a cost-e ff ective solution for automating material handling tasks in various industries, improving e ff iciency, reducing labor costs, and enhancing worker safety.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: AGVs are becoming increasingly popular in warehouses and distribution centers due to their ability to automate material handling tasks, increase e ff iciency, and reduce costs. By integrating AGVs with SAP EWM software, material flows and warehouse operations can be further optimized and synchronized. To integrate AGVs with SAP EWM, follow these steps: 1. Develop a communication interface between SAP EWM and the fleet management system (control system/guidance system) of the AGV system manufacturer or vehicle. This step enables the distribution of warehouse tasks to AGVs and supports the communication of warehouse task confirmations back to SAP EWM.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP EWM supports various communication protocols for integrating AGVs, such as TCP/IP, XML, or APIs as well as IDoc communication. 2. Configure the AGV as a resource in SAP EWM. AGVs are treated as resources in SAP EWM, which can be reserved, scheduled, and tracked like any other warehouse resource. The AGV is defined as a resource with its own set of characteristics, such as maximum speed, capacity, and location. 3. Create and schedule AGV tasks. AGV tasks (transport requests) can be created in SAP EWM using standard transactions or through a custom interface.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These tasks can include picking up and delivering materials, replenishing inventory, and moving empty containers. The tasks are then scheduled based on the availability of the AGV and the priority of the task. AGVs physically pick up the HU from the conveyor system and deliver it to the staging area. The SAP EWM system sends a warehouse task to the AGV, and the AGV confirms the warehouse task back to SAP EWM as the HU stages to the intended location specified by SAP EWM. 4. Monitor and control AGV operations. SAP EWM provides real-time visibility into the status of AGV tasks, allowing warehouse managers to monitor and © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 415 control AGV operations. This visibility includes tracking the AGV’s location, speed, and battery level, as well as receiving alerts if any issues or delays arise. 5. Integrate with other warehouse processes. AGVs can be integrated with other warehouse processes, such as inventory management, order management, and quality control. For example, AGVs can be used to automatically move materials from a receiving dock to storage locations or to transport materials from one workstation to another. Additionally, SAP EWM can communicate with the AGV controller software using its APIs, making it the central brain for orchestrating activity and providing a digital command center for the entire operation, as shown in Figure 6.80.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Most companies typically initiate their integration with an AGV system by linking it with their SAP EWM system. This connection provides insight into the inventory available, its location within a facility, and the quantity of each item present in a specific location. As SAP EWM usually comes equipped with an interface, a standard operating procedure for a minimal integration can be developed to simply record the removal of materials from a particular location in the warehouse and its placement onto an AGV. The AGV will then add it to the new location where it is delivered.

docs.text: 418 7 Yard Logistics SAP Yard Logistics, an all-encompassing software solution provided by SAP, o ff ers a holistic approach to optimizing and managing logistical operations in yard or terminal settings. Its primary objective revolves around enriching the e ff iciency, visibility, and coordination of inbound and outbound logistics activities encompassing transportation, storage, and goods handling. This chapter provides an overview of the integration between SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM) and SAP Yard Logistics.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Yard logistics refers to the management of operations that take place within the confines of a shipping yard, such as a warehouse, distribution center, or freight terminal. These operations typically involve the movement of goods, vehicles, and personnel within the yard, as well as the storage and retrieval of items. Yard logistics can also involve coordinating and tracking the movement of shipments, scheduling delivery times, and managing the flow of vehicles and people in and out of the yard. E ff ective yard logistics is critical for ensuring the e ff icient and timely movement of goods and materials within the supply chain.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Warehousing and transportation meet at yards, which act as the connecting link. The integration of SAP EWM and SAP Yard Logistics seamlessly facilitates the synchronized orchestration and optimization of warehouse operations alongside yard management. Consequently, enterprises can adeptly administer inbound and outbound logistics processes, while adeptly handling the movement and storage of goods within warehouse and yard premises. In essence, the harmonious convergence of SAP EWM and SAP Yard Logistics enables a streamlined flow of goods, engenders heightened operational e ff iciency, and augments the visibility and command over warehouse and yard undertakings.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Ultimately, this amalgamation empowers organizations to attain amplified logistics e ff iciency, culminating in the provision of superlative customer service. We’ll begin this chapter with an overview of the yard logistics process and walk through the SAP Yard Logistics solution and its integration with SAP EWM. Then, we’ll cover using SAP Yard Logistics in depth, detailing both inbound and outbound processes. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 419 7.1 Overview of Yard Logistics The yard logistics process involves a number of steps, including the following: Receiving goods The process typically starts with the receipt of goods into the yard. This step can involve checking the goods against the shipping manifest, ensuring that the correct quantities and items have been received, and organizing the goods for storage or further distribution. Storage and retrieval Once the goods have been received, they must be stored within the yard. This step involves finding an appropriate location within the yard to store the goods and ensuring that they are stored safely and securely.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When the goods are needed for distribution or transportation, they must be retrieved from storage. Inventory management E ff ective yard logistics also requires careful inventory management. This step involves keeping track of the quantities and locations of items within the yard, as well as monitoring the flow of goods in and out of the yard to ensure that inventory levels are maintained. Equipment and personnel management Yard logistics also involves managing the equipment and personnel needed to move goods within the yard.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This step can include coordinating the use of forklifts, pallet jacks, and other handling equipment, as well as managing personnel schedules and ensuring that workers are trained and equipped to carry out their duties safely and e ff iciently. Transportation management Finally, yard logistics also involves coordinating the movement of goods into and out of the yard. This step can include scheduling deliveries and pickups, coordinating with transportation providers, and ensuring that goods are transported in a timely and e ff icient manner.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Businesses across various sectors and industries, engaged in the movement of goods through logistics and supply, have come to acknowledge that transportation disruptions frequently occur not just on the road, but also when resources are situated in the yards of your manufacturing plants and distribution centers. docs.text: 426 7.2 Using SAP Yard Logistics In this section, we’ll provide a detailed explanation of SAP Yard Logistics. We’ll begin with the inbound process and cover the outbound process as well. For both scenarios, we’ll walk through the business process, configuration, and master data setup needed then provide a process demonstration. 7.2.1 Inbound Process The purpose of the inbound logistics process with SAP Yard Logistics is to streamline the flow of goods and materials into a company’s operations, ensuring e ff icient operations, reducing costs, and enhancing customer satisfaction.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll look at the inbound process in detail in the following sections. Business Process As shown in Figure 7.3, the inbound process using SAP Yard Logistics involves the following steps: 1. The first step in the inbound goods process is to create a purchase order for a vendor in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. The purchase order is then converted to an inbound delivery, which is automatically distributed to SAP EWM for warehouse processing. 2. Once the planning is complete, the shipment is distributed to SAP EWM as well as SAP Yard Logistics to trigger the process of truck arrival, loading, and departure.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The message from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA triggers the creation of the yard request in SAP Yard Logistics, which is used to plan the first yard activity. 3. At the same time, the message from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA is also sent to SAP EWM, a dependent document is created, namely the TU, which contains information about the planned content. In addition, an automatic door determination or manual door assignment occurs, allowing SAP EWM to begin the putaway and staging process. Note that, since SAP EWM and SAP Yard Logistics are involved in this process, no yard activities, such as check- in postings or movements, will be executed.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 427 Figure 7.3 Inbound Process Using SAP Yard Logistics 4. While the warehouse begins its activities in SAP Yard Logistics, the yard order is created based on the yard request, which is used for processing in the yard. In an inbound scenario such as this, an inbound yard order will be created. For the departure of the truck, an outbound yard order is required, which can be generated from the inbound yard order. 5. Meanwhile, in SAP EWM, the inbound process is performed, and the products are unloaded and putaway. At the same time, di ff erent yard activities are taking place in SAP Yard Logistics.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Once the movement to the door is activated, another door determination may occur. This step is used when no door determination was triggered earlier or to validate the previously determined door. 6. With confirmation of the yard task in SAP Yard Logistics, the arrival at the door will be posted in SAP EWM. At this point, the TU can no longer be moved in the yard. Activities in the yard will only be possible again after receiving notification from SAP EWM that the unloading has been completed. 7. This notification triggers yard operations to start the movement from the door to the next yard location, such as the checkpoint for departure.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A message about this pending departure from the door is sent from SAP Yard Logistics to SAP EWM. Meanwhile, the goods receipt can be triggered in SAP EWM. The latest point for a goods receipt posting is during the check-out of the TU. Again, after the unloading notification has been sent to SAP Yard Logistics, no further yard activities are allowed in SAP EWM. All postings happen in SAP Yard Logistics. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 428 8. Now that the truck has reached the inbound checkpoint, the check-in can be posted. This check-in will also be sent to SAP EWM, triggering the check- in posting there. Based on the goods receipt and check-in posting in SAP EWM, SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA documents will be updated. Yard logistics play a crucial role in ensuring e ff icient and streamlined operations during the outbound process.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll look at the outbound process in detail in the following sections. Business Process As shown in Figure 7.33, the outbound goods issue process using SAP Yard Logistics involves the following steps: 1. The first step in this process is to create a sales order for a customer in the ERP or SAP S/4HANA system. The sales order is then converted into an outbound delivery, which is automatically sent to SAP EWM for warehouse processing. 2. Once the planning is complete, the shipment is distributed to both SAP EWM and SAP Yard Logistics to initiate the process of truck arrival, loading, and departure.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 442 3. The ERP message triggers the creation of the Yard Request document, which is used to plan the first yard activity. This message is also sent to SAP EWM, where a TU document is created containing information about the planned content. Additionally, automatic door determination or manual door assignment takes place, allowing SAP EWM to start the picking and staging process. 4. It’s important to note that since SAP Yard Logistics and SAP EWM are involved in this process, yard activities such as check-in posting or movements should not be executed.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These steps fall under the scope of SAP Yard Logistics. 5. While the warehouse begins its activities in the yard, the Yard Order is created based on the Yard Request. This document is used for processing in the yard, and since this is an outbound scenario, an outbound Yard Order is created. For the arrival of the truck, an inbound yard order is required, which can be generated from the outbound Yard Order. 6. Meanwhile, in SAP EWM, outbound processes are occurring, and the products are being staged. Simultaneously, various yard activities are taking place in SAP Yard Logistics.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Once the movement to the door is activated, another door determination may occur, either when no door determination has been triggered before or to validate the previously determined door. 7. With the confirmation of the TU in SAP Yard Logistics, the arrival at the door is posted in SAP EWM. At this point, the TU cannot be moved in the yard any longer, and yard activities are only possible again after receiving notification from SAP EWM that loading is complete. 8. This notification triggers yard activities, and the movement from the door to the next yard location, such as the checkpoint for departure, can be executed.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A departure from door message is sent from SAP Yard Logistics to SAP EWM. 9. Goods issue may be triggered in SAP EWM during this process, and the latest possible point for the goods issue posting is the checkout of the TU. After the loading notification is sent to SAP Yard Logistics, no further yard activities are allowed in SAP EWM, and all postings occur in the yard. 10. Now that the truck has reached the outbound checkpoint, the check-out can be posted, which is also sent to SAP EWM and triggers the check-out © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 460 8 Environmental Health and Safety The SAP Environment, Health, and Safety Management (SAP EHS Management) module represents an all-encompassing system meticulously crafted to e ff ectively govern and oversee environmental health and safety (EHS) risks within an organization. This module empowers enterprises to diligently trace and ascertain compliance with regulatory requisites, proactively identify and mitigate workplace hazards, and instill a culture ingrained with safety consciousness among employees. Encompassing myriad aspects such as incident management, risk assessment, safety training, emergency response planning, and compliance reporting, the SAP EHS Management module emerges as a robust framework to uphold the highest standards of health and safety.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The primary objective of this chapter is to explicate the intricacies of the SAP EHS Management repertoire —and its seamless integration with SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM) through the embedded Extended Warehouse Management in SAP S/4HANA (embedded EWM) framework. This SAP component o ff ers comprehensive support for all activities pertaining to product safety and stewardship. If your organization manufactures and sells substances that are potentially harmful, it is of utmost importance to safeguard human beings and the environment from the risks associated with these substances.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Additionally, you must comply with numerous laws and regulations concerning hazardous substances on a global scale. This SAP component aids in the secure handling of hazardous substances, ensuring their safe introduction to the market and automating compliance with all relevant regulations. SAP EHS Management and SAP EWM are distinct modules within an SAP system. The integration of these two modules facilitates a more e ff icient and streamlined management of hazardous materials and related processes. The opening section of this chapter provides an overview of EHS concerns and emphasizes the key functionalities of SAP EHS Management.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We subsequently focus on the various options available for an inbound process using SAP EHS Management, encompassing business processes, configuration, master data, and a comprehensive demonstration of the end-to-end process. The chapter © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 461 then delves into an outbound process using SAP EHS Management, encompassing the business process itself and a process demonstration. Upon completion of this chapter, you’ll have a thorough understanding of SAP EHS Management and its module, product safety and stewardship, as well as SAP EHS Management’s seamless integration with SAP EWM for both inbound and outbound processes. 8.1 Overview of Environmental Health Safety EHS is a broad term to describe the laws, rules, regulations, professions, programs, and workplace e ff orts that aim to protect the health and safety of employees and the public, as well as the environment, from hazards associated with the workplace.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Essentially, EHS encompasses the profession of occupational safety and health professionals, along with their colleagues in the environmental department. EHS is a discipline that focuses on protecting the health and safety of people, as well as preserving the natural environment. The primary objective of EHS is to prevent accidents, injuries, and illnesses in the workplace, while minimizing the impact of business operations on the environment. The roles and functions of EHS professionals may vary depending on the organization and industry, but typically include the following: Developing and implementing safety policies and procedures: EHS professionals are responsible for developing and enforcing safety policies and procedures to ensure compliance with regulations and standards.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Conducting safety training and education: EHS professionals provide safety training to employees to ensure they have the knowledge and skills to work safely and prevent accidents. Conducting safety inspections and audits: EHS professionals conduct safety inspections and audits to identify hazards and risks and recommend corrective actions. Investigating accidents and incidents: EHS professionals investigate accidents and incidents to determine their root causes and to recommend corrective actions and prevent similar incidents in the future.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 462 Managing hazardous materials and waste: EHS professionals manage hazardous materials and waste to ensure they are handled, stored, and disposed of safely and in compliance with regulations. Developing and implementing environmental programs: EHS professionals develop and implement programs to manage environmental risks, such as air and water pollution, waste management, and energy conservation. Overall, the role of EHS professionals is to ensure the safety and well-being of employees, protect the environment, and maintain regulatory compliance in the workplace.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In another words, EHS is a discipline that focuses on implementing practical measures to protect the environment and ensure health and safety in the workplace. From a safety standpoint, it involves creating organized procedures to identify workplace hazards and reduce accidents and exposure to harmful situations and substances. Additionally, personnel are trained in accident prevention, emergency preparedness, and the use of protective clothing and equipment. At its core, EHS aims to develop safe, high-quality, and environmentally friendly processes, working practices, and systemic activities that prevent or reduce the risk of harm to people in general, to operators, or to patients.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: From an environmental standpoint, EHS involves implementing a systematic approach to comply with regulations regarding waste management, air emissions, and reducing a site’s carbon footprint. Regulatory requirements are essential in the EHS discipline, and EHS managers must identify and understand relevant regulations, communicating their implications to executive management so that the company can implement appropriate measures. In the United States, organizations are subject to EHS regulations outlined in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), particularly CFR 29, 40, and 49.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, EHS management is not limited to legal compliance, and companies are encouraged to go beyond what is required by law as appropriate. SAP EHS Management is a software solution provided by SAP designed to help organizations manage their EHS risks and compliance requirements. This integrated solution allows organizations to manage their EHS data, processes, and reporting in a single system. SAP EHS Management works by providing a range of modules that allow organizations to manage their EHS data and processes.

Dangerous goods management This module allows organizations to manage the transportation and storage of hazardous materials in compliance with local and international regulations. Occupational health This module allows organizations to manage the health and safety of their employees, including monitoring and reporting on workplace hazards and incidents.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Industrial hygiene and safety This module allows organizations to manage their industrial hygiene and safety processes, including risk assessments, inspections, and audits. Environ ment This module allows organizations to manage their environmental compliance requirements, including air and water quality monitoring, emissions reporting, and sustainability reporting. SAP EHS Management provides various features that assist organizations in maintaining employee health and safety, product and reach compliance, product safety, and environmental compliance management, including the following: Employee health and safety This functionality deals with processes related to industrial hygiene and occupational health to ensure the well-being of workers and the workplace.
