docs.text: 486 9 Plant Maintenance Plant maintenance is a sophisticated module incorporated within the SAP’s enterprise resource planning (ERP) system, specifically designed to assist organizations in e ff ectively managing and up keeping their plants, equipment, and assets. Its purpose is to optimize maintenance procedures, minimize downtime, and enhance overall operational e ff iciency. By utilizing plant maintenance, your company can bolster asset reliability, reduce maintenance costs, and elevate its overall operational e ff ectiveness.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The primary objective of this chapter is to furnish you with a comprehensive understanding of plant maintenance. Plant maintenance is an integral part of SAP ERP helps enterprises manage and preserve their equipment and systems. The plant maintenance application component is a comprehensive tool to streamline maintenance activities. With plant maintenance, an organization can automate repairs and optimize maintenance requests. This application allows users to document issues within the SAP system, plan labor and material activities, and track and settle costs.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The integration of SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM) with plant maintenance is crucial for optimizing the handling of goods in the maintenance process. By integrating these two systems, an organization can ensure e ff icient coordination between warehouse operations and maintenance activities. This chapter begins with an overview of plant maintenance, highlighting its key benefits and the advantages of integrating plant maintenance with SAP EWM . We also cover various scenarios and functionalities related to plant maintenance- SAP EWM integration, specifically focusing on outbound processes and return (inbound) processes using plant maintenance orders.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This chapter provides detailed information about the business processes, configuration, and master data and o ff ers an end-to-end demonstration of the entire process. Emphasis will be placed on plant maintenance, which is an SAP system meticulously tailored to cater to the requirements of maintaining your plants. The central focus of this chapter is on providing an overview of plant maintenance and elucidating the various involved processes. We will o ff er meticulous insights into the plant maintenance process, coupled with a step-by- © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 487 step guide on executing both goods issue and goods receipt processes for plant maintenance orders. Finally, we’ll delve into the integration of plant maintenance with SAP EWM, SAP’s influential warehouse management system (WMS). This integration plays a pivotal role in facilitating the seamless and e ff icient handling of goods issue and goods receipt processes within the plant maintenance procedure. By the end of this chapter, you’ll have a comprehensive understanding of plant maintenance and its integration with SAP EWM for both outbound goods issues and inbound return processes. 9.1 Overview of Plant Maintenance Plant maintenance encompasses a range of activities to help an organization manage its technical systems e ff ectively.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These activities include inspection , preventive maintenance , and repair , among other measures. Inspection involves conducting a thorough assessment of the current condition of a technical system. This task involves checking the equipment and components of the system to identify any potential issues or areas of concern. The data collected from inspections can be used to create maintenance plans to address the specific needs of the system. Preventive maintenance aims to keep technical systems in an ideal condition by regularly carrying out routine maintenance activities.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This area includes tasks like cleaning, lubricating, adjusting, and replacing components before they fail. By implementing preventive maintenance, your organization can reduce the risk of breakdowns and extend equipment lifespans. Repair involves fixing any issues that arise within the technical system to restore it to its ideal condition. This activity can involve replacing defective components, repairing broken equipment, or adjusting components that are not working properly. Repair work is usually carried out in response to an identified problem or issue.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Other measures taken using the plant maintenance capabilities can include planning and scheduling maintenance tasks, monitoring equipment performance, and managing spare parts inventory. These activities support the overall goal of keeping technical systems functioning e ff iciently and e ff ectively. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 488 In general, the plant maintenance business process involves the following end- to-end functions: Request initiation A maintenance request is generated indicating the need for maintenance or repair work to be performed at an external location. This request can come from various sources such as equipment operators, technicians, or automated monitoring systems. Work order creation Based on the maintenance request, a work order is created, specifying the details of the task, including the equipment or system to be repaired, the location, the required resources, and any relevant documentation or procedures.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Resource allocation The necessary resources for the maintenance task are identified and allocated. These resources might include skilled technicians, specialized tools or equipment, spare parts, and transportation arrangements to reach the external location. Planning and scheduling The maintenance task is planned and scheduled, considering factors such as technician availability, priority of the task, and the logistics of reaching the external site. The schedule should optimize e ff iciency and minimize downtime. Dispatching and logistics Once the schedule is finalized, the work order is dispatched to the assigned technicians or maintenance crew.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Logistics arrangements, such as arranging transportation or providing detailed directions to the external site, are made to ensure timely arrival. Execution Technicians travel to the external site and carry out the maintenance or repair work according to the specifications outlined in the work order. They may perform inspections, diagnostics, troubleshooting, repairs, replacements, or any other necessary tasks to restore the equipment or system to proper working condition. Documentation and reporting Throughout the process, technicians document their activities, findings, and © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 489 any changes made during the maintenance task. This information is recorded for future reference, analysis, and compliance purposes. After completing the task, technicians prepare reports summarizing their work and any additional recommendations. Follow-up actions Depending on the findings during the maintenance task, further actions may be required. These actions can include ordering additional parts, scheduling follow-up visits, or updating preventive maintenance plans to prevent similar issues in the future. Closure and feedback Once the maintenance task is completed, the work order is closed, and relevant stakeholders are notified.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Feedback from technicians, customers, or site representatives may be collected to assess the quality of the maintenance work and identify areas for improvement. Overall, plant maintenance activities are crucial for ensuring that technical systems remain operational and reliable. By conducting inspections, implementing preventive maintenance, carrying out repairs, and taking other necessary measures, your organization can keep its equipment functioning optimally and minimize downtimes. Plant maintenance seamlessly integrates with other components of the SAP ERP system, including materials management, quality management, production planning, sales and distribution, finance, controlling, and human resources.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: By integrating with other modules, such as materials management, production, sales and distribution, personnel management, and controlling, plant maintenance ensures that data is always up-to-date. This integration also triggers necessary processes in plant maintenance and customer service in other areas of the SAP ERP system. For example, when you need to purchase a non- stock material, a purchase requisition is automatically generated in the materials management/purchasing area. The integration of plant maintenance with other SAP ERP modules ensures that the data in each module remains up- to-date and can trigger processes in other functions as necessary.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The cornerstone of plant maintenance is its master data , which is stored in and managed through centralized master data tables. Within plant maintenance, various types of master data exist, including equipment, functional locations, specifications for objects, characteristics, task lists, codes containing Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 490 maintenance history data, material bills of materials (BOMs), measuring points, and captured data about equipment use, such as wear and tear or consumption. This master data serves as the foundation for creating transactional data in SAP ERP. For instance, plant maintenance can use master data to create a maintenance record, material management can create a purchase order, production planning can create a production order, and sales and distribution can create a sales order. The integration of SAP EWM with plant maintenance through SAP Enterprise Asset Management (SAP EAM) enables you to easily use and adapt the system, resulting in a fast time-to-value and a low total cost of ownership (TCO) .

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP EWM o ff ers many advantages for streamlining warehouse operations, increasing productivity, and improving accuracy. Meanwhile, plant maintenance (in SAP EAM) automates the process of handling facility repair and maintenance requests for assets. Plant maintenance order-driven warehouse operations are crucial for ensuring the timely availability of spare parts and for reducing repair time. The primary goal of integrating plant maintenance with SAP EWM is to enhance e ff iciency, integration, and visibility throughout warehouse execution as well as reap the following benefits: Successful deployment of an improved integration package across multiple customer locations.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Flexibility to incorporate customer-specific requirements from plant maintenance orders for integration and warehouse operations. Two integration approach options—the delivery-based option and the production material request (PMR)-based option—can be pursued, depending on the type of industry (i.e., mining, oil & gas, or manufacturing) and the complexity of the customer process. Leveraging SAP EWM’s standard warehouse process capability and functionalities for all core processes, including handheld radio frequency (RF) devices.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Optimizing warehouse operations by utilizing consolidation and cross- docking based on plant maintenance orders. Process and industry expertise in plant maintenance orders and warehouse management. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

Figure 9.1 Plant Maintenance-SAP EWM Integration Let’s briefly discuss these two integration approaches: Delivery-based integration This option is primarily used for the maintenance of heavy engineering assets, such as in the mining and oil & gas industries.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As shown in Figure 9.2, delivery-based integration for plant maintenance mainly covers following high-level processes: Creation and release of plant maintenance orders for pick parts in SAP S/4HANA Creation of an outbound delivery and its replication in SAP EWM Creation of waves for pick parts, based on the outbound delivery order in SAP EWM Picking, staging, and loading plant maintenance parts from warehouses in SAP EWM Performing goods issues in SAP EWM Updating material document and reservation data for the plant maintenance order in SAP S/4HANA Figure 9.2 Delivery-Based Integration Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 492 PMR-based integration This option is primarily used for the maintenance of production assets in manufacturing plants, such as automotive and consumer goods. The PMR-based integration option is not available as an out-of-the-box SAP EWM solution. To use this functionality, an add-on from SAP Consulting is available for the integration with PMR. As shown in Figure 9.3, a plant maintenance order using PMR has several features including the following: A new object, called the production material request , o ff ers greater flexibility in staging processes within SAP EWM.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA

The system supports single-order staging, cross-order staging, and manual staging. Status and quantity updates for manufacturing orders are supported. The system allows for user-driven staging via desktop transactions or staging in the background. Figure 9.3 PMR-Based Integration © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 493 9.2 Using Plant Maintenance Orders In this section, we’ll show you how to use plant maintenance for goods issues and goods receipts. We’ll begin with the outbound process and then cover the inbound process. For both scenarios, we’ll walk through the business process, configuration, and master data setup needed and then provide a process demonstration. 9.2.1 Outbound Process In this section, we’ll thoroughly explore the outbound goods issue process using plant maintenance orders with the delivery-based integration deployment option.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This section is divided into four parts: business process, configuration required for the process, master data, and step-by-step process flow. Business Process An outbound process in plant maintenance typically refers to activities involved in the maintenance and repair of equipment, machinery, or infrastructure outside of the plant or facility where they are located. This process involves coordinating and managing the necessary resources, personnel, and materials to execute maintenance tasks at external sites. The overall business process for a goods issue of a material to a maintenance order is shown in Figure 9.4.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The key steps involved in an outbound process with plant maintenance include the following: 1. The outbound process typically starts in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA when a maintenance order is created. The outbound delivery is created with reference to the maintenance order. The outbound delivery is created in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA but is automatically is replicated to SAP EWM for further processing. 2. In SAP EWM, a wave is created for the outbound delivery order. Upon wave release, a warehouse task to pick the material is automatically created.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 494 Figure 9.4 Outbound Process Using Plant Maintenance Orders 3. The plant maintenance material is further picked, packed, and loaded as per the warehouse process. Once the process is completed, the warehouse team performs goods the issue for the outbound delivery order, and the outbound process is completed. 4. The plant maintenance team consumes the material, and the cost of the material is booked against the maintenance order. By following these steps, the outbound process in plant maintenance ensures e ff ective management of maintenance tasks at external sites, enabling the timely resolution of equipment or system issues to maintain operational e ff iciency and reliability.

Business Process The goods receipt process with plant maintenance involves receiving and recording goods or materials delivered to a plant or facility, as well as managing any associated maintenance activities. The maintenance return order process with SAP EWM typically involves several steps to ensure the smooth return of goods for maintenance or repair purposes. As shown in Figure 9.29, this process involves the following steps: 1.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The process begins with the creation of a maintenance return order in SAP EWM. This order is generated to initiate the return process and includes relevant details such as the material, quantity, and reason for return as well as any specific instructions. 2. A maintenance order is changed in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to initiate the process of returning goods to the store. During the process of goods receipt, an inbound delivery will be created, which is then replicated to SAP EWM in the background. 3. When the material is physically received in the warehouse, the warehouse team generates a warehouse task and physically places the material in the storage area in the SAP EWM system.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A putaway strategy is defined for plant maintenance materials , guiding warehouse operators to physically store the material in the designated area and confirm the warehouse task accordingly. 4. Upon arrival at the warehouse, the returned materials are received into the SAP EWM system. The goods receipt process involves capturing information such as the quantity received, inspection details (if applicable), and any discrepancies identified during the inspection 5. After the material is stored in the designated area, the warehouse team performs a goods receipt in SAP EWM, which generates inventory in both the SAP EWM and SAP S/4HANA systems 6.

docs.text: 542 You have correctly set up web service connections between packaging lines and SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals. Business Process As shown in Figure 10.24, the outbound business process involves the following steps: 1. An outbound delivery is created in the SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA system with reference to a sales order. This delivery is then integrated into both the SAP EWM and SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals systems as an outbound delivery order and an outbound delivery, respectively Figure 10.24 Overview of the Outbound Business Process 2.

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the SAP EWM system, the warehouse operations team is responsible for picking and packing the pallet HUs for the outbound delivery order. Once the truck arrives, the pallets are loaded one by one using either an RF transaction or a desktop GUI transaction. When the pallet HU is successfully loaded, an EPCIS notification is sent to the SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals system to inform it of the loading event, and the SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals system is updated with the loading event for the HU. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Integrating Warehouse Management in SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 543 3. The warehouse operations team then proceeds to perform the goods issue for the outbound delivery order. Successful completion of the goods issue updates the inventory data and material document in the SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA system. At the same time, the SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals system receives an EPCIS notification indicating the shipment. In the SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals system, the pallet HU is updated with the shipping event, and the outbound delivery order status is changed to closed.

docs.text: 549 10.3 Summary That’s it! You’re now prepared to begin working on serializing your pharmaceutical production lines. In this chapter, you provided an overview of SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals. We discussed the advantages of implementing SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals and explored its integration with SAP EWM. Additionally, we delved into the deployment options for integrating SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals with SAP EWM and SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. Furthermore, we explored the inbound goods receipt process as well as outbound goods issue process using the integration of SAP EWM, SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals, and either SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA.

docs.text: Dear Reader, Have you ever planned anything that involved more than, say, five people? It requires a true feat of scheduling! Recently, a friend of mine had a seemingly simple birthday request: a trip to an escape room with a group of her closest friends. I may have spoken too soon when I said, full of confidence, “I can definitely organize that!” Little did I know that the process of con- tacting everyone, comparing schedules to find a day and time that worked well across the board, and getting payment to make the reservation, would put my planning skills to the test.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Luckily, I had an end goal in mind. It took a lot of time and energy, but in the days lead- ing up to the event, I worked out the perfect plan and was ready to enjoy a successful escape room excursion. However, as they say, “the best-laid plans of mice and men often go awry.” Snow . Why didn’t I plan for snow ? We were all soaked, cold, and late to arrive. After all my planning, it was a very frustrating—but also very funny—turn of events. It was a chaotic day, and in the end, we didn’t manage to clear the escape room.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Still, we did have a blast! Luckily my (less than ideal) planning experience doesn’t have to be universal. Organi- zations with specialized production planning and scheduling requirements can escape the complexity using PP/DS functionality in SAP S/4HANA. In this new edition of his well-received book, author Mahesh Babu MG gives an in-depth look at how embedded PP/DS is the key to simplifying your advanced planning processes. What did you think about the second edition of PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA ? Your com- ments and suggestions are the most useful tools to help us make our books the best they can be.

docs.text: 15 Preface Welcome to PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA , a comprehensive review of the SAP S/4HANA production planning and detailed scheduling (PP/DS) functionalities and in-depth cov- erage of planning and scheduling processes and heuristics. This book is based on the SAP S/4HANA 2022 PP/DS features. Features of PP/DS in SAP Supply Chain Manage- ment (SAP SCM) and SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization that are simplified and/ or not available in SAP S/4HANA aren’t covered in this book. Who This Book Is For This book is not only for those who work directly in PP/DS but also for those who work in related supply chain planning and manufacturing areas, such as SAP Integrated Busi- ness Planning for Supply Chain (SAP IBP) and SAP S/4HANA production planning to enhance their understanding of the advanced planning features and integration offered by PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA (embedded PP/DS).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For those who’ve already worked with the PP/DS component in SAP Advanced Plan- ning and Optimization, this book will be of great use in understanding the changes in embedded PP/DS and the integration requirements, as some of the functionalities available in the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization are no longer available in embedded PP/DS. In addition, the core interface integration archi- tecture has drastically changed for most of the master data objects and some of the transaction data objects.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For those who work in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA production planning and want to expand their knowledge of embedded PP/DS, this book provides in-depth knowledge in setting up PP/DS, master data and transaction data integration, planning and scheduling processes, heuristics, tools, some advanced embedded PP/DS features, and administering embedded PP/DS. If you’re a planner or scheduler and you already work with PP/DS or have just started to work with PP/DS, this book is helpful in providing the various options available for users in terms of controlling and executing embedded PP/DS systems.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 19 Chapter 1 Introduction to PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA To start our journey through production planning and detailed schedul- ing (PP/DS), we’ll begin with the basics: What is production planning, what is detailed scheduling, and how have they changed with SAP S/4HANA? SAP’s enterprise resource planning (ERP) software, in its different forms, is widely used by companies around the world across different industries. The various releases of the software over the years have culminated in the latest two supported releases: SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA (the focus of this book).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP ERP supports many relational databases from different vendors, whereas SAP S/4HANA is the latest version, tailored for SAP HANA (the in-memory database created by SAP) and offering many new features. Since the earliest releases of SAP ERP, SAP has provided solutions for production plan- ning, capacity, and scheduling resources. In the SAP ERP software, tools such as sales and operations planning (S&OP), demand management, master production schedul- ing (MPS), material requirements planning (MRP), capacity scheduling, and leveling enable the production planning and scheduling functions.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As businesses and manufacturing processes evolved, a need emerged for more com- plex planning and scheduling algorithms to tackle such complexities. In response, SAP introduced SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, which later became part of the SAP Supply Chain Management (SAP SCM) suite. With SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, the demand planning, supply network planning, and PP/DS tools were introduced to solve complex forecasting, planning (long-term, mid-term, and short- term), and scheduling challenges.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: With the evolution of the SAP Integrated Business Planning for Supply Chain (SAP IBP) cloud solution, support was provided for S&OP, demand planning, and supply and response planning. SAP IBP is the long- to medium- term demand and supply planning tool. In the SAP ERP suite on SAP HANA and, later, in SAP S/4HANA, the classic MRP solution was enhanced with the power of SAP HANA to perform the complex MRP calculations in the SAP HANA database layer, thus making multiplying the speed of access to the MRP results. In combination with the forecasting and long- to medium-term planning capabilities of SAP IBP, MRP Live in SAP S/4HANA is the solution for short-term plan- ning.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 1 Introduction to PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA 20 In 2016, SAP released the 1610 version of SAP S/4HANA software, and the PP/DS compo- nent of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization was made available within the SAP S/4HANA core as PP/DS. This enables the SAP S/4HANA solutions capability not only to support the short-term planning via MRP Live but also to support advanced planning algorithms and detailed scheduling. Over the years, SAP also made enhancements to the existing functionalities and introduced new functionalities in SAP IBP and embed- ded PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The SAP digital supply chain is part of the SAP intelligent suite. SAP IBP and PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA are key components of the plan and manufacture components of the design-to-operate process within the digital supply chain. In 2020, SAP also introduced the SAP Digital Supply Chain version of capabilities such as PP/DS, extended warehouse management (EWM), transportation management, and so on, in the SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA system. The SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA, offers the capa- bility of having the SAP Digital Supply Chain system as a hub system for the previously mentioned capabilities and connecting to multiple ERP systems such as SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If there are multiple SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA systems in the solution landscape, these systems can integrate with SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA, to centrally plan and schedule production. The planning and scheduling results from SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA, are sent to the corresponding ERP system. The master data and transaction data between the SAP Digital Supply Chain system and the corresponding ERP system lever- age the core interface. In this chapter, we’ll introduce the concept of PP/DS using SAP systems.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll also show how the solution landscape evolved over time, the deployment options available prior to SAP S/4HANA, and the simplifications made in PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA compared to the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization. Then, we’ll transi- tion into the detailed architecture of PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA. 1.1 What Is Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling? SAP provides tools to support complete supply chain planning and execution, as well as integration with other processes and areas. One of the core processes within the sup- ply chain is production planning.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The primary objective of production planning is to ensure that the right product is available at the right time and the right place to be delivered to customers and ensure the raw materials are available for production. Detailed scheduling supports the sequencing and scheduling of production operations by taking into consideration the available resource (machine resources and human resources) capacity and the availability of materials. In addition, detailed scheduling is used to ensure the optimal usage of resources. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 21 1.1 What Is Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling? Let’s take a closer look at each in the following sections. 1.1.1 Production Planning The production planning process involves several steps. Let’s walk through the tradi- tional flow in SAP ERP, as follows: 1. Sales and operations planning (S&OP) The production planning process starts with an aggregated sales forecast in S&OP, which can be disaggregated and then transferred to demand management where it will become a concrete production plan with a planning strategy defined. 2.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Master production scheduling (MPS) This production plan will be the input for MPS, which is used to plan finished prod- ucts and products using bottleneck resources. MPS will generate planned orders to cover the forecast by using different planning parameters for each material, but it won’t consider capacity restrictions. 3. Capacity leveling After the MPS execution, capacity leveling should be executed for the generated planned orders, adjusting the planned order dates and ensuring that the production plan is feasible and won’t exceed the capacity available in the work centers. 4.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Material requirements planning (MRP) When all capacity issues are solved, it’s time to execute MRP to plan the remaining products. MRP will generate planned orders to produce semifinished products and purchase requisitions to procure raw materials. Even though SAP ERP offers this complete process for production planning, there are some limitations with the tools offered. For example, materials planning and capacity leveling are two separated steps: MPS or MRP will first generate planned orders with an infinite capacity, and the system will only consider finite capacity restrictions during capacity leveling.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Another limitation is that MPS and MRP won’t consider the expira- tion date of material batches, so the expiration must be controlled separately. These limitations are in place because these very complex planning scenarios would con- sume additional hardware resources during the planning run and could require more time to finish it. In addition, no optimizations are available for planning the produc- tion or the resource usage on the manufacturing shop floor. SAP S/4HANA is basically an evolution of SAP ERP, and many of the older features are being redesigned or even replaced by new features.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Although most of these older fea- tures are still in SAP S/4HANA, they are part of what is called the compatibility scope, which means they aren’t considered future technology and should be retired in the future. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 1 Introduction to PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA 22 Note When a new SAP S/4HANA release is launched, SAP delivers a document called the sim- plification list, which describes the major changes of the new release, including the features that are part of the compatibility scope. An SAP Note linking to the simplifica- tion list can be found in Appendix A. In SAP S/4HANA, S&OP and demand management are gradually being replaced by cloud-based SAP IBP, and capacity planning is being replaced by PP/DS. Production planning in SAP S/4HANA is powered by MRP Live and forms the production planning part of PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: PP/DS also offers optimization of the production plan and capacity utili- zation, including optimized sequencing of orders in the manufacturing resources. 1.1.2 Detailed Scheduling After the production planning process is complete, resulting in the production propos- als for the in-house manufactured products, the next step is to identify the correct resources needed to execute the orders in the manufacturing shop floor where the detailed scheduling processes are used. The detailed scheduling tools should consider the availability of the materials for manufacturing and the available capacity of the machinery, tools, and human resources.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In SAP ERP, detailed scheduling is supported in the form of capacity planning, which comprises two major features: capacity evaluation and capacity leveling. Capacity planning supports long-term rough-cut planning, medium-term planning, and short- term detailed planning. Capacity requirements are created by orders that are generated via the production planning tools, such as MPS and MRP. In addition, capacity requirements are created by networks in project systems and plant maintenance orders. The orders created by the planning tools are scheduled on the resources (also called work centers) based on the planning settings and using the routing master data.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The routing master data defines the calculation of the duration for scheduling and the capacity required to execute a specific manufacturing step. After the capacity requirements are created, the capacity evaluation tool can be used to analyze the capacity load on the resources based on the available capacity. The capacity leveling tools are also used to dispatch and deallocate operations on the resources based on the underload and overload situations. For complex manufacturing scenarios, the SAP ERP capacity planning tools have chal- lenges in optimizing the capacity use of the resources and adhering to the production schedule to minimize delays in manufacturing.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These complex requirements for capacity planning and detailed scheduling are addressed in the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 23 1.2 PP/DS with SAP 1.2 PP/DS with SAP To address those complex planning and scheduling scenarios, SAP created a new PP/DS tool, as mentioned previously. This tool was introduced a long time ago as part of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, which provides a set of advanced supply chain planning tools. Additionally, SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization could be inte- grated into one or multiple ERP systems, planning an entire supply chain together. SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization has the special dedicated SAP liveCache data- base, which was designed to handle very complex algorithms.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The objective of PP/DS is to cover the demand with procurement proposals in the short-term horizon for critical products or to create an optimized production plan con- sidering various costs that may influence the production plan—storage costs, resource/work center costs, and delay penalties—and create an optimized resource schedule for the resources in which the manufacturing operations are performed.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Key features in PP/DS include the following:  Production planning heuristics  Production planning optimizer  Interactive planning tools  Detailed scheduling heuristics  Detailed scheduling optimizer  Interactive detailed scheduling tools  Background planning and scheduling tools  Planning procedures  Pegging relationships  Alert Monitor PP/DS supports various manufacturing processes leveraged by many industries:  Discrete manufacturing In industries such as industrial machinery manufacturing, consumer goods, and so on, the discrete manufacturing process is leveraged in SAP ERP systems. With dis- crete manufacturing, the production steps flow through multiple workstations where activities such as assembly are performed, followed by the final product rolling off the production shop floor.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In SAP ERP systems, discrete manufacturing is sup- ported by routing as the main master data object for the definition of the manufac- turing steps. The execution of the manufacturing is driven by production orders. In PP/DS, the discrete manufacturing master data and production orders are supported to arrive at an optimal production plan and an optimal schedule for the orders.  Production planning for process industries The process industry manufacturing process is used by industries such as chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and food and beverage.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 1 Introduction to PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA 24 material flows and processing of the input materials throughout the process to pro- duce the final product. In process industry processes, the master recipe is the pri- mary master data object to define the manufacturing process. The execution object in the ERP system is called the process order. In PP/DS, specific features such as tank planning, campaign planning, and continuous input/output planning support the process industry requirements.  Repetitive manufacturing In both discrete-based and process industry-based manufacturing, the manufactur- ing is driven by production and process orders.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In repetitive manufacturing, how- ever, production is based on the rate in which the production line can produce the goods. Industries such as electronic/automobile components manufacturing, the same steps are performed repeatedly throughout a set period until the desired pro- duction quantity is achieved. So, in repetitive manufacturing, no manufacturing orders are used and the manufacturing quantity is guided by the planned orders. But the actual manufacturing will happen based on the rate of production of the manufacturing line.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The requirements in repetitive manufacturing industries, such as creation of planned orders per period (shift, day, week, etc.) on specific production lines, are supported by special planning algorithms in PP/DS. PP/DS also supports certain industry-specific features, such as length-based planning required for metal industries, and model mix planning, which is widely used in the automobile industry. 1.2.1 SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization In this section, we’ll take a closer look at the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Plan- ning and Optimization, see how it’s embedded in SAP S/4HANA, and walk through how PP/DS fits into SAP S/4HANA deployment and architecture.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: With the SAP S/4HANA 1610 release, PP/DS was made available in the SAP S/4HANA core. In addition, a side-by-side usage of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization is possible with SAP S/4HANA as the ERP system. SAP introduced the cloud-based SAP IBP solution with capabilities such as demand planning, supply and response planning, and inventory planning, which will replace the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system for advanced planning and opti- mization functionalities such as demand planning and supply network planning.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Therefore, the target architecture for the end-to-end planning and scheduling solution is to have SAP IBP as the demand and supply planning solution and SAP S/4HANA as the PP/DS system for critical products and components. Whether it’s SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, the configuration data, such as organizational structures and master data objects (e.g., material master, bill of materials [BOM], rout- ings, production version, work centers or resources, capacities, vendors, and custom- ers) are maintained in the ERP system.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 25 1.2 PP/DS with SAP Let’s walk through the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization basics, before com- paring it to PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA (embedded PP/DS). SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization with SAP ERP In the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system, the processes start with demand planning, where the historical sales and consumption data is used for forecast- ing the demand. The outcome of demand planning is the constrained forecast, which is used to perform supply planning. Supply planning is executed using supply network planning, which comprises complex algorithms in the form of heuristics and the opti- mizer to plan supplies against demand.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Demand planning and supply network planning are executed for mid- to long-term horizons. The data and process flow between the SAP ERP and SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization systems is shown in Figure 1.1. Figure 1.1 Planning Process and Data Flow between SAP ERP and SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization Systems For the short-term planning horizon, procurement proposals from the supply plan in supply network planning are transferred to PP/DS. Within PP/DS, the plan is refined further.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Comparing the PP/DS component’s capabilities in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimi- zation with the tools available for planning in SAP ERP reveals that the basic structure behind the two solutions is similar; however, PP/DS provides advanced tools and fea- tures that aren’t available in SAP ERP, such as the following:  Materials planning and finite capacity planning  Optimization of production plan  Planning with exact times SAP ERP system SAP APO system Master data (material master, work centers, BOMs, routings, plants, customer, vendor, purchase info records, etc.) Transaction data (purchase orders, requisitions, planned and production orders, sales orders, planned independent requirements) Core Interface Production execution Master data (enhanced with SAP APO-specific fields) Demand planning Supply network planning Production planning and detailed scheduling SAP APO forecast and planning data (forecasts, planned orders, purchase requisitions, schedule line agreement releases) Material requirements planning for non-SAP APO materials/locations Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 1 Introduction to PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA 26  Forecast consumption with descriptive characteristics  Planning runs with multiple planning algorithms  Dynamic pegging and fixed pegging (assignment of receipt elements across BOM levels)  Planning with custom heuristics (planning algorithm that executes the planning on selected objects) Some of these features are only possible in the PP/DS component in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, which uses the SAP liveCache database, designed to algo- rithmically handle complex data and runtime-intensive functions.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP liveCache is an object-based and enhanced SAP MaxDB database. SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization connects directly with SAP ERP, and data is transferred though the core interface. For each piece of master data to be transferred from SAP ERP to SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization via the core interface, you’ll need to create and activate an integration model so that the master data can be sent through the integration queues. After planning in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimi- zation, the planning results are also integrated into SAP ERP via the core interface, and any record stuck in the integration queue can lead to major integration problems between the systems or data inconsistencies.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In planning scenarios where there are planning runs to be executed in different sys- tems, namely, SAP ERP and SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, multiple plan- ning executions are involved, and a lot of dependencies are created due to the same product getting planned in multiple locations, For example, if the supply chain net- work consists of three plants—plants 1 and 3 planned in the PP/DS component in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization and plant 2 planned in the SAP ERP system—and the product structure extends throughout these three plants, then three different plan- ning runs need to be spread across the SAP ERP and SAP Advanced Planning and Opti- mization systems.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, the second and third planning runs need to wait for the planning results to be transferred to SAP ERP from SAP Advanced Planning and Opti- mization and vice versa. SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization versus SAP S/4HANA Embedded PP/DS brings the PP/DS features from SAP Advanced Planning and Optimi- zation into the SAP S/4HANA system, enabling the SAP S/4HANA system to act as a comprehensive planning and scheduling solution for the short-term planning horizon. From a usability perspective, all PP/DS transactions are available within the SAP S/4HANA system, allowing end users to perform all the planning and scheduling functions in one system.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: With the PP/DS component in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, users need to switch between the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization and SAP ERP sys- tems to accomplish the planning and scheduling tasks. In SAP S/4HANA, new SAP Fiori © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 27 1.2 PP/DS with SAP apps have been introduced for detailed scheduling that work seamlessly with the SAP Fiori apps delivered for MRP Live planning. With SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, the master data and transaction data need to be transferred between the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization and SAP ERP systems because both systems need to be in sync in terms of master data. In addi- tion, for certain master data fields that are only relevant for SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization planning, the data is directly maintained only in the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The master data also needs to be synced up fre- quently between the SAP ERP and SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization systems to ensure that the data is consistent and that the planning results are correct in the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system. In SAP S/4HANA, master data maintenance is greatly simplified by maintaining only one version of data for SAP S/4HANA as well as for embedded PP/DS. For most master data objects, there is no need to create an integration model and transfer the data from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Master data objects such as materials and work cen- ters are maintained in SAP S/4HANA transactions and are flagged for use in advanced planning. Note Advanced planning is the term used in SAP S/4HANA to identify the objects and pro- cesses that use the PP/DS capability. The fields relevant to PP/DS fields are also exposed to the SAP S/4HANA master data objects and can be maintained in one transaction. When the data is stored in the data- base tables, it’s saved only in SAP S/4HANA tables, and data duplication is avoided wherever applicable.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Similarly, transaction data such as planned independent requirements (PIRs), planned orders, production and process orders, purchase requisitions and orders, and sales orders are transferred to embedded PP/DS without any need for an active integration model. The relevant transaction data objects are marked as relevant for transfer in Cus- tomizing, and if the corresponding master data object is also marked as active for advanced planning, the transaction data is transferred to embedded PP/DS and from SAP S/4HANA, and vice versa.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Because embedded PP/DS also uses SAP liveCache, the order objects need to be re-created in SAP liveCache upon transfer to embedded PP/DS. In scenarios involving multiple locations that require MRP and advanced planning, just one MRP Live planning run in SAP S/4HANA can plan all the materials and loca- tions, including those in PP/DS. There is no need to set up separate PP/DS planning runs to generate the procurement proposals for the advanced planning material loca- tions. The planning run results are synced between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS in real time, so the risk with the core interface queue failures are greatly reduced.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 1 Introduction to PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA 28 Note Although most of the planning and scheduling features are available in embedded PP/DS, certain features of the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization aren’t available in embedded PP/DS. The critical simplification items are covered in the next section, and the complete list is available in SAP Note 3087008. Embedded PP/DS with SAP IBP The cloud-based SAP IBP) solution replaces the demand planning and supply network planning functionalities of the SAP SCM/SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization solution.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP IBP also has other integrated solutions such as S&OP and inventory plan- ning. The long-term supply planning and midterm operational planning happens within SAP IBP, and the detailed production planning for the shorter planning horizon happens within embedded PP/DS. So, it’s essential to integrate the supply planning results from SAP IBP to embedded PP/DS to further fine-tune the plan and to ensure optimal scheduling of the plan. The concept of synchronous planning was introduced in SAP IBP and in embedded PP/DS to provide a flexible integration of the supply plan from SAP IBP into SAP S/4HANA and the production plan along with the optimized production scheduling results back to SAP IBP from SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The synchronous planning process will also define the responsibility of the SAP IBP and PP/DS systems in terms of the planning horizons each of the systems are responsible for. In SAP IBP, supply planning can be performed in two stages: (1) the time series–based supply planning is a bucket-oriented planning, where the supply elements are calcu- lated in periodic buckets (weekly, monthly, etc.); and (2) the SAP IBP response planning is an order-based supply planning process, where planned orders and purchase requisi- tions are created considering the lot size and selection of the appropriate source of sup- ply.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Typically, the time series–based supply planning is performed for a longer planning horizon (e.g., 24 months, in weekly buckets), and the order-based response planning is performed for the midterm planning horizon (e.g., 3 months). Within the shorter planning horizon (e.g., 1 month), the response planning results from SAP IBP are fine-tuned considering the detailed planning and scheduling constraints defined in embedded PP/DS. SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA, is a new offering to handle complex solution landscape requirements.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, if your landscape con- sists of many ERP systems, including SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA systems, to leverage PP/DS functionalities, you can only leverage them in the SAP S/4HANA systems as they © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 29 1.2 PP/DS with SAP have the embedded PP/DS solution as part of the SAP S/4HANA core. For the SAP ERP systems, you still must have an SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system in the landscape to leverage PP/DS functionalities. In addition, with your ERP system landscape transformation from SAP ERP systems to SAP S/4HANA, if you still choose to have a system landscape consisting of multiple SAP S/4HANA systems to leverage the PP/DS functionalities, the PP/DS setup—including the installation and management of SAP liveCache—needs to be performed in all those SAP S/4HANA systems.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To reduce the complexity of managing each individual system with its own SAP liveCache, SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA, offers a hub solution. With this, multiple SAP ERP and/or SAP S/4HANA systems can be integrated into one SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA, system for leveraging PP/DS functionalities. Different flavors of SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edi- tion for SAP S/4HANA, are available for solution capabilities such as SAP Extended Ware- house Management (SAP EWM) and SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA includes a key capability that supports PP/DS, called SAP S/4HANA Manufacturing for planning and scheduling. Figure 1.2 shows an example of two SAP ERP systems and one SAP S/4HANA system connected to the SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA sys- tem. docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll cover the setup and integration details between the ERP systems and the SAP Digital Supply Chain system in Chapter 9, Section 9.4. 1.2.2 Key Simplifications in PP/DS for SAP S/4HANA In this section, we’ll cover the key differences between the features of the PP/DS com- ponent of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization and the embedded PP/DS fea- tures. These simplification items are dependent on the release version of SAP S/4HANA (this book is based on the on-premise release of SAP S/4HANA 2022). We’ll also cover the specific impacts of the simplification items in the relevant chapters; in this section, we cover the simplification items that aren’t covered in the other chapters.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Embedded PP/DS can’t function as a planning hub. If there are multiple ERP systems, such as SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, in the solution landscape, the embedded PP/DS of one SAP S/4HANA system can’t act as a central planning and scheduling system for all the ERP systems in the landscape. Only the planning data that is part of an SAP S/4HANA system can be used by embedded PP/DS of the same system. Standalone SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization systems can work alongside embedded PP/DS, but the data should be segregated in a way that the same set of data isn’t planned by embedded PP/DS and the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A scenario in which a product location is planned in the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system for supply network planning and the same product location is planned in embedded PP/DS isn’t supported in the standard delivered SAP S/4HANA software; however, custom interfaces may be used to support such a scenario. Let’s walk through the key simplifications, as follows:  Production versions In the SAP ERP system, production-related master data such as BOMs and routings are created and linked via the master data object called the production version.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These production versions, when transferred to the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization systems, are created as production process models (PPMs) or as pro- duction data structures (PDSs) in the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization sys- tem. While PPMs are based on older data models, PDSs are the new objects that can replace PPMs in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization. However, in the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system, both PPMs and PDSs are supported. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 31 1.2 PP/DS with SAP In embedded PP/DS, only PDSs are supported; if you’re using PPMs in your existing SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization systems and plan to use embedded PP/DS, the usage of PDSs is mandatory. If you have any enhancements implemented for the transfer of PPM in the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization or SAP ERP sys- tems, these need to be evaluated and adapted to the enhancements related to PDSs. We’ll cover this further in Chapter 2.  Simplified master data maintenance In SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization systems, it’s possible for local material masters and resources within SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization to be used in the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, with embedded PP/DS, because one of the principal objectives is to reduce data duplication, it’s not possible to create materials and resources just in PP/DS; instead, the materials and work centers (resources) should be created in SAP S/4HANA in the corresponding transactions and should be marked for advanced planning. This will make these mate- rials and resources available in the PP/DS transaction in the SAP S/4HANA system.  MRP-based detailed scheduling In SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, MRP-based detailed scheduling executes MRP in the ERP system (e.g., SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA), and the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization is only used for detailed scheduling features.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The orders created in the ERP system via MRP execution are transferred to the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system where the detailed scheduling is per- formed. After the detailed scheduling step, the new schedule with the new order dates is transferred back to the ERP system. However, with embedded PP/DS, this MRP-based detailed scheduling functionality isn’t available. After a material is activated for advanced planning, it must be planned and scheduled with embedded PP/DS.  MRP execution In the planning solution with SAP ERP and SAP Advanced Planning and Optimiza- tion systems, it’s possible to execute MRP in SAP ERP even though the material is planned by the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This option isn’t available in embedded PP/DS because MRP Live will always plan the advanced planning materials in PP/DS and not use the MRP algorithm in SAP ERP.  Planning areas The demand planning and supply network planning components of the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system use a data object called the planning area. All the demand planning and supply network planning data is stored at the planning area level. Some PP/DS functionalities, such as deployment planning in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, use the planning area data object as well.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In embedded PP/DS, the demand planning and supply network planning compo- nents of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization aren’t available, so the planning areas concept doesn’t exist in SAP S/4HANA, and the PP/DS component features of Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 1 Introduction to PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA 32 SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization that are dependent on the planning area aren’t available in SAP S/4HANA. Therefore, functionalities such as capacity reserva- tion and PP/DS deployment aren’t supported in embedded PP/DS.  Global available-to-promise (global ATP) Global ATP is a tool in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization that can be trig- gered during the sales order creation process in the ERP system to check for the availability of the product and commit an availability date to the sales order.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Simi- larly, capable-to-promise (CTP) is another availability check tool in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization that checks for product availability; if there is no avail- ability, the CTP tool creates a temporary planned order in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization by considering the available capacity of the resources and then proposes an availability date back to the ERP system. The global ATP and CTP tools aren’t part of embedded PP/DS, so these checks during the creation of sales orders aren’t available in SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, for planned orders and production orders, the native available-to-promise (ATP) tool of SAP S/4HANA is integrated for the availability check of planned and production order components. If a planned order is created or converted into a production order in embedded PP/DS, the corresponding order created in SAP S/4HANA trig- gers the ATP check for the components.  Custom sort profiles In the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system, the order conversion and fixed pegging functionalities can use custom sort profiles to define the sequence of orders using the available order properties.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These custom sort profiles are based on the global ATP functionality. Because global ATP isn’t supported in embedded PP/DS, the custom sort profiles also aren’t available in SAP S/4HANA.  Capable-to-match (CTM) CTM is another tool in the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system used to plan the demands in multiple levels of the supply chain finitely. This tool isn’t part of SAP S/4HANA because embedded PP/DS is no longer bundled with other SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization components such as demand planning or supply network planning.  PP/DS optimizer The PP/DS optimizer is a powerful scheduling optimizer that creates an optimized plan according to the objective functions defined for optimization.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, the optimizer can create new supply elements (e.g., planned orders) if there is a supply shortage. In embedded PP/DS, on the other hand, the PP/DS optimizer can’t create planned orders; it can only schedule production orders and planned orders. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 33 1.2 PP/DS with SAP  Data When master data is transferred between the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimiza- tion and the ERP system via the core interface, there are multiple enhancement options (e.g., user exits and business add-ins [BAdIs]) available to add additional fields and to enhance the master data. Such enhancements cover material masters and classification data (classes and characteristics). If these enhancements are used in the existing SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system, you need to adapt those to the corresponding enhancement options available in the SAP S/4HANA sys- tem.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In embedded PP/DS, you can use the extensibility features to add fields to the material master so that any additional fields created in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization can be made available in the SAP S/4HANA material master. 1.2.3 Deployment In this section, we’ll cover the deployment options available for PP/DS. To understand the reduced complexity of the deployment of embedded PP/DS, we’ll discuss the vari- ous deployment options available for the PP/DS component in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization and in SAP ERP, add-on for embedded PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: PP/DS with SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization When introduced, SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization was a standalone system on the Basis platform, which is now the SAP NetWeaver platform. The underlying data- base can be any database system, such as SAP HANA, Oracle, DB2, DB6, or Microsoft SQL Server (MSSQL). The SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system requires a sepa- rate database for high-speed processing of the planning component, which is SAP live- Cache. docs.text: 39 1.2 PP/DS with SAP 1.2.4 Architecture SAP S/4HANA has a new, simplified architecture to remove any redundancies in tech- nologies, applications, and data. In this section, we’ll cover the general architecture of the SAP S/4HANA system and the architecture of embedded PP/DS. SAP S/4HANA simplified the architecture of the previous ERP versions. The principle of one is applied in the new architecture, which simplifies any duplicate functionalities and the need to save the same data in multiple tables for performance purposes.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: From a technical perspective, the multiple frameworks available with the ERP systems to realize functionality have been simplified in SAP S/4HANA. In the ERP systems running on any database, to optimize the performance of the appli- cations, the data is aggregated at different characteristics levels of the data, such as periods (daily, weekly, monthly), and aggregated at certain organizational levels. How- ever, with the power of SAP HANA, these aggregations can be performed on the fly, and there is no need to create redundant data in the database tables.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: With SAP S/4HANA, the applications can use the SAP HANA database to perform complex calculations. An example of how the inventory data storage is simplified in the SAP S/4HANA architec- ture is shown in Figure 1.10. In this example, the data is stored in more than 25 tables in SAP ERP systems, whereas this is simplified to just 2 tables in the SAP S/4HANA system. Figure 1.10 Simplification in the SAP S/4HANA Inventory Management Data Model Architecture Another simplification in the architecture from the usability perspective is in the user interface (UI).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The SAP S/4HANA architecture also makes the platform future-ready for innovations and integration to other cloud solutions. To enable the simplifications in terms of data, usability, analytics, and future readiness, the technical architecture of the SAP S/4HANA system is designed as shown in Figure 1.11. The SAP HANA database layer consists of the database tables, and the CDS views enable simplified access to combined data from mul- tiple tables. The SAP S/4HANA layer contains the transactional and analytical business logic, as well as Enterprise Search, which simplifies and enhances the search capability in the SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP Gateway is the communication layer between the SAP S/4HANA system and the SAP Fiori UI. The SAP Gateway layer contains all the technical artifacts to bring the data from the SAP S/4HANA system to the SAP Fiori apps. docs.text: 41 1.2 PP/DS with SAP Figure 1.12 Simplified Embedded PP/DS Architecture Embedded PP/DS has a simplified master data architecture. The master data is main- tained in SAP S/4HANA and is visible and available for embedded PP/DS. The material master and work center are activated for advanced planning, which makes it available for embedded PP/DS. For the resource master data, the corresponding SAP liveCache time stream is also generated. For PP/DS master data, such as the PDS, a generation report is provided, which will gen- erate and save the PDS in the PP/DS tables by using the remote function call (RFC) within the same SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The business partner data (customers and ven- dors) and the organizational structure data (plant, shipping points, and MRP areas) are transferred to embedded PP/DS using a generation report. The variant configuration classes created in SAP S/4HANA are available for embedded PP/DS without the need to create any specific integration model. For master data elements such as purchase info records, contracts, and scheduling agreements, an integration model is required to generate the external procurement relationship master data in embedded PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, the characteristics-dependent planning (CDP) class type, which is specific to embedded PP/DS and not relevant for SAP S/4HANA, also requires an integration model for the transfer to embedded PP/DS. The transaction data created in SAP S/4HANA is also transferred to embedded PP/DS and saved in SAP liveCache and in the mapping tables to ensure the consistency of the data in SAP S/4HANA and SAP liveCache. Similarly, the planning data created in embed- ded PP/DS is saved in SAP liveCache and sent to SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The transaction data includes planned orders and production orders for in-house manufacturing, purchase requisitions, purchase orders, scheduling agreement releases for external procure- ment, sales orders, forecast elements, and PIRs. The data architecture for most com- monly used master and transaction data is shown in Figure 1.13. docs.text: 1 Introduction to PP/DS with SAP S/4HANA 42 Figure 1.13 Embedded PP/DS Data Architecture The SAP Digital Supply Chain system is similar to an embedded PP/DS system in terms of the technical architecture, but it only runs the PP/DS processes, and all the other manufacturing and logistics processes are executed in the connected ERP systems, which are integrated to the SAP Digital Supply Chain system via the core interface. 1.3 Summary In this chapter, we introduced the basics of production planning, detailed scheduling, and deployment options, as well as the architecture of the PP/DS component for SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, embedded PP/DS, and the SAP Digital Supply Chain Management, edition for SAP S/4HANA (specifically, SAP S/4HANA Manufactur- ing for planning and scheduling) solutions.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We also covered the evolution of the PP/DS architecture in the SAP systems and the embedded PP/DS data architecture in detail. As we discussed in this chapter, the cloud-based SAP IBP system, embedded PP/DS, and SAP Digital Supply Chain PP/DS will eventually replace the on-premise SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system for the demand, supply planning, and PP/DS func- tionalities. In the next chapter, we’ll cover the critical master data objects required to operate embedded PP/DS for executing the PP/DS processes.
