docs.text: 3 Configuration 168 3.7 Application Logs for PP/DS When a planning run is executed in embedded PP/DS based on a log level set in the PP/DS global settings and defaults, as covered in this chapter, application logs are generated for information, warning, error, and termination exceptions, depending on the log level, and then saved in the system. These application logs are useful to identify the rea- sons for materials not correctly planned in the planning run or discrepancies in the planning results, such as unexpected quantities or dates.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the configuration for the application logs in PP/DS, it’s possible to create exception groups so that the application log messages are grouped under the exception groups. This makes it easy to filter the application log messages in PP/DS application log mon- itoring Transaction /SAPAPO/RRPLOG1. For example, in the planning run, you may see an information message such as /SAPAPO/ RRP 013 - No transportation lane/procurement relationship for prod , or warning messages such as /SAPAPO/RRP338 Order 4060251/10/1 with source created late on 30.10.2022 20:41:30; desired date 20.06.2022 02:00:00 .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If you want to filter down these two mes- sages easily in the log monitoring transaction, an exception group can be created for these two messages. To create the exception groups, follow the Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Application Logs for PP/DS Maintain Exception Groups . As shown in Figure 3.54, in this transaction, click on the New Entries button, and enter a name ( Excptn Grp ) and a description ( Short Description ) for the exception group. Select the group, and double-click on the Exception Messages folder.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this screen, click on the New Entries button to add the application log message class 1 and the mes- sage number 2 to the exception group 3 . The No EM column 4 denotes that if it’s checked on for any of the messages in the exception group, the specific log message won’t be generated by the system during the planning runs. Figure 3.54 Configuring Exception Groups for Application Logs in PP/DS © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 169 3.8 PP/DS Optimizer Settings This can be useful if you want to suppress specific information messages from the application log, but you want other information message logs to be generated by the system. In the ExM Prio column 5 , you can set a priority for the application log mes- sage. Value 1 holds the highest priority, and value 99 holds the lowest priority. In the functionality to display the log for the last planning run, which can be accessed by using Transaction /SAPAPO/POV1 and selecting the Planning Run Info. , as shown in Figure 3.55, the message with the highest priority set in the exception group will be dis- played in the Exception Message column.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If the value Create a Database Alert is set in the DB Alert column (refer to Figure 3.54 6 ), the system will also generate an alert for the Alert Monitor and will save this alert message in database table /SAPAPO/ALERT_HP . We’ll cover the details regarding alerts in Chapter 7. Figure 3.55 Display of the Highest Priority Exception Message in the Planning Run Info Warning Don’t set the DB Alert option in the exception messages in the exception group unless you have specific requirements. This may lead to performance bottlenecks in the PP/DS planning runs. 3.8 PP/DS Optimizer Settings In this section, we’ll cover the technical setup of the PP/DS optimizer.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The setup of opti- mizer profiles and other application settings that are used to optimize the production plan and the production schedule will be covered in Chapter 5 and Chapter 6 during our discussion of production planning topics and detailed scheduling topics, respectively. In embedded PP/DS in SAP S/4HANA 2022, there are two optimizer engines available in the standard system:  Production Planning Optimizer The Production Planning Optimizer is a functionality that was introduced in SAP S/4HANA 2020 and continues to evolve with new features and functionalities.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Production Planning Optimizer (also called the Production Planning Solver) is a cost-based optimization engine used to create an optimal production plan. The opti- mizer considers costs such as manufacturing/capacity, procurement, transporta- tion, storage costs and penalties for late fulfillments, and violations of safety stock requirements. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Configuration 170  Detailed Scheduling Optimizer The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer has existed from the initial release of embedded PP/DS, and it’s also available in the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization solu- tion as well. The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is also a cost-based optimization engine, which will optimize the production schedule and optimal resource utiliza- tion of manufacturing resources. It considers various costs such as setup/change- over costs, delay costs, and mode costs (i.e., costs incurred by specific resources) to execute the production.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, you can combine the production planning and detailed scheduling optimi- zation in a single run to arrive at an optimal plan, which the Production Planning Opti- mizer calculates and that will be further optimized by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer for an optimal production schedule. When an optimizer run is executed, the master data and relevant transaction data is read from the SAP S/4HANA database tables and SAP liveCache. Along with this data, the constraints defined in the optimizer profile are sent to the optimizer server.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Then, the optimizer server will execute the optimization program based on the data and the parameters supplied. The output of the Production Planning Optimizer will be new procurement elements, and the output of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer will be changed dates and times. The optimizer server will call the SAP S/4HANA system to cre- ate the procurement elements and the updates to the existing orders in SAP liveCache. This process is shown in Figure 3.56.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 3.56 Technical Data Flow in the Production Planning Optimizer and Detailed Schedul- ing Optimizer Engines and SAP S/4HANA Embedded PP/DS Optimizer Server RFC (TCP/IP connection) RFC (TCP/IP connection) Create/change orders in PP/DS and SAP liveCache PP/DS transaction data (manufacturing orders; procurement orders, including planned orders and purchase requisitions; stocks; demand elements, such as forecasts, sales orders, deliveries; etc.) Execute Production Planning Optimizer program Execute Detailed Scheduling Optimizer program PP/DS master data (materials, resources, setup matrix, cost data from materials and resources, safety stock penalties, delay penalties, etc.) © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 171 3.8 PP/DS Optimizer Settings The optimizer is an optional component of embedded PP/DS. The Production Planning Optimizer and the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer are installed on a separate server with standalone SAP Gateway installed. Another option is to install the optimizer in the same server as the SAP application server for the SAP S/4HANA system. The usual deployment method is to have a standalone server for the PP/DS optimizer that is sized according to the workload expected to be handled by the Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling Optimizers and not sharing the load with any other applications.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the PP/DS optimizer server, it’s possible to install more than one optimizer software instance because the same PP/DS optimizer server can be used by multiple systems, including the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization system. The same PP/DS opti- mizer server may contain the software executables for supply network planning, capable- to-match (CTM), and so on. The Production Planning Optimizer and Detailed Schedul- ing Optimizer installed executables can be used by embedded PP/DS. After the Production Planning Optimizer and Detailed Scheduling Optimizer execut- ables and the required SAP Gateway components are installed in the standalone server, an RFC destination of type TCP/IP is created in the SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For the Produc- tion Planning Optimizer, the path of the corresponding optimizer executable for the Pro- duction Planning Optimizer is maintained in the technical settings of the RFC destination, as shown in Figure 3.57. Embedded PP/DS technically uses the SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization supply network planning (SNP) optimizer engine. So, in the Program path, you’ll notice that program is pointing to the SNP optimizer executable in the optimizer server. Figure 3.57 RFC Destination Settings for the Production Planning Optimizer Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Configuration 172 Similarly, for the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer, the program path should refer to the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Program file in the optimizer server, as shown in Figure 3.58. Figure 3.58 RFC Destination Settings for the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Note For further information, refer to the installation guide for the SAP SCM optimizer found at http://s-prs.co/v495100 . To create the RFC destination, execute Transaction SM59, and click on the Create but- ton. Enter a name for the destination in the RFC Destination field, and select the Con- nection Type as T – TCP/IP Connection .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Under the Technical Settings tab, select the Start on Explicit Host option under Activation Type . Enter the Target Host , which is the server in © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 173 3.9 Summary which the PP/DS optimizer is installed. In the Program field, enter the path of the PP/DS optimizer executable file in the PP/DS optimizer server. After the RFC destination is set up, the configuration of the PP/DS optimizer is main- tained under the Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Basic Settings  Optimization Basic Functions  Maintain Master Data for Optimization Server . In this Customizing transaction, click the New Entries button. Set the Dest. ID as “DPS01” and the Appl. as “DPS”, as shown in Figure 3.59 1 for the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If there are multiple PP/DS optimizer servers available, and you want to pri- oritize one of the servers, enter a number in the P (priority) field that is lower than the other entries. The entry with the lowest number in the P field gets the first preference when the embedded PP/DS application requests the connection to an PP/DS optimizer server. Similarly, for the Production Planning Optimizer, make an entry with Dest. ID as “PPO01” and the Appl. as “PPO” 2 . Figure 3.59 PP/DS Optimizer Technical Settings The maximum number of slots ( M ) determines how many CPU processing cores the PP/DS application can request at once when running an optimization operation.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In Fig- ure 3.59, the maximum number of slots is defined as “10”. Next, enter the RFC destina- tion that is created for the Production Planning Optimizer 3 and Detailed Scheduling Optimizer 4 , respectively, in the Communication Connection field. When you’re done, click the Save button to save the Production Planning Optimizer and Detailed Schedul- ing Optimizer settings. 3.9 Summary In this chapter, we covered in detail the activation and setup of embedded PP/DS, including the technical setup of the PP/DS optimizer.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Configuration 174 explicit activation and the SAP liveCache installed and set up on the SAP HANA data- base that the SAP S/4HANA system is connected to. For most of the transaction data, transfers between the ERP and PP/DS side of SAP S/4HANA don’t require an integration model. However, it internally uses the core interface framework to transfer the data, so the basic setup of the core interface is required in the SAP S/4HANA system. For PP/DS master data elements, the Customiz- ing is maintained under the advanced planning Customizing settings.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We also covered the important settings and profiles required to use the PP/DS applica- tion tools in embedded PP/DS, such as the order views and the detailed scheduling planning board. In the next chapter, we’ll cover the details of the transaction data in embedded PP/DS and how that data is transferred between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS. We’ll also cover how the transaction data is represented in embedded PP/DS, as well as the version management in PP/DS for simulating the master data changes and its impact on transaction data. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 175 Chapter 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data Part of the PP/DS setup is to configure the data transfer for transaction data to PP/DS. In this chapter, we’ll go through how each transaction data object is treated within PP/DS and cover any restrictions in inte- grating these objects. In this chapter, we’ll cover the important transaction data that is relevant for planning and scheduling in PP/DS for SAP S/4HANA (embedded PP/DS). We’ll discuss the data transfer methods for the transaction data and the representation of the PP/DS data for the corresponding SAP S/4HANA objects.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There are changes in the available enhancement points for the transaction data inte- gration in embedded PP/DS compared to the PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Plan- ning and Optimization. Wherever applicable, we’ll also cover some of the enhancement options available for the transaction data in this chapter. We’ll discuss the integration of in-house and external procurement orders, quality management (inspection lots), plant maintenance orders, and forecast elements in detail. 4.1 Activating the Integration of Transaction Data In embedded PP/DS, there is no integration model-based data transfer present for most of the transaction data objects that are based on a material number in PP/DS for planning and scheduling.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For these material-dependent objects, the activation of data transfer is performed in the Customizing settings as a one-time activity. For certain objects that are material independent, such as plant maintenance orders and network orders resulting from SAP S/4HANA project systems, the integration to PP/DS is based on an integration model. To activate the data transfer for the material-dependent objects, you can navigate to the Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Basic Settings  Set- tings for Data Transfer .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You’ll arrive at the screen shown in Figure 4.1, where the mate- rial-dependent objects list is displayed. Select the checkboxes for the objects you want to integrate the data from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS and vice versa. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 176 Figure 4.1 Activation of Transaction Data Transfer in Embedded PP/DS The activation alone won’t integrate all transaction data unless the material is acti- vated for advanced planning. If the material is flagged for advanced planning, then during the transaction data creation in SAP S/4HANA, the system checks for the PP/DS relevancy of that transaction data object from the Customizing setting and sends the data to embedded PP/DS. Even though there is no integration model present for the transfer, the SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS transfer internally uses the core inter- face queues to perform the transfer.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For planned orders, production orders, purchase requisitions, and purchase orders, the data updated in embedded PP/DS is simultaneously updated in SAP S/4HANA via a remote function call (RFC). So, for these objects, the transfer from embedded PP/DS to SAP S/4HANA doesn’t involve the core interface queue–based transfer, but a direct RFC. For the transfer from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS, if there are any problems encountered in embedded PP/DS during the transfer, the core interface queues will fail; these can be monitored and reprocessed if there are errors.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If core interface post- processing is activated, such transaction data queue failures are recorded in the post- processing (Transaction /SAPAPO/CPP) for manual analysis and reprocessing. Tip For the transaction data transfer from PP/DS to SAP S/4HANA, if there are failures due to locking issues, when postprocessing is activated, the locking failures are recorded in the postprocessing transaction (Transaction /SAPAPO/CPP). Scheduling program /SAPAPO/ CIF_POSTPROCESS in the background will automatically process all postprocessing records that are created due to locking transfer. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 177 4.2 Planned Independent Requirements In PP/DS, transaction data objects are internally treated as orders. In other words, the PP/DS system creates an object of type order in SAP liveCache, and the different objects, per their classification from SAP S/4HANA (e.g., sales orders, planned orders, etc.), are represented as order categories in SAP liveCache. Following are the transac- tion data objects that are treated internally as orders in PP/DS:  Stocks  Planned orders, production orders, process orders  Project orders, maintenance orders  Purchase requisitions, purchase orders  Inbound and outbound deliveries  Stock transport requisitions  Stock transfer reservations  Reservations  Sales orders  Planned independent requirements (PIRs) The stocks and sales orders always originate in SAP S/4HANA, and they can’t be changed in embedded PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Within PP/DS, the planned orders, purchase requisitions, stock transfer reservations, and requisitions can be created or changed by the PP/DS planning runs automatically or manually via any of the planning and scheduling tools. In PP/DS, the term manufacturing order is used to represent both the discrete manufac- turing production orders and the process industry process orders. In the Customizing setting, as shown earlier in Figure 4.1, when the transfer of Prod. Orders is activated, this also applies for the process orders.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The manufacturing orders and orders originating from SAP S/4HANA project systems (project orders) can be changed in embedded PP/DS depending on the order status (e.g., production orders with status “created” can be still changed in PP/DS), and the same is transferred to SAP S/4HANA. The purchase orders, reservations, plant maintenance orders, and quality management inspection lots are always transferred from SAP S/4HANA to PP/DS and can’t be changed in embedded PP/DS. These objects can only be changed in SAP S/4HANA. 4.2 Planned Independent Requirements Planned independent requirement (PIR) elements in SAP S/4HANA represent the demand quantity coming in from the forecasting process.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 178 standard delivered Business Application Programming Interfaces (BAPIs) or via inte- gration of the demand from the SAP Integrated Business Planning for Supply Chain (SAP IBP) system. PIRs are transferred to embedded PP/DS without an integration model and with the activation of the data transfer in Customizing. The PIR data can only be maintained in SAP S/4HANA. You can directly enter a forecast element in the PP/DS transactions, but these aren’t integrated back to SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In SAP S/4HANA, PIRs are managed in Transaction MD61 for creation and Transaction MD62 for change. As shown in Figure 4.2 on the bottom screen, the PIR is created in Transaction MD61, and the Reqmts type ( LSF ) is derived from the planning strategy ( Strategy Group 10 ) assigned to the material master in the top screen. Upon saving, the PIR element is transferred to embedded PP/DS. Figure 4.2 Creation of PIRs in SAP S/4HANA The requirement type for the planning strategy assigned to the material master is set in the Customizing settings in the SAP S/4HANA system under the Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Production Planning  Demand Management  Planned Indepen- dent Requirements  Planning Strategy  Define Strategy .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As shown in Figure 4.3, the requirement type for the PIRs is assigned to the strategy. The SAP S/4HANA planning strategy and the PP/DS requirements strategy are mapped by default during the transfer. The PIR quantities are consumed by incoming demand elements, such as dependent demand coming in from a higher-level material in the bill of materials (BOM) structure, sales order demand, stock transfer demand, and so on. The requirements strategy settings allow the incoming demand quantities to consume the PIR quantities.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The PIR quantities are reduced by the corresponding demand ele- ments, and the unconsumed demand can be deleted in periodic intervals. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 179 4.2 Planned Independent Requirements Figure 4.3 Requirement Strategy Settings in SAP S/4HANA The planning and requirements strategy between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS is mapped by default, as shown in Table 4.1. In embedded PP/DS, the PIR is represented as a forecast element in the planning tools such as product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3) or requirements view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP1). The forecast elements are shown as orders with the corresponding cat- egory and the quantity. As shown in Figure 4.4, the PIR element from SAP S/4HANA is represented as FC. req. (forecast requirement in embedded PP/DS).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Planning Strategy in SAP S/4HANA Requirements Strategy in PP/DS 10: Make to stock 10: Make to stock 40: Planning with final assembly 20: Planning with final assembly 50: Planning without final assembly 30, 35 (depending on material configurability): Plan- ning without final assembly 60: Planning with a planning material 40: Planning with planning product Table 4.1 Mapping of Planning Strategies Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 180 Figure 4.4 SAP S/4HANA PIRs Represented as Forecast Requirements in PP/DS Note The PIRs created from SAP S/4HANA can’t be changed from embedded PP/DS. These PIRs are managed in SAP S/4HANA in terms of periodic reorganization of the uncon- sumed PIRs. In PP/DS, Transaction /SAPAPO/MD74 can be used to delete the forecast elements (PIRs). When the forecast is consumed per the settings in the planning strategy in SAP S/4HANA and in PP/DS as well, the forecast consumption will be executed per the set- tings in the Proposed Strategy in the Advanced Planning view of the material master.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The example shown in Figure 4.5 shows that in PP/DS Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3 (Product View), the forecast quantity originally was 9,999 1 , and the sales order with quantity of 100 2 was created in SAP S/4HANA. When this sales order is integrated to PP/DS, it consumes the forecast (as the planning strategy in PP/DS is 20 – planning with final assembly), and the forecast quantity is reduced to 9,899 3 . © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 181 4.2 Planned Independent Requirements Figure 4.5 Forecast Consumption in PP/DS The details of the forecast quantity and the consumption can be displayed from the Forecast tab 4 of the product view transaction as shown in Figure 4.5. The consump- tion period that is set in the material master MRP3 view is also leveraged by PP/DS to determine the periods in the past and in the future 5 to consume forecasts, which is also shown in the product view Forecast tab. As shown in Figure 4.6, the forecast details and the consuming sales orders details can be displayed by clicking on the Forecast tab 1 and the Detail tab 2 within that tab.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The From and To Date fields are set per the PIR creation in SAP S/4HANA. For example, the quantity 3,333,000 forecast is valid from 12.12.2022 to 12.12.2022 . This is because the PIR is created in daily buckets in SAP S/4HANA. Similarly, the quantity 2,999,000 is valid for one week, as it’s created in weekly buckets in SAP S/4HANA, and the quantity 9,999,000 is valid for a month as it’s created in monthly buckets in SAP S/4HANA. The SAP S/4HANA PIR and the buckets 3 as displayed in Transaction MD63 to display the PIRs are also shown in Figure 4.6.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 182 Figure 4.6 Forecast Consumption Details in PP/DS and Forecast Buckets in SAP S/4HANA 4.3 Planned Orders Planned orders are the procurement element for the in-house production of materials. Planned orders can be created manually and automatically by the system during a pro- duction planning run. As planned orders are proposals and not confirmed orders, they can be created and changed both in SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS. If a material is activated for advanced planning, and the Customizing for the advanced planning transaction data transfer is activated for planned orders, the planned orders are transferred between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS as soon as they are cre- ated or changed.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As the planning tools available in SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS can change the planned orders during the planning run, it’s recommended to set the material requirements planning (MRP) type as X0 (without MRP, with BOM explosion) in the material master, so that the classic MRP runs in SAP S/4HANA don’t create or change planned orders, and only the PP/DS planning (as part of MRP Live or PP/DS planning runs) is responsible for planning the material. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 183 4.3 Planned Orders A planned order comprises basic information necessary to manufacture a product, such as the quantity to be produced, the start and end date of the order, and the com- ponents required to manufacture the product. In SAP S/4HANA, a planned order uses the production version (BOM and routing) to derive the components from the master data, and the dates can be entered manually or can be determined by the planning tools according to the demand date and other con- straints supplied to the planning tools.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Planned orders can be created or changed in SAP S/4HANA via Transaction MD11 or Transaction MD12. A planned order in SAP S/4HANA is shown in Figure 4.7. The End date was manually entered, and the Start date was derived using the in-house production duration from the material master. The GR Processing Time is also copied from the material master to the order. The Firming section’s checkboxes determine if the order can be changed by the system automatically or not. If the order is set by choosing the Planned Order checkbox under Firming , the system can’t change or delete the order.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: All the data is sent to embedded PP/DS from the SAP S/4HANA planned order after you save the planned order by clicking on the Save button. Figure 4.7 Planned Order in SAP S/4HANA Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 184 In embedded PP/DS, the planned order is represented with the following three major elements:  Receipts This is the output of the planned order (the header material in the SAP S/4HANA planned order).  Requirements These components are required to produce the material (derived from the produc- tion data structure [PDS] master data in PP/DS).  Operations These are the operations and activities, the resources in which the activities are per- formed, and the calculated duration of these activities derived from the PDS master data.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The planned orders can be displayed or changed in embedded PP/DS using the product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3) or other planning tools. As shown in Figure 4.8, the header information of the planned order is displayed on the right side of the screen, and the Receipts , Requirements , and Operations /activities are displayed on the left side in the tree structure. Figure 4.8 Planned Order in PP/DS The goods receipt (GR) processing time from SAP S/4HANA is created as an activity in the PP/DS planned order, and the inbound handling resource assigned to the location master data is used for this activity. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 185 4.3 Planned Orders The status, like the firming indicator, is also transferred to the PP/DS order. The Sched.Status is determined by the integration strategy maintained in the PP/DS global settings in Customizing. The source of supply for the planned order is selected during the transfer of the planned order in embedded PP/DS, and the selected PDS is used as the Supply Source . The component and operations are derived from the explosion of the PDS master data. The transfer of the planned order from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS internally uses the core interface queue mechanism, so if any problems are encountered during the planned order creation in embedded PP/DS, the core interface queues will fail.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If core interface postprocessing is activated, the queue will be recorded in the post- processing Transaction /SAPAPO/CPP. The transfer of the PP/DS planned order to SAP S/4HANA is done synchronously via an RFC, so if the system encounters any problems in creating the planned order in SAP S/4HANA during the transfer from embedded PP/DS, the corresponding error is logged in PP/DS, and the system stops the change from being saved in PP/DS. When new planned orders are created or existing planned orders are changed/deleted in a background planning run, if there are failures in creating or changing the planned orders in SAP S/4HANA, the planned order will be recorded in the postprocessing transaction.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If there are multiple materials planned at once, and one of the planned orders goes into an error during transfer to SAP S/4HANA, all the planned orders being transferred are recorded in the postprocessing queue. To create a planned order in embedded PP/DS manually, you can use the product view for the product and location. In the product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3), enter planning version “000” in the Plng Version field, enter the Product and Location infor- mation, and press (Enter) to navigate to the Product View screen.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Then, click on the Change button to use the product view in change mode, enter a quantity in the Rec/ ReqQty column and a date for the order in the Avail/ReqD column, and the system will generate a planned order, as shown in Figure 4.9, assigning a PP/DS planned order number. Upon saving the product view, it’s transferred to SAP S/4HANA, and the SAP S/4HANA planned order number is updated back in PP/DS. You can use the Refresh button on the screen to refresh the data displayed in the product view. The system decides the order type (planned order or purchase requisition) based on the procure- ment type of the material.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For in-house produced materials, the system will generate a planned order; for externally procured materials, a purchase requisition will be cre- ated. You can enhance the integration of the planned orders using customer exits and busi- ness add-ins (BAdIs) delivered in the SAP S/4HANA system. Some of the important enhancement options are as follows:  BADI /SAPAPO/CL_EX_CIF_IP This is the embedded PP/DS order inbound BAdI enhancement, which includes the following methods to influence the data transferred: Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 186 – ORDER_INB_MODIFY_AFTER_MERGE : Adjustment of PP/DS Data After Comparison with Core Interface Data – ORDER_INB_REDET_DATES_DECIDE : Decision to Adopt Activity Dates/Times per Order – ORDER_INB_PROCESSING_DECIDE : Decision for Quantity Adjustment and Fixing of Activities – ORDER_INB_REL_X_CHANGE : Adjustment of X Fields for the Relationships – ORDER_INB_MRPDS_BLK_RELEVANCE : Decision to Enable Block Planning for Order Figure 4.9 Creating a Planned Order in PP/DS  BADI /SAPAPO/RRP_SRC_EXIT This BAdI enhancement can be used to influence the source of supply determina- tion within PP/DS when orders are transferred from SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This BAdI has the following methods: – RRP_USEX_PLAN_PUBLISH : Publication of the Plan before Characteristic Propagation – RRP_USEX_SOURCE_FILTER : Restriction of the Selection of the Source of Supply – RRP_USEX_PLORD_CREATE : Planned Order about to Be Created, Scheduling in SAP liveCache – RRP_USEX_CHECK_MATLOC : Check Whether the Planning Is Allowed for Product © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 187 4.4 Production Orders – RRP_USEX_PEGAREA_GET_DATA : Gather Necessary Info for Creating Pegging Areas in LC – RRP_USEX_SOURCING_DATE : Source of Supply - Determination Date – RRP_USEX_IO_NODES_FILTER : Filtering IO Nodes before Forecast Consumption – RRP_USEX_IO_NODES_GET : Determining Filtered IO Nodes for Forecast Consumption – RRP_USEX_IO_NODES_CHANGE : Changing Data for Forecast Consumption – RRP_USEX_PUSH_OTHER_PLANT : Decide If Output Node Should Be Created in Planning Plant – RRP_USEX_UPDATE_GT_PLAN_NOW : Decide If Planning Run or Planning File Entry – RRP_USEX_PURREQ_CREATE : Purchase Requisition Creation – RRP_USEX_SOURCE_REEXPLODE : Restriction of the Selection of the SoS to be Reex- ploded – RRP_USEX_COLLECT_EVENTS : Collect the Events for the Order Transfer to the SAP ERP System – RRP_USEX_PUBLISH_EVENTS : Allow Publication of Orders to the SAP ERP System  CIFORD03 and CIFORD01 These two user exits can be used in SAP S/4HANA inbound when orders are trans- ferred from PP/DS to SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The order type and order data can be influenced using these user exits.  CIFORD02 This user exit can be used to enhance the order data with any custom fields in the planned orders that need to be passed over to PP/DS. 4.4 Production Orders Production orders are the executable in-house manufacturing orders used to instruct the shop floor to perform the manufacturing activities. In discrete industries, the term production order is used, and, in process industries, the term process order is used. There are functional differences between these orders in SAP S/4HANA, but, in PP/DS, for planning and general scheduling purposes, both the production orders and process orders are treated the same.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Production orders can be created manually from SAP S/4HANA or can be created via the conversion of a planned order into a production order. The Conv. Ind. checkbox can be set in SAP S/4HANA and in embedded PP/DS or by using the unified conversion report for both SAP S/4HANA and PP/DS planned orders. For the PP/DS planned orders, it’s recommended to set the Conv. Ind. checkbox from within embedded PP/DS, use the unified conversion transaction (Transaction /SAPAPO/ PROD_ORD_CNV), or use the SAP menu path, Logistics  Production  MRP  Planned Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 188 Order  Convert to Production Order  Batch Conversion of Planned for Adv Planning  Pro- duction Order Conversion . This transaction can be used for planned orders created in SAP S/4HANA or in embedded PP/DS for materials relevant to advanced planning . After the Conv. Ind. checkbox is set, the planned order is converted into a production order, and the information (e.g., material, dates, quantity, and selected master data [production version]) is used for creating the production order.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The production order is then also transferred to embedded PP/DS. To set the Conv. Ind. checkbox for the planned order from the PP/DS product view, exe- cute Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3 to arrive at the screen shown in Figure 4.10. Then, select the Conv. Ind checkbox, and save the data by clicking the Save button. After the Conv. Ind. checkbox is set and saved, the production order is created and updated in PP/DS. You can refresh the product view using the Update button on the screen, which will display the production order number as shown in the bottom of the screen in Fig- ure 4.10.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 4.10 Conversion of a Planned Order in the PP/DS Product View The creation of a production order is a transfer without a queue, so if issues are encoun- tered in SAP S/4HANA during the creation of the production order, they are logged in PP/DS, and the order conversion is terminated in embedded PP/DS. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 189 4.4 Production Orders A production order object in SAP S/4HANA has all the components and operations derived from the production version (BOM, routing), and the component materials of the production order, which are activated for advanced planning, are only available in embedded PP/DS for further planning. In addition, only the operations of the produc- tion order, which has resources relevant to PP/DS, are available in the PP/DS planning and scheduling tools. After the planned order Conv. Ind. checkbox is set in embedded PP/DS, the production order is created in SAP S/4HANA, and then the production order is transferred to embedded PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The transfer of the production order to embedded PP/DS may change the production order dates in embedded PP/DS because of the scheduling of the production order. This change is also sent back to SAP S/4HANA. These changes are reflected in SAP S/4HANA with the production order status. This sequence of change is illustrated in Figure 4.11. Figure 4.11 Production Order Conversion: Data Transfer between the ERP Side and Embedded PP/DS Side in SAP S/4HANA For the retransfer to be performed by embedded PP/DS to SAP S/4HANA for orders, the Customizing settings needs to be created in Transaction /SAPAPO/CP3 in the SAP S/4HANA system for in-house production.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, the retransfer settings are rele- vant for external procurement orders. The production orders created by setting the Conv. Ind. checkbox in embedded PP/DS are set with the statuses EXPL External Conv.of Planned Order and EXTS Changed by external system , as shown in Figure 4.12. Planned order (set with conversion flag) Production order created Planned order deleted Production order created Planned order deleted Production order scheduling Production order updated with PP/DS scheduling dates, status SAP S/4HANA (ERP side) SAP S/4HANA (PP/DS side) Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 190 Figure 4.12 Status of Production Orders Converted from PP/DS The operations scheduled by PP/DS are set with the operation system Status as DSEX . The changes in production order with respect to the quantity and dates are transferred from SAP S/4HANA to embedded PP/DS. If there are any date changes performed by the PP/DS scheduling tools, those are also updated back to SAP S/4HANA in the produc- tion order. When a production order has the SAP S/4HANA status CRTD – Created , it can be deleted in the PP/DS transactions.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This will set the Deletion checkbox in SAP S/4HANA for the production order and set the status DLFL – Deletion Flag . After the order is released in SAP S/4HANA (status REL ), the order can’t be deleted in embedded PP/DS. The production order confirmations are created using transactions such as Transaction CO11N or Transaction CO15 when the production orders are executed in the shop floor to produce the products. After the production orders are confirmed in SAP S/4HANA, the status is updated in embedded PP/DS, as shown in Figure 4.13.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, the quantity reduction of the production order due to GR posted against the production order in SAP S/4HANA is transferred to embedded PP/DS. If the produc- tion order is in a future date and a confirmation is posted on an earlier date, the pro- duction order in embedded PP/DS will be rescheduled to the confirmation date. This rescheduling can be stopped by certain enhancements, if required. After the production orders are confirmed in SAP S/4HANA, the status checkboxes of Partially Confirmed and Started are set in embedded PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 191 4.5 External Procurement Orders scheduling tools. To do any scheduling changes in the system, the production order needs to be set with an interrupt action in the scheduling tools, such as the detailed scheduling planning board where the Interrupt option is available on the context menu of the production order.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 4.13 Production Order Status in SAP S/4HANA and in Embedded PP/DS If the production order is set with any of the following statuses in SAP S/4HANA, the order is deleted from embedded PP/DS:  DLV – Delivered The full order quantity is delivered.  TECO – Technically Completed The order is technically completed in SAP S/4HANA.  DLFL – Deletion Flag The order is set with a Deletion checkbox.  CLSD – Closed The order is set with the Close checkbox in SAP S/4HANA. 4.5 External Procurement Orders External procurement orders are for procuring materials from a vendor or from another plant (stock transfers). The procurement data transfer is activated via the same basic settings for advanced planning in Customizing.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Activating the purchase orders and purchase requisitions in Customizing will activate the transfer of the following objects between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS:  Purchase orders  Purchase requisitions Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 192  Online transactional processing (OLTP) scheduling agreement delivery schedules  Advanced shipping notifications (ASNs) and purchase order acknowledgements The external procurement proposals, such as the purchase requisitions and stock transfer requisitions, can be created in embedded PP/DS manually or automatically by a production planning run (see Chapter 5, Section 5.5). When the orders are created manually in embedded PP/DS, if there are multiple sources of supply valid for the order, the system interactively provides an option to select the source of supply, as shown in Figure 4.14.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the Admissible Sources of Supply section, you can check the applicable sources for your order. During the automatic planning run in PP/DS, the system will select the source of supply with the minimal delay in fulfilling the demand. Figure 4.14 Manual Creation of External Procurement Order and Source of Supply Selection in PP/DS If there is a GR processing time maintained in the material master, an activity is created in the purchase requisition for scheduling this time. This activity won’t be transferred to SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Only the dates and the quantity are transferred to SAP S/4HANA. The structure of the purchase requisition in PP/DS has the receipts, which represent the materials ordered in the requisition. If GR processing is involved, a GR activity is created in the order. Expand the Activities node in the left panel of the screen, and dou- ble-click the Process Goods Recpt activity to navigate to the GR activity, as shown in Fig- ure 4.15. Click the Save button to save the purchase requisition. For subcontracting purchase requisitions, the order will have the list of components to be provided to the vendor under the Requirements section of the purchase requisition.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 193 4.5 External Procurement Orders in PP/DS, the purchase requisition will also have a Requirements section in PP/DS that will show requirements created for the material in the sending location ( Plant ). Figure 4.15 Purchase Requisition in PP/DS Similar to planned orders, from the product view, select the Conv. Ind. checkbox for purchase requisitions. Depending on the type of source of supply selected in the pur- chase requisition, the following types of orders for external procurement can be cre- ated:  Purchasing info record: Purchase order  Scheduling line agreement: Schedule line  Contract: Purchase order with assignment to contract In SAP S/4HANA, if a release procedure is in place for purchase requisition approval, the purchase requisition conversion must be executed in SAP S/4HANA because purchase order creation from the Conv.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Ind. checkbox set in embedded PP/DS will fail if the pur- chase requisition isn’t completely released in SAP S/4HANA. In addition, if the SAP S/4HANA procurement process requires multiple purchase req- uisitions to be consolidated into one purchase order, conversion of the purchase requi- sitions to a purchase order should be executed in SAP S/4HANA. Setting the Conv. Ind. checkbox in embedded PP/DS will create one purchase order per purchase requisition. There could be a GR posted against the purchase order in SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This will update the stock in PP/DS and will reduce the purchase order quantity in PP/DS accord- ingly. When the purchase order is fully delivered or if the purchase order line is deleted, the same is also replicated to PP/DS. When there are ASNs received from vendors for the purchase orders, those may be entered as inbound delivery documents in the SAP S/4HANA system. As shown in Figure Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 194 4.16, when inbound deliveries are created for the purchase order 1 , the quantity for which the inbound delivery is created as an ASN 2 in PP/DS, and the remaining quantity on the purchase order will be also displayed as an additional line in PP/DS product view. Figure 4.16 ASNs in the SAP S/4HANA Purchase Order and in PP/DS 4.6 Stocks and Batches The inventory data in SAP S/4HANA includes the stocks and the associated batches. The stock information is transferred to embedded PP/DS along with the batch information if the material is batch managed.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The stocks are maintained at the plant level, and, for planning purposes, the stock is considered at the MRP area level in SAP S/4HANA if an MRP area is assigned to the plant. The plant-level stock will be transferred as the stock to the PP/DS plant location, and the stocks at the MRP area in SAP S/4HANA are transferred to the MRP area loca- tion in embedded PP/DS. The batch associated with the stock is transferred to embed- ded PP/DS; they are referred to as versions in the PP/DS planning tools. The concept of stock update counters was introduced in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization for improving the performance of the core interface transfer of inven- tory data and to avoid inconsistencies in the stock data being updated by a queue with older values of stocks.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In embedded PP/DS, the stock update counters are activated by default and can’t be turned off. The stock data transferred to embedded PP/DS uses the relative stocks, which refers to the delta between the current stock and the stock to be © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 195 4.6 Stocks and Batches received or issued. The initial transfer of stock can be triggered by the core interface reconciliation tool (Transaction /SAPAPO/CCR) or the initial transfer report (Transac- tion /SAPAPO/PPDS_DELTA_ORD_TRANS). Whenever a stock posting happens in SAP S/4HANA, it’s immediately transferred to embedded PP/DS, along with its batch and storage location information. The stocks maintained in special scenarios, such as stock assigned to customers in make-to-order (MTO) scenarios, are also transferred to PP/DS and displayed under the customer segment in the PP/DS product view.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The stocks are also represented as an order in PP/DS with the category “CC”. As shown in Figure 4.17, the batch information displayed in SAP S/4HANA from Transaction MMBE for the material and plant is repre- sented in the PP/DS product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3) as versions. Figure 4.17 PP/DS Representation of Stocks with Batch Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 196 The Version column in the product view is the name of the batch from SAP S/4HANA, and the sublocation ( Subloc. column) is the corresponding storage location in SAP S/4HANA. If the MRP area is associated with the storage location, the stock will be dis- played only in the MRP area location (location type 1007 – storage location MRP area) in PP/DS. Note As the stock update counters (generation of generic queue names for stock queues, e.g., CFSTWO90Y2Z2W5Z997CACGC0, instead of the material number reference in the queue name) are used by embedded PP/DS by default, you can use ABAP program /SAPAPO/STOCKUC_REORG to delete the obsolete stock update counters from embed- ded PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can also use ABAP program RCIFSTCKUCDEL in SAP S/4HANA to delete the obsolete stock update counters. In SAP S/4HANA, the update counters are created for material and plant combination, so this report in the SAP S/4HANA side need not be executed very frequently. The stock and batch data always originates from SAP S/4HANA, and these elements can’t be changed in PP/DS. The stock elements in PP/DS can be locally deleted using ABAP program /SAPAPO/DELETE_STOCK for reasons such as inconsistencies needing correction. The deletion of the stock using this program isn’t transferred back to SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For an inactive planning version in PP/DS, if you want to delete the stocks to simulate different planning situations, the same ABAP program can be used to delete the stock elements in PP/DS. 4.7 Inspection Lots Inspection lots in SAP S/4HANA are created in the quality management process. The inspection lot data includes the quantity, material, and plant. In the SAP S/4HANA sys- tem, the quantity under inspection is considered quality stock. In embedded PP/DS, for materials and plants for which advanced planning is activated, the inspection lot is transferred to embedded PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Within PP/DS, the inspection lots are represented as an order with receipt, but not as a stock element. In PP/DS, the inspection lot will have only one receipt that corresponds to the material and location assigned to the inspection lot in SAP S/4HANA. No activities or requirements are attached to the inspection lot order in embedded PP/DS. In SAP S/4HANA, the inspection lot is usually linked to an order (e.g., a production order) during in-process inspection, to a purchase order during procurement GR inspection, or to a sales order.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This linkage isn’t sent to PP/DS. Only the release status of the inspection lot is transferred to embedded PP/DS. The inspection lot in SAP S/4HANA (inspection lot displayed from Transaction QA03) and the same in PP/DS (the inspection lot displayed as QM lot in the product view) are shown in Figure 4.18. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 197 4.7 Inspection Lots The inspection lot is represented as an order in embedded PP/DS with an order cate- gory of BU – Insp Lot; this is represented as the QM lot in the Category column in the product view, as shown in the bottom screen of Figure 4.18. The inspection lot order is deleted from embedded PP/DS when the inspection quantity is set to 0, the usage deci- sion is posted, the stock is moved to unrestricted quantity, or the inspection lot is can- celed in SAP S/4HANA. Figure 4.18 Inspection Lots in SAP S/4HANA and Embedded PP/DS In PP/DS, the inspection lot can’t be changed or deleted.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Its date and output are fixed by default, as shown in Figure 4.19 (see the Date Fixed and Output Firmed checkboxes), so that PP/DS planning runs don’t change the inspection lots. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 198 Tip In embedded PP/DS, all the receipt elements are set with a time stamp so that they can be pegged by the requirement elements with the allowed pegging interval. As the inspection lot doesn’t have a time in SAP S/4HANA, it’s set with a time of 00:00:00 on the inspection lot start and end date. You can change this time stamp via user exit QAPO0003 . Figure 4.19 Inspection Lot Represented as an Order with Date/Output Firmed in PP/DS 4.8 Maintenance Orders Plant maintenance orders in SAP S/4HANA are used for planning and executing the maintenance activities on the equipment and assets in the plant.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Maintenance orders can be created for preventive or malfunction maintenance. The maintenance orders in SAP S/4HANA can contain material components required for the maintenance and also operations required to perform the maintenance activ- ity. These activities are scheduled in the maintenance work center. The equipment being worked on can be represented by the functional location, which can be assigned with a production resource or work center going through the maintenance activity. In PP/DS, the maintenance order is only considered for the requirements generated by the maintenance order due to material components assigned to the order that are rel- evant to advanced planning.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To block the availability of the resource on which the maintenance is being performed, a downtime can be created in the resource master © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 199 4.8 Maintenance Orders data. This blocks the resource capacity for consumption by any planned orders or pro- duction orders, and any orders scheduled on the resource during this time will be rescheduled by the system. For integrating the plant maintenance order to embedded PP/DS, an integration model needs to be created and activated because the plant maintenance order is a material- independent transaction data object. As shown in Figure 4.20, you can create an inte- gration model using Transaction CFM1 and activate the integration model from Trans- action CFM2 (refer to our discussion in Chapter 2, Section 2.1).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Select the Maint. Order checkbox, and click the Special Restrictions button next to the Maint. Order field to enter the Order Type and Plant of the maintenance orders for which the integration model is being created. When maintenance orders are created on production resources, they can’t be available for production for the duration of the maintenance. The unavailability of resources for reasons such as maintenance is referred to as downtimes in PP/DS. Figure 4.20 Creation of an Integration Model for Plant Maintenance Orders Maintenance orders are created in Transaction IW31.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For the plant maintenance orders to create downtime on the PP/DS resources, the following prerequisites must be met:  The resource on which the maintenance is performed and on which the resource downtime creation is expected in PP/DS should be assigned to the functional loca- tion or the equipment entered in the maintenance order, as shown in Figure 4.21. The functional location is defined in Transaction IL01 by entering the work center Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 200 name in the Work center field 1 . In the maintenance order, enter the functional location in the Func. Loc. field 2 .  The maintenance order should be assigned with a system condition field ( SystCond. ) 3 , which is marked by the active checkbox in the Reservatn column 4 (production work center reserved by plant maintenance) in the System Condition selection options screen, as shown in Figure 4.21. Figure 4.21 Prerequisites for the Plant Maintenance Order to Create PP/DS Resource Downtime The components entered in the maintenance order are transferred to embedded PP/DS as reservations if the components are marked as active for advanced planning.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These reservations can’t be changed in embedded PP/DS and are always managed by SAP S/4HANA transactions such as goods issue (GI) so the order from the reservation will update the quantity in embedded PP/DS. As shown in Figure 4.22, the component reservation is represented in embedded PP/DS with an order object that is input firmed, date firmed without any receipt elements, and can’t be edited or deleted from embedded PP/DS. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 201 4.8 Maintenance Orders Figure 4.22 Plant Maintenance Order Components in SAP S/4HANA and Embedded PP/DS After the component is completely issued to the order, or the maintenance order is closed, the reservation is deleted from embedded PP/DS. As plant maintenance orders aren’t dependent on materials, the reports to retransfer the PP/DS orders can’t be used to transfer individual maintenance orders. The complete retransfer can be triggered by executing reactivation of the integration model, which is defined on the basis of the maintenance order types.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The operations in the plant maintenance order hold the information of the resource, which is used to perform the maintenance task and the duration of the work. The start date/time and end date/time are calculated based on the scheduling calculations. The start time and end times of the maintenance order can be displayed from the Opera- tions tab of the maintenance order, as shown in Figure 4.23. The Earl.start (early start date) and Earl.star (early start time) columns have the start date and time of the main- tenance operation, and the EarliestEn (earliest end date) and Earliest (earliest finish time) columns show the end time of the maintenance operation.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The start and end times of the operation are used for calculating the downtimes in the PP/DS resource, as shown on the lower part of Figure 4.23. The downtimes of the resource in PP/DS can be displayed from the resource master data using Transac- tion /SAPAPO/RES01. Enter the Resource name and Location , and press (Enter) . Then, navigate to the Downtimes tab. Here, you’ll see an entry with the value PM order in the Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 202 Type of Downtime column. If you want to change the data transferred to embedded PP/DS from SAP S/4HANA, the BAdI BADI_CIF_PM_ORDER can be used in SAP S/4HANA, and the BAdI /SAPAPO/MNT_INBOUND can be used in embedded PP/DS. Figure 4.23 Maintenance Order Creating Downtime in the PP/DS Resource Tip The PP/DS resource downtimes created by SAP S/4HANA maintenance orders can be listed by using report /SAPAPO/MNT_DOWNTIMES_FIND. 4.9 Sales Orders Sales orders are the objects in SAP S/4HANA that represent the orders entered to fulfill customer requirements.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The sales order can also have configurable materials for which the configuration of the product is entered at the time of order entry. Depending on the planning strategy of the material in SAP S/4HANA, sales orders can be created in the make-to-stock (MTS) segment or make-to-order (MTO) segment. The sales orders will consume the PIR quantities at the time of order entry or at the time of delivery, depending on the consumption strategy assigned to the planning strategy. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 203 4.9 Sales Orders Sales orders are transferred to embedded PP/DS for the materials that are activated for advanced planning. The MTO sales orders will be created in the customer order seg- ment in PP/DS. For configurable materials, the configuration entered during the order entry is transferred to the PP/DS sales order, which can be used by PP/DS in planning. The activation of the sales order transfer is set in Customizing for advanced planning, and no integration model is required for sales orders.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Activating the sales order data transfer in Customizing also activates the following transaction data:  Sales orders  Deliveries  Quotations  Customer-independent requirements Depending on the configuration schema set for the PP/DS system, the characteristics assigned to the sales order items are considered by the planning tools in PP/DS to fulfill the demand by supply elements with the same configuration. In PP/DS, the material and location combination creates an object called the pegging area . The pegging area is also created in SAP liveCache and is the unique identifier for the location and material in the SAP liveCache level.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For MTS materials, the pegging area is at the material/location level, and for MTO materials, the individual sales orders, material, and location make up the pegging area. In PP/DS tools such as the product view, the sales order for MTO materials is shown under the corresponding segment (pegging areas), as shown in Figure 4.24. In the product view when there are multiple planning segments present, they are displayed on the left side of the screen under the Planning Segments panel. In the MTO scenario, the planning segments are displayed as shown in Figure 4.24 1 .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the MTS scenario, there is only one planning area, which rep- resents the product and location 2 . Apart from the material, location, quantity, and customer segment for the MTO scenar- ios, another important piece of information that sales orders bring into PP/DS is the order priority. Order priorities are used by PP/DS scheduling tools (e.g., detailed sched- uling heuristics) and by the PP/DS optimizer to avoid delays in scheduling receipts for the sales orders with higher priorities. In PP/DS, the order priority can be entered man- ually or can be automatically derived from the sales order or the priority set in the material master.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The order priority can be entered in the sales order item and transferred to embedded PP/DS. During PP/DS planning, the order priority of the sales order can be propagated to the receipt elements, such as planned orders, and then to the production orders. The source of the order priority is defined in the model version master data configura- tion in Transaction /SAPAPO/MVM. The options for setting the order priority determi- nation were already covered in Chapter 3, Section 3.2.1. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 204 Figure 4.24 MTO versus MTS Sales Orders in PP/DS If the model/version master data is set with the option 0 – In Make to Order from Sales Order Otherwise from Product for the order priority, the MTO segment planned orders derive the priority from the sales order priority. The sales order priority can be set in the sales order (Transaction VA02) item details via the Shipping tab in the Delivery Prior. field. The sales order priority is copied to the planned order and is displayed in the Priority column of the product view, as shown in Figure 4.25.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If the model/version master data is set with option 0 – In Make to Order from Sales Order Otherwise from Product , and the planning scenario is MTS, the order priority is derived from the priority set in the material master. In the material master (Transac- tion MM02), navigate to the Advanced Planning tab, and under the Proc./PPDS section, enter the priority in the Priority field. The same is copied to the planned order. The planned order priority can be displayed in the product view under the Priority column in the Elements tab, as shown in Figure 4.26.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Note In PP/DS orders, the priority value can range from 0 to 255, with 1 as the highest prior- ity, and 255 as the lowest priority. Value 0 or no value is treated as 255, which is the low- est priority. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 205 4.9 Sales Orders Figure 4.25 Order Priority in the MTO Scenario Figure 4.26 Order Priority in MTS: Derivation from the Product Master Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 206 Materials with MTS planning strategies, where the PIRs aren’t consumed by the sales order (e.g., planning strategy 10 in SAP S/4HANA) at the time of the sales order creation, are set with the Not relevant for pegging checkbox in embedded PP/DS. In addition, these orders can’t participate in planning runs. The requirement quantity from such sales orders isn’t considered for the calculation of the net requirement of the material location. Only the PIRs are considered for the net requirement calculation for such materials.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The sales order requirements with Not relevant for pegging selected aren’t pegged with any receipt element and are displayed in PP/DS transactions for informa- tion purpose. When deliveries are created against the sales order and in planning strategies where the deliveries can consume the PIRs, the PIR consumption and the deliveries are trans- ferred to embedded PP/DS. When outbound deliveries are created for the sales order, the same is also transferred to PP/DS. As shown in Figure 4.27, an outbound delivery quantity of 20 1 was created for the sales order with a total quantity of 100.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this case, in PP/DS, the sales order quantity is reduced by the outbound delivery quantity, so the sales order quantity is shown as 80 2 , and the outbound delivery element in PP/DS carries the 20 quantity 3 . Figure 4.27 Outbound Delivery in SAP S/4HANA and PP/DS © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 207 4.10 Production Campaign 4.10 Production Campaign Production campaign is a process within production planning for process industries, and campaigns are used to avoid unnecessary product changes on the same produc- tion line. Often such a change of product on production lines requires longer setup or cleaning activities. We’ll cover the details of production campaign planning within PP/DS in Chapter 8, Section 8.6. The production campaign can be created manually using Transaction /SAPAPO/PCMT, using the detailed scheduling planning board, or using the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Production campaigns are created and multiple planned orders are assigned to them in a way that there is no need to perform any setup or cleaning activities between manu- facturing the products of these process orders. The setup order is placed at the start of the campaign, and the cleanup order is placed at the end of the campaign. The production campaign is planned and created in PP/DS and transferred to SAP S/4HANA. When the planned orders are converted to process orders, the process orders remain in the same campaign as well.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Within PP/DS, production campaigns are only relevant to planning, but in SAP S/4HANA, the campaign data is also relevant for costing and settlement of the costs from the process orders. So, in SAP S/4HANA, the production campaigns must be available until the process orders are completed and cost settlement is executed. As shown in Figure 4.28, the production campaign is created using Transaction / SAPAPO/PCMT and saved. Upon save, the production campaign is saved with a PP/DS campaign number 1 and is transferred to SAP S/4HANA along with the order assign- ment 2 .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The SAP S/4HANA campaign number is updated back as an external campaign number ( Ext. Camp. No. ) 3 in the PP/DS campaign. In SAP S/4HANA, the campaign can be displayed using Transaction PCA3. Figure 4.28 Production Campaigns in PP/DS and in SAP S/4HANA Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 208 4.11 Transaction Data with Flexible Integration Flexible integration is the ability to define how SAP S/4HANA transaction data is inte- grated with PP/DS and what kind of changes are allowed or not allowed for the transac- tion data within PP/DS, which is determined in the Scope Limitation field in the Advanced Planning tab of the material master. We’ve already discussed the basic con- cept of this scope limitation in Chapter 2, Section 2.3. In this section, we’ll cover how the transaction data behaves with the different scope limitation options.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Following are the scope limitation options and how they influence the transaction data within PP/DS:  1 PP/DS Display Only With this scope limitation, as shown in Figure 4.29 1 , all the transaction data is transferred to PP/DS, including in-house and external procurement orders. But within PP/DS, no change is allowed for any of the transaction data, including any manual or automated planning/scheduling runs changing the transaction data. All the transaction data changes are managed within SAP S/4HANA with this scope lim- itation.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the product view in PP/DS (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3), in change mode, all the transaction data is available in display only mode 2 . The scope limitation configuration is already discussed in Chapter 2, Section 2.3. Figure 4.29 Scope Limitation: 1 PP/DS Display Only © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 209 4.11 Transaction Data with Flexible Integration  2 PP/DS Restricted for Inhouse Only With this scope limitation as shown in Figure 4.30 1 , all the transaction data, includ- ing in-house and external procurement orders, is integrated to PP/DS. However, within PP/DS, only the in-house procurement elements (planned orders and manu- facturing orders with certain statuses) can be changed, and automated or interactive planning 2 and scheduling can create and change existing in-house procurement orders. The external procurement elements, such as purchase requirements, are respected as valid procurement elements for planning but can’t be changed or deleted either manually 3 or via automated planning runs.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, in interac- tive or automated planning runs, only the heuristics, which is part of the scope pro- file 4 defined in the material master, is allowed within PP/DS. Figure 4.30 Scope Limitation: 2 PP/DS Restricted for Inhouse Only  3 PP/DS Restricted As shown in Figure 4.31 1 , with this scope limitation, all transaction data is inte- grated to PP/DS from SAP S/4HANA. Within PP/DS, manual change is allowed for in- house 2 and external procurement 3 elements. However, for automated planning runs, it’s only possible to execute heuristics that are part of the scope profile 4 .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If you attempt to execute a heuristic that isn’t part of the scope profile, an error is raised, and the execution of the heuristics will be terminated 5 . Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 210 Figure 4.31 Scope Limitation: 3 PP/DS Restricted  4 PP/DS Entire Scope for Inhouse Only With this scope limitation option shown in Figure 4.32 1 , all the in-house and exter- nal procurement elements are integrated from SAP S/4HANA to PP/DS. Figure 4.32 Scope Limitation: 4 PP/DS Entire Scope for Inhouse Only © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 211 4.12 Initial Transfer and Retransfer of Transaction Data to PP/DS But within PP/DS, only the in-house procurement elements 2 can be changed man- ually or through automated planning and scheduling runs. There is no limitation applied for the possible list of heuristics that can be executed. In addition, all the automated planning and scheduling runs can only create/change/delete in-house procurement elements. The external procurement elements 3 are in display only mode in PP/DS and considered as a valid receipt in the planning runs.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: With no scope limitation set in the material master, all the transaction data will be integrated to PP/DS from SAP S/4HANA, and no restrictions are applied within PP/DS. Manual and automated planning runs can create/change/delete both in-house and external procurement orders in PP/DS. 4.12 Initial Transfer and Retransfer of Transaction Data to PP/DS In an operational SAP S/4HANA system where your logistics and manufacturing pro- cesses are already being leveraged, if you decide to activate PP/DS and set the Advanced Planning flag for materials, you’ll need to do an initial transfer of the transaction data from SAP S/4HANA to PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, in cases where you have to delete the transaction data in PP/DS using appropriate processes and transactions (e.g., inconsistent data which isn’t correctable), you need to perform a retransfer of the transaction data from SAP S/4HANA to PP/DS. ABAP program /SAPAPO/PPDS_DELTA_ORD_TRANS can be used for the initial transfer and retransfer of the transaction data. There is no difference between initial and retransfer; this program reads all the SAP S/4HANA transaction data and transfers the data to PP/DS. For transaction/master data objects requiring the core interface integra- tion model, program RIMODINI can be used to do an initial transfer, and program RIMODAC2 can be used to do a delta transfer.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To trigger an initial transfer of the transaction data objects that doesn’t require an inte- gration model, execute Transaction SE38, enter the program name “/SAPAPO/PPDS_ DELTA_ORD_TRANS”, and execute. In the next screen, you’ll have the option to enter the material number and plant for which the relevant transaction data needs to be transferred to PP/DS, as shown in Figure 4.33. Under the Parallelized Transfer sub- screen, the Parallelize Selection in S4 System checkbox determines if the selection of data in the SAP S/4HANA side is executed in a parallel processing mode.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When this checkbox is selected, in the SAP S/4HANA side, the transaction data is read in parallel. The packet size (how many objects are read at once) for reading the data is determined by the Customizing settings made in Transaction CFC3. The Absolute Max. No. Pro- cesses or the Relative Max. No. Processes , along with the corresponding Server Group will determine how many parallel processes can be executed in the SAP S/4HANA side to select the data. The Parallel Processing in PPDS checkbox determines if the data pack- ets as selected in the SAP S/4HANA side are processed in parallel in the PP/DS side.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 212 Figure 4.33 PP/DS Delta Transfer Report When the Parallelize Selection in S4 System is activated, the defined number of work processes can be leveraged in the SAP S/4HANA side. Without parallel processing, only one work process will be used by the system to select the data in SAP S/4HANA. As shown in Figure 4.34, when parallel processing is activated for SAP S/4HANA selection, multiple work processes 1 are executed in the system to select the SAP S/4HANA data, whereas when it’s switched off, only one work process 2 is leveraged by the system.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The work processes can be displayed from Transaction SM66. Figure 4.34 Parallel Selection and Processing versus Serial Selection and Processing: Work Processes © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 213 4.12 Initial Transfer and Retransfer of Transaction Data to PP/DS In addition, as shown in Figure 4.35, when Parallelize Processing in PP/DS is activated, multiple core interface queues 3 are generated by the system to process the data in parallel in PP/DS.
