When Parallel Processing in PP/DS is switched off, only one core inter- face queue 4 is generated, and all the transaction data objects are processed by just using one core interface queue. The inbound core interface queues can be displayed from Transaction SMQ2.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 4.35 Parallel Processing versus Serial Processing: Core Interface Queues This program transfers all transaction data that is activated in the configuration of the data transfer under advanced planning. However, you can transfer only specific objects such as sales orders, stock, planned orders, and so on, in Transaction SE38 by entering the program name “/SAPAPO/PPDS_DELTA_ORD_TRANS” and executing. As shown in Figure 4.36, enter the material and plant selection 1 . Then, in the dropdown field in the header, enter “ORD_TYP” 2 and press (Enter) .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This opens new selection options in the Order Types for Transfer area 3 . Now, you can unselect the transaction data objects that you don’t want to retransfer to PP/DS. This option is useful when you want to retrans- fer specific transaction data for a large number of materials to PP/DS and want to avoid all other transaction data being transferred, which is a performance-intensive action. docs.text: 4 Data Transfer for Transaction Data 214 Figure 4.36 Object-Specific Retransfer of Transaction Data 4.13 Summary In this chapter, we covered the important transaction data aspects during the integra- tion between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS. We also discussed the details of in-house manufacturing orders, external procurement orders, stocks, batches, sales orders, PIRs, inspection lots, plant maintenance orders, and production campaigns, as well as how the restriction mode impacts the processing of transaction data within PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Out of these, for the material-independent objects, there is a need to create and activate integration models, and for the other material- dependent transaction data objects, the transfer of data between SAP S/4HANA and embedded PP/DS is activated in Customizing. For the commonly used transaction data objects, such as the planned orders, produc- tion orders, purchase requisitions, and purchase orders, the data is transferred via syn- chronous RFC transfer from PP/DS to SAP S/4HANA, which minimizes the effort required to monitor the SAP S/4HANA inbound queues, and the errors are entered in the PP/DS planning logs.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 217 Chapter 5 Production Planning In this chapter, we’ll dive into the production planning process with PP/DS, from evaluating your requirements, to using heuristics and the Production Planning Optimizer, to evaluating the results of the planning run. You’ll see how the process is impacted by integration with other planning solutions as well. The SAP S/4HANA system has multiple options when it comes to planning materials for in-house or external procurement. SAP S/4HANA has sales and operations planning (S&OP), basic forecasting, demand management, long-term planning (LTP), and mate- rials requirement planning (MRP).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Some of these components, such as S&OP and fore- casting, are no longer in further development, and SAP’s next-generation supply chain planning tool, SAP Integrated Business Planning for Supply Chain (SAP IBP), takes over these components. In the SAP S/4HANA system, the traditional SAP ERP-based LTP and MRP went through a lot of improvements to simplify the way these processes are exe- cuted in SAP S/4HANA. Apart from the improved enterprise resource planning (ERP) tools, the SAP S/4HANA system also has the PP/DS component in its core, which provides another option when complex planning problems arise that can’t be solved by the SAP S/4HANA planning tools.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The PP/DS planning is closely integrated to the SAP S/4HANA planning process via the MRP Live function in the SAP S/4HANA system. Starting with SAP S/4HANA 2020, the new Production Planning Optimizer solution was introduced. Apart from the existing planning heuristics, now the Production Planning Optimizer solution can be leveraged to arrive at an optimized production plan, which then can be further opti- mized for detailed scheduling by leveraging the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer. The Production Planning Optimizer is a cost-based optimization engine that optimizes the plan on costs such as demand penalty cost, storage cost, manufacturing resource cost, and violation of min/max inventory costs.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this chapter, we’ll start with the differentiators of PP/DS production planning com- pared to the SAP S/4HANA planning tools such as LTP and MRP, and then we’ll cover the basic concepts in the PP/DS production planning process and the planning process itself, including the various heuristics for performing planning and the transactions and tools available in the PP/DS system for material planning. We’ll also discuss the setup and details of the Production Planning Optimizer. In addition, we’ll discuss how PP/DS, MRP Live, and SAP IBP work in the SAP S/4HANA system, along with the tools Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 218 available in the PP/DS system to evaluate the planning results and monitor the plan- ning runs. Any specific Customizing settings covered in previous chapters will be referred to here when they influence the PP/DS planning. Any new Customizing settings and the func- tionality behind them, such as the specific planning heuristic settings and planning tool settings, also will be covered as required. 5.1 Determining When PP/DS Should Be Used for Planning In classic MRP, the basic concept is to fulfill the requirements with receipt elements by performing a net requirements calculation and calculation of the dates and quantities for the receipt elements per the set master data and Customizing settings.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, this process selects the source of supply for the receipt elements per the master data setup, such as quota arrangements and rules, validity dates, and lot sizes defined. The MRP functionality in SAP S/4HANA works with a set algorithm and provides flexibility in defining the MRP types that determine how the requirements and receipts are pro- cessed during the planning run, the lot sizing procedures that determine the quantity of the receipt elements, and various Customizing settings that can be used by the MRP algorithm during the planning run to handle planning situations.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The MRP process guarantees material availability by balancing the inventory and receipts against the requirements. If your manufacturing and procurement processes require more sophisticated features to optimize the plan, then the PP/DS planning brings in a lot of features covering requirements across industries and processes. The basic decision to use PP/DS plan- ning depends on whether the material is critical to the supply chain and/or if the mate- rial is manufactured in a bottleneck resource. Let’s walk through some of the specific functions required in the planning process that PP/DS can support and that aren’t available in the SAP S/4HANA planning process, such as MRP:  Capacity-constrained production plan SAP S/4HANA MRP doesn’t consider the capacity of the resources on which the receipt orders are going to be manufactured or handled.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If a resource-constrained production plan is required, PP/DS can support this via the Production Planning Optimizer. The production plan isn’t generally required to be constrained with the resource availability, but the Production Planning Optimizer can support a com- bined PP/DS optimization process. In scenarios where the PP/DS bucket capacity is used, finite capacity planning can be performed using planning heuristics.  Shelf-life planning PP/DS can be used if your materials are handled in batch management with shelf life defined, and you want the planning process to consider the shelf life.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 219 5.1 Determining When PP/DS Should Be Used for Planning shelf life of the product, and the requirements of the maximum and minimum shelf life required to fulfill the requirements. The shelf life also can be propagated throughout the order levels when there are multilevel orders present that handle materials with shelf life.  Variable lot sizes In MRP, the lot sizing throughout the planning horizon is defined in the material master lot sizing procedure if you want to plan using different lot sizes for short-, medium-, and long-term horizons so that the supply elements are planned to the granular lot size level, such as daily for the short term and a more aggregated weekly or monthly for the medium term or long term.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Materials that have such require- ments are supported by PP/DS to achieve the desired results.  Characteristics-dependent planning (CDP) In MRP, the planning run only considers the quantity during planning and can’t ensure that components with the same characteristics values are netted against the demand elements that have characteristics values assigned to them. But with PP/DS CDP, you can make sure the characteristics matching is executed during planning, and new receipt elements are created to fulfill the demand of the requirement ele- ments with characteristics if there are no existing receipts with the same character- istics value available to fulfill the demand.  Realignment of supply and demand In MRP in SAP S/4HANA, the planning is unidirectional and recursive only if the master data setup requires such planning.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Therefore, after the MRP execution, it’s possible that there are delays and earliness of receipts in covering the requirement elements. The MRP exceptions or the MRP Live cockpit needs to be reviewed manu- ally to actively address these situations. With PP/DS, functionalities such as top- down and bottom-up rescheduling can be used to realign the demand and receipt elements.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: PP/DS can be used for critical materials for which the alignment of the demand and supply needs to be ensured through the order network.  Optimization Critical materials, which require optimization from a production plan, and the scheduling perspective, needs to be planned by PP/DS, the Production Planning Optimizer, and the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer, or a combined PP/DS optimizer execution can be used to optimize the plan and schedule to arrive at an optimal plan and reduce setup costs and times, reduce delays, and optimize the production plan and schedule based on the costs defined for the Production Planning Optimizer and the objective functions defined for the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer.  Multistep planning The PP/DS planning run need not be just a one-step planning execution like MRP.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In one planning run, multiple steps can be defined to execute multiple planning algo- rithms in sequence. For example, MRP PP/DS heuristics can be followed by a top- down or bottom-up rescheduling heuristics to realign the newly created and Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 220 changed receipts from the MRP heuristic. Scheduling heuristics or even an opti- mizer run can be scheduled in one planning run. Materials requiring such special planning and scheduling apart from MRP in SAP ERP should be activated for advanced planning.  Push production In push production in PP/DS, if materials with shorter shelf life are received or pro- duced in excess, they should be used up in producing materials with longer shelf life. This is applicable in food, dairy, chemical, and pharma industries.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Such materials can be activated for PP/DS planning, so that they can be processed with PP/DS push pro- duction to avoid wastage of raw materials. PP/DS push production can identify the materials that can be produced using the expiring materials based in the production data structure (PDS) master data setup, and the planners can interactively plan the quantity of such material to be produced.  Product interchangeability PP/DS supports simple discontinuation, so if there are materials that are discontin- ued and being replaced by new materials, certain PP/DS planning heuristics can sup- port this by using up the old material before the requirements are passed on to the new material.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Updating the master data, such as bills of material (BOMs) and PDSs, is the right way to handle material changes in production; however, during the interim, when there is existing stock available for the old material, PP/DS inter- changeability can be used for such materials to support the transition from the old to new material without causing wastage of the old product inventory.  Industry-specific functions PP/DS supports certain industry-specific functions such as order combinations where multiple orders going through the same operation can be combined, and a new order is created to simplify and optimize the planning and execution processes.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As many of the industry solutions, such as discrete industry and mill products (DIMP), are part of the SAP S/4HANA core, PP/DS can be used to leverage the indus- try functions in SAP S/4HANA, which can be further optimized using PP/DS plan- ning and scheduling functions.  Alerts-based monitoring The MRP process in SAP ERP works based on exceptions in the planning situation that are preconfigured in the system. Limited options are available to enhance the exception management of MRP in SAP ERP. With MRP Live in SAP S/4HANA, the MRP cockpit is a set of SAP Fiori apps that provide more insights into the planning situa- tion based on key performance indicator (KPI) applications, which are based on mate- rial coverage and capacity consumption.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: PP/DS brings in a much more sophisticated alert framework that is customizable to add the tolerances for the alerts and can be embedded into almost all the planning and scheduling tools. The alerts can be config- ured for receipts, requirements, pegging, shelf life, capacity consumption, and so on, and the materials activated for advanced planning in SAP S/4HANA can leverage the Alert Monitor in PP/DS to manage the exceptions in planning and scheduling. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 221 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning  Planning simulations In PP/DS, the interactive planning tools such as the product view or the product planning table are always launched in simulation mode, so that you can interac- tively change the procurement elements and see the effect of the changes on the inventory and capacity situation in simulation before you finalize the plan by saving the changes you made in the interactive planning tools. 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning In this section, we’ll cover the basic concepts in production planning within PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These concepts are used widely by most of the planning heuristics and planning pro- cesses in PP/DS. The basic task of any planning tool is to consider the receipt elements and the requirement elements, and then perform a net requirements calculation. Then, based on the delta quantity and the dates on which the net quantity falls below zero, the planning tools should create a receipt element based on the quantity restrictions (lot sizes) maintained in the master data. In addition, this section will cover the terminology used in the PP/DS planning process.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ve covered the planning procedures and day’s supply calculation in Chapter 3, where we discussed the configuration. In this section, we’ll cover the details about peg- ging, net requirements calculation, target stock levels, safety stock methods, and source of supply selection concepts. 5.2.1 Pegging Pegging in PP/DS is used to signify the relationship or the link between a receipt (sup- ply) and a requirement (demand) element. By doing so for all the material BOM levels, the overall lead time for the finished material can be calculated.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If there are any delays in fulfilling the requirements generated at any level of the BOM by the demand for the finished material, these delays can be identified, and an alert can be generated accord- ingly. The pegging process is executed by the system after every planning run and after any planning-relevant change in data, so that the receipt and requirements elements are linked at all times. The alerts also can be determined when any planning tool is being loaded with the planning data for any product location. PP/DS supports two kinds of pegging relationships:  Dynamic pegging In dynamic pegging, the system creates the pegging relationship between the sup- ply and demand element based on the current planning situation.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If there is a change, or a new receipt or requirement is created manually or by the system in the planning process, the pegging relationship will be recalculated and re-created. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 222 Under dynamic pegging, there are two pegging strategies available in the standard system, which can be set in the material master Advanced Planning view via the Peg- ging Strategy field: – Use Timely Receipts With this pegging strategy, the system goes through the requirement elements in chronological order of the date and time of the requirement. It then checks for the receipt element, which is closer to the date and time of the requirement element and assigns the receipt (creates pegging) to the requirement element.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If one receipt element isn’t able to fulfill the requirement element, it checks for further receipt elements closer to the requirement element and creates the pegging. – Use Earliest Receipts (first in first out) With the first in, first out (FIFO) pegging strategy, the requirement elements and receipt elements are sorted by their date and time. Then, the earliest require- ments are assigned (pegged) to the earliest receipt elements. The pegging relationships can be displayed from the Pegging Overview tab of the product view transaction (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, Transaction /SAPAPO/PEG1, directly loads the Pegging Overview tab of the product view. As shown in Figure 5.1, the Pegging Strategy 1 is assigned in the material master Advanced Planning view. The receipt elements 2 (planned orders – PlOrd. ) and requirement element (forecast – FC req. ) 3 in the product view are also shown. Figure 5.1 Pegging Strategy: Example As shown in Figure 5.2, with the Pegging Strategy 01 - Use Earliest Receipts , the sys- tem selects the earliest receipt element in the list of available receipts and assigns it to the requirement element.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this example, the first planned order is on 25.12.2022, so the system creates pegging between the first demand element on 01.01.2023 and the first planned order ( PlOrd. ) on 25.12.2022 1 . With Pegging Strategy 00 (or blank value) – Use Timely Receipts , the system searches for a receipt element from the demand date (01.01.2023) in the backward © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 223 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning direction and the first element available to fulfill the demand is used to create the pegging relationship. In this example, the first receipt element closer to the demand date is the planned order ( PlOrd. ) on 31.12.2022. So, the demand date 01.01.2023 is pegged to the planned order on 31.12.2022 2 . Figure 5.2 Pegging Strategy Example: Earliest Receipts versus Timely Receipts Note If there are stock elements present for the product/location in PP/DS, and if the earliest requirements can be covered by the stock elements irrespective of the pegging strat- egy, the stocks will be pegged to the early requirements.  Fixed pegging In fixed pegging, the dynamic pegging relationship created can be fixed so that any future planning situation change won’t alter the fixed pegging relationship.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Manu- ally created fixed pegging can’t be changed or deleted by the system automatically during production planning, but the fixed pegging relationship created by the sys- tem during a planning run can be later changed in a subsequent planning run. How- ever, a mere change in the planning situation won’t change the fixed pegging relationship created by the system. Fixed pegging can be created via execution of the fixed pegging heuristics (covered in Section 5.4.4) or can be created manually from the Pegging Overview tab of the product view Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 224 Quantity button 2 to create a fixed pegging of the complete dynamic pegging quan- tity. To partially fix peg a receipt element to a requirement element in the FixPegQty column 3 , enter the quantity that you want the system to create fixed pegging for, and the remaining quantity will remain dynamically pegged. In this example, 25 out of the 100 dynamically pegged quantity were set for fixed pegging, so the remaining 75 remains with dynamic pegging. Figure 5.3 Fixed Pegging Options in the PP/DS Product View In the Pegging Type column 4 , the system displays the nature of the pegging rela- tionship.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Following are the possible values for this column: – D : Dynamic pegging. – M : Manually created fixed pegging relationship. – A : Automatically created fixed pegging using a heuristics or Business Application Programming Interface (BAPI). – C : Combined fixed pegging relationship. This could be a partial quantity dynami- cally pegged and the remaining quantity fixed pegged manually and/or a fixed pegged quantity using a heuristic or a BAPI. – Blank: No pegging has been created yet for the requirement element. To delete the fixed pegging interactively, select the relevant rows from the list of pegging relationships, and click on the Delete Fixed Pegging button 5 .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Once created, fixed pegging can stay intact when the document type changes. For example, if a sales order is fixed pegged to a planned order, the fixed pegging still can stay intact to the sales order even after converting the planned order to a production order. This is controlled by the configuration in the PP/DS global settings (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRPCUST1) and the settings in the material master. This is covered in Chapter 3, Section 3.2.5. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 225 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning Tip The business add-in (BAdI) /SAPAPO/RRP_HEUR_DO can be used to create fixed pegging relationships during a PP/DS MRP run. However, the standard method for creating a fixed pegging relationship in planning is to execute the heuristics for creating fixed pegging as a subsequent step after the planning heuristics in the PP/DS planning run. For the pegging to be executed between a receipt and requirement element, the follow- ing conditions must be met:  Same pegging area The pegging area is the combination of a product and a location in a planning ver- sion with the account assignment if relevant.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, for a make-to-stock (MTS) material in a plant, the pegging area in the active planning version 000 is the combination of the material and the location. For a make-to-order (MTO) material, every sales order from the customers forms a customer segment, and apart from the material and location, the sales order (as an account assignment object) also becomes a part of the pegging area. The receipt and requirement elements should be part of the same pegging area for them to get pegged to each other.  Pegging interval The receipt elements, including the stock elements, will be pegged to the require- ment element if they are within the pegging interval.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The pegging interval is set by default as 277,000 hours, which is approximately 31.6 years. This is the maximum value technically allowed for this field. So, in embedded PP/DS, the pegging interval is a rolling defaulted 31.6 years (calculated from the requirement element date) and can’t be changed in the material master, as shown in Figure 5.4. Figure 5.4 Default Values of Pegging Interval in the PP/DS Product Master Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 226 Following are a few other settings in the material master that influence the way the pegging relationships are created:  Avoid Alerts When the Avoid Alerts checkbox in the material master is activated in the Advanced Planning tab, the system will respect the pegging strategy assigned, but will try to avoid violating the Alert Threshold for Earliness and Alert Threshold for Lateness . The alert threshold is defined in number of hours (up to six digits) and minutes (two digits). For example, a value of 50000:10 in these fields means 50,000 hours and 10 minutes.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These threshold values must be less than the overall pegging interval, which is 277000 hours. In this example, as shown in Figure 5.5, the pegging strategy is 1 Earliest Receipt (FIFO) 1 ; with this strategy, the first requirement element on 03.03.2023 2 should be pegged to the earliest receipt planned order on 31.12.2022 3 , but the difference in the date/time between these two elements exceeds the value set in the Threshold for Maximum Earliness , which is 48 hours 4 . As the Avoid Alerts checkbox is selected, the system searches for another receipt element that is within the threshold.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Another receipt element on 02.03.2023 5 is acceptable, so the requirement is pegged to the planned order on 02.03.2023 6 . If there are no compatible receipt ele- ments respecting the thresholds, the system will follow the pegging strategy and will peg the earliest receipt element. Figure 5.5 Influence of Avoid Alerts in Pegging  Use Total Receipt / Use Total Stock When the Use Total Receipt and/or Use Total Stock checkbox is selected in the mate- rial master Advanced Planning view, during pegging, the system ensures that the one receipt element (it’s whole quantity) is assigned to only one requirement element. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 227 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning That is, one receipt element can’t be pegged by more than one requirement element. The same applies to stock as well. In the example shown in Figure 5.6, there are two receipt elements 1 , one stock ele- ment with 50 quantities and a planned order for 100 quantities. There are six requirement elements, which are forecasts for 25 quantities each 2 . With Pegging Strategy 1 - Earliest Receipts (FIFO) 3 , all of these requirement elements can be pegged to the existing receipt elements.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: But when Use Total Receipts and Use Total Stock 4 are activated in the material master, the system looks for exact quantities of requirement elements that can be pegged to the receipt elements (planned order and stock). As there are no such requirement elements, no pegging is created 5 . Figure 5.6 Influence of Use Total Receipts and Use Total Stock Checkboxes on Pegging With the activation of Use Total Receipts and/or Use Total Requirements settings in the material master, thresholds can be applied on the receipt quantity, which is allowed to be pegged to a requirement element.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The threshold is set in the under/ overdelivery tolerance values in the material master. As shown in Figure 5.7, in this example, the overdelivery tolerance ( Overdely tol. ) is set as 25 % 1 in the Work scheduling view 2 of the material master. This means if there is a receipt element’s quantity (in our example, the stock element with 50 quantities 3 ) that is up to 25% more than the demand element (the forecast requirement for 40 quantities 4 ), the system can peg this receipt element to the requirement element 5 .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, if there are no other requirement elements that are within the 25% tolerance of the other receipt element planned order for 100 quantities, this planned order isn’t pegged to any of the requirements. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 228 Figure 5.7 Underdelivery and Overdelivery Tolerance for Use Total Receipts and Use Total Stock Checkboxes in Pegging In CDP scenarios, the characteristics values of the receipt and requirement elements are checked for compatibility for creating pegging relationships.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For products that have a defined shelf life, minimum required shelf life, and matura- tion time after production, the dynamic pegging considers these values to make sure that when they are pegged to the requirement element, it’s out of the maturity period of the product and complies with the minimum required shelf life. 5.2.2 Planning Horizon and Planning Time Fence In PP/DS, either the demand can be transferred from an SAP planning system, such as SAP IBP, or a non-SAP system can send in the forecast in the form of planned indepen- dent requirements (PIRs) to SAP S/4HANA, which will be transferred to embedded PP/DS if the material is activated for advanced planning. A planning tool such as SAP IBP is responsible for forecasting and planning the mid- to long-term forecasting and supply planning.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, embedded PP/DS is a short- to mid-term planning tool, and PP/DS is used for short-term detailed scheduling. To define the responsibility of PP/DS for planning only in the short term, a PP/DS plan- ning horizon is defined. Any demand that falls under the PP/DS planning horizon is planned by PP/DS planning tools. The planning horizon is defined in the model version master data (Transaction /SAPAPO/MVM) (see Chapter 3, Section 3.2.1). The horizon defined here is a global setting and considered by all the material locations.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 229 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning product-/location-specific PP/DS horizon is maintained in the material master Advanced Planning view as shown in Figure 5.8. In this example, the global setting (Transaction /SAPAPO/MVM) is 1200 days 1 , and the product-/location-specific PP/DS Horizon is 365 days 2 as defined in the material master. In the product view, you can also see that the value of 365 days 3 is considered from the current date 22.12.2022 4 . In a production planning run, the PP/DS planning heuristics only consider the demand and supply within this horizon for the calculation of the unfilled demand.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 5.8 Planning Version (Global) Level versus Product-/Location-Specific PP/DS Horizon The PP/DS planning time fence is the shorter horizon in the planning horizon within which the system isn’t allowed to make changes to the planning data during an inter- active or background production planning run. Manual changes are allowed within the planning time fence. When the planners adjust the plan and finalize the schedule for the near-term shorter time horizon, the plan must not be altered by the system, and the planning time fence can be defined to such a duration.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The PP/DS time fence is defined in the material master by using Transaction MM02 and navigating to the MRP 1 tab, as shown in Figure 5.9. You can see the Planning Time Fence value of “21” set 1 , in our example. This value defined in the material master is also used by the PP/DS plan- ning time fence if the material is activated for advanced planning and can be seen in the PP/DS product master 2 (Transaction /SAPAPO/MAT1). The planning time fence represented as a separate row 3 in the product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 230 Figure 5.9 Planning Time Fence in the Material Master: PP/DS Product Master Data and Product View 5.2.3 Net Requirements Calculation Net requirements calculation is the process of balancing the demand and supply quan- tities and arriving at the missing quantities so that new receipt elements can be created to cover them. In embedded PP/DS, you can customize the way the receipts and requirement ele- ments are treated by the net requirements calculation process. These customizations are made in the heuristics settings, so that when a planning heuristic is called in the planning run or interactive planning, the system uses the net requirements calculation procedure set in the heuristics to apply it on the planning.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Don’t confuse the concept of pegging with the concept of net requirements calculation. The pegging only links the available receipt and requirement element. But the role of net requirements calculation is to find out when the net quantity (sum of receipts and requirements) falls below zero and trigger a receipt creation at that point in time to fill the open demand. During net requirements calculation, the system starts with the stock and the receipt elements and nets them against the open demand elements. The settings are made in the heuristics Customizing (Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSC11), as shown in Figure 5.10. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 231 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning Figure 5.10 Net Requirements Calculation Procedures in PP/DS Planning Heuristics The following options are available to influence the netting:  FIFO With the FIFO netting procedure, the earliest available requirement element is assigned to the stock element or the earliest available receipt element, and the same chronological order is followed for netting throughout the PP/DS planning horizon.  Avoid Surpluses This procedure will try to avoid new receipt elements creation by assigning the avail- able receipt and stock elements to the requirement elements, irrespective of whether this assignment will cause a delay for the requirement element being ful- filled on time.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This procedure divides the planning horizon into two sections, one for the elements within the PP/DS time fence and another section for the elements outside the planning time fence.  Avoid Delays This netting procedure will try to avoid delays in fulfilling the requirement elements by assigning the stocks and fixed receipt elements to the requirements. If there is a delay, this procedure will propose creating a new receipt element. Thus, this proce- dure may lead to excess supply. This procedure is also referred to as alert minimiza- tion for net requirement calculation.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Alert Threshold for Lateness defined in the material master is considered by this procedure to determine if the system can assign an existing fixed receipt element to the demand. As shown in the example in Figure 5.11, 48:00 (48 hours) 1 is set as the Alert Threshold for Lateness in the mate- rial master. Before planning is executed, a demand element exists on 07.07.2023 for Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 232 250 quantities 2 . There is a fixed receipt element (planned order) for 250 quantities on 10.10.2023 3 . When executing net requirement calculation with the Avoid Delays procedure, the system checks the dates of the receipt and requirement elements. As the fixed planned order is delayed by more than 48 hours from the demand date, the system can’t assign the planned order to the demand during net requirement calcu- lation. This will cause the planning to create a new receipt element (planned order) 4 to cover the demand, irrespective of the fact that it will cause a surplus supply sit- uation 5 at the end of the PP/DS horizon.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 5.11 Example of Avoid Delays - Net Requirement Calculation Procedure The other options available to influence the net requirements calculation are as fol- lows:  Use Total Receipts With this setting active, when one receipt element is assigned to a requirement ele- ment irrespective of the quantity being assigned to the requirement element, the complete receipt element is consumed. If there are partial available quantities from the receipt element, those are left open and aren’t assigned to any other require- ment element.  Use Total Stocks With this option, when the stock element is assigned to a requirement element during the net requirements calculation, then the stock element is completely con- sumed for the purpose of the net requirements calculation, and no other require- ment element can be assigned to the stock element. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 233 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning 5.2.4 Procurement Quantity Calculation When the net requirements calculation determines when to create a receipt element, the procurement quantity calculation will determine for what quantity the receipt quantity should be created. This is determined by the lot size definition. The lot size can be defined in the heuristics-specific settings and in the material master’s Advanced Planning tab. The heuristics-specific settings for lot size provide options that are only relevant for that heuristic.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The lot size data maintained in the MRP 1 view and the Advanced Plan- ning view of the material master are considered by the PP/DS planning heuristics, which needs to determine a quantity for order creation. The lot sizing information from the MRP 1 view, such as lot sizing procedure, minimum and maximum lot sizes, and rounding factors, is considered by PP/DS in addition to the lot sizing unit of mea- sure and other lot sizing-specific fields from the Advanced Planning view of the mate- rial master. The standard planning heuristics, such as the planning of standard lots heuristics, sup- port several lot sizing procedures in the standard embedded PP/DS system.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can access the following procedures in the Lot Sizes tab, as shown in Figure 5.12:  Lot-for-Lot This procedure will propose a receipt quantity exactly the same as the requirement quantity per the net requirements calculation. However, this procedure will con- sider the minimum and maximum lot size settings and the rounding parameters maintained in the material master.  Fixed Lot Size This procedure will propose receipt quantities per the fixed lot size defined in the material master, irrespective of the net requirements quantity.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If one receipt can’t cover the entire net requirements quantity, multiple receipts are proposed with the fixed lot size until the requirement can be covered with the new receipts.  By Period In periodic lot sizing procedures, the net requirements are grouped together per period (day, week, etc.), and one receipt element is proposed per period. This proce- dure also respects the minimum and maximum lot size settings and the rounding settings. Tip With periodic lot sizing procedures, the Period Factor in the Advanced Planning view of the material master and the Use Period Factor checkbox to influence the time of the receipt element availability.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, if the period factor is 0.75, with the daily lot sizing proce- dure, the procurement proposals—such as planned orders or purchase requisitions—are created with a time stamp of 18:00 (instead of the default 12:00:00 time stamp). Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 234  Reorder Point The planning of standard lots heuristic (SAP_PP_002) only supports the Reorder Point Method 2 , which is the Reorder Day’s Supply value maintained in the material master Advanced Planning tab. Figure 5.12 Lot Sizing Maintenance in PP/DS for Advanced Planning Materials Tip Irrespective of the lot sizing method maintained in the MRP 1 view of the material mas- ter, if Reorder Day’s Supply is maintained in the Advanced Planning view of the mate- rial master, then PP/DS planning heuristics will consider this material with a lot sizing procedure with the reorder order point method.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The minimum and maximum lot sizes are maintained in the material master (Transac- tion MM02) MRP 1 tab in the Minimum Lot Size and Maximum Lot Size fields. In addi- tion, the PP/DS-specific lot sizing settings, such as the Reorder Day’s Supply , is defined in the Advanced Planning tab under the Lot Size section, as shown in Figure 5.13. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 235 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning Figure 5.13 Lot Sizing Procedure Definition in MRP 1 and Advanced Planning Views 5.2.5 Target Stock Level and Safety Stock Methods In embedded PP/DS, various target stock level methods and safety stock methods are delivered in the standard solution. We’ll discuss the details of those methods in this section. Target Stock Level Target stock is the inventory level you want to achieve in a planning run. The target stock can be set as an absolute quantity on a periodic basis, or it can be maintained as the number of days in the future within which the inventory should be built ahead to cover the requirement.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Next are the target stock level methods supported by embedded PP/DS. These can be maintained in the Targt Stk Lvl Method field in the Advanced Planning tab of the mate- rial master:  Blank: Target day’s supply from product master With this method for the target stock level, the target day’s supply is maintained in the Target Day’s Supply field in the material master, as shown in Figure 5.14. In this Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 236 example, the target day’s supply is maintained as 10 days 1 , and the target stock method is maintained with a blank value 2 . During the planning run with the stan- dard lots heuristics, when the first receipt element (planned order) is created (in our example, 25.12.2022), the system considers the demand elements up to the next 10 days in the future, which is 04.01.2023 3 , and creates the planned order for this quantity (130 quantity). Whenever the net quantity goes negative in the future (on 10.01.2023) and the planning run is creating another planned order, it will add the demand elements for the next 10 days (till 20.01.2023) 4 , and the planned order is created accordingly.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 5.14 Target Day’s Supply from Product Master: Example  1 : Target day’s supply (time-dependent maintenance) With this target stock level method, the target day’s supply can be maintained in a time-dependent manner. For example, from the current date till the end of June 2023, the target day’s supply is 10 days, and from June 2023 till the end of the time stream (31.12.9999), the target day’s supply is 25 days. The system considers these time-dependent target stock levels during planning with standard lost heuristics and creates the receipt elements to meet the target stock levels. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 237 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning The time-dependent master data for target stock and safety stock are maintained via Transaction /SAPAPO/TDS. In the initial screen shown in Figure 5.15, enter the prod- uct number and the location for which the data needs to be created or changed. Click on the Create button 1 . In the next screen, the materials entered in the selection are listed. Here, enter the required time-dependent safety stock or target stock level val- ues. The first row will be defaulted with the current date as the start date, and the end of calendar 31.12.9999 will be defaulted as the end date, which is also defaulted in the initial screen 2 .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To add a new row for different date ranges in the next empty row, enter the material number and the date from which the new value is to be effective. In the example shown here, 01.06.2023 is entered, and the Target Days is entered as 3 (days). Once you press (Enter) , the initial row will be set with an end date (31.05.2023) of one day before the new date entered (01.06.2023). Finally, save the transaction. Figure 5.15 Maintenance of Time-Dependent Safety Stock and Target Stock Data The Target Day’s Supply (time-dependent maintenance) target stock level method also works like the Target Day’s Supply method from the product master, but it respects the time-dependent data maintained and calculates the receipt element quantities.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this example, till 31.05.2023, the system considered 5 days 1 for calcu- lating the target stock, and after 01.02.2023, it considered 3 days 2 , as shown in Fig- ure 5.16. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 238 Figure 5.16 Target Stock Level Method: Target Day’s Supply (Time-Dependent Maintenance)  Target stock level (time-dependent maintenance) With this target stock level method, an absolute stock value (instead of the day’s sup- ply) is maintained in the time-dependent maintenance. Whenever the system needs to create a receipt element for any demand, it will make sure that an inventory of the quantity that is defined in the master data is achieved. In this example shown in Fig- ure 5.17, the target stock of 100 1 is maintained till 31.05.2023, and the target stock of 200 2 quantity is maintained till 31.12.9999.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: So, in the planning using the standard lots heuristics, the system ensures that till 31.05.2023, a target stock of 100 3 is achieved, and after that, a target stock of 200 4 is achieved. The target stock quantity is added to the first receipt element 5 created. When the target stock level changes to 200 from 01.06.2023, the system adds the delta (between 200 and 100) and adds the 100 quanti- ties to the first receipt element 6 created in the new period (after 01.06.2023). When time-dependent target stock is maintained in Transaction /SAPAPO/TDS, the same is also displayed in the product view in the TargetStk column 7 . © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 239 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning Figure 5.17 Target Stock Level Method: Target Stock Level (Time-Dependent Maintenance)  7 : No target stock level With the no target stock level method, irrespective of the time-dependent target stock or target day’s supply being defined, the system doesn’t consider any target stock levels during planning. Safety Stock Methods Safety stocks are additional inventory held at the plants or at the warehouses to pre- vent out-of-stock situations due to unforeseen challenges such as machine break- downs, supplier delays, and so on In embedded PP/DS, both static safety stock methods and time-dependent safety stock methods are supported.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The safety stock is maintained in the material master for the static safety stock methods; the time-dependent data is maintained in Transaction /SAPAPO/TDS for the time-dependent safety stock methods. The safety stock and safety time fields maintained in the MRP 2 view of the material master are also considered by PP/DS. So, in the Advanced Planning tab, you can use the Sfty Stk Meth Determination checkbox to control whether the system should determine the safety stock method automatically from the safety stock and safety time maintained in the MRP view or Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 240 should respect the settings made in the Advanced Planning tab for the safety stock cal- culations. As shown in Figure 5.18, in the MRP 2 view of the material master, the safety stock of 100 quantities 1 is maintained. In the Advanced Planning tab, the Sfty Stk Meth Determina- tion checkbox 2 (safety stock method determination) is selected. Therefore, the sys- tem automatically determined the safety stock method SB (safety stock from location product master) 3 . In addition, when this checkbox 2 is selected, the Safety Stock Method field 3 in the Advanced Planning tab becomes noneditable.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 5.18 Safety Stock Determination between MRP Views and the Advanced Planning View of the Material Master With the safety stock method determination selected in the Advanced Planning view of the material master, the system applies the following rules to automatically determine the safety stock method:  When the Safety Stock value is filled in the MRP 2 view, the safety stock method SB- Safety Stock from Location Product Master is used in PP/DS.  When the Safety Time in days is filled in the MRP 2 view, the safety stock method SZ- Safety Day’s Supply from Location Product Master is used in PP/DS. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 241 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning  When both the Safety Stock and Safety Time in days are maintained in the MRP 2 view, the safety stock method SM - Max.of Safety Stock and Safety Day’s Sup. from Loc.Prod.Master are used in PP/DS. The following are the safety stock methods available in embedded PP/DS:  SB: Safety Stock from Location Product Master With this safety stock method 1 , as shown in Figure 5.19, the safety stock value is read from the Safety Stock field 2 in the MRP 2 view of the material master.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The safety stock will appear with the current date in the product view 3 . For planning purposes, the safety stock is considered an additional demand element, and the sys- tem will create receipt elements 4 to cover the demand generated by the safety stock. Because the safety stock is a virtual element in PP/DS, no pegging is created 5 . Figure 5.19 Safety Stock Method: SB Note In embedded PP/DS, only virtual safety stocks are supported. Virtual safety stocks aren’t saved in SAP liveCache, so they can’t participate in pegging.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 242 elements aren’t dynamically pegged to the safety stock demand element. So, function- alities such as optimization of delays in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can’t con- sider the safety stock elements because there is no pegging between the safety stock and the corresponding planned order.  SZ: Safety Day’s Supply from Location Product Master This safety stock method uses the safety day’s supply maintained in the MRP 2 view of the material master. With this safety stock method, the demand dates are brought backward virtually by the number of days maintained as the safety day’s supply during the planning run.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As shown in Figure 5.20, the safety stock method is SZ 1 , and the Safety Time is 5 days 2 . In planning, the system created receipt elements 5 days before the demand dates. In this example, demand elements are created every day from 10.01.2023 to 13.01.2023 3 . Using the standard lots heuristics, the system has created receipt elements by considering the demand days are 5 days ahead of the actual dates of those elements. So, the receipts are created every day from 05.01.2023 to 08.01.2023 4 . Figure 5.20 Safety Stock Method: SZ  SM: Max. of Safety Stock and Safety Day’s Supply from Location Product Master With this safety stock method, both the SB and SZ safety stock methods are exe- cuted.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the material master, the safety stock and safety day’s supply are main- tained. During planning, the system first determines the safety stock value from the © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 243 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning material master, and then virtually brings backward the dates of the demand ele- ments by the number of days maintained in the safety day’s supply field. As shown in Figure 5.21, the Safety Stock of 50 1 is maintained and the Safety Time is maintained as 5 days 2 , along with the Safety Stock Method of SM 3 . During plan- ning, the system considered the safety stock and created a receipt element to cover it 4 . In addition, for the other demands, it has virtually brought the dates backward by 5 days and created the receipt elements 5 days early 5 .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 5.21 Safety Stock Method: SM  MB: Safety Stock (Time-Dependent Maintenance) With this safety stock method set in the material master Advanced Planning view, the time-dependent safety stock needs to be maintained in Transaction /SAPAPO/TDS. As shown in Figure 5.22, time-dependent safety stock is maintained 1 as 50 from 26.12.2022, 175 from 01.01.2024, and 25 from 01.06.2024. In the product view, you can see that the first safety stock element is for 50 quantities on 26.12.2022 2 , and the second safety stock demand element on 01.012024 is created for 125 quantities.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This is because with existing safety stock of 50 and the safety stock master data set in Transaction /SAPAPO/TDS as 175, the system offsets the existing 50 quantity with the 175 quantity and creates the safety stock demand element for the 125 quantity 3 . Similarly, the safety stock is reduced to 25 from 01.06.2024, so the system offsets the Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 244 existing safety stocks of the 175 quantity with the 25 quantity and created a safety stock receipt element (positive quantity) for the 150 quantity 4 . When time- dependent safety stocks are maintained, it’s also displayed in the product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3) in the Safety Stk column 5 . Figure 5.22 Safety Stock Method: MB  MZ: Safety Day’s Supply (Time-Dependent Maintenance) With this safety stock method, the time-dependent day’s supply is maintained in Transaction /SAPAPO/TDS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the example shown in Figure 5.23 1 , 2 days of safety day’s supply is maintained from 26.12.2022, 5 days is maintained from 01.01.2024, and 10 days from 01.06.2024. So, during planning, the system will virtually bring backward the demand date by the number of days maintained as the safety day’s supply for the corresponding period, and the receipt elements are created accord- ingly.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For the demand on 10.01.2023, 2 days of safety day’s supply is considered, and the receipt is created on 08.01.2023 2 ; for the demand on 10.01.2024, 5 days is con- sidered, and the receipt is created on 05.01.2024 3 ; and for the demand on 20.06.2024, 10 days is considered, and the receipt is created on 10.06.2024 4 .  MM: Maximum of MB and MZ (Time-Dependent Maintenance) With this safety stock method, both the time-dependent safety stock and the safety day’s supply are considered. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 245 5.2 Basic Functions in PP/DS Planning Figure 5.23 Safety Stock Method: MZ Combination of the Target Stock Level Methods and the Safety Stock Methods All the target stock methods can work with all the safety stock methods. For example, as shown in Figure 5.24, the target stock method ( Targt Stk Lvl Method ) is maintained as a blank value (target day’s supply from product master) 1 with 10 days of Target Day’s Supply 2 maintained in the material master, along with the safety stock method of SZ - Safety Day’s Supply from Location Product Master 3 and the Safety Time as 5 days 4 .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 246 During planning, on the first date of demand, the system considers the demand for the next 10 days (in this example, from 02.04.2023 to 12.04.2023 for a 110 total demand quantity 5 ), respecting the target stock level method. The system virtually brings the demand backward by 5 days, respecting the safety stock method, and creates the receipt element planned order on 28.03.2023 6 (5 days before 02.04.2023). 5.2.6 Source Determination When the time and the quantity are determined by the netting considering the demand elements, including safety stocks, target stock levels, and procurement quan- tity calculation processes, the next step is to determine the source of supply for the receipt element.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Depending on the type of procurement, whether it’s in-house pro- duced material or externally procured material, the source determination process will determine either a valid PDS to produce the material or a valid external procurement relationship to procure the material. For in-house produced materials, the system considers the available PDSs, and the PDS that can produce the material with the minimum delay is selected by the system to cre- ate the receipt element. In interactive planning, if the heuristics setting allows this, the user can select the source of supply manually from a ranked list of all the available sources.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For externally procured materials, the rankings of the source of supplies are calculated per the procurement priority, the procurement costs assigned to the procurement rela- tionships, and the quota. The system will look for the least cost and highest priority source that can fulfill the demand without any delay. For PP/DS source determination in general, on-time delivery is the driving principle in selecting the source of supply. 5.3 Leveraging Planning Heuristics In embedded PP/DS, the planning of a material can be executed in multiple ways, includ- ing MRP Live planning, PP/DS background planning runs, and interactive planning from the PP/DS planning tools.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: All these methods of executing the planning end up calling a planning heuristic, and the heuristic settings, along with the various profiles used by dif- ferent planning tools, determine the planning results. In this section, we’ll discuss the features offered by the commonly used production planning heuristics. The planning heuristics have an algorithm that can determine a shortage quantity and create a receipt to cover the shortage quantity. The algorithm is an ABAP function mod- ule that is designed to execute the specific planning task.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The screens and the available settings in the heuristics Customizing are also part of the algorithm definition. Any of the production planning heuristics can be called in the MRP heuristic, which offer a mechanism to determine the BOM structure and execute the heuristics assigned to the MRP heuristic or the product heuristics following the low-level code of the material. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 247 5.3 Leveraging Planning Heuristics Note Irrespective of the heuristics type (planning, scheduling, or service heuristics), it’s always recommended to create a copy of the heuristics and make the required changes to enable options and functionalities offered by the specific heuristics. 5.3.1 Planning of Standard Lots Planning of standard lots is the most commonly used planning heuristic to fulfill uncov- ered demands. The standard heuristics are delivered with the name SAP_PP_002 and the standard algorithm /SAPAPO/HEU_PLAN_STANDARDLOTS assigned to the heuristic.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The planning of standard lots heuristic executes the standard net requirements calcula- tion and calculates the procurement quantity per the lot sizing definition from the mate- rial master or from the heuristic itself. Then, it executes source of supply determination per the standard logic. After the dates, quantities, and sources are determined, the receipt elements are created by this heuristic. When creating the planned orders for in-house produced materials, these planned orders need to be scheduled on the resources belong- ing to the PDS selected.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Therefore, this heuristic provides options to control the schedul- ing parameters via the scheduling strategy assignment in the heuristic setting. Figure 5.25 Net Requirements Calculation Settings for the Planning of Standard Lots Heuristic Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 248 This heuristic can respect the characteristics values during net requirements calcula- tion to evaluate the characteristics values of the requirement and receipt elements during the netting process. The shelf-life data, such as maturation time and minimum remaining shelf life, is also considered by this heuristic if the heuristics setting is made accordingly (see Chapter 8, Section 8.1). To access this heuristic, execute Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSC11, and double-click on the SAP_PP_002 heuristic in the list displayed.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You’ll arrive at the screen shown in Fig- ure 5.25. The basic settings of the Planning of Standard Lots heuristic has several areas, which we’ll explore in the following sections. Net Requirements Calculation As just shown in Figure 5.25, in the Net Requirements Calculation section of the heuris- tics Customizing, the Procedure for the net requirements calculation is set. The Group Past Requirements checkbox can be used to cumulate all the requirement elements in the past (older than current date) and the requirements within the PP/DS time fence together and consider this as one demand element so that the procurement quantity calculation, including the lot sizing, is applied on this cumulated quantity.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It makes sense to use this checkbox in planning situations where past demands are always pres- ent that weren’t fulfilled on time and need to be fulfilled immediately. Grouping them together will reduce any excess quantities procured due to lot sizing restrictions. For the consideration of the shelf-life restrictions, such as maturity time and the mini- mum required shelf life, the Plan with Shelf Life checkbox needs to be selected. In addi- tion, the corresponding products must have the Plan with Shelf Life checkbox activated in the Advanced Planning tab of the material master.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In planning scenarios where the shortages outside the PP/DS horizon need to be planned within the PP/DS horizon, the Consider Shortages Outside the PP/DS Horizon option can be used. With this option, the system temporarily brings in the require- ments outside of the PP/DS horizon for the duration defined under the Period Outside the PP/DS Horizon section. If there are shortages, then receipt elements will be created inside the PP/DS horizon. Create New Receipt Elements As shown in Figure 5.26, the order of the new receipt creation and the reuse mode is defined for the heuristics.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Sort Procedure has two options:  Chronological Order When the heuristic needs to create several orders due to the dates, netted quantities, and lot sizing procedures, they are created in the order of the earliest order first.  Order Priority, Chronological The orders with higher priorities are created first and then the earliest order within the priority is created next. Along with the scheduling profiles assigned to the © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 249 5.3 Leveraging Planning Heuristics planning of standard lots heuristic, this setting can help ensure that the higher- priority orders are created and scheduled first before other orders are created. Figure 5.26 Settings for New Receipt Creation in Planning of Standard Lots Heuristic The Reuse Mode within the heuristics setting controls how the existing fixed and unfixed receipt elements are treated during the execution of this heuristic. We covered the details of the reuse modes in Chapter 3, Section 3.4.1, where we discussed the PP/DS planning procedure customization.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When the Reuse Mode is set to Use Suitable Receipt Elements , the system also leverages the settings under the Reuse section. The Reuse Strategy defines how the existing receipt elements are used by this heuristic to cover open requirements. Following are the available options:  Use Earliest Receipts (first in first out) Irrespective of the requirement date, use an existing receipt in chronological order (FIFO) when there is a shortage. This may lead to requirement elements covered too early or too late, as well as earliness and lateness alerts for pegging.  Use Timely Receipts The system searches for a timely receipt within the reuse interval defined per the Maximum Earliness of a Receipt and Maximum Lateness of a Receipt fields.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If there are no suitable receipt elements available within the reuse interval, this heuristic will propose a new receipt to be created. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 250 Settings for New Explosion As shown in Figure 5.27, the Settings for New Explosion section is relevant for the stan- dard lot heuristics when the Reuse Mode is set to Re-explode Plan . With this reuse mode, the source of supply is re-exploded. When this happens for an in-house manu- facturing planned order, this may lead to changes in the modes/dates and thus the resources used by the order. To ensure that the heuristics retain the same mode (and the resource) during a re-explosion of the PDS triggered by the planning of standard lots heuristic, the Retain Mode checkbox can be selected.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 5.27 Settings for Re-Explosion, Components, and Interactive Planning in the Planning of Standard Lots Heuristic Note If the mode is no longer available due to a change in the PDS, or the validity date of the mode is no longer under the validity of the order, a mode change can happen irrespec- tive of the Retain Mode checkbox value. A re-explosion of an in-house manufacturing planned order may lead to a rescheduling of the order, and, thus, the operation dates may get changed in this process. To retain © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 251 5.3 Leveraging Planning Heuristics the operation date as it appeared before the re-explosion, you can use the Retain Oper- ation Dates checkbox. When this is selected and the scheduling direction is set as back- ward scheduling, the operation end date is derived from the operation of the order before it’s re-exploded. When the scheduling direction is set as forward scheduling, the operation start date is derived from the operation of the order before the re-explosion is triggered. (The details of the scheduling direction are covered in Chapter 6, Section 6.2.2.) However, because a finite scheduling strategy will lead to a change in the opera- tion dates, it’s generally recommended to perform the production planning run in PP/DS without finite scheduling.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Planning of Components Creating new receipts by the planning of standard lots heuristic will create dependent demand for the components of the material being planned. According to the planning procedure set for the component materials, when the dependent demand is created or changed, the system reacts accordingly (no action, planning run immediately, create planning file entry, etc.). But if you want to override the planning procedure action and always create a planning file entry for the materials for which the dependent demand is created, you can select the Create Planning File Entry for Components checkbox in the heuristic settings.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If the component material has a planning procedure with Don’t Carry Out Any Action defined as the Action , then no planning file entry will be created (see Chapter 3, Section 3.4.1). Interactive Planning The Interactive Planning section (refer to Figure 5.27) determines how the system behaves when the planning of standard lots heuristic is called from an interactive plan- ning tool, such as the product view or order view. During interactive planning, you can change the lot size definition for just that heuristic execution in the planning tool; to allow this, select the Lot Size Dialog Box checkbox in the heuristic settings.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: With this setting, a dialog box with the current lot sizing procedure per the values from the mate- rial master or the values from the heuristics is defaulted on the screen, and the user has an option to change them manually. To understand the planning elements the system has considered during the interactive execution of the planning of standard lots heuristic, you can select the Generate Evalu- ation checkbox in the heuristic settings. The evaluation contains the information of all the requirement elements, the fixed receipts, the receipts the heuristics has deleted, and the planning file entries created during the execution of the planning of standard lots heuristic in interactive mode.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, you can select the Interactive Sourcing checkbox to manually select the source of supply for the external procurement receipts being generated by this heuris- tic. When there are more orders than the value defined in the Max. num. of proposals , the interactive sourcing isn’t enabled. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 252 Lot Sizes The Lot Sizes tab of the heuristic settings has the same lot sizing settings that can be set from the material master MRP 1 and Advanced Planning views (as you saw in Section 5.2.4). But if you want to override the lot size data maintained in the material master and use the one defined in the heuristic settings, select the Use Lot Size Settings from Heuristic checkbox, as shown in Figure 5.28. Figure 5.28 Heuristic-Specific Lot Sizing Overriding Material Master Lot Size Data Strategy As shown in Figure 5.29, the Strategy tab of the heuristic settings determines the sched- uling parameters to be used for scheduling the receipt elements created by the plan- ning of standard lots heuristic.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The scheduling strategy options within the planning of standard lots heuristic are controlled, so that the heuristic can execute and created orders. For example, only the infinite scheduling strategy is available within the heuris- tics setting for the scheduling mode. The following scheduling strategies are available in the Sched. Mode dropdown: © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 253 5.3 Leveraging Planning Heuristics  Infinite Scheduling  Search for Bucket with Free Capacity During planning in PP/DS, most of the planning heuristics only offer infinite schedul- ing modes. You can only finitely schedule on such resources with the scheduling mode Search for Bucket with Free Capacity with bucket capacity being used in the resource master data. So, you should execute a planning run with a planning heuristic such as the MRP heuristic, which may in turn execute the product heuristics such as the stan- dard lots heuristics, and execute a scheduling heuristics or the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer to finitely schedule the orders on the resources with finite capacities.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 5.29 Scheduling Strategy for Planning of Standard Lots Heuristic 5.3.2 Reorder Point Planning The reorder point planning heuristic is delivered in the standard embedded PP/DS sys- tem with the name SAP_PP_007 – Reorder Point Planning and with the algorithm /SAPAPO/HEU_REORDER_POINT_PLAN. The reorder point maintained in the material master MRP 1 tab is considered by this heuristic for refilling the stock up to the reorder point if the current stock level is below the reorder level maintained in the material master.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 254 The net requirements calculation for this heuristic only considers the current stock level, the receipt elements, and the reorder point defined in the material master. No other requirement elements are considered for the net requirements calculation, which may lead to excess supply or supply shortage; therefore, this heuristic should be used for materials that are truly procured based on reorder point planning. In general, for such materials, advanced planning isn’t necessary, and they can be planned in MRP Live in SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If such materials are produced in-house on a bottleneck resource, then those materials can be activated for advanced planning, and the reorder point planning heuristic can be assigned as the product heuristic for those products. The heuristics settings for the reorder point planning heuristic are shown in Figure 5.30. In the Basic Settings tab, the Delete Non-Fixed Receipt Elements option will delete all the nonfixed receipt elements and re-create them if the net requirements calcula- tion determines a shortage. If the Delete Non-Fixed Receipt Elements checkbox isn’t selected, the excess nonfixed receipt elements won’t be deleted by this heuristic.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 5.30 Reorder Point Planning Heuristic Basic and Lot Size Settings The example for the treatment of the nonfixed receipt elements is depicted in Table 5.1 and Table 5.2. Table 5.1 shows the current planning situation with a reorder point of 70 maintained in the material master. docs.text: 255 5.3 Leveraging Planning Heuristics This situation would look the same without the Delete Non-Fixed Receipt Elements option selected. Because the nonfixed receipt element (purchase requisition) isn’t deleted, the total available receipts (stocks + purchase requisition) quantity (10 + 100) is more than the reorder point defined in the material master (70). However, with the option selected, the situation would look like Table 5.2 after the reor- der point planning heuristic. As you can see, the nonfixed purchase requisition with quantity 100 is deleted, and a new purchase requisition is created with quantity 60 to balance the reorder point quantity of 70: stock quantity 10 + new purchase requisition quantity 60 = 70 (reorder point).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Referring back to the settings shown in Figure 5.30, the Fill to Maximum Stock Level checkbox will create a receipt element to fill up to the maximum stock level main- tained in the MRP 1 view of the material master when the net requirements calculation warrants the creation of a receipt element by the system. Note When maintaining the maximum stock level and reorder point in the MRP 1 tab of the material master, the system will raise a warning or an information message saying the MRP procedure doesn’t make use of these fields.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: But with advanced planning, PP/DS uses these fields when the reorder point planning heuristic is executed. The Lot Size settings in the reorder point planning heuristic (shown on the lower area of Figure 5.30) only provide the option to define the maximum and minimum lot sizes because other settings, such as lot sizing procedure, aren’t relevant for the reorder point planning scenario and are ignored by this heuristic. The Strategy tab is like the planning of standard lots heuristic where the heuristic only has infinite scheduling modes available in the heuristic settings. 5.3.3 Planning of Standard Lots in Three Horizons The planning of standard lots in three horizons heuristic is delivered in the SAP stan- dard system with the name SAP_PP_004 and the standard algorithm /SAPAPO/HEU_ PEGID_PERIODIC_LOT.
