docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 256 The planning of standard lots in three horizons is the same as the planning of standard lots heuristic, except for the lot sizing procedure defined in the heuristic settings. The basic settings and the strategy settings are the same as the planning of standard lots heuristic. This heuristic offers up to three different lot sizing procedures that can be used in certain periods. For example, week 1 is planned in the lot-for-lot lot sizing pro- cedure, week 2 to week 5 are planned using a daily (periodic) lot sizing procedure, and week 6 to the end of the PP/DS horizon are planned with a weekly (periodic) lot sizing.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As shown in Figure 5.31, the Lot Size tab of this heuristic offers the flexibility to enter three different lot sizes for different time horizons. The Short-Term Horizon starts from the date of the heuristics execution until the duration defined as the short-term hori- zon, and the Medium-Term Horizon starts at the end of the short-term horizon and runs for the duration defined in the heuristics setting. Figure 5.31 Lot Sizing Settings for the Planning of Standard Lots in Three Horizons Heuristic © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

The strategy settings for scheduling in the planning of standard lots in three horizons heuristic is the same as the standard lots heuristics, which is infinite scheduling. 5.3.4 MRP Heuristic The MRP heuristic in PP/DS is an enabling heuristic that can execute a production plan- ning heuristic assigned to the heuristics or the product heuristics assigned to the mate- rial in the Advanced Planning view of the material master.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It’s delivered in the standard PP/DS system with the name SAP_MRP_001 and with the standard algorithm /SAPAPO/ HEU_MRP_PLANNING. The MRP heuristic is classified as an enabling heuristic because it can’t perform plan- ning (net requirements calculation, procurement quantity determination, and source determination) on its own. However, because it can be used for executing planning heuristics, we’re covering the details of the MRP heuristic in this section.

docs.text: 259 5.3 Leveraging Planning Heuristics CDPSB0). When executing planning using the PP/DS planning run, the MRP heuristic can be leveraged. The MRP heuristic settings are very limited, as shown in Figure 5.32, to the extent of a few heuristics parameters and the technical settings for parallel processing to improve the performance of the PP/DS planning run. Figure 5.32 Settings for the MRP Heuristic The Heuristic section of the settings determines if the MRP heuristic will execute the product heuristic or another heuristic assigned in the heuristic settings.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If there is no product heuristics assigned in the material master, the system will read the configura- tion settings of the PP/DS planning procedure and get the heuristics assigned to the planning procedure. If the product heuristics in the material master are left empty and also the heuristics in the planning procedure are empty, the system will raise an error message as it’s not able to determine any heuristics for planning. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 260 The heuristics parameters are the same as the planning of standard lots heuristic for the Reuse Mode and Create Planning File Entry for Component . The Sort Low-Level Codes in Descending Order setting will change the direction of the planning from the lowest level component to the top-level finished product. This can be useful when exe- cuting other service heuristics via the MRP heuristic to realign the higher-level require- ment with the lower-level supplies. However, in a production planning run (using a planning heuristic), this checkbox must be deselected to avoid adverse impacts in the planning results.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Maximum Package Size is relevant when Parallel Processing is selected for the MRP heuristic. The production planning runs handles a large data volume, and even with the power of SAP liveCache in the PP/DS, the performance can still be a concern. To reduce the runtime of the MRP heuristic, parallel processing can be activated in the heuristic settings. The technical setup of parallel processing for the MRP heuristic is covered in Chapter 3, Section 3.4.2. The package size determines the number of material locations included in one package, which is dispatched to a parallel process to execute the heuristics.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Note When the MRP heuristic is executed, if one of the materials in a planning package ends up with a termination, the planning of all the materials in the package is rolled back. Therefore, it’s important to have a small number as the package size to reduce the impact and avoid one material in the package making the whole package fail. 5.3.5 Demand Propagation Heuristic This heuristic is delivered in standard embedded PP/DS with the name SAP_PP_022 and the algorithm /SAPAPO/HEU_DEMAND_PROPAGATION. It can be used in external procurement scenarios where stocks are transferred between locations.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This heuristic identifies all the locations that supply material to the material location for which the heuristic is being executed, and it propagates the demand to the supplying locations by creating procurement elements such as stock transport requisitions. This heuristic can execute multilevel demand propagation according to the heuristic settings. As shown in Figure 5.33, when the Multilevel checkbox is set, it executes the heuristic across all locations of the material. The Reuse Mode and the Create Planning File Entry for Component function similar to the settings available in the planning of standard lots heuristic (refer to Section 5.3.1). © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 261 5.3 Leveraging Planning Heuristics Figure 5.33 Demand Propagation Heuristic: Available Settings 5.3.6 Quota Heuristic The quota heuristic is delivered in the standard system with the heuristics name SAP_ PP_Q001 and the algorithm /SAPAPO/HEU_PLAN_QUOTA. When inbound quota arrangements are maintained for in-house or external procurement receipts for mate- rials, this heuristic reads and respects the quota arrangement master data maintained for the material and creates the receipts accordingly. As shown in Figure 5.34, the quota arrangement heuristics doesn’t have any special settings.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 262 For the uncovered requirements, the quota arrangement heuristic determines the pro- curement type (in-house or external procurement) and source of supply. The product heu- ristics determines the lot sizes and other parameters used to create the receipt elements. While all the quota master data settings are considered by this heuristic, the maturity time and shelf-life data defined in the material master isn’t considered by this heuristic. 5.3.7 Planning of Standard Lots for Co-Products Co-products are additional output products resulting from the manufacturing of the finished products.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The co-products scenario is commonly used in chemical industries. The co-product materials can be set with the Co-product indicator in the material mas- ter MRP 2 view or in the BOM item 1 , as shown in Figure 5.35. In addition, in the BOM, the co-product is maintained with a negative quantity 2 . With these settings in the BOM, when the PP/DS PDS is generated, the co-product will be created as a nonprimary output 3 material and with an offset relationship of End-End 4 . Figure 5.35 Co-Products in BOM and in PDS The plan standard lots for co-products heuristic is leveraged in scenarios where there are independent requirements such as sales orders, forecasts, or dependent require- ments available in the system.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the standard system, this heuristic is delivered with the name SAP_PP_017 and the algorithm /SAPAPO/HEU_PLAN_COPRODUCTS. During the execution of this heuristic for co-product materials, the system evaluates the demand (sales orders, forecasts, etc.) and the receipts (the nonprimary output from the finished product’s planned orders). If there is uncovered demand, this heuristic creates planned orders for the finished material in such a quantity that it produces enough co- product material to cover its uncovered demand. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 263 5.3 Leveraging Planning Heuristics In the example shown in Figure 5.36, the planned order 1 exists for the finished mate- rial. As the co-product is also an output of this planned order, in the product view of the co-product, you can see the receipt from the planned order 2 . The receipt quantity isn’t editable 3 in the co-product product view, as the planned order is originating from the finished material. In addition, you can see a forecast demand for the co-product pres- ent in the system 4 . Figure 5.36 Co-Product Receipts in Product View When the plan standard lots for co-products heuristic is executed for the co-product, the system creates a planned order for the finished material for a quantity, as shown in Figure 5.37 1 , which ensures that the uncovered demand for the co-product is covered by the resulting output 2 from the finished material planned order.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 264 5.4 Leveraging Service Heuristics In embedded PP/DS, the service heuristics are the algorithms that can’t directly be involved in planning or in scheduling but help in altering the planning data, which is later leveraged by the planning and scheduling heuristics. These heuristics can’t create or change the quantity of the receipt or requirement elements. Service heuristics, such as the fixed pegging creation or deletion, changing the order priorities, or new explosion, trigger a nonplanning or a nonscheduling action but can change the receipt elements with the task they are assigned to perform.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll cover the details of the commonly used service heuristics in this section. 5.4.1 Bottom-Up Rescheduling The bottom-up rescheduling heuristic is delivered in standard embedded PP/DS with the name SAP_PP_009 and the algorithm /SAPAPO/HEU_MIN_PEG_GIV_SUPPLY. The primary purpose of this heuristic is to ensure that the existing supplies that were planned as part of a production planning heuristic for the dependent demands can ful- fill the demands with as little delay as possible. This heuristic evaluates the existing supplies and then shifts the requirement elements (dependent demands) closer to the availability date of the existing receipts, so that there is no or very little delay.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As the components from the orders are assigned to an activity of the order under an operation, this heuristic needs to reschedule the activity to a newer date where the component requirements can be fulfilled with the existing receipts. To keep the delays minimal, this heuristic takes the component availability date (the date of the existing receipt elements) and then reschedules the activity using forward scheduling. If there are related orders due to their BOM structure, depending on the settings made in the detailed scheduling strategy profile of this heuristic, it can update the availability dates of the related orders.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This heuristic can only shift the dependent demand date by rescheduling the corre- sponding activity of the order. However, it won’t shift the customer requirement (sales order or customer-dependent requirement) dates or PIR dates. So, after the execution of this heuristic, even though the receipts and requirements at the lower-level BOM levels are aligned with no or little delay, at the top level (finished product level), there could be a delay in fulfilling the requirement. The available settings for this heuristic are shown in Figure 5.38.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 265 5.4 Leveraging Service Heuristics Figure 5.38 Settings for the Bottom-Up Rescheduling Heuristic Planning Parameters The Planning Parameters have the following functionality:  Fix Shifted Orders If this checkbox is selected, then the orders whose activities are rescheduled by this heuristic will get the Output Firmed indicator so that no other planning run changes such orders automatically.  Sort Sequence The sort sequence is the sequence in which the requirement elements are sorted for matching with an existing receipt element.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The default delivered setting is to sort the requirement elements chronologically. Clicking the Sort Sequence button brings up a popup where the following list of available fields for sorting can be selected: – Requirements Time – Deallocated – Order Priority – Output Firmed Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 266  Scheduling Status When the activities and the corresponding orders are rescheduled to the new dates by this heuristic, the orders can retain the scheduling status (scheduled on a resource or deallocated), or it can be set to either deallocate or set to reschedule on the same resource using the Scheduling Status heuristic settings.  Component Check When the activities are rescheduled by this heuristic, that action may lead to other dependent activities of the order being rescheduled to maintain the order-internal relationship between the activities, which will then lead to a change in the require- ment dates for the components assigned to those activities.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To determine the behavior of the heuristics in the handling of other components of the same order, the following options are available in the Component Check setting: – Do Not Check Other Components With this setting, the heuristic doesn’t check for the availability of the other com- ponents of the order and only works with the selected component’s dependent demand dates. – Check Component to Be Planned Immediately For components that are critical in determining the order availability date, plan- ning procedure 3 (immediate planning) is used so that the component is planned immediately instead of waiting for the PP/DS planning run.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This helps in creating the required alerts as early as possible in the process and avoids any delays for the order. This mode for the component check in the heuristics setting considers all the components with planning procedure 3, checks for their availability, and realigns their requirement dates as well when the bottom-up heuristic is exe- cuted for any one of the components of the order. – Check Other Components This option checks for the availability of all the components of the order, which may result in multiple activities being rescheduled.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Depending on the number of components and activities of the order, this option can be very performance intensive, so it isn’t recommended to have this setting for scenarios where many order activities and components are involved in the planning process.  Assignment Strategy The Assignment Strategy is used to determine the receipt element that can be assigned to the requirement elements. This setting is similar to the settings avail- able in the planning of standard lots heuristic (refer to Section 5.3.1). Date Shift The Date Shift settings determine the direction in which the activities of the requirement elements can be rescheduled.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These activities can be rescheduled into a future date from the current requirement date or toward the current date from the requirement date. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 267 5.4 Leveraging Service Heuristics With the Date Can Be Shifted In Every Direction option, when the delay can be minimized for a requirement element, the activity can be rescheduled into the future or toward the current date of the heuristic execution. Safety time in PP/DS is the time duration with which the requirement dates for a mate- rial are brought forward virtually during a planning run. This is defined in the material master. For the bottom-up heuristics, the safety time consideration during the deter- mination of the requirement elements can be controlled by the Safety Time heuristics setting, which can be set on or off.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, a third option is available where the safety time will participate in the requirement date termination if there is no delay caused by considering the safety time in the calculation. During the execution of the heuristics, the fixed pegging relationship between the receipt and requirement elements is always respected, and the heuristics bring the requirement date closer to the receipt date to reduce any delays. With the other receipt and requirement elements, it uses the Sort Sequence for the requirement elements and the Assignment Strategy for determining the receipt elements.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: By setting the Only Dependent Reqmnts with Fixed Pegging Relationship checkbox in the Date Shift set- tings, the receipt and requirement elements that aren’t in a fixed pegging relationship aren’t selected and processed by the heuristics. Processing Horizon For the bottom-up heuristics to select the receipt and requirement elements for align- ing them, a specific period is required within which this matching and realignment needs to happen. It doesn’t make much sense to execute this heuristic for the whole PP/DS planning horizon as the planning situation changes often for the mid- to long- term horizon.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This heuristic provides the following options for the definition of time duration ( Processing Horizon , as shown in Figure 5.38). If the start date of the activities of an order is within the processing horizon, these activities and the relevant compo- nents are selected by the heuristics for processing.  Use Planning Time Fence The planning time fence defined in the material master is considered the horizon for processing the receipts and requirements. This option is specific to the material location.  Use Planned Delvry Time The planned delivery time defined in the material master is set as the processing horizon.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This option is specific to the material location.  Use User-Defined Time Interval The value is defined in the number of working days, and all the materials selected for the heuristics will use this value as the processing horizon. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 268 Multilevel Planning For enabling the bottom-up heuristics to work in the multilevel execution of a produc- tion planning run (consider the lowest level component of the BOM and work all the way up to the finished product), the bottom-up heuristics needs to be called within the MRP heuristic. The Heuristic settings can be navigated by double-clicking the heuristic in the heuristics list available in Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSC11. As shown in Figure 5.39, the bottom-up rescheduling heuristics can be assigned to the MRP heuristic by selecting the Other Heu- ristic option.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As this heuristic needs to work from the lowest level first to the top level last, the Sort Low-Level Codes in Descending Order checkbox needs to be set in the MRP heuristic setting under the Sort Sequence section of the heuristics setting screen, which is created for executing the bottom-up rescheduling in a multilevel scenario. Figure 5.39 MRP Heuristic Enabled to Execute Bottom-Up Rescheduling Heuristics in Multilevel Scenarios The detailed scheduling strategy assigned to the bottom-up rescheduling heuristics offers infinite scheduling strategies so that the order activities with the requirements assigned can be scheduled with minimal delays and without capacity constraints during the planning to create a feasible plan.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The requirements from the orders that have the status Date Fixed , Started , Confirmed ( Partial or Final ), and Delivered ( Partial or Final ) aren’t changed by this heuristic. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 269 5.4 Leveraging Service Heuristics Interactive Planning The bottom-up rescheduling heuristic also can be executed interactively from tools such as the detailed scheduling planning board. For performing such execution, the SAP_MLO_BU heuristic is delivered, and the bottom-up heuristic (SAP_PP_009) is assigned to this heuristic. The SAP_MLO_BU heuristic is like the MRP heuristic, but it works based only on the orders as an object selected for executing this heuristic. Note When copied to another custom heuristic, the SAP_MLO_BU heuristic can be used for executing any heuristics that work based on order selection.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, in the standard system, it’s only used for bottom-up and top-down rescheduling. In interactive planning, using tools such as the detailed scheduling planning board, the SAP_MLO_BU heuristics starts with the order selected in the planning tool and works all the way up to the finished product level based on the low-level codes. As shown in Figure 5.40, this heuristic is also set with Sort low-level codes in descending order checked, so that after the relevant materials and locations are identified by the order relationships, the heuristic starts with the lowest BOM level to apply the bottom-up rescheduling algorithm.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 270 5.4.2 Top-Down Rescheduling The top-down rescheduling heuristic is delivered with the name SAP_PP_010 and the standard algorithm /SAPAPO/HEU_MIN_PEG_GIV_DEMAND assigned to it. The top-down heuristics can be used in planning situations where the planning run results in the receipt elements scheduled too far from the requirement elements. This heuristic tries to reduce the delay to the requirement element by shifting the receipt elements closer to the requirement date. This heuristic uses backward scheduling from the requirement date to schedule the shifted orders.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Other heuristic settings, such as the Basic Settings and the Strategy settings, are the same as the bottom-up rescheduling heuristic shown in Figure 5.41. The top-down heu- ristic derives the planning period from the time profile assigned in the production planning run (see Chapter 3, Section 3.6.2). Figure 5.41 Top-Down Rescheduling Heuristic Settings For executing the top-down rescheduling heuristic in a planning run, heuristic SAP_ PP_010 can be called within the MRP heuristic. The Sort low-level codes in descending order checkbox must be deselected so that when the low-level codes are determined by the MRP heuristic, it starts with the topmost BOM level (finished materials) and works toward the lower-level components. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 271 5.4 Leveraging Service Heuristics In interactive mode, this heuristic can be executed for an order at the top level of the BOM structure by calling the multilevel order heuristic SAP_MLO_TD. This heuristic calls the top-down heuristics for the selected orders from the top level to the bottom- most component level. 5.4.3 Change Order Priorities In embedded PP/DS, the order priorities are considered during the planning to priori- tize the higher priority orders for scheduling and avoid delay for these high-priority orders.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, the PP/DS optimizer can respect the order priority to reduce pen- alty costs for the high-priority orders by reducing the delays. The priority for the orders is determined based on the setting maintained in the model and version master data in Transaction /SAPAPO/MVM (refer to Chapter 3, Section 3.2.1, for details). Especially in MTO scenarios, one receipt element can be pegged to multiple requirement elements. During a planning run, when the receipt and requirement ele- ments are changed, this will lead to changes in dynamic pegging.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Therefore, the order priorities assigned to the receipt elements before the planning runs are no longer valid as the pegging situation has changed. The change order priority heuristics can be used in such cases to change the priority of the receipt element to the same as the pegged requirement element. This heuristic is delivered with the name SAP_PP_012 and the algorithm /SAPAPO/HEU_PRIO_ CHANGE. The heuristic checks for the priority of all the requirement elements that are assigned to a receipt element, and it sets the highest priority of the pegged require- ment to the receipt element. 5.4.4 Create Fixed Pegging In embedded PP/DS, the pegging structure is generated by the system to maintain the relation of the receipt and requirement elements within a pegging area (material/loca- tion/account assignment object).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The structure comprises the order relationship across the supply chain network, including the in-house production and external pro- curement orders. These relationships are possible due to the relationship between var- ious BOM levels, which is represented by the dependent requirement (demand) elements. The pegging relationship can be displayed from the product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/ RRP3), and the inter-order relationship can be displayed in tools such as the detailed scheduling planning board (see Chapter 6, Section 6.4.1).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The pegging relationships can change when the planning situation changes; therefore, if you want to maintain the pegging structure permanently for the lifecycle of an inde- pendent requirement element such as a sales order or a PIR, you can create a fixed peg- ging relationship between the receipt and requirement elements. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 272 The creation of fixed pegging relationships is delivered with a heuristic named SAP_ PP_019 and the algorithm /SAPAPO/HEU_FIX_PEG_CREATE. The available heuristic settings for the fixed pegging relationship heuristic are shown in Figure 5.42. Figure 5.42 Heuristic Settings for the Fixed Pegging Heuristic The Create Pegging Relationship on Basis of settings define the basis for the pegging relationship, which will be converted to a fixed pegging relationship. The pegging structure is created with fixed pegging as well.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The available options are as follows:  Dynamic Pegging With this setting, the existing dynamic pegging relationship will be converted into a fixed pegging relationship.  Batches For materials with batches when the requirement element and the receipt element has the same batch assigned, they will be fixed pegged to each other.  User-Defined Settings With this setting, you’ll have to define how the fixed pegging relationships are cre- ated between the receipt and requirement elements. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 273 5.4 Leveraging Service Heuristics The User-Defined Settings contain the following options:  Pass On Indep. Reqmts Information This checkbox is used to create fixed pegging in a multilevel fixed pegging creation scenario. The information, such as the available-to-promise (ATP) category of the independent requirement (sales orders, PIRs), is sent to the lower levels. Note The custom sort profiles in which the requirement elements can be sorted according to custom sort rules are only supported in the PP/DS component in SAP Advanced Plan- ning and Optimization.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This custom sort profile isn’t supported in embedded PP/DS, as this functionality is based on global ATP. You may use the BAdI /SAPAPO/RRP_FIXPEG to adjust the filter and sorting of the input and output elements during the heuristic execution.  Confirmed Reqmts Only This checkbox will filter out the requirement elements based on their status. Con- firmed requirement elements, such as the sales order, are only considered for filter- ing out the requirement elements, and other requirements aren’t included in creation of the fixed pegging relationship.  Filter for Reqmts/Filter f.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Receipts You can use these fields to define specific requirement and receipt elements that need to be considered for the fixed pegging creation. The assignment strategy deter- mines the order in which the selected receipt elements are assigned to the selected requirement elements for creating the fixed pegging relationship. For example, if you want the sales orders to be pegged to production orders instead of planned orders that are ahead of the production orders, you can filter the sales order category in the requirement filter and set the filter for production order category for the receipt filter fields.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Pegging Horizon settings are used to limit the duration in which the fixed pegging relationship is created by this heuristic. The start of the horizon is defaulted to No Restrictions , meaning all the receipt and requirement elements, even if they are older than the current date, will be selected by this heuristic. The Horizon End has the follow- ing options from where the number of days of the set parameter is added to the current date (date of the heuristics execution) to determine the end of the horizon:  No Restrictions All the receipt and requirement elements are selected irrespective of their dates.  PP/DS Horizon The PP/DS horizon set in the model version master data is considered as the end of horizon.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 274  Planning Time Fence, Planned Delivery Time These are dependent on the material location and are defined in the material mas- ter.  User Defined A set value can be configured for the number of days that will be used by this heuris- tic to calculate the end of the horizon for fixed pegging.  ATP Check Horizon The global ATP features aren’t supported in embedded PP/DS, and advanced ATP (aATP) can also be used, but it isn’t yet integrated with embedded PP/DS. However, the value maintained for the Tot. repl. lead time (total replenishment lead time) field in the MRP 3 view of the material master is considered the ATP check horizon value at the database table level for the material master.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: But because the ATP checking cal- endar can’t be maintained in embedded PP/DS’s material master, the value derived as the ATP check horizon is used as the number of calendar days and added to the current date to calculate the pegging horizon. Note When a specific setting is maintained for the determination of the pegging horizon, and no value is maintained in the material master for the selected field, this heuristic won’t be able to calculate a horizon end and won’t create any fixed pegging relation- ship for such materials.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: From the product view, you can create fixed pegging by executing the fixed pegging heuristics via the Variable Heuristics button. You then select the fixed pegging heuris- tics from the list of available heuristics in the Variable Heuristics screen and click the Execute button. The details of fixed pegging are covered in Section 5.2.1. 5.4.5 Delete Fixed Pegging When the create fixed pegging heuristic is executed in the production planning run for creating a multilevel fixed pegging structure, it’s recommended to delete any fixed pegging relationships created previously so that the current fixed pegging run will recalculate the pegging link and fix them.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To delete any previously created fixed pegging relationships, the heuristic for deleting fixed pegging named SAP_PP_011 is delivered with the algorithm /SAPAPO/HEU_PEG_ FIX_DELETE_NEW. This heuristic can be interactively called for one material location or can be called within the MRP heuristic in a production planning run. The settings available for the delete fixed pegging heuristic is almost like the create fixed pegging relationship heuristic. As shown in Figure 5.43, under the Delete Pegging Relationship section, the heuristic can be set to Automatically Created Fixed Pegging Relationships , Manually Created Pegging Relationships , or both. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 275 5.4 Leveraging Service Heuristics The Filter for Pegging Relationship section has the same options as the same section for the create fixed pegging relationship heuristic. The Pegging Horizon for the delete fixed pegging heuristic is the horizon in which the heuristic can delete the fixed pegging relationships. If you want the heuristic to delete the fixed pegging relationship only after the PP/DS planning fence, you can set the value accordingly in the heuristic. The end of the horizon for the deletion of the fixed pegging relationship is set as No Restric- tions by default, and this value isn’t changeable in the heuristic settings.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The delete fixed pegging heuristic deletes the fixed pegging relationship according to the heuristic settings maintained. If those elements can be dynamically pegged, the dynamic pegging relationship is established between the requirement and receipt ele- ment. Figure 5.43 Settings for the Delete Fixed Pegging Heuristic 5.4.6 Stage Numbering In PP/DS, the low-level codes determine the position of a material and location in the supply chain hierarchy. For example, for an in-house manufactured material, the low- level code is determined on its position in the multilevel BOM structure.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For materials that are part of the BOM of multiple materials, the lowest position of the usage of the material among all the BOMs is determined as the low-level code for that material/ plant. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 276 Low-level code is very important for the PP/DS planning run, as it determines the sequence of the materials in the planning. If the sequence is incorrect, it may lead to a dependent demand created by a finished material as a semifinished material isn’t ful- filled by creating a receipt element. The incorrect sequencing may plan the semifin- ished material first and then the finished material. As shown in Figure 5.44, the position of a material in the BOM determines its low-level code, and the low-level code deter- mines the sequence in which the planning is executed during a planning run.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the example in Figure 5.44, the Finished 1 material is at the top of the BOM level, so the low- level code (LLC in Figure 5.44) 0 is determined. For the material Raw 1, which is used in all the BOM explosion levels, the low-level code is determined as 3, as that is the lowest BOM explosion level for this material. Similarly, the low-level codes for other materials are also displayed in the example. Figure 5.44 Example BOM Structure and Low-Level Code Calculation When materials are activated for advanced planning in the SAP S/4HANA material master, they are made available for PP/DS planning.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The low-level code determined in SAP S/4HANA is also transferred to PP/DS, which can be used by the PP/DS planning run. If the position of the material changes in the BOM structure or in the stock transfer scenarios, the change in the low-level code isn’t updated back to embedded PP/DS from SAP S/4HANA. Therefore, it’s important to recalculate the low-level code using the stage numbering heuristic in PP/DS if the PP/DS planning run is used as one of the planning tools.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Finished 1 Semifinished 2 Raw 1 Semifinished 1 Semifinished 2 Raw 2 Raw 1 Raw 2 Raw 1 Raw 2 Raw 3 Raw 4 BOM Explosion Level 0 1 2 3 Calculate Low-Level Code (LLC) = Lowest BOM Explosion Level Finished 1 = LLC 0, Semifinished 1 = LLC 1, Semifinished 2 = LLC 2, Raw 1 = LLC 3, Raw 2 = LLC 3, Raw 3 = LLC 3, Raw 4 = LLC 1 Finished 1 Semifinished 1 Semifinished 2 Raw 1 Raw 2 Raw 3 Raw 4 Low-Level Code 0 1 2 3 BOM Structure Planning Direction © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 277 5.4 Leveraging Service Heuristics Note When MRP Live is used as the only tool for planning PP/DS materials in the SAP S/4HANA system, it uses the low-level code calculated in SAP S/4HANA. In these scenarios, the low-level code in embedded PP/DS doesn’t need to be recalculated. In embedded PP/DS, the stage numbering heuristic is delivered with the name SAP_ PP_LLC and the standard algorithm /SAPAPO/HEU_LOLVLCODE. Its settings are shown in Figure 5.45. Figure 5.45 Settings for the Stage Numbering Heuristic The calculation Procedure determines how the low-level code is calculated.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Following are the available options:  Transfer Low-Level Code from R/3 With this option, the low-level code calculated in SAP S/4HANA is adopted in PP/DS.  Calculate Cross-Location Low-Level Codes This procedure also considers the stock transfer relationship of components between locations and sets the low-level code accordingly.  Calculate Location Internal Low-Level Code This option doesn’t consider the stock transfer relationships. It can only be used if the planning is limited internally within a location. In addition, the planning run is executed per location, and the sequence of the location is done manually when scheduling the planning run in PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 278 This heuristic evaluates the sources of supply for determining the low-level codes. The sources of supply that are valid for the current date of the heuristic execution are con- sidered by the heuristic. If you want to shift the current date (to the past or future) for determining the validity of the sources of supply, you can set the required (positive or negative) number of days in the Offset field. In the supply chain model, cycles can occur when two locations are bidirectional (both source and destination) for the same material.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In such cases, the low-level code calcula- tion can’t be performed. The behavior of the heuristic can be controlled by using the Save Low-Level Codes with Cycles checkbox, however. When it’s selected, the heuristic will save the current low-level code calculated so far before the cycle occurred. If the option isn’t selected, the system will write a log message and won’t update the low-level code for such materials. In in-house manufacturing scenarios, recursive BOMs (the header mate- rial of the BOM is also used as a component) lead to cycles in low-level code calculation.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Save Data for LLC-Graph checkbox records the low-level code calculation results in the system to generate a graph to show the relationship of the materials and their low- level codes and the corresponding sources of supplies. The low-level code graph can be accessed after the low-level code calculation by executing ABAP program /SAPAPO/ SHOW_LLC_GRAPH from Transaction SE38 or Transaction SA38. This report is also available in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization, so you’ll see some selection options related to SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization in the selection screen.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For embedded PP/DS, only the selections relevant to PP/DS are valid. As shown in Figure 5.46, the upper-left screen shows the selection options of the low- level code graphical display report. You can navigate to the source of supply details by double-clicking the link lines 1 between the boxes with the material numbers. You can double-click on the material numbers 2 in the graphical object to navigate to the prod- uct view. The highlighted numbers 3 below the material numbers display the low-level code of the material.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 279 5.4 Leveraging Service Heuristics Note If materials are assigned to a planning group, all the materials in the planning group will get the same low-level code and will be planned together in a planning run. 5.4.7 Repetitive Manufacturing In repetitive manufacturing, the manufacturing is performed in a period-based way according to the rate of the resource. Repetitive manufacturing is used in industries where the products are manufactured in a production line with a set production rate, for example, 1 piece of product is manufactured every 2 minutes.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: So, the planned orders need to be generated considering the available resource capacity. The repetitive manufacturing process in SAP S/4HANA leverages master data objects such as work center types of production lines, rate routings, and repetitive manufacturing profiles, which are assigned to the material master. Production versions are created with the BOM and the rate routings in the SAP S/4HANA side and are transferred to PP/DS as PDSs using Transaction CUTROADV_CREATE. In a standard PP/DS solution, there are two standard heuristics delivered for handling the repetitive manufacturing planning, as discussed in the following subsections.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Multiresource Planning (Equal) Multiresource planning (equal) is delivered as a standard heuristic named SAP_REM_ 001 using the algorithm /SAPAPO/REM_HEUR_WAVE. This heuristic can schedule orders from different products manufactured on the same line. This heuristic considers the demand and creates a finite production plan by consider- ing the available capacity of the resources. When there are multiple resources available via multiple PDSs the quantities are equally distributed between the available resources. Following are the prerequisites for this heuristic for it to work correctly:  Only one operation in the PDS is relevant for planning and scheduling.  The products produced on the same line have the same low-level code, and no dependent requirements are planned along the same line.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The heuristics performs a net requirements calculation and lot size calculation, and then the system calculates the utilization of the resources in the buckets defined in the heuristic settings. If no resources are available with the required capacities to produce the lot in the current bucket, it checks the previous period buckets to see if the orders can be scheduled in those buckets. If the lot can’t be produced in the previous periods as well, then no planned orders are generated. The available settings are shown in Fig- ure 5.47.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 280 Figure 5.47 Multiresource Planning (Equal) Heuristic Settings Under the Planning parameters area, these settings are available:  Only selected objects This heuristic can be executed interactively from tools such as the product view and the product planning table or used in the PP/DS planning run. When there are mul- tiple PDSs available with different resources or multiple products are produced on the same line, even if the selection contains one resource or one product, all relevant products and resources are selected by the heuristics for planning.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, products P1, P2, and P3 are produced in line L1, and P3 also can be produced in lines L2 and L3, when executing this heuristic for one of these products or lines (resources), the system selects all the products and resources, so that it can balance the available capacity. When the Only Selected Objects checkbox is selected in the heuristics, it avoids selecting other related products and resources.  Firm Orders When this checkbox is selected, the planned orders created by the heuristics are automatically set with the firming indicator, which means, in subsequent planning runs, these planned orders can’t be automatically deleted by the system.  Maximum resource load % The available capacity on the resources can be restricted by the maximum resource load field.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 281 5.4 Leveraging Service Heuristics consider only 80% to be consumed by this heuristic, you can achieve that by enter- ing “80” in this field.  Safety period reqmts (days) As this heuristic used bucket-oriented scheduling for a requirement on Tuesday, the system may create the order on Wednesday with a weekly bucket setting; to avoid any such delays, you can use this field, and the system will virtually advance the demand by the number of days mentioned here. The Time buckets profile area defines in what buckets the system will check for the available capacity to schedule the orders.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the example shown in Figure 5.48, the product MG_REP_FERT1 can be produced in resources WLINE1_W6 and WLINE1_W7 because they have two different PDSs in PP/DS with these different resources assigned to the operation. In week W01 of 2023, there is a demand of 450 quantity. Line W6 1 has the rate of 1 piece per 10 minutes in its PDS operation, and line W7 2 has 2 piece per 5 minutes. So, when executing this heuristic with the time bucket profile of week, the system has created receipt elements 3 on both PDSs ( VER1 and VER2 ) and distributed the orders evenly so that the capacity con- sumption is equal 4 on both the resources (lines).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As it’s easy to visualize the period- based quantities and capacity consumptions, this example is shown from the product planning table (Transaction /SAPAPO/PPT1). Figure 5.48 Multiresource Planning (Equal) Heuristic: Example Multiresource Planning (Primary Resource) The multiresource planning (primary resource) heuristic SAP_REM_002 works similar to the multiresource planning (equal) SAP_REM001 heuristic, but it can prioritize one resource and occupy 100% of its capacity before switching to the other available resources for the leftover quantities, which can’t be produced on the primary resource Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 282 due to capacity constraints. This heuristic also does a two-step scheduling: first, it does a backward scheduling in the period buckets maintained, and it’s not able to schedule the orders, so, in the second step, it forward schedules the orders. The settings available in this heuristic are shown in Figure 5.49. The Algorithm parame- ters are additional settings compared to the SAP_REM_001 heuristic. Figure 5.49 Multiresource Heuristics (Primary Resource): Settings The Criteria for preferred resources field has the following options:  Highest mode priority/Lowest mode priority The system selects the resource (corresponding PDS) with the highest or lowest mode priority and loads it 100% before loading the other resources.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, if PDS 1 has line 1 with mode priority A, and PDS 2 has line 2 with mode priority C, and Highest Mode Priority is set in this field, PDS 1 with line 1 will be loaded 100% before the leftover quantities are loaded on line 2.  Highest rate/Lowest rate If the alternative resources available have different rates of production, based on the setting made here, the system prioritizes one resource and first loads it 100%. For example, if PDS 1 with line 1 takes 10 minutes to produce 1 piece of the product, and PDS 2 with line 2 takes 5 minutes to produce 1 piece of the product, and this field is © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 283 5.4 Leveraging Service Heuristics set with Highest rate , the system will prioritize PDS 2 with line 5 and load it 100% before loading the PDS 1 with the leftover quantities. The Strategy for forward phase field determines how the scheduling is performed. With the option Find slot , the system searches for a bucket with available capacity to schedule the order. With the other option available in the dropdown, Move to following week , the system moves the orders to the following period if there is no capacity avail- able in the current period.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If there is no capacity available in the next period, the system schedules the order in the next period and moves the orders from the next period to the following period. The Overload strategy determines how the system should behave incase it’s not able to schedule the orders finitely in the given periods. In the example shown in Figure 5.50, the product MG_REP_FERT1 can be produced in resources WLINE1_W6 and WLINE1_W7 because they have two different PDSs in PP/DS with these different resources assigned to the operation.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In week W01 of 2023, there is a demand of 450 quantity. Line W6 1 has the rate of 1 piece per 10 minutes (lower rate) in its PDS operation with mode priority of H (lower mode priority), and line W7 2 has 2 piece per 5 minutes (highest rate) with mode priority of A (highest mode priority). When the Highest mode priority is selected for the Criteria for preferred resources , the system loads resource W7 at 100% 3 , and the remaining quantity is scheduled on line W6 4 . Figure 5.50 Multiresource Planning (Primary Resource): Example for Setting Criteria for Preferred Resources at Highest Mode Priority In the same example, when the lowest rate is set as Criteria for preferred resources , the system loads resource W6 with 100% (Figure 5.51 1 ), and the remaining quantity is scheduled on line W7 2 .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 284 Figure 5.51 Multiresource Planning (Primary Resource): Example for Setting Criteria for Preferred Resources at Lowest Rate Note The repetitive manufacturing heuristic can’t consider the following constraints during planning:  Characteristics-based planning  Sequence-dependent setup times If there are existing firmed orders, the system may not consider the exact start and end time of these orders as these heuristics work in a bucket-based capacity. 5.5 Heuristics for Inactive Planned Orders As we’ve discussed in Chapter 2, Section 2.3, for product master data, you can deactivate the material for advanced planning.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When deactivated, the material master still will have the Advanced Planning flag active 1 , but the planning status is set as Marked for deactivation 2 , as shown in Figure 5.52. When materials are deactivated, they are set with the deletion indicator 3 in PP/DS. There will be a warning raised 4 when accessing such materials from PP/DS in transac- tions such as the product view (Transaction /SAPAPO/RRP3). The existing demand and receipt elements are still present in PP/DS, and those can be accessed from the product view in display-only mode.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: ABAP programs such as /SAPAPO/DELETE_PP_ORDER or other reconciliation tools such as the core interface compare and reconcile tool (Trans- action /SAPAPO/CCR) can’t delete or change these orders from PP/DS. When procure- ment proposals such as planned orders or purchase requisitions are deleted in the SAP S/4HANA system, the deletions are also not sent to PP/DS for deactivated materials. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 285 5.5 Heuristics for Inactive Planned Orders Figure 5.52 Materials with Planning Status “Marked for Deactivation” in PP/DS In addition, when a material is deactivated for advanced planning, you may notice that the activities from the planned and production/process orders are removed from the orders. So, you can no longer interactively change the schedule of these orders in PP/DS using tools such as the detailed scheduling planning board. Still, the order header can have scheduled or deallocated status. But these orders don’t consume any capacity on the resources.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For such deactivated materials, when transaction data is created, changed, or deleted, these aren’t transferred to PP/DS. So, within PP/DS, when there are orders present and you need to operate on them, there are special heuristics provided in the standard solution. Table 5.7 shows the stan- dard delivered heuristics for inactive orders in PP/DS. Standard Delivered Heuristic Description SAP_INAC_01 Firm inactive planned orders SAP_INAC_02 Unfirm inactive planned orders SAP_INAC_03 Deallocate operations of inactive planned orders Table 5.7 Standard Delivered Heuristics for Inactive Orders in PP/DS Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 286 Out of these six heuristics, the only heuristic that is used often is SAP_INAC_05. We’ll cover the details of this heuristic next. If there are procurement elements such as planned orders and purchase requisitions present on a material and location, when the material is set as inactive for advanced planning in the material master, these elements will continue to stay in PP/DS. But to completely remove the Advanced Planning indicator and to make the material irrele- vant for advanced planning, such existing procurement proposals must be deleted in PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When the planning status is active for advanced planning, deleting the planned orders and purchase requisitions interactively will also send the deletion to SAP S/4HANA. So, this may not be preferred if you don’t want to delete the orders from the SAP S/4HANA side. In such cases, you can leverage the heuristics SAP_INAC_05 in the production planning run. This will just delete the orders in PP/DS with no impact on the SAP S/4HANA side. 5.6 Triggering a PP/DS Planning Run In SAP S/4HANA and in embedded PP/DS, triggering a planning run means making a selection for the material that needs to go through the planning process.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In PP/DS, the planning run is passing the materials through one or multiple heuristics (algorithms) according to the business processes involved. In embedded PP/DS, there are various ways to execute the production planning run, but these are the two major ways:  Production planning run  Interactive planning in the planning tools We’ll cover the step-by-step process of setting up and executing the planning process in embedded PP/DS in this section (and how to evaluate our results in Section 5.7). The transaction for the production planning run also can be used to perform scheduling and PP/DS optimizer runs.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this section, we’ll focus on the settings and parameters required to execute the planning run for production planning. SAP_INAC_04 Reschedule operations of inactive planned orders SAP_INAC_05 Delete inactive planned orders SAP_INAC_06 Re-explode inactive planned orders Standard Delivered Heuristic Description Table 5.7 Standard Delivered Heuristics for Inactive Orders in PP/DS (Cont.) © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 287 5.6 Triggering a PP/DS Planning Run 5.6.1 Production Planning Run in Interactive Mode The production planning run can be performed interactively for very few materials and for a few steps. For larger data sets, it’s always recommended to execute the planning run in background mode. To execute the production planning run online, navigate to the transaction from the SAP Easy Access menu, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Production Planning  Auto- mated Production Planning and Optimization  Production Planning Run , or execute Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSB0 to call the planning run transaction.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the production planning run, you can execute multiple heuristics in sequence for the same set or different sets of data. A simple example of a planning run could be exe- cuting the following heuristics in sequence for the same set of data:  Stage numbering algorithm Recalculate the low-level code for the materials.  Delete fixed pegging Remove the fixed pegging constraints for planning.  MRP with the product heuristics Plan supplies for the uncovered requirement using the product heuristics assigned in the material master.  Bottom-up rescheduling heuristics Use for certain materials where the availability of the lower-level material is critical for on-time delivery of the finished product.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: After you call up the production planning transaction, you’ll see the screen shown in Figure 5.53. First, enter the Planning Version , which is the version on which the plan- ning run is to be executed. You can copy the active version 000 to an inactive version and plan them differently for simulation purposes. The Time Profile determines the planning period within which the current planning run can reschedule or deallocate orders on the resources. However, for performing the production planning and certain service heuristics, the PP/DS planning horizon defined in the model version management (Transaction /SAPAPO/MVM) is used as the planning period.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, a time profile is defined with -2 and +3 months (Transac- tion /SAPAPO/CDPSC4; see Chapter 3, Section 3.6.2) and if the PP/DS horizon defined in model version master data is 4 months, a planning heuristic will consider all the requirements within the 4 months of the PP/DS horizon and will create receipt ele- ments within the 4 months horizon, if there are uncovered requirements. The Propagation Range is a limiting factor for the selection of materials and locations determined by the heuristics. The configuration of the propagation range is covered in Chapter 3, Section 3.4.2.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The propagation ranges defined in the configuration are avail- able for selection by clicking on the value help button on the Propagation Range field in the Production Planning Run screen. For example, if a finished material is entered as Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 288 the selection in the MRP heuristic in the planning run, and it creates or deletes orders at the finished material level, the MRP heuristic automatically determines (when the planning procedure allows) that the semifinished material for which the dependent demand is created also needs to be planned. But if the propagation range is created with only the finished material, then the planning will be limited to just the finished material. Even if a material and location are mentioned in the selection under the indi- vidual step, if the material is excluded in the propagation range, that material can’t be planned.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 5.53 PP/DS Planning Run Transaction: Online Mode For certain heuristics, you can write the results of the planning run into a Simulation Version rather than writing the results back to the active version. This can be useful if you want to apply different detailed scheduling algorithms and save the results in sim- ulation versions for analyzing and comparing them later before deciding on the algo- rithm to be executed on active version 000. Not all heuristics allow you to save data in the simulation versions.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If the Saving Data by Using the Heuristic checkbox is selected under the Planning Object field in the planning Step (see Figure 5.53), then such heuris- tics can’t save data to a simulation version. For an allowed heuristic, when you enter a © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 289 5.6 Triggering a PP/DS Planning Run simulation version name, the system creates a new simulation version with the name you entered and writes the result of the planning run into the simulation version. Because the Simulation Version field is at the header level of the production planning run and not at the individual step level, all the heuristics that are defined as steps in the production planning run should support saving results into the simulation version. Tip To identify the heuristics that allow the results to be saved to a simulation version, check database table /SAPAPO/HEURFUNC .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If a function module assigned to the heuristic has the value X for the Impl. Commit ( IMPLICIT_COMMIT ) field, the data will be saved to the planning version during or at the end of the algorithm by the function module. Therefore, such heuristics can’t save data to a simulation version. The Display Logs checkbox enables the display of logs immediately after the comple- tion of the planning run in online mode. The planning logs will be generated by the sys- tem according to the settings maintained in the PP/DS global Customizing, but the immediate display of the log after the online production planning run is determined by this checkbox.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Global Settings in the display log, which you see in the first half of the screen of the planning run transaction, are global to all the heuristics and functions that are exe- cuted in that planning run. In the bottom half of the screen, you’ll see Step 01 through Step 10 . Within these steps, you can define the sequence of the heuristics and the data selection for the individual steps. Up to 10 steps can be defined in one production plan- ning run. Under the step, the heuristics defined in the Customizing (Transaction /SAPAPO/CDP- SC11) or the standard delivered functions that aren’t defined as heuristics can be exe- cuted in the planning run.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Following are the functions that aren’t defined as heuristics but can be executed in the planning run:  Deallocate  Firm objects  Interrupt operation  Optimization  Reschedule  Unfirm objects If you want to execute any of these functions, do a value help (F4) search on the Func- tion/Heuristic field under the Step tabs. After the heuristic or the function for the individual step is defined, a step-specific Time Profile Step 01 , Strategy Profile , and Optimization Profile can be entered. For certain Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 290 functions and heuristics, it’s mandatory to use one or more of these profiles. For exam- ple, if you select the optimization function, then it’s required to make an entry for the Optimization Profile under the step details. The selection of the Planning Object is also dependent on the heuristic or function selected to be executed in the planning step. In general, for production planning heuris- tics, the allowed selection objects are products; for detailed scheduling heuristics, the allowed selection objects are resources, orders, and operations.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The selection of objects can also be controlled by user exit APOCDPS1 . To select the objects via the user exit, select the Copy Object option from customer exit APOCDPS1 in the Planning Object field. When the selection object of product, operation, order, or resource is selected, you can enter the selection criteria for the corresponding objects. For Step 02 onward, you have the option of copying the selection data from the previous step ( Copy Objects from the Previous Processing Step ) to the current step, as shown in Figure 5.54.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The heuristics in the second step can perform the required action only if the current step can work with the data from the previous step. For example, if Step 01 has a detailed scheduling heu- ristic as the selection, and you execute a production planning heuristic (e.g., MRP heu- ristic) in Step 02 with the selection object as Selection from Previous Step , the heuristic execution will end up with an error. Figure 5.54 Executing a Production Planning Run: Online Mode When the production planning heuristics are defined as the production planning run steps, the With Planning File Entry option is shown under the selection details of the © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 291 5.6 Triggering a PP/DS Planning Run selection objects. When this checkbox is selected, only products that have a valid plan- ning file entry (a planning-relevant change for the material/location has updated the planning file entry per the planning procedure assigned to it) are selected for process- ing. Therefore, the behavior of the heuristic will be a net change planning when this checkbox is selected. After you define the steps for all the planning tasks to be executed by the production planning run, you can save the steps and the selection in a variant by clicking on the Save as Variant option in the menu bar.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Settings for Heuristics menu button from the menu bar can be used to display the heuristic settings of the heuristic defined in the planning step. As shown previously in Figure 5.54, to execute the planning run, click on the Execute button on the bottom-right part of the screen. After the planning run is completed, the system will automatically take you to the log screen, if you’ve set the Display Logs checkbox in the selection screen. If you’ve used the option to save the results of the planning run into a simulation ver- sion, then the same information will be written in the planning log, as shown in Figure 5.55.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can see the name provided for the Simulation Version in the top-left corner 1 . The simulation version will be created, and you can see the recorded log in the middle 2 . The simulation version can be accessed from Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSS0 3 . From this transaction, the data saved in the simulation version can be opened in the detailed scheduling planning board or other allowed tools for working on the simula- tion versions. Figure 5.55 Working with Simulation Versions in the Production Planning Run Tip If you want to work with simulation versions, keep the size of the simulation versions smaller by restricting the selection in the planning run, and delete the old simulation versions frequently to avoid overload of SAP liveCache.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 292 5.6.2 Production Planning Run in the Background When the data to be processed in the production planning is larger, the production planning run must be done in the background. By doing so, the system can execute the planning in a background job, and longer executions won’t end up with timeout errors such as in online/dialog mode. The background planning run can be scheduled from Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSB1 or via SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Production Planning  Production Planning Run in the Background .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The initial screen of this transaction dis- plays the list of all the already saved variants, as shown in Figure 5.56. Figure 5.56 Initial Screen with Variants for PP/DS Planning in Background The variants saved from the online production planning run discussed in the previous section (Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSB0) are also displayed in this transaction and can be used to schedule background planning runs. If you want to create a new variant, click on the Variant button on the screen. This will take you through a series of screens to complete the process of a new variant creation.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the ABAP: Variants popup that appears 1 , enter a variant name for the new variant being created, and then click the Create button, as shown in Figure 5.57. For the screen assignment 2 , select the For All Selection Screens option so that all the screens of the transaction are visible for maintaining the selection criteria. The screen for creating the variant for background production planning is like the online planning run transaction except for the Execute option, which is only available in the online transaction.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: After all the global data for the planning run and the individual steps with heuristics/ functions are defined (see our discussion in Section 5.6.1), navigate back from the screen, and as shown in Figure 5.58, you’ll be prompted to save the newly created vari- ant 3 . Click Yes . On the next screen, you can enter a Description of the new variant and then click the Save button 4 . The variants created for the background planning run can be scheduled immediately for execution of the background job or scheduled to be executed in periodic intervals.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, a variant with net requirements planning can be scheduled to execute daily, and a more complex variant can be scheduled to execute every weekend. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 293 5.6 Triggering a PP/DS Planning Run Figure 5.57 Steps to Create a New Variant for a Background Planning Run (1 of 2) Figure 5.58 Steps to Create a New Variant for a Background Planning Run (2 of 2) To schedule a new job, click on the Schedule button on the initial screen of the back- ground planning run (see top portion of Figure 5.59). In the next screen, Background Planning Scheduling: Start Time (see bottom portion of Figure 5.59), you have the options to enter the start time for the job. You set the execution date and time for the job, and if the job is to be executed immediately for one time, select the Schedule once option.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 294 For periodic jobs, enter the start date, for example, a daily job that needs to start at 15:00:00 hours daily; enter the date from which the job needs to be scheduled and the time as “15:00:00”; and select the Schedule periodically option. In the Period Duration popup, under the Repeat period section, you have Months , Weeks , Days , Hours , and Minutes as options. For a job that needs to be scheduled every two days, select the Days option, and enter “2” as the value. After the job frequency is entered, click on the Create button in the Period Duration popup to create the job schedule.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 5.59 Steps to Schedule a Daily Background Planning Run After the job is scheduled, it can be monitored from the background job monitor (Transaction SM37) or from the background planning run transaction itself. The job sta- tus will appear as Released ; after it’s executed, the status will change to Completed , and the system will automatically release the next job per the frequency (daily, weekly, etc.) in the scheduling settings. From the initial screen of the background planning run (refer to Figure 5.56), select the variant for which you want to check the scheduling.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 295 5.6 Triggering a PP/DS Planning Run button. In the next screen shown on the left side of Figure 5.60, you’ll see the list of the scheduled requests of the variant selected. The list will have all the past executions for the variant as well as the next scheduled execution details. You can select the com- pleted executions and navigate to the Log to check the background job log. The Results 1 option on this screen will navigate to the spool request created by the background job (refer to Figure 5.61) 2 , which has the statistics and the results of the planning run.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can double-click on the spool button to navigate to the spool record that contains the results of the production planning run. In addition, you can delete or change the schedule (start date, time) and the frequency of the scheduling by clicking the pencil icon shown in Figure 5.60. You can delete the scheduled executions by selecting a released line and clicking on the Delete Job Defi- nition button. Figure 5.60 Background Planning Run: Job Schedule Monitoring Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 296 Figure 5.61 Background Planning Run: Spool Details 5.6.3 Interactive Production Planning Many of the planning tasks scheduled as planning run steps within the production planning run can be executed interactively to evaluate the results of the planning. In addition, actions such as creating an order, changing or deleting an order, changing the sources of supply, re-exploding the source of supply, setting and removing firming indicators, setting the conversion checkbox, and changing or creating fixed pegging relationships can be executed from the interactive planning tools.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In embedded PP/DS, the following are the commonly used interactive planning tools for production planning purposes:  Product view  Receipts view  Requirements view  Order processing view  Product planning table  Product overview © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 297 5.6 Triggering a PP/DS Planning Run We’ll cover the product view in detail in this section and also give an overview of the other tools and their specific use cases, if any. Some of the tools can be used to perform the detailed scheduling actions as well. But in this section, we’ll cover the functions related to production planning in the interactive planning tools. Product View The product view is the most commonly used transaction for interactive planning and evaluation of the planning results for individual material/locations.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The product view can be accessed from SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Pro- duction Planning  Interactive Production Planning  Product View . You can use Transac- tion /SAPAPO/RRP3 to access the product view as well. The initial screen of the product view, as shown in Figure 5.62, has the Plng Version , Product , and Location options. Entering these three values is the basic minimum requirement. If you work with special stock scenarios, such as sales orders or project orders, you can use the Special Stock indicator and the account assignment object.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 5.62 PP/DS Product View: Selection Screen The Selection Rule can be specified to filter out the receipt and requirements displayed in the product view by period restrictions or by excluding certain order categories from displaying in the results. For any action you perform within the product view, the system generates planning logs according to the PP/DS global settings. For performance reasons, the global set- tings may be set to just error messages. You can override this setting within the prod- uct view by setting the logging level via Settings  Planning Log , as shown on the right side of Figure 5.62, and setting the All Messages option in the dialog box.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This setting is valid for the current session, and when you restart the product view transaction, it will be defaulted back to the original setting. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Production Planning 298 Tip The product view selection rule can be customized from the Customizing IMG menu path: SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Order View  Define Selection Rules for Product View . In addition, by using the Create Order button, the system will take you to the screen where you can create a new procurement element, such as a planned order or purchase requisition (depending on the procurement type of the material). After entering the required selection options, click on the Continue button or press (Enter) to view the result of the product view.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The results screen of the product view has multiple tabs and features, as shown in Fig- ure 5.63. Click on the Change button on the menu bar to make the planning data edit- able in the product view. In edit mode, only the elements that can be changed in embedded PP/DS can be changed in the product view. Figure 5.63 PP/DS Product View Details Screen Following are the different tabs and the functionality and data contained in these tabs, which are used for interactive planning:  Elements The Elements tab has the list of stock, receipt, and requirement elements displayed in chronological order.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The PP/DS planning time fence and the PP/DS planning hori- zon are marked accordingly. The resources on which the orders are manufactured, the dates/times, quantities, and order categories are some of the important fields © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 299 5.6 Triggering a PP/DS Planning Run listed in the Elements tab. You can select individual or multiple orders (by pressing the (Ctrl) key and clicking on the Order Selection checkbox on the screen) to delete them. Double-clicking on the order will take you to the order details screen (see Figure 5.64) where you can perform actions such as setting or removing the firming checkboxes 1 and setting the Conversion Ind. for converting the planned orders to production orders or the purchase requisitions to purchase orders 2 .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For the manufacturing orders (production/process orders), the Life Cycle checkboxes are set according to their execution status in SAP S/4HANA 3 . The list of available sources of supply can be displayed by clicking on the Change source of supply button 4 .
