docs.text: 6 Detailed Scheduling 408 Simulation Session All the schedule changes and the heuristics you executed in the detailed scheduling planning board are always performed in a simulation session (sim session) by the sys- tem, until you adopt the changes to the active version while saving. When you navigate back from the detailed scheduling planning board screen, the system prompts for you to Adopt the current scheduling data from the detailed scheduling planning board into the active planning version or to Save the data to a simulation version, which can be worked on later before merging back to the active version, as shown in Figure 6.54.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 6.54 Detailed Scheduling Planning Board: Option to Save the Data in a Simulation Version Note The simulation version saved from the detailed scheduling planning board scheduling data shouldn’t be confused with the inactive planning versions, which can be created by copying the active planning version 000. These are two different objects. The simu- lation version from the detailed scheduling planning board only has the data loaded onto the planning board. Inactive planning versions (copy of 000) are created and maintained from the version copy report and Transaction /SAPAPO/MVM (Model Ver- sion Management).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When merging the simulation version data or the data from the detailed scheduling planning board session (sim session) back with the active version, the merge will take place depending on the status of the objects. For example, if you’ve rescheduled an operation of a production order in the detailed scheduling planning board, and the order has been confirmed in SAP S/4HANA in the meantime, then while merging the sim session (rescheduled operation) to the active version (operation confirmed), the status in the active version takes higher priority, and the rescheduling change from the detailed scheduling planning board will be ignored during the merge.

docs.text: Figure 6.55 Accessing Simulation Versions Multilevel Time Buffers A multilevel time buffer (MLTB) calculates the buffer for rescheduling orders without impacting the schedule of the upstream or downstream orders in the pegging struc- ture. This is useful in situations where a finished product is produced in a constrained resource with many products scheduled on it. If a change is required in the semifin- ished product’s order schedule, it would eventually impact the finished product’s man- ufacturing resources, which has far more impact due to the line manufacturer’s multiple other products.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this case, if there is a time gap between the finished product and semifinished product orders, the MLTB calculates this exact time gap and displays it as a key figure in the planning board. This will help the schedulers with a time thresh- old within which the semifinished order can be rescheduled without impacting the schedule of the finished product order scheduled on the constrained resource.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There are three types of time buffers that can be calculated and displayed in the plan- ning board:  Time buffer relative to successor This is the time difference between the operation being rescheduled and the imme- diate next operation of the same order or the next order that is pegged to the opera- tion/order being rescheduled.  Time buffer relative to predecessor This is the time difference between the operation being rescheduled and the imme- diate previous operation of the same order or the next order that is pegged to the operation/order being rescheduled. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 6 Detailed Scheduling 410  Time buffer relative to primary demand The primary demand is the top level of the pegging structure, which can be a forecast requirement, sales order requirement, and so on. If there are gaps between the oper- ations of the orders and gaps between the orders, the time buffer relative to primary demand for any level of the order/operation in the pegging structure is the total time that becomes available if all these gaps are closed. The primary demand date is a constant. The orders/operations will be simulated with an infinite backward sched- uling starting at the demand due date till the operation/order for which this key fig- ure is being calculated and that value is displayed.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the example shown in Figure 6.56, the top portion A is the original schedule of the orders on their resources. Here, we’ll take the order 1 for product S4PPDS_MLTB_ HALB1 , which is pegged to the higher level and pegged by a lower-level material, as an example and see how the buffers are calculated. For calculating the time buffer relative to the successor, the system calculates the difference 2 between the end time stamp of this order and the start time stamp of the higher-level pegged order (for product S4PPDS_MLTB_FERT1 ).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 6.56 Example for Calculation of Time Buffers Relative to Predecessor and Successor Orders As shown in the middle part of the screen B , if the order is manually rescheduled within this calculated threshold, this doesn’t impact the schedule of the higher-level order. Similarly, the difference 3 between the start time stamp of the order 1 and the end time stamp of the lower-level order pegged (for product S4PPDS_MLTB_HALB2 ) provides the time buffer relative to predecessor. As you can see in the bottom part of Figure 6.56 C , moving the order in the backward direction within the buffer threshold won’t impact the schedule of the order for product S4PPDS_MLTB_HALB2 . © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 411 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling An example of the time buffer relative to the primary demand is shown in Figure 6.57. The original schedule is shown in the top portion A . Here the time buffer relative to pri- mary demand is being calculated for the order in the lowest level of the pegging struc- ture. The primary demand is a forecast element 2 . For this order 1 , the system calculates the difference 3 of the end time of the order (for which the buffer is being calculated) and the end time of the same order, if it’s rescheduled along with all orders in the higher pegging levels (with no gaps) and without impacting the due date for the primary demand 2 , as shown in the bottom part B .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 6.57 Example of Calculation of Time Buffer Relative to Primary Demand The time buffer can be calculated as a gross duration or as net duration. For example, if an operation is disturbed by a nonworking day or shift break, the gross duration is the difference of the start and end time stamps of the operation. The net duration is the actual operation duration, which doesn’t include the nonworking times. The MLTB Pro- file determines whether the duration calculated in the gross or net duration. The MLTB profile can be configured using SAP IMG menu path, SPRO  Advanced Planning  Detailed Scheduling  Maintain MLTB Profiles .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the MLTB profile settings, under the Time Buffer Calculation Method field, you can set if the duration needs to be calculated in net time or gross time, as shown in Figure 6.58. In the detailed scheduling planning board, you can set the overall profile SAP_MLTB to display the MLTB-related key figures such as the buffer relative to successor/predeces- sor in the order and operation charts in the detailed scheduling planning board. After entering this overall profile and the selection criteria for the detailed scheduling plan- ning board, execute the transaction, and you’ll be in the detailed scheduling planning board.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Within the detailed scheduling planning board, select the resources (see Figure 6.59 1 ) for which you want to calculate the time buffers for the corresponding orders and operations. Then navigate to Functions  Multi-Level Time Buffer  Calculate Time Buffer 2 . This will calculate the time buffer key figures, and in the order chart 3 and operations chart 4 , you can see the values for the buffers updated. When there are changes made to the schedule of the orders, you can use the Refresh Time Buffer 5 to recalculate the buffers based on the new scheduling situation.

docs.text: 413 6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling 6.4.2 Advanced Scheduling Board In embedded PP/DS, Advanced Scheduling Board is delivered as a standard SAP Fiori app. This app can be used to perform order-scheduling functions such as schedule, deallocate, fix, interrupt, creation/deletion of orders, setting conversion indicator for planned orders, and so on. docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The old Production Scheduling Board app is still available as of SAP S/4HANA 2022, but all the new features and func- tionalities are delivered in the new Advanced Scheduling Board app. Activation of advanced planning (PP/DS) is mandatory for using the Advanced Sched- uling Board app, and only the resources activated for advanced planning can be sched- uled via the app. This SAP Fiori app is delivered with the authorization business role SAP_BR_PRODN_PLNR . docs.text: 6 Detailed Scheduling 430 6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is an optional component of embedded PP/DS. The main purpose of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is to create a mathematical model of the scheduling problems and resolve them by reducing the weighted objective func- tions associated with the scheduling problem, such as makespan (total lead time) of the operations on the resources, setup time, setup cost, delay cost, and mode cost. The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer also respects the hard constraints provided and will attempt to respect the soft constraints.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The result is a schedule that is optimized per the objective functions defined in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile. The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can be executed from the detailed scheduling tools such as the detailed scheduling planning board and product planning table. In addi- tion, you can schedule the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer execution as a part of the background production planning run as a planning step. The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer engine is installed in one of the application servers of the SAP S/4HANA system or in a separate server.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: TCP/IP is set up between the SAP S/4HANA system and the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer server. When Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is executed from the PP/DS tools, the data is collected from SAP liveCache and from the PP/DS application, and then the data is sent along with the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile settings. Detailed Scheduling Optimizer creates the optimal plan by executing multiple iterations of the solution and sending the final solution back to embedded PP/DS. The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer settings are maintained in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile from Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Detailed Scheduling  Maintain Optimiza- tion Profiles , or from Customizing Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSC5.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The list of optimiza- tion profiles is displayed in this transaction, as shown in Figure 6.82. Figure 6.82 Optimization Profiles Double-clicking on an optimization profile will take you to the screen with the optimi- zation profile details, as shown in Figure 6.83. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 431 6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Figure 6.83 Optimization Profile: Details We’ll cover the important settings under the different tabs of the optimization profile in the following sections. The objective functions are the main drivers of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer functionality, so we’ll cover the details of the objective functions before covering the critical settings on the different tabs. 6.5.1 Objective Functions The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer works based on the objective functions and the val- ues defined against the objective functions, such as delay cost, mode cost, and so on.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The objective functions are defined in the Basic Settings tab of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile. The following objective functions are supported by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer, as shown in Figure 6.84:  Makespan Makespan is the total lead time. This is the time difference between the earliest start date of the optimized schedule and the end of the last unfixed operation in the hori- zon for which the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is being executed. The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer decreases the makespan by reducing any gaps between the Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 6 Detailed Scheduling 432 operations or by resequencing orders so that the orders aren’t impacted by breaks in the resource. When a weightage value is provided for the makespan, the value for the objective function is calculated as follows: Weighted makespan = Weightage for makespan in profile × Makespan in seconds Figure 6.84 Objective Functions in Detailed Scheduling Optimizer  Total Setup Times When sequence-dependent setup activities are involved in scheduling, the detailed scheduling heuristics can’t optimize the schedule by calculating the setup times in iterations to schedule the operations in the optimal sequence.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In such scenarios, the Total Setup Times objective function can be set with a higher weightage value so that the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer will reduce the total setup time required for all the operations within the optimization horizon by resequencing the operations. The weighted total setup time is calculated as follows: Weighted total setup time = Weightage for setup time in profile × Total setup times of all the operations in the optimization horizon  Total Setup Costs Similar to the setup times, the relative setup costs are also defined in the setup matrix master data.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Especially if the changeovers are based on multiple characteris- tics and generated setup matrices based on characteristics are used, the number of changeovers is high, and the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can help reduce the setup costs. Figure 6.85 shows an example of the generated setup matrix based on © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 433 6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer characteristics. The generated setup matrices based on characteristics can be accessed from Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPS_CHARMAT. The time unit of measure maintained in the setup matrix is converted into an equiv- alent time unit of measure of seconds for consideration by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer weighted objective value. The setup cost is a relative cost—not the actual cost—and no unit of measure or currency is maintained nor conversion applied when calculating the weighted setup cost totals.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 6.85 Generated Setup Matrix with Setup Times and Setup Costs  Maximum Delay Costs/Total Delay Costs The maximum delay and total delay costs are calculated from the delay in seconds. The delay in delivering a requirement is derived by calculating the requirement date and the assigned receipt elements receipt date and then converting it into seconds. The requirement priority drives the delay costs; that is, the higher the priority (1 is higher), the higher is the delay cost. The list of Delay Costs up to a certain priority is defined in the Costs tab of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile, as shown in Figure 6.86.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The delay costs are calculated as follows: Total delay cost = Total of ((Delay for the order in seconds) × (Weightage maintained in the profile) × (Delay cost for the priority of the order)) Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 6 Detailed Scheduling 434  Total Mode Costs When alternative modes are available to manufacture a material, the cost of using different modes can be reduced as an objective function using the Detailed Schedul- ing Optimizer. In general, the higher the mode priority (A is the highest priority), the lesser is the mode cost. The mode cost is calculated as follows: Total mode cost = Fixed costs + (Variable costs × Duration of activity in seconds) The mode costs are also maintained in the Costs tab of the Detailed Scheduling Opti- mizer profile, as shown in Figure 6.86.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSC5, from the list of all PP/DS optimization profiles, double-click the profile you want to change, and navigate to the Costs tab to maintain the mode and delay costs. Figure 6.86 Mode Costs and Order Priority Costs in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Profile The constraints for the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can be configured within the optimization profile, which we’ll discuss in the next section. However, certain con- straints, such as resource availability (working times, utilization percentage), are hard constraints and can’t be changed in the optimization profile. 6.5.2 Optimization Profile We’ve covered the objective functions and cost definition in the optimization profile in the previous section.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Now, we’ll discuss some of the other important settings in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile. Basic Settings Let’s start with the Basic Settings tab, as shown in Figure 6.87, which includes the fol- lowing key settings: © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 435 6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer  Maximum Runtime Depending on the volume of data involved and the complexity of the scheduling problems, the runtime for the optimization can vary. The Detailed Scheduling Opti- mizer will keep iterating the solutions to further reduce the objective functions and to find the best possible solution. After a certain number of iterations, you may observe from the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer logs that the runtime required to perform these iterations isn’t worth the reduction in the objective function values.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this case, you can define a maximum runtime for the Detailed Scheduling Opti- mizer, so that it will end the iteration at the defined maximum runtime and save the best solution found so far. Figure 6.87 Optimizer Profile: Basic Settings  Backwards Scheduling Backwards scheduling is a follow-on step after the optimization to bring orders closer to the requirements. The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer may schedule orders too early to reduce the objective functions defined; in those cases, backwards scheduling can be executed by selecting the Backwards Scheduling checkbox under the Addi- tional Strategies area so that the orders are scheduled closer to the requirement dates.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Executing backwards scheduling may result in gaps between the operations, which can be avoided by selecting the Compact Scheduling checkbox in this same area. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 6 Detailed Scheduling 436 Order Processing In the Order Processing tab, shown in Figure 6.88, you define the options for the order categories of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer run and settings based on the status of the orders and operations. The Other Manufacturing Levels settings determine whether the pegging relationships of the higher level and lower level orders in the pegging struc- ture and their relationship to the order being optimized need to be considered as a sec- ondary constraint by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If you select the Ignore Upstream Orders and/or Do Not Consider Subsequent Orders checkboxes, the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer schedule may look optimized, but the material flow in terms of pegging relationships can be broken. In a combined Production Planning Optimizer and Detailed Scheduling Optimizer run using the Production Planning Optimizer (/SAPAPO/ PPO_OPT), the system dynamically updates the order validity dates for the operations that are to be scheduled within a bucket. So, in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile that is to be assigned in the Production Planning Optimizer execution, it’s required to set the Validity Periods of Orders as at least a soft constraint.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: So that the system respects the Production Planning Optimizer–supplied order validity dates for the operations to be optimized by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer. Figure 6.88 Optimizer Profile: Order Processing Settings © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 437 6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Resource Processing In the Resource Processing tab of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile, as shown in Figure 6.89, the handling of capacities and scheduling relationship parameters and constraints are set for the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer. Figure 6.89 Resource Processing Settings in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Profile When calendar resources are used, they are assigned to the location master data as inbound handling resources for scheduling goods receipt (GR) times of the orders.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There is no capacity consumption with the usage of calendar resources, and these resources are only used for scheduling the GR activities. When there are orders in the optimization horizon with activities that use calendar resources, then how the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer handles such activities is set under the Non-Selected Calendar Resources area of the Resource Processing tab. If the calendar resources are selected as part of the resource selection for optimization, these settings aren’t relevant. When you select Activities Are Fixed , the system reschedules the product activity of the order, but the GR activity stays where it was before the optimization, thus impacting the over- all duration of the order.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 6 Detailed Scheduling 438 Resource Capacity Load settings control which resources are finitely scheduled during the optimization run. With the selection of Always Schedule as Finite , all the relevant resources being optimized will be scheduled finitely. The resource master data setting Rel- evant for Finite Scheduling isn’t considered, and irrespective of the resource master data setting, the resource will be finitely scheduled by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer. The Lowest Mode Priority setting, which the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can select from alternative modes, is defined under the Mode Priority section.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Lower Priority Modes setting directs Detailed Scheduling Optimizer behavior when there are activi- ties with proprieties lower than the lowest mode priority allowed to be selected by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer. The system can choose a higher priority mode when you select Choose a different mode from the Lower Priority Modes dropdown. Horizon In the Horizon tab of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile, the Start of the Optimi- zation Horizon and the End of Optimization Horizon options are set. Options are avail- able to set these dates relative to the current date.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The relative dates work better when running the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer as part of the production planning run as a batch job because there is no manual intervention required to change the dates for every job. Start of the Optimized Plan is the date/time from which the system can start scheduling the optimized orders and operations on the resources. During optimization, the operations that lie entirely within the optimization horizon are considered for rescheduling. The handling of the orders that lie partially within the optimization horizon is defined in the Order Processing tab under the Orders Partially Located Outside the Optimization Horizon section.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Note The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer in embedded PP/DS can’t create new orders to ful- fill any open demand. This is only possible in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer in the standalone PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization. Additional Strategies The Decomposition setting in the Additional Strategies tab is used to split the schedul- ing problems into multiple smaller problems so that the Detailed Scheduling Opti- mizer can efficiently solve smaller problems. Don’t switch on the decomposition to just improve the performance of the optimization run because the quality of the plan- ning results may be affected by switching on the decomposition.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Any increase in the makespan due to the backwards scheduling can be controlled and avoided by selecting the Do Not Increase Makespan checkbox in the Backwards Schedul- ing section of the Additional Strategies tab. With this setting, the previously optimized makespans of the orders are protected from any change due to backwards scheduling. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 439 6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Expert Settings The Expert Settings tab of the profile, as shown in Figure 6.90, has the settings related to logging the messages generated during the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer run. The Explain Result option will write an explanation log on the changes the operations and orders have gone through during the optimization. Log Result and Log Interim Solution will log the resulting objective function values and the value of the objective functions during the iterations performed by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 6.90 Expert Settings for Logging and Parallel Processing in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Profile Parallel Processing is an important aspect of improving Detailed Scheduling Optimizer performance. But the sizing of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer server should be per- formed to handle such parallel processing workloads. The number of slots that can be used by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is defined in the connection properties in Transaction RCC_CUST. The number of parallel processes defined in the Max.

docs.text: 6 Detailed Scheduling 440 6.5.3 Execute and Monitor Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Runs The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can be executed interactively from the detailed scheduling planning board or from the product planning table. You can also run the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer as a background job via the production planning run. In this section, we’ll walk through each execution option. Detailed Scheduling Optimizer in the Planning Run After materials planning with MRP heuristics and, if required, aligning the receipt and requirement elements with a heuristic (e.g., top-down or bottom-up heuristics), the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can be executed to schedule the orders finitely on the critical resources and to optimize the schedule.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 441 6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer The optimization is available in the production planning run as a function, which isn’t a heuristic. The heuristics are defined using an algorithm in the heuristics customiza- tion (Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSC11), but the functions, such as the optimization, aren’t listed in the heuristics list in the Customizing transaction; instead, they are listed as a function to be selected in the planning run transaction. The global parameters, such as Planning Version , Time Profile , and Propagation Range , need to be set as shown in Figure 6.91.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The optimization function takes only the resources as the object selec- tion. The optimization can be one of the planning steps in the production planning run after the MRP steps (refer to Chapter 5, Section 5.6), or a separate variant can be created for the optimization through the planning run in Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSB1 and can be scheduled as an independent job. Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Execution from the Detailed Scheduling Planning Board From the detailed scheduling planning board, the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can be executed for the resources selected as part of the detailed scheduling planning board.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile settings can be changed interactively in the detailed scheduling planning board before executing the optimization. As Detailed Scheduling Optimizer execution from the detailed scheduling planning board is done in dialog/online mode, it’s recommended to have a smaller value entered for the Maximum Runtime for Detailed Scheduling Optimizer in the settings to avoid any timeout situation. Let’s walk through the following steps to execute the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer from the detailed scheduling planning board: 1.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Click on the Optimize button in the menu bar. 2. In the next screen, shown in Figure 6.92, set the Date / Time for the Start of Horizon and End of Horizon for optimization and the Date / Time for the Start of Optimized Schedule . Make sure the orders and operations you optimize are within the optimi- zation horizon. Operations outside the horizon are considered fixed for optimiza- tion. Click Continue to arrive at the optimization screen. Figure 6.92 Horizon Settings for Optimization Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 6 Detailed Scheduling 442 3. Click on the Optimization Profile button 1 (see Figure 6.93) on the optimization screen to navigate to the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile settings 2 . After making any adjustments to the profile, click on the Copy button 3 to save the values for the current Detailed Scheduling Optimizer run. 4. Click on the Execute button to start the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer run 4 . Figure 6.93 Accessing Optimizer Settings from the Interactive Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Execution The list of resources selected for the optimization can be displayed from the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer screen by clicking on the Display Resource List button.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The reduction in the objective values over time of the optimization is interactively shown in a graphical format. After the optimization is completed, the logs, results, and explanation logs are written if the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile has the rele- vant settings in the Expert Settings tab. The messages generated during the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer run with the statistical information about the resources and activities are displayed on the Optimization screen, as shown in Figure 6.94. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 443 6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Figure 6.94 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Interactive Execution and Results The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer finds an initial solution and then keeps iterating the solution to find better solutions. If End Run after First Solution is set in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile settings ( Basic Settings tab), the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer will stop after the initial solution is found. The Absolute Values button adjusts the solution process graph to show the total value of the objective function calculated.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Switching the display to Weighted Values shows the objective function parameter values by applying the weightage defined in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile. The current solution values are also displayed in the screen, as shown in Figure 6.94. The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Log (see Figure 6.95) collects runtime (performance) information of the individual steps of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer run, includ- ing the reading of parameters for the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer, loading the data from SAP liveCache, executing the genetic algorithm in the Detailed Scheduling Opti- mizer server, and writing the results back to SAP liveCache.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If the explanation log is set as Active in the profile, then an Additional information on optimization run available line is shown in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer log, and the explanation log can be displayed by clicking on the Details icon of the additional information log line. The explanation logs show any orders that are still scheduled with a delay because the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer isn’t able to find a solution to Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 6 Detailed Scheduling 444 resolve this delay. The orders fixed for the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer are shown in the Explanation log with the reason behind such Fixings , as shown in Figure 6.96. Figure 6.95 Accessing the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Explanation Log Figure 6.96 Explanation Log: Fixings Detail © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 445 6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer All the activities rescheduled by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer are listed in the Reschedulings tab of the explanation log. In addition, the interim solutions (the reduc- tion in the objective functions) that the system calculated are shown in the Solutions tab of the explanation log, as shown in Figure 6.97. Figure 6.97 Explanation Log: List of Solutions Calculated In the Sol. (solution) tab of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer output (refer to Figure 6.95), the end results of the objective functions are displayed in a bar chart.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Monitoring Background Optimizer Runs When the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is scheduled as a background job from the production planning run, you can use Transaction /SAPAPO/OPT11 (RCCF [remote con- trol and communication framework] Log Display) to monitor the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer execution status and results. The same transaction can also be used to ana- lyze the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer runs executed interactively by users from the detailed scheduling planning board, the product planning table, or any other applica- tions.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The RCCF log display tool displays all the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer executions, as shown in Figure 6.98. The Appl. column displays the value DPS for the Detailed Sched- uling Optimizer execution and PPO for the Production Planning Optimizer execution. From the list of Detailed Scheduling Optimizer executions, you can click the Log icon under the Mess. Log column to display the application logs with the runtime distribu- tion. Click the magnifying glass icon under Ext.Column to open the explanation log for that execution, as shown in Figure 6.98.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 6 Detailed Scheduling 446 Figure 6.98 RCCF Log Display from Transaction /SAPAPO/OPT11 If you want to check the log file generated by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer engine, select the row from the list of executions, and click on the Display Log File but- ton from the menu bar. The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer log file has all the parame- ters and technical information of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer execution. For the most part, the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer log file content can’t be interpreted by users or consultants.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If you want to terminate the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer execution that is currently running in the system, you can use Transaction /SAPAPO/OPT_STOP (RCCF Active Ses- sion). This may be required if during interactive execution of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer, you observe that the objective functions aren’t reduced after a point in time, and you want to save the solution as of that point and terminate the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer run. To do a graceful termination, where the latest solution is saved and sessions are terminated by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer, you can use the Stop Process button, after selecting the current Detailed Scheduling Optimizer ses- sion. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 447 6.6 Summary If you just want to end the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer session abruptly without saving any solutions, click on the End Process button on the RCCF: Active Session screen, as shown in Figure 6.99. Figure 6.99 Optimizer Session Management This transaction can also be used to monitor and terminate background Detailed Scheduling Optimizer executions, if necessary. Tip The list of orders, operations, and resource utilization also can be checked from Trans- action /SAPAPO/CDPS_REPT (Order and Resource Reporting) or by navigating through SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Production Planning  Reporting  Order and Resource Reporting . 6.6 Summary In this chapter, we’ve covered the detailed scheduling functions and tools in embedded PP/DS.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For scheduling in PP/DS, the strategy settings are critical to ensure the schedule is set per the shop floor setup and requirements. We’ve covered in detail the function- ality and working of various aspects of the strategy settings, including the scheduling modes, scheduling direction, cross-order relationships, and order-internal relation- ships. The same strategy settings are also applied within many of the detailed scheduling heuristics. We’ve covered the basic detailed scheduling heuristics to perform functions such as sequencing, resolving backlogs, and scheduling deallocated operations.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The multilevel scheduling framework heuristics, including the stable forward scheduling heuristic, were also covered in detail in this chapter. The multiresource scheduling heu- ristic can be used to schedule operations on alternative modes, including modes from alternative sources of supply (PDSs). We covered the DDMRP-based prioritized schedul- ing for DDMRP planned products. The detailed scheduling heuristics can be executed via background jobs in the produc- tion planning run as well as in interactive mode. We’ve also covered the interactive detailed scheduling tools, such as the detailed scheduling planning board, the Advanced Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 6 Detailed Scheduling 448 Scheduling Board app, the Monitor Capacity Utilization app, and the resource planning table. We covered the concept of the multilevel time buffers in the detailed scheduling planning board section of this chapter. The important settings, functionalities, and workings of the Detailed Scheduling Opti- mizer and the monitoring of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer runs were also dis- cussed in this chapter. We’ve covered the monitoring of the production planning and detailed scheduling applications via the jobs and logs of those application executions.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: From the business process perspective, it’s important to monitor the accuracy of planning and schedul- ing. The Alert Monitor tool is used for monitoring the accuracy of the plan and sched- ule, as well as to proactively monitor for any supply chain issues. We’ll cover the Alert Monitor in the next chapter. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 449 Chapter 7 The Alert Monitor To identify planning and capacity issues in your embedded PP/DS sys- tem, you can use the Alert Monitor. In this chapter, we’ll walk through the setup steps. Even after the PP/DS heuristics are executed in background mode in regular frequen- cies—typically daily—not all planning and scheduling problems are completely solved by the various executed heuristics or by the PP/DS optimizer. In such cases, the plan- ners and schedulers need to be notified to react to the specific planning and scheduling problems.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These actions can be manual decisions to cancel or delay manufacturing orders, to add or reduce shifts and capacities to handle underutilization or overutiliza- tion of a resource, or to schedule production orders to meet specific customer orders that are delayed when the delay can’t be resolved by the planning and scheduling heu- ristics. For enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems such as SAP ERP, in classic material requirements planning (MRP), exceptions are generated during the MRP run that can be reviewed by the planners.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, these are static exceptions with little flexibility to customize the severity or scenarios for which the exceptions are raised. Delivered standard in PP/DS for SAP S/4HANA (embedded PP/DS), the Alert Monitor is a powerful tool for identifying, monitoring, and managing exception situations in the planning and scheduling processes. The Alert Monitor is embedded into most of PP/DS applications and tools, so planners and schedulers always have visibility of the alerts when they are making any plan or schedule changes in the system.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Alert Monitor also has features to identify the alerts and send notifications to the users for alerts that require immediate action. In this chapter, we’ll cover the details of the Alert Monitor and the steps required to set up the alerts in the system. 7.1 Alert Profiles The PP/DS Alert Monitor works based on alert profiles that are assigned to the overall profile of the PP/DS applications, such as the product view, production planning table, or the detailed scheduling detailed scheduling planning board. In addition, the Alert Monitor itself can be used as a standalone tool to monitor alerts.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 The Alert Monitor 450 Monitor is called from the applications, the alerts relevant to the application are dis- played. For example, when the Alert Monitor is called from the product view, the mate- rial-, location-, and order-related alerts are displayed; likewise, when the Alert Monitor is called from the detailed scheduling planning board, it also shows alerts related to resource capacities. PP/DS supports the following two types of alerts:  Dynamic alerts Most of the alerts configured in PP/DS fall into this category.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Dynamic alerts are gen- erated at the time of the call to a planning or scheduling application or while deter- mining the alerts from the Alert Monitor itself. Dynamic alerts aren’t stored permanently and can’t be set as completed or closed until the underlying planning or scheduling problem is addressed.  Database alerts The use of database alerts in PP/DS is very limited. For example, when a material runs into an error or an exception during the production planning run, a database alert can be created and saved in the system for review and later deletion from the system.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this section, we’ll get started by activating the Alert Monitor and walking through how to set up alerts in the alert profile. 7.1.1 Activate and Access the Alert Monitor PP/DS is delivered by default as an active application to be managed by the Alert Monitor. The activation and deactivation of the Alert Monitor for applications in the SAP S/4HANA system can be done from Customizing menu path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Alert Monitor  Activate/Deactivate Applications in Alert Monitor . As shown in Figure 7.1, the PP/DS application is active as delivered.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When advanced planning is activated in the SAP S/4HANA system, the Alert Monitor can be used in advanced planning, which is embedded PP/DS. Figure 7.1 Activation of PP/DS for the Alert Monitor © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 451 7.1 Alert Profiles The Alert Monitor can be accessed from Transaction /SAPAPO/AMON1 or the SAP Easy Access menu path, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Monitoring  Alert Monitor  Alert Monitor . The initial screen of the Alert Monitor transaction includes Favorite Manage- ment , which we’ll discuss in Section 7.2.1. By clicking on the Alert Profile button, you can navigate to the Alert Profile Maintenance screen, as shown in Figure 7.2. Figure 7.2 Alert Monitor: Alert Profile Maintenance On the navigation tree on the left side of the screen, you’ll see the overall alert profiles and the application-specific profiles.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The individual application profiles, such as alert profiles for PP/DS, are created and then assigned to the overall profiles. The individual application profiles created in the Alert Monitor can be assigned to the application tool profiles, such as profiles for the detailed scheduling planning board and order views in PP/DS. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 The Alert Monitor 452 7.1.2 Create Alert Profile Let’s start by creating the application profiles. Under APO Application-Specific Alert Profiles  APO Production Planning/Detailed Scheduling , right-click on the PP/DS folder, or click on the Create Profile button at the top of the screen to create a new application alert profile, as shown in Figure 7.3. Figure 7.3 Creation of an Application Profile in the Alert Monitor In the Create Alert Monitor Profile popup, select the Application Profile radio button, enter a Profile ID and Description , select Production Planning / Detailed Sch. as the appli- cation, and click on the Create button.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This will load the new profile in the right side of the screen with three tabs: Attributes , Selection , and Overall Alert Profile Assignment . © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 453 7.1 Alert Profiles The next steps are to select the relevant alert types and set up the threshold values for generation of the alerts. Select Alert Types Click on the Selection tab, and you’ll see the list of all available PP/DS alert types deliv- ered in the embedded PP/DS standard system. Under each alert type, there are various alerts available for configuration. Expand the Alert Types folders (see Figure 7.4) to see the individual alerts under them. You can select all the individual alerts under any alert type by setting the Select (selection) flag at the folder level or by setting the Select flag at the individual alert type.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Depending on the alert selected, you define the threshold values for the alerts to be raised. You have the following options:  Information Information alerts are considered the lowest-priority alerts to inform the user of a deviation from the plan or schedule. Users’ reaction to an information alert is optional.  Warning Warning alerts can be raised when the plan or schedule is about to cause a problem in the supply chain. User action is required to react to the warning alert.  Error Error alerts can be raised when a violation of the plan or schedule is imminent or has already happened.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These alerts must be addressed by the planners and schedulers immediately. The default priority ( DP ) assigned to the alert is used by the system when there are no thresholds defined for the alert. For example, for the Product too late alert, if no thresh- old values are maintained for the information, warning, and error alerts, then the default priority assigned to the alert will be shown when there is any delay in covering a requirement element. The default priority of the alerts can be set for the alerts under the Customizing node: SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Alert Monitor  Maintain Prioritization of Alert Types .

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Click on the New Entries button, and using the value help (F4) , you can select the alert item for which you want to set a default priority and set the Priority as Information , Warning , or Error (see upper-left area of Figure 7.4). The default priority will only be used when no threshold is defined or for alerts that aren’t relevant to threshold definitions (e.g., Receipt with Violated Resource Network ). When there is no threshold defined for the alert—in Figure 7.4 for the Product too late (dynamic pegging) alert—the priority from Customizing ( 3 Information ) is used in the alert profile, as shown in the lower-right screen in Figure 7.4.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 The Alert Monitor 454 Figure 7.4 Customizing Setting for the Default Alert Priority Set Up Alerts Now, let’s go through the steps to set up an alert in the alert profile. Let’s use the Requirement/Receipt Alerts alert type. Product too late (dynamic pegging) is one of the alerts available under this alert type. You set the Select flag at the alert level, as shown previously in Figure 7.4, and then click on the individual threshold buttons to set the values on the Enter a Threshold Value popup. If the delay for a requirement element exceeds the threshold set in the alert profile, the system will raise an alert accordingly.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the example shown in Figure 7.5, the system will create an information alert if the delay in hours (in covering the requirement element) is more than 24 hours, a warning if the delay is more than 48 hours, and an error if the delay is more than 72 hours. Figure 7.5 Setting Up Alert Thresholds in the Alert Monitor Application Profile © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 455 7.1 Alert Profiles After the required alerts are selected and the thresholds are defined, the following set- tings can be maintained in the Selection tab of the alert profile, as shown in Figure 7.6 (accessed by scrolling down on the screen). Certain settings are only relevant if a cer- tain alert or alert type is selected. We’ll cover some of the important settings that are valid for many of the alerts and alert types.  Network Alerts Network alerts are used to raise the alert at the higher level of the pegging hierarchy to notify the planner of an alert raised in a lower level of the hierarchy.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, a delay alert raised in the raw material coverage can be shown as a network alert of the sales order of the finished material. Select the Display Requirements with Prob- lems in Order Network option to generate an alert when any of the pegged require- ment elements raises an alert and/or the Display Receipts with Problems in Order Network to generate an alert when any of the pegged receipt elements raises an alert. The number of pegging levels the system needs to evaluate the alert for the lower levels is set in the Search Depth field.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, if there are 10 levels of bills of materials (BOMs) and the corresponding pegging network created in PP/DS, and if the Search Depth is set to 3 , only the alerts raised within the top three levels are prop- agated to the top level as a network alert. Note As the network alerts are performance intensive, only use them for specific scenarios as required. Restrict the Search Depth to a minimum number so that the alerts aren’t calculated for the entire pegging network of a product when accessing the product from tools such as the product view.  Selection of Location Products In this area, the selection of location products and available-to-promise (ATP) cate- gories are defined that are relevant for calculating the alerts.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Location Products selection is only applicable in determining the alerts in the Alert Monitor. When the alert profile is used in another application, such as the product view or product overview, the product location selection from the alert pro- file isn’t considered, and the selection entered in the application is considered. To define a set of location products for which the alerts need to be calculated, click on the Selection icon next to the Location Products field, as shown in Figure 7.6. In the next screen for the Selection Object , enter the selection criteria.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, for setting location selections, double-click on the Location Name field under the Loca- tions node 1 . Enter the location to be selected in the Value From and Value To fields 2 . After the selection condition is maintained, it will be moved to the top of the list 3 , and further conditions can be maintained similarly. The checkmark 4 shows that this selection parameter ( Location Name , in our example) has existing selection Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 The Alert Monitor 456 conditions, and the first value of the selection condition from the list of conditions 3 is displayed in the From and To columns next to the checkbox 4 . Figure 7.6 Location Material Selection Restriction in the Alert Profile Tip If multiple values are maintained for a selection (location or product), you’ll see one value on the screen, and the selection parameter maintained (green checkmark) is set. Double-click on the row to see all the values maintained in the selection. After entering the required selection conditions, click on the Save Selection button, and enter a name for the selection.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The name of the selection is transferred back to the Alert Profile screen. For the ATP Categories , similar selection conditions can be set to include or exclude certain receipt and requirement elements based on their ATP category. The selection of the ATP category set in the alert profile will be applied irrespective of the PP/DS tool in which the alert profile is used. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 457 7.1 Alert Profiles  Selection of Resources Under Selection of Resources , you can maintain the restrictions for selection of resources considered for the alert types that are relevant to resources (e.g., average resource utilization). After all the required settings are maintained, save the application profile in the Alert Monitor by clicking on the Save button. This application alert profile can be used in the PP/DS planning and scheduling tools. In the Attributes tab of the alert profile, the basic attributes, such as the description of the alert profile, can be maintained.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Other attributes are also displayed, such as the user who created and/or changed the alert profile and the creation and change time stamps. After the alert profile is assigned to the overall profile as discussed in the next section, the Overall Alert Profile Assignment tab appears in the overall profiles to which the alert profile is assigned. 7.1.3 Create Overall Profile To monitor the alerts from the Alert Monitor or to generate and send notifications to users for the PP/DS alerts, an overall alert profile must be created and assigned to all the relevant application alert profiles and additional settings.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can create the overall alert profile by following the steps to create an application alert profile (Section 7.1.2), but select the Overall Profile option in the Create Alert Monitor Profile popup, as shown in Figure 7.7. In the overall profile, maintain the Planning Version that will be used to determine the alerts, and assign the Alert Profile that will be used to calculate the alerts. The period for which the alerts should be generated when determining the alerts in the background or from the Alert Monitor is defined in the overall profile.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To define a rela- tive period from the current date, select the Relative Time Interval radio button. Then select the period type ( Months , Weeks , Days , or Hours ), and define the duration. The Offset fields can be used to move the current period by the offset defined. For example, if Months is selected as the period, “3” is entered as the duration, and “-3” is entered as the Offset , the alerts will be calculated for the past three months and the future three months. Note The settings made in the overall alert profile are only used by the Alert Monitor when alerts are determined within the Alert Monitor.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For other PP/DS applications (e.g., prod- uct view, detailed scheduling planning board, etc.), the application-specific alert pro- files are selected, and the selection of planning version, materials, locations, resources, and time horizons are determined by the application to generate alerts based on the application-specific alert profile. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 The Alert Monitor 458 Figure 7.7 Creation of the Overall Alert Profile in the Alert Monitor 7.1.4 Transport Profiles The overall profiles, alert profiles, and selection profiles created in the Alert Monitor can be transported to other systems in the system landscape. To do so, execute Trans- action /SAPAPO/AMON1 to arrive at the Alert Profile Maintenance screen. You can gen- erate transport requests using the Transport Profile button. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 459 7.2 Alert Monitoring 7.2 Alert Monitoring You have a few different options when it comes to monitoring alerts using the Alert Monitor. In this section, we’ll cover the monitoring of alerts from the Alert Monitor, alert generation in the background, and Alert Monitoring in PP/DS applications. 7.2.1 Monitor Alerts from the Alert Monitor Overall alert profiles can be assigned to your user as favorites so that the alerts can be generated and monitored from the central alert monitoring (Transaction /SAPAPO/ AMON3). The favorites are managed from the Alert Monitor transaction (Transaction /SAPAPO/ AMON1).

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To manage the favorite overall alert profiles, launch Transaction /SAPAPO/ AMON1, and click the Favorite Management button (see Figure 7.8 1 ). In the Alert Mon- itor Administration popup, the Manage Favorites tab is opened by default. Select the overall alert profile from the right side of the selection window ( Worklist of Overall Pro- files ), and move it to the left side ( Favorites ) using the arrow button, as shown in Figure 7.8. Click the Save and Exit button when you’re done. After doing this, when you launch the Alert Monitor (Transaction /SAPAPO/AMON3), you can select the favorite from the dropdown menu 2 , and the system will determine and display all the alerts per the application profiles and the selection conditions main- tained in the overall profile and the application profile.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 7.8 Alert Monitor: Managing Favorites The Alert Monitor’s display settings for the hierarchy in which the alerts are displayed can be customized from the user settings. From Transaction /SAPAPO/AMON3, choose Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 The Alert Monitor 460 Environment  User-Specific Display Hierarchies , as shown in Figure 7.9 1 . Select and move the fields from the Possible Nodes per Alert View to the User-Specific Display Hierarchies pane 2 in the order in which you want the alerts to be displayed. Click on the Redetermine Alerts button in the initial screen of the Alert Monitor 3 , and the determined alerts per the overall profile are arranged per the hierarchy set in this set- ting. The number of alerts per hierarchy node—in this example, location PPS2 4 , prod- uct identifier S4HANA_PPDS_003 5 , and alert type Product too late (dynamic pegging) 6 —is displayed.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can click on the number of alerts to navigate to the alert details 7 . Figure 7.9 Alert Monitor Display Settings and Monitoring Alerts from the Alert Monitor From the alert details shown in the Alert Monitor screen (see Figure 7.9), there are options to hide the alerts up to a certain duration. The alerts can be sent via email to email addresses. You can forward the alert to another user, and the forwarded alerts will be displayed in the receiving user’s Alert Monitor. You can navigate to the product view transaction from the Alert Monitor to take actions on the alerts. 7.2.2 Generate Alerts in the Background For alert profiles that are time intensive (with a lot of selection objects and many alert types activated in the alert profile), it’s possible to generate the alerts in the back- ground and display them to the users.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To set up the overall alert profiles for processing in the background, you use the Alert Monitor transaction (Transaction /SAPAPO/AMON1). As shown in Figure 7.10, click on the Favorite Management button, and navigate to the Alerts in Background tab 1 . In this screen, click the New button 2 , enter the Ov. Alert Profile 3 for which the alerts are © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 461 7.2 Alert Monitoring to be determined in the background, and click the Save and Exit 4 button. Then, in the bottom of the same screen shown in Figure 7.11, maintain the Priority for processing, Start Date , and StartTime . Enter the Repeat Intrvl [h] in which the background alerts are to be generated and the FctryCalendar , which is used to calculate the date and time of the frequency interval. If you want to trigger an email notification, enter an E-Mail Address . Click the Save and Exit 4 button, and the list of alerts determined in the back- ground will be sent via email to the recipient if an email address has been entered.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 7.10 Alert Determination in the Background: Setup Figure 7.11 Alert Determination in the Background: User-Specific Settings Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 The Alert Monitor 462 After defining the settings for the background alert generation, you must schedule the background job with ABAP program /SAPAPO/READ_ALERTS_BATCH. The frequency of the schedule of this program should match the repeat interval maintained in the set- tings for the background alert generation. For example, if the frequency interval in the settings is defined as 4 hours, and the job /SAPAPO/READ_ALERTS_BATCH is sched- uled only every 8 hours, the alerts in the background will only be generated every 8 hours.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The job looks for all background overall alert profiles that are due to be redetermined per their repeat interval and then regenerates the alerts for all such profiles. In the pro- gram screen, you can either select All Due Overall Profiles or specific Selected Overall Profiles , which can be defined in the selection screen shown in Figure 7.12. If you select the Ignore Due Dates checkbox, irrespective of the repeat interval defined in the alert profile background settings, alerts will be generated for all profiles.

docs.bookTitle: PP-DS with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 7.12 Alert Generation in the Background: Selection Options for the Batch Job You can save the settings made in this screen as a variant by clicking on the Save as Variant button.
