docs.text: 119 3.12 Confirmation If the Process Control field is left blank, then the system performs all activities online and immediately. Refer to Section 3.12.4 for how to control the settings as online, immediate, or in the background. The Checks area controls whether the system should ensure that the user adheres to the Operation Sequence , with varying degrees of controls, from no check to warning to error. Similarly, if the minimum and maximum tolerance limits in the Underdelivery and Overdelivery fields are maintained in the Work Scheduling view of the material master, the system copies this information during production order creation.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When users are performing confirmation of the order and entering the yield, the system checks to see if it’s within the tolerance limits and acts according to the level of control set. If there is an error message, the system won’t allow users to proceed further or save the confirmation until the error is corrected. The system considers the sum of yield and rework quantities for underdelivery/overdelivery calculation. Note During the SAP S/4HANA implementation project, you should discuss and come to agreement with the client on the level of control required and then make the necessary settings.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In general, the control should be neither too loose nor too stringent to meet the day-to-day working needs of business process owners. The level of control also depends on the stability of production processes and business maturity to reflect that optimum production should be within the defined tolerance limits. If there are large variations and deviations in yield, then a less stringent control will suffice. Tips and Tricks If the underdelivery or overdelivery control is set as an error setting, then the system won’t allow the production supervisor to exceed the defined tolerance limits.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To attend to this, you should make changes in the Goods Receipt tab of the production order and perform the confirmation process again. This enables the user to deviate from a one- time or limited deviation to the standard tolerance limits. In the Results Rec. (QM) field and for in-process (during production) inspection, the sys- tem creates a quality inspection lot for one or more operations. This is an integration point between PP and QM processes. It’s possible to control whether the system should check to see if the inspection results of an operation for the inspection lot are already entered before it allows users to perform the confirmation of the next operation.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the Goods Movements area of the screen, you should check the box to set the neces- sary controls for whether the system should perform goods movement for all of the components. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration 120 Choose the Individual Entry General tab, and the screen shown in Figure 3.43 will appear. Here, select the Confirmation Type that the system makes available during the confirmation process. It can be a Partial confirmation , Final confirmation , or Automatic final confirmation . Figure 3.43 Individual Entry General Tab of Confirmation Parameters The settings depend on how frequently the business performs the confirmation pro- cess. If there are large and frequent numbers of confirmations against a production order, then it makes sense to set Partial confirmation as the default.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When performing the final confirmation against the production order, you should manually set the Con- firmation Type to Final confirmation . For Automatic final confirmation , the system checks whether the confirmed quantity is equal to or less than the production order quantity. If it’s less, then the system automatically sets the status to Partial confirma- tion , whereas if the confirmation quantity is equal to or greater than the production order quantity, then it automatically sets the status to Final confirmation .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For Actual Costs and Goods Movements in the Error Handling/Logs area, you should set whether the system should terminate the confirmation processing until the error is corrected. Choose the Indiv. Entry of Operation w. Init. Screen tab, and the screen shown in Figure 3.44 will appear. The system offers a large number of checkboxes to facilitate data entry work. For example, if you check the Propose box in the Quantities area, the system will © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 121 3.12 Confirmation propose the quantity that a production supervisor needs to confirm for an operation or an order. Check the Display boxes to display any information for reference purposes. We suggest that you click the Actual Data radio button in the Screen Control Time Ticket area so that the system will automatically propose the data (quantity and activi- ties) that needs to be confirmed. Otherwise, on the actual confirmation screen, you can manually click the Actual Data button to view the data that needs to be confirmed.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 3.44 Indiv. Entry of Operation w. Init. Screen Tab of Confirmation Parameters 3.12.3 Single Entry Screen for Confirmation It’s also possible to control how the system displays the information on the confirma- tion screen (use Transaction CO11N for discrete manufacturing or Transaction COR6N for process industries). In this step, you set up a profile and assign that profile to an individual user in the CORUPROF user parameter. A profile for a single-entry screen controls the user-defined layout for confirmation.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the layout, you define the fields and the sequence in which they appear on the confir- mation screen. For example, if the production supervisor likes to have a provision to enter long text in the confirmation screen to enable the process operator to write extensive shift details, you select the relevant option. Similarly, you can set a control for whether the system should list the activities to be confirmed as individual fields or in a tabular form. To define a single-entry screen for confirmation, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Shop Floor Control  Operations  Confirmation  Single Screen Entry  Define Single Screen Entry or use Transaction OPK0.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On the screen shown in Figure 3.45, you define the header area so that during the actual confirmation, the system will bring up the relevant fields so the user can enter the details. For example, choose whether the system should only allow Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration 122 the user to enter the confirmation number at the header level or should allow the user to enter the production order number together with its operation. Tips and Tricks At any time, to see how the chosen option will look on the confirmation screen, you can choose Display Detail Areas (the glasses icon), and the system will show you a preview. When choosing the dropdown list options in the Area section (see Figure 3.45), you can select from a large number of options, such as quantities, activities, HR data, short and long text entry provision, dates, and even external IDs if a third-party product is used to integrate the confirmation process with the production process.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can also choose the sequence in which these details appear on the confirmation screen. Figure 3.45 Single-Entry Screen of Confirmation In the Pushbutton Text fields, you can define the text of the pushbuttons to suit your business needs. Checking the Closed box enables a minimized (closed) view of the information on the confirmation screen, which can be opened when the production supervisor is ready for data entry. Tips and Tricks To check that settings are correct, with no duplication or other layout error, you can click the Detail Areas button to make a consistency check.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 123 3.12 Confirmation Note You can activate the CONFPP07 enhancement if there’s a need for more than one reason for variances. As a practical workaround (without activating the enhancement), on the screen shown in Figure 3.45 under Detail Areas , you can add an option that says “Addi- tional data: Reason” as many times as needed from the dropdown list. 3.12.4 Time of Confirmation If there is a large number of confirmations that the production supervisor needs to per- form on a daily basis, then it’s practical to perform confirmations (such as quantity updates or backflushes) in the background, when there is less of a workload on the sys- tem.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, if an immediate update of all quantity and activity data posted is required, then you should make the necessary settings. These are the same settings used for the Process Control field at the beginning of Section 3.12.2. To set up the time of confirmation, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Shop Floor Control  Operations  Confirmation  Single Screen Entry  Define Time for Confirmation Processes or use Transaction OPKC. On the screen shown in Figure 3.46, choose when the system should update the following:  Auto GR (automatic GR)  Backflush  Actual Costs Figure 3.46 Process Control for Confirmation The available update options are listed here:  Immediately Online  Immediately in Update Program  Later in Background Job We’ll cover how to set up background jobs in Section 3.16.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration 124 3.13 Reasons for Variances During confirmation against the production order, when the yield, scrap, and rework is recorded, the user can assign a reason for any variance between planned and actual production. For example, assume that due to machine malfunction or defective com- ponents, the actual production was less than planned. In that case, the user can assign the specific reason for this deviation or variance. Similarly, when entering the scrap quantity, the user can give the reason for the variance.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Later, when executing the pro- duction order information system (Transaction COOIS) or even when using embedded SAP Fiori analytics, the user can filter out the information based on the reason for vari- ance. This helps clarify the reasons behind the problems and helps the production supervisor take corrective or preventive actions. As a PP consultant during an SAP S/4HANA implementation project, you should main- tain a complete list of plant-related reasons for variances and configure them accord- ingly in the system.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You should also perform multiple partial confirmations and enter different reasons for variance for each deviation. Note If there’s a business need to enter multiple reasons for variances, you should engage an ABAP resource and activate the CONFPP07 enhancement. You can also assign a user status to a reason for variance to add further control in the confirmation. Note To set up a new status profile, use Transaction BS02. Figure 3.47 Reasons for Variance © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 125 3.15 Defining Print Control To configure a new reason for the variance for a given plant, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Shop Floor Control  Operations  Confirmation  Define Reasons for Vari- ances or use Transaction OPK5. Figure 3.47 lists the reasons for variance for Plant 1710 . Once you select a specific reason for variance and click the User Status folder, the system prompts you to enter the status profile and then the user status. 3.14 Trigger Points Trigger points are automatic functions that the system can perform when it’s able to meet a user-defined condition.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, when a user releases an operation, the sys- tem can automatically release all preceding operations via a trigger point. Minimal configuration steps are involved in trigger points: you simply define the trigger point usage and then define a group for the trigger points. The Trigger Point Usage field provides a unique identification to list trigger points that will have a common usage. This enables a production supervisor to quickly select the relevant trigger point based on its usage. To define the (standard) trigger points usage, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Shop Floor Control  Master Data  Trigger Point  Define (Standard) Trigger Point Usage .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On the initial screen, enter an alphanu- meric key and give a short description of the trigger point usage. You can group all of the trigger points together and then assign them to an operation. Doing so saves you the time and effort involved in individually creating and assigning trigger points. To define a group for standard trigger points, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Shop Floor Control  Master Data  Trigger Point  Define Group for Standard Trigger Points . On the initial screen, enter an alphanumeric key and give a short description of the trigger points group. 3.15 Defining Print Control During the production process, there’s often a business need to print several shop floor papers—for example, a production order, a pick list, and a GI slip.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The SAP S/4HANA system offers standard layouts for each shop floor paper. During an SAP S/4HANA sys- tem project implementation, you should engage an ABAP resource to develop new scripts or modify the scripts of the shop floor papers to fulfill a client’s requirements. We recommend that you to discuss and evaluate all of the shop floor papers needed as printouts with the client. For example, you can eliminate the layout development of a confirmation and its printout requirement if there’s an SAP S/4HANA system terminal from which to make live data entries, or you can use an upload program to automati- cally enter the confirmation.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Discrete Manufacturing Configuration 126 To make the necessary settings to print shop floor papers, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Shop Floor Control  Operations  Define Print Controls or use Transaction OPK8. The resulting screen, shown in Figure 3.48, lists the shop floor papers that you can individually work on and for which you can make the desired settings. Figure 3.48 Printing Shop Floor Papers Note Chapter 6 shows how we used list LG01 ( Object list ), shown on the right-hand side of Figure 3.48, to get printouts with the SAP S/4HANA system standard layout. 3.16 Background Jobs To optimize the SAP system’s resources, which will help to improve performance and minimize undue burdens, there are several processes that you can set up as back- ground jobs.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A background job enables you to define the frequency with which the sys- tem automatically performs the desired function without manual intervention. For example, if MRP is run on a weekly basis and planners are generally satisfied with the results, then you can set up a background job to automatically convert planned orders into production orders. To set up a background job, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Shop Floor Control  Operations  Schedule Background Jobs or use Transaction SM36. We suggest that you choose the Job Wizard icon and use the wizard because it provides a step-by-step approach for setting up a background job.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Table 3.1 lists the program names of selected background jobs that you can set up, and the system asks for this information. Before setting up the background job, you should also set up the variant of the background job so that the system processes only the relevant data. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 127 3.17 Summary Tips and Tricks On the initial screen of Transaction SE38, you should enter a program name listed in Table 3.1 and choose Execute . The system then navigates to the screen where you can set screen parameters and save them by pressing (Ctrl) + (S) or choosing Goto  Vari- ants  Save as Variant . You can read additional documentation on the background program by choosing the Information icon, where available. 3.17 Summary The logical and sequential configuration steps that we undertook in this chapter will enable a production planner and production supervisor to perform the same set of steps and activities in configuration steps in process manufacturing.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If they follow all of the steps covered in this chapter in a sequential and logical order, then all of the major business processes and scenarios of production involved in production orders (shop floor control) will be covered. docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 129 Chapter 4 Process Manufacturing Configuration Configuration basics in process manufacturing are generally the same as in discrete manufacturing. However, the process management func- tionality demands in-depth coverage because it’s unique to process manufacturing only. The configuration basics of process manufacturing are similar to those in discrete manufacturing. For example, the steps to define order types, assign number ranges, and define the screen layout for confirmation are the same in both production types.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We recommend reading Chapter 3 and Chapter 6 for an in-depth understanding of the configuration settings and business processes, respectively. The focus of this chapter is primarily on the configuration that is unique only to pro- cess manufacturing—for example, the master recipe profile that is only used in process manufacturing. At the same time, this chapter gives extensive coverage to the configu- ration area of process management. We’ll start by covering the standard settings and tools that can be used to optimize most of the configuration work related to process management.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We then cover process messages and process message categories, followed by control recipes and process integration sheets. Next, we’ll discuss the process instructions, types, and categories, as well as how the system can facilitate several configuration steps using wizards. Using the scope of generation functionality further reduces the data maintenance efforts involved in process management. We’ll also cover background jobs for sending control recipes and how to send process messages back to the SAP S/4HANA system as sched- uled (background) jobs.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The concepts and basics we cover in this chapter will enable you to implement a newer and more user-friendly functionality of process management known as execution steps (XSteps). It’s also possible to transition from process management to XSteps and still use all the configuration steps that are discussed in this chapter. We’ll also show you how the entire configuration undertaken so far facilitates the quick definition, simulation, and activation of process manufacturing cockpits. We present a simple example of how to use a self-defined process instruction type and incorporate its details into the PI sheet.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When the system sends process messages back to its pre- defined destination, it also sends the details of the self-defined process instruction characteristic. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Process Manufacturing Configuration 130 Note Refer to Chapter 1 for a features comparison among discrete manufacturing, process manufacturing, and REM, as well as how to decide which manufacturing type is most relevant for a given industry. Let’s get started. 4.1 Master Data in Process Industries The master data in process manufacturing is similar to the master data in discrete man- ufacturing. For detailed configuration settings and business processes, refer to Chapter 3 and Chapter 6, respectively.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The following master data are specific to process industries and will be the main topics covered in this section:  Resource  Materials list (BOM)  Master recipe  Production version The resource in process manufacturing is similar to the work center in discrete manu- facturing, and the creation of the materials list in process manufacturing is similar to the creation of the BOM in discrete manufacturing, so we won’t cover these master data items here (see Chapter 3 and Chapter 6 for those). For process industries, it’s man- datory to have a master recipe and a production version in the system.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: While the con- figuration of the master recipe has some uniqueness and is covered in this chapter, the creation of the production version is once again the same for discrete manufacturing and therefore isn’t covered here. 4.1.1 Master Recipe Profile Although most of the details in the master recipe profile are the same as in routing, the one exception is the option available for process management. Depending on the mas- ter recipe profile used during master recipe creation, the system offers the following options for process management:  Process Instructions  XSTEPS  XSTEPS OPTIONAL © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 131 4.1 Master Data in Process Industries If you choose the XSTEPS OPTIONAL option when creating the master recipe, then the system provides you with the option to select either Process Instructions or XSTEPS . You cannot use both of them at the same time. In addition, if you use process instruc- tions when creating the master recipe and the company later decides that it wants to transition to XSteps, the system will issue a warning message saying that it won’t be possible to revert back to process instructions after saving the master recipe with XSteps activated.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To set up the master recipe profile, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production Planning for Process Industries  Master Data  Master Recipe  Settings for the Task List Type  Define Master Recipe Profiles with Default Values or use Transaction OPN1. On the initial screen, choose Profile/Recipe , which brings up the overview of the master recipe profile with three entries. Select Profile PI01_XS and choose the Details icon, which leads you to the screen shown in Figure 4.1. Here, you can update the available fields, which then apply when a master recipe is created.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Assigning a profile is a mandatory requirement when creating a mas- ter recipe. Notice the Process instruction maintenance dropdown list in the Process management area and the available options, including XSTEPS OPTIONAL . Figure 4.1 Master Recipe Profile Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Process Manufacturing Configuration 132 4.1.2 Task List Assignment to Material Types Task list type 2 is used for a master recipe. When a process order is created, the system looks for the relevant master recipe and for task list type 2 to assign it to the process order. A task list consists of operations, phases, activities, control keys, and the relation- ship to the BOM. If a company has material types other than those available in a stan- dard SAP S/4HANA system, then you should maintain the task list relationship for each material type.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To define the task list assignment to the material type, follow menu path SAP IMG  Pro- duction Planning for Process Industries  Master Data  Master Recipe  Settings for the Task List Type  Assign Material Types . On the screen shown in Figure 4.2, choose New Entries to define the task list type ( TLType ) as 2 and the company-specific material types used in process manufacturing. Figure 4.2 Task List Assignment with Material Type 4.1.3 Task List Status The standard SAP S/4HANA system offers task list statuses to cater to various business scenarios.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, when creating a master recipe of a material in the initial stages, you set the status to 1, which is for Creation . The system won’t make this task list avail- able for selection during process order creation or in production version creation. You can configure a task list that’s specific to product cost controlling, and in that case, it becomes available for costing purposes but not for production. To define a task list status at the header level, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production Planning for Process Industries  Master Data  Master Recipe  Data for the Recipe Header  Define Recipe Status or use Transaction OP46.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 4.3 shows that task list Status 4 enables a user to perform all of the steps, such as using it in production ( RelInd ), using it for costing ( Cstng ), and performing consistency checks ( Cons.chk. ). You can perform a consistency check during master recipe creation to enable the system to point out any deviations or shortcomings in the master recipe that can be dealt with before saving. You can even save a master recipe if the system issues warning or error messages that occur during consistency checks, and then, you can correct the errors later on. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 133 4.2 Order Type–Dependent Parameters Figure 4.3 Task List Status 4.2 Order Type–Dependent Parameters For better control of various order types configured in the SAP S/4HANA system, you can create different order types within a plant. For example, there may be one order type for finished goods, another for semifinished goods, and a third one to capture rework details from normal production. Each order type can have a separate number range and its own order type settings. Furthermore, you can control authorizations to users based on the order type and plant combination.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In order type–dependent param- eters, you should make settings that are applicable each time a user creates a process order for that specific order type and plant combination. To set up order type–dependent parameters, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production Planning for Process Industries  Process Order  Master Data  Order  Define Order Type-Dependent Parameters or use Transaction COR4. On the initial screen, select Plant 1710 and Order Type PI01 , which leads you to the Master Data tab. We’ll discuss each of the tabs for configuring parameters in the following sections. 4.2.1 Master Data Figure 4.4 shows the Master Data tab of order type–dependent parameters.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Here, you select Automatic Selection of Production Version from the Production Version drop- down list, and the system assigns the first available and valid production version during the planning and production execution steps. Alternatively, you can use the Manual Selection of Production Version option, and the system will open a popup during pro- cess order creation to enable the user to select a production version manually. If you check the Approval Required box, then the process order must be approved before it can be released.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When a user creates a process order, the system will require the order to be approved before it will allow the user to release it. Similarly, if you set up the automatic process order release during creation (in the production scheduling pro- file), the system will overrule the automatic release settings if the approval process is set up (see Section 4.3). Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Process Manufacturing Configuration 134 Figure 4.4 Order Type–Dependent Parameters: Master Data Tab Note To grant approval to a process order during its creation, follow menu path Process Order  Functions  Approval  Individual Approval . 4.2.2 Planning In the Planning tab, check the Scrap box if a business process has a need for it (see Figure 4.5). Normally, in process industries, there’s less need to use or record the scrap option. For example, in the fertilizer industry, any visible or overflow material (spilled-over material) is automatically sent back in the production process chain, so there is no scrap recording during production.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, in the steel rerolling industry, it’s com- mon to have production scrap, so the Scrap option needs to be activated in such busi- ness scenarios. For a PP-QM integration scenario, you assign the relevant inspection type for in-process inspection in the Planning tab and make settings for batch determi- nation. Chapter 10 covers batch management. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 135 4.2 Order Type–Dependent Parameters Figure 4.5 Planning Tab 4.2.3 Implementation In the Implementation tab, make sure to check all the relevant boxes, especially in the Shop Floor Information System and Documentation of Goods Movement areas (see Figure 4.6). Checking these boxes will enable the system to update the LIS, and the user will be able to see the documented goods movements (GI or GR) for the process orders. The documented goods movements in the process order information system (Transac- tion COOISPI) also will show all the relevant details.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Process Manufacturing Configuration 136 4.2.4 Cost Accounting In the Cost Accounting tab, we suggest that you coordinate with a controlling resource (who is responsible for cost object controlling) to ensure that the necessary configura- tion settings are in place. 4.3 Production Scheduling Profile The production scheduling profile in process manufacturing is similar to that in dis- crete manufacturing. However, in process manufacturing, it provides an option to automatically generate the control recipe when a process order is released.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A control recipe enables the process operator to record important plant parameters. We cover the details of control recipes in Section 4.4.1. To set up the production scheduling profile, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production Planning for Process Industries  Process Order  Master Data  Define Production Sched- uling Profile or use Transaction CORY (see Figure 4.7). On the initial screen, select Plant 1710 and PS Profile (production scheduling profile) YB0002 . In this example, the Generate Cntrl Recipe box in the On Release area (within the Automatic Actions area) isn’t checked.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In Chapter 7, we’ll show you how to manually generate a control recipe when a process order is released. Figure 4.7 Production Scheduling Profile © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 137 4.4 Process Management Using Transaction MM02 to change the material master, you assign the production scheduling profile in the Work scheduling tab (see Figure 4.8). Whenever a process order of this material and plant combination is created, the system automatically trig- gers the settings made in the production scheduling profile. Figure 4.8 Production Scheduling Profile in Material Master 4.4 Process Management Process management falls within the purview of PP-PI, which covers all the important elements involved in recording the process parameter information and performing specific functions.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Creating a process order forms the basis of the generation of the control recipe (see Figure 4.9). Figure 4.9 Process Management Overview Process Planning Process Order Further Message Destinations Process Management Process Control Execution E-1 E-2 E-3 SAP S/4HANA or External System Control Recipe Process Messages PI Sheet Process Control System Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Process Manufacturing Configuration 138 The control recipe is sent to the process control in the form of a PI sheet, and the pro- cess operator not only follows the instructions given on the PI sheet but also fills in the PI sheet with relevant plant parameters and other important data. The process opera- tor then returns the PI sheet as a process message to either the SAP S/4HANA system or an external system.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Although this section applies more to the business process side of process manage- ment, it’s important for you to gain a basic understanding of the concepts and termi- nologies used in the rest of the chapter before we move on to discussing some standard settings and tools. 4.4.1 Key Terminology The important terms used in process management are as follows:  Control recipe destination The control recipe destination specifies the technical address to which a control rec- ipe is transferred. An operation in a master recipe can have several phases, and each phase can have a different control recipe destination.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the process order, one con- trol recipe is created for each control recipe destination. Therefore, if there are three different phases, it’s possible to have three different control recipe destinations (e.g., mixing, blending, liquid ammonia sections). Typically, at the process order release, the system creates control recipes for each control recipe destination in the process order. All phases of a process order with the same control recipe destination are combined into the same control recipe. A control recipe destination defines whether the process instruction of a phase is transferred to an external system (a process control system) or is converted to a PI sheet for a line operator.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It also specifies which system or line operator executes the process instructions of a phase.  Process instruction characteristic A released characteristic within a characteristic group is available for use in process instruction. Process instruction characteristics are allocated to process instructions either directly in the master recipe or by process instruction category. Process instruction, together with the corresponding characteristic value, determines the information transferred or requested—that is, the status of the control recipe.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It also determines how the requested data is processed (e.g., the message category to be used to report the data).  Process instruction category The process instruction category specifies the type of process instruction (i.e., pro- cess parameter or process data request). It also specifies the characteristics of this process instruction—that is, information to be sent via this instruction.  Process message characteristic A released characteristic within the characteristic group is available for use in process messages.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 139 4.4 Process Management categories. Process message characteristics, together with the corresponding charac- teristic values, determine the content of the process message. The process message can be sent to an external system, SAP Office mail recipients, or custom-defined ABAP tables.  Process message category The process message category specifies the characteristics to be allocated to a pro- cess message—that is, the information to be sent. It also specifies the message desti- nations for the process message.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Every process message sent via process manage- ment must be assigned to a process message category.  PI sheet A PI sheet is used as an input and output form for plant parameters and is customiz- able according to individual production processes. This customized PI sheet is part of either the configuration activity or master data management. Due to its intuitive features, a PI sheet can be used for many functions, such as calling up a transaction while remaining in a PI sheet, displaying documents, recording shift highlights, posting GI/GR, undertaking confirmation of a phase, calculating results, and jump- ing to record results for quality inspections.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To create a custom process message or a custom process instruction, a user can lever- age knowledge of and experience in creating characteristics in the classification sys- tem. The only difference between classification and process message/instruction cre- ation is that the former doesn’t offer the option to incorporate details specific to pro- cess management. In the example in the following section, we’ll show you how to use process instruction to fetch the Process Order Start Date field from the process order automatically and integrate it into the PI sheet.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Now, let’s discuss the important one-time settings to make in the SAP S/4HANA system to activate process management. This entails a sequence of steps in which the standard settings delivered by the SAP S/4HANA system are copied to specific plants. 4.4.2 Standard Settings and Tools The system offers a large number of standard process messages, process message cate- gories, process instructions, and process instruction categories. These are all available in the SAP S/4HANA system’s plant 0001. You can copy all of these standard settings from plant 0001, except for process instruction categories, which you’ll need to copy manually.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: An easier way to do this is to copy the SAP S/4HANA system reference plant 0001 to the desired plants. You’ll need to perform a few important steps in the right sequence to ensure that min- imal work and effort are involved in integrating process management in the business processes. Use menu path SAP IMG  Production Planning for Process Industries  Pro- cess Management  Standard Settings , as shown in Figure 4.10. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Process Manufacturing Configuration 140 Figure 4.10 Standard Settings in Process Management Next, follow these steps: 1. Use Transaction O23C to transport predefined characteristics from the SAP system reference client, which is 0001, to the SAP S/4HANA system client. The Copy Object Lists screen appears when you successfully perform the first step. 2. Access Transaction O22C to transport preconfigured process message categories from the SAP S/4HANA system reference plant 0001 to the desired plants. The screen shown in Figure 4.11 appears after you enter the target plant. 3.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Enter the target plant (in this example, “1710”). Use the Copy icon to copy it to the tar- get plant. The system will then issue a warning message: The SAP standard settings are copied to your target plant. Objects with identical names are overwritten. 4. When the Do You Want to Copy? message appears, choose Yes . 5. Access Transaction CO60_VM to transport the PI sheet’s display variants from the SAP S/4HANA reference plant to the login client. Make sure to select all available dis- play variants and then choose Save before exiting the screen.

When you’re creating a self-defined process instruction or process message characteristic, ensure that you assign it to the relevant characteristics group to enable it to work correctly. Tips and Tricks To ensure that you see the characteristics groups ( PPPI_01 and PPPI_02 ) in the drop- down list, on the main screen, select More  Interaction Design  Visualization1 and then choose Show keys within the dropdown lists . When implementing process management, ensure that you release the process instruction and process message groups to the requisite plants.

docs.text: To release a process messages group, use menu path SAP IMG  Production Planning for Process Industries  Process Management  Process Messages  Define Characteristics Groups for Process Messages  Release for Process Messages or use Transaction O08C. To release a process instructions group, use menu path SAP IMG  Production Planning for Process Industries  Process Management  Process Instructions  Define Characteristics Groups for Process Instructions  Release for Process Instructions or use Transaction O09C.

docs.text: If the process messages or process instruction groups aren’t defined, available, or released for the desired plant, simply copy them with reference to another plant, where these are available and released. To copy all settings from reference plant 0001 to the desired plant, use menu path SAP IMG  Production Planning for Process Industries  Process Management  Tools  Copy Settings between Plants or use Transaction O20C. In the ensuing screen, enter the ref- erence plant (which is “0001”) and the target plant to copy the standard system’s set- tings (“1710” in this example).

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Tips and Tricks If you’re using a new SAP client for the first time (e.g., production system [PRD]), then there’s a possibility that the process management won’t work. If that happens, just run Transaction O23C and then Transaction O22C once (in that order), and that should solve the problem. Alternatively, make it a part of the SAP S/4HANA go-live checklist to run these two trans- actions in the PRD system before starting any PP-related data entry into the system. 4.5 Process Messages Process messages enable the process operator to send the requested data back to the SAP S/4HANA system, which then performs the necessary functions.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, say a production supervisor wants the process operator to inform them (through process messages) about the consumption (GI) of all the materials used in the production pro- cess (against a process order). The process operator fills out the PI sheet, which contains Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 4 Process Manufacturing Configuration 142 the provision to record actual material consumption details, and marks the status of the PI sheet as Complete . The process operator then sends the process message con- taining the consumption details to the process message destination in the SAP S/4HANA system, after which, the system will perform the actual GI posting against the process order in the system. The system offers many standard process messages and process message categories, but it’s also possible to define your own process messages to attend to specific business needs.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, there might be some specific information that the system should send back to the SAP S/4HANA system based on the process operator’s input on the PI sheet. In the following sections, we’ll go through the details of how to create or define and set up a process message. The first step is to create a process message characteristic. 4.5.1 Creating a Process Message Characteristic The first step is to follow menu path SAP IMG  Production Planning for Process Indus- tries  Process Management  Process Messages  Define Characteristics for Process Mes- sages  Create Characteristics for Process Messages or use Transaction O25C.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For this example, you should create process message characteristic ZPI_Creation_Date and define the characteristics group (in the Chars Group field) as Process Message Char- acteristic in the Basic Data tab. Define the Data Type as Date . In Chapter 7, we’ll show you how to use this self-defined process message to send details back to the SAP S/4HANA system. 4.5.2 Process Message Destination To create a new process message destination, use menu path Production Planning for Process Industries  Process Management  Process Messages  Process Messages Desti- nations  Define and Set up Process Messages Destinations or use Transaction O03C .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For this example, you should create a new Destination PP20 process message for Plant 1710 and then choose Target Fields/Message destinations on the left-hand side of the screen. The Change View screen shown in Figure 4.12 will appear, and there, the system will allow you to enter the process message characteristic “ZPI_CREATION_DATE,” which was created in the previous step. It’s possible to set a self-defined process message destination so that the system can send process messages to the defined destination. When the system receives informa- tion from process messages, it processes them in the SAP S/4HANA system using func- tion modules.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For external systems, process messages with information are sent back to the SAP S/4HANA system using remote function call (RFC) connections. Check the Individual box (not shown) if the system should process each process message individ- ually. This option is generally used in complex process messages involving function module destinations. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 143 4.5 Process Messages Figure 4.12 Target Field in Process Message Destination Note We suggest that you engage an SAP NetWeaver resource to manage the configuration of RFC destinations. 4.5.3 Process Message Categories In process management, the system first sends the control recipe to the control recipe destination as a manual or automatic (background) job. The plant operator receives the control recipe in the form of a PI sheet and fills in the requisite data. When the data entry is complete, the process operator sets the status of the PI sheet as Complete .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This enables the system to communicate the data back into the SAP S/4HANA system in the form of process messages , which are instructions to proceed with performing the nec- essary functions, such as data entry or data updates. The system embeds the process message category within the process instruction cate- gory. For example, the system embeds the PI_PROD process message category within the APROD_1 process instruction category. The APROD_1 process instruction category enables a process operator to record the production and also perform GR against the process order through the PI_PROD process message category.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When a user creates a process order, generates a control recipe, sends it to the control recipe destination, maintains the PI sheet, and sets the status to Complete , the system processes the pro- cess messages by sending the completed data (such as quantity produced or GI) to the SAP system, which then process the data using function modules or Business Applica- tion Programming Interfaces (BAPIs). There are several process message categories that cater to different business scenarios, such as the material consumption message, messages about the control recipe status, confirmation of a phase, or even new batch creation messages (provided that batch management is already active for the material).

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA

The system automatically assigns the relevant process message category in the process instruction category in the standard offering. For self-defined process message and process instruction categories, you should ensure that you incorporate the relevant process message category within the process instruction category. docs.text: 147 4.6 Process Instruction Categories 4.6 Process Instruction Categories A process instruction category consists of different process instruction types. In the master recipe, you have to assign the process instruction category, which then auto- matically incorporates the different process instruction types assigned to the process instruction category. In the following section, we deliberately took a longer route to explain the various pro- cess instruction types in order to cover the concepts and fundamentals involved in each type.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Toward the end of this section, we also show you how to use a wizard to cre- ate any of the seven different process instruction categories for various business sce- narios. 4.6.1 Process Instruction Types When you define a process instruction category, it’s mandatory to assign a process instruction type to enable the system to process the data accordingly. Eight different process instruction types are available:  Process parameters  Process data requests  Process message subscriptions  Calculations  Inspection results requests  Dynamic function calls  Sequence definitions  Universal Table 4.1 summarizes the different process instruction types, their descriptions, and their usages, which we explain in detail later.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Universal isn’t included here because it applies to all types. We discuss each of them in the following sections. docs.text: 149 4.6 Process Instruction Categories Process Instruction Type 2: Process Data Requests Process instruction type 2 requires the user on the shop floor to enter the required data and send it back to the SAP S/4HANA system through process messages so that the sys- tem can perform the necessary data entry or updates. Either the system requires the user to enter the process parameter value manually, or the system can fill in the value automatically, depending on how you’ve set up the process instruction characteristics.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll cover both types of process parameter value entry (manual input and automatic). The process operator also enters val- ues ( PPPI_Requested_Value ) in the PI sheet. During process message sending, the sys- tem sends the entered information back to the SAP system for further processing. Another example for process instruction type 2 is process instruction category AREAD1 . It contains process message category READ to enable the system to send back the parameter values that the shop floor operator has entered.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this specific example, the process operator sends the quantity produced against the process order for which the operator wants to record GR against the process order. The process operator records the goods-produced information on the PI sheet and sets the status of the PI sheet as Complete . Once the process operator processes the process message—that is, sends it back to the SAP S/4HANA system—the system updates the goods-produced information in the process order and also creates the material and accounting docu- ments.

Process Instruction Type 7: Sequence Definitions When process instruction type 7 is incorporated into the process instruction of a master recipe, the system prompts the user to enter the phases’ relationships with each other.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This enables the system to provide the business process owner with the necessary con- trol so that unless a predecessor phase is complete, the successor phase can’t start or the user can’t enter its data into the PI sheet. Only when a process operator sends a process message of a predecessor phase will the system enable the user to enter the details of operation of the next (successor) phase. In this process instruction type, you assign the following process instruction character, along with its value (see Figure 4.24).

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Two of them are used when transfer- ring information within the SAP S/4HANA system, and the other two facilitate the trans- fer of information to external systems. The system creates a control recipe when a pro- cess order is released, and this can be automatic (controlled in order type−dependent parameters; Section 4.2) or generated manually. Creating the control recipe and then sending the PI sheet to its destination enables the process operator to begin recording important plant parameters. Table 4.7 provides the necessary details for the different types of control recipes.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Note Although they’re still available in SAP S/4HANA 2023, ABAP list−based PI sheets are already obsolete and may not be available in future releases of SAP S/4HANA. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 163 4.7 Control Recipe/Process Instruction Sheets If the control recipe destination is of either type 1 or type 4, then the system sends the recipes to different destinations within the SAP system. The system creates a control recipe, either driven by the user (manually) or automatically, and consolidates the pro- cess instructions for a given order and destination in the form of the PI sheet. The PI sheet contains user-defined details—for example, process notes, process steps, input fields, calculations, options to sign the phases of the PI sheet, details to enter GI (con- sumption), and navigation to the confirmation screen or to record in-process quality results.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When the process operator sets the status of the PI sheet to Complete , the sys- tem sends the data back to the SAP system in the form of process messages. The system then uploads the information from the process messages into the SAP S/4HANA system tables using function modules and BAPIs. If the control recipe destination is of either type 2 or type 3, then the system consolidates the process instructions in the control rec- ipe of the process order and sends them to an external process control system. An internal SAP S/4HANA system destination can be any logical or virtual destination where the process operator receives the PI sheet and fills in the data.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, inter- nal destinations could include a mixing unit, packing unit, blending section, ammonia section, urea section, or quality section. For external destinations—that is, external pro- cess control systems—these are the RFC destinations of the external system. It’s also possible to integrate a digital signature using an SAP Universal ID and pass- word. The following options are available for use with digital signatures:  Activating or deactivating the PI sheet  Locking or unlocking the PI sheet  Changing the status of the PI sheet to Complete  Entering each parameter value into the PI sheet Digital signature options are also available in case a parameter value deviates from pre- defined limits, as well as for completion of each phase in the PI sheet.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If there’s a busi- ness need to automatically generate process instructions to minimize maintaining them in the master recipe, then you can achieve this when creating the control recipe destination. See Section 4.7.2 for information on the scope of generation. In the follow- ing sections, we’ll explain how to set up a control recipe destination and how to make the necessary settings for the scope of generation for process instructions. docs.text: Tips and Tricks When creating the process instruction category SIGN , make sure to assign a character- istic value (e.g., PI Completion Signoff ) to the process instruction characteristic PPPI_ INPUT_VALUE . 4.8 Background Jobs Background jobs help to automate processes that otherwise require manual interven- tion. For example, when a user creates a process order and generates its control recipe, the user will have to manually send it to the control recipe destination. The system can be configured to automatically send the control recipe as soon as the system generates it or even periodically.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Similarly, sending back process messages to the SAP S/4HANA system can be a manual effort that users can manage as a background (automatic) job. Apart from sending control recipes and process messages, it’s also possible to delete them periodically to save precious system resources. For example, there may not be any need to preserve process messages older than six months, in which case, those can be deleted. In this section, we show you how to set up a background job for sending a control rec- ipe.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The same steps apply to sending process messages and deleting process messages as background jobs. 4.8.1 Sending Control Recipes To set up the background job for sending a control recipe as soon as the system creates it, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production Planning for Process Industries  Process Management  Control Recipe/PI Sheet  Define Background Job for Sending or use Transaction SM36. Figure 4.32 shows the initial Define Background Job screen to define the background job. Enter “ZPP_PI_SEND” in the Job Name field and press (Enter) .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On the next screen, enter “SAP_NEW_CONTROL_RECIPES” in the Event field, which causes the system to send the control recipe as soon as the system creates it. If you click the Start Condition button, you can define the schedule for sending control recipes to © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

Figure 4.32 Defining Background Job to Send Control Recipe Tips and Tricks Use the Job Wizard button to enable the system to provide guidance in a step-by-step process to set up a background job. This works not just for sending a control recipe to a destination but for any background job. It’s important to know the program name for which to define the background job. 4.8.2 Sending Process Messages In Transaction SM36, you can use program RCOCB004 to send newly created process messages as a background job.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system also processes the process messages that have statuses of To Be Submitted and To Be Submitted with Warning . This program is for sending process messages within your plant. If you need to send process messages to different plants, then use program RCOCB002. The corresponding event is SAP_NEW_ PROCESS_MESSAGES . Tips and Tricks Whenever you define a background job by using Transaction SM36, you need to assign a variant to it. Use Transaction SE38 to create a new variant for any background job (and its associated program).

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On the initial screen, enter the program name, click the Variants radio button, and then click the Change button. On the next screen, give the variant name and click Create . 4.8.3 Deleting Process Messages The background program also lets you delete process messages as a background job. Use Transaction SM36 to set up the background job. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 4 Process Manufacturing Configuration 168 4.9 Process Manufacturing Cockpit The process manufacturing cockpit finds diverse applications in areas where the activ- ities performed, actions taken, or results recorded don’t reference any specific process order. In the cockpit, it’s possible to use function calls—for example, to call up a trans- action or display a document. You can also create a cockpit for a predefined set of activ- ities that a process operator performs on a specific resource or in a specific work center.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The cockpit also facilitates input or output data entry as well as calculations. The sys- tem creates a PI sheet with reference to a process order, and the system reflects any changes or updates made to it. In a cockpit, there’s no need to give reference to a pro- cess order. Here are some examples in which creating process manufacturing cockpits meets business needs:  There’s a need to record the values of five specific process parameters of the plant and report them back to the main control room.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The reporting for the parameters doesn’t reference a specific process order but is used to ensure that there is regular recording and consistent transmission of this information.  The production process generates an ancillary product (a by-product of low value), but the production supervisor doesn’t want to record it with reference to any spe- cific process order or book the cost of generating the by-product to a process order. There’s also a need to record the quantity of the by-product every three days, along with other details, such as the date of recording, the name of the person who recorded the information, and that person’s signature.  A company has installed a new production line for which it wants to ensure that the latest technical drawings and manuals are available for process operators to refer to.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These drawings are for each work center or work station. In the process manufactur- ing cockpit, the process operator only has to click the relevant drawing’s icon, and all details will become visible. You can create process manufacturing cockpits for as many business applications or activities as needed. Because the cockpit uses a process instruction category, it’s also possible to incorporate a process message category into it. When you make entries are into the cockpit, the system generates process messages that you can send to pre- defined destinations.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To define a process manufacturing cockpit, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production Planning for Process Industries  Process Management  Define Process Manufacturing Cockpits (see Figure 4.33). Here, you define Cockpit PP10 for Plant 1710 . Notice that you can check a newly created cockpit for correctness by choosing the Check icon, and it you can simulate it by choos- ing Simulate at the bottom of the screen. Finally, you need to activate the process man- ufacturing cockpit so that it becomes available and changes you make to the cockpit become effective.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, the process management area in PP for pro- cess industries requires detailed coverage. The concepts and fundamentals covered in this chapter apply equally whether a company plans to implement XSteps in discrete manufacturing or use process manufacturing cockpits. The next chapter covers the configuration basics of the last main manufacturing type we’ll discuss in this book: repetitive manufacturing. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 171 Chapter 5 Repetitive Manufacturing Configuration Configuration steps in repetitive manufacturing include creating a repetitive manufacturing profile, setting scheduling parameters for a run schedule quantity (planned orders), and selecting backflush settings for use online or in the background. The configuration steps in repetitive manufacturing (REM) are relatively straightfor- ward, without many complexities when compared to discrete manufacturing or pro- cess manufacturing types. In fact, the very purpose of REM is to enable lean manufac- turing in actual business scenarios with correspondingly fewer entries in the SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: REM may not be able to manage complex manufacturing processes, but you can use it to bring about significant process optimization with a decreased data entry workload and improved system performance. This chapter begins by explaining how to set up the REM profile using the REM assis- tant. The assistant guides the user with a step-by-step approach to ensure that the cor- rect settings are made during the REM profile creation stage. The assistant also pro- vides the detailed function of each configuration step and gives recommendations where necessary.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The user can choose the desired production method, such as MTS or MTO. We deliberately took the long route to REM profile creation by using the assistant because we wanted to focus on explaining every available option in detail and with business examples. After we finish creating the REM profile by using the assistant, we explain the “normal” or prevalent method of creating an REM profile with a single screen (and multiple tabs). We also explain the options that aren’t available in the REM profile assistant. If you’re configuring an REM profile for the first time, we recommend that you to use the REM profile assistant.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: But if you’re already familiar with REM profile creation and the func- tionalities it offers, then proceed directly to using the single-screen REM profile cre- ation option. This chapter also covers scheduling REM planned orders and running the schedule quantity, and then, it discusses the layout and display settings available on various screens in REM processing. The effects of the REM configuration will become clear in Chapter 8, which covers the production planning for REM in detail. Finally, this chapter Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Repetitive Manufacturing Configuration 172 also covers the settings available to optimize day-to-day business transactions, such as backflushing. Note Refer to Chapter 1 for feature comparison among discrete manufacturing, process manufacturing, and REM, as well as to see how to decide which manufacturing type is most relevant for a given industry. Let’s get started. 5.1 Repetitive Manufacturing Profile The REM profile offers several controls for important business functions that form the basis of regular or periodic data recording in the system.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This includes options to post activities online or at a later date, automatic goods movements of all or some of the materials, and stock and/or automatic batch determination, among other things. To create an REM profile using the REM profile assistant, follow SAP menu path SAP IMG  Logistics  Production  Repetitive Manufacturing  Control  Create Repetitive Manufac- turing Profile Using Assistant or use Transaction OSPT. The following sections will explain the steps involved in setting up an REM profile. 5.1.1 Repetitive Manufacturing Production Type When creating a RE M profile, you need to decide whether to use the profile for the MTO or MTS production method.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Alternately, you can cater separate REM profiles to meet MTO or MTS business scenarios. Note Chapter 12 covers MTO and MTS production methods. Depending on the option you select, the system will display the relevant screens and options to choose from. If you choose MTO production, then the system will create a profile suited to REM that references the sales order. If you choose MTS production, the system will create a profile suited to REM that doesn’t reference the sales order. It’s also possible to use an REM profile template to copy previously created and avail- able REM profiles to create a new REM profile.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This step copies all the settings of the REM template profile into the new REM profile, and then, you can make the desired changes as needed. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)
