It also keeps on updating the planned costs with actual costs to provide a quick evaluation. This is an integration point between PP and the product cost con- trolling team. Figure 6.78 Item Cost Overview of Production Order 6.12 Summary The production process in discrete manufacturing entails the creation of important master data followed by production execution that itself consists of order creation, GI, confirmation, and GR.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Handling scrap, coproducts, by-products, completion, and set- tlement processes occurs in both manufacturing types (discrete and process). Shop floor papers, such as object lists, can also be printed. A large number of tools and func- tionalities can be used to optimize business processes, such as backflush, automatic GR, mass processing, and postprocessing. WIP batches can also be implemented to gain better control over the entire production process. The next chapter discusses the business processes in production planning for process industries (PP-PI). © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 277 Chapter 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing Building on the important configuration of process manufacturing undertaken in Chapter 4, this chapter covers important business pro- cesses and functions, as well as the vital and logical links of configura- tion with those business processes. It places greater focus is on process management in the master recipe, which is unique to process industries but can also be implemented in discrete manufacturing if there’s any business need for it. Production planning for process industries (PP-PI) is characterized by product com- plexity.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In many industries, it’s necessary to integrate batch management and quality management (QM) with process manufacturing in PP-PI. Some of the industries in which process manufacturing finds extensive implementation include chemicals, edi- ble oil refining, pharmaceuticals, fertilizers, beverages, food, and food processing. Any manufacturing industry that deals with liquids, where the product flows in a liquid or semisolid form or where the processed material can’t be brought back to its original state or disassembled, requires process manufacturing.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this chapter, we begin with an overview of process manufacturing and how it fits into the planning and production perspectives. The process manufacturing process flow provides a comprehensive and step-by-step explanation of each stage involved. Next, we cover important process manufacturing master data, with extensive focus on the master recipe, in which the system facilitates not only material quantity calcula- tion but also process management. We cover some of the standard features available in process management, such as input and calculated values, integration with the SAP Document Management service, and digital signatures.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We then cover the end-to-end business processes involved, from the creation of the process order to how process management integrates with it. Next, we cover the highly versatile and intuitive functionality of execution steps (XSteps) when a company either wants to implement them or simply transition from process instructions to XSteps. We then demonstrate more features and functionalities of XSteps, as well at their correlations with the configurations made in Chapter 4. We then cover process message evaluations and the process manufacturing cockpit (configured in Chapter 4) to see how they help to facilitate business processes.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 278 Because PP-PI processes, such as GI, confirmation, and GR, are all similar to those in dis- crete manufacturing, we suggest revisiting the relevant sections of Chapter 3 and Chap- ter 6. Lastly, we’ll discuss how to set up and use a resource network. 7.1 Process Manufacturing Overview Figure 7.1 shows an overview of the end-to-end process involved in process manufac- turing. The business processes involved can be divided broadly into the following areas:  Process planning  Process order execution  Process management  Order closure Production planning in PP-PI begins when a materials planner converts the output of MRP, which in this case is a planned order, into a process order.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This is then followed by a material availability check to ensure that the required quantities of components needed to produce the material are available. If the material quantity calculation func- tionality is enabled in the master recipe of the material, the system calculates the com- ponents’ quantities. If not, the system reads the information from the material’s BOM. At this stage, the system can perform batch determination of the components that are going to be used in the production process. The next step is to proceed with releasing the process order, as well as printing the pro- cess order.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: With a released process order, a control recipe can be generated. A generated control recipe takes the form of a PI sheet. Several of these process order management activities can run automatically or in the background to minimize the need to manage them manually. For example, say a planner determines that when they create a process order, the system can automatically release it too. If it can’t, the process order will have to be released manually. Alternatively, they can use a separate transaction to release a large number of process orders (mass processing), which again they can do as a manual task.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The MM functionality plays an important role when raw materials and components need to be issued against a process order. QM processes, if integrated with PP, enable extensive in-process (during production) quality inspection checks. During this time, the planner also maintains the PI sheet and assigns it a Complete status. Then, they undertake confirmation of the process order, either at the individual phase level or at the entire process order level. When goods are produced, it’s again time to engage MM to ensure GR against the process order.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 279 7.2 Master Data in Process Manufacturing Figure 7.1 Production Planning and Execution in Process Industries Cost object controlling activities—such as WIP determination, variance calculation, and settlement—are order specific in nature and usually processed in the background. PP completely integrates with cost object controlling in the SAP S/4HANA system, so it’s imperative to ensure extensive coordination for comprehensive business processes mapping. To optimize and bring greater visibility to the business processes, you can implement and integrate several additional processes and functionalities, such as digital signa- tures, engineering change management, SAP Document Management service, coprod- ucts and by-products, shift notes, and shift reports.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can also integrate QM during production (in-process quality inspection) or at the time of GR. 7.2 Master Data in Process Manufacturing Process manufacturing has its own unique master data that often overlaps with other production types, such as discrete manufacturing and (REM). If the master data is set up in the right sequence, it’s much easier and more logical to interconnect the master data because the predecessor-successor relationship is already taken care of. Master data creation for process manufacturing begins with the material master of the product (a finished good or an assembly).

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You create a BOM for the product, via which Order Request Process Order Creation Availability Check Resources/Line Scheduling Resource Selection Batch Determination Process Order Release Order Printing Send Control Recipe Maintain PI Sheet Process Messages for Different Destinations Material Staging/ Material Withdrawals Order Confirmations Goods Receipt Variance Calculation Process Order Settlement Batch Record Archive/Delete Material Quantity Calculation Order Closing Process Planning Process Management Process Order Execution In-Process Quality Inspection Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 280 the company will produce and assign components, together with the quantities needed to produce the product. If needed, you can define a scrap percentage at the operation or component level. The next master data creation step is to create the resource and then create the master recipe for the material, in which the previously created resource is assigned. Finally, a production version for the material is created and the material’s BOM and the master recipe are assigned to it.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When all the master data is in place, the CO team can create a product cost estimate of the material and release it. Note We strongly recommend that you maintain close coordination and liaison with the CO team to ensure that when they’re working with the PP team, both teams are com- pletely aligned with their working and reporting needs. For example, for each resource, there’s a need to assign a cost center, which the CO team should provide to the PP team. It may provide one cost center for multiple resources or one cost center for an individual resource, depending on how the CO team wants to see the cost center reporting and evaluation.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The following make up the important master data in PP-PI:  Material master  BOM  Resource  Production version  Master recipe We’ll discuss each in detail in the following sections. 7.2.1 Material Master The material master is the central master record in logistics and the supply chain. The system defines a material as a substance or commodity that a company buys or sells on a commercial basis. A material can also be either consumed or produced. Some exam- ples of materials are raw materials, packing materials, consumables, semifinished goods, and finished goods.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The material isn’t just restricted to production-based pro- cesses but is used in all those processes for which the company wants to maintain inventory (stock items). Therefore, a company may also have materials that are used in plant maintenance (PM) processes, or it may even have nonvaluated materials. In PP-PI, there is extensive use of batch management . A batch is a uniquely identifiable partial quantity of a material, and batches of a material are managed in separate stocks. In a production process, a batch is a quantity of a specific material produced during a standardized production run.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 281 7.2 Master Data in Process Manufacturing unit with unique specifications. The key properties of a batch are homogeneity and nonreproducibility. A batch can be traced across the entire supply chain—that is, from the receipt of the raw material to processing in production and the creation of the final product, all the way through sales and delivery to the customer. Complete batch traceability, batch determination, and batch derivation functionalities are available. The batch informa- tion cockpit (Transaction BMBC) can be used for complete top-down or bottom-up evaluation of material batches.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system creates batches for a material, and the data of the material master is valid for all batches assigned to it. In contrast to the material master, a batch master record contains data that uniquely identifies the corresponding batch and characterizes the unit as one that can’t be reproduced. The characteristic batch specifications are assigned using characteristics from the classification system in the material master and are inherited by the corresponding batch master records. Note Chapter 10 covers batch management. 7.2.2 Bill of Materials The BOM in PP-PI is the same as in discrete manufacturing.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Refer to Chapter 3 and Chapter 6 for a detailed understanding of the configuration of BOMs and the business processes they’re involved in. The material quantity calculation is unique only to PP-PI and uses components of the material defined in its BOM. When you’re calculating the components’ quantities that the system should use in reference to each other, it refers to the information in the BOM. See Section 7.2.5 concerning the master recipe for a detailed understanding of material quantity calculation. To create a BOM, you use Transaction CS01. 7.2.3 Resource The resource in process manufacturing is the same as the work center in discrete man- ufacturing.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Refer to Chapter 3 and Chapter 6 for a detailed understanding of the config- uration and business processes involved in work centers (resources in PP-PI). To create a resource, use Transaction CRC1. The system offers and makes available a standard configuration for PP-PI that you can use if your company’s business processes aren’t too complex. For example, you can set the Usage as “008” (for master recipe + process order) and the Standard Value Key as “SAP4” (process manufacturing), in which only Duration is listed as an activity.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 282 7.2.4 Production Version A production version determines which alternative BOM the system should use in combination with the master recipe for process manufacturing. In PP-PI, it’s manda- tory to define a production version. The system uses the production version during the creation of a master recipe to identify the BOM for the material and pull the BOM details from the master recipe. When creating the master recipe for a material and plant combination, you must also enter the production version for the material on the initial screen.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You should create the production version prior to creating the master recipe and then use it to create the master recipe. To create a new production version, use Transaction C223. You can also create a produc- tion version in the MRP 4 view of the material master or even in the Work Scheduling view. Refer to Chapter 6, Section 6.2.5, for a detailed understanding of the business pro- cess of a production version and how to create one in the SAP system. Note Creating a production version directly from Transaction MM02 should be an exception because there may still be some incomplete data at this stage.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Use Transaction C223 to achieve this objective instead. 7.2.5 Master Recipe Creation Before creating a master recipe, you can create a production version and include BOM details only (without the master recipe details because these aren’t available at that time). Next, create the master recipe and give reference to the production version because it’s mandatory to enter a production version during master recipe creation. Then, go back to the production version and incorporate the master recipe details, including the group number and group counter that the system generated when the master recipe was saved.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system suggests the master recipe group number and the group counter when the production version is again called up. With this approach, cre- ating a master recipe makes a materials list (BOM) available in the master recipe, and you can then use it in the material quantity calculation. A second approach that you can use to creating the master recipe is to first create a master recipe group without reference to a material and plant combination. When the system generates the recipe group number, create a production version of the material and enter the BOM and master recipe details.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Finally, when the header material num- ber is assigned in the change master recipe option for the master recipe group, the sys- tem prompts you to enter a production version to enable it to explode the BOM. To create a master recipe for which the production version already exists, follow menu path Logistics  Production—Process  Master Data  Master Recipes  Recipe and © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 283 7.2 Master Data in Process Manufacturing Material List  Create or use Transaction C201. On the initial screen of the master rec- ipe, enter the Material , Plant , and Profile (see Figure 7.2), and the header screen will appear. Recall from Chapter 4 that the master recipe’s profile is a control function to allow or disallow certain functions, such as XSteps being optional or mandatory. The Key date controls when the master recipe will be available for production process. You can enter the key date manually or, if no entry is maintained, the system will use the date of master recipe creation as the key date.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 7.2 Initial Screen of Master Recipe Creation We’ll discuss the different elements of this screen in the following sections. Recipe Header Figure 7.3 shows the master recipe header details screen. The Charge Quantity Range area is valid for the lot size quantities in the master recipe, and it contains the default values for the operation, the phase, and secondary resources. A proportional relation- ship exists between the default values for operation quantities and their unit of mea- sure and the recipe quantities and their unit of measure.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In contrast to master recipes, you maintain this relationship directly in the operation details in routing and rate routings. For example, say the master recipe unit of measure is pieces (PC) and the operational unit of measure is kilograms (kg). That means that for every 7 kg of the operation, there are 4 PC of the master recipe, with a quotient of 4/7. The charge quantity is 4 PC, and the operation quantity is 7 kg. The system also provides the option to maintain a base quantity for detailed work. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 284 Figure 7.3 Header Details of Master Recipe Materials The master recipe integrates the details of the operations and the BOM together into one master data element by using the production version. The system explodes the BOM in the master recipe to bring up the details of the material BOM. The material BOM details in the task list (the master recipe) help enable a feature unique to process manufacturing known as material quantity calculation . Note It’s crucial to adopt one of the two approaches mentioned previously to create a pro- duction version in relation to the master recipe to ensure the master recipe contains the materials (the BOM).

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Material Quantity Calculation In a process order, the system calculates the components’ quantities directly from the BOM and takes the material quantity calculation into account. With the material quantity calculation, the following options are available:  Change the header product quantity with reference to the components’ quantities or even with respect to the active ingredient proportions. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 285 7.2 Master Data in Process Manufacturing  Calculate the planned scrap at the phase level; the system includes it in the planned production cost.  Change the components’ quantities with reference to each other, the header prod- uct, or the active ingredient proportions (the batch characteristics and their values).  Change operation or phase quantities when these aren’t in proportion to the prod- uct quantity. For material quantity calculation to work effectively, you need to make sure to create the master recipe with reference to the BOM consisting of components and quantities.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Because the planned scrap of the component is entered either in the material master or in the BOM, the system automatically increases the component quantity during planned order or process order creation. You should therefore use the planned scrap of a component as a variable to calculate the other component’s quantity using the mate- rial quantity calculation formula. When a process order is created, the system automatically calculates the quantities based on the formulas. For a formula that is processed at the batch level and that also uses active ingredient proportions (batch characteristics values), the material quantity calculation needs to be triggered manually in the process order and after batch deter- mination.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Note Note that the system only considers batch characteristics with numeric values. When the system explodes the BOM in the master recipe, you should go to the Material Quantity Calculation screen shown in Figure 7.4 by choosing Goto  Material Quantity Calculation or by clicking the Material Quantity Calc. (calculation) icon in the Materials tab of the master recipe. Figure 7.4 Material Quantity Calculation in Master Recipe Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 286 In general, you perform the following steps when entering the formula for the material quantity calculation: 1. On the screen shown in Figure 7.4, place the cursor on the field for which you want to change the quantity using a formula and choose the Select Formula button in the menu bar. 2. In the Formula Definition box, enter the formula or equation, which derives the out- put field value. 3. While creating a formula, double-click the variables to be included in the formula or place the cursor on the variable and choose the Insert in formula button on the menu bar.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can also use formula operators such as + , – , * , / , DIV , and MOD , as well as exponen- tial, rounding ( ROUND ), absolute values ( ABS ), truncation ( TRUNC ), EXP , LOG , SIN , COS , TAN , square roots ( SQRT ), IF THEN ELSE conditions, and IF THEN NOT conditions. Operations and Phases Master recipes use a phase , which works in the same manner as operations do in rout- ing for discrete manufacturing. It’s easier to maintain detailed levels working at the phase level in the master recipe because a production supervisor can manage and incorporate more production details, including process management.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the master recipe, you assign activities such as production duration and labor hours at the phase level and not at the operation level. Hence, the confirmation of a process order is recorded for a phase and not an operation. A resource (work center) is assigned at the operation level, and the phases below the operation then adopt the resource that was assigned at the operation level. The system assigns the standard values and activi- ties (controlled by a control key in the resource) as active at the phase level and not at the operation level.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The sum total of standard values at a phase is in fact the total time required to process the operation. The system assigns the components of the BOM (materials list) to phases and not to operations. However, integration of in-process quality inspections of QM can take place either at the operation level or the phase level. To create a phase below an operation, you check the Phase box in the Operations tab, which then automatically copies the resource from the operation. At the same time, when you’re defining a phase, you must assign the superior operation so that the sys- tem knows which specific phase relates to which operation.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can maintain relationships among various phases, such as start-finish, finish-start, finish-finish, and start-start. The phases can work either in parallel or in overlapping sequences. In the Operations tab of the master recipe, you can access the phase rela- tionship screen for phases by selecting the phases and choosing Goto  Relationships. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 287 7.2 Master Data in Process Manufacturing You can assign individual control recipe destinations at the phase level and assign the process instructions in the respective phases of the master recipe. If the scope of gener- ation is defined in the configuration of the process instructions, it reduces data mainte- nance efforts at the master recipe level. Alternatively, you can maintain the desired pro- cess instruction details either in the master recipe or in the process order. You can assign process instructions that have characteristic values based on a material at the master recipe level.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To assign process instructions to the phases in the Operations tab of the master recipe, use the menu path Goto  Process Management  Process Instructions . Figure 7.5 shows the Operations tab of the master recipe, in which the Operation is 0010 . Enter the “PACKING” Resource at the operation level and the system will auto- matically copy it to all of the phases below it. The phase is 0020, you denote it by check- ing the Phase Indicator box. When you define an operation as a phase, you also have to define the Sup.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Operation , which, in this example, is 0010 (the operation). The control recipe Destinatn (destination) is PP . This is the same control recipe destina- tion that was configured in Chapter 4. Figure 7.5 Operations Overview in Master Recipe Notice that the system automatically copies the Control key , PI01 , from the PACKING Resource . Select the phase 0020 and double-click the line item 0020 (the operation, which is basically a phase), and the system will bring up the screen shown in Figure 7.6. This shows the Standard values tab of the master recipe, where you can maintain the duration of the activities, such as the Machine , Labor , and Setup (not shown) hours required to produce the material in each operation.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: From here, choose the Process instructions tab to configure the process instructions that are an integral part of pro- cess management. We’ll visit this screen a bit later, in the upcoming section. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 288 Figure 7.6 Standard Values in Master Recipe Because characteristics have such an important role to play in process management, we’ll cover them in the next section. 7.3 Characteristics A characteristic describes an object and can have one value or a range of values that are valid. In this section, we’ll begin by covering the steps required to create a characteristic and the available options. We’ll also cover the associated configuration settings that can help users effectively create characteristics and put relevant controls in place.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You use Transaction CT04 to create a characteristic, via the menu path SAP Menu  Cross-Application Components  Classification System  Master Data  Characteristics . On the screen shown in Figure 7.7, information related to the characteristic is defined, such as description, data type, number of characteristics, decimal places (if any), and unit of measure. Table 7.1 lists descriptions some of the important fields seen in the var- ious tabs shown in Figure 7.7. Field Names Field Descriptions and Values Description Description of the characteristic; for example, thickness.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Char. Group Groups together similar characteristics in one group. Status Status of the characteristic, for example, Released , to indicate it’s ready for use. Table 7.1 Details of Individual Fields of Characteristic © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 289 7.3 Characteristics Figure 7.7 Basic Data Screen for Transaction CT04 Data Type Indicates the type of data this characteristic has; for example, date, time format, or numeric format. Number of Chars Indicates the number of characters a value of this characteristic can contain. Decimal Places Indicates the number of decimal places if the format is numeric. Unit of Measure Unit of measure of the characteristic (quantitative/numeric), if any. Single-value/Multiple Values (radio buttons) Option for whether a single value or multiple values are allowed for a characteristic.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: An example of multiple value usage is when you can select a surface finish as coarse, pitted, and uneven. For multi- ple values, the system offers a checkbox for each value to select from the dropdown list. Negative Vals Allowed (checkbox) Option for whether negative values are allowed. You can’t enter a negative value for a characteristic if you don’t check this box. Entry Required (checkbox) Option to indicate whether the user must enter a value for this characteristic. If you don’t check this box, then entering a value is optional.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 290 Next, switch over to the Values tab (see Figure 7.8) and maintain values for this charac- teristic. For example, say a characteristic provides an option to record the pump value, which you can search for in the material master along with any other characteristic. Check the Additional Values box to ensure that values other than the prefixed 10, 20, or 30 are also allowed for entry as input values. Next, choose the Addnl Data tab in Figure 7.7 to see more options. Enter the relevant SAP Document Management service document’s number, document type, document part, and document version, if any.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The following are the details of the various check- boxes and their functions:  Not Ready for Input No value can be maintained for this characteristic. In other words, a preassigned default or calculated value automatically fills the characteristic field, and the user has no option to make an entry.  No Display The system won’t display a characteristic.  Display Allowed Values If several values are already available from the Values tab of the characteristic, the system displays those values to help the user with data entry.  Unformatted Entry If this box is checked, the system makes the provision to set the characteristic’s field length to a maximum of 30 so the user can make multiple entries, separated by colons.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If it’s not checked, then the system displays the exact length of the character- istic for data entry.  Proposed Template If this box is checked, the system proposes or displays a template to help the user during data entry. Choose the Basic Data tab to view the template details. Finally, on the Restrictions tab, you can restrict the use of a characteristic to specific class types; otherwise, it will be available for use in all class types. For example, entering class type “001” will restrict this characteristic to the material class type only.

docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 292 Figure 7.9 Defining Characters for Characteristic Templates Figure 7.10 Creation and Modification of New Characteristic Value Templates 7.4 Process Management Because a large number of features and functionalities of process instructions exist within an operation’s phase of the master recipe, the topic of process instructions war- rants a separate section in this chapter. This section deals with process instructions (which are part of process management) that need to be defined in the Process instruc- tions tab shown previously in Figure 7.6.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In a manufacturing organization, there is a permanent requirement to monitor system performance and plant parameters. For example, when the production of a certain item is scheduled, the plant operator needs to have a series of clear and comprehensive instructions to follow. Similarly, the plant operator is required to record and report back data, such as steam temperature twice a shift or an abnormal vibration in the © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 293 7.4 Process Management suction pump, so that it will be available for future reference or to help with corrective action. Therefore, a functionality is needed in the SAP system that can transfer and communi- cate all such information in a timely manner from the plant operator back to the pro- cess control system. This has been made possible by the process management func- tionality. Note Transmitting information between an SAP S/4HANA system and a process control sys- tem is made possible by defining the type of the control recipe destination.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We focus on the transfer of information to PI sheets to show that implementing process man- agement can still yield significant added value without the need to integrate SAP S/4HANA with a process control system. Process management completely integrates with core functional areas such as MM, QM, and SAP Document Management service. It offers functionality such as GIs and GRs, process order confirmations, and results recording of quality inspection data. All of this information helps in analysis and report generation functions, and it also bene- fits business process owners who directly use the information.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The following list summarizes the functions supported by process management in PP-PI:  Receiving control recipes from released process orders  Sending control recipes to process operators or process control systems  Preparing process instructions as texts so that the process operators can display them on their computer screens  Receiving, checking, and sending process messages with actual process data  Monitoring process messages and control recipes  Manually creating process messages In the following sections, we’ll cover some of the elements of process management and how to intuitively create a PI sheet. 7.4.1 Elements in Process Management Figure 7.11 illustrates the various elements involved in process management for data flow.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 294 Figure 7.11 Overview of Process Management The system sends the control recipe to the predefined control recipe destinations, in the form of a PI sheet. The process operator follows the instructions given on the PI sheet and also fills out the PI sheet with relevant plant parameters and other important data. The process operator then returns the PI sheet as a process message to either the SAP S/4HANA system or an external system. 7.4.2 Integrating Process Management In an automated environment, object linking and embedding (OLE) for process control (Open Platform Communications [OPC]) and SAP OPC Data Access enable the system to read and write data points and events using the OPC server for the SAP S/4HANA sys- tem.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This function is also available in production orders (discrete manufacturing). Note OPC is a standard that uses component object model/distributed component object model (COM/DCOM) technology to define interfaces independent of the manufacturer for use in an industry. SAP designed the OPC standard especially for the process control level. OPC servers allow access to various data sources, such as process control systems, programmable logic controllers, and temperature sensors, and thus, they provide pro- cess data that can be requested by OPC clients.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP Manufacturing Integration and Intelligence offers an adaptive manufacturing solution for production. SAP Manufacturing Integration and Intelligence provides manufacturing companies increased flexibility through improved linking of the SAP S/4HANA system to the production process level and by making real-time information available, and SAP Manufacturing Integration and Intelligence can also be used in both the process order environment and the production order environment. It provides standardized, preconfigured connectors to enable real-time data integration in manu- facturing execution systems and supervisory control and data acquisition systems.

docs.text: 295 7.4 Process Management A process operator can run real-time analyses and display the results in browser- and role-based dashboards. These analyses provide important information for checking and supporting decision-making, such as warnings, job lists, analyses, reports, and real- time messages about production variance. 7.4.3 Process Instructions An operation in the master recipe may have several phases, and each phase requires a control recipe destination. After a control recipe destination is defined for an opera- tion, it automatically applies to all phases of that operation.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Within each phase, process management-related information is incorporated, including process message catego- ries, process instruction characteristics, and control recipe destinations. You can assign process instructions to the phases in the Operations tab of the master recipe. To do this, select the specific phase and use the following path in the Operations tab: Master Recipe—Goto  Process Management  Process Instructions . In the resulting screen, shown in Figure 7.12, there are two process instruction catego- ries: AREAD1 and PP20 .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, when a user executes a function, they are required to digitally sign the PI sheet in the popup box that appears. 7.5 Process Order Execution Process order execution has the following differences from and similarities to produc- tion order execution in discrete manufacturing:  Batch allocation, either automatic or manual, can occur within the process order.  The system automatically executes the formulas of the material quantity calcula- tion that is defined in the master recipe using batch allocations.  When a process order is released, the system can create the control recipe automati- cally, or the user can choose the relevant icon within the process order creation screen to do it manually.  A user can also create a test control recipe in a process order to check or validate set- tings.  The system creates a control recipe for each control recipe destination of the process order.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If there are three control recipe destinations in the process order, then the sys- tem creates three control recipes for the process order. When the process order is released and the control recipe is generated, the system creates a PI sheet. 3. The next step is to send the generated control recipe to the predefined destination in the master recipe (in this example, it’s PP—Chemical Mixing ).

All the necessary checks and balances are maintained, such as defining tolerance limits for parameter values, requiring sign-off at the end of each operation or phase, and integrating digital signatures in process management. If you realize that incorrect information was provided on the PI sheet, then you can create a new PI sheet (by generating a new control recipe) to attend to this scenario. This situation arises after a user has already performed all the necessary steps in process management.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To generate a new PI sheet, follow these steps: 1. Use Transaction CO67. On the Worklist for PI Sheets screen containing the PI sheet with the Complete status, select the PI sheet. Then choose PI Sheet  Delete . The system then issues a message stating that the selected entry (PI sheet) was deleted. 2. Use Transaction CO57 to create a process message manually. In this option, enter the Plant and use Process Message Category PI_CRST . Enter the process order number of the deleted control recipe, enter the number of the deleted control recipe (from the previous step), and set the Control Recipe Status to 00007 ( Discarded ). 3.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Save the process message, and the system will state that a new process message has been created and will give the process message number. 4. Use Transaction CO54XT, and on the initial parameter selection screen, enter the process order number and the process message category as “PI_CRST.” Press (F8) or choose the Message List icon. 5. Select the process message number created in the previous step and choose Send to send the process message. The system will issue an information message to inform you that the process message has been processed. 6.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Use Transaction CO53XT. On the initial screen, enter the Plant , the process order number, and the destination address (in this example, it’s “Chemical Mixing”). Press (F8) or choose Display . 7. On the Control Recipe Monitor screen, select the relevant control recipe number and choose the Delete icon. The system issues an information message that the control recipe has been deleted and, at the same time, assigns the status of the control recipe as Discarded . 8. Use Transaction COR2 for the change in process order and click the Generate Control Recipe icon to create a new PI sheet for the same process order. 7.6.3 Downloading and Sending a Control Recipe You can manually download a control recipe to a destination in a nonautomated envi- ronment (as a background job).

docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 312 When the PI sheet is set to the Completion status, the system automatically sends the process message category PI_CRST to the SAP S/4HANA system. This process message category has the process message characteristic PPPI_CONTROL_RECIPE_STATUS , for which the system automatically sets the value to Processed . In the process order, the system sets the status of the control recipe to CRFI . This is one of the statuses that you’ll find in Table 7.10. The Control Recipe Monitor screen provides comprehensive information on the discarded, terminated, and sent control recipes.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When the system downloads control recipes of destination type 1 or 4, it’s known as a PI sheet. When the system downloads control recipes of destination type 2 or 3, it reaches an external system or an external PCS. Note You can schedule a background job for downloading and sending control recipes by using program RCOCB006 (batch job name: SAP_NEW_CONTROL_RECIPE ). Detailed set- tings for the background job are covered in Chapter 4, Section 4.8. 7.6.4 Maintaining Process Instruction Sheets To maintain the PI sheet, follow menu path Logistics  Production—Process  Process Management  Process Instruction Sheet  Worklist—Maintain or use Transaction CO55.

You can also check the relevant box to use this transaction to display completed PI sheets. Control Recipe Statuses Control Recipe Descriptions Details CRCR Created This status appears in the process order when the system generates a control recipe.

Figure 7.33 Work List of PI Sheets for Operating Group Production Floor This is the process instruction work list, which meets the selection criteria. docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 314 Figure 7.34 Maintaining PI Sheet Tips and Tricks You can control whether an entry in the field is optional or mandatory by checking the relevant box in the characteristic (Transaction CT04). In SHIFT HIGHLIGHTS text box (not shown, but located further down the same screen), a process operator can enter detailed text. They can also make entries in the table of the PI sheet. Notice that P.O. Basic Start Date is automatically filled, based on the configu- rations you made in Chapter 4. 7.6.5 Completing Process Instruction Sheets When you’ve finished making all entries into the PI sheet, you can either save it or mark it as Complete by using the light-blue buttons at the top of the PI sheet (refer to Figure 7.34).

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA

docs.text: 315 7.6 Process Management in Action Note If the relevant settings were made in the configuration (see Chapter 4) of the control recipe destination, then the system will show you a popup message that will prompt you to digitally sign the PI sheet when you complete it. 7.6.6 Sending Process Messages The PI sheet automatically creates a process message with all the information that the system needs to send to specific destinations. This information may be a GI against a process order, a GR against a process order, or a confirmation of a process order.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Send- ing the process message executes the function module with the gathered information. Process messages in a productive system are typically sent via a background job of pro- gram RCOCB002 (cross-plant) or program RCOCB004 (plant-specific). Warning Be sure to monitor process messages; sometimes, a process message sending fails if, for example, data is missing from the PI sheet. You can also monitor and delete process messages with Transaction CO54XT and manually create them with Transaction CO57. Figure 7.35 Process Message Monitor Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 316 You can also create, test, check, and monitor process messages, although the system doesn’t process these process test messages at the destination as it does for normal process messages. Test process messages are created to check whether the system can transfer all the relevant information from various systems and destinations. To send a process message, follow menu path Logistics  Production – Process  Process Management  Message  Message Monitor or use Transaction CO54XT.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Enter the Plant and the Creation Date range for the process message (see Figure 7.35) and then click the To Be Sent button to send the messages. In the process messages work list shown in Figure 7.36, there is a process message cate- gory, SIGN , that the system needs to send. Notice that the sender of these process mes- sages is Chemical Mixing (which you configured in Chapter 4). Select the first process message, SIGN , and choose Change (the pen icon). Figure 7.36 Process Messages from Production Floor Sender In Figure 7.37, the system automatically incorporates the Char.

docs.text: 317 7.7 Execution Steps Some of the other salient features of process messages are as follows:  Process message categories that have errors or are terminated during processing can be resubmitted for processing using the Process Messages Monitor screen.  Process messages can be created manually using Transaction CO57. Then these man- ually created process messages will be visible on the Process Messages Monitor screen, where they can be processed further.  The system uses Business Application Programming Interfaces (BAPIs) or function modules to update the process messages.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system processes the received process messages using these function modules.  The system uses a remote function call (RFC) connection to communicate with an external process control system using process messages. It’s important to define the RFC destination for every external system, so we recommended that you engage an SAP NetWeaver (basis) consultant for this task.  The system issues alerts for critical situations or milestones in the production run. The alerts can be from either the external control system or the internal shop floor operator.  A special destination type, SAP Office user, is used in the process message to inform specific SAP S/4HANA system users about the status of process messages (and also control recipes). 7.7 Execution Steps XSteps are extensively used not only in PP-PI but also in discrete manufacturing.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In fact, all of the concepts, fundamentals, features, and functionalities covered in Chapter 4 and this chapter apply if there’s a business need to integrate XSteps with discrete manufacturing. In the following sections, we’ll discuss where you can find a repository of standard XSteps that you can use as a reference to create your own XSteps and how to set up a specific function or parameter in the PI sheet. We then address the transition required from process management to XSteps. The remaining sections then focus on how to leverage the configuration made in Chapter 4 and the process management concepts developed earlier in this chapter for XSteps. 7.7.1 Repository for Standard XSteps The standard XSteps repository is an invaluable resource that you can use to gain a bet- ter understanding of how to use XSteps.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It contains detailed step-by-step instructions for how to effectively use all the features and functionalities of XSteps. To access the repository of standard XSteps, follow menu path Logistics  Production— Process  Master Data  Standard XStep Repository or use Transaction CMXSV. For this example, enter Plant “1710” and click Execute . The screen shown in Figure 7.38 will then appear, containing comprehensive details on XSteps. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 318 Figure 7.38 XSteps Repository Note SAP provides a standard XSteps library that you can downloaded from the SAP for Me website ( https://me.sap.com ) in an XML format and import into the SAP system. You can use the XSteps provided in this library as a starting point or even as a model for cre- ating your own XSteps. Refer to SAP Note 3156358 to gain a detailed understanding of and step-by-step instructions to implement the technical and functional areas of XSteps. It is also important to use Transaction CMX21 to create plant-wise entries with necessary con- trols in place that the system will check while importing XML files into the SAP system. 7.7.2 Importing the Standard XSteps Library To import the XML file containing the standard XSteps library, you use Transaction CMXSV.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: After executing Transaction CMXSV, define the plant by populating the Plant field in the initial screen that the system displays. Then, click Execute or press the (F8) key to access the XSteps repository. With the repository open, right-click the Standard XSteps folder and then choose Cre- ate  Folder to create a new folder in which to store the standard XSteps. The newly created folder appears on the next screen with the description <Folder> . After double-clicking this folder, you should change the description in the popup screen that appears.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The next step is to import the downloaded XML file containing the standard XSteps library to the newly created folder. To complete this step, right-click the folder you just created and select the Import Standard XStep option. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 319 7.7 Execution Steps In the popup screen that appears, select the file named SXS Library BASICS V1_0.XML under the previously mentioned folder ( XML_files_V_1_0 ) and then click the Open button. 7.7.3 Switching from Process Instructions to XSteps Whenever you’re transitioning from process instructions to XSteps in the master rec- ipe, the system issues the warning message that all previously created process instruc- tions become invalid when the changes made in the master recipe are saved. In addi- tion, the profile in the master recipe (see Chapter 4, Section 4.1.1) should allow for the creation of XSteps.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A warning message appears when you click the XSteps icon in the master recipe. (This icon is located on the top menu bar in Figure 7.39.) Choose Yes to proceed further (see Figure 7.39). Figure 7.39 Switching from Process Instructions to XSteps 7.7.4 General Information On the XSteps creation screen in the master recipe, choose XStep Tree and the system will create an XSteps icon on the left-hand side of the screen. Select the XStep Tree icon again, right-click on it, and select Properties from the dropdown list. Tips and Tricks You can also select relevant fields in XSteps, such as process instruction or calculation.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 320 On the Node Attributes screen that appears as shown in Figure 7.40, you enter a short description that then becomes visible throughout the XSteps tree. Choose the Parame- ters tab to bring up the next screen, which is described in the next section. Figure 7.40 Node Attributes in XSteps 7.7.5 Parameters Figure 7.41 shows the screen on which you can define all the parameters that will be used in the XSteps for data entry or calculation. docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA

However, in this case, you use charac- teristic value “PPPI_PARAMETER_VALUE,” which is delivered by the SAP system. docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 322 Figure 7.43 Destination in XSteps Figure 7.44 Process Instruction Creation in XSteps 7.7.8 Process Instructions You can create a new process instruction d by right-clicking New Process Instruction , choosing Create  Control Data , and then choosing the appropriate option. Here, you can freely define the input parameters, output parameters, function modules, and even control data. For example, you can manage calculations, process messages, com- mands, and function calls. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 323 7.7 Execution Steps The screen shown in Figure 7.45 appears when you select a process instruction and bring up the properties (by either pressing (Enter) or right-clicking to select the Prop- erties option). For this example, enter a description to identify the process instruction. Note Now that we’ve explained how to access the Properties option of any element in XSteps, we’ll only cover the details of the element, such as input value, output value, and calculation, without repeatedly referring to the Properties option.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 7.45 General Tab in Calculations The following sections cover some XSteps features that we previously touched upon to help you understand the similarities between process management and XSteps. We’ll also show additional features in XSteps. Parameter Values in XSteps The screen shown in Figure 7.46 appears when you create the first parameter by follow- ing menu path Create  Entry  Parameter Value . In Description , enter “Viscosity_Ini- tial”, and in the Parameters area, select T01 Viscosity_Initial from the Name dropdown list.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Notice that this is one of the same parameters defined when the XStep tree was first created. The remaining three tabs provide in-depth options to validate the values entered for a parameter. A user can choose to always accept a value, accept it with a dig- ital signature, or never accept an out-of-range value. You can also create your own text that the system will display in case of a failed check. Repeat the same process to create the second parameter value, with a description of “Viscosity_Final,” and select the parameter’s name from the Name dropdown list.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 324 Tips and Tricks As an alternative, you can choose Create  Entry  Numeric Value to achieve the same results as just described, but make sure you select the Parameters option from the dropdown list in the Default Value tab. Figure 7.46 Characteristic Details and Validation in XSteps Calculation in Execution Steps Now that you’ve created two parameter values in the XStep tree, let’s use them in calcu- lations. You can perform any kind of calculation, as long as the parameters are already defined in the XStep tree.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For this example, use the simple calculation of subtracting the value of one parameter from another to display the result as a calculated field. To perform a calculation, follow menu path Create  Control Data  Calculation . The screen shown in Figure 7.47 will then appear. Enter a short description: “Difference.” On the lower half of the screen, enter “T02 - T01” in the Calculation Formulas box. An important aspect to note is the Event field, in which “PARAMETER_CHANGED” is entered. An event is a control function that triggers the necessary action when the user or the system fulfills a specific and predefined event.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For this example, you stipulate that whenever there is a change (an event) in the Viscosity Difference field, the system should automatically calculate and update the value in the field. If an event isn’t defined, then the user will have to manually choose the Calculator icon to update the calculation in the Viscosity Difference field, based on any changes made to the param- eter values. Other examples of events include the system unlocking the table fields when the user maintains the PI sheet, locking the tables when all entries in the table are made, and activating or deactivating the PI sheet. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 325 7.7 Execution Steps Tips and Tricks To view all the available options in events, place the cursor on the Event field and press (F4) or choose the dropdown option. Figure 7.47 Calculation Formula in XSteps To simulate the fields, place the cursor on either the XStep tree or the process instruc- tion and then either press (F8) or right-click and choose Simulate . Figure 7.48 shows how the screen looks when you enter not only the two parameters but also the calculation. Notice that the calculated Difference field has a small Calcula- tor icon next to it to denote that the value in the field is a calculated value.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Many input, output, and control options are available in the XStep tree, so we briefly discuss the most relevant ones in the following sections. Note We encourage you to explore the large number of options available in XSteps, includ- ing the option to incorporate website addresses and images/figures (e.g., hazard or gloves signs), the option to enter long text or a short note, and so on. You can immedi- ately simulate the results to see if the settings are correct. If they aren’t correct, the sys- tem provides guidance to correct them or points out the shortcomings or deviations.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 326 Figure 7.48 Simulation of Calculation Formula in XSteps Output Characteristics and Values in Execution Steps If there is a business need to display a fixed value in an XStep or subsequently on the PI sheet, then you should use the Output Characteristic option. For example, you can enter the description “Value Output (Fixed)” and use the PPPI_Parameter_Value charac- teristic with a fixed value of 40. On the left-hand side of the same figure, you can again use the Output Characteristic option, but this time, select Note as the Characteristic , and in the Long Text field, enter the text shown.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This is fixed text that will display when the PI sheet is processed. Control Instruction You can also change the description of how each control instruction in the PI sheet appears. This option helps combine the relevant process instructions in one visual tab so that it’s easier for the line operator to either enter the details of the process parame- ters or simply use the available functions. To ensure that the system displays control instructions as a tab, you first enter the desired description of the control instruction and then select the Control Instruction characteristic from the dropdown menu.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Tables in Execution Steps To generate a table in the PI sheet using XSteps, you first create a process instruction and then follow menu path Create  Control Data  Table . The screen shown in Figure 7.49 provides the option to enter the minimum and maximum number of lines (rows) that must appear in the table. When you create a table, you maintain the input value of the parameters by following menu path Create  Entry  Numeric Value (or Parameter Value) . Figure 7.50 shows an example of a table created in XSteps with calculation and a signature option. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 327 7.7 Execution Steps Figure 7.49 Tables Settings in XSteps Figure 7.50 Tables in XSteps Scope of Generation in Execution Steps Whenever an XStep is created, the system provides the option to define the scope of generation, just as it does for process instructions. In this step, define the scope of gen- eration for materials, resources/work centers, documents, or orders. XSteps offer far greater generation options as compared to process instructions. Figure 7.51 lists the available options for scope of generation.

docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 328 Figure 7.51 Scope of Generation in XSteps Signature in Execution Steps At the process instruction level in XSteps, you can incorporate a signature at various steps of data entry (or other input) to validate the information entered (see Figure 7.50 again). You can even enter the details of a digital signature; the digital signature func- tionality is already configured in the system, and you can choose it by following menu path Create  Control Data  Signature . Process Messages in Execution Steps At the same level on which you enter a signature in the process instruction, you can select the associated process message.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To do so, follow menu path Create  Control Data  Process Message . Use the same process message example here that you created in Chapter 4. Enter Process Message Category “PP20” and the relevant message character- istic will automatically appear. Execution Steps Overview Place the cursor on any level and press (F8) to simulate the PI sheet, and it will appear on the right-hand side of the figure. For example, if Table Entries should appear earlier than you want in the XStep tree, simply select it and drag it to your desired new location. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 329 7.8 Process Message Evaluation 7.8 Process Message Evaluation The system offers process message evaluation as a report that you can use to access information on process messages. Process message evaluation integrates with Micro- soft Excel and offers the option to save the evaluated information either as a pivot table or simply as an Excel worksheet. You can use all the standard and self-defined process message characteristics in the evaluation. You can also self-define the layout for evaluation—that is, decide how the system should display the information during evaluation.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: But it’s important to first create an evaluation version before using it to evaluate process messages. For process message evaluation, use menu path Logistics  Production—Process  Pro- cess Management  Evaluation  Process Messages or use Transaction CO52. On the initial screen, enter the Plant as “1710” and the Evaluation version as “SAPS4” and then choose the Create icon. But first, create an evaluation version before using it in process message evaluation. You can also create a new evaluation version with refer- ence to an existing version.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To create an evaluation version, simply enter the Plant and choose the SAP XXL icon. The system will then bring up the screen shown in Figure 7.52, wherein a user can check the relevant boxes and save. The system will then ask the user to enter the Evaluation version and its Description . Figure 7.52 Selection Screen of Process Message Evaluation For this example, shown in Figure 7.52, you use the previously created Evaluation ver- sion SAPS4 and check the boxes in the line characteristics ( Line char. ) and column char- acteristics ( Col. char. ) columns for the characteristics (process messages) that need to be evaluated.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 330 appears in horizontal lines (in rows). For the Col. char. option, check the requisite boxes so that the data appears in columns. In this example, the control recipe status appears in a column, whereas the control recipe destination appears in a row. If you select the Evaluate option, the system downloads the information either in an Excel spreadsheet or in a pivot table format. Alternatively, you can use the Preview option. The first column and the related rows will show the control message ID.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the second column, the first row pertains to the control recipe status, whereas the second row reflects the control recipe number. 7.9 Process Manufacturing Cockpit Building on the configuration made in Chapter 4 for the process manufacturing cockpit, PP10, we now show how it appears when a user wants to use it for data entry and report- ing purposes. To access the process manufacturing cockpit, use menu path Logistics  Production—Process  Process Management  Manufacturing Cockpit  Start or use Transaction COPOC.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On the initial screen, enter the Plant as “1710” and the cockpit Name as “PP10.” Then, choose Execute . Figure 7.53 shows manufacturing cockpit PP10, in which the required details are main- tained. All details are optional, except for the Material quantity consumed field, which is mandatory, as denoted by the red asterisk. When you exit the process manufacturing cockpit, the process messages automatically become available in the message monitor (Transaction CO54XT). From there, you can send them to the predefined destinations.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 331 7.10 Resources Network 7.10 Resources Network A resource network is a group of individual resources used in the production process. The ability for a user to pick and choose from the available or even required resources during process order creation ensures smoother production. Using a resource network also eliminates the need to create a production version for every variant of the production. We’ll show you a real-time example in which several resources are available and usable for similar production processes, but the business process entails a user deciding which resource to use just before production begins.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For this purpose, a planning resource is defined that is only used for planning and that represents several resources that can be used in the same way. There’s a case of three equivalent resources (mixes), and the business requirement is that the user wants to dynamically (and in real time) select the actual resource while creating a process order level (before release). To map this business requirement in SAP S/4HANA, you use the resource network functionality. You begin by creating a specific task list usage type and checking the rel- evant box.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Then, you create the relevant master data (including the resource network), create a resource hierarchy, and assign them to a master recipe. Then, when a process order is created and ready to be released, the system will prevent the user from releas- ing it until the user selects one resource from a resource network. Let’s go through this step by step. First, you access the screen shown in Figure 7.54 via Transaction OP45 and create a new task list usage, Z08, by copying standard task list usage 008. In the detailed view, check the until rel. box to denote that this task list usage will only allow for release of a pro- cess order after one of the resources from the resource network is selected.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 7.54 Configuration Settings for Task List Type 2 Then, using Transaction CRC1, assign the previously created task list usage Z08 to Resource MIX_PLAN , as shown in Figure 7.55. Simultaneously, create a few additional resources (Mix1, Mix2, and Mix3) and assign standard task list usage 008 to them. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 332 Figure 7.55 Assigning Task List Usage in Planning Resource Next, access Figure 7.56 via Transaction CR24 to create Resource network MIX_RN . Here, assign all the previously created resources, including planning resource MIX_PLAN, by first choosing New Assignment and then entering individual resources in the popup that appears. Be sure to also check the Assignment Indicator box for each of the resources you’re adding to the resource network. To create relationships among these assigned resources in the resource network, choose Graphic in Figure 7.56, which brings up Figure 7.57.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 333 7.10 Resources Network The three resources in the resource network MIX_PLAN shown in Figure 7.57 appear connected to the planning resource MIX_PLAN . To connect a resource, first select the relevant resource and then choose Connect (shown on the right-hand side of Figure 7.57). Choosing a resource will also enable currently disabled options (such as Duplicate , Modify , and even Delete) to delete a resource from a resource network. Figure 7.57 Creating Resource Network Next, access the screen shown in Figure 7.58 via Transaction C201 or C202 (create or change a master recipe).

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Then, in the Recipe Header tab, enter “MIX_RN” for Resource netwrk to assign it. Figure 7.58 Assigning Resource Network in Master Recipe Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Production Planning for Process Manufacturing 334 Next, choose the Operations tab, which opens the screen shown in Figure 7.59. Then, assign only planning resource MIX_PLAN at the operation and phase levels and main- tain any additional details if required. Figure 7.59 Assigning Planning Resource in Operation and Phase Figure 7.60 shows the process order creation screen (Transaction COR1). While you’re trying to release the process order, the system sends an error message ( BS013—System Status WCRE Is Active ) to indicate that the process order release has failed.
