docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 337 Chapter 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing This chapter covers the important business processes and functions in repetitive manufacturing, along with the vital and logical links to required configuration. Repetitive manufacturing (REM) is mainly used for production scenarios with high rep- etition rates, high product stability, and low product complexity. REM is characterized by quantity-based and period-based production (uninterrupted production over a long period of time). The REM type is often mixed up with takt-based flow manufacturing, which is usually used whenever the production process is based on takt time (e.g., in the automobile industry).

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The two production types (REM and takt-based flow manu- facturing) have different business backgrounds and properties, and they use different SAP technologies, different master data, and even different planning tools. Note Refer to Chapter 1 for comparisons of discrete manufacturing, process manufacturing, and REM, as well as how to decide which manufacturing type is most relevant for a given industry. This chapter will discuss what REM is and how it fits into the planning and production perspectives. A walk through the REM process flow will provide you with a comprehen- sive, step-by-step understanding of each process involved.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll discuss the important REM master data and walk through how to run the end-to-end MRP process and how to use planning to optimize the production and procurement processes. We’ll also discuss performing the material availability check for missing components, as well as the capacity available check and overload, if any. Then, we’ll cover the actual and daily business processes in REM: planning tables and material staging, based on the current material situation; the creation of a production list; REM confirmation at the assembly, component, and activity levels; and capacity requirements planning.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Next, we move into handling scrap at various levels, cancella- tions, and reversals. A short discussion of cost object controlling is next, followed by discussing heijunka and its role in REM. Finally, we conclude with a few important eval- uation reports available in REM. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing 338 As often as possible, we link this chapter’s discussions with the configurations you made in Chapter 5. If necessary, we also give pointers to necessary configurations. 8.1 Overview Companies that work with high-volume and mass-produced materials (e.g., pens, pen- cils, keyboards, batteries) find that REM (rather than discrete manufacturing or process manufacturing) best reflects their production processes. If your actual business pro- cess is simple and straightforward, you should consider implementing the lean REM production type, as long as it can fulfill your business needs from a functional perspec- tive.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The SAP S/4HANA system supports and offers make-to-order (MTO) REM, which enables handling of configurable materials. REM also supports handling unit manage- ment , in which goods and packaging are mapped as a logistic unit. Serial number assignment for unique identification is also possible in REM, and make-to-stock (MTS) REM is equally possible. The following sections will cover how REM plays a central role in production planning and production execution, and they will also discuss the REM process flow. 8.1.1 Roles of Repetitive Manufacturing in Planning and Production Figure 8.1 provides an overview of the role of REM in the planning and production areas of the SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The planning process starts with requirements coming from SAP S/4HANA Sales or from the material forecast, and it then becomes a part of demand management. The system runs the MRP based on the figures given in the demand program, and the outcome of the MRP run (the planning run) is the creation of procurement proposals. These procurement proposals can be planned orders (order proposals), purchase requisitions for external procurement, or delivery schedules for scheduling agreements with vendors. In REM, the planned orders can’t be converted because these are sufficient to trigger the production process.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In fact, the REM planned orders take on the new order type of the run schedule quantity when the system assigns a production version to them. After actual production execution, the system records the relevant information, such as components consumption, activities consumption, and production yield. Finally, because REM is a period-based manufacturing type, the product costing team proceeds to the settlement process, in which it settles variances and overheads during cost col- lector settlement. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 339 8.1 Overview Figure 8.1 REM in Production Planning 8.1.2 Repetitive Manufacturing Process Flow Figure 8.2 illustrates the end-to-end process flow in REM. The process flow sequence is as follows: 1. The process begins when requirements from MRP (through planned independent requirements [PIRs]) or SAP S/4HANA Sales flow in, based on which the production must be initiated. The system covers the infinite requirements with planned orders during the MRP run. 2. The system performs the line loading and checks the capacity requirements to see if it’s able to produce the required quantities.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If it can’t, it’s overloaded. 3. The system checks for the availability of the components needed to produce the material. 4. The operational methods sheet that contains detailed instructions for producing the material can be printed. 5. It’s also possible to print the production list, which contains quantities to produce and important dates. A production list specific to a material or a production line can also be printed. Following the lean manufacturing principle, these are the only two shop floor papers. 6. The material needs to be staged by undertaking a transfer posting from the main store to the production floor, from where the components are issued to the produc- tion lines.

docs.text: 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing 340 7. The production execution step is the actual and physical production of the material. 8. If the business process entails working and reporting with reporting point back- flush (milestone confirmation), then the WIP can be calculated. 9. The production yield, record issuance, consumption of components, and postpro- duction activities are recorded. Excess component consumption, excess activities such as machine hours or labor hours consumed (as compared to standard dura- tions), and scrap can also be recorded.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It’s also possible to record any deviation in consumption. 10. The last step reflects the integration of CO with PP, in which the product costing team performs settlement using the product cost collector. docs.text: 341 8.2 Master Data 8.2 Master Data Before running processes and jobs in the SAP S/4HANA system, you must set up com- plete and comprehensive master data. REM has its own unique master data that often overlaps with other production types, such as discrete manufacturing and process manufacturing. If master data is set up in the right sequence, it’s much easier and more logical to interconnect because the predecessor-successor relationship is already taken care of. Table 8.1 provides an overview of the master data that is needed in REM.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It begins with the material master of the product (a finished good or an assembly), which you specifi- cally mark as the REM type in the MRP 4 view of the material master by checking the relevant box. You also assign it the REM profile that you previously configured (in Chapter 5). You then create a BOM of the product that needs to be produced, and you assign the components together with the quantities needed to produce that product. If needed, you can also define a scrap percentage at the operation or component level.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Then, you create a work center or production line, followed by a rate routing for the material, in which you assign the previously created work center. Finally, you assign the material’s BOM and rate routing to a production version for the material. You then check the REM box to denote that the material produced will follow the REM process. When all of the logistics master data is in place, the CO team can create product cost col- lectors of the material. This can be specific to or independent of the production version.

docs.text: 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing 342 Note We strongly recommended that you maintain close coordination and liaison with the CO team to ensure that when they’re working with PP, both teams are completely aligned in terms of their working and reporting needs. For example, each work center (production line) must be assigned a cost center, which the CO team should provide. It may provide one cost center for multiple work centers or one cost center for an individual work center, depending on how the team wants to see the cost center reporting and evaluation.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: One possible approach to having several cost centers within one production line is to incorporate additional cost-relevant operations (in the rate routing) and still adhere to the principle of just one work center for production (and PP). Let’s now discuss how to set up each of the REM-specific master data areas. 8.2.1 Material Master The first step in creating REM-specific master data begins with creating the necessary settings in the material master of the product (an assembly or a finished good). To change the material master, you follow menu path Logistics  Materials Management  Material Master  Material  Change  Immediately or use Transaction MM02.

Loc. “171A.” Choose Continue to bring up Select Views , in which you select MRP 4 and press (Enter) again. On the screen shown in Figure 8.3, you maintain the details related to REM production processes in the MRP 4 view of the material master. Then, you check the Repet. Manu- facturing box to denote that the material will undergo the REM production process. Then, select PP10 in the REM Profile field.

A REM profile is a four-digit code that determines the following:  The movement type that the system uses to post GRs and GIs  How the system reduces planned orders and run schedule quantities in the confir- mation process  How the system makes the correction in the assembly’s components (according to BOM), which enables you to define whether GI posting isn’t possible in the system due to forgotten GR postings or whether the system should process the same later on in a separate backflush processing transaction © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

Refer to Chapter 6, Section 6.2.2, which covers the details of material BOM creation. 8.2.3 Work Center (Production Line) The alternative term for a work center in the SAP S/4HANA system is a production line .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Work center is a term specific to discrete manufacturing, whereas production line is spe- cific to REM. Production lines are usually created as simple work centers in the system (and because the SAP system refers to these as work centers , we’ll use both terms throughout this chapter to maintain a logical connection between the SAP terms and real-world business scenarios). In the work center, you define the availability of the production line. In REM, following the lean manufacturing principle, you don’t model all workstations in the production line as individual work centers.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Rather, you model the entire production line (with all of its work centers) as one work center. You enter the production line you create as the work center in the Production Line field in the pro- duction version, and you specify this same work center in the single operation of the Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

To create a work center (production line), you follow menu path Logistics  Production  Master Data  Work Centers  Work Center  Create or use Transaction CR01. On the ini- tial screen you use to create the work center, enter Plant “1710” to create a production line. It’s mandatory to assign a plant while creating a production line. Enter “KBASSY” for Work Center .

A production line can be a production facility, a processing unit, a machine or group of machines, or a laborer or group of laborers directly involved in the production process. Some of the activities include production time, setup time, processing time, and labor time.

docs.text: 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing 348 For this example, enter the following in each field or check the relevant box:  Capacity Category short text (not shown): “Keyboard Assembly Line-1” This short text describes the capacity category—for example, the specific produc- tion line or machine.  Capacity Responsible : “A” It’s important to assign a capacity planner group to a production line, so that during evaluation of capacities, the capacity planner group can be one of the evaluation cri- teria.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The capacity planner group shouldn’t be the name of the person but instead the area or domain of responsibilities.  Capacity Base Unit : “Min” (for minutes) This is the unit of measure (in minutes) in which the system displays the capacity of a production line.  Start Time : “08:00:00” This is the start time of a production line.  End Time : “17:00:00” This is the end time of a production line.  Length of Breaks : “01:00:00” This is the total length of breaks during the start and end of shifts. Break time reduces the availability time of the capacity of a production line.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, if a machine runs 12 hours a day, with two hours of daily breaks, then the available capacity of the production line is 10 hours. Note that this fact is considered in lead time scheduling of orders.  Capacity Utilization : “100” (percent) This is the actual capacity utilization factor. This factor has to be as realistic and as close to the actual capacity of a production line as possible to enable the system to calculate the available capacity of the production line. The capacity utilization is reduced accordingly if the production line can’t be used for a certain percentage of time—for example, due to machine failure.  No.

For example, four individual ice cream mixers are created as one production line, so the individual capacities are four in number and directly multiplied by the timings of the capacity of the production line. For example, if the available capacity of a pro- duction line is 10 hours a day, and if there are four individual capacities, then the total available capacity of the production line is 40 hours.  Relevant to Finite Scheduling Checking this box requires the system to consider capacity overload during capacity evaluation.  Overload % A capacity overload of a certain percentage directly increases the capacity availabil- ity of the production line by the defined percentage.

docs.text: 351 8.2 Master Data  Activity Type (production time) The activity type denotes the predefined rate at which the system calculates the work performed by a production line.  Formula Key (production time) A formula denotes the parameters that the system considers while calculating the cost incurred in performing work at a production line. Then, save the work center. 8.2.4 Rate Routing Rate routings are designed for the maintenance of production rate−based task lists and are used in REM, among other business scenarios.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In a standard routing, the base quan- tity (e.g., pieces) generally remains constant, and the time-related data, such as the pro- cessing time, is maintained using standard values. Rate routing works in exactly the opposite way. The production quantities are maintained on the basis of individual items, and the reference time is constant. Thus, a rate routing describes the quantity of an item that must be produced within a given period of time. A rate routing can contain a series of operations. The production rate is defined for each operation based on the production quantity, production time, and associated unit of measure.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The production rate is determined as the quotient of the production quan- tity and production time. This enables a production planner to determine the produc- tion quantity in terms of tons per shift, for example. Usually, only one operation is pro- duction relevant, and the others may be controlling or print relevant. Using line hierar- chies, several production-relevant operations can support capacity leveling in different work centers along the production line. All other aspects of the functionality and maintenance of standard routings and rate routings are identical.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Work centers are assigned to the rate routing, which should also contain the standard value key in which the standard values for production time, setup time, and teardown time are predefined. A reference routing is used as a reference or template in routings. A reference rate rout- ing contains a sequence of operations. As with a rate routing, the production rate for an operation is defined on the basis of the production quantity and reference time. The functionality and maintenance of reference routings are similar to those of reference operation sets.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To create a rate routing, you follow menu path Logistics  Production  Master Data  Line Design  Rate Routing  Create or use Transaction CA21. On the initial screen where you create a rate routing, enter Material “2256” and Plant “1710.” In the Key Date field, enter “07/01/2024” and denote the date when the rate routing becomes available in the pro- duction process. Because the rate routing validity starts on July 01, 2024, this rate rout- ing won’t be available if, for example, a production planner creates an REM planned order for the month of April 2024.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing 352 If you provide no date during rate routing creation, then the system will automatically assign the rate routing’s creation date as the valid from date. In the following sections, we’ll cover the various elements of rate routing. Header Details Choose the Header icon. In the header details of the rate routing, enter the following:  Usage : “1” (for production) This makes the rate routing available during subsequent production activities, in which the system will use the rate routing during the creation of the REM planned order.  Status : “4” (released) This makes the rate routing available during subsequent production activities, in which the system will use the rate routing during the creation of the REM planned order.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If the status of the rate routing is set to Being Created ( Status 1 ), it won’t be available when a REM planned order for the material is created.  Planning Work Center : “KBASSY” This is the production line that you previously created and is now used in the plan- ning and production of the material.  From Lot Size : “1” PC This denotes that the smallest quantity of the REM planned order must be at least 1 PC for the system to consider using this rate routing. In other words, this rate rout- ing is applicable when you create the REM planned order of a quantity greater than or equal to 1 PC.  To : “999,999” PC This denotes that the maximum quantity of the REM planned order is 999,999 PC for the system to consider using this rate routing.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In other words, this rate routing is applicable when a REM planned order with a quantity greater than or equal to 1 PC but less than or equal to 999,999 PC is created. Note Because QM also integrates with REM, you need to engage the QM resource for this activity. Next, choose the Operations button. Figure 8.10 shows the resulting screen, in which KBASSY is the work center (in the Work Ctr column). This denotes assigning a previ- ously created work center (production line) to an operation, which is used in the pro- duction of a material and for which you’re creating the rate routing.

On this screen, choose the Components Allo- cation icon. Figure 8.12 shows the component allocation in rate routing.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These components are directly taken from a material’s BOM, which you created in the previous step. Figure 8.12 Material Component Overview in Routing If you don’t assign a specific component to a specific operation, the system will assign all components to the first operation of the rate routing. This means that all compo- nents must be available at the time of the first operation so that during backflush, the system can consume all components in the first operation. If a business process entails that a few components will be used or needed in the later stages of the production process, then you select them and use the Reassign button to assign specific components to the operation. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 355 8.2 Master Data Because there is only one operation in REM, the preceding scenario of material assign- ment is broadly more applicable in discrete manufacturing than in REM. Material Assignment Going back to the rate routing header screen (Figure 8.12), choose the New Assignment button. A production planner can assign several materials, together with their respec- tive plants, to this rate routing group ( 50000003 ). All such materials belonging to this rate routing group will have the same group but with an ascending group counter number.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In other words, many of the materials undergoing the same production process will need separate routings. To accomplish this, just create one rate routing and assign rel- evant materials (with plants) to it. This saves time and effort in creating an important part of the master data (rate routing) and also eliminates or reduces redundant data entry efforts. Finally, save the rate routing. 8.2.5 Production Version Production versions denote different ways in which a company produces a material— for example, a material with one rate routing but multiple BOMs.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Therefore, for each BOM and the same rate routing, the system needs a separate production version to denote its uniqueness during REM planned order creation. The requirement to create a separate production version also applies when there is one BOM for a material but multiple routings. In the REM process, it’s mandatory to create a production version and make it available. The production version can also be specific to the quantity range, thus acting as a control function. For example, you can create one production version that has a quantity limita- tion of 1 to 1,000 PC and another production version for a quantity greater than 1,000 PC.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The production version can also be specific to the validity period, thus acting as a con- trol function. For example, a production version can be valid from April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2025, and from April 1, 2025, on, a new production version will be effective. When the system has to assign the production version to the REM planned order, it searches for specific validity dates and automatically assigns the relevant production version when it finds it. If the system can find multiple production versions that fulfill the search and applica- tion criteria, it assigns the first available production version to the REM planned order.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The first available production version refers to the list that can be called from the mate- rial master (in the MRP 4 or Work Scheduling views). To create a new production version, you follow menu path SAP Menu  Logistics  Pro- duction  Master Data  Production Versions or use Transaction C223. Then, in the Selec- tion Conditions area of the screen shown in Figure 8.13, enter Plant “1710” and Material Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing 356 “2256” and then press (Enter) . If the system is unable to find a production version for the material, then the lower half of the screen will appear blank. If the system is suc- cessful, then it will display the relevant production versions. Figure 8.13 Production Version Creation Initial Screen A menu bar is available at the bottom of the production version creation screen that has just about all of the options you’ll normally need while creating production version master data, including copying, deleting, copying from a template, and so on.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Choose the Create Production Version icon and an almost empty screen will appear for maintaining details, as shown in Figure 8.14. Figure 8.14 Production Version of Material 2256 © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing 358 The Lock field in the Production Version area of the screen provides the flexibility to lock or unlock the production version anytime to allow or restrict access to the produc- tion version during REM planned order creation. A locked production version won’t be available for selection during REM planned order creation. Finally, click the Check button for a consistency check to evaluate whether the details incorporated in the production version are correct and valid.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system confirms that it’s able to find a relevant task list (a rate routing) as well as the BOM, which meets the other criteria of the production version. This includes hav- ing validity dates for the rate routing and the BOM, which falls within the validity spec- ified in the production version, as well as the lot sizes mentioned in the production ver- sion. docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If the system returns a warning or error during the consistency check, it will indicate it with a yellow or a red traffic light, respectively. Note Performing a consistency check isn’t a prerequisite for using a correct production ver- sion, but it can give you confidence that eventually, a valid production version will be available to work with. Finally, choose Close Detailed Screen and Adopt Changes and save the production ver- sion. Note If detailed scheduling and capacity planning functionalities are required in the REM business processes of your company, then we recommend that you use a routing (instead of a rate routing) and assign it to the production version.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Details of how to cre- ate a routing were covered in Chapter 6. Later in this chapter, we’ll cover detailed scheduling and capacity planning in REM while using a rate routing. The formulas used in rate routing (such as SAPR02, in this example) should allow you to perform scheduling and capacity calculation, and you can do this by checking the relevant boxes in the formula you’re using in the rate rout- ing (Transaction OP55). 8.3 Material Requirements Planning in Repetitive Manufacturing Extensive coverage of MRP is provided in Chapter 13.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 359 8.3 Material Requirements Planning in Repetitive Manufacturing process entails that a production planner has already planned to produce predeter- mined quantities of a product and use MRP for comprehensive planning, including the components (the BOM) of the product. It’s important to note that there are no REM-spe- cific details for MRP; REM uses standard MRP. For example, preplanning isn’t a prereq- uisite for REM. REM based planning can also be used on sales orders only (MTO). For this example, we use strategy 40 (the MTS production method), which is a typical case in REM.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can use any planning strategy in conjunction with REM (MTO and MTS), and we’ll focus on a typical real-world example in the keyboard manufacturing industry. For normal and standard planning, the planning process starts with either a sales order forming the basis of planning or quantities calculated from forecasting. Any or all of these quantities are forwarded to demand management, which ends up forming the PIRs. The MRP considers PIRs and generates procurement proposals, including planned orders. A production planner then evaluates the planning results and converts them into procurement elements for external procurement; these don’t need to be con- verted any further or for REM types.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The steps are as follows: 1. Maintain planned independent requirements You use Transaction MD61 to enter the PIRs into the screen shown in Figure 8.15. Enter Material “2256,” Plant “1710,” and Version “00,” and then define the planning horizon from “07/01/2024” to “08/05/2025.” Press (Enter) . Next, enter the planning quantities as maintained in Figure 8.15 and save the PIR. The next step is to run the MRP. Figure 8.15 Planned Independent Requirements 2. Run material requirements planning In this step, the materials planner runs MRP Live by using Transaction MD01N.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 8.16 shows the initial screen to run MRP. You set the parameters as shown and choose Execute (not shown) to begin the process of running MRP. As soon as the sys- tem completes the planning process (the MRP run), it displays the planning results. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing 360 Figure 8.16 Initial Screen of MRP Live 3. Display planning results Figure 8.17 shows the planning results for both material 2256 and its associated com- ponents. The next step is to evaluate the planning results of material 2256 by either double-clicking the material directly or first saving the planning results and then using Transaction MD04 for the material and plant combination to see the stock/ requirements list. For this example, use the first option: double-click the planning results of material 2256.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 8.17 Planning Results of MRP Run The system also creates multiple planned orders ( PldOrd ) to cater to the PIRs (see Figure 8.18). © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

Save the MRP results and all of these planning details will become available on the REM planning table. 8.4 Planning Table The planning table in REM is highly interactive and enables the planner to perform many functions and activities with all details automatically updated. For example, if you create a new planned order in the planning table, the system automatically updates the capacity requirements in the upper half of the planning table screen.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The planning table also provides comprehensive visibility into material and capacity avail- abilities. In fact, important planning in REM, such as line loading planning, is generally undertaken in the planning table. In the following sections, we’ll discuss the planning table parameters and how to create orders. 8.4.1 Parameters Selection To access the planning table in REM, you follow menu path Logistics  Production  Repetitive Manufacturing  Planning  Planning Table  Change Mode or use Transaction MF50. Figure 8.19 shows the initial screen for the selection criteria, which allows you to enter important selection parameters.

Some of the other selection options are Pro- duction Line , Material , Product Group , MRP Controller , and so on.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA

docs.text: 365 8.4 Planning Table Tips and Tricks If a production planner can’t see editable fields such as KBASSY or Not Assigned , as shown in the planning table in Figure 8.22, double-click the Not Assigned field under Material Data and these fields will appear. 8.4.2 Creating a Repetitive Manufacturing Planned Order As a planner, you have to make changes to existing planning elements, such as planned orders, and you also have to create new planned orders to account for production con- straints or other practical realities, such as an unplanned plant or machine shutdown.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Because the REM planning table is interactive, you can perform all of these important planning functions and much more within the REM planning table. When you exit the REM planning table, save the interactive planning to enable the system to update the information accordingly. Then dou- ble-click the field in which you entered the quantity of 350. docs.text: 369 8.4 Planning Table 8.4.4 Changes and Evaluations You can make any changes and evaluations in the planning table, and the system will update all the information on a real-time basis. Some of these functions are listed in Table 8.3. 8.4.5 Range of Coverage If you’ve already made the necessary configuration for the range of coverage profile and you’ve assigned this coverage profile to the material master in the MRP 2 view of the material master, then you have the option to evaluate the coverage in the planning table.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, you must first activate this in the View menu. The range of coverage profile contains the parameters for calculating the dynamic safety stock, and this is a statistical calculation on the basis of average daily requirements. The range of coverage profile includes, for example, maximum stock level, minimum stock level, target stock, and the statistical and actual range of coverage. docs.text: 371 8.5 Material Staging 8.5 Material Staging Material staging is the step in which the components from the replenishment storage location are transferred to the issuing storage location. These components are con- sumed during the actual production process. This step involves the stock transfer transaction with standard movement type 311, and it transfers stock from the replen- ishment storage location to the issuing storage location. The system issues or back- flushes the components of the material from an issuing storage location.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Tips and Tricks The alternative term used for material staging is pull list . A pull list provides details on which material’s components are faced with shortages. At the same time, it also trig- gers stock transfers. You can also use storage location MRP or Kanban as the pull list. You can view the current or existing material situation of the planned orders before proceeding to stage the materials. Evaluating the current material situation gives a materials planner a better perspective, and it helps them decide which components should be staged first.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Material staging in REM is typically carried out with reference to a certain time horizon or a certain time interval—for example, a shift or until the end of the week. Except for MTO, materials aren’t staged with reference to any specific planned order. Similarly, the GR of the material produced is period based, with or with- out reference to planned orders. In the following sections, we’ll explain how to view the current situation, trigger replenishment, evaluate the material documents that the system created for material staging, and perform collective availability checks. 8.5.1 Current Situation To view the current situation in the pull list, you follow menu path Logistics  Produc- tion  Repetitive Manufacturing  Material Staging  Pull List—Current Situation or use Transaction MF63.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On the initial parameter selection screen, you choose from a large number of selection options and also define the end date for requirements in the Selection Horizon for Rqmts field . This is the date until which the system will consider the requirements of materials. There are also selection options for when a company uses the Kanban produc- tion process or has integrated with either warehouse management in SAP S/4HANA or embedded extended warehouse management (embedded EWM) in SAP S/4HANA. For this example, you define the Plant as “1710” (this is a mandatory entry requirement) and set the Selection Horizon for Rqmts as “12/02/2025,” which is the end date until which the system will consider all materials requirements.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing 372 Then, you limit the selection to Production Line (work center) “KBASSY” and choose Execute or press (F8) . This brings up the screen shown in Figure 8.30. Figure 8.30 Pull List This screen shows the current stock and requirements situation of the planned orders in detail. It also shows the available stock, as well as the shortage quantities for the period under evaluation. The screen also shows the shortage quantity of each individ- ual material. 8.5.2 Trigger Replenishment To trigger replenishment from one storage location (the replenishment storage loca- tion) to another (the issuing storage location within a plant), you follow menu path Logistics  Production  Repetitive Manufacturing  Material Staging  Pull List—Trigger Replenishment or use Transaction MF60.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Then, enter the initial parameters in the selection screen, which brings up the screen shown in Figure 8.31. Note that this screen’s appearance will greatly depend on the parameters that you defined on the initial parameter selection screen. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA

This shows the same quantity shortage seen previously in Section 8.5.1. Figure 8.31 Pull List at Storage Location Level Next, choose the Additional Data button to see detailed information on the require- ments for a material.

docs.text: Then, enter the Quantity Staged as “9750,” and in the lower half of the same screen, enter the RepLoc (replenishment storage location) as “171A” (not shown). If the staging is successful, the system will display the relevant message on the left- hand side of the screen (see the Staging column and the green checkmark), and it will also turn the status traffic light green.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Because this is a transfer posting between two storage locations, the system creates a material document , which records the details of inventory movements. Use Transaction MIGO to view the material document created after material staging. 8.5.3 Collective Availability Check As a production planner, you must frequently and consistently monitor the availabil- ity of the components that are needed to produce materials. While you can always per- form an availability check of an individual planned order in REM, it’s more efficient to Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing 374 do a collective availability check on several materials simultaneously to gain a better understanding of the material availability situation and then plan or take action accordingly. In the collective availability check option, you use a large number of selection parame- ters to choose the information that the system should display. To perform a collective availability check, use menu path Production  Repetitive Man- ufacturing  Planning  Collective Availability Check or use Transaction MDVP.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On the initial screen, enter the desired parameters and choose Execute or press (F8) . If the sys- tem finds a materials shortage, it identifies the shortage with a red traffic light. Choose the Missing Parts icon for an in-depth analysis and evaluation; it contains details of the requirements versus available quantities, as well as the dates when the required and shortage material should be in stock to initiate the production process on a timely basis. The availability check function in SAP checks the availability but can’t trigger replenishment. 8.6 Production List A production list is a list of REM-planned orders that can be printed for information and record-keeping purposes.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A production list can also be created and printed for a specific production line or work center hierarchy. This is helpful for production supervisors and line operators (on the shop floor) who don’t have access to the SAP system, to give them information access and for necessary planning and action, where needed. On the selection screen, you can choose how the ensuing production list should appear as an output. To create a production list, follow menu path Logistics  Production  Repetitive Manu- facturing  Planning  Production List or use Transaction MF51.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On the initial selection parameters screen, you can choose to print the production list based on the defined period and whether the system should consider only firmed planned orders, scheduled planned orders, or dispatched planned orders. For this example, you define the period of examination as 07/01/2024 to 12/31/2024 and enter the Production Line as “KBASSY.” Then, choose Execute or press (F8) to open the screen shown in Figure 8.32. This screen shows the production list of REM planned orders. In the period under evaluation, there are a few REM planned orders in the pro- duction list.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These are run schedule quantities, which means that production can pro- ceed because they are already assigned to the KBASSY production line. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 375 8.7 Confirmation Figure 8.32 Production List Operational Methods Sheet The operational methods sheet is primarily used by production personnel to obtain a clear understanding of and step-by-step directions for producing a material. You can configure the layout of an operational methods sheet to set the information that needs to appear in it. It integrates with Microsoft Word, and you can make any last- minute changes before printing it. Furthermore, there is an option to print the sheet at the header level or at the operation level.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To print an operational methods sheet, follow menu path Logistics  Production  Mas- ter Data  Line Design  Rate Routing  Print Operational Method Sheets or use Transac- tion LDE1. On the initial parameter selection screen, enter Material “2256” and Plant “1710.” It’s also important to select a template for either the cover sheet, the individual operation, or both. For this example, select the template for the individual operation and choose Execute or press (F8) . Word will open, and when the system asks you to, you can choose to enable or disable the macros.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this example, choose Enable Macros . 8.7 Confirmation Assume that a company manufactures products on a long production line with a long lead time. With long lead times, the GIs for the components may be posted much later in the system than when they are actually physically withdrawn. All components used Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing 376 along the production line are usually backflushed during final confirmation, but the GIs for the first components at work centers are posted on time and not by backflush- ing with a final confirmation at the end of the production line. An REM confirmation indicates that the actual production has happened and that the production supervisor is now entering the details of the goods produced in the system. It’s important to note that during the assembly backflush, the system automatically posts the component consumption (the GI).

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system performs the necessary functions depending on how the REM profile is set up and assigned to a material. In this case, it makes sense to use reporting point confir- mation to post the withdrawal of components (and production activities) at an earlier stage, after operations are already completed. In the following sections, we cover how to perform confirmation for REM assembly, REM components, and REM activities.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll also give an overview of when and how backflushing should be used in REM situations, as well as the different types of back- flushing that are available in REM. 8.7.1 Overview When the GR is posted for the finished parts during confirmation, a number of differ- ent actions are performed by default (these are controlled to a large extent by using the REM profile):  Posting GI for the components used by using the backflush option  Reducing run schedule quantities/planned orders and the associated capacity requirements on the production lines  Posting production costs incurred (material costs, production activities, and over- head costs) to a product cost collector  Creating a data entry document (a material and/or financial document)  Updating statistics in the LIS Other optional actions (see the Details icon in the confirmation transaction) include the following:  Taking account of the setup costs for material quantities that are independent of their lot sizes  Posting component and assembly scrap  Performing collective entry for different materials in a line  Archiving confirmation documents  Performing GI confirmation only or activity confirmation only (more or less activity)  Using reporting point confirmations  Decoupling confirmation processes © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 377 8.7 Confirmation  Performing aggregation  Using postprocessing and reversal options In addition, production based on sales orders enables confirmation with reference to sales orders. Note We configured REM profile PP10 in Chapter 5, Section 5.1; revisit that chapter to see the settings that were made. Although the consumption of system-recorded components is based on a BOM calcu- lation, it’s possible to make changes to consumption quantities during the REM assem- bly backflush. Separately, a production supervisor can also use this component’s back- flush option to record excess component consumption, either against a specific REM planned order or for general consumption during the production process.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The confirmation can be any of the following types:  Assembly confirmation The production of goods is complete, and the production supervisor wants to record the yield of the produced material. At the same time, there’s a need to record the consumption of the components against the produced goods based on the standard BOM. The user can also record the assembly scrap on the same screen with a differ- ent posting.  Component confirmation The user can record extra consumption of the components against the produced goods, based on the standard BOM.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The user can also record component scrap on the same screen. Furthermore, components can be issued if backflush isn’t applicable. (This scenario isn’t used often.)  Activity confirmation The user can record excess consumption of the activities, such as machine hours, labor hours, or setup hours, against the produced goods based on the rate routing. Furthermore, the user can record activity scrap on the same screen. As with assembly backflush, several options are available on the component backflush screen:  Record corresponding information during REM confirmation and backflush.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This flexibility is available because the REM production type caters to all MTS and MTO productions.  Record components’ scrap, either with reference to the assembly material or stand- alone. The movement type for scrap is 551.  Reverse the material document for an already posted consumption or scrap.  Perform a reversal function, without reference to any material document. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing 378 8.7.2 Assembly Confirmation To access the REM confirmation for an assembly backflush, you follow menu path Logistics  Production  Repetitive Manufacturing  Data Entry  Repetitive Manufactur- ing Confirmation or use Transaction MFBF. On the initial screen of REM confirmation, select the Assembly backflush radio button (see Figure 8.33). Use this screen to confirm the production yield and to record components’ consumption and activities (if config- ured in the REM profile).

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 8.33 Assembly Backflush in REM Confirmation Also, record assembly scrap, if any, by choosing the Scrap button. We cover how to record assembly scrap later in this chapter, in Section 8.8.3. Next, choose the Details button. The system will bring up the REM profile (in this exam- ple, PP10), in which you can still do the following:  Post activity backflush  Make stock postings to unrestricted, quality, or blocked stock  Change backflushing options—for example, from online to background  Post ordering costs © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA

Furthermore, you use this screen for document-specific or docu- ment-neutral reversals of the entered values. We cover document-specific reversal in Section 8.8. It’s also important to note that you have flexibility to record the yield of the assembly without reference to the REM planned order because then, the system can account for period-based confirmation. However, doing so won’t reduce the quantity specific to the planned order for the MTS scenario (if such settings are made in the REM profile).

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For MTO, the system reduces the planned order quantity. The three tabs— Make-to-Stock , Make-to-Order , and Production by Lot —cater to vari- ous production scenarios. 8.7.3 Component Confirmation When you select the Component backflush radio button in Figure 8.33, the system will offer you the following two options:  No BOM explosion (Manual Component Entry) In this option, you enter the assembly in the Material field so that the system can find the link with the product cost collector. If you select No BOM Explosion , the Pro- cess Component List will be empty.  Propose Components Acc.to BOM This option lets you enter a quantity of the assembly material, and the system will explode the assembly BOM and propose the component quantities for backflush or excess consumption.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If you select this option, you must provide the reference quan- tity of the assembly material. A production supervisor can also select the relevant radio button to indicate whether excess component consumption for a specific reporting point or after the last report- ing point took place. This radio button only appears if a valid reporting point is entered. 8.7.4 Activities Confirmation When you select the Activity backflush radio button in the REM confirmation screen (Transaction MFBF) shown earlier in Figure 8.33, the system displays the following two options:  No Planned Activities from Rate Routing In this option, you enter the material number together with the activity types, as well as the corresponding duration of each activity.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system doesn’t make any suggestions.  Fetch Planned Activities from Rate Routing With this option, you enter the quantity of the assembly material and the system will refer to the rate routing of the assembly material and propose the details. When you select this option, you must give the reference quantity of the assembly material. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing 380 8.7.5 Actual Assembly Confirmation In the screen shown in Figure 8.34, you perform the actual assembly backflush posting for Material 2256 , Plant 1710 , and Production Version 0001 . The yield confirmation for the material in this REM assembly backflush is 10 EA . Because the configured and assigned REM profile PP10 stipulates that there should be mandatory reporting point backflushing, you check the RP Confirmation box and also assign Reporting Point 0010 . Figure 8.34 Assembly Backflush against Planned Order Reporting point backflush in REM occurs when the system is able to automatically backflush several operations in the processing sequence.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Using the reporting point backflush procedure, a production supervisor can backflush components synchro- nized with actual consumption as much as possible. From the controlling perspective, reporting point backflush displays WIP for assemblies that haven’t completely been backflushed. The REM profile controls whether to use the reporting point backflush for a material; furthermore, the control key is used to determine whether an operation is a reporting point operation (a milestone). If so, then all previous operations that haven’t been confirmed yet or all previous operations that aren’t mandatory reporting points are automatically backflushed together.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 381 8.7 Confirmation points, the system should backflush components according to the processing sequence of the reporting point operations. You save the entries at this stage, and the system performs the following three func- tions:  It performs GR (yield confirmation) of 10 PC for material 2256.  It performs backflush (GI) of components according to the BOM of 2256.  It records and updates activities according to the rate routing of material 2256. Choose the Post with Correction button in the menu bar to open the screen shown in Figure 8.34, which shows that the system is performing two functions simultaneously.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: First, it’s confirming the yield of 10 EA for assembly Material 2256 ; then, in the second step, it’s recording the consumption of all the components that are used in the produc- tion of the assembly. Notice Movement Type 261 , which indicates consumption or GI, as shown in Figure 8.35. You can change the quantity of any component, if needed, and you can add or delete components as necessary. For example, to overwrite (change) the quantity of compo- nent 10, you can overwrite the quantity given in the Quantity column (see Figure 8.35).

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 8.35 Posting Excess Consumption Similarly, to delete a component from this screen, you first select the component and then choose Delete . On the ensuing Processing Activities screen (see Figure 8.36), you can make changes to activities such as Production time and Teardown . This screen takes the standard duration details from the rate routing of material 2256. If you make any changes to durations to reflect actual durations (whether on the higher or the lower side), the system will correspondingly and automatically update the cost details when you save the confirmation.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the Reason field, you can define the reason for the excess consumption of activities. This is also known as the reason for variance . You can also give reasons for variance as one of the selection criteria to generate a standard SAP system report, which can even- tually help in analysis and evaluation. Examples of reasons for variance can be machine malfunctions, electrical faults, labor shortages, emergency shutdowns, and so on. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

Tips and Tricks When you’re defining reasons for variance, we recommend that you take past experi- ences into account as the major or possible reasons for delayed production, excess con- sumption, and so on. Also, consider which reasons are important for analysis and reporting purposes and thus should be available as selection options when running standard or custom-developed reports.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When you’re saving the REM assembly backflush, the system issues the following mes- sage at the bottom of the screen to confirm the goods movements (GI and GR) and activities you’re posting: GR and GI with document XXX and activities posted . This means that the system successfully posted the GR (production yield), GI (components consumption), and recording of the actual production activities’ durations. It’s import- ant to add that the business process depends on whether or not the planned activities, per the rate routing, have been adjusted manually during the confirmation according to the real production efforts. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 383 8.7 Confirmation 8.7.6 Separated Backflush If you need to manage a large number of backflush processes—that is, a high volume of data entry for GI and for activity postings—then you should use the separated back- flush functionality. In separated backflush, the system posts GI and activities during a slower time of the day (or even at night). You control the separated backflush option in the REM profile creation (configuration). To perform separated backflushing, follow menu path Logistics  Production  Repeti- tive Manufacturing  Data Entry  Separated Backflush or use Transaction MF70.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Enter the appropriate parameters on the initial screen and check the appropriate boxes, such as Post Goods Issue and/or Post Production Activities . 8.7.7 Postprocessing of Components If you’ve defined that the system should not perform online error correction during REM confirmation, then you can correct these errors later on. The nature of the error can be that there were insufficient component quantities for backflush (GI) during confirmation—for instance, due to incorrect or delayed postings in MM. Alternatively, there can be errors when the system is unable to find the storage location to backflush (GI) components from.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It’s important to attend to these errors in a timely manner because they’ll continue to accumulate in the incorrect goods movement log. To postprocess components (or other errors), follow the SAP menu path Logistics  Production  Repetitive Manufactur- ing  Data Entry  Postprocess  Postprocessing Individual Components or use Transac- tion COGI. Note To use Transaction COGI, select the Also Create Individual Postprocessing Records option in the REM profile. Enter the appropriate parameters on the initial screen and then choose Execute or press (F8) .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The ensuing screen will list all the confirmations in which the system found errors and wasn’t able to process them successfully. The details of the errors can be dis- played to help a production supervisor understand why they occurred—for example, because of a missing storage location. Note The standard tool for REM postprocessing is Transaction MF47. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing 384 8.7.8 Collective Confirmation The SAP system provides an option for you to collectively enter a large volume of data at once that you don’t need to enter and post individually. However, this option is lim- ited to recording assembly backflush and assembly scrap. As already covered, with assembly backflush, the system records production yield and consumes components according to the BOM. For assembly scrap, it consumes additional components of the assembly with reference to the assembly’s BOM.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To use the collective confirmation functionality, follow menu path Logistics  Produc- tion  Repetitive Manufacturing  Data Entry  Collective Entry or use Transaction MF42N (see Figure 8.37). Figure 8.37 Collective Confirmations For this example, enter the details shown, including assembly Material “2256” and a Backflush qty of “30” PC . Also, though it’s not shown here, on the second line, you can enter the Material “2256” and the Scrap quantity of “1” PC . The system will then create two material documents, one for the assembly backflush and another for the assembly scrap (excess components consumption, without any yield). 8.8 Reversals and Scrap In a normal business scenario, the process operator occasionally faces a situation in which there has been a data entry error or the confirmation details posted in the sys- tem differ from the actual production figures.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In such cases, reversal becomes inevita- ble. In REM, you can perform document-specific reversal or document-neutral reversal. You can also perform a reversal while remaining on the REM confirmation screen (Transaction MFBF) and selecting the Doc-Specific Cancellation icon. When you select © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 385 8.8 Reversals and Scrap this option, the system navigates to Transaction MF41. Alternatively, you can use a sep- arate transaction code (Transaction MF41) to reverse a specific document. (We use this option in this example.) In the following sections, we’ll discuss how to perform reversal of the documents already posted in the system, such as during reporting point backflush. As already stated, there are two types of document reversals. In document-specific reversal , you select a specific document that needs to be reversed.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On the other hand, in document- neutral reversal , you simply correct the total confirmed quantity—for example, for a day. In this case, you just reverse the difference between the previously posted quan- tity and the correct quantity, which reduces the overall posting efforts. Later in this sec- tion, we also cover how to manage REM actual scrap for components, assembly, and activity. 8.8.1 Document-Specific Reversal To proceed with a document-specific reversal of confirmation, you follow menu path Logistics  Production  Repetitive Manufacturing  Data Entry  Reverse or use Transac- tion MF41.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA

Figure 8.38 Document-Specific Cancellation of Confirmation Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: On the initial screen, the system provides the option to enter a document and the posting dates and make further selections, which are specific to the material or pro- duction line. Choose the RP Overview icon to display reporting point information. Once you’ve selected the desired parameters, choose the Save icon (on the initial screen) and the system will reset the reporting point confirmation. 8.9 Costing Activities (Cost Object Controlling) Before you record the actual yield confirmation, components backflush, or activities recording, all of which have financial implications, we recommend that you to coordi- nate with the cost object controlling person to ensure that the necessary and prelimi- nary work on the costing side is taken care of.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing 390  Creating a product cost collector  Creating a material cost estimate  Releasing the material cost estimate  Performing settlement During confirmation in REM, the material costs for the components and the produc- tion activities are automatically posted to the product cost collector during backflush- ing (unless a material cost estimate with price update has been carried out in advance). You must enable the option to post activities in the REM profile before the activities can be posted.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The product cost collector is debited with the material costs, production activities, and overhead. A product cost collector such as an order (a cost controlling object) may have an infinite validity. In the REM profile, a cost controller defines whether the actual data entry of the activities is to be made with reference to the stan- dard material cost estimate or according to preliminary costing for the product cost collector. While creating a product cost collector, you must decide whether there should be several production version−specific cost collectors or one production version− independent cost collector.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: During confirmation, the product cost collector is credited with the valuation price (materials controlled with standard price) or with the moving average price of the assembly (materials controlled with the moving average price). Overheads aren’t determined with reference to an operation—that is, not for each goods movement or activity confirmation. Rather, they are determined periodically during period-end closing in CO using an overhead structure and are posted to the product cost collector. Components that are different from the planned components may be used in produc- tion, or the overhead cost rates may change.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This results in variances in the product cost collector, and a settlement must be carried out. The aim of the settlement is to credit the product cost collector in full. During settlement, the costs not yet credited to the product cost collector are transferred. For a material that is valuated using the stan- dard price, the variant costs are posted to the price difference account. Settlement in REM is always based on the period and on the costs in the product cost collector (product-related cost object controlling). 8.10 Heijunka REM is also often used in production planning in the Japanese automobile industry, and it’s known as heijunka .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Heijunka is used effectively for production smoothing, and it also uses sales and operations planning (S&OP), demand management, MRP, capac- ity requirements planning, and sequencing. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 391 8.10 Heijunka Heijunka allows for even distribution according to the every part every interval (EPEI) principle , which suggests that you have every part on the schedule for every period. That is, a small amount of each part should be produced every shift, every day, every week, or every month, depending on how the scheduling periods are defined. Heijunka then distributes orders evenly over a specific period and sequences them according to the principle of equal distribution. In Japanese, heijunka means leveling .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Leveling can be done by volume or by product. If, for example, a family of products that uses the same production process has demand that varies between 500 and 800 units, then it might seem like a good idea to produce the exact amount that was ordered by the cus- tomer. Distributing the demand in equal, average quantities over a certain period of time provides a much more reliable supply to fulfill fluctuating order quantities. Many value streams produce a mix of products, and therefore, decisions have to be made in terms of product combinations and sequences.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The economic order quantities play an important role and are driven by changeover times and the inventory required. Imple- menting heijunka results in a different situation: it reduces the time and cost of change- overs so that smaller and smaller batches aren’t prohibitive and lost production time and quality costs aren’t significant. The demand for products could be leveled for upstream processes, reducing lead times and total inventories along the entire value stream. As mentioned earlier, in a REM environment, the option of using heijunka is already available.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There is an option in takt-based scheduling to plan according to the heijunka principle of equal distribution. Heijunka—the scheduling of rates according to equal distribution—is just such a mixed model scheduling method. In fact, you’d look at the total demand for the week and then distribute the rates according to the every part every interval principle To do this, first, you must split the demand into lot sizes that allow equal distribution. The MRP run does that automatically by taking the total weekly demand and splitting it into individual planned orders according to the lot-sizing procedure maintained in the MRP 1 view of the material master. (Lot sizing is covered in detail in Chapter 13.) To show how this looks in the SAP S/4HANA system, you create a model mix using Transaction LDD1 (to create) or Transaction LDD2 (to maintain).

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A prerequisite for line balancing is the existence of a line hierarchy with a maximum rate. You create line hierarchies by using Transaction LDB1 and represent the assembly line with all its work centers. Note that the line hierarchy doesn’t represent the flow of the product but rather the hierarchy of the work centers the product flows through (or doesn’t flow through). The line hierarchy can consist of line segments and feeder work centers assigned to a level- by-level hierarchical structure. The line hierarchy can have a scheduling segment (usu- ally the bottleneck work center) that is then used in the production version of the materials being assembled on the line.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the production version, you also assign the routing that is used to assemble the product, which consists of a sequence of opera- tions that follows the assembly line. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 8 Production Planning for Repetitive Manufacturing 392 8.11 Reporting We’ll be covering standard reporting extensively in Chapter 19, Chapter 20, and Chapter 21, including several reports available specifically for REM. In the following sections, we briefly cover two of them:  Document log information  Reporting point statistics 8.11.1 Document Log Information The SAP system maintains a comprehensive log of each and every material document posted or canceled, which is known as the document principle . As a planner, it’s often important for you to have access to the material document information for evaluation purposes, as well as for identifying individual documents against which incorrect or incomplete entries have been made and must now be reversed or canceled.

On the initial parameters selection screen, enter the parameters, such as Plant , Material , Production Version , and Posting Date , and choose Execute or press (F8) . Not only will the system bring up relevant documents for display, but it will also provide the option to reverse any documents if needed. We’ve already covered document-specific reversal in Section 8.8.1 (see Figure 8.43).

This statistical report provides details on the confirmed quantity at each reporting point, as well as the confirmed scrap recorded. You can switch to different views—for example, date-wise evaluation, reporting point−wise evaluation, production version−wise evaluation, or production line−wise evaluation—by choosing the Switch drilldown button and then selecting the desired radio button. You can use these reporting point evaluations as valuable reporting tools to evaluate the WIP.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 8.44 REM Reporting, Reporting Point Statistics 8.12 Summary Companies can implement the REM production type for materials that are produced in bulk quantities with relatively few production steps and low complexity, when com- pared with production types such as discrete manufacturing and process manufactur- ing. Line loading, material staging, backflush assembly, components, and activities can be planned and recorded as frequently as is deemed necessary and practical from the business perspective. All costs associated with REM production of a material continue to accumulate in the product cost collector, and the company can periodically settle these.

docs.text: Due to the highly integrated nature of PP with product cost controlling, you must maintain extensive coordination to ensure that the inventory, financial, and business results are in line with the company’s business processes.
