However, due to human error, such updates often need adjustment. To make © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 449 9.7 Evaluating and Reporting Kanban adjustments, you use Transaction PK21 or follow menu path Logistics  Production Planning  Production  Kanban  Control  Kanban Signal  Manual Entry . 9.6.8 Logical Stock and Physical Stock Setting a kanban to EMPTY doesn’t lead to a goods issue posting. In general, the requested replenishment order is confirmed and kanban materials are backflushed simultaneously (via goods issuance for components). The backflush has no influence on the kanban’s status. Upon consumption of relevant material, the kanban is set to EMPTY .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This action is based only on the physical stock and is completely independent of any stock posting in the system. However, with insufficient control or monitoring, considerable variances can occur between physical stock and logical stock because goods movements aren’t posted simultaneously. In conventional production control, the lot size calculation determines production quantities. With Kanban, fixed container quantities are deter- mined (the lot size is always the same). The procured quantity within a period of time depends on the frequency with which the kanbans are set to EMPTY .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Replenishment frequency is based on actual consumption. The more of a material that is required, the faster the kanbans flow between supply and demand sources. If material consumption decreases, the flow of kanbans slows down. There is never more material in circulation than the quantity defined by the number of kanbans in the control cycle. If a material isn’t required for a certain period of time, all kanbans remain at the demand source. Use the Kanban calculation to adjust the number of kanbans to suit the current requirements situation. 9.7 Evaluating and Reporting Kanban Timely, accurate, and comprehensive information helps a planner make better- informed and overall better business decisions.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this section, we’ll cover a few evalu- ation and analysis reports that are specific to Kanban. It’s important to note that the Kanban board only offers an overview of the kanbans at a certain point in time. The standard analyses in LIS and in SAP Fiori apps provide tools for creating evaluations of kanban circulation for a specified interval. 9.7.1 Control Cycle and Kanban Evaluation To access the control cycle and Kanban evaluation, use Transaction PK18 or follow menu path Logistics  Production Planning  Production  Kanban  Evaluations  Control Cycles/Kanbans .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 9 Kanban 450 Figure 9.54 shows the initial screen of the control cycle and Kanban evaluation. Enter the desired selection parameters so that the system only presents the information rel- evant for evaluation. Enter “1710” for Plant and “KANBAN” for Prodn Supply Area . Choose Execute (not shown) and the screen shown in Figure 9.55 will appear. Figure 9.54 Initial Screen for Control Cycle and Kanban Evaluation Figure 9.55 Control Cycle and Kanban Evaluation © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

The difference between the reports and standard analysis is that in information systems, the information is dynamic and changes when the business user performs relevant business functions.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In standard analysis, the system draws from historical information to enable the business user to make better business decisions. In other words, information from information sys- tems flows into analyses. To access the Kanban analysis, use Transaction MCQ. or follow menu path Logistics  Production Planning  Production  Kanban  Evaluations  Information System . Figure 9.56 shows the initial screen of the Kanban analysis. Enter “1710” for Plant , “KAN- BAN” for Prodn Supply Area , and a date range for Kanban analysis.

As in all standard reports and analyses, you can display or hide the available fields. Double-click a key fig- ure, such as Total Act. Qty , and the screen shown in Figure 9.58 appears. It shows all of the important Kanban key figures associated with plant 1710. From various lead times to quantities to additional information, the Kanban analysis has them all covered.

The evaluation of delayed replenishment should pro- vide not only the necessary visibility but also the option to issue timely alerts. Figure 9.61 Set Kanban Container Status App In addition, you can use the Schedule Kanban Control Cycle Status Change app to schedule regular updates to the statuses of various kanbans without making manual entries. 9.7.5 Kanban Control Cycle Analysis While Chapter 21 is focused on discussing many SAP Fiori apps for production plan- ning, we’ll discuss one app here that is specific to Kanban: the Kanban Control Cycle Analysis app.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Kanban Control Cycle Analysis app evaluates the Kanban control cycles with focus on the status of the circulating kanban containers. It identifies critical situations early and quickly, for example, Kanban control cycles containing errors or having too many open replenishments (visualized by the number of empty kanban containers). You can use it to get insights into the overall Kanban replenishment situation at the aggregated level (for example, at the plant level) and then drill down to the details at the Kanban control cycle level.

docs.text: 455 9.8 Summary Figure 9.62 Kanban Control Cycle Analysis app 9.8 Summary Implementing Kanban isn’t restricted to the production process; it can be imple- mented in procurement, stock transfer, and interplant transfer processes. In this chap- ter, we covered the Kanban configuration that needs to be in place so that configured objects can be assigned to the master data. We discussed the entire production process using Kanban, including the use of the Kanban Board app. We also discussed handling Kanban errors, as well as Kanban evaluation and reporting.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 457 Chapter 10 Batch Management Batch management is an important part of a company’s ability to pro- cure, produce, store, and sell materials. The batch defines a quantity of material by characteristics unique to that batch. Those characteristics determine how the material in that batch is used, sold, or moved. Certain materials can be defined in SAP S/4HANA as being batch managed. A batch is a quantity of material that represents a homogeneous unit with unique specifications. The batch of material may refer to a quantity of a chemical that is produced in one pro- cess or a quantity of bottles of water that were filled on a certain filling line from a spe- cific tank.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There are many ways in which a batch can be defined. In SAP S/4HANA, a batch is used to identify units of material as they move through the system. A batch can also have specific characteristics that enable users to identify and use it within the MM or PP functionality. This chapter describes the processes involved in creating and changing a batch and the process of batch determination. The first section gives an overview of batches and how they’re used in industry. We’ll start out this chapter by covering the configuration settings you need to start using the batch management functionality in the SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: After configu- ration, we cover the requisite master data, followed by the business processes associ- ated with batch management, such as manually creating a batch master and how the system automatically creates the batch master during various business transactions. We’ll then discuss specialized but important batch management topics, such as auto- matic batch determination, active ingredient management, batch derivation, and shelf life expiration of batches. The chapter will conclude with some important batch man- agement reports, including the Batch Information Cockpit. 10.1 Batch Management Overview The definition of a batch differs among companies, industries, and countries.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For exam- ple, in the pharmaceutical industry, strict guidelines and regulations determine what a batch is. These regulations on batches and batch control include the ANSI/ISA-88 stan- dard and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) 21 CFR Part 11 specifications in the United States. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 10 Batch Management 458 Although there is no one exact definition of a batch, the following definition from ExxonMobil Aviation may help: A batch is the specific quantity of a material produced in a single manufacturing process (i.e., under the same conditions, thus featuring identical properties). Each batch of material is given a batch number. Each batch of a material is tested with regard to relevant characteristics to ensure it meets the values or is within the range for those characteristics. A second definition of a batch is from Marathon Oil Company, and it significantly dif- fers from other definitions: “A batch is a shipment of a single product that is handled through the pipeline without mixing with preceding or following shipments.” This third definition of a batch is from the Hawaiian Coffee Association: A batch refers to a quantity of coffee coming to the roaster.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Quantities of the same coffee arriving at different times would be viewed as separate batches. Changes from batch to batch—even of the same variety of bean—must be detected by the roaster if he is to produce coffees that are consistently the same. Whatever the definition, the fact is that the batch has to be identified by a batch record. This can be as simple as identifying bags of coffee beans as they arrive at the plant or as complex as identifying a batch by numerous qualifying characteristics to ensure qual- ity and safety.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A batch of material can either be purchased from a supplier or produced internally. We’ve discussed the need to manage materials by batch; however, in SAP, the material must be identified as batch relevant. The identification of a batch record is especially important for the pharmaceutical industry, due to the regulations set down by the FDA in the United States and other reg- ulatory bodies around the world, such as the Drugs Controller General of India, Bundes- gesundheitsamt in Germany, Health Canada, and the Medicines and Healthcare Prod- ucts Regulatory Agency in the United Kingdom.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These regulatory bodies are primarily interested in public safety. Regulations such as FDA 21 CFR Part 11 in the United States are aimed at improving the efficiency of quality control and the quality assurance process. Each batch produced has to be quality tested, with the results stored electronically against the batch number. The most critical use of batch numbers in the pharmaceutical industry is for product recall. Batch numbers also can be used as tracking devices for companies in case of errors or contamination.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Manufacturers publish product recalls every day, but for the pharmaceutical industry, product recalls can save lives. A pharmaceutical company can voluntarily recall a product. If the company finds that a result from a test on a batch was incorrect, putting the batch out of tolerance, then the product made from that batch could be hazardous. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 459 10.2 Batch Level and Batch Status Management The errors could go all the way back to the supplier, if any of the material was pur- chased. If a supplier informs the company that a batch of purchased material was out of tolerance, then that batch must be traced through the production process to find all finished goods batches that may have used components or ingredients from the faulty batch. In the United States, the FDA has the power to request that a company initiate a recall when it believes that a drug violates the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The FDA will request a recall when it concludes the following:  A drug that has been distributed presents a risk of illness, injury, or gross consumer deception.  The manufacturer or distributor hasn’t recalled the drug.  FDA action is necessary to protect public health. In a recall, the manufacturer informs the retailer, wholesaler, or even consumer about how to identify the batch number on the product and which batch numbers are a part of the recall. Let’s begin with the configuration basics of batch management. 10.2 Batch Level and Batch Status Management In the following sections, we’ll follow a step-by-step approach to the configuration steps required to set up batch management in the SAP system. 10.2.1 Defining the Batch Level A batch can be defined at different levels, but it’s defined at the plant level by default.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: At the beginning of an SAP S/4HANA implementation project, an MM consultant helps the company decide the batch level at which it requires batch monitoring and report- ing. Use the following guidelines to determine that batch numbers are unique at the follow- ing three levels:  Plant and material combination level At this level, the plant and material combination have unique batch numbers. Dif- ferent materials in the same plant can be assigned the same batch number, and the same material in different plants can also be assigned the same batch number.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this context, the material is transferable from one plant to another, and although the batch number is the same, the specification of the destination batch will remain unchanged.  Material number level As batch numbers are created at the material level, the same batch numbers can be Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 10 Batch Management 460 used for other materials as well. After setting the batch level as the material in the system, a material can have the same batch number even though the materials are in different plants with the same specifications. The same batch number can be reas- signed to other materials with different specifications.  Client level The batch level is set at the client level, which is the highest level. The same batch number can’t be used for different materials or different plants. The batch number assigned is unique and can be assigned only once; thus, every material will always have a new or different batch number.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system’s default setting is the plant level. As mentioned earlier, this can be custom- ized to the batch level as needed. However, it’s important to note that while switching to a higher level is always possible, it’s only possible to lower the batch level from the client level to the material level. This is because the batch data is organized so that it has to be converted whenever it’s switched to another batch level. To define the batch level, you follow these steps: 1. Go to SAP IMG  Logistics—General  Batch Management  Specify Batch Level and Activate Status Management .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Choose the batch level as we just discussed (client, plant, or material level) and then save. 2. Choose Batch Status Management to activate batch management status in the cli- ent, check the Active box, and then save. 3. Choose Plants with Batch Status Management and check the Batch Status Manage- ment box in the resulting list for those plants where batch status management has to be active. Check the boxes and save. 4. Choose Initial Status of a New Batch , specify which initial new batches are to be assigned for each material type , and check the Initial Status box for each material type that will be batch managed. 10.2.2 Assigning a Batch Number In this step, you define the batch number range and assignments.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To do so, follow menu path SAP IMG  Logistics—General  Batch Management  Batch Number Assign- ment  Activate Internal Batch Number Assignment . On the resulting screen, select the Active radio button to activate the internal batch number assignment. You can also define whether internal batch number assignment is allowed for goods receipts that have an account assignment via menu path SAP IMG  Logistics—General  Batch Management  Batch Number Assignment  Internal Batch Number Assignment for Assigned Goods Receipt .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the next step, define the number ranges for internal batch number assignment by following menu path SAP IMG  Logistics—General  Batch Management  Batch Num- ber Assignment  Maintain Internal Batch Number Assignment Range . © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 461 10.2 Batch Level and Batch Status Management In the standard SAP S/4HANA system, you can set the number range object BATCH_CLT . Number range 01 from 0000000001 to 9999999999 has already been defined. As with internal batch number assignment, you can assign a number range for external number assignment. Follow menu path SAP IMG  Logistics—General  Batch Manage- ment  Batch Number Assignment  Maintain Number Range for External Batch Number Assignment . Maintain the external number range by clicking the Number Ranges button and then the Change Intervals button.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Here, you can use the already-defined number range or create a new number range by clicking the Inset Interval button. Enter the number ( No. ), From number , and To number , and then choose Save . Note You can use SAP enhancement SAPLNOIZ for internal batch number assignment. This enhancement comprises two function module exits to define number ranges or tem- plates for batch numbers:  EXI_SAPLVO1Z_001 This exit is used to replace the number range object and/or interval proposed with its own number range object. It’s also used to stop the system from assigning an internal number based on the material or plant.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This exit can be used to stop the dialog box from appearing.  EXIT_SAPLVO1Z_002 This exit helps assign its own number or even change the number assigned by the system. 10.2.3 Creating New Batches in the Production Process This configuration step is how the system creates new batches for processes and process orders. To define the new batch creation for processes and process orders, you follow menu path SAP IMG  Logistics—General  Batch Management  Creation of New Batches  Define Batch Creation for Production Order/Process Order or use Transaction CORW.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can make specific settings in batch management for the existing production con- trol profiles. You can also choose the production control profile for making the settings by selecting the required option (see Figure 10.1) for automatic batch creation:  Automatic batch creation at order creation  Automatic batch creation at order release  No automatic batch creation in production/process order Then, you select the batch classification option in the Batch Classification field. In addi- tion, check the Extended Classification box so that more batch-specific functionalities become available.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 10 Batch Management 462 The production scheduling profile ( PS Profile ), which in this example is YB0001 , is then assigned in the Work Scheduling view of a material master. Figure 10.1 Batch Management in Production Process 10.2.4 Creating Batches for Goods Movement You can define the new batch creation settings for movement types. To do so, follow menu path SAP IMG  Logistics—General  Batch Management  Creation of New Batches  Define Batch Creation for Goods Movements . For instance, when batch numbers aren’t determined by the system automatically, the user may want to assign a batch number for goods receipt on a production or a process order (movement type 101) manually.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To achieve this, you choose the Automatic/man- ual without check option for Movement Type 101 , as shown in Figure 10.2. Figure 10.2 Batch Management with Movement Type © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 463 10.3 Master Data in Batch Management For each material type, you can also define whether a new batch can be created via the batch master creation transaction (Transaction MSC1N). To do so, follow menu path SAP IMG  Logistics—General  Batch Management  Creation of New Batches  Define Initial Creation of Data for Batch Master Transactions . If a company only wants the sys- tem to assign the batch numbers automatically and doesn’t want users to have the option to assign them manually, especially for finished products, then you choose Automatic / no manual creation for material type FERT.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This completes our discussion of the basic configuration settings needed for batch management. In the next section, we discuss how to set up master data in batch man- agement. 10.3 Master Data in Batch Management A first step when working with batch management is to identify the material that needs to be batch managed and then update the material master record by setting the batch management requirement. In the following sections, let’s go over the different master data management processes and steps specific to batch management. 10.3.1 Activating Batch Management in the Material Master In the SAP S/4HANA system, batch master records always depend on material master records.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Therefore, the first step is to define batch management requirements in the material master. Go to Transaction MM02 (Change Material Master), enter all the required details, and check the Batch mgmt (batch management) box to denote that the material has to be handled in batches (see Figure 10.3). The following views of the material master contain the checkbox for batch management:  Sales: General/Plant  Plant Data/storage 1  Purchasing  Work s cheduling All views are the same, and any changes and updates in one view appear in all views.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Tips The indicator for the material can be changed from batch-managed to nonbatch- managed only if there has been no stock for the current period and the previous period. This is to allow for transaction posting of batch-managed materials in any previous period. In the SAP S/4HANA system, batches are posted for a material, so the batch master records are always dependent on material master records. If there is a mismatch between subjected material and the batch requirement, then you need to post all stocks from the previous fiscal year, the previous period, and the current period.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 10 Batch Management 464 Similarly, you can cancel the batch requirement for any material that your company doesn’t want to batch manage anymore. If there’s a need to reorganize the batch master records, then you must uncheck the Batch mgmt box, post the required batch requirement, and then post the stock back into the SAP S/4HANA system using Transaction MIGO. Figure 10.3 Activation of Batch Management in Material Master 10.3.2 Batch Classification To differentiate batches of material depending on their individual properties, you use characteristics to define the properties.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, the paint industry uses color, cov- erage, and viscosity as characteristics to classify different batches. The cold-roll coil industry uses finish, thickness, and quality to classify different batches. These characteristics are created in the SAP S/4HANA system and assigned to the mate- rials. The same classification concept as in materials classification is applied in defining batch classification. Say that a company that deals with various types of paints wants to capture the charac- teristics of paint: shine, color, and viscosity.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A class has to be created with the character- istics for coverage, color, and viscosity wavelength, and this class has to be assigned to a material. Also, every time a new batch is created for the material, the characteristic values need to be entered. Let’s briefly define characteristics and assign them to a class specific to batch management. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 465 10.3 Master Data in Batch Management Defining Characteristics First, you create the various characteristics for the materials, such as thickness, viscos- ity, density, and so on. To create characteristics, follow menu path SAP Menu  Cross-Application Components  Classification System  Master Data  Characteristics or use Transaction CT04. In the resulting screen, enter the Characteristic name and choose Create . Then, enter a description, as shown in Figure 10.4. The Status field has In Preparation , Locked , and Released options.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A Released status means that the characteristic can be used; a status of In Preparation or Locked means that it can’t be used. Figure 10.4 Characteristic In the Value assignment area, select either Single-value or Multiple Values . Clicking the Single-value radio button specifies that only one value can be assigned to this character- istic; you use the Multiple Values radio button when more than one value is possible. Next, select the Values tab and enter the possible values for this characteristic, as shown in Figure 10.5.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Checking the Additional Values box allows you to enter character- istic values that aren’t defined. After defining the values, save the characteristic. In this example, we’ve set the Thickness characteristic, and the value of thickness can be within a range of 8.00 to 12.00 mm. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 10 Batch Management 466 Figure 10.5 Characteristic Values Now that you’ve created a characteristic, the next step is to assign existing characteris- tics to the class, which we explain in the following section. Defining a Class and Assigning Characteristics A class represents a group of characteristics. Classes are defined based on the material classification, such as garments, oil and grease, or metals. To define a class, you follow menu path SAP Menu  Cross-Application Components  Classification System  Master Data  Classes or use Transaction CL02.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Enter the Class type as “023” ( Batch ) and fill in the appropriate Class name, which in this example is “ZPP.” Figure 10.6 Assignment of Characteristics to Class © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 467 10.3 Master Data in Batch Management Then, choose New . Enter a description, set the Status to Released , and enter the validity dates. On the Char. tab, assign the characteristics to the class, as shown in Figure 10.6. In this case, we’ve assigned three characteristics: MM02 ( Thickness ), MM10 (Product Class) , and MM11 ( Date of Manufacture ). 10.3.3 Assigning a Classification in the Material Master After you’ve defined a class, the next step is to assign it to the material master via Transaction MM02. Choose the Classification view for Material 2264 and enter Class Type “023” to assign the previously created ZPP class.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Doing so will automatically bring up all three characteristics assigned to the class, as shown in Figure 10.7. Here, you can maintain specific characteristic values pertaining to this material. Because this is a master data step, note that characteristic values assigned are for the material master only and not for batches of a material. Figure 10.7 Classification View of Material Master Now that you’ve created the requisite master data for batch management, the next sec- tion discusses the business processes associated with batch management.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 10 Batch Management 468 10.4 Business Processes of Batch Management In the following sections, we’ll cover the business processes of batch management in the SAP S/4HANA system. Some of these business processes include manually or auto- matically creating a batch, changing or deleting a batch, using the classification func- tion in a batch, and attaching documents to a batch. 10.4.1 Creating a Batch Master Manually A batch master record for a material can be created either manually by a user or auto- matically in the background by the system when goods are received for the first time.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A manually created batch of a material can then be assigned during stock posting, such as during goods receipt of a material from the procurement or production processes. To create batch master records manually, you follow menu path SAP Menu  Logistics  Central Functions  Batch Management  Batch Create or use Transaction MSC1N (see Figure 10.8). Figure 10.8 Manually Creating Batch of Material Enter a material, plant, and storage location to create a batch master record. If an internal number range is defined, then the system will create the batch number automatically © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 469 10.4 Business Processes of Batch Management after you press (Enter) . The data in a material master applies in general to all the batches assigned to this master record. By contrast, a batch master record contains data that uniquely identifies the corresponding batch and characterizes the unit as one that can’t be reproduced. Various types of information are stored in the batch master record. Some can be updated manually, and some can be updated automatically. We’ll discuss some of the relevant information in different tabs in the following sections.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Basic Data 1 Important fields and checkboxes in the Basic Data 1 tab shown in Figure 10.8 are as fol- lows:  Date of Manufacture You can enter the date when the batch was produced into this field. In some indus- tries, this field is also used to enter the date when the material was tested or retested. If a material is found to be still in tolerance after the shelf life date has expired, the material can be retested, and the date of the retest is entered into this field, in addi- tion to a new Shelf Life Exp. Date .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We recommend that you check with clients to determine whether they need to use this field.  SLED/BBD The SLED/BBD (shelf life expiration date/best by date) field is where you enter the date when the shelf life of this batch will expire. The shelf life of a product can vary between plants. This date can be used in the sales process, as customers may have set a requirement for the acceptable number of days of shelf life remaining. Some companies use this field to indicate the date on when a batch needs to be retested.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If the company has implemented the QM functionality, then the system uses this field to see if the material’s batch expiration is about to be reached so that the system can create a quality inspection lot for retesting the material.  Available From This field indicates when the batch will be available. For example, if a material needs to remain in the quality inspection process for a certain number of days after test- ing, then the quality department can enter a date here to inform other departments of when the batch is expected to be available.  Batch Status These radio buttons allow you to classify the batch as having restricted or unre- stricted use.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If you click the Unrestricted radio button, then the batch has no restric- tion placed on its use. If you click the Restricted radio button, the batch will be treated like blocked stock in planning but can be selected by batch determination if the search includes restricted-use batches. You can change the Batch Status to restricted from unrestricted by changing the checkbox in the batch record. A material document will be posted that shows the movement of stock between the two statuses. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 10 Batch Management 470  Next Inspection (not shown) This date field allows the quality department to enter the date of the next quality inspection of the batch, if applicable to this material. This field is helpful when a company must retest a material’s batch after every predefined period. This material retesting process is known as recurring inspection .  Supplier Batch (not shown) If the material is purchased, then you can add the batch number assigned by the sup- plier to the batch record. It’s important to any product recall procedure to note the supplier batch number here.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Supplier Batch field allows you to enter a 15-charac- ter string. Basic Data 2 In this tab, you can maintain the Texts and Freely Definable Date fields. There are six date fields, and maintaining them is optional and only necessary if a user wants to use these dates somewhere in the process. The other fields on the screen are six date fields: Date 1 , Date 2 , and so on. These fields don’t have any standard functionality. The six Date fields can be used for whatever purpose is defined by the client. For example, these fields could contain the dates on which the material was inspected by the quality department.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Classification In this tab, you use the class that was assigned to a material during material master classification, and you maintain the characteristics values here by clicking the New button (not shown). After clicking the New button, you maintain the values of all the characteristics listed based on the material class, as shown in Figure 10.9. Figure 10.9 Classification Tab of Batch Master © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 471 10.4 Business Processes of Batch Management Material Data In this tab, you use the information from the material master record. Choosing the All Changes icon will display the change history of the batch. This tab won’t appear when a batch is created for the first time but will appear in the change or display batch transac- tions (Transaction MSC2N and Transaction MSC3N, respectively). Tips and Tricks If there’s also a business need to link documents to a batch, then you must complete another configuration step.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Follow menu path SAP IMG  Logistics—General  Batch Management  Batch Master  Activate Document Management for Batches or use Transaction ODOC. The configuration in Transaction ODOC consists of simply switching on the field to allow SAP Document Management service for batches. The options are Active and Inactive . 10.4.2 Changing a Batch After you’ve created the batch, there may be occasion to amend the batch record, either to modify a characteristic or to add a new linked document. To change a batch record, follow menu path SAP Menu  Logistics  Materials Management  Material Master  Batch  Change or use Transaction MSC2N.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can make changes to the batch record, but these changes will be recorded and available to review. The Change Batch screen has an extra tab in change mode, and it accesses a screen to view all changes made to the batch record. The Changes screen (refer to Figure 10.8) shows the changes made to the batch record. The information recorded includes the user who created and changed the record, as well as the fields that have been changed, including their values. This information is important to some companies because a strict audit record is needed to show compliance with federal or local regulations.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the pharmaceutical industry, companies manufacturing items that are to be consumed are under strict regulations from the FDA. Companies should at all times ensure that their record keeping is compliant with FDA regulations. 10.4.3 Deleting a Batch There is no transaction used solely for deleting a batch, but a batch can be deleted through Transaction MSC2N. The screen shown back in Figure 10.8 shows the initial screen of the change batch transaction, which has a Batch Deletion Flag box that you can check if the batch is to be deleted.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, checking the deletion flag box doesn’t immediately delete the batch. Checking the box allows the batch to be processed by an archiving program that will determine whether the batch can be deleted. If the batch can’t be deleted, the deletion flag will remain until either the archiving program deter- mines that the batch can be deleted or until the deletion flag is removed. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 10 Batch Management 472 10.4.4 Automatic Creation of a Batch in Goods Movement It’s possible to define the automatic creation of batch numbers in the SAP S/4HANA sys- tem, whether for movement types or production and process orders. For instance, the system can be customized to automatically create unique batch numbers whenever goods are delivered against a process order. This means that every time goods with movement type 101 are received, the unique batch number for the material received is created by the system automatically.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Here, we present an example of how the system automatically creates a batch master upon goods receipt with reference to a process order (movement type 101). To receive goods with reference to a process order and via movement type 101, you go to Transaction MIGO (see Figure 10.10). Select Goods Receipt and R08 Order from the two dropdowns located in the top-left corner of the screen, and then enter process order number “1002203.” In the item details, there’s one more tab: Batch . Notice that the system has automatically created batch 0000000127 .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Choose the Classification button (not shown but located further down the same screen) in the Batch tab in Figure 10.10 to enter the values of the characteristics, as shown in Figure 10.11. Figure 10.10 Goods Receipt of Batch-Managed Material On the screen shown in Figure 10.11, maintain characteristic values such as Thickness , Product Class , and Date of Manufacture . © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 473 10.4 Business Processes of Batch Management Figure 10.11 Classification View of Batch during Goods Receipt 10.4.5 Stock Overview You can use the stock overview report to view how stock is kept under different batches. Use Transaction MMBE, enter the plant code and material number, and execute the report. In the report, you can see the stock overview of a material and the respective batch numbers, such as batch number 127 (which was just received in the previous step). Figure 10.12 shows batch 000000127 of material 2264 with a quantity of 10.0 PC.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When a batch-managed material needs to be issued, if there are multiple batches of the same material in stock, the system automatically lets the user choose the batch num- ber from the material to be issued. If there’s a business need to assign a batch number based on some strategy, you should configure the batch determination strategy. We cover the entire batch determination topic in the next section of this chapter. Batch usage transactions can be used to track batches and for analysis. Transaction MB56 will give the details of a batch where-used list.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP S/4HANA also provides the Batch Information Cockpit, a central tool for tracking batches, which is also discussed in this chapter. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 10 Batch Management 474 Figure 10.12 Stock Overview Let’s discuss batch determination in the following section. 10.5 Batch Determination The batch determination process can be implemented in one or more logistics and sup- ply chain components of SAP S/4HANA, including in PP, QM, MM, SAP S/4HANA Sales, and embedded EWM. Batch determination uses strategy types, search strategies, and search procedures to identify a batch in the relevant area. In a real-world scenario, a warehouse supervisor receives one material in a number of batches, and this will be kept in storage location stock or in warehouse storage bins.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When the material needs to be issued to production, a strategy needs to be in place for the system to choose different batches. Batch determination is the process of defining the strategy in the system by which the system determines and offers the right batch to pick. Batch determination uses the condition technique. Strategy records of the respective application—such as PP, QM, MM, SAP S/4HANA Sales, or WM/embedded extended warehouse management (embedded EWM)—determine batch determina- tion. Different strategy records in the system have to be created for different purposes, such as goods issue to production, goods issue to customer, goods issue to cost center, © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 475 10.5 Batch Determination and so on. Batch determination can be used in production order, process order, goods movement, sales order/delivery, cost center, and transfer order functions. Configurations for each application—such as production, inventory, sales, and stock transfers—are stored in search procedures, which run the batch determination. After the batch determination procedure is set up, the system automatically accesses the corresponding entry of the application, which further refers to the relevant entries in configuration.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 10.13 shows how the system searches for the batch number by using the batch determination procedure. In any transaction, the system will first determine the appli- cation area—which will be PP and PP-PI, MM, WM and embedded EWM, or SAP S/4HANA Sales—and then, it will determine the search procedures, which are assigned based on different combinations ( 1 and 2 ). In the case of PP or PP-PI, the system will determine the order type and plant from the transaction and then find a search proce- dure ( 3 and 4 ). For MM, the system will find a search procedure based on movement type.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For SAP S/4HANA Sales, the search procedure will be based on sales organization, distribution channel, division, and sales document type. The search procedure helps the system determine the search type 5 , and the search type helps to identify the condition types and condition tables 6 . The system will find the appropriate batch number based on the access sequence system. Figure 10.13 Batch Determination Flow in Logistics and Supply Chain Material Issue Mat Price UOM Mat-1 1000 50.00 pcs.

docs.text: 10 Batch Management 476 In the following section, we start out with the necessary configuration steps required to set up automatic batch determination in the production process of PP-PI for process manufacturing (process order). However, the same logic and process steps we cover here can be used to set up automatic batch determination in other applications, such as PP (discrete manufacturing), MM, SAP S/4HANA Sales, and WM and embedded EWM. Then, we cover the necessary master data required for batch determination. Finally, we show how the configuration and the master data setup eventually are reflected in the batch determination business process.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Next, let’s perform the following configuration steps in their logical and sequential order. 10.5.1 Defining Condition Tables The batch determination condition table includes a number of fields that you can select and use to record and assign values. There are five options for condition table creation, depending on which business process your company wants to use batch determination for:  Production order (Transaction OPLB)  Process order (Transaction OPLB)  Inventory management (Transaction OMA1)  SAP S/4HANA Sales (Transaction V/C7)  WM (Transaction OMK4) To define the condition table of a process order, you follow menu path SAP IMG  Logistic—General  Batch Management  Batch Determination and Check  Condition Tables  Define Process Order Condition Tables or use Transaction OPLB.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There are also options to define condition tables separately for each application area— that is, production order, process order, inventory management, SAP S/4HANA Sales, and WM and embedded EWM. For this example, as shown in Figure 10.14, we created a new table (table 550 ) by copying it from standard condition table 030 . Copying a table allows you to use the batch deter- mination procedure specific to the Order Type/Plant/Component combination. Tips and Tricks We recommend that you always copy any new configuration object from an existing one and then make the desired changes to the newly configured object.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Doing so not only saves you time and effort but also reduces the chances that you’ll miss important configuration settings that will then be unable to give the desired results in transac- tion processing. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 477 10.5 Batch Determination Figure 10.14 Condition Table in Batch Determination Figure 10.15 shows newly created condition table 550 , in which the three selected fields are Order Type , Plant , and Material (which is basically the component), as shown on the left-hand side of the figure. You can also choose additional fields from the catalog shown on the right-hand side of the same figure so that they too will be available for selection during the batch determination procedure. For example, if you place your cursor on Valuation Type from the field catalog and choose the Select Field button, then during batch determination, the system will only suggest batches of materials that are available with specific valuation types.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 10 Batch Management 478 Next, click the Generate button, and the system will create the condition table, as shown in Figure 10.16. Here, you can see the log generated on the successful creation of new condition table 550 . Figure 10.16 Log after Condition Table Creation 10.5.2 Defining the Access Sequence For each batch strategy type, there is a batch determination access sequence. This allows the batch strategy type to access the condition tables in the correct sequence. To define an access sequence for PP-PI, you follow menu path SAP IMG  Logistics— General  Batch Management  Batch Determination and Batch Check  Access Sequences  Define Process Order Access Sequences .

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 10.17 shows the access sequence for a process order. First, you select the access sequence and choose Edit . Here, you define the sequence of tables that the system should follow. For example, the system will first search the Order Type/Plant/Material combination, then the Order Type/Plant/Component combination, and so on. Figure 10.17 Access Sequence in Batch Determination In the standard system for process orders, access sequences CO01 and CO02 are defined (just as in the standard SAP S/4HANA system for inventory management) and access sequences ME01 and ME02 are also defined.

docs.bookTitle: Production Planning with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the standard system for SAP S/4HANA Sales, access sequences SD01, SD02, and SD03 are defined. We recommended that you make a copy of the standard access sequences available and then make changes in the condition table sequences to meet any unique business requirements. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 25 Preface A company that’s in the business of manufacturing a product that it sells to its cus- tomer goes through the rigor of using logistics, operations, supply chain management, and product lifecycle management in SAP S/4HANA. The quality management func- tionality (which we’ll refer to as QM throughout the book) in the SAP S/4HANA system plays a critical role in the company’s logistics functions to accomplish just that. QM enables the company to erect quality gates in as many of the business processes as deemed necessary to improve product quality, reduce or eliminate product defects and manufacturing waste, or simply transition toward optimizing its business processes.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: QM seamlessly integrates with the company’s sales, procurement, production, ware- housing, maintenance, projects, human capital, finance, and controlling functions. In fact, it isn’t an understatement to mention that no other area so deeply and exten- sively integrates with other SAP S/4HANA system functionalities as QM does. This inte- gration, depending on the size of the organization, can possibly lead to big data that promises to provide invaluable insight to companies in making informed and timely business decisions, thereby ensuring business continuity and business growth.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: That said, it also demands that the organization’s QM team have an enormous and in- depth understanding of business processes of other SAP S/4HANA system functional- ities so that business processes can work in tandem and in complete synchronization with each other. QM in SAP S/4HANA offers wide-ranging business processes and functions to ensure that your products and their ingredients or subcomponents conform to your quality standards, whether they are regulatory, based on industry standards (e.g., the industry- sector US Food and Drug Administration [FDA], International Organization for Stan- dardization [ISO], Good Manufacturing Practices [GMP], or Federation of the German Motor Industry [VDA]), or based on internal quality standards.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The QM processes within the SAP S/4HANA system support the entire product lifecycle from conception to disposal during all parts of the logistics and supply chain. QM pro- vides a completely integrated quality management solution based on the total quality management approach, an integrative approach for continuously improving product and process quality. Total quality management includes making sure that the interac- tions of the processes are supported by an electronic data processing system. So, the QM activities that are within the scope of this book are the processes and activities put in place to ensure that the quality of end products, ingredients, and subcomponents used to produce the end product conform to quality standards.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Preface 26 Goals of This Book The first goal of this book is to provide you with a step-by-step approach to configure and implement individual business processes that integrate with QM. Each chapter lays the initial foundations in the form of configuration, and then the rest of each chap- ter shows how the configuration eventually impacts the business processes. This approach (configuration first, followed by business processes) is maintained in most parts of the book. Where it’s relevant or makes more sense to first cover business pro- cesses to help you develop a good understanding of concepts, the relevant configura- tion steps are covered at the end of the chapter instead.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In short, here’s the general approach to any topic that you’ll find in most parts of this book:  Configuration  Master data  Business processes  Reports, analyses, or optimization tools and pointers The next goal is to provide comprehensive coverage of the many features and function- alities that QM offers. However, we encourage you to evaluate each and every feature, option, and functionality to determine whether implementing it will bring clarity or improvements to your business process. You’ll need to maintain a fine balance between implementing and integrating QM in business processes to bring greater control, visi- bility, and improvement to business processes with the time, efforts, and resources involved.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Further, there are significant “hidden” or lesser-used functionalities in QM that you can integrate even when (and long after) your SAP S/4HANA system imple- mentation is complete. These tools are covered to bring greater optimization to your business processes and greater return on your investment in the SAP S/4HANA system. The SAP S/4HANA system provides a wide range of tools for quality control, which we’ll cover throughout the book.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These are as follows:  Usage decision (Chapter 3)  Dynamic modification of inspection frequency and severity (Chapter 3)  Quality notification including problem-solving processes (Chapter 12)  Quality management reporting, including SAP Fiori apps (Chapter 18)  Failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) and control plans (Chapter 16)  Audit management (Chapter 14)  Supplier evaluation (Chapter 19)  Quality level (Chapter 19)  Statistical process control (Chapter 19)  Document Management System (DMS) (Chapter 20) © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 27 Target Audience Due to the extensive nature of the details involved in maintaining and improving qual- ity controls, we’ll cover them separately in various chapters of this book. The book offers several real-life examples and other modeling hints and tips to help you decide which option best meets your company’s business needs. Extensive use of screen- shots is supported by in-depth coverage of concepts and terminologies. The SAP S/4HANA 2023 release is used in the screenshots. The menu paths or transaction codes for perform- ing each step are given.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Where specific or unique data is used, all necessary prerequisites and hints are given to enable you to set up the data or meet the prerequisite before attempting to run a business process. While this book can only cover so much of a topic, we highly encourage you to explore and try out a large number of options, icons, menu paths, and other pointers available to continue the process of self-learning and eventually become a subject matter expert in the QM area of SAP S/4HANA. In this book, we’ll also cover several cross-area functionalities that enable you to lever- age their strengths not only in QM but also in other logistics functions that are imple- mented in your company.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, you can use the classification system, digital signature, Early Warning System (EWS), SAP Fiori apps, standard analyses, Document Management System (DMS), engineering change management, information systems, and reporting in many other logistics areas. In other words, this book goes beyond the QM area to help optimize business processes in other logistics areas. Because QM is often synonymous with batch-managed materials of the process indus- try, we’ve made a deliberate attempt to cover these areas as much as possible.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This approach has helped provide greater coverage of specific topics that depend on materi- als being batch-managed. However, companies using discrete or repetitive manufactur- ing types will find that their business processes (with or without batch management) are covered in significant detail. Target Audience This book is intended for all readers who use QM in the SAP S/4HANA system. They may be the team leader, project team members in an SAP S/4HANA system implemen- tation, integration managers, quality planners, or quality control and quality assurance personnel working in operational positions in the company.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 35 Chapter 1 Quality Management in SAP S/4HANA The quality management functionality in SAP S/4HANA enables a com- pany to improve the quality of its products by continuously assessing them at any given step of the logistics and supply chain. By doing so, the company can ensure that its products conform to relevant product reg- ulations, industry standards, and/or company quality standards. Companies that want to maintain, retain, and continuously improve the quality of their products find quality management (QM) in SAP S/4HANA to be their trusted and steadfast companion in the logistics and supply chain management functions.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: From prequalifying potential suppliers for supplying raw and packing materials, conducting preliminary inspections before goods reach the company premises, and conducting quality tests when suppliers deliver the materials to ensuring quality inspection during and after production finds, QM integrates into all-important business processes. QM also ensures that companies can conduct another, customer-specific round of quality checks and, before dispatching goods to customers, extensively evaluate defects in their own returned products, with the aim of eliminating those defects.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: QM covers it all: new products developed with a stability study, continuous product and process improvements with failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), and internal and external audits using audit management. Quality control ensures that companies fre- quently evaluate suppliers to maintain business relationships with them, as well as monitor critical statistical process control for products that are produced in house. The optimization in QM allows added functionality such as digital signatures that eliminate manual approval processes, manage incoming and outgoing quality certificates, and integrate Document Management System (DMS) into important business functions.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: QM integrates completely with several key logistics and supply chain areas, including procurement, production, and sales. It can check the quality compliance of raw materials when they’re first delivered by suppliers and later during production and postproduc- tion. The QM area can also check for compliance with customers’ quality specifications before the finished goods are shipped out. QM is a wide-ranging solution that supports the company throughout the product life- cycle and along the supply chain. In particular, the QM solution offers the following benefits:  Provides a single quality management solution for all company processes, giving you a single source of truth and access to the most current quality information at any time Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: First, however, we’ll give you a good starting point: SAP’s organizational structures, which you need to understand to know how various areas of SAP work together. 1.1 Organizational Structure in SAP S/4HANA At the start of an SAP S/4HANA implementation project, one of the first and most intensive activities undertaken is the finalization of the organizational structure. This involves having intermodular and intramodular discussions and deliberations to © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 37 1.1 Organizational Structure in SAP S/4HANA ensure that the SAP S/4HANA system can both cover the legal aspects of the company’s organizational structure and attend to area-specific reporting needs. In other words, the business process owners, business analysts, and SAP consultants review the exist- ing organizational structure of the company and then simultaneously begin mapping it in the SAP S/4HANA system. A practical approach to adopt while finalizing the organizational structure in SAP S/4HANA is to ensure that the organizational structure isn’t so generic that it loses its signifi- cance and prevents the business process owner from extracting the required informa- tion from the system, nor is it so minute or detailed that it becomes cumbersome to collate and consolidate the information.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You should also keep a forward-thinking view of your organizational structure. If you foresee that you’ll need certain organizational elements in your SAP S/4HANA system in the future, for example, it’s better to have them available in the system than to add them at a later point. Although QM itself doesn’t have any of its own organizational structure to configure from an implementation perspective, you need to understand the important organiza- tional units: client, company code, plant, storage location, and warehouse number.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this chapter, we’ll review the structure as it applies to QM. If QM integrates with the procurement processes, it requires an understanding of the purchasing organization and purchasing group. Similarly, if QM integrates with SAP S/4HANA Sales business processes, then you need to have a decent understanding of the sales organization, dis- tribution channel, and division, which together form the sales area. If the company has also implemented and is using embedded extended warehouse management (EWM) in SAP S/4HANA, then a decent understanding of the EWM structure is helpful for a QM consultant and business user.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll also discuss the importance of the organizational units and explain how they work together to accomplish the organizational, legal, and reporting requirements of the company. The organizational structure in the SAP S/4HANA system is equally applicable to all important business functions that we cover in the entire book. Figure 1.1 shows the cli- ent as the highest level of the organizational structure in the SAP S/4HANA system. The profitability analysis of the company is performed at the controlling area level, and the cost center and profit center accountings are performed at that level as well.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A company can consist of several legal entities, each including separate, individual financial statements that must be prepared at the end of the financial year. This is reflected as a separate company code for each legal entity. The valuation area represents the level at which the company values its material stock consistently. It’s part of the logistics area of the SAP S/4HANA system. A one-to-one relationship exists between the valuation area and the plant. For example, a material at one plant may have a different standard price than at another plant, where its price control may be a moving average.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 39 1.1 Organizational Structure in SAP S/4HANA 1.1.1 Client A client represents the highest element of the SAP S/4HANA system’s organizational structure. Often, the client represents a company or group of companies, within which there are several independent company units. An SAP S/4HANA system can contain several clients in logical units. The additional organizational elements and the master and transaction data are created and managed within a client. From the SAP S/4HANA system’s landscape perspective, you normally have at least three clients (systems): DEV (development), QAS (quality assurance system), and PRD (production).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The actual configuration of the SAP S/4HANA system takes place in the DEV system and is then transported to the QAS system for testing and training. The final configuration eventually moves to PRD, which is the final live system in which the business process owners of the company make real-time, live entries. 1.1.2 Company Code The company code is the level below the client in the SAP S/4HANA system, and it reflects the level at which the company legally reports income statements and balance sheets. It’s an organizational element (unit) of the financial accounting area.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can have a separate company code for each line of business—for example, textiles and chemicals—so long as the two are legally separate entities. Similarly, separate company codes can exist if the company has operations in foreign countries. 1.1.3 Plant A plant is an organizational unit in the logistics area. You can classify a plant from the point of view of production, procurement, maintenance, warehouse, and planning. The plant can be, for example, a manufacturing site, a head office, or a distribution center within a company.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It organizes the tasks for logistics, and it can be a physical produc- tion site or the logical grouping of several sites in which materials are produced or goods and services are provided. 1.1.4 Storage Location A storage location is a physical or virtual storage site for materials. Examples of physi- cal storage locations include raw material store, components store, returned goods store, finished goods store, and so on, whereas a virtual storage location can be self- defined and may be a scrapyard, a production shop floor in which semifinished goods are temporarily stored, and so on.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 1 Quality Management in SAP S/4HANA 40 1.1.5 Warehouse Number A warehouse complex is represented in the SAP S/4HANA system as a warehouse num- ber, and all the warehouse processes, such as picking and putaway, are executed using this warehouse number. The warehouse number doesn’t have an address but has a short descriptive text. This is unlike a storage location, which holds an address. Within the SAP S/4HANA system, assignment of a warehouse number to a plant and storage location combination identifies which storage location is controlled by the warehouse management system (WMS). 1.2 Quality Management in the SAP Landscape QM offers a wide range of functions and business processes that fully integrate with SAP Product Lifecycle Management (SAP PLM) and focuses on ensuring and managing the quality of products and assets.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Accordingly, QM is an integral part of the SAP PLM solution map under the main process product development and collaboration (see Table 1.1). It includes the prevention of quality-related problems and offers continuous process improvement abilities through collaboration and sustained quality control. So, in the broader sense, QM focuses on the entirety of all QM-relevant processes for a product (quality planning, quality certificate, quality notification, quality control, test equipment management, and stability study).
