docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 76 2.6 Inspection Method An inspection method offers the provision to maintain detailed instructions for con- ducting physical or chemical quality tests of a material. The quality inspector can refer to the relevant inspection method for information or instruction while conducting an actual test. An inspection method can have several versions, which you can use to dif- ferentiate among various validity periods. To create an inspection method, use Transaction QS31 or follow menu path SAP  Logis- tics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Inspection Method  Create .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On the initial screen that appears, enter Insp. Method (inspection method) “QMINSP10” and Plant “1710”. You don’t need to enter the inspection method number or a date because the system automatically assigns an internal number to the inspection method and proposes a current date for the creation of the inspection method. Notice that it’s also possible to create a new inspection method by referencing an existing one. To create a new inspection method with reference to an already created inspection method, enter the details of reference fields such as plant, inspection method, key date, and version, and the system automatically copies all the information from the refer- ence inspection method to the new one.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can then change or update the new inspection method accordingly, saving data entry efforts. Tips and Tricks The option to create QM master data using templates or the copy function is generally available, and you can use it to quickly maintain master data, saving time and effort, as well as reducing data entry errors. In Figure 2.7, set the Status to 2 Released ; this makes the inspection method available during subsequent QM activities in which you use the inspection method. If the status of the inspection method is set to Being Created , it isn’t available in further QM activities.

docs.text: You can enter a short text, and a good search term always helps in finding the relevant information when you’re searching in the system. An entry in the Authorization Group field controls authorization to create or make changes, or even display an inspection method. You may want to allow very few people access to make changes to an inspec- tion method because it’s critical, sensitive information. Inspector Qualific. (inspector qualification) is the minimum credential or experience a person must have to perform the tasks listed in an inspection method—for example, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) certified quality inspector or total quality management (TQM) accredited expert.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 81 2.9 Master Inspection Characteristics  Qualitative  Quantitative A quantitative characteristic defines a physical or chemical property of a material as a numerical value (e.g., 2.3 kg, 1.8 lbs., or 11 ft.). Qualitative characteristic s are attributes of a material or property having to do with nonnumerical qualities (e.g., smooth, pitted, and rusted for a surface, or red, tan, and brown for paint/color). You use master inspection characteristics when creating task lists as copy templates, or you reference (include) them in the inspection plan.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The individual objects and control functions are the same as those of the characteristic in the inspection plan. From the organizational point of view, the master inspection characteristics, like the inspection plans, are assigned to the plant. docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 90 Figure 2.14 Inspection Catalog You can assign defect codes to the characteristics. In many cases, performing valuation of a qualitative characteristic with OK/NOK or a quantitative characteristic with a mea- surement value is too general. For a more precise defect description in the case of a rejection, you can make a special catalog with catalog type 9 , Defect Types , available to the characteristic. This catalog is then automatically highlighted with a Rejected valua- tion in the results recording, and the system prompts you to enter a defect code.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Another important characteristic of this function is the automatic generation—during the results recording—of a defect record in the form of a quality notification. To acti- vate this functionality, select the Results Recording checkbox in the control indicators of the characteristic. You can then continue to fully edit the messages with the message type Q2 , Internal Quality Notifications . 2.10 Sampling Procedure A sampling procedure enables the system to calculate the sample size of the inspection lot for quality inspection and then inspect and record its results.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 91 2.10 Sampling Procedure Example A supplier delivers 100 kg of PET chips (a raw material used in making plastic bottles) against a purchase order. The system should be able to calculate a sample size of 5 kg because the sampling procedure stipulates inspecting 5% of the delivered goods as the sample size for inspection. To create a sampling procedure, use Transaction QDV1 or follow menu path SAP  Logis- tics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Inspection Planning  Basic Data  Sample  Sampling Procedure  Create .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On the initial screen that appears, enter sampling proce- dure “FIX10” to denote the relevancy and the settings made. Press (Enter) , and the screen shown in Figure 2.15 appears. From the Sampling Type dropdown, you can choose one of the four available sampling types:  100 Fixed sample Regardless of the quantity delivered by the supplier or produced in house, the sys- tem always calculates a fixed sample quantity for inspection. For example, for a pro- duced/procured quantity of either 100 kg or 1,000 kg, the system calculates the fixed sample size of 3, if the sample size is 3.  200 100% Inspection Regardless of the quantity delivered by the supplier or produced in house, the com- plete quantity is available for inspection.  300 Using sampling scheme A sampling scheme uses an incremental method of calculating sample size.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The big- ger the produced/procured material is, the smaller the overall sample size available for inspection can be. For example, for a procured quantity of up to 100 kg, the sam- ple size is 5 kg, whereas for a procured quantity between 101 kg and 1,000 kg, the sample size is 8 kg. It’s impractical to inspect a large sample quantity if the overall delivered quantity is too big.  400 Sample percentage A percentage of the total produced/procured quantity is available as a sample size for quality inspection. For example, for a procured or produced quantity of 200 kg of material, the sample size is 4 kg because the sample percentage is defined as 2%.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Whenever the system creates an inspection lot for produced or procured material, it automatically and immediately calculates the sample size. The purpose of a sampling procedure is to be able to calculate the sample size for quality inspection from the total inspection lot quantity. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 92 Figure 2.15 Sampling Procedure Next, choose Valuation Mode: Attributive inspection nonconf. units . The valuation mode defines how the system decides to accept or reject an inspection characteristic (valuation mode). Some of the manual or automatic decision options available are as follows:  A manual decision is required for attributive characteristics (i.e., characteristics for which no values are recorded). These are characteristics you simply accept or reject. This type of decision is also used in all other cases in which an automatic valuation isn’t possible or allowed.  Code valuation forms the basis of qualitative attributes.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The decisions are stored in the catalog for characteristic attributes.  A decision can be based on a sampling plan for attributive inspection with the options of considering the number of defects, number of nonconforming units, or deviation from tolerance limits for quantitative characteristics.  A decision can be based on a sampling plan for quantitative characteristics (variable inspection) with the options to comply with the distribution limits of the character- istic values (s-method) or the mean value limits of characteristic values (checking the tolerance specifications).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 93 2.11 Inspection Plan Because you’re not going to use this sampling procedure for statistical process control, you don’t have to choose or enter anything in Control Chart Type . The Independent Multiple Samples option should be used only if you want to record multiple results for a characteristic of a part or results from multiple samples for a char- acteristic. An example of an independent multiple sample is the repeated measuring of the diameter at different points of a wave. Note that the inspection results should be attributed to only one unit of inspection in this case.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system can then calculate an arithmetical mean value of the measurements in a subsequent calculated characteristic. Choose Sample in the menu bar of Figure 2.15 to define the percentage of the sample for calculation. Enter a Sample Size of “10” in the popup. You can enter up to three decimal places to define the sample size as a percentage. Enter an Acceptance Number of “2” to denote that that the system still valuates the characteristic as acceptable if up to 2 out of 10 units are rejected. Note When you’re incorporating sampling procedures in the inspection plan, the system dis- plays only the allowed sampling procedure selection screen for the characteristic.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the worst case, no selection options are available. The rules that you previously created for the sampling procedure then need to be rechecked. It can happen, for example, that you’ve selected Scope Not Fixed in the control indicators and are trying to assign a sampling procedure for a control chart. In this case, the sampling procedure doesn’t appear in the selection because the sample size for a control chart has to be fixed. Therefore, you should set a fixed scope in the master inspection characteristic before assigning it to the inspection plan. 2.11 Inspection Plan You use the inspection plan’s task list type in QM to process procurement-, production-, or sales-related quality inspections.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Its typical application areas are model inspections, goods receipt inspections, goods issue inspections, and goods receipts from produc- tion. Its main functions are the same as those of the routing. Besides assigning to the material, you can also assign the following to the inspection plan:  Material and business partner (supplier)  Material and business partner (customer) The inspection plan can include the reference operation set in their operations and thus use a modular system of operations and inspection characteristics.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the SAP S/4HANA system, the inspection plan is the production-based task list type that’s available in PP and PP-PI. From a QM perspective, this has the advantage that the inspection plan is structured in exactly the same way as the routing and thus already Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 94 has useful and tried-and-tested planning instruments at its disposal. The basic structure consists of operations (work operations, inspection operations) and is the same in all task list types, including the inspection plan. In addition, every task-list type also has its own features that reflect its specific usage. The inspection plan is completely integrated into the supply chain of the SAP S/4HANA system and provides extended functions for task planning that cover capacity and costs. Therefore, having a good understanding of this topic is a prerequisite for ensuring that you effectively manage this important QM master data.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To gain a better understanding of inspection plan management, let’s now look at the structure of the inspection plan and its individual components:  Task list header  Material assignment  Test equipment (PRT assignment)  Operations  Inspection characteristics  Dependent characteristics Figure 2.16 shows how various QM master data fits into an inspection plan. Figure 2.16 Inspection Plan In the following sections, we’ll explain the entire structure of the inspection plan you just saw in Figure 2.16 and how various QM master data elements connect with each other in an inspection plan.

docs.text: 95 2.11 Inspection Plan Tips and Tricks As part of your inspection planning, set up integration meetings with the procurement, production planning, and sales project groups early in the planning phase. In these meetings, introduce the participants to the whole area of inspection planning, and explain how it’s integrated with the various other technical departments. You should also use this opportunity to explain the organizational aspects and areas of responsi- bility that will be important when the team is working together on the inspection plan and routing. 2.11.1 Task List Header To create an inspection plan, use Transaction QP01 or follow menu path SAP  Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Inspection Planning  Inspection Plan  Create .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 2.17 shows the initial screen where you enter Material “RM17” and Plant “1710”. The Key Date holds significance as the system looks for this date during inspection lot creation and the assignment of an inspection plan. In Chapter 3, you’ll see that the sys- tem is unable to assign an inspection plan to an inspection lot because it can’t find the relevant inspection plan on the key date. If you don’t enter the key date , the system automatically assigns the current date at the time of creating the inspection plan.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 96 You can also use the Copy Model button at the top of the screen to create new inspec- tion plans. The system then takes you through the individual task list selection steps by means of a special dialog box. The contents of the selected task list template are then copied to your new task list. Note one exception at this point: the copy function doesn’t work if the template already contains references to the set reference operation. 2.11.2 Inspection Plan Header Choose Header so that the screen in Figure 2.18 appears, showing the corresponding view of the inspection plan.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The number of the task list group is usually set by an internal numbering system (i.e., the system assigns a number itself). If you want to use an external numbering system, set the number range interval in configuration accordingly. Notice that the system assigns Group Counter 1 to the inspection plan. You can have up to 99 group counters for a task list group. Figure 2.18 Inspection Plan: Header Details Enter Usage “5” ( Goods Receipt ). A usage denotes the activity that uses the inspection plan. An inspection plan for a material can have different usages, such as goods issue for a customer, goods receipt for a production order or a purchase order, or material check.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Because QM also integrates with PM, there’s a specific usage for this purpose. You can have multiple inspection plans for a material with different usages. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 97 2.11 Inspection Plan Enter Overall Status “4” ( Released (General) ). This makes the inspection plan available during subsequent QM activities, in which you use the inspection plan. If the status of the inspection plan is set to Being Created , it isn't available for assignment to the inspection lot. You can also use the status to lock a task list that hasn’t been released or is obsolete. Don’t confuse the planner group with the task list group. The planner group is an independent ordering criterion. You can use the planner group when selecting task lists for selection.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The unit of the material procured or produced is used in the whole task list. It has to be converted to the base unit of measure of the material to be produced, as specified in the material master record. If the conversion isn’t maintained, the system outputs an error message during the task list inspection. After the unit of measure is set in the first task list, the unit of measure for the whole task list is set and can’t be changed. In Lot Size From and Lot Size To , you can specify the allowed lot sizes for this task list group counter.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The inspection point is a sample taken during production for the purpose of statistical process regulation or, simply put, to record continuous inspection data. You can there- fore use inspection points in not only the routing or master recipe but also in the inspection plan. The dynamic modification of the inspection points is carried out on the basis of the sampling procedure, which was assigned on the characteristic level.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: After you set the Inspection Points indicator (not shown but located further down the same screen), the Field Combination and Partial-Lot (PL) assignment fields appear, as follows:  Field Combination This user field is available to specify the quantities assigned to the inspection points if you’ve defined the inspection points as a quantity, for example, “container,” “drum,” or “pallet.” If this task list is used to carry out an inspection, the selected field combination is displayed on the entry screen of the results recording function.  Partial-Lot (PL) You indicate here whether the material quantities that are assigned to the inspec- tion points also apply to partial lots.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Depending on the requirements of the produc- tion process, you can do one of the following: – Assign only inspection points to the produced quantities (no partial lots). – Assign partial lots to the quantities for which one or more inspection points have been produced. – Assign one or more partial lots to batches (provided that the material is batch- managed). The Dynamic Modif. Level is used to specify the level in the task list on which the dynamic modification rule (Chapter 3) is defined (e.g., the header level or the character- istic level of the inspection plan).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 98 The Inspection Procedure (not shown but located further down the same screen) con- trols how the system calculates primary, pooled, or reserved samples using sample management (see Chapter 10). Choose the Material Assignment button in the menu bar of Figure 2.18 to go to the screen in Figure 2.19. 2.11.3 Material Assignment Material assignment functionality in the inspection plan enables you to significantly reduce your master data maintenance efforts. This is achieved by assigning multiple materials, suppliers, or customers with the same inspection requirements into one task list group (inspection plan) as long as they have the same set of operations and master inspection characteristics of the materials.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Example Your company produces and packs a product (e.g., tomato ketchup) in different sizes. For each product’s size, there’s a separate material master code available in the system. Instead of creating one inspection plan for each size of the product, you can create one inspection plan and assign multiple material codes to it via the material assignment functionality. Because inspection plans are also used for supplier-procured materials or finished goods sold to customers, you can introduce further visibility and controls by using inspection plans that are specific to suppliers or customers.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 2.19 shows that the system automatically group assign a Group number (the inspection plan number), with Group Counter 1 , to Supplier 9980000067 when the inspection plan is saved. If you have to assign multiple materials for the same or differ- ent plants, then you can enter them all here, and the system continues to increase the group counter number. Figure 2.19 Material Assignment Later, you’ll see how you can further increase visibility into inspection control by using the dependent characteristic functionality that applies to a specific customer or sup- plier. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 99 2.11 Inspection Plan Tips and Tricks In Figure 2.19, the Supplier and Customer fields are generally not immediately visible until you continue scrolling to the far right side of the screen. Further, though suppliers and customers are referred to as business partners in SAP S/4HANA, you’ll still fre- quently come across the terms suppliers and customers in various SAP transactions and business processes. 2.11.4 Test Equipment You create the link to the test equipment in the operations overview by clicking the More dropdown option for PRTs.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can create several inspection resources and other resources for each operation by using the following categories:  Material  Equipment  Document  PRTs After you create the first item, you can also insert the operation test equipment for each operation into an overview list and process it there. Because assignments for test equipment on the operation level are often too imprecise, the system allows you to continue using the individual PRT items on the characteristics level and link them with the characteristic in an organized way.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, the system assumes that the test equipment in question was previously assigned to the operation and that the relevant control indicator is set in the characteristic. Choose Operations in the screen in Figure 2.18 to see the screen shown in Figure 2.20. Figure 2.20 Inspection Plan: Operation Overview 2.11.5 Operations View Figure 2.20 shows the Operation Overview screen, where you can maintain all the important information for the business user to perform quality inspection activities. This information maintenance includes the work center, as well as the master inspec- tion characteristics.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 100 The Operations screen with the overview list contains the central control elements of the inspection plan. The information that’s important for task planning, such as calcu- lation and scheduling data, is assigned to the operation. In the case of the routing or master recipe, you assign the inspection characteristics to the operations (production operation), just as in the inspection plan. If you’re using the inspection plan task list type, the operations divide the inspection plan into individual inspection steps.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The other assignments relate to the master data for the PRTs and work centers. When you’re planning operations, do this first in the overview list. You can then double-click to see the detailed screen for the operation. Enter the previously created Work Center “QCLAB” and a short description of the oper- ation to help the business user identify the step for conducting the quality inspection of a raw material. Because you already maintained control key QM04 while creating the QM work center, the system automatically incorporates it here.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Choose Operation 0010 , and then choose More  Inspection Characteristics to add master inspection characteristics to the inspection plan of the material. This leads to Figure 2.21, in which you enter master inspection characteristic QMHT10 . This is the same master inspection characteristic that you previously created. This means the material number RM17 will undergo the quality inspection of master inspection char- acteristic QMHT10 (herbal tea - aroma) during quality inspection and when the com- pany receives the goods from the supplier.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Choose line item 10 , and then click the Quantitative Data button to maintain or change the upper, lower, and target values of the master inspection characteristic. Although the master inspection characteris- tic may have previously maintained lower and upper limits, the business user can change the same in the inspection plan to suit the individual material’s specifica- tions. In other words, you can overwrite the original values of the master inspection characteristic if needed. Figure 2.21 Inspection Plan: Characteristic Overview © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 101 2.11 Inspection Plan 2.11.6 Long-Term Characteristics Figure 2.22 shows the qualitative characteristic with the Long-Term Inspection check- box selected (not shown) in the qualitative master inspection characteristic. Here, you need to assign the Catalog Type 1 ( Attribute ) with the code/group selected set ( CGr/ SSet ) assigned. A long-term characteristic enables the quality inspector to record the results of a characteristic even after the usage decision of the inspection lot is made. Figure 2.22 Catalog Assignment to Master Inspection Characteristic 2.11.7 Calculated Characteristics Figure 2.23 shows Characteristic 30 , which is a calculated characteristic.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A calculated characteristic uses data from other characteristics, as well as calculation formulas, to perform calculations and come up with the calculated value of the characteristic. Because this is a calculated characteristic (the relevant indicator that you set in the master inspection characteristic), the system automatically selects the Calculate For- mula checkbox. For this example, in the Formula field, enter “(C010)*1.15”, where C0 (zero) is the formula parameter for the arithmetic mean value of characteristic 10 (refer to Figure 2.21 and look for the Char. column).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To summarize, the system first looks for the arithmetic mean value of characteristic 10 and then multiplies it by 1.15 to come up with the calculated value for characteristic 30. If you place the curser on the Formula field in Figure 2.23 and choose the dropdown, the system brings up the formula parameters list that you see in Figure 2.24. Here, you find a list of available standard formula parameters that you can use to calculate a charac- teristic. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 103 2.11 Inspection Plan 2.11.8 Classed Characteristics Figure 2.25 contains settings for classed characteristics. A classed characteristic enables you to enter the inspection results of samples that fall within a class or a range of acceptable (or unacceptable) values. You can manually enter all the information, such as lower and upper limits and the tar- get value, as well as maintain the information in the Class Definition area. Alternately, you can enter the target value, enter the upper and lower limits of a classed character- istic, enter the number of classes, and enter “*” (an asterisk) in the Class width and Class midpoint fields, and then the system automatically calculates these two values.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: By entering the number of classes, you’re telling the system to divide up and create the same number of classes or ranges that fall within the upper and lower limits of the characteristic value. Figure 2.25 Class Characteristic Figure 2.26 shows a system-suggested Class width with of 7 and Class midpoint of 105 . Figure 2.26 Class Definition Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 104 2.11.9 Dependent Characteristics Let’s now look at the prerequisites of leading and dependent characteristics:  Dynamic modification control indicator on the characteristic level  Mandatory characteristic control indicator Using this combination in an operation for your characteristics can cause inconsisten- cies in the inspection process. This means that the calculated characteristic can’t work with different dynamic modification levels for the characteristic if the calculation input characteristics are in a skip level (inspection is skipped).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can quickly set up leading and dependent characteristics. First, enter a dynamic modification rule for the leading characteristic in the dynamic modification screen. Next, in the screen for the dependent characteristics, set a reference to the characteris- tic number. Note that each operation may contain only one leading characteristic. As soon as you use a data record for an inspection plan or an inspection characteristic, the system sets a usage indicator. This indicator is used, among other purposes, to rep- resent the relationships in the form of a report and thus to clarify them.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Let’s review the steps involved in setting up dependent characteristic values for a spe- cific supplier. Refer to the screen in Figure 2.27, which appears after you first choose Char “50” (the leading characteristic 50), and then choose Dependent Characteristic Specifications (refer to Figure 2.21). Initially, the screen appears blank or with no values. Choose Insert assignment as shown in Figure 2.27, and then enter Material “RM17” so that the screen in Figure 2.28 appears. Materials available for assignment here must be previously assigned, as shown earlier in Figure 2.19.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 2.27 Assignment of Supplier in Dependent Characteristic The screen in Figure 2.28 enables you to choose the material for a dependent characteris- tic’s specifications, including upper and lower limits. Notice the Supplier 9980000067 , © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 105 2.11 Inspection Plan and set the upper, lower, and target values of characteristic 50 and dependent character- istic 10. With these settings, wherever supplier 9980000067 delivers material RM17, the system incorporates supplier-specific characteristic settings in the inspection lot for the quality inspector to inspect and confirm the results. These supplier-specific specification limits differ from the normal specification for the leading characteristic. Figure 2.28 Dependent Characteristic Figure 2.29 shows the inspection characteristic overview for operation 0010, consisting of different master inspection characteristics.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Short Text Charc of characteristics are deliberately written this way so that you know the master inspection characteris- tic’s control settings that were already made, such as a characteristic having the long- term characteristic checkbox selected or a characteristic that’s a classed characteristic or a calculated characteristic. Figure 2.29 Overview of Master Inspection Characteristics in the Inspection Plan Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 106 Here, you also incorporate the previously created inspection method, as well as the sampling procedure for the relevant characteristics. Notice that characteristic 20 also requires you to record defects if the inspection results of the master inspection charac- teristic valuation is rejected. Further, for characteristic 50, you can simply maintain its short text and all other details in case the master inspection characteristic doesn’t already exist and you need to make it part of an inspection plan.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can also check for completeness and consistency of the inspection plan by clicking Consistency Check . Save your inspection plan, and the system will confirm that the inspection plan has been saved. You can also set or change control indicators, sample size, or associated catalogs of any characteristic. 2.12 Material Specification Material specification is managed without reference to any plant-specific master inspection characteristics. This alternative to the general inspection plan (with opera- tions and characteristics) in the SAP system provides a simple variant of the inspection plan structuring process that doesn’t contain any operations.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Simply put, a work regu- lation for quality inspections is prepared in the material specification, using com- pletely maintained master inspection characteristics or general characteristics. This avoids redundant or duplicate data entry efforts or information in the SAP system. To create a material specification, use Transaction QS61 or follow menu path SAP  Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Inspection Planning  Material Spec- ification  Edit . On the initial screen that appears, enter Material “RM17”, and press (Enter) or choose Characteristics , and the screen in Figure 2.30 appears.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Here, just like with the QM inspection plan, you can also use master inspection characteristics of other plants while creating the material specification. When assigning a master inspection charac- teristic in the material specification, the system looks for complete copy model or ref- erence characteristic. If the master inspection characteristic is either of the two, it’s possible to assign it while creating a material specification. However, a material speci- fication doesn’t allow usage of an incomplete copy model of a master inspection char- acteristic.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: QMHT10 is a reference master inspection characteristic; therefore, all information, such as decimal places or upper and lower specification limits, is automatically copied from the master inspection characteristic when you create a material specification and is initially available in noneditable mode. Notice the Lock icon in the Ref column that shows the master inspection characteristic is a reference characteristic. You can unlock this lock and make desired changes for the master inspection characteristic in the material specification. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 107 2.12 Material Specification Figure 2.30 Material Specification To do so, choose QMHT10 , and then choose Unlock Charc . (not shown but located on the lower half of the same screen). Once it’s unlocked, choose Details , which leads to the screen in Figure 2.31. This screen offers just about all the options for making changes to the master inspection characteristic that you’ve previously seen. Figure 2.31 Details of Master Inspection Characteristic in the Material Specification Note All the QM master data that you maintained in this chapter will be available for you to work on in Chapter 3, so you can immediately connect the importance of maintaining complete, comprehensive, and correct master data to ensure the smooth functioning of business processes.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 2 Quality Planning 108 2.13 Summary This chapter extensively highlighted the importance of setting up complete, correct, and comprehensive master data for quality planning. It also covered the sequence in which you need to maintain the QM master data to enable you to understand and, accordingly, manage the interdependencies of various master data. Because QM heav- ily and extensively integrates with logistics areas of the SAP S/4HANA system, having a good understanding of the master data of other areas can also bring significant effi- ciency of master data to quality planning.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The next chapter covers quality inspection, as well as some tips and tricks that you can use to efficiently manage your quality planning (master data maintenance as well as business processes). © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 109 Chapter 3 Quality Inspection Quality inspection entails automatic or manual inspection lot creation, results recording, making usage decisions, and stock posting (if applica- ble). A dynamic modification rule enables a better and more practical quality control for logistics and the supply chain. Multiple specifications functionality brings many more choices to quality planning and quality inspection. Continuing with the quality planning master data that you set up in Chapter 2, this chapter delves into turning the same quality planning setup into a quality inspection.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A quality inspection is a series of business process steps that users undertake to per- form inspection of a material, record any defects found, and make appropriate deci- sions to use the material in further logistics and supply chain functions. This chapter begins by walking you through the business processes in quality inspec- tion. Then it explores several optimization and productivity enhancement options available for quality inspection and quality planning. Next, the chapter covers material specifications, an intuitive and user-friendly functionality that caters to the specific needs of process industries.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Then, we discuss the dynamic modification rule and how it helps in maintaining various inspection levels in the production or procurement pro- cesses. Next, we examine a case study that lets you configure a new inspection type, maintain its master data, and execute the business processes of quality inspection. Finally, this chapter covers the combined configuration basics of quality planning and quality inspection. 3.1 Business Processes in Quality Inspection Figure 3.1 illustrates a straightforward business process of quality inspection.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The pro- cess begins when the system automatically or a business user manually creates an inspection lot 1 , which is the beginning of the necessary quality inspection process. The quality inspector records the inspection results 2 , records any defects 3 , and makes a usage decision 4 . The results recording step is the actual and factual data entry of the results of each characteristic that is slated for an inspection. The inspection results help you decide whether to use the material for further processing, such as in Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 110 procurement, production, or sales. The stock posting 5 is the last step in quality inspection and determines whether the stock kept in quality inspection will be released to unrestricted use, blocked, scrapped, or returned to the supplier. Several inspection types aren’t stock-based; that is, no stock posting is required, and the quality inspec- tion process ends with a usage decision only. Figure 3.1 Inspection Lot Processing We’ll discuss each in the following sections, though we’ll discuss defect recording after the rest of the processes and use it to lead into the inspection report. 3.1.1 Inspection Lot Creation When the system or the user creates an inspection lot in the system, the inspection lot requires an inspection plan or material specification to calculate the sample size.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This sample size is then used for results recording and making a usage decision. However, if the system is unable to calculate the sample size due to a missing or invalid inspection plan or material specification, you can’t record results or make a usage decision for the inspection lot. To view the details of the inspection lot, use Transaction QA02 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot Processing  Change . Figure 3.2 shows Inspection Lot 40000000653 of Material FG233 , which the system automati- cally creates at the end of the production process.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Here, the process order (or produc- tion order) against which the production took place is 700020. One of the system statuses for the inspection lot 40000000653 is CHCR, which means that the inspection plan (or material specification) is missing. As explained previously, unless the system is able to assign an inspection plan to an inspection lot to calculate its sample size, you can’t record results or make a usage decision. Inspection lot (automatic/ manual) Results recording Defects recording (if any) Usage decision Stock posting (if applicable) © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 111 3.1 Business Processes in Quality Inspection Figure 3.2 Inspection Lot In the following sections, we’ll look at the various elements of an inspection lot in detail, including how to troubleshoot a missing inspection plan. Assign Inspection Specifications Choose the Inspection Specifications tab, shown in Figure 3.2, to go to the screen in Figure 3.3. Here, the system automatically assigns the inspection plan with Usage 5 (if it was created properly, which isn’t the case in our example). If an automatic assignment isn’t possible, then the user can manually assign the inspection plan to an inspection lot so that the sample size can be calculated.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Usage 5 indicates that the inspection plan is for goods receipt against a process, production, or purchase order. Because the sys- tem was unable to find the inspection plan for Usage 5 , the lower half of the Assigned Specifications area is blank. Another possible reason could be a problem with the Key Date . The system needs to find and be able to assign a valid inspection plan on the key date. For example, say that during inspection plan creation, the key date is 04/27/ 2024—but the key date that you see in Figure 3.3 is 02/27/2024.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system isn’t able to assign an inspection plan with a key date that is later than the inspection lot creation date. Hence, on this date (02/27/2024), the system is unable to find a relevant or active inspection plan and is therefore unable to assign it to the inspection lot to calculate sample size. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 112 Figure 3.3 Unassigned Task List Specifications Tips and Tricks During an SAP S/4HANA implementation project, it’s generally a prudent practice to agree to a key date that’s in the past for creating inspection plans of materials to avoid the missing inspection plan error on the key date. There are several options to troubleshoot and manually assign an inspection plan to the inspection lot with a missing inspection plan:  You can select a different material in the Material field and assign its inspection plan to this inspection lot.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, tea bags and tea packs are different materials, but if they have the same inspection plan, you assign one to the other.  You can also keep the Material the same (FG233) but use a different Plant for which an inspection plan exists and assign that plant-specific inspection plan to this inspection lot.  You can select an inspection plan for the same material but a different usage and assign it to this inspection lot. For example, if no inspection plan with usage 5 exists, but one with usage 9 (material check) exists, you can enter it in the Usage field.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For this example, change or overwrite the key date to 03/27/2024, as shown in Figure 3.4, and then choose the Task List/Spec. button. The system assigns the inspection plan with the details shown in the Assigned Specifications area: Group 4 and Group Counter 2 . © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

Choose the Sample tab, and you’ll see that the sample size is zero. Choose the Sample button. The system calculates the sample size as 100 , as shown in Figure 3.5, and displays a message at the bottom of the screen (not shown). The system also updates the status of the inspection lot to CALC . Figure 3.5 Calculated Sample Size Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 114 Save the inspection lot. With the inspection plan assigned and the sample size calcu- lated, you can now record the results of the inspection lot and make a usage decision. Status Monitoring Whenever you or the system performs any business functions, the system automati- cally updates the status of the inspection lot. It makes sense to monitor these statuses because they reveal important details. It’s particularly useful in the search for short- comings, when the system doesn’t behave as you expect it to.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Table 3.1 shows the long text of the statuses, which you can display by choosing Extras  Inspection Lot Status or clicking the blue icon located right next to the System Status field. 3.1.2 Results Recording In this step, you enter or record results of an inspection lot. In results recording, the system automatically or manually valuates each entered result as either accepted or rejected, depending on the master data setup (inspection planning). Also available are the graphical representation of different results recording, along with other important historical values.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To record results of an inspection lot, operation, or inspection point, use Transaction QE51N or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Work- list  Results Recording .

docs.text: 119 3.1 Business Processes in Quality Inspection Figure 3.11 shows the SAP Fiori app Display Results History with the key figures such as mean value, variance, and Cp and Cpk indices, along with associated graphs (both mean values and single values). These values (of Cp and Cpk) are the process capability indi- ces. The first value (Cp) is a measure for the process dispersion (is the process con- trolled?), that is, how closely a process is running to its specification limits relative to the natural variability of the process.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The second value (Cpk) describes the position of the mean value in relation to the tolerance limits and therefore indicates whether the process is capable. The Cpk is an adjustment to the Cp, affecting its noncentered distri- bution. In other words, Cpk measures how consistent the target values are with normal performance. For a controlled and capable process, both values should be higher than 1.33. In many industries, the minimum requirement for a process capability index is now 2.0 or higher! Details of Cpk and Cp are covered in Chapter 19.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 121 3.1 Business Processes in Quality Inspection Tips and Tricks Following are the transactions for different variants for results recording; all are avail- able through menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Work- list  Variants for Results Recording :  For physical samples: Transaction QE52  For all inspection lots: Transaction QE72  For inspection points: Transaction QE71  For master inspection characteristics: Transaction QE73 Remember that you can also use Transaction QA32 (Worklist for Inspection Lots) for results recording and making usage decisions.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Refer to Chapter 18 on reporting, which covers Transaction QA32 and its features in detail. Note Although you can use any variant of results recording that meets your business needs, we’ll use Transaction QE01 for this purpose here and for the rest of this book. 3.1.3 Usage Decision Now that results and defects (if any) are recorded for an inspection lot, the final steps are to make a decision to use the material, which is known as the usage decision , and to perform a stock posting of an inspection lot. The stock posting transfers the stock placed in quality inspection into either an unrestricted-use stock or any other stock type.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The stock posting depends on the inspection type and inspection origin. To record the usage decision of an inspection lot, use Transaction QA11 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot  Usage Deci- sion  Record . The screen that appears provides an option to enter a usage decision for a single inspection lot. However, there are several other options available to efficiently manage the task of performing a usage decision.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The various icons (discussed in Sec- tion 3.2) located in the menu bar are as follows:  Mass Usage Decisions This ensures that for all inspection lots for which the quality management (QM) user needs to assign a single “accepted” code to several inspection lots, the user can do so on a single screen and with one transaction.  Quantity Posting Required The entire activity of recording a usage decision stipulates two steps: the first step is to assign a usage decision code to an inspection lot, and the second step is to per- form stock posting. This option is available to business users; the usage decision code is already assigned to an inspection lot (the first step is already performed), but Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 122 the user still needs to perform the important step of stock posting (the second step). All such open inspection lot quantities are available in the form of a worklist to work on.  UD Not Taken Yet This option brings up a complete worklist of all the inspection lots for which the QM user needs to make usage decisions.  Inspection Lots without Completion This option offers a complete worklist of all inspection lots that are incomplete in one form or another and are therefore open. For this example, enter inspection lot “10000000702” and press (Enter) so that the screen in Figure 3.14 appears.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Here you see the Defects tab, which appears only when the system records any defects during results recording. Moreover, you can also record defects during a usage decision by choosing Defects located on the top menu bar or cre- ate and activate a quality notification by choosing Notification . Defect recording is cov- ered in detail in Section 3.1.5. On this screen, choose the Characteristics tab to see the summarized results recording available for evaluation before the user makes a usage decision. You can expand the characteristic details by choosing All Characteristics .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 3.14 Characteristics in Usage Decision Select the box to the right of UD Code and press (F4) or choose the dropdown option. The popup that appears provides a list of options available to the user to choose a usage decision code. Each usage decision code valuates the inspection lot as either accepted or rejected. The usage decision code also internally assigns a quality score to help in © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 123 3.1 Business Processes in Quality Inspection overall quality calculation of supplier-delivered material. These quality scores form the basis of future procurement decisions with a supplier. Quality scores are automatically updated with each usage decision. The relevant quality score isn’t shown until the user selects the usage decision code. Choose UD Code A, and the system automatically also assigns its associated catalog or selected set, 01. With usage decision code A assigned, the system automatically assigns the corresponding quality score of 100 (see Chapter 19 for more information on quality scores).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Depending on the settings made in the material master, the system automatically cal- culates and incorporates the shelf-life expiration date/best-before date (SLED/BBD), or you can enter it manually. You also have the option to enter the long text of the usage decision by choosing the Long Text icon located next to Code Valuation to enter any additional details. 3.1.4 Stock Posting In the Inspection Lot Stock tab shown in Figure 3.15, you enter the inspection lot quan- tity into one of the several options available to perform the stock posting.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These options are as follows:  To Unrestricted Use The quantity placed in quality inspection is available as free to consume.  To Scrap The company destroys some or all of the quantity placed in quality inspection due to the defective quality of the material. The scrapped quantity is charged to the rele- vant cost center that you assigned in configuration.  To Sample Consumptn Either the system or the user can enter some quantity of material consumed as sam- ples.  To Blocked Stock Some or all of the quantity placed in quality inspection is placed in blocked/ restricted-use stock.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This stock isn’t available to use.  To New Material You can perform transfer posting of one material into another material after evalu- ating that the material fits more with the new/different material than the original material.  To Reserves You can assign some quantity to reserve stock for subsequent use.  Return Delivery (not shown) You decide to return complete or partial quantity to the supplier due to defective quality or noncompliance with specifications. For example, you can choose the Document button (which will show Details when you hover over it) of the To Scrap field and change the default cost center. In Figure 3.15, the system shows that out of 100 PC of inspection lot quantity ( Insp. Lot Qty ), you can post up to a quantity of 90 PC to unrestricted-use stock (or any other stock type available), while the system automatically calculates the sample use of 100 PC.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 3.15 Inspection Stock Posting This sample calculation is based on the settings that you made for the relevant master inspection characteristic. You can enter any combination here that reflects the actual stock posting that you want to perform. For example, you can delete the sample-use quantity of 10 PC, and post the entire 100 PC of inspection lot quantity to unrestricted- use or blocked stock. For this example, enter To Unrestricted Use as “90” and To Sample Consumptn as “10”. Choose the Document button, and Figure 3.16 appears.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 125 3.1 Business Processes in Quality Inspection Figure 3.16 Usage Decision Header Data If a material is batch-managed, then you can also change the batch status to restricted or unrestricted, as deemed necessary. Otherwise, you can separately change the status of a batch using Transaction MSC2N (Change Batch). 3.1.5 Defect Recording During results recording, the quality inspector finds quite a few defects, and the need to record these defects becomes evident for subsequent action by either returning the defective material to the supplier or requesting replacement (or rework, in the case of in-house-produced material).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As already explained, you perform defects recording during results recording and usage decision. Once a usage decision for an inspection lot is made, you can no longer record defects. To record defects, use Transaction QF11 or use menu path Logistics  Quality Manage- ment  Quality Inspection  Defects  Record for Inspection Lot . On the initial screen that appears, enter inspection lot “10000000701” and report type “00000010”. Whenever a user enters the defects of an inspection lot, it’s mandatory for the user to choose the relevant report type .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A report type denotes that when the user runs the corresponding defects reports in the system, the relevant information is available for display and analysis purposes. Several standard defect report types are available, or you can config- ure new report types to cater to any specific business processes (see more about report- ing in Chapter 18). Some of the options available for report types are in several combinations of defect types, number of defects, defect locations, causes of defect, and activities for the QM user to perform on recording the defects.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Press (Enter) , and the system offers three options through a popup to record the defect data at the inspection-lot level, operation level, or master inspection characteristic level. The defects recording at the inspection lot stipulates that the quality inspector found the defects in the entire inspection lot. At the operation level, it’s the specific operation or stage/phase in which the quality inspector found the defects. At the char- acteristics level, it’s the particular master inspection characteristic for which the qual- ity inspector intends to record defects.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 126 Tips and Tricks You can also use Transaction QF21 for operation defect recording and Transaction QF31 for characteristics defect recording. Select the Inspection Lot radio button and then choose Continue , so that Figure 3.17 appears. Figure 3.17 Defects Recording To begin recording defects, first choose Defects from the top menu bar. In the popup that appears, choose the Code Group column, and press (F4) . A code group and its asso- ciated codes represents the logical grouping of different defect types available in a cat- alog.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A few examples of different defect code groups and types of different defects in pumps are combined together in one code group, and all types of electrical defects are combined in one defect code group. All supplier-related defects, which the company normally observes or handles, are grouped together in one defect code group, and all the production-related defects on one machine or group of machines are combined into one defect code group. The quality inspector can enter the number of defects against each defect code.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, these defective quantities aren’t directly related to or integrated with the inspection lot quantity or goods receipt quantity. For this example, enter a Code group of “QM-E” and Code of “1” ( Defect Type: Out of Specification ). When the user selects a defect code, the system automatically assigns a defect class to it to categorize the nature of the defect. A defect class denotes the sever- ity of the defect. Some of the defect classes are critical defect, major defect, and minor defect. These defect classes are available as standard options in the system, but you can also configure and make available new defect classes to meet your business needs. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 127 3.1 Business Processes in Quality Inspection The user can also enter a short description for each defect code in the corresponding Description column, as well as a long text. When the necessary entries are made, Figure 3.17 shows three defects along with other details such as the defect type, number of defects for each defect type, and defect class. 3.1.6 Inspection Report The inspection report displays the inspection results and comments of every charac- teristic on the screen as a print preview or in the form of a printout.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This means it can also be used to provide an overview of the inspection carried out, or it can be referred to as a basis for the usage decision. It can also serve as an attachment to a quality noti- fication to the supplier or to internal departments to describe in detail the deviations of individual characteristics according to type and scope, in the case of defects. To display the inspection report, use Transaction QGA3 or follow menu path Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Result  Print . The system displays the Results Print selection screen.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If you know the inspection lot number, you can enter it directly. Otherwise, the selection allows you to set limits through known parameters such as material number, supplier, and date, among others. Figure 3.18 shows an exam- ple of a print preview (selective) of an inspection report for inspection lot 10000000701 for material RM17. Figure 3.18 Inspection Report Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 128 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection Just as we covered the standard QM business processes in the specific sequence in which they occur, this section covers optimization and other productivity enhance- ment options available in the following areas:  Master data  Inspection lot  Digital signature  Results recording  Usage decision  Engineering Workbench 3.2.1 Master Data Let’s begin with master data. We started with the fundamentals in Chapter 2; the fol- lowing information represents specific optimization.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Replace Inspection Characteristic or Inspection Method To replace characteristics, master inspection characteristics, or inspection plans, use Transaction QS27 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Plan- ning  Basic Data  Inspection Characteristic  Replace . Figure 3.19 shows the initial screen where you enter the original or existing characteristic number and its plant. Figure 3.19 Master Inspection Characteristic and Inspection Method Replacement © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 129 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection In the Replacement Master Inspection Characteristic with Inspection Method area, you can enter only the new characteristic or the new characteristic and its associated inspection method. Choose Continue (not shown, but located on the bottom right hand side of the screen) and the screen in Figure 3.20 appears. Here, you can choose to replace some or all of the characteristics listed online or as a batch input (background job). Choose Start Replacement located on the bottom-right side of the screen (not shown) to start the replacement process.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 3.20 Replace Master Inspection Characteristic Warning You need to engage an ABAP resource to activate user exit QPAA0004 to be able to use this replace characteristic functionality. However, implementing this user exit in isola- tion leads to other problems, such as not being able to incorporate inspection charac- teristics in an inspection plan. We suggest that while implementing this user exit, you also implement dependent and subsequent user exits or function modules that your ABAP resource should be able to manage.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Where-Used List At any time, you can leverage the where-used list to find the inspection plan in which a specific characteristic is used. For this, use Transaction QS26 or follow menu path Logis- tics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Inspection Characteristic  Where-Used List . List Inspection Characteristic You can view a complete list of inspection characteristics and all their settings in the form of a list or report. To view this characteristic list, use Transaction QS28 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Inspection Characteristic  List .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 130 Delete Task List (Inspection Plan) To delete obsolete or wrongly created inspection plans, use Transaction CA98. Be sure to choose Task List Type Q , which is specific to inspection plans. Note Although we cover only limited change, replace, delete, or report options for quality planning master data, we suggest that you explore these options available for every QM master data element. The relevant options are available in the same menu paths that you use to create or change any QM master data, such as inspection plan, inspec- tion method, work center, class characteristic, or inspection characteristic. 3.2.2 Inspection Lot Let’s now cover the inspection lot and its various business scenarios.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Correct Errors To correct quantity-related errors of an inspection lot, use Transaction QAC1 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot  Pro- cessing  Lot Quantity  Correct Errors . You can use this option to correct or change both stock-based and non-stock-based inspection lots. The stock-based quantity update is especially helpful when the system automatically creates an inspection lot on receipt of goods for a purchase or process order and accordingly suggests an inspection lot quantity, which you can change, if needed.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Stock Transfer Let’s say that you receive a quality stock of material, and on inspection, you conclude that you need to keep it in a separate storage location or transfer it to a different plant. In this case, you use the stock transfer option. When you use this option, the stock that’s transferred to a different plant or storage location still remains in quality inspec- tion until you record results, make a usage decision, and perform stock posting. To transfer stock plant-to-plant or store-to-store for an inspection lot, use Transaction QAC2 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspec- tion Lot  Processing  Lot Quantity  Stock Transfer .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On the initial screen that appears, enter the stock of which you want to transfer-post in the inspection lot, and press (Enter) . The Transfer Posting Insp. Lot Stock area shows the current location of the quality stock. You can enter a different plant for stock for plant-to-plant stock transfer, or simply keep the same plant (as in this example) and change the storage location of inspection stock from 0001 to 0002 (see the St.Loc.ILotStock field) in the Stock Transfer Based On area. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 131 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection Cancel Sample Calculation On inspection lot creation (manual or automatic), the system assigns an inspection plan or material specification and calculates a sample size. If you realize that you or the system incorporated an incorrect or obsolete inspection plan and therefore calculated a wrong sample size, you can cancel the sample calculation. Canceling the sample cal- culation also enables you to reassign a new or different inspection plan and accord- ingly recalculate the sample size.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In other words, you have to cancel the sample calculation before the system allows you to reassign an inspection plan and then recal- culate the sample size. To cancel a sample calculation, use Transaction QAC3 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot  Processing  Cancel Sample Calculation . On the initial screen that appears, enter the inspection lot of the sample you want to cancel, press (Enter) , and then simply save. Tips and Tricks To cancel, you can also use Transaction QA02 (Change Inspection Lot); on the initial screen, enter the inspection lot number, and choose Cancel Sample .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Inspection Lots with Outstanding Quantities It’s of interest to the quality inspector to have a complete list of inspection lots for which a usage decision may or may not be made, but for which stock posting is still pending or outstanding. To access inspection lots with outstanding quantities and be able to make usage decisions on the same screen, use Transaction QVM2 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Worklist  Inspection Lot Completion  Inspection Lot with Stock . In Figure 3.21, notice that the system sta- tuses of a few inspection lots stipulate that the usage decision has already been made, but its stock posting remains.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 132 Tips and Tricks Transaction QVM1 is for inspection lots with inspection completion, whereas Transac- tion QVM3 is for inspection lots without a usage decision. Cancel Inspection Lot If you or the system has created an inspection lot that you no longer want to inspect or use, you’ll want to cancel it. This option is helpful when you’ve mistakenly activated an inspection type against which the system created an inspection lot. To cancel, first go to Transaction QA02 (Change Inspection Lot), then navigate to Inspection Lot  Func- tions  Cancel Lot .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system sets the status of the inspection lot to LTCA . Similarly, if you want to reset an inspection lot cancellation, navigate to Inspection Lot  Functions  Reset Cancellation . Block Inspection Lot To temporarily block an inspection lot so that you can perform additional tests, or to prevent the quality inspector from making its usage decision or stock posting, you can block the inspection lot. To do so, first go to Transaction QA02 (Change Inspection Lot), and then navigate to Inspection Lot  Functions  Block Lot .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system sets the status of the inspection lot to LKD . Similarly, to unblock an inspection lot, navigate to Inspection Lot  Functions  Unblock Lot . 3.2.3 Digital Signature The digital signature functionality reduces the number of printed documents that need to be signed within an organization. You can define and then assign digital signatures in an SAP system during various transaction processes, such as recording results and mak- ing usage decisions in QM, changing the status of a document in Document Manage- ment System (DMS), or completing a process instructions sheet in production planning (PP).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Digital signatures can be internal, such as an SAP system user’s password, or even use external devices, such as fingerprint readers or card slides. Digital signatures can confirm important business decisions in QM, such as according approval to the quality inspection lot, validating the correctness of shift reports in plant maintenance (PM), or simply confirming the values of process parameters in production planning for process industries (PP-PI). They do all of this electronically, saving significant time and effort, eventually bringing about improvements in business processes and saving money.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The following are some of the areas in QM in which you can integrate digital signatures with relevant business processes:  Inspection lot approval  Results recording © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 133 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection  Usage decisions  Physical-sample drawing  Header or item level of QM notification Note Throughout this book, we’ve highlighted the business processes in which you can inte- grate digital signatures. It’s important to highlight that the digital signature configuration that you undertake here for QM is directly assigned at the material level (we’ll show this later). Hence, from the implementation consideration point of view, consider some or all of the preceding combinations of business processes in which you’ll use the same digital signature strategy.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, will a material require a digital signature for approval of only the inspection lot, or will it also need a digital signature at the time of results recording? If the latter, then a combination of a single QM material authorization group that encom- passes both the business processes (inspection lot approval and results recording) will suffice. If the business process requires a digital signature on physical sample with- drawal, then configuring a separate QM material authorization group to cater to this business need and then assigning it to the material master serves the needed purpose.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Note If you further integrate digital signature functionality with SAP Business Workflow, then the person responsible for digitally signing a particular SAP system object auto- matically receives the relevant information via the SAP system inbox. This section begins by covering the important steps you need to take to configure dig- ital signatures. Then, we’ll run the entire end-to-end business process in QM to show how digital signatures work. Note The concepts and flows that we’ll cover for digital signatures in QM are equally appli- cable to all the other areas of SAP S/4HANA that digital signatures apply to.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Configuration Basics Following are the six important steps in configuring a digital signature: 1. Define authorization groups. 2. Define individual signatures. 3. Define a signature strategy. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 134 4. Create authorization groups for QM master data. 5. Configure the material authorization group, inspection lot approval, digital signa- ture. 6. Create a signature method. Tips and Tricks Although this section focuses on digital signatures in QM, the general menu path for digital signatures is SAP IMG  Cross-Application Components  General Application Functions  Digital Signature . We’ll now discuss each of the steps for configuration in the following sections. Define Authorization Groups An authorization group is used to limit the authorization of a transaction or group of transactions to a specific user or group of users performing the same role.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Once config- ured, this authorization group can be controlled through authorization object C_SIGN_ BGR . You need to coordinate with your SAP NetWeaver (Basis) team members to get the right authorization group assigned to the right user. To create an authorization group, follow SAP system menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Environment  Central Functions  Signature Strategy  Define Authoriza- tion Groups . Here, you can see the initial screen for the creation of an authorization group for digital signatures (see Figure 3.22).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Choose the New Entries button (not shown) to create a new authorization group, UD , and enter a description (“Digital Signa- ture for UD”, in this example). Save the authorization group. Figure 3.22 Creating New Authorization Group Define Individual Signatures An individual signature is a unique identification in the SAP system to which a user is assigned. To create a new individual signature, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Environment  Central Functions  Signature Strategy  Define Individual Signatures .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the screen that appears (see Figure 3.23), choose New Entries , and define two individual signatures— UD01 and UD02 —with descriptions. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 135 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection Figure 3.23 Two Individual Signatures Both individual signatures are assigned to the same authorization group— UD —as shown in Figure 3.23. Save the entries. Define a Signature Strategy A signature strategy is the combination of different individual signatures that are assigned to an authorization group. A signature strategy also defines the sequence and flow of individual signatures and maintains the predecessor-successor relationships. The signature strategy is used to control the level to which the document can be con- sidered released.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA

docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 144 3.2.4 Results Recording Let’s now cover results recording and its various business scenarios—specifically, copying inspection results of one inspection lot to another as well as copying inspec- tion results into batch classification.
