docs.text: The configuration settings are inspection-type-specific for a particular plant in which available copy controls are at the inspection-lot-creation level and at the results-recording level. While this functionality is more commonly used in recurring inspections (inspection type 09), you can also use this functionality for any other inspection type/plant combi- nation, as this example shows. docs.text: 151 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection Copy Inspection Results into Batch Classification Now that you’re familiar with how to manually or automatically copy inspection results of one inspection lot to another, you can also copy inspection results into batch classifications. In this business process, the results of an inspection lot are directly transferred as characteristic values of a batch. The following sections explain the steps involved. Configuration Setting You need to make the following two settings: 1.

In the Classification tab, you’ll find the inspection results transferred as batch characteristics. 3.2.5 Usage Decision Let’s now cover the different types of usage decisions, including collective usage deci- sions and automatic usage decisions:  In collective usage decisions , several inspection lots that are already accepted during the results recording processes are accepted via assignment of a single usage deci- sion code (accepted) to multiple inspection lots.  In automatic usage decision , the system reduces the time and effort required from business users to record usage decisions of accepted inspection lots by automati- cally assigning a usage decision code (accepted) to these inspection lots.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll also cover how to reset a usage decision, as well as two ways of reversing one. Collective Usage Decision If you’ve inspected several inspection lots and found the results acceptable, then you can release the material placed in quality inspection to the next processing step. It makes sense to assign an accepted usage design code to all the accepted inspection lots at once, instead of one at a time, saving you time and effort. To perform a collective usage design, use Transaction QA16 or follow menu path Logis- tics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Worklist  Inspection Lot Completion  Collective Usage Decision (General) (see Figure 3.42).

Automatic Usage Decision Consider a business scenario in which your reliable, long-time supplier routinely sup- plies material that meets your company’s specification. To bring efficiency to the qual- ity inspection process, as well as reward the supplier for reliably supplying quality product, you can use automatic usage design functionality.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Similarly, after a major plant upgrade, the quality of the in-house-produced goods has greatly improved. In this case, you repeatedly end up recording the same acceptable results of the inspected material. If the supplier regularly supplies satisfactory goods and all inspection lots are accepted, then the company starts skipping the results recording step in QM until a problem in any of the inspection lots arises. In the SAP system, these inspection lots have the SKIP status. To optimize the entire business process in QM, you can perform an automatic usage decision for all the inspection lots with the SKIP status, as follows: 1.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the plant settings, maintain the time lapse for automatic usage decisions. A time lapse is the time that the system must wait before it proceeds with automatic usage decision business process. See Figure 3.88 later in this chapter to see where you need to maintain the requisite configuration settings. 2. You also need to ensure that the Automatic UD checkbox is selected in Inspection Setup of the inspection type of the material-plant combination for which you want to perform an automatic usage decision. 3. Use Transaction QA10 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Worklist  Inspection Lot Completion  Automatic Usage Decision (Gen- eral)  Trigger Manually to perform an automatic usage decision.

To perform automatic usage decisions, use Transaction QA40 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Worklist  Inspection Lot Comple- tion  Automatic Usage Decision (Order)  Trigger Manually .

docs.text: On the initial screen that appears, enter the relevant plant, and then choose whether the order must be com- pleted, only technically completed, or just confirmed for the system to perform auto- matic usage decisions. You then need to assign a usage decision code to the inspection lots for orders. Reset Usage Decision Sometimes, an incorrect usage decision is entered for an inspection lot, due to either an incorrect manual data entry or an error made during collective or mass usage deci- sions for quality inspection lots.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Because an incorrect usage decision code leads to an incorrect calculation of quality scores, it’s imperative that the user correct this anom- aly as soon as possible. To reset or change the usage decision code of an inspection lot, use Transaction QA12 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot  Usage Decision  Change with History . If you choose Reset UD , the existing usage deci- sion code disappears. You can enter the new usage decision code at that time or do so later.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When you reset the usage decision, the system assigns the status UDRE to the inspection lot. Upon resetting the usage decision code, you’re also able to change the results of an inspection lot, if there’s any such business need. Changes to the previously recorded inspection results aren’t possible if a usage decision for an inspection lot is already made. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 158 Tips and Tricks If you can’t see the Reset UD option in your SAP system, you’ll need to engage an ABAP resource who will implement and activate user exit QEVA0008 . Reverse Stock Posting If you have an inspection lot that is stock-based, have your ABAP resource implement user exit QEVA0008 to complete the reversal process. A stock-based inspection lot rever- sal means that you’re resetting the usage decision code and placing the quality-cleared inspection stock (unrestricted stock) back into quality inspection.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Such business sce- narios are applicable in goods receipt against a purchase order or a goods receipt against a production or process order, in which you not only assign a usage decision code to the inspection lot, but also simultaneously perform stock posting. The user exit uses movement type 322 and transfers the quality-cleared stock back into quality inspection stock. When implementing this user exit, you need to have a custom- designed transaction to achieve the reversal objective. Your ABAP resource will be able to manage this activity.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can also use Transaction MIGO to reverse the material document even after a usage decision for an inspection lot is made. The specific movement type is 101, against which the system creates an inspection lot, which is for goods receipt for procurement. The reversal of movement type 101 is 102. To perform the reversal, follow these steps: 1. From the first dropdown, choose Cancelation . 2. From the second dropdown, choose Material Document . 3. Enter the relevant manual documentation number that needs to be canceled. 4.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Save your entries, and the system creates a material document number, which is basically a reversal material document. At the same time, the system brings the material’s stock quantity back into quality inspection stock, and you can either put it into blocked stock or return it to the supplier using the usage decision business process (Transaction QA11 or QA12). 3.2.6 Engineering Workbench The Engineering Workbench tool allows you to make mass changes to inspection plans and task lists with an integrated and intuitive interface.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can edit, exchange, change, and delete the operations of a task list, just as you can with the characteristics. Also integrated here are the maintenance functions for the material routing assignment and for the allocation of PRTs to support QM. The work area settings make it possible for you to adapt your inspections to the special planning tasks in the QM area. docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 160 Figure 3.48 Headers Overview of Engineering Workbench 3.3 Multiple Specifications Multiple specifications attend to one of the critical requirements of the process indus- try: to store specifications depending on freely selectable objects. There, you can use different limits for various suppliers or customers in the same inspection plan.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA

With multiple specifications, for example, custom- ers often ask questions such as, “Does the tolerance limit of the active substance con- tent of a supplier-delivered substance meet the approval in a selected country?” The following example addresses the same question about the usage of a substance for a specific country and covers not just the configuration basics or the master data that you need to set up but also the business processes of multiple specifications. 3.3.1 Configuration Settings To begin, you need to ensure that the following configuration settings are in place: 1.

docs.text: 169 3.4 Dynamic Modification Rule 3.4 Dynamic Modification Rule The dynamic modification rule eliminates the need to routinely record all inspection results of every incoming raw material of a supplier or continuous manufacturing of finished goods having acceptable quality. Integration of the dynamic modification rule into procurement and production processes promises to bring about significant opti- mization and efficiency. It skips a predefined number of inspection lots for results recording purposes and requires a user to enter only a usage decision for the inspection lots.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, a rejected inspection lot automatically triggers a normal or even tight- ened inspection (see Figure 3.59). This ensures that necessary checks and balances are in place, despite moving toward optimizing or automating some of the processes by means of implementing the dynamic modification rule for reduced inspection efforts. Figure 3.59 Dynamic Modification Rule at a Glance In procurement, the dynamic modification rule helps to quickly bring the raw material or packing material to the production line if the supplier adheres to the stringent qual- ity control of the company.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The dynamic modification rule provides for inspections at periodic intervals. As soon as any problem in quality is observed, it reverts back to reg- ular or tightened inspection until the supplier again meets the quality standards. With the dynamic modification rule in place, the company benefits from reduced data entry effort and is able to reduce the lead time to quality clear, which is in the time it takes to process received goods in SAP S/4HANA and make them available to the production process. It also helps to reduce inventory carrying costs.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It enables suppliers to negotiate better payment terms and a better selling price for their product, given that reliability with the company has been established. Eventually, all these factors add up to a process Time Skip Tightened Normal Reduced Rules for changing the inspection stage Inspection Stage Dynamic modification rule Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 170 called annual or periodic supplier evaluation in SAP S/4HANA (see Chapter 19). Quality plays a very important role in this process, in addition to price and timely deliveries. This section covers the master data you need to set up the dynamic modification rule, including sampling scheme and sampling procedure. This is then followed by the busi- ness processes of the dynamic modification rule. Note Although this example covers integration of the dynamic modification rule into the production process, the same principles apply to procurement processes. 3.4.1 Master Data Maintenance You need to make two quick checks of your master data to ensure that the dynamic modification rule is effectively implemented when conducting transactions.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The checks are in the material master and master inspection characteristic, which we’ll dis- cuss in the following subsections. Material Master The material has previously been created, but you need to activate its QM view at the organizational level (plant). In addition, you need to activate inspection type 01 for goods receipt against a purchase order. If the dynamic modification rule is imple- mented in the production process, then make the relevant settings for inspection type 04 for process or production order.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Choose the Inspection Type detail for inspection type 01. Select the Skips Allowed checkbox. This ensures that when the dynamic modification rule is working for inspec- tion type 01, it allows skipping of inspection results recording. Inspection type 01 is used to activate QM for goods receipts against a purchase order. Save your settings. Note If you intend to use the dynamic modification rule for goods receipt against the pro- duction process, then you need to make the same Skips Allowed check in the material master for inspection type 04.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Inspection type 01 is the QM activation for goods receipt for a purchase order or scheduling agreement with a supplier. You can also activate this check in any other inspection type for which you want to integrate the dynamic modification rule process. Sampling Procedure in the Master Inspection Characteristic You need to ensure that the Sampling Procedure checkbox is checked in the master inspection characteristic. Just like the master inspection characteristic, the sampling © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 171 3.4 Dynamic Modification Rule procedure is also QM master data, and you use it to define the sample size of an inspec- tion lot and how the system calculates it. To change the master inspection characteristic, use Transaction QS23 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Inspection Characteris- tic  Change . Choose Control Indicators , and select the Sampling Procedure checkbox. Save your settings. To effectively implement the dynamic modification rule in the production process, maintain the QM master data in the sequence we’ll specify in the following sections.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Define a Sampling Scheme In a sampling scheme, sample size is defined based on the total quantity of the goods receipt. The sampling scheme also incorporates the information related to the number of samples that can be accepted or rejected in a sample size to help decide whether the quality inspector should accept or reject an inspection lot. To create a sampling scheme, use Transaction QDP1 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Sampling  Sampling Scheme  Create . On the initial screen, enter the sampling scheme (“QSS” in this example), and press (Enter) to see the header data for the sampling scheme.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Select the Valuation Parameters as Attributive Insp. to ensure that the system automatically valuates all master inspection characteristics within the tolerance limits as accepted and that the nonconforming master inspection characteristics have the rejected valuation. Select the Sampling Tables For as Severity/AQL . Note Acceptable quality level (AQL) is the international industry standard to define the total percentage of samples that are either accepted or rejected from an overall sample cal- culation. Hence, an AQL level of 3.5% allows defects of 3.5% of the overall sample size calculation.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If the system calculates the sample size of an inspection lot to be 100 and its AQL is 3.5%, then not more than 3.5 samples out of the 100-sample lot can be rejected for the system to consider the inspection lot as acceptable. Although various international AQL standards, such as those of ISO, are available in SAP as standard offerings and you can immediately begin using them, we’ll cover how to create an AQL in detail, just in case there is a business need that is company-specific. Choose Continue to define the inspection severity and AQL value.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Choose the Inspec- tion Severity dropdown, and the system brings up the four different severity levels. Choose inspection severity 002 , which denotes a reduced inspection; enter an AQL Value of “3.000”; press (Enter) or choose QSS ; and the screen in Figure 3.60 appears. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 172 Figure 3.60 Sampling Table for Inspection Severity 2 (Reduced Inspection) and AQL Value of 2.000 Here, you see the sampling table for sampling scheme QSS with an inspection severity of 002 and an AQL value of 3.000. Note that it’s standard SAP system behavior that all leading zeros are eliminated, but up to three decimal places are shown. Therefore, in Figure 3.60, the inspection severity of 002 has been changed to 2. Although the AQL value is defined as 3.0 in Figure 3.60, the system shows up to three decimal places.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Here, define that the sample size is five units for an inspection lot quantity up to 500 units. Of that, a minimum of two units (column c1 ) has to be accepted, while a maxi- mum of three units (column d1 ) is allowed for rejection. This is applicable for all the inspection lots for which there is a reduced inspection. For an inspection lot of 10,000 units or more, the sample size is 10 units, while the number of acceptable samples is 4. A maximum of 6 rejections is acceptable. Choose Other Table to go to the screen in Figure 3.61.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The same process for creating another set for inspection severity and AQL is repeated for an inspection severity of normal, which is denoted by 004 and with an AQL level of 4.000. This screen defines that for an inspection lot quantity of 500 units, there is a sample size of five units, out of which a minimum of three units (column c1 ) has to be accepted, while a maximum of four units (column d1 ) is allowed for rejection. For an inspection lot of 10,000 or greater, the sample size is 10, and the number of acceptable samples should be five.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 173 3.4 Dynamic Modification Rule Figure 3.61 Sampling Table for Inspection Severity 4 and Acceptable Quality Limit Value of 4.000 Depending on business requirements, there can be several variations for defining reduced, normal, and tightened inspections in SAP S/4HANA. For example, with a reduced inspection, there can be fewer sample sizes to inspect, while the acceptance and rejection samples stay the same. In this example, we’ve kept the sample size for reduced and normal inspection the same, which is 5 units for an inspection lot up to 500 units, but defined that for a reduced inspection, the acceptable samples should be at least 2 units, and the maximum rejected samples should be 3 units.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For a normal inspection, at least 3 units must be acceptable, and a maximum of 4 units can be rejected. You can use the same process to define a tightened inspection. The produced good is then monitored more frequently for quality checks until it’s able to maintain and sus- tain the acceptable quality products over a longer period of time. Once this is achieved, the tightened inspection can be brought back to normal inspection or even reduced inspection. The option to define a tightened inspection with an inspection severity code of 006 is defined.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: All subsequent steps remain the same as for reduced or normal inspections. Configuration Tip To set up an inspection severity that meets your company’s business needs, follow the configuration menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Sample, SPC  Define Inspection Severities . Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 174 Setting Up a Sampling Procedure A sampling procedure is the QM master data that helps you define how the system cal- culates the sample size of an inspection lot. To create a sampling procedure, use Trans- action QDV1 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Sampling  Sampling Procedure  Create . On the initial screen of the sampling procedure, define the sampling procedure (in this example, it’s “QMSP”) and press (Enter) to bring up the screen in Figure 3.62, the assignments screen of the sampling procedure.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Here, assign the Sampling Type as Use sampling scheme , which you just cre- ated in the previous step. Other sampling types available are Fixed Sample , which entails that regardless of the inspection lot size, the sample size is fixed, and Percent- age , which entails that the sample size is calculated based on a defined percentage of the inspection lot. For Valuation Mode , select Attributive inspection nonconf. units to ensure that the sys- tem valuates a master inspection characteristic as accepted if the results are within the specified tolerance limits.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If any result is not, then the system valuates the master inspection characteristic as rejected. As Sampling Type is selected as Use sampling scheme , assign the relevant sampling scheme, which in this example is QSS . Figure 3.62 Sampling Procedure with Sampling Type and Valuation Mode © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 175 3.4 Dynamic Modification Rule In the Inspection Points area, choose Others so you can enter any relevant identifier as an inspection point. If you’re creating a sampling procedure for eventual use in PM or sample management, then choose the relevant radio button. Note Chapter 7 provides information on integrating QM with PM, and Chapter 10 discusses sample management. In both chapters, use the relevant inspection points that we dis- cuss here. Choose Continue to go to the screen in Figure 3.63, assign the previously created sam- pling scheme QSS , and then choose Additional Data to go to Figure 3.64.

docs.text: Figure 3.63 Assigning Sampling Scheme in Sampling Procedure Figure 3.64 Sampling Procedure QMSP with Inspection Severity of 002 and AQL Value of 2.000 Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 176 Figure 3.64 requires you to assign the inspection severity and the AQL value for the pre- viously created sampling scheme QSS. Press (F4) or choose the dropdown box to the right of the Inspection Severity field (not shown). The system brings up two options for sampling scheme QSS from which to choose—namely, reduced inspection with an AQL of 3.000 and normal inspection with an AQL of 4.000. Choose Reduced Inspection with an AQL value of 3.000, and then choose Continue to go to Figure 3.64. Save your entries, and the system opens a popup that asks if you want to create an allowed relationship between the sampling scheme and a dynamic modifi- cation rule.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As you have yet to create a dynamic modification rule that meets your business needs, which we’ll cover in the next section, choose No in the popup. Dynamic Modification Rule The dynamic modification rule consists of user-defined rules that define the factors that trigger a move from normal inspection to reduced inspection or vice versa. The dynamic modification rule also enables you to define when the system should skip results recording of inspection lots. The dynamic modification rule defines the number of inspection lots that have the accepted or rejected statuses before the system switches inspection stages from normal to reduced to tightened or vice versa.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To create a dynamic modification rule, use Transaction QDR1 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Sampling  Dynamic Modification Rule  Create . On the initial screen, enter “DMR” (in this example), and press (Enter) . On the header data screen for the dynamic modification rule, enter the short descrip- tion, and select the dynamic modification rule as For Usage Decision . This option ensures that the basis for the system to trigger the dynamic modification rule is a usage decision of an inspection lot; that is, if an inspection lot has been accepted during the usage decision, the dynamic modification rule decides whether there is a need for an inspection stage change.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Warning We suggest that you use the dynamic modification rule for usage decisions because, in this case, the system only updates quality scores based on the usage decision, and in the case of rejections and/or partial acceptance, the system updates the quality score accordingly. To use the dynamic modification rule at an inspection lot level, it entails that there will be hardly any rejections, and the system updates the quality scores based only on inspection lot creation. If you reject the material, the system doesn’t update the quality scores, even though you run the cancellation process of the usage decision and results recording. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 177 3.4 Dynamic Modification Rule Choose Continue to bring up the detailed screen to define inspection stages of a dynamic modification rule (see Figure 3.65). An inspection stage enables the user to define the number of accepted or rejected inspection lots that lead to an inspection stage change. Inspection stages are also referred to as stages. For this example, there are two stages: 1 and 2 . For stage 1 , define an inspection severity of 2 , which is the normal inspection. Also acti- vate the ISt checkbox (initial stage) to ensure that the dynamic modification rule pro- cesses always start with normal inspection (stage 1) before the stage changes to reduced inspection (stage 2).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In stage 2 , activate the checkbox for Skip inspection, which means that system allows skips in results recording for the inspection stage 2 (reduced inspec- tion). Next, select the row of inspection Stage 1 shown in Figure 3.65, and choose Stage Change . This leads to Figure 3.66. Figure 3.65 Dynamic Modification Rule with Details about Inspection Stages Figure 3.66 1 shows the detailed screen for inspection stage changes for inspection stage 1. Here, define that at least one inspection lot must have the usage decision OK or Accepted so that inspection stage 1 changes to stage 2.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If there is a single rejection 1 with Not OK or a rejection in the Rejections field, then the next inspection stage is 1, which is the normal inspection and requires results recording. Choose Continue, which leads back to Figure 3.65. Repeat the same process from the screen in Figure 3.65 by selecting Stage 2 and Stage Change to go to the screen in Figure 3.66 2 , which stipulates that there can be a maxi- mum of two skips before the system considers stage change. If there is a skipped inspection lot during results recording (for which no result recording is needed in the first place), the system still creates the next inspection lot with the skip status on goods receipt against the process order.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Similarly, if there is one rejection ( Not OK ), then the next stage remains 1, which is a normal inspection. In the case of infrequent inspec- tions, you can define the maximum skip duration in days, after which the system must take inspections into account. Choose Continue to go to the screen in Figure 3.67. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 183 3.5 New Inspection Types Figure 3.72 Quality Level History App 3.5 New Inspection Types In Chapter 2, we explained that creating new inspection types to meet business needs normally doesn’t serve the purpose because the functions and functionality offered are the same as you find with standard inspection types. However, in unique business sce- narios, when you need to distinguish a quality inspection process from a routine or normal inspection, you proceed with the necessary configuration of a new inspection type and its associated dependent configuration that enables you to run the business process.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The example in this section shows that you want to create a new inspection type to attend to special inspection needs for tea leaves that come from specific tea gardens— Darjeeling and Kenya gardens. Here, you perform step-by-step configuration and assign the configured objects to master data that lets you run the business process. Let’s get started. 3.5.1 Configuration Settings You need to perform the following four configuration steps: 1. Create a task list usage. 2. Maintain the inspection type. 3. Maintain the inspection lot origins, and assign inspection types. 4.

docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 184 Create a Task List Usage You’re already familiar with the concept of inspection types from Chapter 2. If an inspection type is active, the system creates an inspection lot after a particular event, even if there is no inspection plan yet. This event can be a goods receipt for the goods movement for a purchase order or simply a manual inspection lot creation. When the system creates an inspection lot, it looks for the relevant task list usage that you’ve assigned in the inspection plan. You create a new task list usage to distinguish it from your regular inspection or standard task list usage available in the system.

docs.text: Defect Classes You may have different types of defect classes, such as critical or minor defects. Together with the quality score in a defect class, the system uses characteristic weighting to come up with an overall quality score of an inspection lot, which forms the basis of supplier evaluation. The system calculates the quality score based on the following equation: Quality score = Quality score in defect class × Characteristic weighting ÷ Sum total of all characteristic weightage Batch Valuation Without Material Spec.

docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 204 Catalogs In the context of quality planning and quality inspection, the term catalog refers to a collection of unique keys that describe a subject, both in the positive and the negative sense. A catalog is a group of codes that you normally use to categorize different aspects and activities of QM (and PM) and include defects, causes, tasks, actions, or usage decisions. An example of a catalog of defects can be defect codes, which contain all the possible defects of electrical or mechanical parts of the machinery.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the SAP S/4HANA system implementation project, designing the defect catalogs and other catalogs often takes significant time and effort because the existing catalog struc- tures in the enterprise have to be migrated to a schema that suits the QM area. There- fore, the most frequently occurring problem isn’t missing catalogs, but rather the sheer number of catalogs and the fact that problem descriptions often overlap. The better- suited and practical approach of classifying problem descriptions in catalogs according to defect location, defect type, and defect cause also often causes uncertainty with assigning the corresponding codes.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The following sections will discuss the various standard catalog types available in the SAP S/4HANA system. Although standard catalog types available are generally suffi- cient to meet most business needs, new catalog types can also be configured. Each cat- alog type has specific codes that are then used in the business processes. Further, each code within a catalog type provides an option to perform subsequent follow-on func- tions too. Catalog Types You can select the defaults for catalog types or add additional ones if there is a business need.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To view the available catalog types, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Manage- ment  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Catalog Types . Figure 3.90 shows the initial screen of catalog types. You must not change SAP catalog types 1–9. However, you can create new catalog types within the P–Z range. The following catalog types are available in the SAP S/4HANA system:  Catalog type 0: Action reasons This catalog type is specific defects recording wherein specific action can be assigned when a defect is first identified and recording.  Catalog type 1: Characteristic attributes This catalog type is specific to results recording and is for defining qualitative char- acteristics.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It has special importance in the catalog system. One reason for this is that you can maintain both OK and NOK definitions here; another is that you can only assess the catalog entries only via selected sets. If you’re using a rejected-defect class for supplier evaluation, you have to enter a defect class (major defect, minor defect, etc.). Rejecting defect classes are by nature the same as the defect types (defects) and are structured in the same way. If a qualitative characteristic has been created in the © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: Define Tolerance Key The tolerance key defines the tolerance range for the quantitative characteristic. When the results of an inspection characteristic fall within the tolerance key/range, it’s viewed as acceptable for the purpose of valuating the characteristic. To create or change a tolerance key, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Inspection Characteristic, Inspection Method  Define Tolerance Key. The screen that appears consists of a long list of industry-standard toler- ance keys that you can evaluate before proceeding to create new ones.

docs.text: 211 3.6 Configuration Basics: Quality Planning and Quality Inspection Figure 3.96 Tolerance Key Figure 3.97 Details of Tolerance Key A10 Define the Estimation Procedure for Fraction of Defects In this step, you can define your own procedure to estimate the percentage of defective material using the characteristic inspection results. The following are the fraction esti- mates: Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 212  Nonconforming units (with regard to a characteristic and in the inspection lot)  Characteristic values outside of the tolerance range The keys for the procedure are defined in the inspection characteristic. The system maintains fraction estimates for the following distributions:  Binomial distribution The system uses binomial distribution when there are exactly two mutually exclu- sive outcomes of a result. The outcome is either a success or a failure.  Poisson distribution The Poisson distribution uses the model of number of events occurring within a given time interval.  Normal distribution Mean and standard deviations are taken into account in a sample’s results.

Fur- ther, if you want to control automatic creation of inspection lots for any movement types, you can activate/deactivate them. Adapt Rules for Sample Determination If the standard sampling procedure doesn’t fulfill your company’s business needs, then you can assign additional or different rules by assigning a specific function module to the sample determination rule. Use the menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Sample, SPC  Define Sampling Determination  Adapt Rules for Sample Determination .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Define Valuation Mode Valuation mode enables the system to valuate inspection characteristics based on whether the mode of valuation will be manual or automatic and is for attributive (qual- itative) or variable (quantitative) characteristics. When you’re creating a sampling pro- cedure, you need to choose the relevant valuation mode that’s directly linked to the valuation rule. Let’s explain this with an example. Consider valuation mode 110 (Attr. Insp. Nonconforming Units/Manual) , which con- tains valuation rule 111 (Attr.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Insp. Nonconforming Units/Manual) . The combination of valuation mode 110 and valuation rule 11 means that the system decides to accept or reject an attributive (qualitative) characteristic based on how many of the inspected samples of an inspection characteristic fail. For example, say that the total number of samples inspected is 20 units, and you record 3 units as rejected due to defects or non- conformance. Whether that characteristic passes or fails depends on the formula used for valuation rule 11 or function module QEBR_NONCONFORM_UNIT_OR_MANUAL .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You’ve defined the actual number of samples allowed for pass or fail in the sampling proce- dure. In this specific case, though the system automatically valuates the characteristic as either accepted or rejected, it also provides an option for the user to manually valu- ate or overrule the automatic valuation. This option to perform manual valuation (despite the system’s automatic valuation) isn’t available if you use valuation rule 10. To summarize, a few valuation modes are valuation by number of defects, number of nonconforming units, or defect code, and they are for attributive or variable character- istics with the option of automatic, manual, or both valuation controls of an inspection characteristic.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Tips and Tricks If the characteristic is quantitative, then choose a valuation mode in the sampling pro- cedure as one of the variable types. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

In the screen that appears, choose Valuation Mode 100 . You’ll see a screen that shows valuation mode 100 for attributive (qualitative) inspec- tion by number of nonconforming (or number of defects) units, with valuation rule 10 assigned to valuation mode 100.

docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 216 If you have any unique business need to valuate a characteristic that’s not available in the standard system offering, then you can create a function module and assign it in this step. Statistical Process Control Organizations use the statistical process control as a tool to improve product quality by reducing process variations.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There are two sources of process variation:  Chance variation (later renamed to common cause variation ) that is inherent in the process, stable over time, and assignable  Uncontrolled variation (later renamed to special cause variation ), which is unstable over time—the result of specific events outside the system Control charts attempt to distinguish between these two types of process variation:  Common cause variation, which is intrinsic to the process and will always be present  Special cause variation, which stems from external sources, indicates that the pro- cess is out of statistical control, and needs evaluation on a case-by-case basis When you create an inspection characteristic, you select the SPC checkbox to let the sys- tem know that you’ll be monitoring this specific characteristic through the statistical process control.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In addition, remember to simultaneously select the Sampling Proce- dure checkbox; otherwise, the system deactivates the SPC checkbox that you previously selected. Later, when you assign this statistical process control characteristic to an inspection plan, the system prompts you to enter the sampling procedure, as well as the statistical process control criteria. To navigate to the statistical process control criteria settings, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Sampling, SPC  Statistical Process Control  Define SPC Criteria.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In Figure 3.101, you’ll find several combinations of task list characteristics that align with the material, supplier, customer, and even equip- ment or the functional location of PM. Choose SPC Crit. 0 10 1 , and the details appears on the screen on the right 2 . Usage is the option to select a specific task list to use the statistical process control cri- teria. In addition, the radio buttons enable selection of the assignment of the control chart either on every inspection lot or at every inspection point. Note See Chapter 19 on quality control to understand how to leverage statistical process control to improve your business processes. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 217 3.6 Configuration Basics: Quality Planning and Quality Inspection Figure 3.101 Statistical Process Control Criteria Define Control Chart Type Control charts are most commonly used in the production area. Your system comes with several preset sampling procedures for statistical process control inspection planning. To define your own statistical process control sampling procedure in the SAP S/4HANA system, proceed exactly as you would for the lot inspection. The sam- pling procedure input mask contains one extra attribute: the indicator for the inspec- tion point.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 218 interval—that is, whether the inspection is to be container-based, time-interval- based, or event-based. Define the following first:  Sample type Only a fixed sample is allowed.  Valuation mode Select the special valuation mode, statistical process control inspection. With this setting, valuations of samples or characteristics use the action limits of the quality control chart. A rejection occurs if the action limits are violated. If there aren’t yet enough measurement values to calculate an action limit, the procedure switches to manual calculation until the measured values are sufficient.  Control chart type You have to assign a control chart type for statistical process control sampling pro- cedures.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When you do so, the system checks whether the sampling procedure will use inspection points or independent multiple samples. With independent multiple samples, control chart types with samples are allowed; otherwise, control chart types without samples are allowed. In control charts with memory (moving average chart, mean-value chart, or moving- range chart), the control variable isn’t restricted to the current sample. These control chart tracks don’t support the statistical process control inspection valuation mode.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When defining the sample size, there are some quality aspects that you have to take into account. If you want to use the sample size n = 1, you should ensure the following:  There is no S track in the control chart you intend to use.  The overall dispersion, and not the internal dispersion, is used to calculate the pro- cess dispersion in the calculations for the action limits. The reason for this is that in samples with the size n = 1, the standard deviation is always 0. Tips and Tricks In statistical process control inspections with measured recording, sample sizes from 3 to 10 are normal, with n = 5 the most commonly used value.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For quantitative characteristics, the original values of which don’t have a normal distri- bution, you can select a larger sample size to use the central specification limit set of the statistics, whereby the distribution of the mean values is almost normal. You can then use Shewhart charts for the mean value, even if the distribution of the population isn’t normal. The more the distribution deviates from the norm, the greater the sample size should be. The statistical process control criteria determine the update process for the control chart and are controlled by function modules.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 219 3.6 Configuration Basics: Quality Planning and Quality Inspection chart (during results recording), this system checks whether a suitable chart already exists. The function modules are well documented and can be easily adapted to suit your own needs. It’s also a simple matter to create a control chart for a characteristic or supplier only.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The standard SAP system already contains the following function modules:  QRKS_CHARACTERISTIC : Control chart for characteristics  QRKS_INSPECTION_LOT : Control chart for characteristics or inspection lots  QRKS_MATERIAL : Control chart for characteristics or materials  QRKS_MATERIAL_CUSTOMER : Control chart for characteristics, materials, or customers  QRKS_MATERIAL_MANUFACTURER : Control chart for characteristics, materials, or manu- facturers  QRKS_MATERIAL_SOLD_TO_PARTY : Control chart for characteristics, materials, or sold- to parties  QRKS_MATERIAL_VENDOR : Control chart for characteristics, materials, or suppliers  QRKS_MATERIAL_WORK_CENTER : Control chart for characteristics, materials, or work centers  QRKS_PURCHASING_DOCUMENT : Control chart for characteristics or purchasing docu- ments  QRKS_SALES_ORDER : Control chart for characteristics or sales orders Statistical process control defines which charts are available, how you process them, and how you assign them to the processes.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To define or make changes to the control settings of a control chart, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Sampling, SPC  Statis- tical Process Control  Define Control Chart Type . docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA

Referring again to Figure 3.102, this time choose Control chart tracks on the left side, which leads to the screen in Figure 3.104. This screen shows the system-suggested upper and lower warning and action limits for numeric parameters. You can choose to optionally or always display these limits in the control chart. The system calculates and displays all limits, but after choosing the Change Control Limits checkbox (not shown, but will be visible when scrolled further down in Figure 3.104), you can also manually enter the control limits, and the system clearly identifies them too.

docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 220 After basic data is set up, you need to set up inspection planning data. Inspection plan- ning consists of two subcomponents: general (applies for all operations) and operation- specific. Quality inspection uses task list type Q. Quality inspection integrates with production-related task list types, such as routings, rate routings, and master recipes, or a reference operation set can also be used. docs.text: In QM, you configure and assign planner groups in task lists. Planner groups eventually help in reporting, when you want to see task list(s) of specific planner groups. To create a planner group, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Inspection Planning  General  Define Planner Group . Define an Identifier for Inspection Points You can define an identifier for inspection points for physical samples, partial lots in production, and maintenance objects (e.g., equipment or functional locations).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A con- figured identifier for the inspection point then needs to be filled with relevant informa- tion before you can record the results of an inspection lot or an inspection point. docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA

The inspection points available are as follows:  (blank): Freely defined inspection point  1: Inspection point for equipment  2: Inspection point for functional location  3: Inspection point for physical sample You can define up to six user fields, with the flexibility to define the user field’s text per the business need. For example, a user field can be titled “Shift” and have the field for- mat Number , and the field length is three numeric values.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On the Valuation tab, you can set the default options for valuating inspection points and assigning codes and code groups to facilitate the data entry efforts during results recording. On the Function modules tab, you can either use the preset or predefined function modules or assign your own custom-defined function module. Inspection-Characteristic Origin You can define a unique identifier to denote the origin of inspection characteristics so that when you use them in an inspection plan, you know the origin of the characteristic.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 224 For example, in Chapter 16 on FMEA and the control plan, you copy an inspection char- acteristic undergoing the FMEA process into an inspection plan. docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the resulting screen, you can define a numeric origin, together with the description of inspection-characteristic origin. Engineering Workbench The Engineering Workbench facilitates the modification or updating of a large number of QM master data and associated objects to save time and reduce the chances of data entry error. You can either create a new working area or modify the existing ones to meet your business needs. A working area makes available all the different fields and options that you’ll use while using the Engineering Workbench.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA

docs.text: 225 3.6 Configuration Basics: Quality Planning and Quality Inspection You can select various radio buttons and checkboxes to ensure that the system dis- plays only the relevant information while working in the Engineering Workbench. You can also set a lock in the Lock Automatically section at the relevant level (header or operation) to prevent anyone from making changes in the inspection plan while another user is working in the Engineering Workbench. Notice that you can activate Classification (see Chapter 9 on batch management, which also covers classification) and see the classes and their associated characteristics.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Object dependencies find greater usage when you’re using the variant configuration functionality or even the advanced classification functionality. When you complete an inspection lot after the completion of a physical inspection, you may or may not make the usage decision. You’re determining the quality valuation and updating the quality level. If you have links to a batch class, you can transfer inspection results to batch specifications. Based on the usage decision, the system can perform follow-up actions. Note that short-term and long-term inspection completion are two separate steps.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For short-term inspection, you need to enter the results before making the usage decision. For long-term inspection, you can enter the results even after the usage decision has been made for an inspection lot. 3.6.4 Quality Inspection You can set up catalogs for usage decisions based on your business needs. Catalog type 3 is for usage decisions. To implement any usage decisions, you need to first imple- ment a quality score procedure, follow-up actions, and inventory postings. This section covers these configuration steps.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Define Quality Score Procedure You can set a default value for determining a quality score in the inspection type. To do this, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot Completion  Define Quality Score Procedure . The screen that appears shows the available standard options. Chose Q-Score Procedure 01 to see the screen in Figure 3.108. Notice that a function module is assigned to under- take the necessary calculation for the quality score procedure. The Permitted Share of Scrap checkbox enables a certain percentage of defects to be considered during quality scores calculation.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA

Chars field provides an option to define whether the results of master inspection characteristics are considered for quality score calcula- tion, especially if the master inspection characteristics are closed and valuated. docs.text: 227 3.6 Configuration Basics: Quality Planning and Quality Inspection Define Inventory Postings As you know, while performing a usage decision, you need to perform two sets of activ- ities:  Assigning the usage decision code, based on which the system calculates quality scores  Actual posting of inspection stock (for stock-based inspection) The menu path to define inventory posting is SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot Completion  Define Inventory Postings . Define Parameters for Calculated Characteristics In this step, you can define the formula parameters for the input values of calculated characteristics.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can achieve this in the following two ways:  The formula parameters directly reference the fields in the input characteristics.  The formula parameters reference function modules, which calculate the values in the fields of the input characteristics. For example, to determine the difference between the mean values of two characteris- tics or samples, you need mean values for either characteristics or samples as input val- ues. Because these mean values are available in the characteristic record, you can give reference to the corresponding fields in the input characteristics.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: But to determine how many values for a quantitative characteristic are above a target value, you need a spe- cial function module that calculates this using a counting function. To define a parameter for a calculated characteristic, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Results Recording  Define Parameters for Calculated Characteristics . In the popup that appears, choose Define Parameters for Calculated Characteristic . A long list of standard parameters is available, and this is generally suffi- cient to cater to different business needs.

Once the system checks whether the entered value (result) is inside or outside of the predefined range of values (speci- fications), it valuates the result for acceptance or rejection.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 3 Quality Inspection 234 Note Screen fields and groups are found in several other submenus of the QM area, but the basics covered in this section remain the same. 3.7 Summary Quality inspection entails following a series of business processes that record complete inspection results, record defects, and make usage decisions that may or may not include stock posting. When these business processes begin to mature and stabilize, you can optimize some or all of them by automating them to reduce or eliminate redundant data entry.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Digital signature functionality brings greater business controls and transparency to business processes. Dynamic modification rules enable a com- pany to adjust quality levels based on the quality of products produced in house or materials delivered by suppliers. Multiple specifications functionality offers far greater flexibility in adapting to specific business needs of companies and span beyond a material’s customer or supplier assignment. The next chapter discusses how the QM functionality in SAP S/4HANA integrates with the materials management functionality. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 237 Chapter 4 Integrating with Materials Management Most of the QM features and functionalities that SAP S/4HANA delivers as standard offerings are sufficient for you to quickly and completely integrate QM with MM, and they don’t require much configuration. The key to successfully integrating quality management (QM) with materials manage- ment (MM) functionality depends on two elements: a well-planned setup of master data and exhaustive training of business process users. This chapter begins by conducting a quick check on configuration to ensure that the material type for which you need to activate QM is properly configured or is available.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The next configuration object is the QM control key, which controls several business functions. Then, the focus of this chapter shifts toward maintaining the minimum QM master data required to run the relevant business processes. Because the master data creation processes are already covered in Chapter 2, in this chapter, you’ll find either the QM master data checklist or specific details within the master data you need to run the business processes. Finally, this chapter will also provide an understanding of end-to-end business pro- cesses involving various business scenarios in procurement and inventory manage- ment (IM) within the MM area.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll also cover a new functionality, first article inspection for the production part approval process, which can be used as an alterna- tive to status-based inspection. shows various inspection types that find greater usage in procurement and inventory management processes and into which you can integrate QM. We’ll cover all these inspection types and their applications in this chapter. docs.text: 4 Integrating with Materials Management 238 4.1 Configuration Basics Let’s begin with a configuration check to ensure that the material type-related settings are in place in SAP S/4HANA so that you can successfully integrate QM with MM. 4.1.1 Material Type/Task List Combination If the company uses the standard material types, such as raw materials (ROH), finished goods (FERT), or trading goods (HAWA), then their task list types are available in the system. However, if any material type that you want to go through the quality inspec- tion and control process (e.g., spare parts [ERSA] or a company-specific material type) isn’t available, then you need to ensure that the combination of task list type Q with the material type exists in the system.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To do so, follow configuration menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  QM Planning  Inspection Planning  Assign Task List Type to Material Type . Choose New Entries , add the material type/task list type combination, and then save your entries. 4.1.2 Control Key for Quality Management in Procurement The QM control key plays a crucial role in meeting the business needs of a company. For example, using control keys in procurement, you can block supplier payments or all supplier activities until delivered goods clear the quality control process.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: After mak- ing the necessary configuration settings for the QM control key, you need to assign it in the QM view of the material master, which we’ll cover in Section 4.2.1. docs.text: 241 4.2 Procurement Business Processes Figure 4.2 First Article Inspection Plan Usage 4.2 Procurement Business Processes Let’s now delve into the various business processes of procurement and IM. Each sec- tion will provide an overview of the integrated QM and MM business processes, detail the master data checklist, and then provide more details. 4.2.1 Goods Receipt in Procurement: Inspection Type 01 Figure 4.3 shows a commonly used business process in which a standard procurement process integrates with QM. This process begins with creating a purchase order for a supplier to deliver the material.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As soon as the company records the goods receipt with reference to the purchase order, the system creates an inspection lot. Standard QM pro- cesses, such as results recording, occur, followed by usage decisions and stock posting. On quality clearance of goods, the supplier submits the invoice for payment. Figure 4.3 QM Integration into Procurement Process In the next sections, you’ll either set up the master data required for this business pro- cess or check that the relevant master data exists. Upon ensuring master data availabil- ity, you’ll see impacts of configuration and master data setup on business processes.

docs.text: 249 4.2 Procurement Business Processes 4.2.2 Source Inspection: Inspection Type 0101 Source inspection in QM ensures that the quality of procured goods is checked and approved for compliance before the supplier delivers the goods at the company’s ware- house. In source inspection, the supplier can then immediately deal with any defects in a product’s quality. The company can use this functionality to track when source inspec- tion needs to occur and carry it out. This saves the time that otherwise would be lost if the defective goods were delivered by the supplier and rejected (or asked to be reworked) by the company.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can quickly set up source inspection functionality to bring about sig- nificant overall process improvements and optimization to reduce the overall lead time incurred in ensuring that only quality goods are delivered by the supplier. You can implement source inspection at any time, even after an SAP S/4HANA system and the QM functionality are already implemented in a company. The option to inte- grate source inspection in the procurement process can be part of ongoing improve- ments and optimization in business processes in general and the procurement process in particular.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For source inspection, create a purchase order so that you can see the importance of the delivery date and how source inspection takes it into account. Then, create an inspection lot by manually triggering the source inspection program. Record the results and make a usage decision about the goods by rejecting them, so that on goods receipt from the supplier and against the same purchase order, the system creates a new inspection lot. All of these settings are the direct result of configuration settings that we made in QM Control Key (see Figure 4.12).

docs.text: 253 4.3 First Article Inspection for Production Part Approval Process The remaining QM business processes for source inspection are the same:  Record results for source inspection (Transaction QE01)  Usage decision (Transaction QA11) Invoice Receipt The business process of the invoice receipt is the same as we previously covered in Sec- tion 4.2.1. 4.3 First Article Inspection for Production Part Approval Process SAP has introduced first article inspection for the production part approval process to cater to the quality control and quality assurance needs of industries, such as automo- tive, aerospace, and so on to ensure comprehensive pre-inspection of underproduction products by a company.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It’s an alternate to pilot run inspection, which we’ll discuss in Section 4.4. A model inspection is used to identify and rectify quality issues beforehand prior to the production of remaining products. The first article inspection for the pro- duction part approval process is a new feature in SAP S/4HANA and can be easily set up as long as the necessary configuration, master data, and business processes are put in place that enable effectively reporting for timely and informed business decisions. Once the supplier has passed the quality process of first article inspection for the production part approval process for the material to be supplied to the company, then the regular quality inspection can take place.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As needed, first article inspection for the production part approval process can also be reinitiated to begin the reevaluation of a supplier. Figure 4.18 shows the end-to-end business processes for first article inspection for pro- duction part approval. In the business process, the first step is to make the relevant set- ting in the quality info record, which is relevant for first article approval for production part approval. This is then followed by the regular procure-to-pay process (purchase to goods receipt), and the goods receipt will generate an inspection lot of type 01 (goods receipt inspection for purchase order) associated to standard inspection plan usage 51 (goods receipt model inspection).

docs.text: 4 Integrating with Materials Management 258 Now that we’ve discussed the new feature, first article inspection for the production part approval process, let’s discuss a similar (and overlapping) feature of run pilot inspection in the next section. It’s important to note here that a company can only use one at a time: either first article inspection for the production part approval process or run pilot inspection business process (and not both). 4.4 Pilot Run Inspection: Inspection Type 0102 Before “upgrading” the status of a first-time or new supplier to that of a regular sup- plier, a company often has stringent and comprehensive procedures and processes in place to ensure that a new supplier is able to provide material of sufficient quality.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To achieve this objective, the company makes the supplier go through a series of trial runs or pilot runs of materials until the supplier is able to fulfill the quality requirements. Here, the SAP system can help by enabling the procurement and quality planners to put a series of checks and controls in place via status management. With each mate- rial’s delivery from the supplier, its corresponding inspection lot creation, results recording, and usage decision update the status (and controls) for the supplier. The following sections begin with discussing the necessary configuration settings that need to be in place for pilot run inspection so the same can then be assigned in the mas- ter data.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The master data is then used to discuss the business processes of pilot run inspection. 4.4.1 Configuration Basics Before we cover the configuration basics of the pilot run, see Figure 4.25, which shows the Status tab of the quality info record (Transaction QI01), in which we assigned Status Profile QM_P_001 . A status profile controls various business functions and whether they are allowed. A status profile is a cross-application component, so you can use it to control business functions not just in the QM area but also in other logistics and supply chain management areas.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 259 4.4 Pilot Run Inspection: Inspection Type 0102 In this example of a pilot run inspection, use status profile QM_P_001, which SAP delivers. Alternatively, you can amend an existing status profile or create a new one with menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality in Logistics  QM in Procure- ment  Define Status of Supply Relationships . Figure 4.26 shows the standard supplier relationship status profile QM_P_001 available in the system. Here, there are multiple statuses, and the initial status is 0001 ( Supply Relationship Initiated ).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The initial status is denoted by the checkbox selected in the Init. status column. The low and high numbers of the status control how the system changes from one status to another. Figure 4.26 Status Profile Figure 4.27 shows the assignment of different statuses of status profile QM_P_001 to inspection lots. To assign statuses to inspection types so that the system is able to fol- low the sequence in creating various inspection types, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality in Logistics  QM in Procurement  Maintain Inspection Lot Origins & Assign Inspection Types .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For this example, choose three different statuses of status profile QM_P_001, and cor- respondingly assign three different inspection types: 0101, 0102, and 01. When the sys- tem receives the material from the supplier and against the purchase order, it creates an inspection lot of inspection type 0101. This is because you assigned status 0002 to inspection type 0101, and this is the first status among the three statuses. On accepted usage decision for this inspection lot (and of inspection type 0101), the system auto- matically switches to the next status, which is 0003 (and correspondingly having inspection type 0102; look for the Next status column in Figure 4.27 to see how status change works).

Had it been a rejected inspection lot, the system would have maintained the previous status until acceptable results (and a usage deci- sion) were in place. 4.5 Subcontracting: Inspection Type 0130 The subcontracting process begins when the company hands over (issues) the compo- nents to a subcontractor, who is usually a supplier, against the subcontracting pur- chase order, to either assemble or add value to the product. The company takes the components’ inventory out of its books, and the same is reflected in the supplier’s inventory.

The supplier invoices the company for the services rendered and receives payment.

docs.text: 269 4.6 Inventory Management Processes 4.6.1 Stock Transfer Inspection: Inspection Type 08 Components procured or produced in one plant may be required for assembly or con- sumption in another plant, which requires a stock transfer. In the quality inspection business process of stock transfers, it’s possible to conduct a quality inspection process not just for interplant or plant-to-plant stock transfer but also for other inventory man- agement functions, such as for store-to-store stock transfer within the same plant and material-to-material stock transfer.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this example, we’ll cover interplant transfer posting—that is, plant-to-plant stock transfer using a stock transport order. For a stock transport order for interplant transfer, the following sequence of steps is involved: 1 Create a stock transport order that consists of supplying plant and receiving plant details, along with other materials and quantities. 2 Goods are issued from the supplying plant with reference to the stock transport order. These goods are shown as stock in transit. 3 Goods are received at the receiving plant with reference to the same stock transport order. 4 Upon goods receipt at the receiving plant, the system creates an inspection lot for interplant stock transfer.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 4.39 shows the end-to-end business process of a stock transport order and for stock transfer between two plants. For such business processes, SAP S/4HANA offers a standard inspection type to ensure that material received without reference to a purchase order still gets inspected.

docs.text: 275 4.7 Handling Inspection Stock at QM Activation: Inspection Type 0800 Figure 4.46 Inspection Lot of Inspection Type 05 4.7 Handling Inspection Stock at QM Activation: Inspection Type 0800 You can integrate QM even after implementation of SAP’s core business processes such as in areas of MM, SAP S/4HANA Sales, production planning (PP), finance, and con- trolling. Until then, the only limited option available to restrict a material’s free-to-use stock (aka unrestricted stock) is to transfer or receive the stock as quality inspection stock.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On quality clearance (out of SAP) from the quality department, the user performs the transfer posting of quality inspection stock to unrestricted-use stock by using Transaction MIGO and movement type 321. When the company implements QM and integrates it in logistics areas, the system requires that all stock placed in quality inspection within MM and not QM undergoes quality inspection again. This activity prevents inconsistencies between the stocks placed in quality inspection within MM and the stock that requires handling in QM.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To attend to this scenario of ensuring stock consistency upon integrating QM with logis- tics, SAP S/4HANA offers standard inspection type 0800. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 4 Integrating with Materials Management 276 However, to use inspection type 0800, you need to ensure that a single configuration setting is in place and then run its business process. Let’s first cover the configuration settings that you need to activate to use inspection type 0800. 4.7.1 Configuration Settings At the plant level, you need to assign inspection type 0800 to each of the plants in which you plan to integrate QM. For this example, use plant 1710, and assign inspection type 0800. To perform the necessary configuration setting, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Basic Settings  Maintain Settings at Plant Level .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA

Notice that the stock of material 2232 is in quality inspection stock. So far, we haven’t activated or implemented QM for this material (2232) in the system. The quality inspection stock of 100 PC that you see in Figure 4.47 is due to using the option available in MM at the time of receiving the material from the supplier.
