docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In Appendix A, you’ll find a selected list movement types and associated inspection origins. You can use that list to integrate QM into many more business processes of procurement and inventory management as deemed necessary to meet business needs. 4.8 Summary In this chapter, you’ve seen how standard configurations and functionalities offered by SAP are sufficient to integrate QM into procurement and inventory management pro- cesses. The QM master data plays a central role in the effective implementation of QM in the procurement and inventory management processes.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This one-time setup requires sig- nificant planning and concerted efforts, the importance of which can’t be overempha- sized. Apart from the routine procurement and inventory management processes in which you can integrate QM functionality, the SAP system also offers several options to man- age the complex and diverse businesses processes involved in the entire supply chain and logistics functions. Some of these are subcontracting, stock transfer, and goods receipt without reference to any procurement element, and you can integrate QM in all these business processes.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 281 Chapter 5 Integrating with Production Planning When a customer registers a product complaint, it’s far easier for the company to trace the origin of raw materials used in production when QM is an integral part of the production process. You have the option to integrate QM into several production processes as deemed applicable to the business requirements. Companies implementing QM are uniquely positioned to take advantage of various checks and balances on the quality of materials being produced. This ensures that there are no raw materials released to production until quality specifications have been adhered to and that no finished goods are dis- patched to the customer until they meet the quality standards set by the company.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: When defective goods are produced, quality issues not only affect the quality of the final goods produced but also result in loss of machine and man hours. Companies integrating QM in their production processes have access to a vast amount of data and information to help them make long-term decisions. This chapter begins by covering the configuration basics of setting up QM with produc- tion planning (PP). Then, the focus shifts to required QM master data and culminates in running the entire end-to-end business process of the production cycles.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As you’ve seen the master data creation processes extensively in Chapter 2, here we provide the QM master data checklist only to ensure that it’s available in the system. Table 5.1 describes the various inspection types used in production processes that can also be used in QM. We’ll cover all these inspection types and their applications in this chapter. Inspection Type Inspection Plan Usage Inspection Type Description 02 6 Goods issue inspection 03 1 In-process inspection for process order 04 5 Final inspection for goods receipt from produc- tion 13 1 In-process inspection for run schedule header Table 5.1 Inspection Types in Production Planning Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Integrating with Production Planning 282 Note The focus and examples of QM integration with PP in this chapter are on production planning for process industries (PP-PI). However, it’s important to note that the same configuration, master data, business process concepts, and fundamentals apply equally to the discrete manufacturing (shop floor control) production type. Where there is any difference, it will be specifically highlighted. 5.1 Configuration Basics The following sections discuss the configuration settings that you need to ensure are available in the system to integrate QM with PP. 5.1.1 Material Type/Task List Combination If the company uses the standard material types, such as raw materials (ROH), finished goods (FERT), or trading goods (HAWA), then their task list types are available in the system.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, if any material type that you want to go through the quality inspec- tion and control process (e.g., spare parts [ERSA] or company-specific material types) is not available, then you need to ensure that the combination of task list type Q and the material type exists in the system. To do so, follow configuration menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  QM Planning  Inspection Planning  Assign Task List Type to Material Type . Choose New Entries , add the material type/task list type combination, and save your entries. 5.1.2 Order Type-Dependent Plant Parameters Process order creation signals to the production department to start production of the material and to check the material’s quantity during various stages of production.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The process order quantity denotes the target or planned quantity for production. When the production department has actually produced some or all of the target/planned quantity, it proceeds to confirm this produced quantity in the SAP S/4HANA system. Although there are more PP-specific settings to enable the system to control different functions during process order creation, you make a single setting that is specific to QM. To set up order type-dependent plant parameters, use Transaction COR4 or follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Production Planning for Process Industries  Process Order  Master Data  Order  Define Order Type-Dependent Plant Parameters (see Figure 5.1).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 5.1 shows the Planning tab for plant 1710 and order type YBM2. Incorporate inspection type 03 to enable the system to perform in-process (during production) inspection of the material. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 283 5.1 Configuration Basics Figure 5.1 Order Type-Dependent Parameters Note In shop floor control (discrete manufacturing), you can use Transaction OPL8 to access Figure 5.1. This is an integration point between QM and PP. In Section 5.3.2, we’ll cover in-process inspection (inspection type 03). Tips and Tricks If you’ve configured any other inspection types of inspection origin 03, then these will also appear in the dropdown list for you to choose from. 5.1.3 Confirmation Parameters When you perform confirmation against a process order, whether it’s for an entire order or milestone confirmation, the system makes actual data updates of the yield, scrap, and rework objects.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Integrating with Production Planning 284 The confirmation process comprises the quantity produced at each phase of the pro- duction process. If there are quality checks and steps involved in the production pro- cess, then you can control whether the system adheres to the sequence of quality inspections with the configuration settings of confirmation parameters. Example After you mix paint, you want the quality inspector to inspect the mixed paint and record the results. Unless this step is ensured, the system shouldn’t allow the produc- tion person to confirm the next step of production.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Further, if you have another step in which the quality inspector must check for filled-up paint cans before they are packed and sealed, then you can control these sequences of steps via the confirmation param- eters’ control. To set up parameters for order confirmation, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Production Planning for Process Industries  Process Order  Operations  Confirmation  Define Confirmation Parameters . Figure 5.2 shows the parameters for the order confirmation for plant 1710 and order type YBM2.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To ensure that the system adheres to confirming various phases of process order and according to the defined sequence, set the operation sequence to E Error when operation sequence is not adhered to . We’ll show how it works in Section 5.3.1. Figure 5.2 QM-Specific Settings in Order Confirmation © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 285 5.1 Configuration Basics Similarly, set the Results Rec. (QM) to 1 Error message if no insp. results exist . This set- ting ensures that unless the quality inspection record results in an in-process inspec- tion, the system doesn’t allow confirmation of that specific phase. You’ll see how this setting works in Section 5.3.2. Note During the SAP S/4HANA system implementation project, you discuss, evaluate, and agree with the client on the level of controls required and then make the necessary set- tings. In general, the control should neither be too loose nor too stringent to compro- mise the day-to-day work of business process owners.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The level of control also depends on the stability of production and quality processes, as well as business maturity, for optimal production without comprising on quality controls. 5.1.4 Control Key With the relevant settings in the control key, you can control whether inspection char- acteristics are required or optional and whether the system is to undertake automatic goods receipt. Parameters also exist for scheduling, costing, and printing that are more relevant to PP than QM. Finally, you can also control how the system processes the con- firmations.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To set the required parameters of the control key, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Inspection Planning  Operation  Define Control Keys for Inspection Operations (see Figure 5.3). Figure 5.3 Control Key for Operations Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Integrating with Production Planning 286 Table 5.2 lists the details about the functions that occur when you enable any field by selecting the relevant checkbox. In general, there is no need to specifically configure control keys in QM; rather, you need to coordinate with a PP resource (or consultant) to enable you to integrate QM- related processes in production. We’ll show you how configuration settings made for control key QM04 apply in the business process for in-process quality inspection (inspection type 03).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In Section 5.2.2, you’ll see the actual use of a control key in a mas- ter recipe, and then in business processes. Print confirmation Enables the option to print a process order confirmation (the quantity produced in a shift). Det. Cap. Reqmnts Enables capacity requirements planning in the production process. Print Enables printing of shop floor papers. Insp. Char. Required Requires that a master inspection characteristic be assigned to a rout- ing or master recipe.

docs.text: External Processing Option to allow or disallow external processing of operations for a process order. Confirmations Dropdown option to allow or disallow confirmation of operations. If you want the system to adhere to an operation’s sequence during con- firmation, then you need to choose 2 Confirmation required . If you’re using PP-PI, then the same principle applies to the phases’ confirma- tion (instead of the operations’ confirmation, which applies to shop floor control). Table 5.2 Control Key Parameters © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 287 5.2 Master Data Tips and Tricks To ensure that you can incorporate master inspection characteristics for in-process inspection (during production), select the Insp. Char. Required checkbox. 5.2 Master Data Although significant master data pertaining to PP is managed by the PP team, the focus of this section is to show where, specifically, QM integrates with PP.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: During the SAP S/4HANA implementation project, QM consultants (or business users) coordinate with the PP team to incorporate the required QM master data (e.g., inspection charac- teristics) into the PP master data (e.g., master recipe or routing). 5.2.1 Production Planning and Quality Management Master Data Checklist The following is the PP master data that you need to ensure is available in the system:  Material master  Bill of materials (BOM)  Master recipe, rate routing, or routing  Production version The QM master data that you need in the system is as follows:  Inspection types 03 and 04 active in the QM view of the material master of the fin- ished good  Inspection type 02 active in the QM view of the material master of the raw material or semifinished good  Inspection plan usage 5 (for inspection type 04) and 6 (for inspection type 02), both with status 4 (for released)  No inspection plan needed for inspection type 03 5.2.2 QM Data in Master Recipe A master recipe uses something called a phase , which works in the same manner as operations do in routing for discrete manufacturing.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It’s easier to maintain detailed levels working at the phase level in the master recipe because you can manage and incorporate more production and quality details. In the master recipe, you assign activities such as production duration or labor hours at the phase level and not at the operation level. Therefore, the confirmation of a process order is recorded for a phase and not an operation. You also assign a resource (work Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 5 Integrating with Production Planning 288 center) at the operation level. The phases below the operation then adopt the resource that you assign at the operation level. The system assigns the standard values and activities (controlled by a control key in the resource) as active at the phase level and not at the operation level. You can, however, integrate in-process quality inspections of QM at either the operation level or the phase level. Tips and Tricks For process manufacturing, we suggest that you integrate QM with PP at the phase level because it offers better controls and visibility, which we’ll show in this chapter.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For discrete manufacturing, QM integration with PP for in-process inspection takes place at an operation level. To create a master recipe for which the production version already exists, use Transac- tion C201 or follow menu path Logistics  Production—Process  Master Data  Master Recipes  Recipe and Material List  Create . On the initial screen of the master recipe, enter Material “SG2200”, Plant “1710”, and Production Version “0001”, and the header screen appears. Figure 5.4 shows the Operations tab of the master recipe, in which the operation is 0010.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Enter the Resource “QCLAB” at the operation level, and the system automatically copies it into all the phases below it. The system denotes phase 0040 by the Phase checkbox. When you define an operation as a phase, you also have to define the supe- rior operation, which, for this example, is 0030 (the operation). Operation 0010 and phase 0020 refer to the production process of filling (not shown), but it’s operation 0030 and phase 0040 (the superior operation of which is 0030) that are relevant to QM. Notice the control key QM04, the settings of which you previously made in Section 5.1.4.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system should adhere to the sequence of operations (essentially the same as phases in PP-PI) during confirmation; therefore, you must first confirm phase 0020, then phase 0040, and so on. If you deviate from or miss the phases’ confirmation sequence, the system displays an error message and doesn’t allow you to proceed fur- ther. Similarly, if you don’t record the results of phases 0020 and 0040, the system doesn’t allow you to confirm the respective phases. Because this is an in-process inspection, you also need to enter the master inspection characteristics that then form the basis of your results recording and usage decision.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To enter master inspection characteristics, choose a relevant phase, such as 0040 , and choose Inspection Characteristic , and the system brings up the screen shown in Figure 5.5. Here, you can enter the QM data elements, such as master inspection characteris- tics, maintain their values as shown in Figure 5.4, and save your settings. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 289 5.2 Master Data Figure 5.4 Master Recipe Figure 5.5 Quality Data in Master Recipe Tips and Tricks For the system to ensure it adheres to the defined phases during the confirmation pro- cess, you must maintain a predecessor-successor relationship between any two phases. To maintain the relationship of one phase to another, select the desired phase (e.g., phase 0040 ), and choose the Relationship icon (the chain link icon) shown in Figure 5.4. Once on the detailed screen of a phase relationship of phase 0040, enter the predecessor phase, which in this example is “0020”; here the relationship type needs to be “FS” (finish-start), which means that phase 0020 needs to finish before phase 0040 can start.

docs.text: 309 Chapter 6 Integrating with SAP S/4HANA Sales QM integration with SAP S/4HANA Sales brings far greater visibility to the logistics, operations, and supply chain management processes. Integrating QM with SAP S/4HANA Sales helps organizations ensure that only accept- able and approved products eventually reach the customer. Organizations may also have requirements that the customer inspect the product before or after a product’s delivery. This chapter begins by covering the configuration basics of setting up QM with SAP S/4HANA Sales.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Then, the focus shifts to required QM master data before culminating in running the entire end-to-end business process of various sales cycles. Because you’ve seen master data creation processes extensively in Chapter 2, here we provide the SAP S/4HANA Sales and QM master data checklist just for you to make sure that it’s available in the system.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Table 6.1 consists of various inspection types that find greater usage in sales processes and into which you can integrate the QM area. 6.1 Configuration Basics The following are the configuration settings that you need to ensure are available:  Assignment of inspection lot origin to delivery type  Assignment of inspection type to delivery category Inspection Type Inspection Plan Usage Inspection Type Description 06 6 Inspection for customer returns 10 6 Inspection for delivery to customer (with order) 11 6 Inspection for delivery to customer (without order) 12 6 General inspection for delivery Table 6.1 Inspection Types in SAP S/4HANA Sales Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 323 Chapter 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance When integrating QM in the logistics and supply chain management processes, you need to take great care with test equipment that you use to conduct various quality tests. You can broaden the QM scope by inte- grating test equipment management into the business functions of plant maintenance. Building on the functions of plant maintenance (PM) and quality management (QM), SAP S/4HANA provides integrated test equipment management that combines important planning and processing functions of PM and QM.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You should therefore view the combination of the planning and processing functions not as a separate area, but as an operating interface that combines the appropriate functions of the different areas for test equipment management and monitoring to facilitate business users meeting their business needs. It’s essential that all quality inspections and quality tests be undertaken using reliable test equipment and measuring devices that give accurate results. For this reason, test equipment management and its calibration are of paramount importance.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Equipment or functional locations are defined as PM master data. A piece of equipment can be a boiler, a condenser, or a chiller, while a functional location can be a utility room or chiller room of a manufacturing plant. The steps to integrate QM with any of PM’s equipment or functional locations are the same that we show for test equipment man- agement in this chapter. Test equipment can be specific laboratory equipment such as a weighing scale that is used to conduct physical or chemical quality tests of materials.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Note In this chapter, we’ll describe the functionality of PM in sufficient detail for the pur- poses of test equipment management; however, we can’t cover every possible busi- ness scenario. We’ll restrict the scope of this chapter to typical and routine business processes that use PM, QM, and materials management (MM). Due to the integrated nature of QM with other areas, it’s always best to coordinate with experts or consul- tants of other SAP areas to ensure meeting end-to-end business scenarios of a client where SAP S/4HANA is being implemented.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The business process requires that you fulfill the requirements of managing the monitoring of test equipment according to relevant quality standards. To do this, the Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 324 monitoring and test equipment (referred to as test equipment in the rest of this chap- ter) requires that you maintain detailed data on device type, usage site, inspection frequency, inspection method, and acceptance criteria, as well as measures to take in case of unsatisfactory results. In addition, the business requirement is to list, evalu- ate, and make available the inspection results for the test equipment. The SAP system can meet the standard requirements. Note Given its very high importance in ensuring business continuity, you’ll find test equip- ment management in SAP via menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Test Equip- ment Management .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll start this chapter with the factors that you need to consider to help you decide which SAP S/4HANA system areas you need to implement to map the business pro- cesses of PM. Next, we’ll cover the configuration basics of the serial number profile that you’ll need for equipment, and then delve into covering the important master data required to run the business processes. We’ll also cover the business processes of QM integration with PM and will also discuss some PM reports available in the system.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Finally, we’ll also discuss an end-to-end setup to successfully create an inspection checklist, which is a new functionality available in SAP S/4HANA 2023. 7.1 Deciding which Functionalities to Implement As already mentioned, apart from the central role that the QM plays, two other areas of SAP S/4HANA that contribute significantly to test equipment management business processes are PM and MM. Figure 7.1 shows the four possible business scenarios in which you need to decide on integrating PM, MM, both, or neither to meet business needs.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ll evaluate all four possible business scenarios in the following sections. Figure 7.1 Possible Scenarios to Handle Test Equipment Management PM MM PM MM PM MM PM MM Test Equipment Management x x x x © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 325 7.2 Defining Test Equipment 7.1.1 Scenario 1: PM without MM In PM, you maintain test equipment as a piece of equipment, hierarchically structured and assigned to a detailed maintenance plan. This makes it possible to monitor inspec- tion dates and to create and process maintenance plan orders (e.g., for calibration). With this option, you create and manage pieces of equipment independently of mate- rial master data. Because equipment in PM isn’t stock-relevant, business functions of MM, such as purchase requisition, purchase order, goods receipt, invoice receipt, and inventory management (storage of equipment), aren’t in scope. 7.1.2 Scenario 2: PM with MM Implementing this business scenario is the most workload-intensive, but its enormous benefit is that it enables extensive visibility and availability of information across the logistics and supply chain management.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this chapter, we’ll be covering this business scenario so that you have the maximum available information to help you decide whether it’s worth the time and effort to integrate QM with both PM and MM or just with one. Because MM is also in scope, the business user can procure and store the test equipment. Moreover, it’s also possible to serialize and manage as a piece of equip- ment. This is also the option to synchronize the material master, equipment master, and serial number. 7.1.3 Scenario 3: MM without PM With this business scenario, you create test equipment as the material master and pro- cess all management of purchase requisitions, purchase orders, and goods receipt.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Fur- thermore, the materials that you create also integrate with the different task list types in the same way as the production resources/tools (PRTs). This business scenario doesn’t include any of the PM business processes, such as calibration planning, calibra- tion monitoring, and their documentation. 7.1.4 Scenario 4: Neither MM nor PM This business scenario has only a restricted management of test equipment as a PRT or a document master record. Ultimately, it’s available as the where-used list in QM.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There is no calibration planning, execution, or documentation or information availability in the SAP system, nor does it go through the procurement process available in MM. 7.2 Defining Test Equipment In quality planning, you can manage test equipment as a PRT, which you can define in the SAP system by using different types of master records: Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 326  Material master record  Equipment master record  PRT master record  Document master record Let’s briefly review each of these available options. 7.2.1 Test Equipment as a Material If you need logistics functions, such as procurement, storage, or quality inspection, then it makes sense to represent test equipment in the material master records. This provides all the views of the material master record. The material merely defines the type of test equipment. This is sufficient for processing purchasing and planning oper- ations (task lists, inspection plans, etc.) because the individual pieces of test equipment of a given type usually have the same properties and are therefore interchangeable.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For IM, the individual pieces of test equipment aren’t relevant; rather, it’s the number of pieces of test equipment that is important. With the option for serializing materials, the system also provides the option to repre- sent individual pieces of test equipment. In this case, the material itself corresponds to a particular configuration for test equipment, and the serial number represents the individual test equipment. 7.2.2 Test Equipment as PM Equipment A significantly higher range of functionality is available if you represent the test equip- ment as equipment in PM.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Equipment master records are maintained in PM and allow you to define individual devices and structure them hierarchically. This means that you can represent both individual test equipment and combined test equipment or more complex measuring tools. PM provides comprehensive functions for managing, monitoring, maintaining, and calibrating the test equipment. When pieces of equip- ment are included in task lists, you can check whether all the relevant test equipment is available when production lots are issued. When material numbers are serialized, the system provides an option for defining and linking both master records (material master and equipment master) in one process.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: First, you enter the material number or select an existing number. Then, you generate a new serial number using the serialization function. In the subsequent dialog box, you can then switch to the equipment view, activate the equipment master record, and add device-specific data. You can generate reports such as results history, graphical trend analyses, and usage lists. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 327 7.3 Configuration Basics 7.2.3 Test Equipment as a Production Resource/Tool Creating test equipment as a PRT enables you to store information about its status and location, as well as the standard SAP system management data. You can also group the test equipment (e.g., measurement equipment, inspection equipment, etc.) or classify it using the central classification system. The master record for PRT doesn’t contain a great deal of data, which greatly restricts the related functionality in the SAP system. In most cases, when you represent test equipment as a PRT, you maintain only rough master data, while the system doesn’t support other logistics functions either.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For this reason, representing test equipment as a PRT is the simplest option and doesn’t allow any additional functionality beyond providing a where-used list. 7.2.4 Test Equipment as a Document You can use the PRT master record to refer to document data, or you can directly use the document master records in task lists and inspection plans as a PRT. The interfaces and functions in document management enable direct access to drawings and other documents. The representation of test equipment in document records or the inclusion of docu- ment records in the other types of PRTs makes it possible to use test equipment in terms of documents (e.g., drawings, descriptions, etc.).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This method is also used primar- ily for planning and documentation of test equipment usage. It’s characterized by spe- cial document management functions. Due to the many alternatives for representing test equipment in the SAP S/4HANA sys- tem, we suggest that you evaluate every option very carefully on the requirements that test equipment management should satisfy. 7.3 Configuration Basics In this section, we’ll cover the minimal configuration steps that you need to integrate QM with test equipment in PM. Apart from the QM configuration steps that you have to perform separately at various levels, these configuration steps will help you if you need to generate QM inspection lots while creating and releasing PM orders.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For this, the first configuration step is to assign the inspection type with the PM inspec- tion origin. Each piece of test equipment also has a unique serial number that you use to identify one from another, and you can maintain control of a piece of equipment’s serial number usage and identification in business processes. If your business process requires the system to create an inspection lot for a functional location, then you need to perform only the first configuration step. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 328 7.3.1 Inspection Type Assignment to PM Order Type To integrate QM with PM so that you can calibrate test equipment using a PM order, you need to assign inspection type 14 to the relevant PM order and plant combination. Inspection type 14 of inspection origin 14 (plant maintenance) is specific to handling QM’s integration with PM and is available as a standard offering in the SAP system. To assign any configured, specific inspection type of inspection origin 14, use standard inspection type 14 via menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot Creation  Define Inspections in Plant Maintenance (see Figure 7.2).

docs.text: 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 336 Figure 7.10 Material, Equipment, and Serial Number Synchronization Tips and Tricks Depending on how deeply you want to go to integrate equipment calibration of PM with QM, you can also integrate Measuring Points/Counters for test equipment. A measuring point is the identifier that you use to measure a piece of equipment’s char- acteristic. This identifier can be, for example, a sensory test, and it maintains its value at 100. So, after every 100 sensory tests, the sensory test equipment is due for calibra- tion.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: With measuring documents, you maintain the actual number of sensory tests that this equipment performed. A sensory test is one of the tests (others are aroma and taste) found often in the food industry to measure consumers’ reaction to under- development or under-trial products. Measuring points also use classification. 7.4.5 General Task List The SAP S/4HANA system provides two tools for planning test equipment monitoring. First, it provides the maintenance plan that specifies when and how frequently you should calibrate test equipment.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 337 7.4 Test Equipment Master Data You need to assign a unique maintenance plan and general task list to every piece of test equipment. Theoretically, you can assign a common maintenance plan to several pieces of equipment if they all have exactly the same maintenance date. In this exam- ple, however, we create a separate maintenance plan for every piece of equipment. In the same way, you can assign separate general task lists to every piece of equipment. In this example, we create a shared task list named equipment calibration tasks .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You first need to create a general task list. This is a type of routing that business users use to perform maintenance and calibration tasks. In some places in the SAP S/4HANA system, the term task list or PM task list is used. In this section, we provide only limited information on the required entries. You can create operations for the individual work steps, assign workstations and PRTs to the operations, schedule setup times and work times, and enter corresponding costs. Assume that one general task list suffices for all equipment, which you can then assign to all maintenance plans from the very beginning.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Also assume that there is only one central calibration point with one workstation. Costs are entered at a flat rate through cost center accounting and aren’t dependent on calibration duration. This configura- tion provides you with a relatively easy-to-implement scenario, which you can still enhance and adapt to changing requirements at any time after a productive start. To create a general task list, use Transaction IA05 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Test Equipment Management  Calibration Planning  Maintenance Task List  General Task List  Create .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On the initial screen, you don’t have to enter any infor- mation. The system automatically assigns a group number and a group counter. In this example, it’s group 40, and the group counter is 1. You can also assign an external group number if there is any such business need. Similarly, you can enter a key date if you want the task list to be effective from any specific date. If you don’t enter any date, the system incorporates the date of general task list creation as the key date (or effec- tive date). Press (Enter) , and the screen in Figure 7.11 appears, which is the header of the general task list.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Enter the task list name “Equipment Calibration Tasks” and fill out the other manda- tory fields, such as Overall Status as 4 ( Released ) and Usage also as 4 ( Plant Mainte- nance ). You can also assign a maintenance strategy that applies to all the equipment to which this task list is assigned. Any information that you enter on this screen applies to the entire task list. For example, entering Work Center “RES-0100” and Plant “1710” automatically copies to all operations of the task list. In the QM Data area, assign Inspection Points as 300 , as the system will refer to it during results recording for inspection lot.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA

docs.text: 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 340 Tips and Tricks If you need to create a task list that is specific to a piece of equipment, then you can use Transaction IA01 to create an equipment task list. The principles and fundamentals that apply to general task lists also apply to equipment task lists, with the difference that an equipment task list is specific to individual pieces of equipment only. 7.4.6 Maintenance Plan The purpose of a maintenance plan is to plan maintenance deadlines and cycles for cal- ibration.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Although this example uses time-dependent planning, the system also sup- ports activity-specific planning (e.g., calibration after 300 uses) or a combination of both (e.g., check after every three months or 300 uses). In addition, you can assign order specifications or maintenance strategies. The type of activity is defined using a reference in the maintenance plan to the corresponding task list. A prerequisite for cre- ating the maintenance plan is that you’ve already created the test equipment that you want to calibrate with this maintenance plan, as well as the corresponding general task list.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To create a maintenance plan, use Transaction IP41 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Calibration Planning  Maintenance Planning  Maintenance Plan  Cre- ate Single Cycle Plan . On the screen that appears, for Maintenance Plan Category , choose Maintenance Order . This means that you want the system to create the PM order (the calibration order) each time the test equipment’s calibration is due. Other options available are inspection lot creation for stability study, physical samples, PM notification, and even service orders for the services that the supplier provides.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the Maintenance plan cycle tab, enter the cycle (frequency) of the calibration inter- val. This value denotes the frequency with which you need to conduct equipment cali- bration. Typical values can be three months, six months, or one year. In the screen in Figure 7.14, enter “365 DAY”. Scroll down so that the screen in Figure 7.15 appears. In the Reference object area of Figure 7.15, enter the serial and material numbers for the test equipment in the respective fields. Then, fill out the Task List area with the infor- mation shown.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This is where you create the link between this maintenance plan and the general task list. If you know the task list type, plan group number, and plan group counter for your general task list, then you can enter them directly in the respective fields. Otherwise, you can search for the general task list using the binoculars icon in the application toolbar and copy the data. In this case, look at Task List Typ A (task list). You’ve already entered task list type A (general), so enter “40” in Task LstGrp . If you entered the data completely and correctly in the equipment and if the necessary settings are in place, the system automatically copies the available data to the Planning Data area, and you don’t have to make any more entries.

(release) Immediately indicator, the system doesn’t release the cali- bration order on its creation. Putting this control in place can help business users if there is a need to evaluate the system-created calibration orders before releasing them for further processing or action. Figure 7.14 Maintenance Plan Figure 7.15 Planning Details in Maintenance Plan Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 342 Lastly, you need to set the scheduling parameters. Refer to the Maintenance plan scheduling parameters tab in the maintenance plan header (see Figure 7.16). Figure 7.16 Scheduling Parameters of the Maintenance Plan You can change the testing schedule of maintenance planning. This may be the case when there is a need to change the testing frequency of calibration equipment. You can also use this option to enter any missing or incomplete information in the mainte- nance plan. Tips and Tricks You can also use Transaction IP02 to directly make changes to the maintenance plan.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Enter maintenance plan “151” on the initial screen, and press (Enter) , and you’re taken to the screen in Figure 7.16. Figure 7.16 shows the screen where you can define when the system should include test equipment requiring calibration in the worklist and when the next cycle for calibration should start again. For example, the worklist can contain upcoming calibrations that are due four weeks before the deadline. A call horizon, defined as a percentage, enables the business process owner to control when the system creates a call object on its planned or due date.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, a 0% call horizon means that as soon as the planned or due date of the call object (which, in this case, is a calibration order) occurs, the system immediately creates the calibration order. Similarly, a 90% call horizon means the system will call the object on a time horizon of 90% from the date of the next planned inspection lot creation. Other available options are how the system should respond when there are deviations between planned and actual tasks. You can define not only the tolerance for early or late completion in © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 343 7.4 Test Equipment Master Data percentages, but also how much (as a percentage) the system should shift in dates when it finds deviations between planned and actual tasks. Save your entries, and the system creates maintenance plan 151. Note For the example in Figure 7.16, Scheduling period is set to one day. In a real-life busi- ness scenario, you need to evaluate how frequently, such as monthly or after every six months, the system should schedule and then create calibration orders for equipment. 7.4.7 Schedule Maintenance Plan To start automatic monitoring of calibration deadlines, scheduling must begin after you create test equipment and its maintenance plan.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To schedule a maintenance plan, use Transaction IP10 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Calibration Plan- ning  Maintenance Planning  Maintenance Plan  Scheduling . On the initial screen, enter maintenance plan “151”, which you created in the previous step, and press (Enter) , and the screen in Figure 7.17 appears. Choose the Start button, and the system opens a pop-up that defines the date from which you want the system to schedule the maintenance plan. Choose Yes to confirm the start of maintenance plan scheduling, and then enter the date for the system to start the planning cycle.

When the system asks for the date (in a Manual Call popup), enter today’s date. Save your entries, and check for the newly created calibration order using Transaction IW33, which should have the latest/ last created calibration order number.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We’ve put this manual call option to use, which you’ll see in Section 7.5.1. 7.4.8 Deadline Monitoring For deadline monitoring of maintenance plans, you need to manually trigger schedul- ing monitoring in the system. Maintenance plans apply to calibration orders, as well as to other objects in which they integrate with PM; the details that we cover here remain the same. To set up deadline monitoring for a maintenance plan, use Transaction IP30 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Calibration Planning  Maintenance Planning  Maintenance Plan  Deadline Monitoring .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 346 7.5 Business Processes in Test Equipment Management The example in this chapter stipulates that the system automatically create a calibra- tion order of order type YBA2, according to maintenance plan 151. Further, the neces- sary configuration settings will also ensure that the system automatically creates an inspection lot of inspection type 14 on release and on saving the calibration order. Before we get into that process, we’ll also cover the business scenario in which a busi- ness user needs to inform the maintenance personnel of faulty or defective test equip- ment.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 7.21 shows that a business user can also create a maintenance request (a PM noti- fication in the system by using Transaction IW26) to communicate the need to perform equipment calibration. The business user may also create a PM notification due to equipment malfunction by using Transaction IW24. All of these scenarios apply when there is an actual and practical need to calibrate the test equipment instead of waiting for the system to create calibration orders according to the maintenance plan. Figure 7.21 Business Processes in Test Equipment Management The maintenance planner can evaluate the PM notification to see if there is a need to convert it to a PM order.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If so, the maintenance planner can use the PM order creation option available right in the PM notification creation screen. Alternately, using Trans- action IW34 enables the maintenance planner to reference the PM notification while creating a PM order, which is basically converting a PM notification into a PM order. On release and on saving the PM order, the system automatically creates the QM inspec- tion lot of inspection type 14. Maintenance engineers can then approach the ware- house to issue the components or spare parts required for equipment maintenance.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The next quality steps entail recording results and making a usage decision. If PM is to further integrate with QM, then the business user can perform confirmation of opera- tions (tasks) performed with Transaction IW31. Finally, the business process ends with completion of the PM order—both technical and business completion. Note There is a great similarity of functions and functionality between PM notification cre- ation and that of QM notification. If there’s a business need to create a PM notification before converting it into a PM order, then refer to Chapter 12 on quality notification.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Let’s detail our example in the following sections. PM notification PM order (calibration order) Components goods issuance QM inspection lot (Insp. type 14) Results recording and usage decision PM order confirmation PM order completion © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 347 7.5 Business Processes in Test Equipment Management 7.5.1 Calibration Order Via Transaction IW33, Figure 7.22 shows display calibration order 4000840 for equip- ment 10002974. We used the Manual Call option shown earlier in Figure 7.17, which enables the system to create this PM order through maintenance plan 151 and mainte- nance item 381 automatically. Figure 7.22 Calibration Order for Equipment Notice that the order type is YBA2, and the system automatically released it on its cre- ation. The system denotes the released status of the PM order with REL .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Further, the sys- tem also automatically creates an inspection lot for this PM order and denotes it with the status ILAS . Tips and Tricks If the system doesn’t automatically trigger inspection lot creation, you can do so manu- ally. While in the change PM order screen (Transaction IW32), navigate to Order  Func- tions  Inspection Lot  Create Inspection Lot . Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 349 7.5 Business Processes in Test Equipment Management Figure 7.24 Inspection Lot of Inspection Type 14 7.5.3 Results Recording The advantage of entering results and a usage decision in the SAP S/4HANA system is that this provides complete information visibility for the inspection in the same sys- tem. If you’ve made the necessary settings in the system, you can skip one or both activities of results recording or usage decision. This makes it possible to proceed directly from order release and inspection to inspection completion.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The list is filled auto- matically by the periodic batch program for scheduling monitoring. The list is pro- cessed manually. docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 351 7.5 Business Processes in Test Equipment Management To start calibrating the test equipment, you first need to select the required line and release the order using the Release Order function. This creates an inspection lot with all the data required for calibration inspection. At the same time, the status of the order is changed to In Process . You can also automate this manual release step with the right configuration settings. 7.5.5 Calibration Orders Completion As soon as calibration of the test equipment is complete, you select all the pieces of test equipment that have the status In Process .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Referring once again to the list that you cre- ated using Transaction IW38 (Section 7.5.4), you use menu path Order  Functions  Com- plete (Technically) to inform the system that you’ve completed calibration of the selected test equipment. To fully complete the calibration order, however, you also need to complete it in business terms through menu path Order  Functions  Complete (Business) . Now the calibration order is fully completed for the SAP system, and the next planning cycle starts. Tips and Tricks If the calibration operation takes a longer (e.g., after being sent to an external calibra- tion station), you must remember to also set the user status accordingly in the equip- ment view of the serialized material.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Don’t confuse the status of the PM order with the user status of the equipment. 7.5.6 Evaluations As in in all applications, real-time reports and standard or flexible analyses are avail- able for test equipment management. There can be any number of required evalua- tions: for example, total number of pieces of test equipment; where-used lists for test equipment for specific departments, individuals, or warehouses; calibration costs; number of calibration orders; and reported errors. With the results history, you can dis- play changes to specific characteristics of a piece of test equipment across defined peri- ods.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can also display these changes in a run chart. You can use the evaluation options for the standard configuration of the SAP S/4HANA system to cover most business requirements. Consider the cost-center-specific usage list. This may be of interest to managers who want to identify test equipment in certain locations within their own cost centers. If you want to identify the location of specific test equipment within your own cost center, start with Transaction IQ09 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Logistics Master Data  Serial Numbers  List  Display .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system dis- plays a list selection screen for serial number selection (the same as in other applica- tions), in which you can select according to many criteria. In this example, you want to Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance 352 select test equipment within the cost center, so you fill out the Plant , Maintenance Plant , and Cost Center fields with the required values. Although Plant and Maintenance Plant aren’t mandatory fields, restricting the search scope (in this case to the plant) when dealing with large data stocks and several locations can significantly reduce the search time. Note See Chapter 18 for evaluation and reporting in the SAP S/4HANA system. 7.6 Inspection Checklists: Inspection Type 8916 While the PM-QM integration has generally been used as a workaround to manage rou- tine or periodic inspections of technical objects (equipment or functional locations), SAP has introduced the inspection checklist functionality to process this critical main- tenance process of results recording in the system in the form of a checklist.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Depending on the configuration settings, the system can even trigger follow-on activities, such as creating notifications for prompt and timely maintenance. Inspection checklist is again a PM-QM integration process, and SAP has introduced a new inspection type, 8914, as well. Further, standard configuration is already predeliv- ered that can either be used right away or can be used as a reference to create different checklists. Apart from results recording and usage decisions undertaken by the maintenance team, another alternate is using the mobile solution from SAP called SAP Service and Asset Manager , which is intuitive and more user friendly than using the SAP Fiori and SAP GUI options available in the SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The following sections cover the configuration and other prerequisites that need to be in place for an inspection list, followed by setting up the required master data. This is then followed by discussing the end-to-end business process of the automatic creation of an inspection checklist when a maintenance order is released. 7.6.1 Configuration Basics and Other Prerequisites We’ll need to first activate a business function followed by assigning two business roles to the business user so that the necessary option to configure and implement inspec- tion checklists is available, as follows: 1.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Activate the business function LOG_EAM_CHECKLIST using Transaction SFW5. 2. Assign the business roles SAP_BR_MAINTENANCE_PLANNER and SAP_BR_QUALITY_PLANNER to your business user. 3. To check or make changes to the already available plant-order type combination for the inspection checklist, use menu path SAP IMG  Plant Maintenance and Customer © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 353 7.6 Inspection Checklists: Inspection Type 8916 Service  Maintenance and Service Processing  Maintenance and Service Orders  Functions and Settings for Order Types  Configure Checklists for Maintenance Order Types . 4. Figure 7.27 shows the Plant 1710 and Order Type PM07 combination in which the Inspection Type 8914 is assigned. Be sure to select all checkboxes so that the system is able to automatically generate a checklist on order release, which we’ll show later in this section. You can use already-delivered and available order type PM07 and associated configuration settings or create new entries, if deemed necessary.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 363 Chapter 8 Integrating with Embedded Extended Warehouse Management Embedded extended warehouse management in SAP S/4HANA makes it far more efficient and effective for companies to perform quality func- tions in logistics and the supply chain that involve complex warehousing functions. Warehousing operations are closely linked with the sales, procurement, production, and distribution (inbound and outbound) processes in the supply chain, as well as with financial accounting. Good warehousing management should both support the smooth flow of materials to and from the warehouse and provide useful information to run the operations within the warehouse.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Embedded extended warehouse management (EWM) in SAP S/4HANA has led to the following massive simplifications:  Direct access to master data and configuration objects  Elimination of the core interface (CIF) for transferring master data  Reduction of redundant transaction objects in embedded EWM and SAP S/4HANA Note The queued remote function call (qRFC) is still required to transfer transaction data from and to SAP S/4HANA and embedded EWM (see Figure 8.1). Engage an SAP Net- Weaver consultant to ensure the required qRFC setup is up and running.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The chapter begins by explaining the minimal configuration required to integrate QM with embedded EWM, followed by discussing the relevant master data setup. Next, we provide an end-to end walkthrough of the integrated business processes. The chapter concludes with reporting, including the warehouse management monitor. Note In this chapter, we’ll describe the functionality of embedded EWM in sufficient detail for the purposes of its integration with QM; however, we won’t cover every possible business scenario. We’ll restrict the scope of this chapter to typical and routine busi- ness processes that use materials management (MM), QM, and the embedded EWM Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

Due to the highly integrated nature of QM with other areas, it’s always best to coordinate with experts or consultants in these SAP areas to ensure you’re meeting the end-to-end business scenarios of a client where SAP S/4HANA (with embedded EWM) is being implemented. docs.text: 365 8.1 Configuration Basics The following sections discuss the QM-specific configurations that need to be in place so that the configured objects are then assigned to the master data. 8.1.1 Activate Inspection Object Type An inspection object type defines the following:  Business process for the inspection  Inspected object—for example, the product, the handling unit, or the delivery  Warehouse number Each inspection object type can have many inspection rules. Based on selection criteria (also known as properties), the inspection rule determines which objects to trigger an inspection for and specifies the inspection details—for example, the inspection pro- cess, the procedure, the inspection frequency, and usage decision codes, as well as their associated logistical functions.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There are six inspection object types to cater to different business processes, as shown in Table 8.2. docs.text: 8 Integrating with Embedded Extended Warehouse Management 376 8.3 Business Processes With the necessary and QM-specific configuration and master data already set up, let’s now discuss the business processes. Starting from the top-left side, Figure 8.15 shows an end-to-end process flow wherein a purchase order for a supplier is created while ensur- ing that confirmation control (inbound delivery) is in place. Next, an inbound delivery in SAP S/4HANA is created with reference to the purchase order and the supplier. On saving the inbound delivery document, the data automatically gets transferred or dis- tributed to the warehouse management system (WMS).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This automatic distribution of data creates a corresponding but completely interlinked inbound delivery document in embedded EWM. Embedded EWM processes such as unloading and goods receipt are performed. On goods receipt in embedded EWM, the system automatically creates a QM inspection lot, for which results are recorded and a usage decision is made. The stock is put away and the inventory figures updated in not just the inventory manage- ment area of SAP S/4HANA but also in embedded EWM. Figure 8.15 Quality Management Integration with Embedded EWM Next, let’s show the integration business process in SAP S/4HANA and in embedded EWM. 8.3.1 Create Purchase Order with Inbound Delivery Figure 8.16 is the display purchase order for the NB Standard PO 4500001852 .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 389 Chapter 9 Batch Management Batch management is an important part of a company’s ability to procure, produce, store, and sell material. The batch defines a quantity of material by characteristics unique to that batch. Those characteristics determine how the material in that batch is used, sold, or moved. Certain materials can be defined in SAP S/4HANA as being batch-managed. A batch is a quantity of material that represents a homogeneous unit with unique specifications. The batch of material may refer to a quantity of chemical that is produced in one pro- cess or a quantity of bottles of water that were filled on a certain filling line from a spe- cific tank.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There are many ways in which a batch can be defined. In SAP S/4HANA, the batch is used to identify units of material as they move through the system. The batch can have specific characteristics that enable it to be identified and used within the materials management (MM) or production planning (PP) functionality. This chapter describes the processes involved in creating and changing a batch and the process of batch determination. The first section gives an overview of the batch and how it’s used in industry. We’ll start out this chapter by covering the configuration settings needed to start using the batch management functionality in the SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: After configuration, we cover the requisite master data, followed by the business processes associated with batch management, such as manually creating a batch master and how the system automatically creates the batch master during various business transactions. We’ll then discuss specialized but important batch management topics, such as automatic batch determination, active ingredient management, batch derivation, and shelf-life expiration of batches. The chapter will conclude with some important batch manage- ment reports, including the Batch Information Cockpit. 9.1 Batch Management Overview The definition of a batch differs among companies, industries, and countries.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, in the pharmaceutical industry, strict guidelines and regulations determine what a batch is. These regulations on batches and batch control include the ANSI/ISA-88 standard and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) 21 CFR Part 11 specifications in the United States. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 9 Batch Management 390 Although there is no one exact definition of a batch, the following definition from Exxon- Mobil Aviation may help: A batch is the specific quantity of a material produced in a single manufacturing process, i.e., under the same conditions, thus featuring identical properties. Each batch of material is given a batch number. Each batch of a material is tested with regard to relevant characteristics to ensure it meets the values or within the range for those characteristics. A second definition of a batch is from Marathon Oil Company, and it significantly dif- fers from other definitions: “A batch is a shipment of a single product that is handled through the pipeline without mixing with preceding or following shipments.” This third definition of a batch is from the Hawaiian Coffee Association: A batch refers to a quantity of coffee coming to the roaster.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Quantities of the same coffee arriving at different times would be viewed as separate batches. Changes from batch to batch—even of the same variety of bean—must be detected by the roaster if he is to produce coffees that are consistently the same. Whatever the definition, the fact is that the batch has to be identified by a batch record. This can be as simple as identifying bags of coffee beans as they arrive at the plant or as complex as identifying a batch by numerous qualifying characteristics to ensure qual- ity and safety.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A batch of material can either be purchased from a supplier or produced internally. The need to manage materials by batch has been discussed; however, in SAP, the material must be identified as batch-relevant. The identification of a batch record is especially important for the pharmaceutical industry due to the regulations set down by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in the United States and other regulatory bodies across the world, such as the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI), Bundesgesundheitsamt (BGA) in Germany, Health Canada, and the Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) in the United Kingdom.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These regulatory bodies are primarily interested in public safety. Regulations such as FDA 21 CFR Part 11 in the United States are aimed at improving the efficiency of quality control and the quality assurance process. Each batch produced has to be quality tested, with the results stored electronically against the batch number. The most critical use of the batch number in the pharmaceutical industry is for product recall. The batch number also can be used as the tracking device for companies in case of subsequent errors or contamination.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Manufacturers publish product recalls every day, but for the pharmaceutical industry, product recalls can save lives. A pharmaceutical company can voluntarily recall a product. If the company finds that a result from a test on a batch was incorrect, putting the batch out of tolerance, then the product made from that batch could be hazardous. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 391 9.2 Batch Level and Batch Status Management The errors could go all the way back to the supplier, if any of the material was pur- chased. If a supplier informs the company that a batch of purchased material was out of tolerance, then this batch must be traced through the production process to find all finished goods batches that may have used components or ingredients from the faulty batch. In the United States, the FDA has the power to request that a company initiate a recall when it believes that a drug violates the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A recall will be requested when the FDA concludes the following:  A drug that has been distributed presents a risk of illness or injury or gross con- sumer deception.  The manufacturer or distributor hasn’t recalled the drug.  FDA action is necessary to protect the public health. In a recall, the manufacturer informs the retailer, wholesaler, or even consumer about how to identify the batch number on the product and which batch numbers are a part of the recall. Let’s begin with the configuration basics of batch management. 9.2 Batch Level and Batch Status Management In the following sections, we’ll follow a step-by-step approach for the configuration steps required to set up batch management in the SAP S/4HANA system. 9.2.1 Define the Batch Level The batch can be defined at different levels, but it’s defined at the plant level by default.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: At the beginning of an SAP S/4HANA implementation project, a MM consultant helps the company decide the batch level at which it requires batch monitoring and reporting. Use the following guidelines to determine that batch numbers are unique at the follow- ing three levels:  Plant and material combination level In this level, the plant and material combination have unique batch numbers. Differ- ent material in the same plant can be assigned the same batch number, and the same material in different plants can also be assigned the same batch number.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this given context, the material is transferable from one plant to another, and although the batch number is the same, the specification of the destination batch will remain unchanged.  Material number level As the batch numbers are created at the material level, the same batch numbers can be used for other material as well. After setting the batch level as the material in the Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 9 Batch Management 392 system, a material can have the same batch number even though the materials are in different plants with the same specifications. The same batch number can be reas- signed for other materials with a different specification.  Client level The batch level is set at the client level, which is the highest level. The same batch number can’t be used for different material or different plants. The batch number assigned is rather unique and can be assigned only once; thus, every material will always have a new or different batch number.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system’s default setting is the plant level. As mentioned earlier, this can be custom- ized to the batch level as needed. However, it’s important to note that while switching to a higher level is always possible, lowering the batch level is only possible from the cli- ent level to the material level. This is because the batch data is organized so that it has to be converted whenever it’s switched to another batch level. To define the batch level, follow these steps: 1. Go to SAP IMG  Logistics – General  Batch Management  Specify Batch Level and Activate Status Management .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Choose the batch level as just discussed (client, plant, or material level), and then save. 2. Choose Batch Status Management to activate batch management status in the cli- ent, select the Active checkbox, and then save. 3. Choose Plants with Batch Status Management , and set the Batch Status Manage- ment checkbox in the resulting list for those plants where batch status management has to be active. Select the checkboxes and save. 4. Choose Initial Status of a New Batch , then specify which initial new batches are to be assigned for each material type, and check the Initial Status box for each material type that will be batch-managed. 9.2.2 Batch Number Assignment In this step, define the batch number range and assignments.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To do so, follow menu path SAP IMG  Logistics – General  Batch Management  Batch Number Assignment  Activate Internal Batch Number Assignment . In the resulting screen, select the Active radio button to activate the internal batch number assignment. It’s also possible to define whether internal batch number assignment is allowed for goods receipts that have an account assignment via SAP IMG  Logistics – General  Batch Management  Batch Number Assignment  Internal Batch Number Assignment for Assigned Goods Receipt .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the next step, define the number ranges for internal batch number assignment by following menu path SAP IMG  Logistics – General  Batch Management  Batch Num- ber Assignment  Maintain Internal Batch Number Assignment Range . © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 393 9.2 Batch Level and Batch Status Management In the standard SAP S/4HANA system, you can set the number range object BATCH_CLT , and the number range 01 from 0000000001 to 9999999999 has been defined. Similar to the internal batch number assignment, you can assign a number range for external number assignment. Follow menu path SAP IMG  Logistics – General  Batch Management  Batch Number Assignment  Maintain Number Range for External Batch Number Assignment . Maintain the external number range by clicking the Number Ranges button and then the Change Intervals button.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Here, use the already-defined number range or create a new number range by clicking the Inset Interval button. Enter the number ( No. ), From number , and To number , and then choose Save . Note SAP enhancement SAPLNOIZ can be used for internal batch number assignment. This enhancement comprises two function module exits to define number ranges or tem- plates for batch numbers:  EXI_SAPLVO1Z_001 This exit is used to replace the number range object and/or interval proposed with its own number range object by the system and/or interval.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It’s also used to stop the system from assigning an internal number based on the material or plant. This exit can be used to stop the dialog box from appearing.  EXIT_SAPLVO1Z_002 This exit helps assign its own number or even change the number assigned by the system. 9.2.3 Creation of New Batches in the Production Process This configuration step is how the system creates new batches for processes/process orders. To define the new batch creation for processes/process orders, follow menu path SAP IMG  Logistics General  Batch Management  Creation of New Batches  Define Batch Creation for Production Order/Process Order , or use Transaction CORW.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Make specific settings in batch management for the existing production control pro- files. Choose the production control profile for making the settings by selecting the required option (see Figure 9.1) for automatic batch creation:  Automatic batch creation at order creation  Automatic batch creation at order release  No automatic batch creation in production/process order Then, select the batch classification option in the Batch Classification field. In addition, select the Extended Classification checkbox so that more batch-specific functionalities are available.

docs.text: 9 Batch Management 394 The production scheduling profile ( PS Profile ), which in this example is 101 , is then assigned in the Work Scheduling view of a material master. To do so, follow menu path SAP IMG  Logistics – General  Batch Management  Creation of New Batches  Define Batch Creation for Goods Movements . docs.text: 395 9.3 Master Data in Batch Management For each material type, also define whether a new batch can be created via the batch master creation transaction (Transaction MSC1N). To do so, follow menu path SAP IMG  Logistics – General  Batch Management  Creation of New Batches  Define Initial Cre- ation of Data for Batch Master Transactions .
