docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This ends the basic configuration settings needed for batch management. In the next section, we discuss how to set up master data in batch management. 9.3 Master Data in Batch Management A first step when working with batch management is to identify the material that needs to be batch-managed and then update the material master record by setting the batch management requirement. Let’s go over the different master data management processes and steps specific to batch management in the following sections. 9.3.1 Activate Batch Management in the Material Master In the SAP S/4HANA system, batch master records always depend on material master records.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Therefore, the first step is to define batch management requirements in the material master. Go to Transaction MM01 (Create Material Master), enter all the required details, and select the Batch mgmt (batch management requirement) check- box to denote that the material has to be handled in batches (see Figure 9.3). The follow- ing views of the material master contain the checkbox for batch management:  Sales: General/Plant  Plant data / stor. 1  Purchasing  Work s cheduling All views are the same, and any changes/updates in one view appear in all views.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Tips The indicator for the material can be changed from batch-managed to nonbatch- managed only if there has been no stock for the current period and the previous period. This is to allow for transactions posting of batch-managed materials in any previous period. In the SAP S/4HANA system, batches are posted for a material, so the batch master records are always dependent on material master records. If there is a mismatch of sub- jected material and batch requirement, all stocks need to be posted from the previous Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 9 Batch Management 396 fiscal year, the previous period, and the current period. To do this, reset the Batch mgmt checkbox, and repost the stock in batches into the system. Similarly, it’s possible to cancel the batch requirement for any material that a company doesn’t want to batch-manage anymore. If there’s a need to reorganize the batch mas- ter records, then it’s mandatory to reset the Batch mgmt checkbox to empty, post the required batch requirement, and then post the stock back into the SAP S/4HANA sys- tem using Transaction MIGO.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 9.3 Activation of Batch Management in Material Master 9.3.2 Batch Classification To differentiate batches of material depending on their individual properties, charac- teristics are used to define the properties. For example, the paint industry uses color, coverage, and viscosity as characteristics to classify different batches. The cold-roll coil industry uses finish, thickness, and quality to classify different batches. These characteristics are created in the SAP S/4HANA system and assigned to the mate- rials.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The same classification concept as in materials classification is applied in defining batch classification. Say a company that deals with various types of paints wants to capture the characteris- tics of paint: shine, color, and viscosity. A class has to be created with the characteristics for coverage, color, and viscosity wavelength. This class has to be assigned to a material. Every time a new batch is created for the material, the characteristic values need to be entered. Let’s briefly define characteristics and their assignment to a class specific to batch management. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 397 9.3 Master Data in Batch Management Define Characteristics First, create the various characteristics for the materials, such as thickness, viscosity, den- sity, and so on. To create characteristics, follow menu path SAP Menu  Cross-Application Components  Classification System  Master Data  Characteristics , or use Transaction CT04. In the resulting screen, enter the Characteristic name, and choose Create . Enter a description, as shown in Figure 9.4. The Status field has In Preparation , Locked , and Released options.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A Released status means that the characteristic can be used; a status of In Preparation or Locked means that it can’t be used. Figure 9.4 Characteristic In the Value assignment area, select either Single-value or Multiple Values . The Single- value radio button specifies that only one value can be assigned to this characteristic; the Multiple Values radio button is used when more than one value is possible. Select the Values tab, and enter the possible values for this characteristic, as shown in Figure 9.5. The Additional Values checkbox allows a user to enter characteristic values that aren’t defined.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: After the values are defined, save the characteristic. In this example, we’ve set the value of thickness to be within a range of 8.00 to 12.00 mm. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 9 Batch Management 398 Figure 9.5 Characteristic Values Now that a characteristic is created, the next step to assign existing characteristics to the class, which is explained in the following section. Define Class and Assign Characteristics A class represents a group of characteristics. Classes are defined based on the material classification, such as a garment, oil and grease, or metals. To define a class, follow menu path SAP Menu  Cross-Application Components  Classification System  Master Data  Classes , or use Transaction CL02.

Enter the validity dates. On the Char. tab, assign the characteristics to the class, as shown in Figure 9.6. In this case, we’ve assigned three characteristics: MM01 ( Thickness ), MM10 ( Product Class) , and MM11 ( Date of Manufacture ). Figure 9.6 Assignment of Characteristics to Class 9.3.3 Assigning Classification in the Material Master After a class is defined, the next step is to assign it to the material master via Transaction MM01.

Doing so will automatically bring up all three characteristics assigned to the class, as shown in Figure 9.7. Here, you can maintain © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 399 9.4 Business Processes of Batch Management specific characteristic values pertaining to this material. Because this is a master data step, note that characteristics values assigned are for the material master only and not for batches of a material. Figure 9.7 Classification View of Material Master With requisite master data created for batch management, the next section discusses the business processes associated with batch management. 9.4 Business Processes of Batch Management In the following sections, we’ll cover the business processes of batch management in the SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Some of these business processes include manually or auto- matically creating a batch, changing or deleting a batch, using the classification func- tion in a batch, and attaching documents to a batch. 9.4.1 Create a Batch Master Manually A batch master record for a material can be created manually or automatically in the background by the system when goods are received for the first time. A manually Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 9 Batch Management 400 created batch of a material can then be assigned during stock posting, such as during goods receipt of a material from the procurement or production processes. To create batch master records manually, follow menu path SAP Menu  Logistics  Cen- tral Functions  Batch Management  Batch Create , or use Transaction MSC1N (see Figure 9.8). Enter a material, plant, and storage location to create a batch master record. If an inter- nal number range is defined, then the system will create the batch number automati- cally after (Enter) is pressed.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The data in a material master applies in general for all the batches assigned to this master record. By contrast, a batch master record contains data that uniquely identifies the corresponding batch and characterizes the unit as one that can’t be reproduced. docs.text: 401 9.4 Business Processes of Batch Management Basic Data 1 Important fields and checkboxes in the Basic Data 1 tab shown in Figure 9.8 are as fol- lows:  Date of Manufacture The date when the batch was produced can be entered into this field. In some indus- tries, this field is also used as the date the material was tested or retested. If a mate- rial is found to be still in tolerance after the shelf-life date has expired, the material can be retested, and the date of the retest is entered into this field, in addition to a new Shelf - Life Exp.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Date . It’s recommended to check with clients to determine whether they need to use this field.  SLED/BBD The SLED/BBD (shelf-life expiration date/best by date) field is the date on which the shelf-life of this batch will expire. The shelf-life of a product can vary between plants. This date can be used in the sales process, as customers may have set a requirement on the acceptable number of days of shelf-life remaining. Some companies use this field to indicate the date on which a batch needs to be retested. If the company has implemented the quality management (QM) functionality, then the system uses this field to see if the material’s batch expiration is about to be reached so that the system can create a quality inspection lot for retesting the material.  Available From This field indicates when the batch will be available.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, if a material needs to remain in the quality inspection process for a certain number of days after test- ing, then the quality department can enter a date to inform other departments of when the batch is expected to be available.  Batch Status These radio buttons allow the batch to be classified as having restricted or unre- stricted use. If the Unrestricted option is set, then the batch has no restriction placed on its use. If the Restricted option is set, the batch is treated like blocked stock in planning but can be selected by batch determination if the search includes restricted-use batches.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Batch Status can be set to restricted from unrestricted by changing the check- box in the batch record. A material document will be posted that shows the move- ment of stock between the two statuses.  Next Inspection This date field allows the quality department to enter the date of the next quality inspection of the batch, if applicable to this material. This field is helpful when a company must retest a material’s batch after every predefined period. This material retesting process is known as recurring inspection .  Supplier Batch If the material is purchased, then the batch number assigned by the supplier can be added to the batch record.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 9 Batch Management 402 supplier batch number is noted. The Supplier Batch field (not shown) allows a 15- character string to be entered. Basic Data 2 In the Basic Data 2 tab, maintain the Texts and Freely Definable Date fields. There are six date fields. This is optional and only necessary if a user wants to use these dates somewhere in the process. The other fields on the screen are six date fields: Date 1 , Date 2 , and so on. These fields don’t have any standard functionality. The six Date fields can be used for whatever purpose is defined by the client.

docs.text: For example, these fields could contain the dates on which the material was inspected by the quality department. Classification In the Classification tab, use the class that was assigned to a material during material master classification, and maintain the characteristics values here by clicking the New button (not shown). After clicking the New button, maintain the values of all the char- acteristics listed based on the material class, as shown in Figure 9.9. docs.text: 403 9.4 Business Processes of Batch Management Tips and Tricks If there’s also a business need to link documents to a batch, then a configuration step must be completed. Follow menu path SAP IMG  Logistics – General  Batch Manage- ment  Batch Master  Activate Document Management for Batches , or use Transac- tion ODOC. The configuration in Transaction ODOC is simply switching on the field to allow docu- ment management for batches. The options are Active and Inactive . 9.4.2 Changing a Batch After the batch has been created, there may be occasion to amend the batch record, either to modify a characteristic or to add a new linked document.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To change a batch record, follow menu path SAP Menu  Logistics  Materials Management  Material Mas- ter  Batch  Change , or use Transaction MSC2N. You can make changes to the batch record, but these changes are recorded and are available to review. The Change Batch screen has an extra tab in change mode. This tab accesses a screen to view all changes made to the batch record. The Change Batch screen (refer to Figure 9.8) shows the changes made to the batch record. The informa- tion recorded includes the user who created and changed the record, as well as the fields that have been changed, including their values.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This information is important to some companies because a strict audit record is needed to show compliance with fed- eral or local regulations. In the pharmaceutical industry, companies manufacturing items that are to be consumed are under strict regulations from the FDA. Companies should at all times ensure that their record keeping is compliant with FDA regulations. 9.4.3 Deleting a Batch There is no transaction used solely for deleting a batch, but a batch can be deleted through Transaction MSC2N. Figure 9.8, shown earlier, shows the initial screen of the change batch transaction, which has a Batch Deletion Flag checkbox (not shown, but located further down the same screen) that can be set if the batch is to be deleted.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: How- ever, setting the deletion flag doesn’t immediately delete the batch. The checkbox allows the batch to be processed by an archiving program that will determine whether the batch can be deleted. If the batch can’t be deleted, the deletion flag will remain until either the archiving program determines that the batch can be deleted or until the dele- tion flag is removed. docs.text: 9 Batch Management 404 9.4.4 Automatic Creation of a Batch in Goods Movement It’s possible to define the automatic creation of batch numbers in the SAP S/4HANA system, whether for movement types or production/process orders. For instance, the system can be customized to automatically create unique batch numbers whenever goods are delivered against a process order. This means that every time goods with movement type 101 are received, the unique batch number for the material received is created by the system automatically.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Here, we present an example of how the system automatically creates a batch master on goods receipt with reference to a process order (movement type 101). To receive goods with reference to a process order and via movement type 101, go to Transaction MIGO (see Figure 9.10). Enter the process order number “1000090” after selecting Goods Receipt and selecting Order from the two dropdowns located on the top-left side of the screen. In the item details, there’s one more tab: Batch . Notice that the system has automatically created batch 16 .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Click the Classification button in the Batch tab in Figure 9.10 to enter the values of the characteristics, as shown in Figure 9.11. docs.text: 9 Batch Management 406 When a batch-managed material needs to be issued, and if there are multiple batches of the same material in stock, the system automatically lets the user choose the batch number from the material to be issued. If there’s a business need to assign a batch number based on some strategy, the batch determination strategy should be config- ured. We cover the entire batch determination topic in the next section of this chapter. Batch usage transactions can be used to track the batches and for analysis.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Transaction MB56 will give the details of a batch where-used list. SAP also provides the Batch Informa- tion Cockpit, a central tool for tracking batches, which is also discussed in this chapter. 9.5 Batch Determination The batch determination process isn’t unique to QM. The process is important in SAP S/4HANA Sales, PP, MM, and embedded extended warehouse management (EWM) in SAP S/4HANA as well. Batch determination uses strategy types, search strategies, and search procedures for a batch to be identified in the relevant area.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In a real-world scenario, a warehouse supervisor receives one material in a number of batches, and this will be kept in storage location stock or in warehouse storage bins. When the material needs to be issued to production, a strategy needs to be in place for the system to choose different batches. Defining the strategy in the system by which the system determines and offers the right batch to pick is the process of batch deter- mination. Batch determination uses the condition technique. Strategy records of the respective application, such as PP, MM, SAP S/4HANA Sales, or warehouse manage- ment WM/embedded EWM, determine batch determination.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Different strategy records in the system have to be created for different purposes, such as goods issue to produc- tion, goods issue to customer, goods issue to cost center, and so on. Batch determina- tion can be used in production order, process order, goods movement, sales order/ delivery, cost center, and transfer order functions. Configurations for each application, such as production, inventory, sales, and stock transfers, are stored in search procedures, which run the batch determination. After the batch determination procedure is set up, the system automatically accesses the corre- sponding entry of the application, which further refers to the relevant entries in config- uration.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 9.13 shows how the system searches the batch number using the batch determi- nation procedure. In any transaction, the system will first determine the application area—PP and production planning for process industries (PP-PI), MM, WM/embedded EWM, or SAP S/4HANA Sales 1 —and then determine the search procedures, which are assigned based on different combinations 2 . In the case of PP or PP-PI, the system will determine the order type and plant from the transaction 3 and then find a search pro- cedure 4 . For MM, the system will find a search procedure based on movement type.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For SAP S/4HANA Sales, the search procedure will be based on sales organization, distri- bution channel, division, and sales document type. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 407 9.5 Batch Determination The search procedure helps the system determine the search type 5 . The search type helps to identify the condition types and condition tables 6 . The system will find the appropriate batch number based on the access sequence system. Figure 9.13 Batch Determination Flow in Logistics and the Supply Chain In the following section, we start out with the necessary configuration steps required to set up automatic batch determination in the production process of PP-PI for process manufacturing (process order).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, the same logic and process steps we cover here can be used to set up automatic batch determination in other applications, such as PP (discrete manufacturing), MM, SAP S/4HANA Sales, and WM/embedded EWM. These configuration steps are then followed by covering the necessary master data required for batch determination. Finally, we’ll also show how the configuration and the master data setup eventually are reflected in the batch determination business process. Next, let’s perform the following configuration steps in their logical and sequential order. 9.5.1 Define Condition Tables The batch determination condition table includes a number of fields for selection and to record and assign values to those fields.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There are five options for condition table creation, depending on which business process a company wants to use batch determi- nation for: PP/PP-PI MM WM Sales Determine from document: • Order type • Plant Determine from document: • Movement type Determine from document: • Warehouse number • Warehouse type Determine search procedure from from warehouse number and warehouse movement type Get strategy type from search procedure Get strategy type from search procedure Get strategy type from search procedure Condition type: WM0001 Access sequence: WM0001 Condition type: ME01 Access sequence: ME01 Condition type: CO01 Access sequence: CO01 Determine the application area, i.e., PP/PP-PI, MM, WM, or SD Material Issue Mat Plant Price UOM Mat-1 1000 50.00 pcs.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Batch No B201 Determine search procedure from order type and plant Determine search procedure from movement type Determine from document: • Sales organization • Distribution channel • Division and sales doc type Determine search procedure from sales org, distribution center, and division Get strategy type from search procedure Condition type: SD02 Access sequence: SD02 Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

Sort sequence can be maintained on this screen if desired. Later in this section, we’ll also cover how to create a sort sequence and assign it to a condi- tion record.  Batch split This area contains the No. of splits field that defines the number of batch splits that are allowed during the batch determination.

docs.text: 9 Batch Management 414 With these steps performed, the necessary configuration required for batch determina- tion is complete. Next are two master data management steps required to set up auto- matic batch determination. 9.5.7 Creating Sort Rules A sort sequence enables the system to choose batches that meet the user-defined sort criteria of characteristics. For example, batches of a material expiring first are prime candidates to be sorted in ascending order so they can be consumed at the earliest pos- sible date.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This sort strategy is known as first expiration first out (FEFO). Other sort strat- egies include first in first out (FIFO) and last in first out (LIFO). Any other type of sort sequence is also possible, which we’ll soon show with an example. Access the screen shown in Figure 9.24 by following menu path Logistics  Central Func- tions  Batch Management  Batch Determination  Selection and Sort  Sort Rule  Create or by using Transaction CU70. Create a new sort sequence “ZPP”, assign the previously created characteristic MM01, and select the Ascending checkbox.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Doing so will lead to the system suggesting batches of material with values in ascending order during the batch determination process. For example, say there are four batches of a material with thicknesses (characteristic MM01) of 0.35 mm, 0.5 mm, 0.6 mm, and 0.9 mm. The system will first suggest batches of material with a thickness of 0.35 mm followed by batches with a thickness of 0.5 mm, and so on, to adhere to the ascending order of thickness during the batch determina- tion procedure. Figure 9.24 Creating a Sort Sequence in Batch Determination 9.5.8 Maintaining Condition Records As a last step in automatic batch determination, maintain the relevant condition records.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA

To maintain a condi- tion record, follow menu path SAP Menu  Logistics  Central Functions  Batch Manage- ment  Batch Determination  Batch Search Strategy  For Process Order  Create , or use Transaction COB1. Select the strategy that you defined in the earlier configuration steps (in this case, CO03 ), and select the Order Type ( PI01 ) and Plant ( 1105 ) combination. docs.text: 9 Batch Management 416 Tips and Tricks Before running the business process to test batch determination of a component, it’s a good idea to use this checklist: 1. Make sure the component is managed in batches (i.e., the Batch Management checkbox is selected in the component’s material master). 2. Ensure the component is part of the material’s bill of materials (BOM), for which the process order is created. 3. Ensure that along with sufficient stock of the component’s batches, there are also multiple batches with different characteristic values (in this example, thicknesses) so that the completeness and correctness of the batch determination process can be tested. 4.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Reconfirm the entry in the Batch Entry field in the Work Scheduling view of the component’s material master. For example, choose whether you want to automat- ically or manually trigger batch determination upon release of a process order. 5. If the same material is batch-managed in one plant but not in the other, then ensure that you select/deselect the Batch Management (Plant) checkbox. 9.5.9 Business Process Use Transaction COR1 to create a process order of order type PI01 for plant 1105. Enter “81” for the header Material , and maintain other basic process order details, such as order quantity and dates.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Navigate to the Component Overview shown in Figure 9.27. Notice that component 104 needs a total of 195 KG to produce the main material 81 . Select component 104 , and then choose Execute batch determntn (batch determina- tion). The system not only determines the relevant batches that meet the sort sequence of the thickness characteristic but also splits the total required quantity of 195 KG into multiple batches. Figure 9.27 Batch Determination © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 417 9.5 Batch Determination Here, the system has automatically determined and then assigned four batches of material 104: 7, 8, 9, and 10. Let’s evaluate this in more detail. The system first evaluates the thickness sort criteria to see which batch has the lowest thickness value and assign that batch’s quantity to the process order. However, if the assigned batch’s quantity isn’t sufficient to cater to the complete requirement (in this case, 195 KG), the system proceeds to the next batch with the next highest thickness value and assigns the batch’s quantity to the process order.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system continues in this way until multiple batches in the total required quantity are assigned to the process order. Let’s now also quickly check whether the batch determination for the process order is correctly configured. Figure 9.28 and Figure 9.29 show that batch 7 has the lowest char- acteristic (thickness) value of 8.10 mm but is only available in a quantity of 100 KG, which was assigned to the process order. Figure 9.28 Batch Determination according to Sort Sequence (1/2) Figure 9.29 Batch Determination according to Sort Sequence (2/2) Next, the system found that batch 8 had the next highest thickness value of 8.50 mm in a quantity of 20 KG.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This batch too was assigned to the process order while the system continued searching for more batches to meet a total required quantity of 195 KG. Next, Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 9 Batch Management 418 it found that batch 9 with thickness value 9.20 mm had a quantity of 50 KG, which was therefore assigned to the process order. Finally, for the available quantity of 25 KG for the fourth batch (10) with the highest thickness value of 12.00 mm, the system accord- ingly assigned the same to the process order. These settings validate the ascending sort sequence of the thickness characteristic that was set up for batch determination. docs.text: Figure 9.30 Multiple Batches Assigned Now, let’s discuss recurring inspection and expiration dates of batches. 9.6 Recurring Inspection and Expiration Dates The ability to inspect batch-managed goods—whether procured raw materials or pro- duced semifinished or finished goods—before their expiration dates ensures there will be sufficient time and flexibility for companies to respond to any unforeseen situations. Recurring inspection (also called repeat inspection ) at regular intervals allows business users to take advantage of standard functionality to automatically create inspection lots when the expiration dates of batch-managed goods approach.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The details related to the shelf life of materials are managed in individual batches. The batches nearing expiration can go through quality control checks of results recording and usage deci- sions to decide whether they can still be used. This functionality offers time and cost savings by enabling the business to act proactively and thus optimizes the full logistics and supply chain operations of the company. A significant challenge for any organization is to keep track of batch-managed materi- als with shelf-life expiration dates.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 419 9.6 Recurring Inspection and Expiration Dates tries for slow-moving materials or materials with a short shelf life. Tracking this information allows an organization to ensure that those materials are consumed first in the case of raw materials and sold first in the case of finished goods. This minimizes the material and financial costs associated with the need to destroy and scrap the goods or materials. At the time of goods production, the system is able to calculate and suggest a best before date (BBD). Similarly, on procurement of goods, the system is able to calculate and suggest a shelf-life expiration date (SLED).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Therefore, it makes sense to ensure that recurring inspection takes place before the goods are about to expire. Note Although this example shows the integration between PP and QM in the SAP S/4HANA system, a company can still use several batch-specific functions even if QM isn’t yet implemented. We recommend engaging a PP consultant to ensure an end-to-end integration among MM, PP, and QM functionalities for the batch-managed business processes covered in this section. This section outlines the important master data needed to successfully set up recurring inspection.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA

docs.text: 425 9.7 Active Ingredient Management 9.7 Active Ingredient Management Active ingredient management in batch management enables organizations to take advantage of material valuation at the batch level, as well as the potency or active propor- tion in the overall quantity of material. This functionality is especially helpful when you’re using an active element or ingredient of a material that contains carrier materials, including impurities. If the total physical quantity of a material is a mixture, then the active or potent material within the mixture is known as the active ingredient quantity .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This section begins by covering configuration basics and important master data that forms an integral part in running the end-to-end business processes involving active ingredient management. Finally, for business processes in active ingredient manage- ment, we run an entire procurement process that begins with creating a purchase order for an active ingredient material, moving to goods receipt, results recording, and finally usage decision and stock posting. 9.7.1 Configuration Basics We’ll list the most important settings and steps necessary to implement batch ingredi- ent management in procurement in this section.

Figure 9.62 Displaying Purchase Order History Let’s now delve into how and why the system made these stock and financial adjust- ments. As explained earlier, 100 kg of material is expected to have a planned propor- tion of 85 AIU (85%). In this case, and after results recording, the actual percentage of active ingredient was found and recorded to be 65%.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Hence, the system undertakes the following calculation: ((100 AIU × 0.65) ÷ 0.85) = 76.471 AIU This is the quantity of active ingredient that the supplier has delivered and should accordingly be paid for. Because it costs 100 USD for each unit (AIU) of material, we get 100 USD/KG × 76.471 KG = 7,647.10 USD. In addition, the delivered percentage of active ingredient for the material is less than expected (65% actual, as compared to 85% expected), so the system uses movement type 142 to make necessary quantity and financial adjustments.

docs.text: 9 Batch Management 448 9.8 Batch Derivation With batch derivation, a user can efficiently and automatically transfer a batch’s char- acteristics values from the sender material’s batches to the receiver material’s batches, thereby saving time, data entry effort, and cost. Batch derivation enables a user to maintain one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-one relationships between the sender’s and the receiver’s materials for complete visibility of information and data. Whenever a batch-managed material is processed in the production process, its charac- teristics change and the batch-managed material attains different physical and chemi- cal attributes.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These changed attributes are maintained as characteristic values of the batch-managed materials. With batch derivation, you can control how the system man- ages the characteristic values flowing from a sender material to a receiver material. In this section, we’ll cover the basic configuration settings needed to activate batch der- ivation. Next, we’ll move on to the master data you need to set up, including settings in the material master, classification, and batch derivation. Finally, we’ll cover the end-to- end business process in which we show how the settings made for master data are reflected in the batch derivation process.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For this example, the sender material is 104 (a semifinished material consumed during the production process to produce finished good 81), whereas the receiver material is 81 (a finished good). Let’s start with the configuration basics of batch derivation. 9.8.1 Configuration Basics Activate batch derivation in the configuration settings by following menu path SAP IMG  Logistics – General  Batch Management  Derivation of Batch Data  Activate Batch Derivation or using Transaction DVSP. On the screen that appears, select the Der- ivation Active radio button, and save the settings.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the following sections, we’ll cover the end-to-end business process of setting up batch derivation master data, which entails setting up the details of the sender and receiver materials of a batch’s data. We’ll then use an example to show how the sender material’s batch data automatically flows into a receiving material’s batch data through the batch derivation process. 9.8.2 Classification in Material Master In the material master of the sender material and receiver material, maintain the clas- sification view, wherein class type 023 is incorporated, which is specific to batch-man- aged materials.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To maintain the classification view or make changes to the already maintained classification view in the material master, follow menu path Logistics  Materials Management  Material Master  Change  Immediately , or use Transaction MM02. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: Figure 9.79 Batch Derivation Monitor Cockpit 9.9 Batch Traceability of Work in Process Batches Batch traceability is a key functionality used not only in the chemical and food indus- tries but also in almost all industries, including in discrete manufacturing. SAP delivers the batch where-used list (Transaction MB56) in the SAP S/4HANA system. This where- used list enables business users to trace the batch from the finished product to the raw material (top down) or from the raw material to the finished product (bottom up).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The work in process (WIP) batch is used to keep the batch traceability for a process order when several batches of raw material are consumed and several batches of a finished product are generated. Transaction MB56 works well in most cases. However, there is a limitation on a process order with N:N batches. In a standard process order, there is no link between the raw material batch consumed and the finished product’s batch received in the warehouse; therefore, the batch where-used list determines all the batches of raw material for each batch of the finished product.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Imagine, for example, that a problem was detected in a raw material batch after produc- tion. In this case, it isn’t possible to identify exactly which batch of finished product was produced with this problematic batch of raw material. In previous releases, the only solution for this scenario was to create separate process orders for each raw mate- rial batch, but that required more data entry, inefficient business processes, and a sig- nificant amount of manual work. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 459 9.9 Batch Traceability of Work in Process Batches In this example, we focus on the WIP batch functionality that is available in the system for production and process orders in SAP S/4HANA. More specifically, we explain how to enhance the batch where-used list to show a link between each raw material batch consumed and the respective finished product batch produced on a process order. Our example involves a simple process order with two operations and a few components. In the following sections, we start with the necessary configuration needed to set up WIP batches, followed by the required master data setup.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Then we transition to the business processes involved in WIP batches, and finally we conclude by using the Batch Information Cockpit reporting tool to trace WIP batches. 9.9.1 Configuration Settings The following subsections cover the configuration steps you need to perform before creating the confirmation profile. Activating Work in Process Batch Business Functions Two business functions are related to the WIP batch functionality that must be acti- vated using Transaction SFW5: LOG_PP_WIP_BATCH and LOG_PP_WIP_BATCH_02 .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For the basic use of the WIP batch and for the scenario covered here, it’s only necessary to activate the first business function. However, the second business function should be activated as well because it brings additional functionalities for the WIP batch, such as inventory valuation, use with documentary batches, and use on an order split. To activate the business function using the Switch Framework (Transaction SFW5), select the business function, and choose the Activate Changes button. Warning You can’t deactivate these business functions after they’re activated.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Activate the Work in Process Batch After the business function activation, it’s also necessary to activate the WIP batch functionality in the configuration. To complete this step, use Transaction OMCWB, choose the Active radio button, and then save. Warning Once activated, this configuration setting also can’t be reversed. In other words, when a user allows the use of the WIP batch functionality in the SAP S/4HANA system, it isn’t possible to get back to the original state in which WIP batches can’t be used. docs.text: 9 Batch Management 462 However, because WIP batching is a very specific functionality that may not be used in all scenarios, here’s an alternative. docs.text: 469 9.10 Batch Information Cockpit 9.10 Batch Information Cockpit In process industries, such as food and pharmaceuticals, traceability of the ingredients or components within a production or procurement process is of paramount impor- tance. Batch traceability across logistics and supply chain processes is also a legal requirement in many industries and good manufacturing practice to maintain in case there is a batch recall. Companies often develop complex custom reports to view and analyze batch traceability when the Batch Information Cockpit can serve the same pur- pose.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: With the Batch Information Cockpit, you can do the following:  Perform top-down and bottom-up traceability analysis. With top-down analysis, a finished good traces all the raw, packaging, and semifinished materials that were used in making the finished product’s batch. With bottom-up analysis, it’s possible to trace the ingredients or raw materials and trace all the finished goods that were made using these ingredients or raw materials’ batches.  Access the batch master to display and change information related to the batch directly from Batch Information Cockpit while performing the traceability analysis of a batch.  Display the stock information of the batch.  Display the stock position of a material and its associated batches.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To access the Batch Information Cockpit, follow menu path Logistics  Central Functions  Batch Management  Batch Information Cockpit , or use Transaction BMBC . Figure 9.93 shows the initial screen to set parameters that the system then considers to bring up relevant batches of materials. Notice the various tabs available on the right side, which can be used to enter specific information. The left side of the screen provides a search functionality. Figure 9.93 Batch Information Cockpit Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 471 9.11 Electronic Batch Record Figure 9.95 Central Area of the Batch Information Cockpit 9.11 Electronic Batch Record In highly regulated industries, such as pharmaceuticals, there’s often a legal require- ment to maintain a complete trail and record of all the batches used in the logistics and supply chain of manufacturing a product. Often, it’s not just the batches received from the procurement process or batches consumed in the production process that are important for record keeping; maintaining a complete record of various quality inspec- tions that took place in the manufacturing process is important as well.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The electronic batch record , or batch record for short, captures these inspection details too. Access the screen shown in Figure 9.96 by following menu path Logistics  Central Func- tions  Batch Management  Tools  Batch Record or using Transaction COEBR. On the left side, you can see a complete trail for material 81 and its associated Batch 15 . As you drill down in the same node, the related process orders will appear: (1) the two types of quality inspections ( 04 for finished goods inspection, 03 for in-process inspection) if the PP-QM integration is in place, and (2) the Material List (BOM) used in the produc- tion process.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: On the upper-right side of the same screen, you can only approve an electronic batch record for archiving with the Approve button if the statuses of various elements (e.g., process or process order, inspection lots, etc.) are set as required for electronic archiving. Here, the system also guides you to check all the prerequisites for electronic batch record. After approval, an electronic batch record can be archived by clicking the Archive button. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 9 Batch Management 472 Figure 9.96 Electronic Batch Record The lower-right side shows comprehensive details of the electronic batch record in PDF format. Note We recommend engaging an SAP NetWeaver consultant to ensure that the necessary authorizations required for archiving electronic batches are granted. The SAP Net- Weaver consultant will also set up a document repository required to store the elec- tronic batch records being archived. In some industries, such as consumer products or automotive suppliers, there are legal requirements to store where-used data of materials used for production and delivered to customers.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Enabling recall actions becomes a mandatory and critical issue for these industries. Data can be recorded by managing all relevant materials in batches, but this method has a negative impact on data volume. When turning on batch management, entering a batch number becomes obligatory for all goods movements. Then, all inven- tory postings must be executed on the batch level, and labor costs for inventory man- agement will increase. With the documentary batch record, it’s important to ensure that a partial stock of a material is traceable without having to maintain a batch’s data.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This reduces the effort and complexities involved in maintaining batch data. The documentary batch record finds greater use in automotive and consumer goods industries but is unsuitable for use in dangerous goods. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 473 9.12 Summary Documentary batch processing can be achieved in the following ways:  Documentary batches can be entered during goods movements.  In a process order, entering documentary batches is only possible at backflush.  In WM, entering documentary batches must be enabled during transport order con- firmation. 9.12 Summary Batch management is important to a large number of process-based industries. It has developed from just an identification of a group of items to a process that allows com- panies to perform product recalls, select and sell by batch characteristics, and identify expiring stock.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As the drive for competitive advantage continues, companies will fur- ther investigate how batch information can lower production time and hasten material to the customer. Chapter 10 will discuss sample management. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 475 Chapter 10 Sample Management In process industries such as chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and food, com- panies that integrate sample management into their business processes reap the greater business benefits of comprehensive information, data visibility, and traceability by putting the necessary quality controls in place. Manufacturers in general and process manufacturers in particular often require exten- sive visibility and traceability of every important material procured, produced, or received through a stock transport order (interplant transfer).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system’s standard options are limited when there is a need to have separated yet categorized physical samples that the quality inspectors and other laboratory personnel can record results of and use to make usage decisions. Sample management provides a comprehensive and in-depth solution to physical samples of various sources (externally procured, pro- duced in house, customer or supplier complaints, etc.).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: With sample management, the system supports the following types of sample generation:  Automatic generation of physical samples during inspection lot creation  Manual generation of physical samples—if needed, with reference to an inspection lot or other reference objects  Manual and multiple generation of inspection lots for existing physical samples  Sample data records For each physical sample, the system creates a physical-sample record, which contains the following essential information:  Sample number  Sample type (from goods receipt, from procurement or production, from customer complaints, from stability study)  Physical sample category (primary sample, pooled sample, reserve sample)  Sample origin (material, batch, order) In this chapter, we’ll explain the necessary plant settings that need to be in place.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Then you’ll learn how to set up a sample-drawing procedure, which is an important master data step in sample management, followed by the checklist for quality management (QM) master data that you need to ensure is already in place. Then, the chapter moves Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 10 Sample Management 476 on to goods receipt from the procurement process and how the system automatically creates planned physical samples of various sample categories. Next, we move on to how sample management integrates with production processes, especially for in- process or during-production inspection. The chapter ends with the configuration basics of sample management. 10.1 Plant Settings In this step, you make the necessary configuration settings that act as a control for business users to enter information on the number of containers at the time of goods receipt for a purchase, process, or production order.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You also incorporate the sampling procedure that the system refers to if it’s unable to find the required information in the master data setup for sample management. This is necessary for the system to calcu- late the sample size on inspection lot creation for sample management by using the sampling procedure. For the relevant plant-wise settings for sample management, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Basic Settings  Maintain Settings at Plant Level . Choose the relevant plant, which in this example is plant 1710 (see Figure 10.1).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the Insp. Lot Creation tab, choose Recording of number of containers required in Enter Container at GR . This setting doesn’t let the business user save the goods receipt for a purchase or process order until information about the number of containers is entered. Further, in the Settings for Sampling Procedures area, enter the code for a previously created sam- pling procedure, “PFIX5”, in the Sample Management field. This sampling procedure denotes that the system will create a fixed sample size of five units upon goods receipt.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 477 10.2 Master Data Note Refer to Chapter 3 for how to create a sampling procedure that you can use in this step. While creating a sampling procedure, choose the Sample Management radio button that’s available in the Inspection Point area. 10.2 Master Data As with other business processes into which QM integrates, sample management also requires that you maintain the master data before you can run the business processes. Apart from the regular master data, such as relevant inspection type activations in the material master and creating inspection plans, you also need to maintain a sample- drawing procedure and assign it to the material’s inspection plan for planned physical samples.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the following section, we’ll discuss master data specific to sample management, including the sample-drawing procedure, inspection plan, and ensuring the QM master data checklist is adhered to. 10.2.1 Sample-Drawing Procedure You can use the sample-drawing procedure to plan automatic (planned) physical sam- ple generation during inspection lot creation. In a sample-drawing procedure, you define how many samples the system should draw, whether the business user needs to confirm a sample’s drawing, and which category of physical sample to draw.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The fol- lowing physical sample categories are available for selection:  Primary sample You draw the primary sample directly from a material/batch stock. You can inspect these samples or create pooled samples from them.  Pooled sample You create this sample by mixing other physical samples from the same material/ batch.  Reserve sample You draw the reserve sample from a material/batch stock and store it for other inspections. With the sample-drawing procedure, you can also control when the system should automatically print out the sample-drawing instructions, which contain detailed infor- mation on how to draw a sample.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If the material is supplied in different physical sample containers, you can store corresponding drawing instructions depending on the phys- ical sample container. For all planned physical sample creation, you assign the sample- drawing procedure to the material’s inspection plan, master recipe, or routing. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 10 Sample Management 478 In sample management, it’s often also necessary to draw physical samples that weren’t originally planned and are therefore known as unplanned physical samples . This busi- ness scenario generally applies when you have to conduct additional tests on a mate- rial that didn’t show satisfactory inspection results and for which you need more physical samples to conduct another round of testing. For such unplanned physical samples, the following two options are available:  You can manually generate an entirely new physical sample.  You can manually generate a physical sample for an existing physical sample record.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the sample-drawing procedure, you can determine whether the system automati- cally or manually releases (or confirms) the automatically created physical samples. When you confirm a physical sample drawing, the system releases some or all corre- sponding physical samples. Considering the compliance aspects of Good Manufactur- ing Practice (GMP), there may be a need for quality inspection to manually confirm physical sample drawing. Further, there is the option to enter digital signatures (see Chapter 3), which ensures that only authorized employees can execute certain activi- ties (e.g., the confirmation).

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You have to manually confirm the manually created phys- ical samples. To make the relevant settings for the sample-drawing procedure, use Transaction QPV2 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Sample  Sample-Drawing Procedure  Edit . Note To display the sample-drawing procedure, use Transaction QPV3 or menu path Logis- tics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Sample  Sample-Drawing Procedure  Display . Figure 10.2 shows the initial screen for the sample-drawing procedure.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For this exam- ple, enter “S200” and select the Consider No. of Containers checkbox so that the system makes it mandatory for a business user to enter the container information in the inspection lot. In addition, and only if required, select the Confirmation Req. checkbox to enable the business user to confirm sample drawing as a separate step. For example, if you enter a size factor of 2, then the system creates a physical sample quantity double the originally calculated value. docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, in the pro- duction process, an important business process is the in-process or during-production process for which you want to carry out quality inspection using sample management. Sample management integrates with all production types, such as discrete, process, and repetitive manufacturing (REM). A typical production process involves processing a material that goes through various operations and phases during the production pro- cess. During the course of its production, the material attains different physical and chemical attributes and requires physical inspections.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There are two options to handle quality inspection in production processes using sam- ple management. The first option is that for planned physical sample drawings, you Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

The second option is to manually draw the physical sample on different criteria, such as drawing a physical sample after every five hours or after every 100 PC of production. In such cases, you don’t plan the drawing of physical samples in a sample-drawing procedure. You create the samples manually with reference to an inspection lot or order.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 501 Chapter 11 Quality Certificates Leveraging quality certificate functionality in your company’s procure- ment and sales business processes can bring about significant optimiza- tion, efficiency, and control. Quality certificates bring greater visibility and control to the quality-related documen- tation involved in procurement and sales. Procurement process optimization occurs when you implement incoming quality certificates . By putting the necessary controls in place, you can prevent the release of procured raw materials into production or the release of defective procured spare parts into maintenance until the accompanying incoming quality certificate from the supplier is available in the system.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If a customer complains about a defective product, incoming certificates provide complete traceabil- ity of a supplier’s compliance when supplying raw materials by displaying whether the details noted in the incoming quality certificate adhered to your organization’s specifi- cations. You can also quickly and comprehensively set up and use outgoing quality certificates for a more diverse range of stakeholders than only customers to whom the company sells its products. The critically focused area in outgoing quality certificates is again QM master data, if you intend to ensure complete and comprehensive visibility and avail- ability of information.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This chapter is logically divided into two sections: incoming quality certificates and outgoing quality certificates. In each section, we’ll discuss the important configuration and master data highlights, as well as explain how to use the different certificates in your business processes. 11.1 Incoming Quality Certificates The first step toward integrating quality certificates into the procurement process begins when the person overseeing QM operations assigns a certificate type , which is needed for a procured material.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A certificate type confirms the specific type of certifi- cate that the company needs from the supplier at the time of goods receipt and shows compliance with the quality standards set by the company. The next step is to put the necessary control levels in place for incoming quality certificate submission. Such con- trol levels can vary from a lenient information message to a more stringent error mes- sage that occurs if the incoming certificate doesn’t accompany the receipt of the goods. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 11 Quality Certificates 502 An information message by the system simply informs the warehouse staff of the missing quality certificate. An error message doesn’t allow for a goods receipt until the supplier submits the quality certificate. Let’s get started with setting up the configuration basics. 11.1.1 Configuring the Control Key A control key controls the allowed (or disallowed) business functions by setting the parameters or settings that the system should check during transaction processing. To define a new control key or make changes to an existing one, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  QM in Logistics  QM in Procurement  Define Control Keys .

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the screen that appears, select QM Control Key 0005 followed by choosing Details and Figure 11.1 will appear. Figure 11.1 Control Key for QM in Procurement Select at least the two checkboxes for Release Required and Certificate Required . The Release Required checkbox confirms that the user must maintain the supplier’s rela- tionship to the material before initiating any procurement activity in the system. This relationship is referred to as a quality information record , which we’ll discuss in Section 11.1.3. The Certificate Required checkbox ensures that the supplier submits an incoming © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 503 11.1 Incoming Quality Certificates quality certificate at the time of goods delivery. Although these are related to QM, the remaining checkboxes aren’t directly related to incoming quality certificates. Tips and Tricks You can define a new control key if the standard control keys available in SAP S/4HANA don’t fulfill your business requirements. 11.1.2 Define Control Functions for Certificate Processing Just like a control key, you also assign a certificate type in the material master data and assign further control functions for incoming quality certificates.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To define the control function of a specific certificate type, use Transaction V_TQ05 or follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  QM in Logistics  QM in Procurement  Define Keys for Cer- tificate Processing . Choose Define Certificate Types. The screen that appears contains a list of the standard available certificate types. You can either use the available certificate types or define a new one. If the existing certifi- cate types meet your company’s business needs, then we suggest that you use them as is or make changes to them.

docs.text: 11 Quality Certificates 504 The configuration for incoming certificates is now complete. The next step is to main- tain the relevant information in the material master data and create the quality infor- mation record. 11.1.3 Master Data for Incoming Quality Certificates You need to set up the QM master data for the incoming quality certificate in SAP S/4HANA before starting the procurement process. We’ll discuss the required master data in the following sections. Certificate Type Control Detail of Control Function Certificate for Each PO Item The system requires a separate certificate for each item in the purchase order.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If not selected, then one certificate is suffi- cient for the entire purchase order containing multiple line items. Certificate for Each GR Item The system requires a separate certificate for each item on the goods receipt. If not selected, then one certificate is sufficient for the entire goods receipt containing multiple line items. Certificate Check Required This checkbox is generally used in business scenarios involv- ing electronic certificates and in which the user must still check the certificate to ensure that all parameters of the ordered goods are in conformity.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Control Without Certificate Enforces a required action if a certificate isn’t received. The various available options include no information message, just an information message, warning message, error mes- sage, moving material, and blocked stock. Enhanced Certificate Pro- cessing Used for enhanced certificate processing. No Certificate Confirmation at GR With selection of this checkbox, as well as the Enhanced Certifcate Processing checkbox, the business user must separately record the incoming certificate instead of simply confirming certificate receipt at the time of material goods receipt.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Rem. Deadline (Days) This option is maintained in number of days to create a system-generated reminder if the supplier fails to deliver the quality certificate after the delivery of goods. Escalation Deadline Also maintained in number of days, this option stipulates that the system must escalate the reminder if the supplier still fails to deliver or submit the quality certificate. IDocs are beyond the scope of this book. 11.2 Outgoing Quality Certificates Be it a business need or a practice to send accompanying outgoing quality certificates for every delivery of the customer’s order to enable sharing quality results for inter- company communication, it’s quick and easy to integrate outgoing quality certificates in QM. Most of the needed groundwork can be successfully undertaken by an SAP func- tional consultant or even by the client’s business users who have sufficient exposure to the SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Outgoing quality certificates integrate with SAP S/4HANA Sales, where goods delivered to the customer are accompanied by the relevant (outgo- ing) quality certificate. A practical approach is to thoroughly assess and evaluate all the areas and processes in which different and diverse usages of outgoing quality certificates are needed and can be implemented. Upon completing this activity and gaining insight into the series of activities involved, you may treat implementing an outgoing quality certificate as a mini project or part of an ongoing business processes improvement.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In the sales process, the company needs to engage the person looking after the QM operations to define the certificate type that will accompany its product as a physical document at the time of goods dispatch to the customer. The next step is to define a certificate profile in the system, consisting of the inspection results of the physical and chemical attributes of the product. The quality inspector conducts a quality inspection on the product, consisting of various tests, and eventually records the actual results in the system.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The quality inspector prints these actual inspection results on the outgoing quality certificate. This printed outgoing quality certificate is the actual physical docu- ment that the company sends to its customer with each goods dispatch. Let’s now begin with the configuration steps involved in setting up outgoing quality certificates. 11.2.1 Define Keys for Certificate Processing You have to assign a certificate type when you define a certificate profile for the out- going certificate. You can either use the standard certificate keys available in the SAP S/4HANA system or create a new key.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To create a new control key for a certificate type, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Certificates  Certificate Profile  Define Keys for Certificate Pro- cessing . In the popup that opens, double-click Define Certificate Types . The ensuing © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 513 11.2 Outgoing Quality Certificates screen contains a standard list of available certificate types. As already mentioned, here you can either use an available certificate type or create a new one. In this example, use standard certificate type E23C, which is already available in the SAP S/4HANA system. This is the only configuration step you need for the outgoing quality certificate pro- cess. The next step is to create or update the QM master data that is specific to outgoing quality certificates. 11.2.2 Master Data for Outgoing Quality Certificates We begin with QM master data you need to set up for outgoing quality certificates in the SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The required QM master data is the certificate profile and the assignment of the certificate profile, which we’ll discuss in the following sections. Note Make sure that other QM master data elements for the material, such as the relevant inspection type activation in the material master, master inspection characteristics, and inspection plan, are already created and available in the system. Certificate Profile The first step in generating an outgoing quality certificate is to create a certificate pro- file. A certificate profile holds extensive user-defined information about what the com- pany would like to see in the printout of its outgoing quality certificate and how it should be presented.

docs.bookTitle: Quality Management with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For example, the company may have five different master inspec- tion characteristics for results recording of a material but wants only two master inspection characteristics printed on the outgoing quality certificate. Similarly, you can group together several materials with the same set of master inspection character- istics in one certificate profile, thereby reducing the time and effort you put into main- taining the QM master data. To create a new certificate profile, use Transaction QC01 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Certificates  Outgoing  Certificate Profile  Create .

docs.text: 7 Preface If you’re familiar with the classic SAP Business Suite, you’ve likely encountered some of the 16,000 transaction codes that exist in the system. These transaction codes formed the bedrock of a robust and long-standing enterprise resource planning (ERP) system, which is still used by thousands of customers around the globe today. However, since the advent of SAP S/4HANA in 2015, a new user experience has been introduced: SAP Fiori. What exactly is SAP Fiori, and how does it differ from the traditional SAP GUI transac - tion codes that have served SAP so well for so long?

docs.bookTitle: SAP Fiori Apps for SAP S4HANA The Quick Reference Guide
docs.text: SAP Fiori is both a design system and a technology platform. This book deals with SAP Fiori as a technology platform, but it is worth spending a few short sentences on what SAP Fiori offers as a design system. SAP Fiori as a design system is built for three key experiences: the web, mobile devices, and a conversational user experience (UX). The system is a suite of tools and guide - lines that can be harnessed to design SAP Fiori apps that meet a consistent and SAP- approved standard. SAP offers various tools for achieving this, including SAP Screen Personas, SAPUI5, SAP Build, SAP Build Work Zone, and Joule.

docs.bookTitle: SAP Fiori Apps for SAP S4HANA The Quick Reference Guide
docs.text: The documentation available in the SAP Fiori suite of products also includes guidelines for working with mobile development kit (MDK) and software development kit (SDK) tools, Apple’s iOS, Android, Bot Builder, Slack, and Alexa. This book serves as a reference for the most useful and commonly used SAP Fiori apps in SAP S/4HANA. The entries list the apps in alphabetical order, include the SAP Fiori app ID, and give a small amount of detail about the purpose of each app and how it can be used in a business context. In addition, we will highlight tips wherever applicable to help you maximize the potential use of these apps.

docs.bookTitle: SAP Fiori Apps for SAP S4HANA The Quick Reference Guide
docs.text: The focus of this book is on the pri - vate cloud and on-premise offerings of SAP S/4HANA and the associated SAP Fiori apps. This is not to say that these apps are not available for SAP Cloud ERP (the public cloud offering), but the focus remains on the more widely used SAP Cloud ERP Private and the on-premise solutions. SAP Fiori has over 15,000 apps available as part of its private cloud offering. This book does not attempt to detail all 15,000; that would require far too many pages and would likely not be at all intuitive.

docs.bookTitle: SAP Fiori Apps for SAP S4HANA The Quick Reference Guide
docs.text: Instead, we have focused entirely on usefulness, relying heavily upon our extensive experience in SAP S/4HANA projects to focus on the SAP Fiori apps that are likely to give the most value. The apps contained within the book are native to SAP S/4HANA 2023, which is the latest version at the time of writing. The SAP Fiori version used for detailing these apps is SAP Fiori 3. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: SAP Fiori Apps for SAP S4HANA The Quick Reference Guide
docs.text: Preface 8 Some of the apps also have an associated SAP transaction code; where these exist, we have listed them to help those who are familiar with SAP GUI map their workflow to SAP Fiori. It is not, however, the intention of this book to detail all the SAP transaction codes that have also been rendered, unchanged, as SAP Fiori apps. For that purpose, consider consulting another SAP PRESS book: SAP Transaction Codes: Your Quick Refer - ence to Transactions in SAP ERP (Krishnamoorthy et al. 2016). Target Audience This book is written for professionals who are using SAP Fiori as part of their day-to-day work.

docs.bookTitle: SAP Fiori Apps for SAP S4HANA The Quick Reference Guide
docs.text: This includes SAP consultants, SAP architects, SAP project managers, SAP devel - opers, super users, business users, configuration specialists, business process special - ists, architects, and administrators. Maybe you need to understand SAP Fiori apps and how they can help you in an upcoming SAP S/4HANA implementation or SAP migra - tion, or maybe you simply want to delve a little deeper into your chosen area of SAP. Regardless of your specific role, if you interact with SAP Fiori apps, this is the book for you. Navigating This Book The apps detailed in this book are organized based upon the functionalities within which they are used.

docs.bookTitle: SAP Fiori Apps for SAP S4HANA The Quick Reference Guide
docs.text: There are several apps, such as My Inbox, that cross all SAP S/4HANA functionalities, and these types of apps are detailed in Chapter 11 . The apps are listed alphabetically, but they also contain the SAP Fiori app ID. This allows you to use the book’s extensive index to find the app you are looking for. You can search by one of three methods: ▪ Search by app name. This is the most common method of searching. ▪ Search by SAP Fiori app ID. ▪ Search by keyword. If you are not aware of the app ID or the exact name of the app, then you can search by keywords that relate to the specific function of the app.

docs.bookTitle: SAP Fiori Apps for SAP S4HANA The Quick Reference Guide
docs.text: In SAP Fiori, as with SAP GUI transactions, functionality can be achieved via a variety of different apps. In these circumstances, we mention all the various SAP Fiori apps. Note that in some cases, apps may appear in multiple chapters when they're relevant to more than one functional area. For example, there is a potential overlap between ma - terials management and warehouse management. If apps are truly cross functional, they appear in Chapter 11 . © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)
