Note that goods receipts for stocks for consumption purposes are not supported in this app.  Post the receipt of shelf life–managed materials into stock.  Assign batches during goods receipt processing for those materials that require them.  Assign serial numbers during goods receipt processing for those materials that require them.  Use predefined output forms in output management for material documents, which can be copied and changed according to your requirements.

Manage Stock The Manage Stock app (see Figure 7.5) can perform the following types of goods move- ments in the SAP S/4HANA system:  Initial entry of stock balances for unrestricted use, quality inspection or blocked stocks.  Scrapping of material for unrestricted use, quality inspection or blocked stocks.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 251 7.3 Goods Movements The Manage Stock app supports movement-type-dependent reason codes. Reason codes let you add a short explanation for the underlying purpose of a specific goods movement, such as poor quality. You can also enter free texts for the document header or for an individual line item. The Manage Stock app lets you check the range of cover- age based on the consumption of unrestricted stock in the last 30 days. If you notice that you’ve made an error in posting goods movements, you can correct the error by reversing the material document and posting the goods movements again.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To reverse the material document, use the Material Documents Overview app. The Manage Stock app is assigned to the inventory manager standard authorization role. Post Subsequent Adjustment The Post Subsequent Adjustment app (see Figure 7.7) is used to make correction entries in stocks consumed during a subcontracting process. When a goods receipt for a sub- contracted item is posted, goods issues are done for the components sent to the sup- plier, based on the bill of material maintained in the purchasing document line item.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Sometimes, suppliers consume more or less of a component than planned. This app allows component corrections, both over- and underconsumptions, to be made after the original goods receipt is posted. This app requires the following:  The referenced purchasing document line item must have a subcontracting item category.  A goods receipt must have already been posted for the selected line item. Figure 7.7 Post Subsequent Adjustment App Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA

Material Documents Overview The Material Documents Overview app (see Figure 7.8) lets you display generate a list of material document items based on filter criteria and display the details for a selected material document item. You can also reverse a material document through this app.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA

The Material Documents Overview app is assigned to the inventory manager and ware- house clerk standard authorization roles. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 253 7.3 Goods Movements Post Goods Movement The Post Goods Movement app (see Figure 7.9) is used to perform goods movements, including goods receipts, in the SAP S/4HANA system. It can also be used to review a specific material document and its associated documents. This app is used when the simplified goods receipt SAP Fiori apps do not support all aspects of the type of goods receipts needed for your enterprise—for example, if custom goods receipt movement types are used. The Post Goods Movement app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MIGO.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA

The Output Material Documents app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA sys- tem and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MB90. The Out- put Material Documents app is assigned to the inventory manager and warehouse clerk standard authorization roles.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Inventory Management 254 Figure 7.10 Output Material Documents App Processing Goods Receipts via Inbound Deliveries There are a variety of apps that can be used to record the arrival of goods at your facility if your supplier transmits details to you via an advance shipment notification. docs.text: 259 7.3 Goods Movements Figure 7.17 My Inbound Delivery Monitor App 7.3.2 Goods Issues Goods issues are classified as goods movements that result in a decrease in stock quan- tities. Goods issues can be planned in the SAP S/4HANA system or can be executed without preplanning. Planned goods issues are issued with reference to an existing document, such as an outbound delivery for a customer order or a reservation for production materials. Those customers requiring shipping integration with their goods issue processes will generally reference outbound delivery documents created by the warehouse.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Unplanned goods issues are issued without any reference. Examples include scrapping of defective material or issuing samples from stock. Here are the movement types for goods issues with and without reference documents:  Movement types for goods issues with reference to documents – 261: Goods Issue to Production Order – 601: Goods Issue to Outbound Delivery to Customer – 641: Goods Issue to In-Transit Stock between Plants in Same Company Code – 643: Goods Issue to In-Transit Stock between Plants in Differing Company Codes  Movement types for goods issues without reference – 201: Goods Issue to Cost Center – 333: Goods Issue to Sampling from Unrestricted Use Stock – 551: Goods Issue to Scrap from Unrestricted Use Stock Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Inventory Management 260 Note Apps used for goods issues without reference include the following:  Manage Stock  Post Goods Movement These apps were described in Section 7.3.1. If you use outbound delivery documents to manage shipping operations, then you can post goods issues in inventory management via these documents. The following apps can be used to manage outbound deliveries in the SAP S/4HANA system:  My Purchase Orders—Due for Delivery  Manage Outbound Deliveries We’ll describe these apps in the following sections.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: My Purchase Orders—Due for Delivery The My Purchase Orders—Due for Delivery app (see Figure 7.18) is used to create out- bound deliveries for those purchase orders that involve outbound movements of material. These types of purchase orders include returns of material to suppliers or the provisioning of component materials to a subcontractor out of storage location stock. Specific selection criteria are entered, and a list of eligible purchase orders is shown. Outbound deliveries then can be created for the selected orders.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 261 7.3 Goods Movements The My Purchase Orders—Due for Delivery app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction VL10B. The My Purchase Orders—Due for Delivery app is assigned to the shipping spe- cialist standard authorization role. Manage Outbound Deliveries The Manage Outbound Deliveries app (see Figure 7.19) produces a list of outbound deliveries to your specifications. You can click a specific outbound delivery to see details about the document, such as the ship-to customer, weights, or volumes.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA

docs.text: 7 Inventory Management 262 7.3.3 Stock Transfers Stock transfers are goods movements in inventory management that result in a change in physical or logical location for the goods being transacted. Stock transfers can be done within a plant or between two distinct plants. There are three types of stock transfers:  From one storage location to another storage location within a plant  From one plant to another plant within a company code  From one plant to another plant, where the plants are in different company codes Stock transfers can take place using one-step or two-step processes.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In one-step stock transfers, the material moves from the issuing plant and storage location to the receiv- ing plant and storage location immediately upon posting. One-step stock transfers are typically used when goods movements are performed in the system after the physical transfer takes place or when the transit time between the two storage locations is min- imal. The following movement types are used for one-step stock transfers:  301: Plant to Plant  311: Storage Location to Storage Location Two-step stock transfers are used to separately record the goods issue from the issuing plant and storage location from the goods receipt into the receiving plant and storage location.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This two-step process has the benefit of providing visibility into in-transit stock quantities between the two locations. The following movement types are used for two-step stock transfers:  303: Plant to Plant—Goods Issue from Shipping Plant/Storage Location  305: Plant to Plant—Goods Receipt in Receiving Plant/Storage Location  313: Storage Location to Storage Location—Goods Issue from Shipping Storage Loca- tion  315: Storage Location to Storage location – Goods Receipt in Receiving Storage Loca- tion Note that these movement types can only be used with unrestricted use stock.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Simple movements of stock can be recorded in the SAP S/4HANA system with just a material document. The following apps can be used to perform stock transfers using inventory management goods movements:  Transfer Stock—In-Plant  Transfer Stock—Cross-Plant We’ll describe these apps in the following sections. Following their discussion, we’ll dive into the methods by which these are done, via stock transport orders and in-transit stock reporting. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 267 7.3 Goods Movements Stock Transport While using inventory management goods movement to process material transfers is a simple method, most companies require more precise tracking of goods movements in materials planning, purchasing, and the warehouse. SAP offers the use of stock trans- port orders (STOs) to facilitate these detailed requirements. A stock transport order is a kind of purchase order. A stock transport order uses a sup- plying plant code in lieu of a supplier in the header of the purchase order. You can think of a stock transport order as a purchase from an internal supplier to your company group instead of an external supplier.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There are two kinds of stock transport orders:  Intracompany stock transport orders The supplying and receiving plants belong to the same company code.  Intercompany stock transport order The supplying and receiving plants belong to different company codes. Stock transport orders have the following advantages over inventory management stock transfer movements:  The goods receipt can be planned in the receiving plant.  A separate freight supplier can be entered in the order and freight bills matched to these freight suppliers.  Delivery costs can be captured and billed.  Materials planning can see the planned supply in the receiving plant, and the demand in the issuing plant once the stock transport order is created.  Outbound deliveries are used to manage the outbound process in the warehouse, similar to the process used to deliver goods to the customer.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There are three process variations, which we’ll discuss in the following sections, for the stock transfer process using stock transport orders:  Stock transport order without delivery  Stock transport order with delivery using shipping  Stock transport order with delivery and billing document The process variation used depends on your business requirements for tracing the logistics flow from planning, shipping, in-transit stock, and receiving the goods. Stock Transport Order without Delivery The stock transport order without delivery process variant uses only stock transport purchase orders to manage the process.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: No logistics documents are utilized. The pur- chase order type in the standard system is UB, and the item category on each line item is U. The goods movements are valuated at the price of the material in the issuing plant. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Inventory Management 268 The Post Goods Movement app can be used to post goods movements with reference to the stock transport order. The movement types are 351 for the goods issue in the issuing plant and 101 for the goods receipt in the receiving plant. Note that the stock transport order without delivery process can only be done with a two-step process. All goods movements are recorded in the purchase order history of the stock transport order. Both the intracompany and intercompany variants are supported. The prerequisites for the stock transport order without delivery process variant are as follows:  Material masters for the goods being transferred are set up in both plants  A ship-to customer master is set up that represents the receiving plant The steps in the stock transport order without delivery process flow are as follows: 1.

A goods receipt with reference to the stock transport order is done in the receiving plant Stock Transport Order with Delivery via Shipping The stock transport order with delivery via shipping process variant uses outbound deliveries in addition to stock transport purchase orders to manage the process.

docs.text: The pur- chase order type in the standard system is UB, and the item category on each line item is U. The goods movements are valuated at the price of the material in the issuing plant. This process variant supports both one-step and two-step movements of material. Stock transport orders with deliveries is the most common process used to execute intracompany stock transport orders as it has integration with the logistics depart- ment and does not require billing documents to be exchanged between the plants. Outbound deliveries are used to manage the outbound process in the warehouse, sim- ilar to the process used in sales to deliver goods to customers.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: All goods movements are posted with reference to the outbound delivery created with reference to the stock transport order. The movement type for the goods issue in the issuing plant is 647 for the one-step process and movement type 641 for the two-step process. The movement type for the goods receipt in the receiving plant is 101 for the two-step process. Note that no goods receipt is necessary in the one-step process as the goods move into the unrestricted stock of the receiving plant immediately upon goods issue from the issuing plant. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

In-Transit Stock Reporting It’s important to monitor the status of in-transit stocks in the system, especially those that involve a two-step process. This will ensure that all physical stock transfers are posted in a timely manner and that up-to-date stock information is available for mate- rials planning.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP S/4HANA provides the following apps to obtain reports for in-process stock trans- fers:  Display Stock in Transit  Stock in Transit on Key Date  Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit We’ll describe these apps in the following sections. Display Stock in Transit The Display Stock in Transit app (see Figure 7.26) is used to show all stocks that have been issued from one plant and are currently in transit to another plant. It also shows stock transport purchase order references and the value of the goods transferred.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Inventory Management 272 The Display Stock in Transit app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA system and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MB5T. The Display Stock in Transit app is assigned to the inventory manager standard authorization role. Stock in Transit on Key Date The Stock in Transit on Key Date app (see Figure 7.27) is used to show all stocks that have been issued from one plant and are currently in transit to another plant on a spec- ified key date. It also shows stock transport order references and the value of the goods in transit.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 7.27 Stock in Transit on Key Date App The Stock in Transit on Key Date app runs directly on the backend SAP S/4HANA sys- tem and is functionally equivalent to the classic SAP ERP Transaction MB5TD. The Stock in Transit on Key Date app is assigned to the inventory manager standard authoriza- tion role. Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit The Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit app (see Figure 7.28) provides information on materials for which a stock transport order has been created and issued, but which have not been received to date.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can identify these materials to complete the stock trans- fer process or to investigate potential issues with the transfers. Use the Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit app to do the following:  Review the stock transport orders for which materials are scheduled to arrive in a plant.  Display a list of stock transport order line items for which the stock transfer process hasn’t yet been completed, has been completed, or both.  Follow up on the results by choosing a purchase order or a material from the list, and then choosing one of the following apps: Post Goods Receipt for Purchasing Docu- ment, Stock—Single Material, or Stock—Multiple Materials.  See the stock value of overdue stocks in transit; stock value calculation is based on stock quantity of the selected reporting date multiplied by the current material price.  Use a predictive analytics model to forecast the delivery date for a stock transport order. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 273 7.3 Goods Movements The Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit app is assigned to the shipping specialist, receiving specialist, and warehouse clerk standard authorization roles. Figure 7.28 Overdue Materials—Stock in Transit App 7.3.4 Transfer Postings Transfer postings are goods movements that result in a change in identity, usability, or ownership for a quantity of stock. Typically, the stock doesn’t physically move in the system during a transfer posting. However, it is possible to combine some types of transfer postings with changes in location as well.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Transfer Stock—In-Plant app is used to post transfer postings in the SAP S/4HANA system. The Post Goods Movements app also can be utilized to create transfer posting goods movements. Descriptions of these apps can be found in Section 7.3.3. Let’s take a closer look at the types of transfer postings, as follows:  Stock identity Transfer postings that result in a change in stock identity involve a change in mate- rial. Note that a material can only to transferred to the stock of another material if both materials share the same base unit of measure.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If a material is batch-managed in the SAP S/4HANA system, a change in batch identity can also be posted. Both the material and batch can be changed at the same time. The 309 movement type is Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 7 Inventory Management 274 used to change material or batch quantities in stock. Use the Post Goods Movements app to post changes in material or changes in batches.  Stock usability Transfer postings that result in a change in stock usability involve a change in the stock type. In general, most stock types can be transferred interchangeably. How- ever, if quality management is active for a material in a plant, then transfers into or out of quality inspection stock must be done in conjunction with a quality manage- ment process, such as inbound inspection.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA

Use the Transfer Stock—In- Plant app for transfer postings from one stock type to another within a plant.  Stock ownership If you have stocks delivered to your facility by a supplier on a consignment basis and you wish to take financial ownership of these stocks prior to consumption, you enter a transfer posting to recognize that fact. Similarly, if you accept returns of stock delivered on a consignment basis to your customer, you post a transfer post- ing as well.

docs.text: 275 7.4 Physical Inventory ances also optimize the benefits of MRP for assuring availability of material for produc- tion and sales processes. The system provides a variety of physical inventory methods to accomplish this requirement. Regardless of the method used, all physical inventory processes encom- pass the following three phases (see Figure 7.29): 1. Creation of the physical inventory documents 2. Entry of the physical counts into SAP S/4HANA 3. Posting of physical inventory differences Figure 7.29 Physical Inventory Process Phases A physical inventory document is required to start the process.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This document forms the basis for planning and performing a physical inventory, for recording counts, and for posting any differences found between the system and the physical stocks. Physical inventory documents contain a header, which holds information about the count event itself, such as the document number, the person responsible for the count, and the planned count date. Line items on the physical inventory document contain the materials being counted and hold the system and actual count information. Stocks are counted in inventory management based on the following:  Material  Plant  Storage location  Stock type  Valuation type/batch  Special stock Each combination of these elements will be counted separately during a physical inventory.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Print physical inventory lists Enter count Post differences Create physical inventory documents 1 Stock count 2 Analyze differences 3 Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 7 Inventory Management 276 The method of creating physical inventory documents is dependent on the technique used for the count. SAP S/4HANA supports the following techniques:  Manual physical inventory (spot inventory)  Annual physical inventory  Continuous physical inventory  Cycle counting  Sample-based physical inventory For additional information on these physical inventory methods, consult the SAP Help website. Once the documents are created, it is common to print the physical inventory count sheets. These are then distributed to the counters, who record the physical quantities on the sheet.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Count sheets can be transferred to a mobile application for counting as well. After the physical count is recorded, this information is entered into the SAP S/4HANA system. The system can provide feedback to the entry clerk if the quantity recorded during the count exceeds the system count based on a defined threshold percentage. This helps prevent data entry errors. Once the counts are entered, they can be analyzed by authorized personnel. This anal- ysis may result in a recount of the material in that storage location.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Once the physical inventory counts are confirmed, any differences detected need to be posted to inven- tory management so that the physical and system counts are reconciled. This action results in a goods movement posting either incrementing or decrementing the quan- tity of goods in stock. Financial postings are also made at the same time. SAP S/4HANA supplies apps to use in managing the physical inventory processes sup- ported by the system. There are apps to support the execution of a physical inventory and others for monitoring the physical inventory processes and reporting.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP sup- plies the following SAP Fiori apps to support physical inventory processes:  Create Physical Inventory Documents  Schedule Physical Inventory Document Creation  Manage Physical Inventory Count  Manage Physical Inventory Documents  Cycle Counting—Classification These apps are described in more detail in the following sections. The system also con- tains legacy apps for managing the physical inventory process, which will be described as well. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 283 7.5 Reporting in Inventory Management 7.5 Reporting in Inventory Management Proper control of physical stocks requires a robust set of reporting capabilities. S/4HANA builds on SAP ERP’s inventory management reporting strengths by adding new capabili- ties to visualize the current stock situation, thus enabling fast action in the case of logis- tics bottlenecks. These capabilities include inventory analytics, which show key perfor- mance indicators in real time, and the inventory overview pages, new in SAP S/4HANA, which show multiple key analytics on a single screen.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There are a number of inventory management reporting apps that come delivered with the SAP S/4HANA system. These apps can be broadly grouped into six types:  Inventory overview pages  Goods movements reporting apps  Stock balances reporting apps  Monitoring financial inventory values apps  Inventory management object pages  Inventory analytics We’ll discuss each type in the sections that follow. 7.5.1 Inventory Overview Pages Inventory overview pages allow inventory managers, analysts, and warehouse person- nel to see all relevant metrics for their operations on one page.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These metrics are arranged as actionable cards that can be rearranged or hidden. Filters can be applied to the overview pages, which instantly reflect on the displayed metrics. This allows the user to focus on important items, enabling decision-making and follow-on actions in a timely manner. For list cards, selecting the header of a card brings you to the app itself; selecting an item shows more detailed item information. For graphical or analytical cards, selecting the card displays detailed analytical information.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Display Physical Inventory Progress MIDO Use this app to get an overview of the progress of physical inventories in your facility. Inventory manager Display PI Document Line Items for Materials MI22 Use this app to determine the physi- cal inventory documents used to count specific materials over time. docs.text: 303 7.5 Reporting in Inventory Management SAP S/4HANA supplies the following inventory management analytics apps for use by inventory managers:  Goods Movement Analysis  Inventory Turnover Analysis  Slow or Non-Moving Materials  Dead Stock Analysis  Inventory KPI Analysis We’ll discuss each app in the following sections. docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Goods Movement Analysis app has the following features:  Define filters to narrow your search scope, such as plant, material, and material group.  Choose from a variety of dimensions for analysis, such as plant, storage location, material, year/month, calendar week, and day of year.  Choose from a variety of key figures, such as stock change quantity, stock change amount, consumption quantity, consumption amount, movement count, issue count, and receipt count.  Drill down to an individual material document item if required. Inventory Turnover Analysis The Inventory Turnover Analysis app (see Figure 7.58) assists you in monitoring the turnover of material in a plant. Turnover is defined as the relation between goods issue quantities and stock quantities within a set time period. This app provides detailed information on materials that have turnover issues based on a specified time horizon.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Inventory Turnover Analysis app lets you do the fol- lowing:  Perform research on turnover-related issues down to individual materials.  Display detailed turnover analysis results using different representations—for example, as a scatter or bubble chart.  See the stock value of materials with turnover issues; stock value calculation is based on stock quantity of the selected reporting date multiplied by the current material price. The Inventory Turnover Analysis app is assigned to the inventory manager standard authorization role.

docs.text: The app compares a KPI over two defined time periods and visually represents this in a meaningful way. There are five KPIs that can be monitored using this app:  Stock Changes Change in stock values in the company code currency over the specified time period.  Consumption Changes Change in consumption values of materials over the time period. Consumption value is the sum of the consumption quantities times the current material price.  Inventory Aging Changes Changes in the percentage relationship between the average stock quantity and the consumption quantity over the time period. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 307 7.6 Configuring Inventory Management  Inventory Turnover Changes Changes in the relationship between consumption quantities and average stock quantities in the time period.  Range of Coverage Changes Changes in the relationship between the current stock quantity and the average con- sumption (defined as the relationship between consumption and number of days in the time period) in the time period. Details on the KPI calculation logic can be found in the app documentation on the SAP Help website. The Inventory KPI Analysis app is assigned to the inventory analyst standard authori- zation role.

docs.text: Figure 7.61 Inventory KPI Analysis App 7.6 Configuring Inventory Management Inventory management is a core supply chain capability of the SAP S/4HANA system. Inventory management functions are delivered by SAP to work based on standard set- tings. However, to realize the full features and functionalities of this component to support an enterprise’s goals, the system does need to be fine-tuned based on business requirements. This section details the standard SAP-recommended configuration steps for inventory management.

docs.text: 7 Inventory Management 308 With SAP S/4HANA, it is possible to take advantage of the SAP Best Practices activation approach for customizing, as explained in Chapter 2. However, if you use the tradi- tional customizing approach, this section can help. This information also helps validate the SAP standard configuration.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The following management configuration elements are described in the sections ahead:  General configuration elements – Number Assignment assigns customer number ranges to inventory management documents.  Configuration elements for goods receipts and goods issues – Set Expiration Date Check controls how expiration date checking is done in a plant. – Allow Negative Stocks controls whether negative stock balances are allowed and in which storage locations.  Configuration elements for movement types – Record Reasons for Movement Types assigns specific codes to describe the pur- pose of a goods movement. – Copy, Change Movement Types allows the creation of new movement types.  Configuration elements for stock transport purchase orders – Define Shipping Data for Plants assigns the customer and sales area data needed to process stock transport orders with delivery documents. – Configure Delivery Type & Availability Check Procedure by Plant determines the delivery document types used for intracompany and intercompany stock trans- port orders for a plant. – Assign Document Type, One-Step Procedure, Underdelivery Tolerance assigns the proper outbound delivery document type for a specific plant pair.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It also contains settings to control one-step or two-step processing and tolerances for goods receipt.  Configuration elements for physical inventory – Default Values for Physical Inventory sets the values that default into each physi- cal inventory document. – Settings for Physical Inventory sets additional values for the control of the physi- cal inventory process for each plant. – Allow Freezing of Book Inventory Balances in Storage Locations controls the freez- ing behavior of book inventories during the physical inventory process. – Cycle Counting sets specific controls for cycle counting per plant. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

Number Assignment All goods movements in the SAP S/4HANA system result in material documents. Based on the transaction/event type of the goods movement, a unique number is assigned from a specific number range to the document. Transaction/event types that are rele- vant for SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement in the system are listed in Table 7.3. docs.text: In this section, we’ll explore how to set expiration date checks and how to allow negative stocks. Set Expiration Date Check SAP S/4HANA can check that a perishable item has sufficient shelf life remaining at the time of goods receipt. To do this, a minimum remaining shelf life has to be maintained in the material master record. In addition, the ability to check shelf life for each plant and movement type has to be maintained in configuration. These checks are not enabled in the standard SAP S/4HANA system. The menu path to enable shelf life expiration date checks is IMG (SPRO)  Materials Management  Inventory Management and Physical Inventory  Goods Receipt  Set Expiration Date Check .

docs.text: 7 Inventory Management 312 Allow Negative Stocks Normally there needs to be sufficient stock in a storage location prior to a goods issue or transfer movement that depletes the stock. However, the SAP S/4HANA system can allow negative stock balances for unrestricted stocks in a storage location if the record- ing of goods receipts into that storage location can’t always be done in a timely man- ner. The default setting is to not allow negative stock balances. To make these settings, navigate to IMG (SPRO)  Materials Management  Inventory Management and Physical Inventory  Goods Issue/Transfer Postings  Allow Negative Stocks .

docs.text: In this section, we’ll discuss recording reasons for movement types and how to copy and change movement types. Record Reasons for Movement Types It’s possible to have the system record a reason for a goods movement at the time of posting. For example, you can require a reason to be entered when a goods issue to scrapping is performed. With this configuration item, you can require the entry of a reason for a specific movement type and also maintain the valid reasons that can be selected. To make these settings, navigate to IMG (SPRO)  Materials Management  Inventory Management and Physical Inventory  Movement Types  Record Reasons for Movement Types .

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: For instance, you may want new move- ment types to handle a goods issue for consumption to support research and develop- ment. SAP S/4HANA allows you to create new movement types to support your enterprise’s requirements. There are three rules to follow when creating new movement types: 1. Always copy an existing movement type that is similar to the type of movement you are creating. For example, if you’re creating a new goods issue movement type, copy Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

Copy all dependent entries, as there is a large amount of integration of inventory management with other areas of SAP S/4HANA, such as finance and quality management. Don’t attempt to create a move- ment type from scratch! 2. Always copy the copied movement type’s reversal movement type as well. All move- ment types require a reversal movement. 3. There are ranges of codes that SAP sets aside for customer-created movement types. Most SAP S/4HANA customers create new movement types that start with Y, Z, or 9.

docs.text: 325 7.6 Configuring Inventory Management Allow Freezing of Book Inventory Balances in Storage Locations This configuration item allows you to determine if freezing of book inventories will be done when physical inventory documents are activated. If book inventories are frozen, inventory differences found during the count will be calculated from the frozen stock balance. If book inventories are not frozen, then inventory differences will be calcu- lated from the stock balance at the time the count is recorded. This indicator can be set at the storage location level.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 327 Chapter 8 Contract and Scheduling Agreement Management Purchase contracts and scheduling agreements are agreements made by a buying organization with a supplier for materials and services over a specified period of time. These long-term arrangements are often the result of supplier negotiations and are often linked to legal contract doc- uments. This chapter describes the process of managing and monitoring these documents, including creation, execution, monitoring analysis, and renewal in SAP S/4HANA. This chapter explains the processes used to manage outline agreements in SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Outline agreements are documents used to manage delivery of goods or services from a supplier over a specified period of time. Outline agreements in SAP S/4HANA come in two forms: contracts and scheduling agreements. The properties and apps used to manage and analyze these documents are described in the sections ahead. We’ve also provided the detailed configuration steps required in SAP S/4HANA to set up contracts and sched- uling agreements based on your enterprise’s requirements. Businesses are becoming increasingly competitive and success-driven in today’s digi- tal economy.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: To be a successful organization, it’s essential that the procurement pro- cess, which is one of the core lines of business for any industry, is run with high efficiency and low costs. Most companies use the concept of longer-term purchasing agreements with suppliers to achieve procurement process optimization and improved financial performance. Such agreements are defined as outline purchase agreements , which may be referred to as blanket or umbrella agreements outside SAP systems. Outline purchase agreements in SAP S/4HANA consist of contracts, centrally agreed upon contracts, distributed contracts, scheduling agreements, and scheduling agreements referencing a centrally agreed upon contract.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The solution addressing these agreements is referred to as purchase contract management under the sourcing and contract management stream in SAP S/4HANA, as shown in Figure 8.1. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 8 Contract and Scheduling Agreement Management 328 Figure 8.1 Sourcing and Contract Management 8.1 What Is Contract and Scheduling Agreement Management? Contract and scheduling agreement management within SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement refers to the management of long-term purchasing arrangements with suppliers for supply of materials or performance of services. Purchases made with ref- erence to these documents help streamline the procurement process. Well-designed contracts and scheduling agreements can help reduce prices and guarantee on-time supply, which helps plan and optimize the business processes of both the purchasing organization and the supplying organization.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The analytics capabilities and innova- tions offered by SAP S/4HANA enable procurement processes that are in real time and efficient. A purchase contract is a document created and maintained in the SAP S/4HANA sys- tem. This document holds all the information relevant to the agreement between the purchasing organization and the supplier. Once the quantities, prices, terms, and con- ditions are finalized, the purchase contract is created in the system. The different types of contracts and how they’re created in the system are explained in this section. 8.1.1 Types of Purchase Contracts A purchase contract is a type of supplier outline agreement in SAP S/4HANA that allows for the issue of release orders (a.k.a., call-off orders) for the agreed-upon materials or services of the contract over the life of the document.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A contract is suitable when a long-term agreement with a supplier is in place but the demand for the goods or ser- vices cannot be pinned to a predictable schedule. This means that release purchase orders are created, either manually or via materials planning, when they are needed to fulfill sales or production demands. These purchase contracts in SAP S/4HANA consist of items , which are materials, material groups, or services. It’s possible to create the fol- lowing types of contracts, depending on the business requirements: SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Contract Management Purchase Contract Management Source Assignment © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 329 8.1 What Is Contract and Scheduling Agreement Management?  Quantity contract This type of contract stipulates the quantity, negotiated price, and conditions for purchase of materials or services from the supplier with whom the contract is estab- lished. This allows the purchaser to issue multiple release orders to the supplier with reference to the contract until the total released quantity reaches the target quantity defined in the contract.  Value contract These contracts are generally used for purchasing materials or services that belong to certain material groups defined in materials management.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These contracts stipu- late the total value of the contract—which is also known as the target value —and of the material groups and the supplier. Specific materials or services are not listed as line items in the contract, but the contract allows purchase of materials or services that belong to the material groups that are listed as line items in the contract. Pur- chasers can create release orders for materials or services that belong to the material groups identified in the contract. This allows the purchaser to issue multiple release orders to the supplier with reference to the contract until the total released value reaches the target value defined in the contract.  Contract release order It’s possible to create a release order, which is simply a purchase order referencing a contract, using SAP GUI Transaction ME21N.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this transaction, if you enter the con- tract number in the Outline Agreement field under the Items pane, the system will populate all the information from the contract and expect you to input the quantity and delivery date. After creating the release order, it’s possible to edit and display the document using Transactions ME22N and ME23N. With the introduction of SAP Fiori apps in SAP S/4HANA, the UI has moved away from the old SAP GUI–based transac- tions to the new SAP Fiori UX, which is explained in the next section. 8.1.2 Manage Purchase Contracts The Manage Purchase Contracts app is used for creating and editing purchase contract documents.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These documents can be created either directly by entering all the data manually or by referencing purchase requisitions, RFQs/quotations, or existing con- tracts. With the introduction of SAP Fiori apps for SAP S/4HANA, the Manage Purchase Contracts app is used for creating or editing contracts, as follows: 1. Log into the SAP Fiori launchpad and click the Manage Purchase Contracts tile to open the app. 2. Click the Create button to create a contract. The header screen, shown in Figure 8.2, is presented for entering header information.

docs.text: 339 8.3 Contract Reporting and Analytics 8.3.2 Off-Contract Spend Often, purchases are made without using a negotiated price for materials or services. This may be because no negotiated price exists or because there is ignorance that a contract exists for that material or service. Procurement managers always want to know how much or what percentage of materials are procured outside of negotiated contracts. Analyzing this information helps buyers determine the types of products and areas in need of further contracts and negotiated prices.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA

Log into the SAP Fiori launchpad, navigate to the Contract Expiry app, and click its tile to execute the app. 8.4 Configuration To realize the features and functionalities of contract management, the system needs to be configured based on business requirements. This section provides the details of standard SAP-recommended configuration steps for contract management.

docs.text: These set- tings are made in the SAP S/4HANA system by following the customizing paths pro- vided in the following sections for each step. 8.4.1 Configuring Contracts With SAP S/4HANA, it’s possible to take advantage of the SAP Best Practices activation approach for customizing, as explained in Chapter 2. docs.text: 349 8.5 Scheduling Agreement 8.5 Scheduling Agreement Scheduling agreements are another form of outline purchase agreement in SAP S/4HANA. These agreements are used to procure materials over a specified period of time following a set schedule of delivery. The predetermined delivery schedules in the agreement indi- cate quantities of items and dates of delivery. These delivery schedules are periodically communicated to the supplier instead of sending purchase orders to meet the require- ments. Conditions for scheduling agreements can be maintained at the header level, which applies to all the items, or at the item level, which applies only to a specific item.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These agreements have the account assignment function, which allows the buyer to allocate costs by maintaining details of controlling objects at the item level within the docu- ment at the time of creation.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The benefits of using scheduling agreements include the following:  Shorten processing times and reduce the amount of paperwork required otherwise  Delivery schedule can replace a large number of discrete purchase orders or contract release orders  Reduced inventory  Possible to run manufacturing operations with the just-in-time principle  Suppliers require shorter lead times with smaller deliveries spread over a long period, resulting in better planning and efficient resource allocation for suppliers  Scheduling agreement can work in conjunction with MRP, especially in repetitive manufacturing involving large quantities There are several different types of scheduling agreements available in SAP S/4HANA. We will describe each type in detail.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: We will then describe the various apps available to create and manage these documents. We will also describe a useful app that lets you monitor spend and invoice history for scheduling agreement line items. 8.5.1 Scheduling Agreement Types The different types of scheduling agreements are defined in the SAP S/4HANA system by document types defined in customizing. The three document types that are pre- defined in the standard system are explained in the following sections. In addition to these three, it’s possible to define your own custom document types depending on your business requirements.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: More details are provided in Section 8.6. Scheduling Agreement with Release Document This type of scheduling agreement is created by choosing document type LPA. In this case, the schedule lines entered within the agreement aren’t transmitted to the sup- plier at the time of creation of the agreement and are internal to the system. The Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 8 Contract and Scheduling Agreement Management 350 schedule lines maintained in this agreement can be changed at any time during the life of the agreement, which allows some level of flexibility in scheduling procure- ment based on changing requirements. Whenever a scheduling agreement release is created, the information stored in the schedule lines is aggregated into time buckets, and then transmitted to the supplier. Two types of releases available with this type of scheduling agreement (LPA) are the forecast delivery schedule (FRC) and the just-in-time (JIT) delivery schedule.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The JIT delivery schedule is firm within a defined time fence, and the supplier can rely on these numbers rarely changing. The forecast delivery schedule is usually generated for time periods further out and used for planning purposes. The release documentation gener- ated in this process provides information about the releases transmitted to the sup- plier over a set period, and are stored in the SAP S/4HANA system for reference. Scheduling Agreement without Release Document This type of scheduling agreement is created by choosing document type LP.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The scheduling lines created in this type of agreement are external and official. This means that the scheduling lines are transmitted to the supplier as soon as they’re created. Also, there is no release documentation associated with this agreement. Stock Transport Scheduling Agreement If a company is procuring materials internally from another plant on a regular basis, it’s possible to set up a stock transport scheduling agreement by choosing document type LU at the time of creation. SAP standard uses item category U (Stock Transfer) for this type of agreement. 8.5.2 Managing and Creating Purchase Scheduling Agreements Scheduling agreements can be created manually or by referencing purchasing docu- ments such as purchase requisitions, RFQs/quotations, other scheduling agreements, or centrally agreed-upon contracts.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It’s possible to create a scheduling agreement by copying any one of the purchasing documents and then making changes before saving the agreement. Scheduling agreements can be created using the Manage Purchase Scheduling Agreements app. The Manage Purchase Scheduling Agreements app provides the capability to search and filter scheduling agreements by purchasing organization, agreement type, sup- plier, material, status, validity period, and more. It allows the user to display, copy, edit, create, and delete scheduling agreements.

docs.text: 355 8.6 Customizing Scheduling Agreements 8.6 Customizing Scheduling Agreements With SAP S/4HANA, it’s possible to take advantage of the SAP Best Practices activation approach for customizing, as explained in Chapter 2. However, if you use the tradi- tional customizing approach, this section can help. docs.text: 359 8.7 Integrating with SAP Ariba Contracts 8.7 Integrating with SAP Ariba Contracts SAP Ariba Contracts is a comprehensive contract management solution that allows an enterprise to create and manage legal contracts with their suppliers. These contracts can be collaboratively created in SAP Ariba, and then routed for approval in SAP Ariba. Once the contracts are fully approved and are ready for use, they can be automatically integrated into SAP S/4HANA for use as operational outline agreements. The steps in this flow are detailed here: 1.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Contract administrators create the contract document in SAP Ariba Contracts. The use of contract templates or copying from existing contracts are two options for manual creation. If integration with SAP Ariba Sourcing is available, then the con- tract as awarded in that module can be imported and augmented in SAP Ariba Con- tracts, thus speeding up contract creation. 2. The specific terms and conditions that apply to that contract are stipulated in the body of the contract, along with payment terms, validity periods, and a listing of the agreed upon items, contract quantities, and pricing that has been negotiated with the supplier. 3.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You then select the follow-on document type in the operational system. For SAP S/4HANA, this would be either a contract or a scheduling agreement document type. 4. The completed contract is then routed for approval through an approval process that is set up for your enterprise in SAP Ariba Contracts. 5. Once the contract approval is obtained, the contract is then released in SAP Ariba Contracts. This triggers the integration of the approved, released contract into SAP S/4HANA. 6. Once the outline agreement (contract or scheduling agreement) document is cre- ated via the integration, an optional approval process flow can be optionally kicked off in SAP S/4HANA for that document.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: As the document goes through the approval process in SAP S/4HANA, this progress is reflected via status changes that are sent back to SAP Ariba Contracts, which updates the original contract. 7. Once the operational document is fully approved in SAP S/4HANA, it can then be set up as a valid source of supply via a source list in SAP S/4HANA for automatic source assignment. 8. If the approved operational document is a value or quantity contract, purchase orders can now be created with reference to the contract document in the usual manner. 9.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If the approved operational document is a scheduling agreement, then delivery schedule lines can be generated during materials planning, and delivery schedules can subsequently be created and transmitted to the supplier. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 8 Contract and Scheduling Agreement Management 360 8.8 Summary Contract and scheduling agreement management is a core area for procurement orga- nizations. Without an existing agreement in place, it’s difficult to drive disciplined pric- ing and terms. Contracts can be tied to catalog items to underpin a clear ordering process and user experience, representing a model way to conduct corporate purchas- ing. SAP S/4HANA updates many older transaction codes and screens with SAP Fiori apps, but much of the setup and configuration remains the same.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: However, there are now shortcuts in the form of SAP Best Practices activation, which automatically sets up standard functionality in the system. This chapter focused on the operational contracts and scheduling agreements. Organi- zations can also use SAP S/4HANA to manage their legal contract documents as well. The next chapter will focus on the SAP offerings for enterprise contract management and assembly. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 361 Chapter 9 Enterprise Contract Management and Assembly SAP S/4HANA Cloud for enterprise contract management is a suite of applications designed and developed for the creation and governance of legal content in enterprises. It can be integrated into all core business processes, such as procurement processes, sales and distribution, inter- nal policies, and intercompany agreements. SAP S/4HANA Cloud for enterprise contract management provides a central repository for all legal documents, such as contracts, policies, and nondisclosure agreements.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This solution provides the capability to trace both internal and external tasks, signatures, and responsibilities. In this chapter, we’ll cover the features and functionalities pro- vided by this solution and the SAP Fiori apps for process executions. We’ve provided the customizing steps required in SAP S/4HANA for implementation of this solution. SAP offers this solution to create and manage legal content in an organization. It can be deployed as SAP S/4HANA Cloud for enterprise contract management, private edition or SAP S/4HANA Cloud for enterprise contract management, public edition.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP S/4HANA Cloud for enterprise contract management comprises two innovative solu- tions to manage enterprise contracts and other legal content across the enterprise: SAP S/4HANA for enterprise contract management and SAP Enterprise Contract Assembly are seamlessly integrated here. 9.1 What Is Enterprise Contract Management and Assembly? Legal content in SAP S/4HANA includes contracts, agreements, security policies, and other documents with legal significance in an organization. Such content is generated throughout an enterprise as part of different business processes, including procure- ment and sales and distribution.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Legal content could include company policies and intercompany agreements as well. SAP S/4HANA Cloud for enterprise contract man- agement is designed and developed for the creation and management of legal content in enterprises. This solution allows such legal content to be integrated into the core business processes of SAP S/4HANA and also provides the ability to store the content in a single repository. This means that an organization has complete control over all the legal content relevant to the company. Some of the challenges faced by businesses Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 9 Enterprise Contract Management and Assembly 362 today in enterprise contract management include distributed repositories for storage of legal content, lack of comprehensive search capabilities, unstructured content in multiple formats, no consistent risk and compliance management, inefficient or unclear workflow in document processing, and content management in silos within the organization. The new approach with enterprise contract management in SAP is to provide a central layer for legal content within SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The concept is to use legal content as mas- ter data and allow all information to follow the same data structure and be categorized semantically. This makes it possible to create and reuse text blocks and adapt to chang- ing regulations and business needs.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The new features offered for enterprise contract management are as follows:  Single repository for all legal documents  Search for legal content (e.g., contracts)  Request a new contract  Manage different versions of legal documents  Upload of a signed contract into a contract repository  Monitor contracts (e.g., expiration, open issues)  Link legal content to an operational real estate contract  Link legal content to an operational purchase contract  Link legal content to an RFQ  Trigger/create workflows for reviewing, informing, approving, and processing legal content  Collaborate internally  Send reminders about action items for managed contracts  Manage contract relationship hierarchies  Save all contract related documentation and communication together with the con- tracts  Standardize contract management scenarios SAP Enterprise Contract Assembly lets you create and manage the complete lifecycle of templates and text blocks that can be used for generating virtual legal documents that are used in enterprise contract management.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This solution offers the legal experts of the enterprise a way to create and manage clauses and templates for the creation of legal content. It integrates seamlessly into SAP S/4HANA Cloud for enterprise contract management and enables the automatic assembly of legal contracts and other legal documents based on clauses and templates developed by legal experts. The integration of SAP S/4HANA Cloud for enterprise contract management with SAP Enterprise Con- tract Assembly enables the business to integrate with all core business processes. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

A context covers a particular business scenario, such as procurement or sales and distribution processes, and provides a foundation for how a legal transaction is processed and what kind of information needs to be provided. Log into the SAP Fiori launchpad, navigate to the Manage Contexts app, and click its tile to execute the app. This app displays existing contexts and allows for filtering/search by Context ID, Owner , Status , Editing Status , and validity dates, as shown in Figure 9.5.

However, the user can add addi- tional categories if needed. 3. docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA

docs.text: To access this app, log into the SAP Fiori launchpad, navigate to the Manage Workflow Templates app, and click its tile. docs.text: This solution ensures legal compliance and increases contracting performance. docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 391 Chapter 10 External Sourcing Procurement of materials and services is one of the main functions of most business organizations. Identifying the best sources for those materials and services in terms of price, timeliness, quality, and so on is one of the important tasks of a purchasing organization. Whether fulfilling a one-time requirement of high-value items or a continuing require- ment of any item, a buyer engages in a strategic process of finding one or more sources to fulfill the requirement from a pool of competing suppliers.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This process is generally known as strategic sourcing and sometimes known as external sourcing . Sourcing within a procurement function is the process of finding suppliers of goods and services for an organization. Sourcing in SAP S/4HANA uses the request for quotation pro- cess, which begins with a purchase requisition and ends with creation and award of a pur- chase order or a contract. This process involves communication between the purchasing organization and suppliers who are external to the SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: With the intro- duction of SAP S/4HANA, this sourcing solution is offered as an extended solution linked to SAP Ariba’s cloud applications, which enables external communication and interaction with the suppliers. SAP provides standard integration between SAP S/4HANA and the SAP Ariba solutions required for this sourcing process. Because SAP Ariba solutions are used by both buyers and suppliers, this approach eliminates the need for every purchasing organization to create a dedicated portal for the suppliers to interact.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this chapter, we’ll cover the complete end-to-end external sourcing business pro- cess, including variations available within sourcing in SAP S/4HANA. All the SAP Fiori apps offered in this solution are explained and illustrated with screenshots. We’ve also provided the configuration steps and illustrative screenshots to help you implement the entire solution. 10.1 Sourcing Strategies A sourcing solution is offered in SAP S/4HANA that integrates with SAP Ariba and SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network helps establish easy and quick connections to millions of suppliers worldwide who are already in the network.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: In this approach, the sourcing process is initiated in SAP S/4HANA, from which you reach out to suppliers in SAP Business Network, identify the sources through SAP Ariba Sourcing, award the Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 10 External Sourcing 392 suppliers in SAP Ariba Sourcing, and bring the data back to SAP S/4HANA to create a purchase contract or purchase order to complete the process. The process flow is shown in Figure 10.1. Within SAP Best Practices, this scope item is known as sourcing with SAP Ariba Sourcing. Figure 10.1 Sourcing with SAP Ariba Sourcing: Process Flow Sourcing optimization is achieved in SAP S/4HANA with the help of the SAP Fiori apps described in the next section, as well as the features and functionalities available within SAP Ariba solutions.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The sourcing solution helps achieve the following:  Provides visibility and identifies savings opportunities  Standardizes source-to-contract processes across business units © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 393 10.2 Request for Quotation  Drives materials cost savings and optimization across all spend categories  Increases speed and efficiency across different teams  Reduces risk by finding better suppliers and innovation partners 10.2 Request for Quotation A request for quotation (RFQ) is a request from a purchasing organization of a company that’s sent to suppliers, soliciting them to submit a quotation for the supply of materi- als or services. The request for quotation document is a purchasing document created in the SAP S/4HANA system either from a purchase requisition or by copying an exist- ing RFQ.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: RFQs also can be created manually without referencing any other document. RFQs for lean services can be created by selecting Services as the Product Type Group at the item level. It’s possible to create a single RFQ that contains both material and service items. It’s important to note that the RFQs created in the new SAP Fiori app can’t be viewed or pro- cessed in the SAP GUI environment and vice versa. The RFQ and quotation solution offered using SAP GUI processes and transactions in SAP ERP isn’t a strategic choice in SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Support for this legacy RFQ solution is likely to end at some point in the future. 10.2.1 Sourcing with SAP Ariba Sourcing and SAP Business Network Sourcing is the ability of the purchasing organization to work in collaboration with the millions of suppliers available in SAP Business Network. The buyers together with the suppliers can improve efficiency and meet compliance requirements across the entire sourcing process. This approach incorporates seamless processes, transparent commu- nications between the buyers and suppliers, and trust between the parties involved in the sourcing process.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Sourcing capability is achieved through SAP Ariba Sourcing. This section explains the process steps on the SAP S/4HANA side. In this process, once the RFQ is created and published in SAP S/4HANA, it’s sent to SAP Ariba Sourcing, where a sourcing request is created based on the RFQ received from SAP S/4HANA. The RFQ type used for this process in SAP S/4HANA is an external sourcing request . The buyer then creates a sourcing project in SAP Ariba Sourcing with reference to the sourcing request and publishes the project.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This sourcing project results in RFQs in the SAP Ariba Sourcing application for the suppliers to respond to. The suppliers can access these RFQs and submit their responses or quotations through their SAP Ariba accounts in SAP Ariba Sourcing. After the RFQ closing time, the buyer can review all the responses from different suppliers, compare them, and award one or more suppliers in SAP Ariba Sourcing. The awarded quotations are automatically sent to SAP S/4HANA, in which purchase orders or contracts are created, depending on the document type selected in SAP Ariba Sourcing.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 10 External Sourcing 394 10.2.2 Sourcing with Standalone SAP S/4HANA It is possible to execute sourcing without utilizing SAP Ariba integration. In this sce- nario, a request for quotation is created in the SAP S/4HANA system. Bidders are selected, and the request for quote is sent out of the SAP S/4HANA system directly. Responses from the bidders to the RFQ are received back via email or other communi- cation channels and then manually entered into the system. The received quotes can then be compared. Once the winning bid is selected by the sourcing group, it is marked as awarded in SAP S/4HANA, and another communication is sent to the winning sup- plier.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The losing bids can also receive a communication as well. The winning bid can then be manually converted by the sourcing group into a purchase order or a contract, depending on the situation. 10.2.3 Quote Automation for Procurement If a purchasing organization is interested in requesting only price and quantity infor- mation or shipping costs, it’s possible to use the external price request RFQ type. This RFQ type, once saved and published in SAP S/4HANA, is sent to SAP Business Network, where the suppliers can create their responses.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These bids submitted by suppliers through their SAP Ariba accounts are sent back to SAP S/4HANA, where they can be processed. The buyer can compare the bids (quotations) received, award one of those in the SAP S/4HANA system, and then create a purchase order or contract from that win- ning bid. This process, called quote automation integration for procurement , is now integrated into the automation of source-to-pay with the SAP Business Network best practice. 10.2.4 Request for Price This RFQ process helps the buyer to create price requests in SAP S/4HANA and send them directly to suppliers by email or send a printed version by mail.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The internal sourcing request RFQ type is used for this process. Suppliers respond to the RFQ by pro- viding their quotations via email or mail. The buyer manually creates quotations in the SAP S/4HANA system using the Manage Supplier Quotations app based on the quota- tions received from the suppliers. The quotations created in the SAP S/4HANA system are compared, and the best one is awarded. It’s possible to award the best quotation in one of the following ways: directly within the quotation by clicking Award , from the list in the Manage Supplier Quotations app, or from the list in the Compare Supplier Quo- tations app.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: After awarding the quotation, the follow-on document, either a purchase order or a contract, is created in SAP S/4HANA. Quotations that do not meet the requirements should be set to Rejected or Completed manually. After completion of this process, the RFQ may be set to Completed as well. The process flow is shown in Fig- ure 10.2. Within SAP Best Practices, this scope item is known as request for price . © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 395 10.3 SAP Fiori Apps for External Sourcing Figure 10.2 Request for Price: Process Flow 10.3 SAP Fiori Apps for External Sourcing There are several SAP Fiori apps that are used to enable the external sourcing processes described in the previous section. In the following sections, we will describe each of these apps in detail. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 10 External Sourcing 396 10.3.1 Manage Requests for Quotation The Manage Requests for Quotation SAP Fiori app is used to create RFQs in the SAP S/4HANA system. The RFQ created is sent to SAP Ariba Sourcing based on the configu- ration explained later in this chapter. Then the sourcing process is carried out in SAP Ariba and the awarded quotation is sent back to SAP S/4HANA to create a purchase order or purchase contract. This SAP Fiori app provides the capability to display the list of all existing RFQs and to search for RFQs by RFQ Number , RFQ Type , Status , Company Code , Purchasing Organi- zation , Purchasing Group , Quotation Deadline , and so on.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This app also helps copy an existing RFQ, create a new RFQ from scratch, and delete an RFQ. It’s possible to custom- ize the filters and display columns, as shown in Figure 10.3. Here you can do the follow- ing:  Customize and save your own filter settings  Customize the filter bar individually  Copy , Delete , or Create a request for quotation  Customize and save your own table layout From this app, you also can display an existing RFQ by clicking any of the listed RFQs. This allows the user to review all the information within the RFQ, including output details/status, legal transactions associated with the RFQ, and process flow.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Manage Requests for Quotation app is assigned to the purchaser standard authorization role. docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 10 External Sourcing 398 The system adds all the information, including item details, from the purchase requisi- tion. It’s also possible to specify the follow-on document, either a purchase order or con- tract, for the RFQ on this screen. This app allows you to maintain delivery and payment terms, add bidders if desired, and add attachments. Once all values are entered, the RFQ is published. At this point, the RFQ is sent from SAP S/4HANA to SAP Ariba Sourcing. Then the sourcing process is carried out in SAP Ariba and the awarded quotation is sent back to SAP S/4HANA to create a purchase order or purchase contract.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Process Pur- chase Requisitions app is assigned to the purchaser standard authorization role. 10.3.3 Monitor Request for Quotation Items The Monitor Request for Quotation Items app, shown in Figure 10.6, enables the strate- gic purchaser to monitor RFQ items. It allows the user to display the list of all the RFQ items in a table view, along with a chart for awarded quotation value and submitted quotation value. By default, the chart is displayed per supplier; you can change the set- tings to display the chart per company code, plant, purchasing organization, and many more options.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The app provides options to choose the chart type, such as bar chart, line chart, pie chart, and more. The output results can be filtered by RFQ number, RFQ type, quotation deadline, purchasing category, material group, company code, plant, pur- chasing organization, and so on. The user can select any RFQ item to view the corre- sponding quotes and general information and navigate to view contextual information related to a supplier or material. The Monitor Request for Quotation Items app is assigned to the purchaser standard authorization role.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 399 10.3 SAP Fiori Apps for External Sourcing 10.3.4 Compare Supplier Quotations The Compare Supplier Quotations app (see Figure 10.7) enables the purchaser to com- pare supplier quotations received against an RFQ and to find the best offer. It allows you to search for a specific RFQ and display all quotations received for it; it also allows you to check whether all the invited suppliers have submitted their quotations. To select the quotation to be awarded, press the radio button next to the quotation num- ber. Selecting Award creates a purchase order or contract.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Document icon exports the list of quotations to a spreadsheet. In this app, you can see how to do the following:  Select the best quotation  Create a purchase order or contract  Export the list of quotations to a spreadsheet The app displays an overview of all quotations for a selected RFQ, providing informa- tion such as basic supplier data, total net value (which reflects the complete net costs for the goods or services, including transportation costs), and fully quoted items (fully quoted items are items that the supplier can deliver in the requested quantity).

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 10.7 Compare Supplier Quotations App This app identifies the lowest-priced item as the best-priced item. Other factors, such as supplier evaluation score, are not included in the calculation. The purchaser can award the best quotation directly from this app and create a purchase order or con- tract. The Compare Supplier Quotations app is assigned to the purchaser standard authorization role. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

It also allows the user to select any quotation and view its detailed information. The Manage Supplier Quota- tions app is assigned to the purchaser standard authorization role.
