docs.text: Figure 10.8 Manage Supplier Quotations App The app’s features include the following:  Search for a quotation by quotation number, type, status, submission date, supplier, RFQ number, RFQ type, and more  Display detailed information for a quotation by selecting the quotation from the search result list  Display item details, such as the actual item, quantity, and pricing details  Submit quotations that are in the In Preparation status  Edit quotations that are in the In Preparation or Submitted status  Delete quotations that are in the In Preparation status © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 401 10.3 SAP Fiori Apps for External Sourcing  Award quotations  Set quotations to Completed  Navigate to detailed information about suppliers and RFQs 10.3.6 Manage Workflows for RFQs The Manage Workflows for RFQs app enables the business process specialist to config- ure workflows for RFQs in the SAP S/4HANA system. Both one-level approval by the manager of the workflow initiator and multilevel approval by the manager of the work- flow initiator and by higher-level managers are possible. This app allows the user to perform the following activities:  Display the list of existing workflow definitions.  Display detailed information for a workflow definition.  Create new workflows and define the step sequence.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can define the start condi- tions and the order in which the start conditions are checked. You can also define the order of the steps. If you have more than one workflow defined, the workflow is selected depending on the fulfilment of the start condition.  Copy an existing workflow and modify it according to your business needs.  Set validity periods for workflows and activate or deactivate workflows. 10.3.7 Manage Workflows for Supplier Quotation The Manage Workflows for Supplier Quotation app lets you define an approval process for supplier quotations, which allows the approver to check the awarded quotations before a follow-on document is created.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The awarded quotation can be approved or rejected. For external sourcing request (RE) types, the workflow process isn’t relevant because these quotations are approved and awarded in SAP Ariba Sourcing. The default setting for quotations of the price quotation (RSI) and internal quotation (RQ) types is auto- matic approval. This app helps the user define a workflow process based on the busi- ness requirements for these quotation types. Both one-level approval by the manager of the workflow initiator and multilevel approval by the manager of the workflow initi- ator and by higher-level managers are possible.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This app comes with the following standard features:  Display the list of existing workflow definitions  Display the details of an existing workflow definition  Create new workflows by defining start conditions and step sequence  Copy an existing workflow to create a new start conditions  Activate or deactivate workflows Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.text: 411 10.5 Configuring Flexible Workflow 10.5 Configuring Flexible Workflow In SAP S/4HANA, the process owners—such as the person responsible for the sourcing process—are provided with the tools necessary to configure the approval workflow rel- evant to the business processes they own. They can configure the workflow needed for the business processes themselves without needing to go to the IT department. This strategy empowers the process owner and eliminates costs associated with develop- ment. The Manage Workflows app allows process owners to use this new flexible work- flow procedure in SAP S/4HANA.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This approach also provides the flexibility to change the workflow as and when required to meet changing requirements. docs.text: 419 Chapter 11 Product Sourcing In this chapter, we delve into SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA, a dedicated solution tailored to the unique needs of the automotive and industrial manufacturing industries. We explore how this specialized software seamlessly integrates with SAP Ariba Central Procurement, private cloud edition and SAP Business Network, offering a comprehensive ecosystem that optimizes supplier management and drives collaboration within the direct sourcing processes.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The unique sourcing requirements of the automotive and industrial manufacturing sectors stem from the complex, highly engineered nature of their products, stringent quality standards, and the need for resilience in the face of supply chain challenges. Effective sourcing strategies in these industries require a deep understanding of tech- nical specifications, global supplier networks, and a focus on quality, cost, and long- term sustainability. Traditional sourcing solutions often need more specialized capabilities to manage the intricate bills of materials and stringent quality standards inherent to highly engi- neered automotive and industrial manufacturing products.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These solutions may strug- gle to navigate the complexities of global supplier networks and regulatory compliance specific to these industries. Consequently, the limitations of traditional sourcing tools hinder procurement teams from effectively addressing the unique challenges and requirements of materials cost management for such products, potentially leading to quality issues, production delays, and increased costs. SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA caters to the needs of automotive and industrial manufacturing indus- tries.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These solutions aim to assist procurement teams in streamlining sourcing proce- dures for direct materials and cost optimization of complex, highly engineered products. The solutions also offer benefits such as demand aggregation, supplier col- laboration, and simplified operationalization of contract terms. This chapter of the book provides a comprehensive overview of the suite, covering all its key components, process areas, and configuration options, making it a valuable resource for anyone seeking to leverage these solutions.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 11 Product Sourcing 420 11.1 What Is Product Sourcing? In the past, the automotive industry faced significant challenges with demand-driven lifecycles, particularly during the product design phase for traditional gasoline-powered cars. Lengthy lead times for design and manufacturing made it difficult to respond swiftly to changing market conditions or consumer preferences. The industry’s inflex- ible production lines and reliance on specific vehicle models hindered adaptability to shifts in demand, leading to large inventories and increased costs.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Moreover, the risk of obsolescence loomed as consumer preferences shifted toward electric vehicles (EVs) due to environmental concerns. Automotive companies, facing pressure from stricter emissions regulations and market competition from innovative EV startups, needed to make a fundamental shift in design and manufacturing pro- cesses. As a result, many companies began investing heavily in EV technology, necessi- tating not only a redesign of their products but also a transformation of their supply chains and manufacturing methods to stay relevant in an era of electric mobility.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This transformation underscored the importance of adaptability in an industry undergoing a profound shift toward sustainable transportation solutions. The transformations in the supply chain have a profound impact on procurement pro- cesses for several reasons. First, the emergence of global supply chains has expanded the pool of potential suppliers, increasing the complexity of supplier selection and evaluation. Second, advances in technology, such as supply chain automation and real- time data analytics, enable more efficient and data-driven procurement decisions.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Third, the shift toward sustainable and responsible sourcing practices necessitates rig- orous monitoring and compliance checks. Finally, the growing emphasis on supply chain resilience, in the face of disruptions like the COVID-19 pandemic, compels pro- curement teams to reassess risk management strategies and supplier relationships, ultimately shaping the way they source goods and services. A similar situation exists in the industrial manufacturing and components (IM&C) industry. The heightened competition in this industry necessitates aggressive cost management and rapid responses to market dynamics.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: With a more competitive land- scape, companies must focus on cost efficiency to maintain profitability and remain competitive. Quick responses to market changes, such as shifts in customer demand or emerging trends, are vital for staying ahead of rivals and capturing new opportunities. Moreover, fluctuations in commodity prices can significantly impact production costs. Being able to swiftly adapt to these price changes, whether for raw materials or compo- nents, is crucial to maintain pricing competitiveness and profit margins.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Failing to respond promptly to rising commodity costs, for example, can erode profitability or result in higher product prices, potentially driving customers to competitors. The role of procurement in IM&C is pivotal as it directly influences product quality, cost, and supply chain efficiency. Procurement teams are responsible for sourcing raw materials, components, and services, ensuring the timely delivery of materials to © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 421 11.1 What Is Product Sourcing? support production. With innovations and process transformations, this role is grow- ing in significance. First, technological advancements in procurement, such as digital procurement plat- forms and data analytics, empower teams to make informed decisions, optimize sup- plier relationships, and identify cost-saving opportunities. Second, as these industries evolve with innovations like EVs and Industry 4.0, procurement becomes essential for securing specialized components and technologies.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Third, sustainability and responsi- ble sourcing are gaining prominence, making procurement instrumental in meeting environmental and ethical standards in the supply chain. Finally, global supply chain complexities require procurement professionals to navigate international markets, logistics, and regulatory requirements, further emphasizing their role in driving oper- ational excellence and maintaining a competitive edge in these dynamic industries. As businesses transform their processes, they need modern ERP systems that can han- dle large amounts of data, optimize workflows, and incorporate machine learning and artificial intelligence.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: SAP is a popular choice for clients looking to upgrade their sys- tems. However, with the end of support for SAP SRM, businesses are searching for pro- curement solutions that align with their strategic vision. SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA (see Figure 11.1) is an excellent option for sourcing and commodity man- agement teams. It allows them to establish high-value agreements for direct materials, such as raw materials, components, and assemblies. This solution is particularly useful for industries with rapidly changing demand, as it improves supplier collaboration on product development, shortening time to volume and reducing direct materials sourc- ing costs.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Moreover, because SAP Ariba Direct Materials Sourcing for Automotive and Industrial Manufacturing in SAP S/4HANA is integrated with SAP S/4HANA, it supports comprehensive sourcing program management and native access to procurement execution systems, material masters, and contract management functionality. As shown in Figure 11.1, the processes for development of new products (forward sourc- ing) and product lifecycles encompass various stages from the initial design to the eventual manufacturing and possible contract renegotiation.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Here’s an overview of each step: 1. Design product The process begins with the design of a new product. During this stage, product spec- ifications, features, and requirements are defined. Procurement teams collaborate closely with design and engineering departments to ensure that the product’s design is feasible and aligns with cost and sourcing considerations. 2. Develop procurement launch plan After finalizing the product design, a procurement launch plan is developed. This plan outlines the procurement strategy, supplier selection criteria, and sourcing requirements.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA

Source supply With the procurement launch plan in place, the next step is to identify and source the required materials, components, and suppliers. This involves supplier scouting, negotiations, and contract agreements to secure a reliable supply chain for the pro- duction of the new product. 4. Contract Procurement teams establish contractual agreements with selected suppliers. Con- tracts detail the terms and conditions of the supply, including pricing, delivery schedules, quality standards, and any other relevant terms.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Contracts are legally binding and set the framework for the supplier-buyer relationship. 5. Procure supply Once contracts are in place, the procurement team executes the procurement pro- cess. This includes issuing purchase orders, managing supplier relationships, and ensuring that the supply of materials and components is in alignment with the pro- duction schedule.

docs.text: 451 Chapter 12 Invoice and Payables Management Entry of a supplier invoice, matching this information with data from purchasing and receiving, and the subsequent processing of invoice data to facilitate payment completes the procure-to-pay process cycle enabled by SAP S/4HANA. Invoice management and payables management are essential end-to-end processes delivered with SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement. The entry and validation of a supplier’s invoice into the system records the billing details and enables the matching and approval processes.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Once the invoice is entered, matched, and optionally approved, the process to pay a supplier for the goods and services rendered is per- formed. These two processes complete the procure-to-pay end-to-end business pro- cess. This chapter will describe the applications supplied by SAP S/4HANA to enable the invoice processing and accounts payable business processes. We’ll first delve into sup- plier invoice processing, describing how to manage the entry and validation of invoices in the SAP S/4HANA system. Then we’ll explore the transactional and analytic apps that enable accounts payable, which results in optimal payments being rendered to suppli- ers.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Finally, we will touch on the integration of SAP Invoice Management by OpenText with SAP S/4HANA, SAP Ariba Central Invoice Management with SAP S/4HANA Cloud, and Taulia, an SAP company. 12.1 What Are Invoice and Payables Management? In invoice management, all pertinent details of a supplier invoice are entered into the system, which are then verified against both the purchasing documents to which they reference and the quantities of goods or services that have been received to date. If the document details, such as the prices and quantities in the entered invoice, match the information contained in the SAP S/4HANA system, then the supplier invoice docu- ment is accepted and posted to the system.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If discrepancies are found, then the docu- ments can be held or parked and the discrepancies addressed with the supplier and with the purchasing and receiving departments. Once the discrepancies are reconciled, then the supplier invoice document can be successfully posted in the system, with appropriate accounting documents created to reflect the general ledger impact of the invoice entry. Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 12 Invoice and Payables Management 452 In payables management, the accepted invoice becomes eligible for payment. A pay- ment proposal is generated by the system. Once the proposal is reviewed and approved, it is included in a subsequent payment run. Funds are then transferred from the enterprise to the supplier’s banking accounts via a variety of payment methods. The SAP S/4HANA system contains integrated capabilities to handle the complete invoice verification and payables processes.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: There are three main solution capabilities available in SAP S/4HANA:  Invoice processing Entry and validation of supplier invoices into the system  Accounts payable Processing of payments due to suppliers  Invoice collaboration Working with suppliers to integrate invoices and payables via SAP Business Network We’ll describe each solution’s capabilities in detail in the following sections. 12.2 Invoice Processing The invoice processing capability of SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement is focused on the entry, validation, and posting of supplier invoice details in the SAP S/4HANA system. The information contained in the invoice presented by the supplier is checked for accuracy against the customer’s referenced purchasing documents and the goods receipts that have been logged into the system.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Price, quantity, tax, and accounting information are all checked. If the total invoice amount is in balance with the reference documents, then the invoice document can be posted successfully in the system. The appropriate financial postings are also posted at the same time due to the integration of invoice processing with financial accounting. If the total invoice amount isn’t found to be in balance or additional information or expertise is needed to process the invoice document, then the invoice entry can be held or parked by the invoice entry processor for later processing by knowledgeable personnel.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Entry of supplier invoices that reference purchasing documents is supported, as are financial invoices without a specific purchase document reference. SAP S/4HANA brings many innovations to invoice processing. Managing supplier invoices in classic SAP ERP involved a good deal of transferring back and forth between multiple screens. First, selection criteria had to be entered on an invoice listing screen. The resulting report listed all invoice documents that satisfied the entered selection criteria. Detecting issues and resolving them involved moving back and forth between © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 453 12.2 Invoice Processing the invoice list screen and the invoice details screen. If you needed to change the selec- tion criteria of the invoice list, you needed to fully regenerate the invoice list first. With SAP S/4HANA, the dynamic search capabilities in the Manage Supplier Invoices app provide a streamlined way of selecting and managing invoices of concern. The many apps available to support invoice processing make the job of entering sup- plier invoices streamlined and simple.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The following native SAP Fiori apps for invoice processing are available:  Manage Supplier Invoices  Create Supplier Invoice  Supplier Invoices List  Display Supplier Balances Note The following SAP GUI for HTML transactional apps for invoice processing are also available from SAP:  Create Supplier Invoice (Advanced) (MIRO)  Display Supplier Invoice (Advanced) (MIR4)  Park Supplier Invoice (MIR7)  Release Blocked Invoices (MRBR)  Clear GR/IR Clearing Account (MR11)  Display/Cancel Account Maintenance (MR11SHOW)  Create Consignment and Pipeline Settlement (MRKO)  Create Evaluated Receipt Settlement (MRRL) We’ll take a deep dive into invoice processing in the next sections. First, we’ll look at the different types of supplier invoice documents available in SAP S/4HANA.

docs.text: Then we’ll describe the results of a successfully processed supplier invoice. Next, we’ll describe the two types of supplier invoice processing available. The methods of entering supplier invoices into SAP S/4HANA are described, along with detailed descriptions of the apps supporting invoice entry and reconciliation. Finally, we will describe supplier invoice reporting apps and useful object pages for this area. 12.2.1 Supplier Invoice Documents The supplier invoice document in SAP S/4HANA is a representation of the presentation and acceptance of a bill from a supplier to a customer.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: It also passes information needed to complete the procure-to-pay cycle to financial accounting. Entry of a sup- plier invoice document is a necessary step in most procure-to-pay processes; it ensures that a supplier will be paid for the goods or services provided. docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 12 Invoice and Payables Management 454 There are four types of supplier invoice documents supported by the SAP S/4HANA system:  A supplier invoice is a document presented by a supplier for reimbursement of goods or services rendered. It contains details about the supplier, bank information, iden- tification of items and quantities purchased, supplier pricing, unplanned delivery costs, and tax and account determination information.  A credit memo is a document used to record the entry of an invoice for a credit claimed from the supplier.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: This document arises from a return of defective goods, a reduction of an invoice, or for other reasons. These documents can be considered debits for the vendor. The accounting postings for credit memos typically are the reverse of a normal supplier invoice posting. Credit memos can be entered directly into the system or can be generated automat- ically via evaluated receipt settlement (ERS).  A subsequent credit invoice document is posted when you’ve entered and settled an invoice for which the supplier has billed you at too high a price.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The subsequent credit memo entered is a value-only document and doesn’t affect the quantities originally invoiced. It’s valuable to enter subsequent credits when needed in the sys- tem to preserve the invoice history.  A subsequent debit invoice document is posted when you’ve entered and settled an invoice for which the supplier has billed you at too low a price. The subsequent debit memo entered is value-only as well and doesn’t affect the quantities originally invoiced. Invoice documents can be created automatically in the system, based on regularly scheduled settlements of procurement processes.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These include ERS, consignment or pipeline settlement, or billing based on invoicing plans. These processes produce invoice documents based on data in your SAP S/4HANA system, rather than relying on a bill submitted by the supplier directly. 12.2.2 Results of Invoice Processing The following actions take place on successful posting of an invoice document in SAP S/4HANA:  A logistics invoice document is created to reflect the supplier billing details.  One or more financial documents are created based on the data entered.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: These finance documents reference and are traceable to the logistics invoice document. These documents post the amounts entered for the invoice line items to the appro- priate general ledger accounts.  The purchase order history in the referenced purchasing document line items is updated, which provides a complete audit trail of activities linked to line items.  If required, the prices on the material master are adjusted. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 455 12.2 Invoice Processing 12.2.3 Types of Supplier Invoice Verification There are two types of supplier invoice verification supported by the SAP S/4HANA sys- tem. They differ in the data that is proposed during the entry of the invoice document. These two types are purchase order-based invoice verification and goods receipt-based invoice verification. Purchase Order–Based Invoice Verification In the purchase order–based invoice verification technique, illustrated in Figure 12.1, the system generates one invoice line for each referenced purchase order item.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The quantities proposed during invoice entry are determined by the difference between the total delivered quantity and the total invoiced quantity. If the quantities and amounts on the supplier invoice differ from those proposed, as in the case of a partial goods receipt, these items will need to be adjusted by the invoice processor. Figure 12.1 Purchase Order–Based Invoice Verification Goods Receipt–Based Invoice Verification In the goods receipt–based invoice verification technique, illustrated in Figure 12.2, the quantities and amounts proposed on the invoice entry must match one or more goods receipts recorded in the SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.text: With goods receipt–based invoice verification, the invoice can’t be entered without a goods receipt reference. This procedure is useful if you want to ensure that goods have been received prior to posting a supplier’s invoice. docs.text: If desired, this same setting can be made at the purchasing organization and plant levels as well by maintaining alternate purchasing data for the business partner. This setting for a PIR is adopted into the purchasing document pref- erentially over the settings maintained in the supplier master. 12.2.4 Entry of Invoice Documents A supplier’s invoice can be entered via a variety of techniques into the SAP S/4HANA system.

docs.text: 457 12.2 Invoice Processing Online Invoice Entry Using SAP Fiori Apps Use the available online SAP Fiori apps to enter a supplier invoice when the document is presented to you via normal delivery methods, such as the postal service or email. The SAP S/4HANA system automatically adopts referenced documents to minimize data entry, and it verifies that the prices and quantities presented by the supplier match the information in your system. Basic header data about the invoice is entered into the system, such as the invoice date, invoice reference from the supplier, and total invoice amount.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A tax code can be entered here if needed. References to purchasing documents such as purchase orders, scheduling agreements, or service entry sheets are then entered. The system will adopt key information from these documents such as quantities, prices, and tax information, thereby speeding up invoice data entry and reducing errors. The system checks that the invoice data from the supplier matches the information in the reference documents. If the total amount doesn’t balance or is outside of config- ured tolerances, then the system will flag the invoice and won’t allow posting until cor- rections are made.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Sometimes freight charges passed onto you from the supplier are present on an invoice. If these weren’t planned for in the purchase order itself, this amount can be added to the invoice in the form of unplanned delivery costs. The invoice can be held, parked, saved as complete, or posted by the invoice processor as needed. Figure 12.3 shows these invoice statuses. Figure 12.3 Supplier Invoice Statuses Holding a document lets you save the invoice document in its current state, with only the minimum amount of validation.

docs.text: 12 Invoice and Payables Management 458 company code and supplier. A logistics invoice document is created during hold, but no financial documents are posted and no updates to purchase order history are per- formed. Held invoices need to be monitored and subsequently processed for the procure-to-pay process to continue. Parking an invoice document is useful if you’re missing data needed for posting and you don’t want to have to reenter the data. The invoice document doesn’t have to be in balance to be parked. A logistics invoice document is created, and the purchase order history is updated as well.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: An open, parked supplier line item is also generated and finance document numbers assigned. A duplicate invoice check also occurs during parking. Parking a document can trigger a workflow to commence further processing on the invoice document. Save as complete is another option that you can use if you have a complete, balanced document but don’t want to post the document at that point. Like parked documents, a logistics invoice document is created, and the purchase order history is updated as well. An open, saved-as-complete supplier line item also is generated and finance document numbers assigned.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: A duplicate invoice check also occurs when saving as complete. The SAP Fiori apps used to enter an invoice into the SAP S/4HANA system are described in more detail in the following sections. If required, entered invoices can go through an approval process. There are standard workflows available in the SAP S/4HANA system to route a supplier invoice document to approvers based on your company’s requirements. Posting a supplier invoice in SAP S/4HANA will typically result in the following post- ings:  Debit to the supplier subaccount of the invoicing supplier partner on the invoice  Credit to the GR/IR account Invoice Entry Using Electronic Data Interchange EDI can be used between two trading partners to facilitate the exchange of documents.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Transmitting a supplier invoice and the subsequent posting of that document in the system is a key process often enabled via this technique. The system validates the data sent by the supplier and, if acceptable, posts the invoice into the system without the need for human intervention. SAP S/4HANA supports multiple EDI protocols for the transmission and acceptance of supplier invoice documents. Invoice Entry via SAP Business Network SAP Business Network is a cloud-based business-to-business marketplace in which buyers and suppliers can connect and do business on a single, networked platform.

docs.text: 459 12.2 Invoice Processing Invoice Reduction If you dispute the values or quantities on the supplier invoice presented, you can reduce the invoice entered to match what you think is correct. This is known as invoice reduction in SAP S/4HANA (see Figure 12.4). To reduce an invoice, take the following steps:  Mark the line item as Vendor Error: Reduce Invoice .  Enter the reduced value or quantity (or both) into the reduction fields provided.  Verify the values and quantities given on the supplier invoice and enter them in the fields provided.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The system posts two documents when invoice reduction is used. First, an invoice doc- ument for the invoiced quantities and values is created. Second, a credit memo is gen- erated for the difference quantities and values. Optionally, you can also generate a complaint document that can be transmitted back to the supplier in this situation. Figure 12.4 Invoice Reduction Simulation of Invoice Postings SAP S/4HANA can simulate the accounting postings for an invoice prior to the actual posting of the invoice document. This capability allows the invoice processor to observe the general ledger account postings based on the entered data.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Click the Simulate button to see the resulting simulated postings. You can also post the invoice directly from the simulation if you wish. docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Create Supplier Invoice This native SAP Fiori app allows you to create a supplier invoice based on information received from your supplier. You can reference one or more purchase order items to which this invoice refers. Once entered, SAP S/4HANA compares the quantity and amount data for each supplier invoice item with the data of the related purchase order item. If goods receipt–based invoice verification has been defined for a purchase order item, the system compares the supplier invoice data with the related goods receipt data as well.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: If the quantities or amounts lie outside defined tolerances, the invoice is posted as automatically blocked for payment. An invoice approval process also can be triggered by the system based on your company’s requirements. When looking at the details, you can reverse a posted supplier invoice or release a blocked invoice. These features are available in the Create Supplier Invoice app (as shown in Figure 12.5 and Figure 12.6):  Create a new supplier invoice document. You can create credit memos, subsequent credits, and subsequent debits as well.  Edit fields on the invoice document, which the system then transfers to financial accounting.  Change the currency exchange rate displayed, if allowed by customization.  Enter invoice line items and reference them to one or more purchase orders for which the invoice was received.

These referenced items can also have multiple account assignments.  It’s possible to create a supplier invoice without a purchase order reference. In this case, additional data will need to be entered manually in the invoice document, such as currency, baseline date, terms of payment, and invoicing party.  Create additional general ledger account items as required.  Enter and check tax data for the invoice. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 477 12.3 Accounts Payable 12.3 Accounts Payable Accounts payable is the second capability provided by the invoicing and payables func- tionality in SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement. Accounts payable departments handle invoice entry and payment processes so that an enterprise’s suppliers are paid while optimizing cash flow. There is tight integration between the invoice processing and payables processing components of SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement: one feeds the other. There are three major areas of accounts payable that the SAP S/4HANA system supports:  Supplier payment processing  Supplier account management  Correspondence 12.3.1 Supplier Payment Processing Supplier payment processing apps assist the accounts payable accountant in running the operational payables function and assure that payments are made to the suppliers at the optimal time.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The following native SAP Fiori apps for supplier payment processing are available:  Post Outgoing Payments  Clear Outgoing Payments (Manual Clearing)  Manage Payment Blocks  Manage Automatic Payments  Revise Payment Proposals  Monitor Purchase Order Down Payments  Manage Supplier Down Payment Requests  Create Single Payment  Manage Payment Media  Approve Bank Payments  Monitor Batches and Payments Note The following transactional apps for supplier payment processing are also available:  Create Supplier Down Payment Requests (F-47)  Post Supplier Down Payments (F-48)  Schedule Automatic Payments (F110)  Post Supplier Outgoing Payments (F-58) We’ll discuss these apps in the following sections.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 12 Invoice and Payables Management 478 Post Outgoing Payments The Post Outgoing Payments app (see Figure 12.31) allows you to post and clear a single outgoing payment in one step. Normally, enterprises process outgoing payments auto- matically based on payment proposals. However, if you want to issue a payment to a supplier immediately, you need to enter the payment data manually. You can clear these outgoing payments with open supplier line items. You can also post an outgoing payment to a general ledger account. The following features are available in the Post Outgoing Payments app:  List open items that can be cleared with the outgoing payment.  Add or change the discount to be applied to each invoice.  Create residual items by entering a residual amount and assigning one or more rea- son codes and reference information about the business partner.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can define in configuration if a new item is to be posted to the business partner account or if the difference is to be cleared.  Post an outgoing payment to a general ledger account, if required with account assignment.  Post an outgoing payment on account , which means to a customer or supplier account without reference to a specific item if clearing isn’t possible.  Search for open items of selected suppliers or of all suppliers via fuzzy logic.  Create notes and affix attachments while posting the clearing document.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: 479 12.3 Accounts Payable  Enter characteristics for profitability-related postings to assign profitability seg- ments in profitability analysis.  Arrange open items using an invoice reference.  Simulate the resulting journal entry.  Clear the payment with the selected open items. The Post Outgoing Payments app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant stan- dard authorization role. Clear Outgoing Payments (Manual Clearing) Normally, the system will clear outgoing payments automatically. However, if you’ve paid your supplier manually without reference to an open item, you can use this app to find the matching items and clear the payment manually.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: The Clear Outgoing Payments (Manual Clearing) app (see Figure 12.32) can provide the following functions:  View open outgoing payments in your area of responsibility in My Worklist.  List open items to clear the open payments.  Apply or change the discount to be applied to each invoice.  Create residual items by entering a residual amount and assigning one or more rea- son codes and reference information about the business partner.  Post an outgoing payment to a general ledger account, if required with account assignment.  Post an outgoing payment on account —that is, to a customer or supplier account without reference to a specific item—if clearing isn’t possible.  Search for open items of selected suppliers or of all suppliers via fuzzy logic.  Enter characteristics for profitability-related postings to assign profitability seg- ments in profitability analysis.  View the withholding tax posted for each open item.  Create notes and attachments while posting the clearing document.  Simulate the resulting journal entry.  Clear the open payment with the selected open items that match the payment.  Clear open items for a supplier account instead for a payment.  Clear open items for down payments.

You can use the search and sort functions to select and display invoice documents that are blocked. Figure 12.33 Manage Payment Blocks App The Manage Payment Blocks app provides the following functions:  Search for open invoices by supplier, purchase order, invoice number, or journal entry.  Display supplier accounts and open invoices and view their blocking status. © 2026 by Rheinwerk Publishing Inc., Boston (MA)

docs.text: 481 12.3 Accounts Payable  Display open invoices with payment details and related documents.  View the status of invoices and supplier accounts.  Select supplier accounts and invoices to block them for payment or unblock them.  Enter payment block reasons and comments. The Manage Payment Blocks app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant stan- dard authorization role. Manage Automatic Payments The Manage Automatic Payments app (see Figure 12.34) allows you to schedule pay- ment proposals or payments. You then can obtain an overview of the status of the pro- posals or payments.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: Figure 12.34 Manage Automatic Payments App The Manage Automatic Payments app has the following features:  Schedule payment proposals or payments directly.  Automatically create payment media after scheduling payment runs. You can find the created payment media in the Manage Payment Media app.  Create payment advices.  Search proposals and payments by identifier, run date, user ID, and company code.  Check for completeness via the log. Revise Payment Proposals The Revise Payment Proposals app (see Figure 12.35) allows you to check and revise pay- ment proposals and the details of open items. This app helps you ensure that all sup- plier payments are made in a timely and accurate manner and that these payments remain compliant with company policies.

docs.bookTitle: Sourcing and Procurement with SAP S4HANA
docs.text: You can perform the following using the Revise Payment Proposals app:  Display open payment proposals.  Edit payment proposals to change payment methods, partner bank account, or other payment-related information if needed.  Block and unblock items in payments and reallocate items among payments.  Mass block items in payments.  Calculate the total payment amount by payee, currency, and other criteria.  Check the exceptions log.  Navigate to the Manage Payment Proposals app. The Revise Payment Proposals app is assigned to the accounts payable accountant standard authorization role.

docs.text: Note The key performance indicator shown on the Revise Payment Proposals tile displays only the number of outgoing payments; it doesn’t include incoming payments that could be part of a payment proposal.
